text: In-sequence tutorials improved ORS topic post-test scores by 19% (d=0.85) compared to out-of-sequence tutorials (d=0.38). Time spent was longer but not statistically significant. Pre-test scores were similar between groups.

memory: Cinacalcet vs. control: iPTH decreased 42.3% vs. 30.7% (P=0.483). Primary endpoint achieved by 48.5% vs. 51.5% (P=1.000). iPTH target 150-300 pg/ml achieved by 24.3% vs. 18.2% (P=0.764).
text: Cinacalcet showed a greater reduction in iPTH (42.3% vs. 30.7%) compared to control, though not statistically significant (P=0.483). Achievement of the iPTH target (150-300 pg/ml) was 24.3% vs. 18.2% (P=0.764), also not significant.

memory: All 24 subjects tolerated four products without clinically significant adverse events, serious adverse events, or discontinuations. Gastrointestinal events were reported for both DC161-DP0292 and comparator, with no differences in incidence or type. Source: [PMC5839221].
text: Both Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 demonstrated comparable safety profiles, with no clinically significant adverse events, serious adverse events, or discontinuations reported among the 24 subjects. Gastrointestinal events were observed but showed no differences in incidence or type between the two products. Source: [PMC5839221].

memory: CYP2C9 IM vs EM showed significant sildenafil ratio differences in Caucasians (P=0.0165). CYP3A5 PM had higher, non-significant concentrations (P>0.14). CYP3A4 IM had higher sildenafil ratio (P=0.045). Age and BMI correlated with sildenafil ratio (P<0.0001). Adjustments included age, BMI, and ancestry PCs.
text: CYP3A4 Intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil levels than Extensive metabolizers (P=0.045). Adjustments for age, BMI, and ancestry were made.

memory: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations increased IgG titers (median 8100, 24300) and antibody concentrations (0.861–17.75 μg/ml). No ADCC responses observed. One severe hypoglycaemia case and 15% mild adverse events. No HIV infections reported.
text: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations increased IgG titers and concentrations but no ADCC responses were observed compared to baseline (source: working notes).

memory: A study found no significant differences in ACR20, ACR50, or ACR70 responses between biosimilar and reference adalimumab. Adverse events were mild, unrelated, and resolved. No persistent lab changes, musculoskeletal abnormalities, or bilirubin changes were observed.
text: Biosimilar adalimumab shows no significant effect on bilirubin levels compared to reference adalimumab, as no persistent bilirubin changes were observed in the study.

memory: MSDC-0160 (N=16) vs. placebo (N=13) in mild AD showed no change in whole brain glucose metabolism but preserved cerebellum metabolism. text: MSDC-0160 showed no improvement in cognitive test battery global cognitive score compared to control in mild AD (PMC4153084).
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: JQJT tablets reduced diabetes incidence (16.5% vs. 28.9%, P=0.005) and improved normalized blood glucose (41.8% vs. 27.8%, P=0.0049) compared to placebo. Adverse events were similar (2.8% vs. 1.7%, P=0.501).
text: JinqiJiangtang tablets significantly reduced the risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes compared to placebo (16.5% vs. 28.9%, P=0.005). They also improved normalized blood glucose levels (41.8% vs. 27.8%, P=0.0049), with similar adverse event rates.
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
outcome: risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes

text: Group A (clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG) had a higher bleeding complication rate (7.1%) compared to Group B (post-CAG if PCI: 0.7%, P=0.006; adjusted OR 3.03). Female gender and GP IIb/IIIa use also increased bleeding risk.
intervention: group A ('non-selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG;

memory: Daikenchuto (DKT) significantly reduced GSRS indigestion/constipation (P < 0.001), bloating VAS (76→30, P = 0.005), and face scale pain/bloating (P = 0.039/0.008). No changes in bowel frequency or stool form. 40% SIBO positive. Source: [PMC4812817].
text: Daikenchuto significantly reduced indigestion and constipation scores compared to control (P < 0.001). It also improved bloating VAS and face scale pain/bloating (P = 0.005, 0.039, 0.008). No changes in bowel frequency or stool form. Source: [PMC4812817].

memory: In a porcine model, α-MSH post-DBD kidney transplant reduced urine output (p<0.05) and impaired GFR recovery during 10-hour follow-up. Sodium excretion decreased (p<0.05). No effect on inflammatory markers; trends showed lower blood pressure and higher heart rate. No anuria observed.
text: α-MSH post-DBD kidney transplant in a porcine model reduced urine output (p<0.05) and impaired GFR recovery during 10-hour follow-up, with decreased sodium excretion (p<0.05). No effect on inflammatory markers was observed.

memory: TCC showed higher CPAP use (4.1 vs 2.8 hrs/night, P=0.07) and better continuation rates than usual care. No significant AHI reduction difference (TCC: 38.1±18.4; UCC: 32.2±14.8; P=0.32). Both groups reported satisfaction and no concerns about data monitoring.
text: Telemonitored clinical care (TCC) was associated with higher CPAP use (4.1 vs 2.8 hrs/night) and better continuation rates compared to usual care, though the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.07). outcome: Patients rated their likelihood to continue using CPAP

memory: A study compared usual care (UC) and manual therapy (UCMT) for headaches. Both groups showed significant improvements in primary and secondary outcomes with no inter-group differences. Baseline characteristics were similar, and global perceived effect and HIT-6 scores improved equally. Sample size remained low.
text: The study found no significant difference between usual care and manual therapy in reducing headache frequency, pain intensity, medication use, absenteeism, or need for additional help. Both groups improved similarly in all secondary outcomes.
outcome: Reduction in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and use of additional professional help (secondary outcomes)

memory: Frovatriptan reduced 24h migraine recurrence (10% vs 32%, p < 0.01) compared to rizatriptan in menstrually related migraine, with similar 2h and 24h pain relief (p = NS). Frovatriptan showed a more favorable sustained effect. Source: PMC3208043.
text: Frovatriptan significantly reduced the cumulative hazard of recurrence during follow-up in menstrually related migraine compared to rizatriptan (10% vs 32%, p < 0.01), with similar pain relief. Source: PMC3208043.
outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine

memory: A study found no significant differences in operated or discharged patients between RMC and UNN (p=0.432). RMC had longer casting consultation times (29.0 vs. 22.6 min, p=0.0063) but similar consultation numbers per patient. RMC was not inferior to standard care.
text: Video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) resulted in longer casting consultation durations (29.0 min) compared to standard consultations (UNN, 22.6 min, p=0.0063), though RMC was not inferior to standard care.
outcome: The mean consultation duration in the subgroup patients who required casting

memory: ProTaper Universal retreatment removed more filling material (12.96%) than Mani NRT-GPR (24.26%, P=0.0056) and caused greater dentin removal (5.02% vs 1.36%, P=0.0028). No complications were reported for either system.
text: ProTaper Universal retreatment removes more filling material (12.96%) than Mani NRT-GPR (24.26%, P=0.0056), but causes greater dentin removal (5.02% vs 1.36%, P=0.0028). No complications were reported.

memory: Combined prostaglandin gel + dilators improved Bishop score change (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) and reduced induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hrs, P=0.085) compared to prostaglandin alone. However, infection rates were higher (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003).
text: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators significantly improved Bishop score changes (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) compared to prostaglandin gel alone, though induction time reduction was not statistically significant (P=0.085). intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours

memory: The Sonas programme improved communication ability (Holden Communication Scale) compared to reading and control groups (p < 0.05), with significant benefits in severe dementia after 12 weeks. text: The Sonas programme did not significantly affect MMSE scores compared to control groups. While it improved communication ability in severe dementia, no overall difference in cognitive function, as measured by MMSE, was observed (p < 0.05 for communication, no significant effect on MMSE).

memory: RFA vs resection for CRLM: No OS/DFS diff for <3cm (P=0.962, 0.980). ≥3cm DFS worse with RFA (P=0.015). 5-year DFS: RFA 6.4%, resection 16.2%. OS: RFA 47.6%, resection 56.0% (P=0.308).
text: For tumors <3 cm, RFA and resection show similar 5-year DFS (6.4% vs 16.2%, P=0.980). For ≥3 cm, RFA is associated with worse DFS (P=0.015). No significant OS difference was found. Source: Working notes.

memory: 13 subjects; PJ (5.8 mg anthocyanin/100ml) reduced SBP (7%, P=0.013) and DBP (6%, P=0.010). No significant changes in FMD or inflammatory markers (CRP, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, E-selectin, IL-6; P>0.172).
text: Pomegranate juice significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (7%, P=0.013) and diastolic blood pressure (6%, P=0.010) compared to baseline in 13 subjects. No significant changes were observed in inflammatory markers or FMD. Source: Working notes.

memory: rFSH + HMG improved total fetuses (p=0.02) and fertility outcomes (live birth, chemical, clinical pregnancy rates; p<0.05) compared to rFSH + rLH. No differences in follicles, oocytes, or fetus quality (p>0.05). Source: [PMC5601935].
text: The combination of rFSH + HMG showed no significant difference in the number of oocytes or M2 oocytes compared to rFSH + rLH (p>0.05). Source: [PMC5601935].
intervention: Recombinant- follicle stimulating hormone (r-FSH) plus recombinant-luteinizing hormone (rLH)
outcome: Number of oocytes or M2 oocytes

memory: Endobutton and Rigidfix showed no significant difference in knee stability (P=0.99) or tibial displacement (P=0.46). Endobutton had better patient satisfaction (P=0.006) and sports ability (P=0.006), similar pain scores (P=0.08), and slightly improved range of motion (P=0.06).
text: Endobutton showed significantly better patient satisfaction (P=0.006) compared to Rigidfix in the IKDC 2000 questionnaire, with no significant difference in knee stability (P=0.99) or tibial displacement (P=0.46).
outcome: the mean scores of satisfaction with surgery by using a subjective questionnaire IKDC 2000

memory: Telephone follow-up improved eligibility screening attendance (17.5% vs. 9.1%, RR 1.92, P < 0.001) and RCT enrollment (12.3% vs. 7.4%, RR 1.66, P=0.01) compared to mail. Groups were similar in age (mean 55.7 vs. 55.6 years). Study halted due to funding issues.
text: The effect of "Follow-up invitation by telephone" compared with "Follow-up invitation by mail" on "Age of the participants" was minimal, as groups were similar in age (mean 55.7 vs. 55.6 years). Source: Study halted due to funding issues.

memory: Study [PMC4048120] found no significant differences in implant success, bone loss, or peri-implant health (CFV, plaque, gingival indices) between immediate and delayed implants at 12 months. Higher maxillary CFV in immediate implants at some time points, but not overall significant.
text: The effect of receiving implants immediately after extraction versus placing them in healed sites on maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3 showed no significant overall difference (PMC4048120). Some time points showed higher maxillary CFV in immediate implants, but these were not statistically significant.
comparator: implants were placed in healed sites
outcome: maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3

memory: Misoprostol+celecoxib vs. vehicle+celecoxib increased diastolic (p=0.0071) and mean blood pressure (p=0.0153) and reduced potassium excretion (p=0.0011). No significant changes in aldosterone or KIM-1. Source: PMC3931696.
text: Misoprostol + celecoxib reduced potassium excretion compared to vehicle alone (p=0.0011). Source: PMC3931696.

memory: A study compared a neuromuscular blocking agent (Group A) with atracurium infusion (Group B). Heart rate was similar during surgery but higher in Group B post-extubation (P=0.02). Mean arterial pressure and brain relaxation scores were similar. Recovery characteristics, including extubation time and Aldrete score, were comparable. No differences in hemodynamic parameters or surgical conditions were observed.
text: Group B (Atracurium infusion) had a higher heart rate than Group A (Neuromuscular blocking agent) 30 minutes after extubation (P=0.02). Other parameters like mean arterial pressure and recovery characteristics were similar between groups.

memory: POMx vs. PLAC showed no significant SBP change (p > 0.05) but increased NO3− (p < 0.04). ALTPOMx improved VO2 max at 5 min (p = 0.001) vs. ALTPLAC, but not SEAPOMx. Altitude reduced performance (p < 0.02). Submaximal VO2 unchanged by POMx.
text: Exercise at 1657 m with pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx) significantly improved VO2 max at 5 minutes (p = 0.001) compared to placebo (ALTPLAC). Altitude reduced overall performance (p < 0.02), but submaximal VO2 was unchanged by pomegranate extract.
intervention: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx)
comparator: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Placebo (ALTPLAC)
outcome: Level of VO2 max after 5 minutes into cycling time trial to exhaustion at 100%VO2max

memory: Baseline characteristics and scores (MAQ, SAUMD) were similar between self-management and treatment-as-usual groups. At 30 months, self-management showed better medication compliance, insight, and higher antipsychotic dosages (p=0.003). Re-hospitalization rates were lower in the self-management group (1.9% vs. 14.3%).
text: The self-management group had a significantly lower re-hospitalization rate (1.9%) compared to treatment-as-usual (14.3%) at 30 months (p=0.003). This suggests that self-management is more effective in reducing re-hospitalizations.

memory: Groups A and B had similar baseline OSDI, TBUT, staining, and Schirmer scores (p > 0.05). After 4 weeks, both showed significant improvements in OSDI and staining (p < 0.001), with no significant changes in Schirmer or TBUT (p > 0.05). No significant differences in efficacy between single and multiple dose artificial tears (p > 0.05).
text: Both single and multiple dose artificial tears significantly improved OSDI after 4 weeks (p < 0.001), with no significant difference in efficacy between the two (p > 0.05).

memory: A 10-week telephone intervention improved outcomes compared to 3 calls for blood sugar monitoring. At 28 weeks, the intervention group had lower 2h post-lunch blood glucose (123±18 vs 137.5±25.7, p=0.008) and higher postpartum glucose screening rates (p<0.001).
text: The 10-week telephone intervention significantly reduced mean 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose levels at 28 weeks of pregnancy compared to three monitoring calls (123±18 vs 137.5±25.7, p=0.008).
intervention: telephone intervention was performed for 10 weeks
comparator: three times of telephone call was established to record blood sugar levels
outcome: mean level of blood glucose, 2 hours after lunch at 28 weeks of pregnancy

memory: A study compared text message feedback to no assistance, showing near-zero to small, nonsignificant effect sizes for PHQ-9, PTQ, FFA, and SCS-D (PMC5434251). Intervention favored symptom measures (PHQ-9, PTQ), while control favored FFA and SCS-D. Largest differences were in perseverative thinking, mindfulness, and exercise frequency.
text: Patients receiving text message–based feedback showed near-zero to small, nonsignificant effects on PHQ-9 scores compared to those without assistance (PMC5434251). Intervention slightly favored symptom measures, but differences were not statistically significant.
comparator: Patients not receiving text message assistance during follow-up

memory: Bio-Gro™ had no effect on metabolic panels, SBP, DBP, or HR (p > 0.05). Time effects observed for BUN, sodium, chloride, CO2, calcium, albumin, and alka phosphate (p < 0.05). No group × time interactions. Group effects for RBC, creatinine, eGFR, and BUN/creatinine (p < 0.05).
text: The bio-active peptide supplement had no significant effect on heart rate compared to placebo (p > 0.05).

memory: Anxiety scores were lower in the intervention group (14.53±2.44) compared to the control group (21.28±2.86; p=0.04). Pain scores showed no significant difference (p=0.15), with no gender differences in pain (p=0.71). Source: PMC5951568.
text: Providing written information about electrodiagnostic testing reduced anxiety scores compared to the control group (14.53±2.44 vs. 21.28±2.86; p=0.04). Source: PMC5951568.
intervention: provided with written information about the electrodiagnostic testing

memory: A study compared cefepime alone (C), cefepime + amikacin (C-A), and cefepime + levofloxacin (C-L) for VAP. No significant differences were found in ICU stay, ventilator-free days, biomarker trends (temperature, leukocytosis, CRP), or mortality (p > 0.05).
text: The study found no significant difference in ICU length of stay between cefepime alone (C), cefepime with amikacin (C-A), and cefepime with levofloxacin (C-L) for VAP (p > 0.05).
intervention: cefepime (C group), cefepime with amikacin (C-A group)
outcome: length of stay in the intensive care unit after infection

memory: ILF (Irinotecan + HFOL) vs ELF (Etoposide + HFOL) in metastatic gastric cancer showed higher response rates (43% vs 24%, RR 0.56, P=0.0467). ILF had better PFS (4.5 vs 2.3 mo) but more diarrhea (18% vs 0%). ELF had higher neutropenia (57% vs 18%).
text: ILF caused more Grade 3/4 digestive system toxic events (18% diarrhea) compared to ELF (0%) in metastatic gastric cancer, according to the study.

memory: Maraviroc intensification in 21 HIV-cART patients improved FMD (+0.73%, p=0.049) vs. control (-0.42%). CCR5 expression increased in CD4+ (2.4%) and CD8+ (14.0%) T cells. No effect on D-dimer or immune activation. 8-week intervention, no washout; carry-over effect noted.
text: Maraviroc intensification increased CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells by 14.0% compared to unchanged cART (p=0.049). This effect was observed alongside improved FMD and no changes in D-dimer or immune activation.
outcome: CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells

memory: Study [PMC5695311] showed significant THI score reduction in the effective sound masking group (t=-14.07, P<0.001) compared to no change in the non-effective group (t=-1.98, P=0.054). Pre-intervention THI scores were lower in the non-effective group (t=4.11, P<0.001).
text: Intensive sound masking therapy significantly reduced THI scores in the effective subgroup (t=-14.07, P<0.001) compared to no change in the non-effective group (t=-1.98, P=0.054) (PMC5695311).
intervention: intensive sound masking therapy on tinnitus in effective subgroup

memory: LNG-IUS showed higher regression rates at 3 (67.8% vs. 47.5%), 6 (79.7% vs. 60.7%), and 12 months (88.1% vs. 55.7%) compared to NET (p<0.001). No difference in median regression time (3 mo). NET had higher hysterectomy rates (57.4% vs. 22%).
text: The Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) showed a higher regression rate at 3 months (67.8%) compared to oral norethisterone acetate (47.5%, p<0.001). No difference in median regression time was observed.

memory: In a CKD-MBD study, adding calcium carbonate to calcitriol did not significantly alter 25(OH)D, PTH, or serum calcium/phosphorus compared to calcitriol alone. FGF23 increased in both groups, with a trend toward greater increase in the combination group (P=0.097). Source: [PMC5565373].
text: In CKD-MBD patients, combining calcium carbonate with calcitriol did not significantly affect serum calcium levels compared to calcitriol alone. Source: [PMC5565373].
intervention: a combination of calcium carbonate and calcitriol group

memory: MgSO4 (30-50 mg/kg) vs. saline showed no HR difference (P>0.3). MgSO4 groups had lower SBP, DBP, MAP at 1, 3, 5 min post-intubation. SBP changes <20% or >20% not significant at 10 min. Extubation time and adverse events were similar. [PMC4418140]

intervention: MgSO4 - Group I, II, III: 30. 40/ 50 mg/kg
comparator: normal saline as a control group (S)
outcome: (SBP) systolic blood pressures at 1, 3, and 5 minutes after intubation

text: Tranexamic acid (TXA) showed no significant difference compared to placebo in the risk of unfavorable outcome on the Glasgow Outcome Scale. Source: PMC4221638.
outcome: Risk of unfavorable outcome on the Glasgow Outcome Score

memory: In a study [PMC4610775], UK treatment improved cognitive status. At 4 weeks, Aβ1-40 decreased, but Aβ1-42 remained stable. By 8 weeks, both Aβ1-40 and Aβ1-42 significantly decreased with continued cognitive improvement.
text: The study [PMC4610775] found that UK treatment led to a decrease in Aβ1-40 levels at 4 weeks and a significant reduction by 8 weeks, alongside cognitive improvement. No direct comparison with a control group was provided in the notes.

memory: Probiotic Bifidobacterium lactis increased monocyte phagocytosis compared to maltodextrin (P < 0.001) and prebiotic (P < 0.001). Prebiotic (galacto-oligosaccharides) had no effect on monocyte/granulocyte phagocytosis vs. maltodextrin. Source: PMC4153077.
text: Bifidobacterium lactis significantly increased monocyte phagocytosis compared to both maltodextrin and galacto-oligosaccharides (GOS) (P < 0.001). GOS had no effect on monocyte phagocytosis relative to maltodextrin. Source: PMC4153077.

memory: Study [PMC5019463] compared navigator vs usual care. Follow-up attendance was 69.8% (G1), 82.5% (G2), 73.3% (G3) for ≥1 visit; 91.3% (G1), 74.3% (G2), 66.7% (G3) for ≥2 visits (P=0.11).
text: The study [PMC5019463] found no significant difference (P=0.11) in adherence rates for patients attending two or more follow-up appointments between the navigator group (91.3%) and usual care groups (74.3% and 66.7%). memory: KOH and TCA improved hydration/texture over time, except D14 (KOH hydration) and D7 (TCA texture). KOH improved elasticity; TCA worsened it. No significant group differences except D7 TCA texture (p=0.00). Callus area reduced significantly by D7-D21 for both. [PMC4869362]

memory: PE chemotherapy showed higher clinical response (76.06% vs 59.95%) and lower pathologic stages (P < 0.001) than FEC, with similar pCR rates (10.61% vs 12.31%, P = 0.665). PE caused more severe neutropenia (11.97% vs 5.96%, P = 0.031).
text: The PE regimen caused a higher frequency of severe neutropenia (11.97%) compared to FEC (5.96%, P = 0.031).
intervention: receive 4–6 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy with tri-weekly 5-fluorouracil–epirubicin–cyclophosphamide (FEC) regimen

memory: Bimatoprost PF and standard bimatoprost both significantly reduced IOP (p<0.001) with <0.4 mm Hg difference (not significant). text: Bimatoprost 0.03% PF and Lumigan both significantly reduced intraocular pressure (p<0.001) with no significant difference in efficacy (<0.4 mm Hg). memory: T-EO and Af-EO reduced PL-biofilm BV and CG vs. water (P<0.001). Af-EO showed greater reduction in thickness and CG after 4 days (P=0.012, 0.001). Neither significantly reduced 48h biofilm thickness post-single rinse. Outer layers exhibited higher BV.
text: Both T-EO and Af-EO formulations significantly reduced biofilm biomass (BV) and colony count (CG) compared to sterile water (P<0.001) after 4 days. memory: A study of 40 children (11.5 ± 1.175 years) found that vitamin D supplementation increased HDL-C (P=0.007) and vitamin D levels (P<0.001) compared to placebo. Adjusted analysis confirmed higher HDL-C (P=0.04) and vitamin D (P<0.001) in the treatment group. Source: PMC5045666.
text: Vitamin D supplementation in children increased HDL-C (P=0.007) and vitamin D levels (P<0.001) compared to placebo, with adjusted analysis confirming these effects (P=0.04 for HDL-C; P<0.001 for vitamin D). Source: PMC5045666.
outcome: Baseline levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and vitamin D

memory: Study [PMC4467206] found TA and IT improved SF-36 MCS and SOC more than CT (p = .001), with no difference between TA and IT. Large effect sizes: MCS ES = 1.12 (TA), 0.82 (IT).
text: Both therapeutic acupuncture (TA) and salutogenic dialogue (IT) significantly improved SF-36 MCS and SOC compared to conventional treatment (CT) (p = .001). TA and IT showed similar effects, with large effect sizes (MCS ES = 1.12 for TA, 0.82 for IT). (Source: PMC4467206)
outcome: SF-36 mental component summary (MCS), sense of coherence (SOC)

memory: Oral glutamine (10g in 1000ml water) given 2h pre-radiation reduced grade 3-4 mucositis (14.29% vs 37.14%, p=0.02; 2.86% vs 17.14%, p=0.04) and delayed onset (p<0.001) compared to no intervention.
text: Oral glutamine suspension (10g in 1000ml water) given 2h before radiation significantly reduced the mean duration of grade 3-4 mucositis compared to baseline (14.29% vs 37.14%, p=0.02; 2.86% vs 17.14%, p=0.04) and delayed its onset (p<0.001).
intervention: oral glutamine suspension daily 2h before radiation in the study arm (10 g in 1000 ml of water)
outcome: The mean duration of grade 3 mucositis or worse (grade 3 and grade 4)

memory: A study compared DCS and PCB in schizophrenia patients, finding no significant differences in age, illness duration, or CPZ equivalents. DCS did not improve symptoms or cognitive dysfunction but may worsen negative symptoms in early-onset schizophrenia. Source: PMC5508614.
text: The effect of "DCS D-cycloserine first" compared with "PCB placebo first" on "duration of illness (schizophrenia patients)" showed no significant difference. Source: PMC5508614.

memory: Steroid therapy (10 days) vs. standard therapy in sepsis showed no significant differences in SOFA score changes (P=0.624), hospital stay (P=0.406), or 28-day mortality (P=0.343). Mortality rates were 40% vs. 60%. Source: PMC125315.
text: The addition of 10 days of physiological-dose steroid therapy to standard sepsis treatment did not significantly affect 28-day mortality (P=0.343), with mortality rates of 40% vs. 60% (PMC125315).
intervention: received standard therapy for sepsis and physiological-dose steroid therapy for 10 days;
comparator: received only standard therapy for sepsis

memory: SRP with antibiotics showed no significant PD or CAL differences vs SRP alone (P > 0.05). Test group had improved TIMP-1/MMP-1 balance at 6 months (P < 0.05). Both groups had reduced MMP-1 levels at 3 and 6 months (P < 0.05).
text: SRP combined with amoxicillin plus metronidazole showed improved TIMP-1/MMP-1 balance at 6 months compared to SRP alone (P < 0.05), despite no significant differences in PD or CAL. Both groups had reduced MMP-1 levels at 3 and 6 months (P < 0.05).
intervention: scaling and root planning (SRP) in combination with amoxicillin plus metronidazole

memory: AIT showed greater VO2max improvement than WALK (p=0.027, ITT): +1.01 vs. -1.03. MVIT was non-inferior but not superior. AIT had 74 min/week vs. WALK’s 116. Waist, body fat, and BP decreased, possibly due to Hawthorne effect.
text: Aerobic interval training (AIT) significantly improved VO2max more than walking (p=0.027, ITT: +1.01 vs. -1.03). AIT required less time (74 min/week vs. 116). Other benefits like reduced waist, body fat, and BP may be due to the Hawthorne effect.

memory: Study [PMC3622020] evaluated 0%, 1%, and 5% glucose acetated Ringer’s during cesarean delivery. Group III (5%) showed the lowest neonatal blood glucose (29.2 ± 7.5 mg/dL) and highest maternal post-infusion glucose (252.5 ± 41.8 mg/dL). Nine neonates in Group III required glucose infusion therapy.
text: Infusing 5% glucose acetated Ringer’s during cesarean delivery significantly increases maternal blood glucose levels compared to 0% or 1% (Study [PMC3622020]). Maternal post-infusion glucose was 252.5 ± 41.8 mg/dL in the 5% group.
intervention: 5 %  glucose acetated Ringer’s solution infusion during cesarean delivery
comparator: 0 % or 1 %, glucose acetated Ringer’s solution infusion during cesarean delivery

memory: ESWT and TPI+TENS showed similar neck ROM improvements (p>0.05). ESWT had greater pain threshold increases (p=0.045) and larger VAS reduction (p=0.010). McGill and PRS showed no group differences (p>0.05). Time effects were significant for ROM (excluding extension).
text: ESWT showed greater VAS reduction (p=0.010) compared to TPI+TENS, indicating more effective pain relief. Both treatments improved neck ROM similarly (p>0.05). No significant differences were found in McGill or PRS scores.
comparator: trigger point injections (TPI)+transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS)
outcome: The changes in visual analog scale

memory: A 4-week WBV training program (15 min, 5x/week) had no significant effect on COP sway velocity or path length compared to control or baseline. It significantly improved anterior, non-paretic, and paretic reach (p<0.05). Source: [PMC4175246].
text: The task-oriented training program with WBV for 4 weeks did not significantly affect average velocity or total path length of COP compared to baseline. Source: [PMC4175246].
intervention: task-oriented training program with WBV, which was performed for 15 minutes, five times per week, for four weeks and control
outcome: average velocity and total path length of COP

memory: No significant differences in QoL, overall survival (median 13.0 vs 11.0 months), or progression-free survival (10.2 vs 10.8 months) between immediate and delayed treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Adjustments and multiple scales confirmed consistent results. Early treatment did not improve survival or QoL.
text: There is no significant effect of receiving immediate treatment compared to delayed treatment on overall QoL in metastatic colorectal cancer patients. Results showed similar QoL, overall survival, and progression-free survival between the two groups.

memory: Educational workshops significantly improved knowledge and attitudes (P < 0.0001) in mothers, couples, and controls. Normal vaginal delivery was preferred (P = 0.017). No pre-intervention attitude differences (P = 0.120, 0.112), but post-intervention differences emerged (P < 0.0001). Age and education varied across groups.
text: The couples' educational workshop significantly increased preference for normal vaginal delivery compared to the control group (P = 0.017). This effect emerged post-intervention, with notable differences in knowledge and attitudes (P < 0.0001).
outcome: Most preferred method; normal vaginal delivery

memory: Liraglutide 1.8 mg significantly improved weight loss, SSPG, SBP, fasting glucose, and triglycerides compared to placebo (P < 0.001).
text: Liraglutide 1.8 mg significantly reduced systolic blood pressure, fasting glucose, and triglycerides compared to placebo (P < 0.001).
outcome: systolic blood pressure, fasting glucose , and triglyceride

memory: Both home- and centre-based CR improved peakVO2 similarly (discharge +11% vs +15%; 1-year +16% vs +17%). Home-based CR showed higher satisfaction (p=0.02) and non-significantly lower costs (€437, p=0.39), suggesting potential cost-effectiveness. No differences in physical activity, HRQoL, or long-term outcomes.
text: Home-based training with telemonitoring and centre-based training similarly improve peakVO2 (discharge +11% vs +15%; 1-year +16% vs +17%). No significant differences in long-term outcomes, but home-based training showed higher satisfaction and non-significantly lower costs.

memory: Vaccine group showed higher HIV-1 incidence (4.7% vs 3.0%, p=0.01). Men had increased infection hazard ratios (2.46, p=0.01), while women showed a non-significant increase (1.42, p=0.18). No significant changes in condom use or number of partners reported.
text: The vaccine group had a higher infection hazard ratio for men compared to the placebo group (2.46, p=0.01). This effect was not significant in women (1.42, p=0.18). No significant differences in condom use or number of partners were reported.
outcome: Estimated infection hazard ratios for men

memory: Linagliptin reduced UACR by 32% (P<0.05) and HbA1c by 0.61% (P<0.0001) vs. placebo. Adverse events were similar (63.0 vs. 63.6%), but drug-related AEs were higher with linagliptin (14.2 vs. 7.3%).
text: Linagliptin significantly reduced urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) by 32% (P<0.05) compared with control at 24 weeks. It also improved HbA1c by 0.61% (P<0.0001). Adverse events were similar, but drug-related events were higher with linagliptin.

memory: Transurethral access (1.2 vs 1.28, P=0.643) and operative time (32.7 vs 34.3 min, P=0.428) were similar between groups. Group 2 had a longer hospital stay (2.1 vs 1.2 days, P=0.000). Both groups achieved 100% stone clearance.
text: The transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath was associated with a shorter hospital stay compared to conventional percutaneous cystolithotripsy (2.1 vs 1.2 days, P=0.000).
intervention: transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath

memory: PIVC failure rates (per 1000 hours) were not significantly different between 3 mL vs 10 mL flush (4.84 vs 7.44, p=0.06) or 24h vs 6h frequency (5.06 vs 7.34, p=0.05). No significant interaction (p=0.21). Average dwell time was 3.1 days.
text: The effect of 0.9% sodium chloride 10 mL flush compared with 3 mL flush on PIVC failure rates per 1000 hours was not statistically significant (4.84 vs 7.44, p=0.06).
outcome: Peripheral intravenous catheter failure rates per 1000 hours

memory: A study compared Aloe cream and Calendula ointment for diaper dermatitis. No baseline differences were found. Both improved rash severity (P < 0.001), but Calendula showed fewer rash sites (P = 0.001). No adverse effects were reported.
text: The study found no baseline differences between Aloe cream and Calendula ointment groups. Both improved rash severity (P < 0.001), with Calendula showing fewer rash sites (P = 0.001). No adverse effects were reported.

memory: Mobiletype significantly improved GP decision-making in medication (p=0.013, d=0.55), referrals (p=0.012, d=0.56), diagnosis (p=0.002, d=0.69), and communication (p=0.031, d=0.47) vs. attention control. No effect on GP confidence (p=0.131).
text: The intervention group showed significant improvements in diagnosis, medication decisions, referrals, and communication compared to the attention-comparison group (p<0.05, d=0.47–0.69). No effect on GP confidence was observed. Source: Working notes.
intervention: intervention group (where mood, stress and daily activities were monitored with program mobiletype)
comparator: attention-comparison group (where only daily activities were monitored)
outcome: helping to diagnosed and communication, specific medical and mental health problems

memory: A study compared MAT with a control group on workaholism and job performance. Baseline scores were similar. MAT improved workaholism, job satisfaction, engagement, and reduced work hours without performance decline. Results support MAT's efficacy in reducing workaholism symptoms and improving psychological well-being. Source: PMC5520118.
text: Meditation Awareness Training (MAT) reduces workaholism symptomatology more effectively than a control group, improving job satisfaction and engagement without performance decline. Source: PMC5520118.

memory: The intervention showed no significant effect on early fetal loss (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.88–1.08) or stillbirths (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.76–1.04), but was associated with reduced neonatal mortality (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68–0.93).
text: The intervention of neonatal bag and mask resuscitation and oral antibiotic therapy showed no significant effect on early fetal loss (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.88–1.08) compared to routine care.
intervention: neonatal bag and mask resuscitation and oral antibiotic therapy
comparator: routine care through the existing national programme

memory: Study [PMC3504298] found face-based ABM reduced depressive and anxious symptoms compared to placebo, with effects lasting a month and lower cortisol awakening response. Word-based ABM showed no significant effect. ABM type × stimuli × time interactions were significant for symptoms. Word-based ABM had differential attentional bias effects, but no difference between face- and word-trained groups.
text: Face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) significantly reduces anxious symptoms compared to placebo, with effects lasting up to one month (PMC3504298). Word-based ABM showed no significant impact.

memory: In an ALI model with IAH, PSV vs. PCV showed lower mean airway pressure and reduced IL-6 and type III procollagen mRNA. PSV improved oxygenation, reduced alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, and DAD, and increased SP-B expression. No differences in nIAP animals. Source: [PMC5444773]
text: In an ALI model with IAH, PSV compared to PCV reduced alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, and DAD scores, while improving oxygenation and SP-B expression. These benefits were not observed in nIAP animals. Source: [PMC5444773]
outcome: Alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, or DAD score in animals with IAH

memory: No significant differences in respiration return (A: 2 min, R: 3.3 min, P=0.08), eye opening, verbal response, or recovery discharge between 40 patients (A: Alfentanil, R: Remifentanil). Nausea/vomiting higher in R (n=6) vs A (n=1, P<0.05).
text: No significant differences were found between Alfentanil and Remifentanil in stopping anesthesia drugs, eye opening, verbal response, or discharge from recovery. However, Remifentanil was associated with higher nausea/vomiting (P<0.05). Source: Study of 40 patients.
intervention: 10 μg/kg of Alfentanil, infusion of Alfentanil 1 μg/kg/min
comparator: Remifentanil 0.5 μg/kg, infusion of Remifentanil 0.1 μg/kg/min
outcome: stopping the anesthesia drugs up to opening eyes, return to verbal response, and discharge from the recovery

memory: Primaquine with DHP reduced gametocyte clearance time (1 vs. 12 days, HR 7.3, p=0.01) and carriage (2.1% vs. 15%, p=0.03). Hemoglobin drop was higher in the primaquine group (24.8% vs. 7.1%, p=0.14). G6PD screening excluded 5 patients with severe deficiency.
text: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine + primaquine significantly reduced gametocyte carriage (2.1% vs. 15%, p=0.03) and clearance time (1 vs. 12 days, HR 7.3, p=0.01) compared to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine alone. Hemoglobin drop was higher with primaquine (24.8% vs. 7.1%, p=0.14).

memory: Source [PMC5350209]: Health warning labels (text/image) reduced alcohol acceptance (p < .002) and slowed consumption speed (p < .001) compared to no warning. No difference between text and image warnings; presence, not type, affected consumption rate.
text: Visual warning (text) slowed the speed of alcohol consumption compared to no warning (p < .001). The presence of any warning, not the type, affected consumption rate, with no difference between text and image warnings. Source: [PMC5350209].

memory: Raloxifene reduced blood glucose (AUC, p=0.048) and diabetes incidence in rats, improving femoral toughness and post-yield properties. No DXA, pQCT, or μCT differences were found in L4 vertebrae or femoral midshaft. Diabetic controls had worse distal femur trabecular parameters.
text: Raloxifene improved femoral toughness in diabetic rats compared to controls, despite no differences in bone density measures. This suggests a potential beneficial effect on bone quality beyond structural parameters.

memory: No significant differences in pain (P=0.22), visual acuity (P=0.08-0.36), or refractive error (P=0.23) between alcohol-assisted and mechanical epithelial removal. Alcohol-assisted was faster (96±18 vs. 118±26 sec, P=0.035). Complications and re-epithelialization time were similar.
text: No significant difference in mean spherical equivalent between alcohol-assisted and mechanical epithelial removal (P=0.23). Both methods had similar outcomes in pain, visual acuity, complications, and re-epithelialization time, though alcohol-assisted was faster.

memory: In a study [PMC3441280], ATP supplementation via proximal-release pellets or naso-duodenal tube increased uric acid by ~50% vs. placebo (P < 0.003). Distal-release pellets had no effect. Proximal pellets caused higher plasma lithium levels (P = 0.001) but lower lithium AUC than placebo.
text: Administration via proximal-release pellets increases plasma lithium levels compared to distal-release pellets (P = 0.001). This effect was observed in a study [PMC3441280], though lithium AUC was lower with proximal pellets than placebo.

memory: A study compared Pap smear (intervention) vs no intervention (control) on cervicovaginal lavage (CVL) inflammatory markers. Baseline groups were similar. No significant changes in total protein, IL-8, IL-1β, or IL-6 were found. However, IL-10, TNF-α, and IL-12 p70 were significantly elevated in the intervention group.
text: Pap smear at enrollment significantly increased IL-10 levels compared to no intervention, as shown in a study comparing cervicovaginal lavage inflammatory markers. Baseline groups were similar, but IL-10, TNF-α, and IL-12 p70 were significantly elevated in the intervention group.

memory: SB4 (etanercept biosimilar) demonstrated therapeutic equivalence to ETN in RA patients on MTX, with similar ACR50/70 response rates at week 24 (46.6% vs 42.3% and 25.5% vs 22.6% in PPS). SB4 had a lower ADA incidence (0.7% vs 13.1%). Source: PMC5264222.
text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, showed therapeutic equivalence to etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate, with similar ACR50/70 response rates at week 24 (46.6% vs 42.3% and 25.5% vs 22.6% in PPS). SB4 had a lower ADA incidence (0.7% vs 13.1%). Source: PMC5264222.
outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: Robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) showed higher acute LGE encirclement (72% vs. 60%, P=0.002) and 6-month LGE (56% vs. 45%, P=0.04) compared to standard navigation. Recurrences had higher LGE in the robotic group (43% vs. 30%, P=0.001).
text: Robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) resulted in higher mean LGE encirclement at 6 months compared to standard navigation (56% vs. 45%, P=0.04).
outcome: mean LGE encirclement at 6 months follow-up

memory: Paracetamol 250 mg reduced fever ≥38°C in infants (43% efficacy) but not toddlers. It significantly reduced fever >39°C in toddlers (79% efficacy, PP population). Decreased activity (p=0.005) observed in prophylaxis group. No serious adverse events. [PMC3698010]
text: Paracetamol 250 mg reduced fever but had no significant effect on activity in toddlers. A decrease in activity was noted in the prophylaxis group (p=0.005), though this may not be directly attributable to the drug. [PMC3698010]

memory: In a crossover study of 24 infants, NF showed higher soft stool frequency (17% vs. 0%, p=0.046) and a trend for improved stool consistency (90% vs. 50%, p=0.14). Defecation frequency (5.5 vs. 5.9/week, p=0.38) and painful defecation or abdominal mass were similar between groups.
text: The new formula (NF) increased soft stool frequency compared to the standard formula (17% vs. 0%, p=0.046), with a trend toward better stool consistency (90% vs. 50%, p=0.14). Defecation frequency and abdominal pain were similar between groups. Source: crossover study of 24 infants.

memory: Kegel exercises improved FEV1, FVC, PEFR, FEF 25–75%, IC, and MVV in the experimental group vs. no improvement in the control group (PMC4668172). FEV1/FVC changes were not statistically significant.
text: A Kegel exercises program improved Peak Expiratory Flow Rate (PEFR) compared to control (PMC4668172). No significant changes in FEV1/FVC were observed.

memory: Peramivir and oseltamivir showed no significant differences in symptom disappearance time (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65), TSSs (P = .69), fever-alleviation time (40.0 vs. 37.8 hours, P = .69), or virus titer reduction (P = .51). Source: [PMC5534217].
text: Peramivir (Rapiacta) and oseltamivir (Tamiflu) had no significant difference in the number of days required for influenza symptoms to disappear (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65). Source: [PMC5534217].
outcome: The numbers of days required for the disappearance of influenza symptoms

memory: Telemonitoring increased costs by £115.32/patient (p<0.001) due to service, training, and consultations. Medication cost differences were trivial. Higher hospital admission costs of £105.47 (p=0.424) and no significant difference in accident and emergency visits (p=0.286) were observed. Systolic BP reduction cost £25.56/mm Hg.
text: The "Hypertension telemonitoring-based service" increased accident and emergency visits costs by £115.32 per patient compared to control (p<0.001), mainly due to service, training, and consultations. There was no significant difference in accident and emergency visits costs between groups (p=0.286).

memory: In DPP/DPPOS, continuous antidepressant use was linked to higher diabetes risk in placebo (HR 2.34) and lifestyle (HR 2.48) arms, but lower risk with metformin (HR 0.55). Intermittent use showed a trend in placebo (HR 1.34). ADM type had no effect.
text: In DPP/DPPOS, antidepressant users had higher diabetes risk in the lifestyle arm (HR 2.48) compared to non-users. This effect was reduced with metformin (HR 0.55). Intermittent use showed a trend (HR 1.34). ADM type did not influence the outcome.

memory: BMDMC therapy improved CLP mouse survival (70% vs 40%), reduced lung elastance, alveolar collapse, collagen, and IL-1β, while increasing chemokine expression. Effects varied with insult type (LPS or CLP), influencing adhesion molecule expression. LPS and sham groups had 100% survival at day 7. Source: PMC3856598.
text: BMDMC therapy reduced alveolar collapse in CLP mice compared to controls (PMC3856598).
intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)

memory: In vaginal operative deliveries, infants showed lower pain responses with plastic caps vs. metal cups (p < 0.001), with full recovery within 72h. Metal cups caused more scalp trauma (13.2% vs. 6.6%, p=0.51). No significant differences in EDIN ≥5 proportions. No subgaleal or intracranial hemorrhage reported.
text: In vaginal operative deliveries, infants exhibited lower pain responses with plastic caps compared to metal cups (p < 0.001), with full recovery within 72 hours. Metal cups caused more scalp trauma (13.2% vs. 6.6%, p=0.51), but no significant differences in EDIN ≥5 proportions were observed. No subgaleal or intracranial hemorrhage was reported.

memory: Phase 2a study: AN1792 (Aβ42) vs placebo. Antibody responders had less decline in DAD (p=0.015), Dependence Scale (p=0.033), and CDR-SOB (20.2% less, p=0.185). Non-responders lacked detectable antibodies. Similar brain volume loss noted in follow-up MRI.
text: In a Phase 2a study, synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) showed a statistically significant reduction in Dependence Scale scores compared to placebo (p=0.033) only in antibody responders. No significant effect was observed in non-responders.

memory: Levamisole with IM or ID HB vaccination increased antibody titers (p<0.01) and reduced 6-month decline. Groups C (IM+Levamisole) and D (ID+Levamisole) achieved 90% seroconversion, with IM+Levamisole showing greater titer increase than ID+Levamisole.
text: The IM 40 μg HB vaccine achieved higher seroconversion rates (90%) and greater titer increases compared to ID 20 μg HB vaccine, both with Levamisole (p<0.01).

memory: PA+HE+ significantly reduced cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.49, p<0.001) and overall mortality (HR 0.53, p<0.001) compared to control, with greater benefits than PA or HE alone.
text: "Physical activity + Healthy eating" significantly reduced cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.49, p<0.001) compared to control, showing greater benefits than either intervention alone.

memory: Web-based CME, feedback, and tools had no significant effect on medication intensification for glucose, BP, or LDL in rural diabetic patients (p=0.948). Both groups showed increased intensification for A1c >9%, but no difference in BP or LDL. Source: PMC3467590.
text: The intervention had no significant incremental benefit on medication intensification for glucose, BP, or LDL (p=0.948). Both groups showed similar improvements for A1c >9%, but no difference in BP or LDL. Source: PMC3467590.
intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

memory: Cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day, 8 weeks) reduced DM-induced nitro-oxidative stress, restored PKG activity (p-VASP/VASP ratio), and improved contractility (PRSW, Ees) and diastolic function (Tau) in diabetic rats vs. placebo. No effect in non-diabetic rats.
text: Cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic rats compared to placebo, restoring PKG activity and improving cardiac function. No effect was observed in non-diabetic rats. (Source: Working notes)
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

memory: Lemon verbena extract showed trends toward increased GPxP (p=0.0681) and reduced exercise-related muscle strength loss (p=0.0311) vs. placebo, with less movement-induced pain (p=0.0788). No significant changes in CK or IL-6; placebo had higher CK elevations. Source: [PMC5781260].
text: Lemon verbena extract showed a trend toward reduced exercise-related muscle strength loss (p=0.0311) compared to placebo, along with trends for increased GPxP and less movement-induced pain, though these were not statistically significant. Source: [PMC5781260].

memory: Arformoterol vs placebo showed greater FEV1/FVC improvements (P < .05), lower respiratory SAE risk (50% reduction, P = .003), and better quality of life. Similar AE rates, fewer COPD exacerbations, but more cardiac SAEs numerically. Common AEs: headache, nausea, UTI.
text: Arformoterol compared with placebo showed better quality of life improvements, as measured by the St. George's Hospital Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire. This conclusion is supported by the working notes, which indicate overall better quality of life outcomes with arformoterol.
outcome: improvements in quality of life (overall St. George's Hospital Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire)

memory: FOS (GF, GIF) improved Ca absorption and femur strength vs. control (GC), while isoflavone (GI) did not. GIF had higher equol and lower daidzein than GI. FOS reduced bone fragility post-GX, with no significant Ca absorption difference between GC and GI.
text: Fructooligosaccharides (GF, GIF) improved femur strength and Ca absorption compared to control (GC). GIF showed better equol levels and reduced bone fragility post-GX, while isoflavone (GI) alone had no significant effect on bone strength.
intervention: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF)

memory: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg) vs. saline showed similar PTEF increases (P=0.6). TEF10 and 25/PT decreased significantly (P<0.05) with albuterol. No significant changes in VPTEF/VE, tPTEF/tE, HR, RR, SpO2, or wheeze score. Source: PMC111183.
text: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg) did not significantly affect PTEF compared to saline but significantly decreased the 25/PT ratio (P<0.05). Source: PMC111183.
intervention: nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline)
outcome: ratio of the tidal expiratory flow at 25% of the remaining tidal volume to PTEF (25/PT)

memory: GENRES Study: Male patients with moderate hypertension (mean OBP 152/100 mmHg) and elevated BMI. Bisoprolol showed greatest BP reduction (11.1/8.3 mmHg). SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) in ACY3 gene linked to ASBP response.
text: Bisoprolol demonstrated greater systolic blood pressure reduction than losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide in hypertensive males. SNPs rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037 on chromosome 11 (ACY3 gene) were associated with ASBP response in the GENRES study.
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

memory: A study found metformin+alogliptin improved HbA1c ≤7.0% (18.18% vs. 10.81%) compared to metformin alone, with reductions in TC, LDL-C, and TG, and increases in HDL-C. No changes in BMI, WC, or BP. Pulmonary function was similar, but headaches were more common in the intervention group.
text: The combination of metformin (500 mg, bid po) and alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) significantly increased the proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤7.0% (18.18%) compared to metformin alone (10.81%). This effect was accompanied by favorable lipid profile changes, though no differences were noted in BMI, WC, BP, or pulmonary function. Headaches were more common with the combination therapy. (Source: Study)
intervention: metformin (500 mg, bid po) combined with alogliptin (25 mg, qd po)
outcome: proportion of patients with glycosylated hemoglobinA1c (HbA1c) ≤7.0%

memory: FAST treatment led to higher pulse rate (P=0.022), MAP, SBP, and DBP (P<0.046) compared to SLOW. No significant differences in DO2, biochemistry, or CI/SVRI. Pulse rate increased more during FAST resuscitation.
text: FAST treatment significantly increased pulse rate (P=0.022), MAP, SBP, and DBP (P<0.046) compared to SLOW treatment, with greater pulse rate elevation during FAST resuscitation. No significant differences were observed in DO2, biochemistry, or CI/SVRI.

memory: Desmopressin vs. placebo in surgery showed no significant difference in bleeding rate (P=0.208) or complications. Control had higher thrombocytopenia (P=0.012). Post-surgery, Hb levels decreased significantly (P=0.0001), with no inter-group difference. Platelet changes were significant (P=0.038). Source: PMC5101425.
text: Desmopressin did not significantly affect thrombocytopenia rate compared to placebo (P=0.038). Source: PMC5101425.

memory: Resistance exercise (SR + RT) increased fat-free leg mass (9332 ± 254 vs. 9206 ± 258) without changing femoral artery diameter, leg blood flow, or mean arterial pressure. No changes in intracellular free phenylalanine enrichments. Heart rate was higher in fed vs. fasted state (P < 0.0001). Source: PMC4562579.
text: Resistance exercise (SR + RT) did not significantly alter leg blood flow compared to control, as femoral artery diameter, leg blood flow, and mean arterial pressure remained unchanged. Source: PMC4562579.

memory: Trametinib showed longer PFS (4.8 mo) vs chemotherapy (1.5 mo, HR 0.45). Selumetinib improved PFS (5.3 vs 2.1 mo) but not OS in NSCLC.
text: Oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) showed a longer progression-free survival (4.8 months) compared to intravenous chemotherapy (1.5 months, HR 0.45), but data on overall survival at 6 months were not provided. Selumetinib improved PFS but not OS in NSCLC.
comparator: intravenous chemotherapy consisting of either dacarbazine (1000mg/m2) or paclitaxel (175mg/m2), every 3weeks
outcome: At 6 months, the rate of overall survival

memory: A study found that Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula significantly improved GSRS total score (p=0.048) and abdominal pain subscore (p=0.046) in adults with postprandial gas symptoms, with a trend for abdominal distension (p=0.061). Other endpoints were not significant, possibly due to a strong placebo effect.
text: The Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula significantly improved GSRS total score (p=0.048) and abdominal pain subscore (p=0.046) compared to placebo in adults with postprandial gas symptoms, with a trend for abdominal distension (p=0.061). Other endpoints were not significant, possibly due to a strong placebo effect.
intervention: Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) group

text: Bupropion and NRT have similar smoking cessation rates (27.9% vs. 24.2%) with behavioral support. Bupropion may be more effective for individuals with depression. However, it is associated with more side effects.
