text: The ZA10 group showed no significant difference in creatine kinase levels compared to A20 or A40 groups (P>0.05). Lipid reductions were similar to A40, with no increased myopathy or GI adverse events.
comparator: atorvastatin 20 mg (A20 group) or atorvastatin 40 mg (A40 group)

memory: Hesperidin (100 mg) + p-synephrine (50 mg) + naringin (600 mg) increased RMR by 183 kcal vs. placebo (p<0.02). 1000 mg hesperidin + same combo increased RMR by 79 kcal vs. placebo. No changes in heart rate, blood pressure, or self-reported symptoms.
text: The effect of p-synephrine (50 mg) alone on RMR is not directly stated, as the study evaluated a combination with hesperidin and naringin. Therefore, the specific effect of p-synephrine alone on RMR remains unclear.

memory: YM (2g) vs. PLC increased TEE AUC (p<0.001) and FAO (p=0.037) during exercise. YM reduced Hunger (p=0.019), Prospective eating (p=0.022), and desire to eat (p=0.079). No effects on HR, RPE, or fullness. Most VAS measures showed no time or interaction effects.
text: Administration of 2 g YM compared to placebo significantly reduced prospective eating (p=0.022). This suggests YM may help control eating behavior.

memory: Both underwater treadmill and control groups showed significant reductions in anteroposterior, mediolateral, and total postural sway (p<0.05) and improved dynamic balance (p<0.05) post-intervention. No significant differences were found between the groups in these outcomes.
text: Both the underwater treadmill and control groups showed significant reductions in anteroposterior, mediolateral, and total postural sway (p<0.05) compared to baseline, with no significant differences between groups.
outcome: anteroposterior, mediolateral and total postural sway

memory: Lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg showed better symptom control (P < 0.001) for hyperhidrosis and headache vs. microparticles 30 mg. GH levels were lower with Autogel® (3.8 vs 4.3 ng/ml; P < 0.001). IGF-1 normalization rates were 40% vs 35%. Symptom control was better with Autogel®.
text: Lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg showed better symptom control (P < 0.001) for hyperhidrosis and headache compared to lanreotide microparticles 30 mg. This conclusion is supported by the study data provided.

memory: Perindopril showed no significant improvement in FMD compared to placebo at 36 months (0.55%, p=0.23) or 6 months (0.12%, p=0.07). Nitroglycerine response was unchanged.
text: Perindopril did not significantly improve flow-mediated vasodilatation compared to placebo after 6 months (0.12%, p=0.07) or 36 months (0.55%, p=0.23). Nitroglycerine response remained unchanged.

memory: Oat cereal reduced total cholesterol (p=0.015), LDL-C (p=0.028), and waist circumference (p=0.002) compared to wheat noodles. HDL-C decreased in control vs. oat (p=0.017). No significant blood pressure changes. Oat group had increased dietary fiber.
text: Consuming 100 grams of instant oat cereal significantly reduced waist circumference (p=0.002) compared to 100 grams of wheat flour-based noodles. This effect was associated with increased dietary fiber intake and improvements in lipid profiles.

memory: 200 patients randomized to diazepam + chlorpheniramine vs. control. No differences in pain (P=0.75) or anxiety (P=0.2). Premedicated group had higher local pain (30% vs 16%, P=0.018) and more catheter spasms (4% vs 0%, P=0.04).
text: Diazepam + chlorpheniramine did not significantly affect local pain compared to control (P=0.75). However, premedicated patients had higher local pain (30% vs 16%, P=0.018). Source: Study of 200 patients.

memory: Study [PMC3751553] found Ramadan fasting delayed bedtime and wake-up times (p < 0.05) and reduced REM sleep (p < 0.05) compared to baseline. No significant changes in serum glucose, JDS scores, or blink durations were observed.
text: Ramadan fasting reduced REM sleep percentages compared to a non-fasting baseline (p < 0.05). Baseline fasting had no significant effect on REM sleep. Source: [PMC3751553].
intervention: 4 weeks before Ramadan while performing the Islamic fasting for 1 week (baseline fasting) (BLF) or during the second week of Ramadan while fasting (Ramadan)

memory: Aripiprazole low- and high-dose significantly improved YGTSS-TTS vs. placebo (p=0.002, p<0.0001). High-dose had higher response rates (57.1%) and greater discontinuation (10/10) than low-dose (40.5%). Randomization stratified by weight and region. Results remained significant after multiple testing adjustments.
text: High-dose aripiprazole was associated with a higher discontinuation rate (10/10) compared to placebo, though it showed greater response rates. The results were statistically significant (p<0.0001).

memory: No pre-weaning differences in Pimax, Pemax, FVC, or RSBI. Respiratory physiotherapy group had higher PSV and PEEP at extubation (p <0.001), shorter weaning duration (p <0.001), but similar mechanical ventilation duration and extubation failure rates (p =0.467, p =1.00).
text: Respiratory physiotherapy-driven weaning resulted in higher PSV and PEEP at extubation (p <0.001) and shorter weaning duration (p <0.001) compared to progressive discontinuation of PSV with SmartCare™, with no differences in extubation failure rates.
intervention: progressive discontinuation of pressure support ventilation (PSV) with SmartCare™
outcome: pressure support ventilation (PSV)  and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)

memory: Breast cancer patients in internet vs. control groups had similar trial result expectations (p>0.4). Internet group found it more suitable (43.5% vs 17.6%, p=0.006) but preferred face-to-face. They had higher result understanding (18.8% vs 5.6%, p=0.039). Oncologists were most preferred for information.
text: The internet group showed higher accurate understanding of trial results (18.8% vs. 5.6%, p=0.039) compared to the control group. However, both groups had similar expectations about trial results (p>0.4). The internet group found the method more suitable but preferred face-to-face communication.
intervention: Internet group (who received the letter of invitation)
comparator: control group (who did not receive it)
outcome: accurately understanding the results - Breast cancer patients participating in a trial on the efficacy of Trastuzumab

memory: Vegetable intake increased similarly across groups (P>.05). Plus intervention increased fruit intake more than control and basic (ES=0.25–0.37, P<.01). Basic and plus groups reduced high-energy snack intake more than control (ES=–0.30–0.27). Plus showed greater effects in high-educated participants.
text: The "Individual cognition and self-regulation processes intervention" led to greater reductions in high-energy snack intake compared to control (ES=–0.30–0.27). This effect was more pronounced in high-educated participants.
intervention: Individual cognition and self-regulation processes intervention

memory: CGM Sensor On reduced hypoglycemia time (19 vs 31 min/day, p=0.009), improved HbA1c (-0.43%, p<0.001), increased boluses (6.8 vs 5.8, p<0.0001), and more temporary basal use (0.75 vs 0.26, p<0.0001).
text: The CGM Sensor On arm was associated with an increased mean number of daily boluses (6.8 vs. 5.8, p<0.0001) compared to the CGM Sensor Off arm.
comparator: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) Sensor Off arm
outcome: The mean number of daily boluses

memory: Study [PMC4636858]: 28M/43F. Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone vs no treatment showed no significant differences in MRI plaques (P=0.782) or EDSS (P=0.953) at treatment end or 6 months post.
text: A study found no significant difference in MRI plaques (P=0.782) or EDSS (P=0.953) between Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone and no treatment in MS patients. Thus, the combination does not significantly affect MS plaques compared to no treatment (PMC4636858).

memory: Artesunate (2/4 mg/kg/day) showed similar PCT to quinine+doxycycline (P<0.001), faster FCT (P=0.001), 97.8-100% cure rates, and comparable adverse events.
text: Artesunate monotherapy (2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily) resulted in a faster median FCT compared to quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days (P=0.001), with similar PCT and high cure rates.
intervention: artesunate monotherapy with 2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily
comparator: quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days

memory: Metformin and sitagliptin reduced hyperglycemia relapse risk (HR 0.28–0.31 vs. placebo, P < 0.05), with higher relapse-free survival (P = 0.015). No drug difference (P = 0.75). Remission correlated with higher DI and AUCi (P < 0.001).
text: Metformin 1,000 mg daily and sitagliptin 100 mg daily significantly improved hyperglycemia relapse-free survival compared to placebo (HR 0.28–0.31, P < 0.05). No difference was observed between the two drugs (P = 0.75).
intervention: metformin 1,000 mg daily, sitagliptin 100 mg daily

memory: Isomaltulose vs. sucrose showed no significant differences in HbA1c (P=0.844), fasting glucose, or fructosamine. Isomaltulose significantly reduced triglycerides (b=34.01, P=0.016). Source: PMC3357231.
text: Isomaltulose significantly reduced triglycerides compared to sucrose (b=34.01, P=0.016), while showing no significant differences in HbA1c, fasting glucose, or fructosamine. Source: PMC3357231.

memory: Study in 42 OA dogs: CCOT diet (curcuminoids, collagen, green tea) vs control showed no significant change in PI (p=0.063), but improved ability to rise (p=0.029) and significant PS improvement (p=0.009). PVF and weight unchanged. No major side effects.
text: The experimental diet with CCOT did not significantly affect pain interference (p=0.063) in OA dogs. However, it improved ability to rise (p=0.029) and pain severity (p=0.009), with no major side effects.
intervention: an experimental diet supplemented with Curcuminoids extract, hydrolyzed COllagen and green Tea extract (CCOT)

memory: LG2055 in FM increased fecal fat post- vs. pre-intake (p<0.05), unlike control FM. No significant fecal wet weight differences. LG2055 showed greater effects on fat emulsion and lipase activity than other strains. (Source: PMC4391304)
text: Consuming 100 g of fermented milk with Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 significantly increased fecal fat levels compared to 100 g of fermented milk alone (p<0.05). This effect was not observed in the control group. (Source: PMC4391304)
intervention: 100&amp;nbsp;g of fermented milk (FM) + Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055)

memory: Saline enema had no significant effect on episiorraphy dehiscence (12% vs 17%, P=0.30) or infection rates (RR 0.66-1.12, P>0.05). Labour time was similar (515 vs 585 min, P=0.24). Follow-up rate was 86%. Source: PMC1468428.
text: A 1 litre saline enema did not significantly affect puerperal and neonatal infection rates compared to no enema (RR 0.66-1.12, P>0.05). Source: PMC1468428.

memory: 10-week yoga improved flexibility (p<0.001), increased HRV LF:HF (p=0.04), and reduced pNN50 (p=0.04). High adherence (≥70%) reduced state anxiety (p=0.02) and slightly improved push-up test (p=0.07). No QoL changes (p>0.05).
text: A 10-week yoga program significantly improved flexibility compared to control (p<0.001). Other outcomes showed mixed results, but flexibility was the most notable improvement. Source: Working notes.

memory: Istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg reduced daily OFF time by −0.99 and −0.96 hours vs. placebo (−0.23 h; P < .003), with no dose difference. Common adverse event: dyskinesia (13%, 12.1%). No increase in ON time with dyskinesia. Source: PMC3842830.
text: Both Istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg reduced daily OFF time by −0.99 and −0.96 hours, respectively, compared to placebo (P < .003), with no dose difference. Neither dose increased daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia. Source: PMC3842830.
outcome: Daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia

memory: Liarozole (150/75 mg) vs. placebo showed no significant AE differences (P ≥ 0.062). 150 mg improved daily activities, leisure, and symptoms/feelings (P ≤ 0.026). 75 mg significantly improved DLQI (P = 0.014), while 150 mg did not (P = 0.06).
text: Oral liarozole 150 mg significantly improved daily activities, leisure, and symptoms/feelings compared to placebo (P ≤ 0.026). However, it did not significantly improve DLQI (P = 0.06).

memory: ATP study compared 15-pulse vs. 8-pulse, finding no significant differences in shocks (p=0.907), FVT termination (p=0.504), acceleration (p=0.993), or syncope/near-syncope (p=0.690). 71% ATP efficacy (unadjusted).
text: A study comparing 15-pulse vs. 8-pulse ATP found no significant difference in syncope/near-syncope episodes (p=0.690). Both had 71% ATP efficacy. No conclusion on effectiveness for preventing syncope.

memory: Prednisolone 7.5 mg and 30 mg reduced insulin suppression of lipolysis (11% and 34%) and glucose production (17% and 46%) vs placebo. 30 mg decreased peripheral glucose uptake by 34% (p < 0.0001) and increased proteolysis (5%, p = 0.06). No side effects reported.
text: Prednisolone 30 mg and 7.5 mg once daily reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis by 34% and 11%, respectively, compared to placebo. These findings suggest glucocorticoid doses impair insulin's ability to suppress lipolysis. (Source: Working notes)
intervention: prednisolone 30 mg once daily and  prednisolone 7,5 mg once daily

memory: Online vs. mailed questionnaires showed non-significant trends in shortness of breath (p=0.074), asthma (p=0.096), ER visits (p=0.146), and health distress (p=0.116). Internet users were more likely to be married (p=0.043). ANCOVAs adjusted for asthma and demographics. ER visits were skewed.
text: The effect of online vs. mailed questionnaires on married subjects showed non-significant trends in health outcomes. Internet users were more likely to be married (p=0.043). Adjusted analyses found no significant differences in reported symptoms or health distress between married individuals in the two groups.

memory: A study found similar psychosocial stress recovery between Facebook use and quiet reading, with no significant differences in tension, anxiety, or well-being. Controls showed greater cortisol decrease post-stressor (F(1,84)=5.03, p=0.03). High-engagement female Facebook users had minimal cortisol reduction.
text: Using their own Facebook profile had a similar effect on subjective stress markers as quietly reading, with no significant differences in tension, anxiety, or well-being. However, controls showed greater cortisol decrease post-stressor (F(1,84)=5.03, p=0.03), while high-engagement female Facebook users had minimal cortisol reduction.

memory: No differences in laryngeal view, intubation success, or axes alignment between 8 cm and 4 cm pillow groups. Higher discomfort scores in the 8 cm group during head elevation. One 8 cm patient needed a 4 cm pillow after two failed intubation attempts.
text: Using an 8 cm pillow during tracheal intubation was associated with higher discomfort scores compared to a 4 cm pillow, with no differences in laryngeal view, success rate, or alignment. One 8 cm patient required a 4 cm pillow after failed attempts. Source: Working notes.

memory: Prednisone (60 mg/day) vs. placebo showed no OGTT changes in glucose/insulin. Prednisone increased uNTX/uCr by Day 2, with dose-dependent rises through Day 8. Plasma osteocalcin and P1NP decreased dose- and time-dependently from Day 1. Neutrophils increased; lymphocytes rebounded. Source: PMC4947329.
text: Daily prednisone increased uNTX/uCr and decreased P1NP compared to placebo, indicating increased bone resorption and reduced bone formation. Source: PMC4947329.

memory: A study compared gutta-percha with AH26, MTA, and a new endodontic cement, finding no significant differences in apical dye penetration. The SGP/NEC group showed significantly less coronal dye penetration (P<0.001) than others. Source: PMC3712263.
text: The use of "Gutta-percha + new endodontic cement" significantly reduces coronal dye penetration compared to "Gutta-percha + AH26" (P<0.001). Source: PMC3712263.

memory: Intermediate multifocals showed significant differences vs. full bifocals in vertical toe clearance variability (χ²=12.0, p=0.0005), ascent duration (χ²=12.7, p<0.0001), and heel clearance on descent (χ²=8.7, p=0.003). No significant differences were found between intermediate PALs and distance single vision lenses in gait safety parameters.
text: Intermediate progressive addition lenses had no significant effect on ascent vertical toe clearance compared to distance single vision lenses (p>0.05). Full bifocals showed significant differences in related gait parameters.

memory: Behavioral lifestyle intervention reduced BMI-SDS (P=0.02), WC-SDS (P=0.03), improved VO2peak-SDS (P<0.01) and HOMA-SDS (P=0.04) at 1 year; no lipid changes. BMI-SDS remained lower at 2 years (P=0.02). Control group showed no improvement.
text: Behavioral lifestyle intervention significantly reduced waist circumference compared to control (P=0.03) at 1 year, with sustained BMI reduction at 2 years (P=0.02). Control group showed no improvement. Source: Working notes.

memory: Participants had higher energy intakes (8672 kJ) than the national average, with 34.6% from discretionary foods. Macronutrient profiles matched national averages, with stable intake across groups. Saturated fat intake remained unchanged via FFQ but may have decreased via meat choices. Baseline energy intake did not differ between completers and non-completers.
text: Participants had higher energy intakes (8672 kJ) than the national average, with 34.6% from discretionary foods. Macronutrient profiles matched national averages, with stable intake across groups. Saturated fat intake remained unchanged via FFQ but may have decreased via meat choices. Baseline energy intake did not differ between completers and non-completers.

memory: ES10/20 and R10 reduced PLAC and Lp-PLA2 more than doubling statin doses. ES10/20 showed greater LDL-P reduction and HDL-P increase. Both increased apoA-I more than doubling. Source: PMC4845107.
text: The combination of ezetimibe/simvastatin 10/20mg (ES10/20) resulted in a greater reduction in LDL-particle number compared to rosuvastatin 10mg (R10), as shown in a study (PMC4845107).

memory: A weight management intervention increased fiber intake (5.7 g/day, p < .001) and predicted 4-month weight loss (−1.98 kg, p < .01). Fiber intake remained significant at 12 months (p < .005), and weight loss (M Diff 2.9 kg) became significant after adjusting for co-interventions (p = 0.014).
text: The weight management intervention targeting diet and physical activity plus usual care significantly increased fiber intake at 12 months compared to usual care (p < .005). This effect was sustained beyond the initial 4-month weight loss (−1.98 kg, p < .01), with adjusted weight loss of 2.9 kg at 12 months (p = 0.014).
intervention: weight management intervention targeting diet and physical activity plus usual care

memory: A study compared tamsulosin 0.4 mg/d vs. 0.2 mg/d in LUTS-improved patients. IIEF-5 scores improved significantly (p=0.002) in the 0.4 mg group (4.6) vs. 0.2 mg (1.7). No significant IPSS score differences at week 4 (p>0.05). [PMC3580298]
text: In patients with no improvement in LUTS, increasing tamsulosin to 0.4 mg/d significantly improved IIEF-5 scores compared to maintaining 0.2 mg/d (p=0.002). [PMC3580298]
comparator: increase their dose to 0.4 mg once daily (escalators)
outcome: International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5)  in patients who showed no improvement of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)

memory: Gepotidacin 1,800 mg had a higher AE rate (64%) vs 1,000 mg (46%), with vomiting (15%), nausea (8%), and throat tightness (2%). QTc prolongation (mean ΔΔQTcF 22.2 ms; slope 1.45 ms/μg/ml) was observed. 9% discontinued due to AEs.
text: The 1,800 mg dose of gepotidacin in healthy volunteers resulted in a higher rate of moderate adverse events (64%) compared to 1,000 mg (46%), with vomiting, nausea, and throat tightness reported. QTc prolongation was also observed. Nine percent discontinued due to AEs. (Source: Working notes)

memory: Etomidate compared to propofol shows lower vasopressor support (VSF) requirement and hypotension incidence, but higher myoclonus occurrence.
text: Etomidate compared with propofol based on midazolam is associated with a higher incidence rate of myoclonus. This finding highlights a trade-off between reduced hypotension risk with etomidate and increased myoclonus occurrence.

memory: Almonds (85g/day) increased plasma α-tocopherol by 10.2% (P=0.0065) and decreased γ-tocopherol by 16.5% (P=0.047). No significant changes in lipid profile, inflammatory cytokines (CRP, TNFα, IL-6), or endothelial markers (E-selectin, VCAM-1, NO).
text: Consuming 85 g/day of almonds increased plasma α-tocopherol by 10.2% (P=0.0065) compared to a control diet, with no significant changes in other measured parameters.

memory: A computerised diabetes register (intervention) vs standard care (control) showed no significant differences in HbA1c, BP, or patient-reported outcomes. Intervention patients had lower cholesterol (-0.15 mmol/l, 95% CI -0.25, -0.06). Increased recording of appointments, foot checks, dietary advice, and BP. No cost differences per patient. Initial setup cost: £27,885.
text: The intervention showed increased recording of diabetes appointments, foot checks, dietary advice, and blood pressure compared to standard care, though no significant differences in HbA1c or BP. Cholesterol was lower in the intervention group. (Source: Study)
intervention: area-wide, computerised diabetes register incorporating a full structured recall and individualised patient management system
comparator: standard structured and recall management system
outcome: Frequency of at least one diabetes appointment, a foot check, receiving dietary advice, recording of blood pressure

memory: FAT group showed increased alpha power during pre-recognition in FAR task post-training (F(1,18)=5.61, p=.03) compared to baseline. No emotion-related effects. Source: PMC4215531.
text: Facial affect training (FAT) in 20 daily 1-hour sessions increased alpha power during pre-recognition in the FAR task post-training compared to baseline (F(1,18)=5.61, p=.03). No emotion-related effects were observed. Source: PMC4215531.
intervention: facial affect training (FAT) in 20 daily 1-hour sessions

memory: Singing training (music therapy) vs. control reduced Japanese Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices time (p=0.026), decreased Neuropsychiatric Inventory score (p=0.042), and increased sleep duration (p=0.039). fMRI showed increased activity in the right angular gyrus and left lingual gyrus (before-minus-after). Source: PMC4608626.
text: Singing training reduced Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores compared to control (p=0.042). Source: PMC4608626.

memory: A study compared RCF, RF, and RC. Hemodynamic parameters showed no significant differences (P>0.05). RCF significantly reduced side effects (P<0.05), improving patient comfort. Demographics and block characteristics were similar across groups.
text: The effect of Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine (RCF) compared to Ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) on hemodynamic parameters showed no significant differences (P>0.05). RCF significantly reduced side effects, improving patient comfort.

memory: Study PMC5684963 found that a low GI diet significantly reduced glycemic response after lunch (p=0.02) and daily AUC (p=0.03). It also lowered IAUC following a low GI breakfast (p=0.03).
text: A low glycemic index intervention significantly reduces glycemic response after lunch compared to a high glycemic index intervention (p=0.02). This finding is supported by Study PMC5684963.

memory: Study PMC4141382 found that patients receiving caudal sufentanil plus neostigmine required fewer dipyrone doses (P < 0.005) compared to those with sufentanil alone (P > 0.05). Facial pain VAS and postoperative nausea/vomiting were similar between groups.
text: Caudal sufentanil plus neostigmine reduces dipyrone needs compared to sufentanil alone (PMC4141382). Facial pain and postoperative nausea/vomiting were similar between groups.

memory: T group (transillumination) vs R group (midline approach) showed similar intubation success rates and times (P > 0.05), but T had longer second attempt time (P = 0.0006). T group had higher dry throat, sore throat, and hoarseness incidence (all P < 0.05). Source: PMC5320759.
text: The transillumination-assisted technique group (T group) showed similar intubation success rates at first, second, and third attempts compared to the midline approach group (R group) (P > 0.05). However, the T group had a longer second attempt time (P = 0.0006) and higher incidence of dry throat, sore throat, and hoarseness (all P < 0.05). Source: PMC5320759.
outcome: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempt

memory: In a study comparing PLMA and ETT, cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation were significantly lower in the PLMA group (p=0.024). Within groups, cortisol increased after CO2 insufflation compared to anesthesia induction (p=0.001). No significant differences were found in adrenaline, noradrenaline, or dopamine levels between or within groups (Table 4 and 5).
text: The laryngeal mask (PLMA) significantly reduces cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation compared to endotracheal intubation (ETT) (p=0.024). Both groups showed increased cortisol compared to baseline (p=0.001). No significant changes were observed in adrenaline, noradrenaline, or dopamine levels.
outcome: cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation

memory: Source [PMC4776564] found similar baseline demographics and QOL scores between groups. Post-intervention, significant QOL differences (P < 0.05) were observed in four dimensions and satisfaction/importance areas. Repeated measures ANOVA indicated time-related changes in the control group.
text: Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs did not significantly affect baseline characteristics compared to no interventions, as both groups had similar demographics and QOL scores at baseline (PMC4776564).
intervention: Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs

memory: Butoconazole 2% vaginal cream (Gynazole-1) showed faster symptom relief than oral fluconazole 150 mg (Diflucan). Median time to first relief: 17.5 h vs. 22.9 h (p < 0.001). Time to 75% relief: 24.5 h vs. 46.3 h (p < 0.001).
text: Butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream (Gynazole-1) provided faster relief of symptoms compared to oral fluconazole 150 mg (Diflucan). The median time to first relief was 17.5 hours vs. 22.9 hours (p < 0.001).
intervention: butoconazole nitrate 2% Site Release vaginal cream (Gynazole-1)
outcome: The median time to first relief of symptoms

memory: Vit D (50,000 IU/week) vs. placebo showed no significant differences in FBS, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP (P>0.05). Proteinuria levels differed significantly post-study (P=0.028). Source: PMC5106877.
text: Vitamin D (50,000 IU/week) did not significantly affect fasting blood sugar, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP compared to placebo (P>0.05). Source: PMC5106877.
outcome: fasting blood sugar (FBS), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1C), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels

memory: A study compared LPA to FME in fibromyalgia patients, finding LPA significantly reduced FIQ scores (P = .032) and pain (P = .006) post-intervention, with no baseline differences. The six-minute walk test approached significance (P = .067). No changes in BMI, fatigue, depression, or tender points were observed. Source: [PMC2888205].
text: LPA significantly reduced pain (P = .006) compared to FME in fibromyalgia patients, with no baseline differences. Source: [PMC2888205].
intervention: lifestyle physical activity (LPA) - 30 minutes of self-selected moderate-intensity LPA, five to seven days per week
comparator: fibromyalgia (FM) education control (FME) group - received information and support

memory: Green tea increased post-exercise (p < 0.01) and resting (p < 0.05) fat oxidation vs. placebo. Plasma glycerol rose post-green tea, more in untrained (p < 0.05). Epinephrine higher in green tea (p < 0.05); norepinephrine only in untrained. [PMC4899895]
text: Green tea significantly increases post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo (p < 0.01) [PMC4899895].

memory: Experiment 1 associated red/blue cursors with opposing curl fields. MPE decreased during exposure (F1,5=58.220; P=0.001), but force compensation did not increase (F1,5=0.223; P=0.657). No postexposure trajectory deviation, suggesting no learned compensation. Source: [PMC3653044].
text: The initial trial showed a decrease in MPE over the exposure period for red and blue cursors, but no significant difference was found between initial and final trials. No learned force compensation occurred. Source: [PMC3653044].
outcome: over the course of the exposure period maximum perpendicular error (MPE) decrease - cursor color (red or blue)

memory: BZA/CE (20 mg/0.45 or 0.625 mg) showed no significant increase in breast tenderness compared to placebo, raloxifene, or BZA alone in SMART-1, SMART-2, and SMART-5. In SMART-5, BZA/CE had significantly lower breast tenderness than CE/MPA. BZA/CE did not affect age-related breast density changes.
text: BZA/CE did not significantly increase breast tenderness compared to placebo in SMART-1, SMART-2, and SMART-5 trials. It also showed lower breast tenderness than CE/MPA in SMART-5.
intervention: BZA/CE combines bazedoxifene (BZA), a selective estrogen receptor modulator, with conjugated estrogens (CE),

memory: Intervention reduced Processed (−0.14; P <0.0001) and Snacks (−0.24; P <0.0001) scores at 28 weeks, maintained at 36 weeks. No change in Fruit/vegetables or African/Caribbean scores. Source: PMC5126873.
text: The intervention of "Diet and physical activity" did not significantly affect "African/Caribbean food intake," as no changes were observed in related scores (PMC5126873).

memory: Resveratrol vs. placebo: Ibuprofen use (mg, mean ± SD [n]) - 1200 (848) [5] vs. 5640 (328) [5]; p=0.09. Source: PMC5686687.

memory: Sevoflurane + ondansetron reduced vomiting (17.5%, 7.5%, 10%) vs. sevoflurane alone (55%, 27.5%, 30%) (P < 0.05). Nausea also lower: 55% (group I) vs. 42.5–30% (others). Source: PMC3633335.
text: Sevoflurane + ondansetron significantly reduces vomiting (17.5%, 7.5%, 10%) compared to sevoflurane alone (55%, 27.5%, 30%) (P < 0.05). Nausea rates were also lower in the combination group. Source: PMC3633335.

memory: BLTR showed greater under-correction at 12 months vs. PLTR (Table 3). No difference in surgery pain (p=0.84), but BLTR had higher post-op pain/discomfort (OR 1.46, p=0.004). Satisfaction for trichiasis and cosmetic outcomes was similar (p=0.20, 0.64). Source: [PMC5075282].
text: No significant difference in surgery pain (p=0.84) between Posterior lamellar tarsal rotation (PLTR) and Bilamellar tarsal rotation (BLTR) surgery. However, BLTR was associated with higher post-op pain/discomfort (OR 1.46, p=0.004). Source: [PMC5075282].
outcome: Pain between surgery and stitches removal

memory: Dovitinib vs placebo showed higher AE-related discontinuation (38.3% vs 8.0%), with diarrhea (6.4%), ALT (4.3%), AST (4.3%), and rash (4.3%) as common reasons. Four on-treatment deaths occurred: 2 in each arm. Dovitinib-related deaths: 1 breast cancer progression, 1 pulmonary embolism. Source: PMC5301372.
text: Dovitinib significantly increased discontinuation due to rash compared to placebo (4.3% vs 8.0%). Source: PMC5301372.

memory: No serious adverse events; no significant group differences. Three excluded due to hyperparathyroidism/high calcium. Four had transient calcium >2.59 mmol/L but remained in the study. Source: [PMC2818614].
text: The study found no significant group differences in the rate of adverse events between the DD, DP, and PP groups. No serious adverse events were reported. Source: [PMC2818614].
intervention: Vitamin D3 40.000 IU (DD group) or Vitamin D3 20.000 IU (DP group)

memory: LIPUS showed no immediate FD differences (1.338 vs 1.319). After six months, FD-mesial improved more in intervention (0.342) vs control (0.132), with Cohen's d = 4.85 vs 2.64. FD-distal also showed greater improvement in intervention (Table 5, Figure 5).
text: The intervention group with added LIPUS showed greater improvement in FD mesial values after six months (0.342) compared to the standard protocol (0.132), with a larger effect size (Cohen's d = 4.85 vs 2.64).
intervention: intervention group with added low-intensity power ultrasound treatment (LIPUS)
outcome: FD mesial values after six months of follow-up

memory: Curry meal improved FMD (5.2% to 6.6%, P=0.001) vs. control (5.8% to 5.1%, P=0.039; P=0.002 vs. curry) [PMC4082484]. Spices had no effect on hemodynamics or oxidative stress markers.
text: A single serving of curry meal improved flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal (P=0.002) [PMC4082484]. Spices did not affect hemodynamics or oxidative stress markers.

memory: Infliximab vs. ciclosporin: 3 deaths in infliximab group (2 from pneumonia/sepsis, 1 from cancer). Infliximab increased 30-month health service costs by £5632 (p=0.001), with no significant difference in QALYs (p=0.350).
text: Infliximab increases 30-month health service costs by £5632 compared to ciclosporin (p=0.001), with no significant difference in QALYs (p=0.350).

memory: NBUVB (9 J/cm², 6 weeks) and prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg, 6 weeks) showed no significant difference in pre-treatment disease duration (p = 0.910) for generalized lichen planus. NBUVB had significantly better efficacy (p = 0.008). No sex effect on disease duration (p > 0.73). Source: PMC3434899.
text: NBUVB (9 J/cm² for 6 weeks) and prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) showed no significant difference in disease duration for generalized lichen planus (p = 0.910). Source: PMC3434899.

memory: Source [PMC5827302]: Exercise group had significantly lower BAI scores (5.6±3.9) vs control (0.1±2.3), p=0.02, very large effect size (1.40). See Table 2, Fig. 4.
text: Exercise significantly reduces Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scores compared to control (5.6±3.9 vs. 0.1±2.3, p=0.02, effect size 1.40) [PMC5827302].

memory: Smokers taking 200 mg/day palmvitee had lower NK cell percentages at baseline and after supplementation compared to nonsmokers (p < 0.0001). Subgroup analyses (S1, S2, S3) showed significant differences (p < 0.05 to p < 0.01). (Source: Table 8, 9)
text: Smokers taking 200 mg/day palmvitee had significantly lower NK cell percentages at baseline and after supplementation compared to nonsmokers (p < 0.0001). Subgroup analyses confirmed these differences (p < 0.05 to p < 0.01). (Source: Table 8, 9)

memory: Lifestyle-induced weight loss reduced total GLP-1 (p=0.003) but not FGF-19; controls remained stable. GLP-1 changes correlated with insulin, BAs, and MetS parameters. Source: [PMC4958948].
text: The "Active Body Control" lifestyle intervention reduced total GLP-1 compared to baseline (p=0.003), while controls remained stable. This effect correlated with changes in insulin, bile acids, and metabolic syndrome parameters. Source: [PMC4958948].

memory: GSLiM led to 19.6% weight loss vs. 4.1% (RR 4.75, 95% CI 1.68-13.45) with higher retention (83.5% vs. 82.5%). Improved physical discomfort, self-efficacy, and QoL. Comparison group showed reduced negative self-thoughts. [PMC4990415]
text: GSLiM significantly improved physical discomfort compared to dietary counseling, with greater weight loss (19.6% vs. 4.1%, RR 4.75) and higher retention. [PMC4990415]

memory: Source [PMC4860224]: Participants (mean age 26.5) were mostly single (61%), Hispanic (68%), with incomplete high school education (44%); 35% were first-time mothers. No baseline group differences. 44% (n=74) and 40% (n=61) of intervention and control groups were lost to 1-month follow-up.
text: The intensified anticipatory guidance program did not show baseline characteristic differences compared to the routine program (PMC4860224). Both groups had similar demographics, including age, ethnicity, education, and parity.

memory: A study compared Gallium maltolate (GaM) to clarithromycin + rifampin (CLR) in foals with lesions (median size 27 mm). Smaller lesions showed similar resolution rates between groups. Larger lesions had lower GaM resolution rates, though not statistically significant. Logistic regression modeled resolution based on treatment, lesion size, and their interaction.
text: Gallium maltolate (GaM) showed similar lesion resolution rates compared to clarithromycin + rifampin (CLR) for smaller lesions, but lower rates for larger lesions (>27 mm), though not statistically significant. The study suggests treatment effectiveness may depend on lesion size. Source: Study on foals with median lesion size 27 mm.

memory: Group A (mini-open anterior approach) had shorter anal exsufflation time (1.21±0.48 days) vs. Group B (2.12±0.82 days; p<0.05). Operation time, blood loss, and hospitalization time slightly favored Group A but were not statistically significant. Both groups showed significant post-surgery decreases in Cobb angle and ESR (p<0.01).
text: The mini-open anterior approach (Group A) significantly reduced anal exsufflation time compared to the conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach (Group B) (1.21±0.48 vs. 2.12±0.82 days; p<0.05). Other outcomes showed no significant differences.
intervention: The mini-open anterior approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group A
comparator: conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group B

memory: 100 breast cancer patients randomized to fibrin glue or control during lumpectomy and axillary dissection. Subgroup analysis in level II/III dissection showed shorter drainage duration (3.5 vs. 4.7 days; p=0.0006) and lower drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255) with fibrin glue.
text: Fibrin glue applied to the axillary dissection site during lumpectomy significantly reduced overall drain output compared to the control group (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255). This effect was observed in patients undergoing level II/III dissection.
intervention: fibrin glue group (glue sprayed onto the axillary dissection site)

memory: A study compared plasma exchange (PE) and IVIG, finding a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and mechanical ventilation duration in the PE group (p=0.037), not in IVIG (p=0.132). Hospital stay was shorter in the PE group, though not statistically significant. Source: [PMC3387601].
text: Plasma exchange (PE) showed a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation (p=0.037), unlike IVIG (p=0.132). Source: [PMC3387601].
outcome: negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation

memory: A positive psychology intervention enhanced children's well-being and positive learning behaviors, as reported by parents and teachers, compared to a wait-list control (PMC5662620).
text: A positive psychology-based intervention improved subjective well-being in children compared to a wait-list control, as reported by parents and teachers (PMC5662620).

memory: Source [PMC4879328]: GHSH intervention led to significant reductions in weight (-1.35 kg, P=.003), increased weekly moderate activity (0.56 sessions/week, P=.008), and higher MVPA (24.16 min/week, P=.007) after 6 months vs. no contact. No significant changes in waist circumference, other activity, or diet.
text: The "Get Healthy, Stay Healthy" (GHSH) intervention significantly increased accelerometer-assessed MVPA by 24.16 minutes/week (P=.007) compared to no continued contact after 6 months, according to [PMC4879328].
outcome: accelerometer-assessed moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA)

memory: In-sequence tutorials improved ORS knowledge gain by 19% (95% CI +7%, +31%, Cohen's-d 0.85) vs. out-of-sequence. FWS showed a 6% increase (95% CI -3%, +16%, Cohen's-d 0.38), not significant. Results consistent across topics. Source: PMC3517358.
text: In-sequence computer tutorials improved ORS knowledge gain by 19% (95% CI +7%, +31%, Cohen's-d 0.85) compared to out-of-sequence tutorials. This effect was consistent across topics, while FWS showed a non-significant 6% increase. Source: PMC3517358.

memory: Cinacalcet reduced iPTH by 42.3% vs. 30.7% in control (P=0.483). Similar proportions achieved iPTH target (24.3% vs. 18.2%, P=0.764) and 30% reduction (48.5% vs. 51.5%, P=1.000) [PMC3669111].
text: Cinacalcet reduced iPTH by 42.3% compared to 30.7% in control (P=0.483). Similar proportions achieved the iPTH target (150–300) (24.3% vs. 18.2%, P=0.764) [PMC3669111].

memory: A study with 24 subjects using Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 found no clinically relevant abnormalities, serious adverse events, or discontinuations. Gastrointestinal events occurred once each for both products, with no differences in incidence or type (Source: PMC5839221).
text: Both Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 showed similar safety profiles, with no clinically relevant abnormalities, serious adverse events, or discontinuations (Source: PMC5839221). Gastrointestinal events were rare and comparable between the two products.

memory: In a sub-study of 85 patients, 77 had sildenafil concentrations measured. CYP3A4 IM (*22 carriers) showed higher sildenafil ratios than EM at weeks 12 and 24 (P=0.045). Age and BMI significantly influenced sildenafil ratios (P<0.0001).
text: CYP3A4 Intermediate metabolizers (*22 carriers) had higher sildenafil levels compared to Extensive metabolizers at weeks 12 and 24 (P=0.045). Age and BMI also significantly influenced sildenafil ratios (P<0.0001).

memory: Study [PMC4871571] found that two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations failed to induce ADCC-mediating antibodies in unprimed volunteers. One showed neutralizing activity against CM235 CRF01_AE. The Mann-Whitney test was used for statistical comparison.
text: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations failed to induce ADCC-mediating antibody responses in unprimed volunteers compared to baseline (PMC4871571). One volunteer showed neutralizing activity against CM235 CRF01_AE, but this was not linked to ADCC. The Mann-Whitney test was used for statistical analysis.

memory: In a study comparing biosimilar and reference adalimumab, total bilirubin levels were similar at screening (0.3 ± 0.18 vs. 0.3 ± 0.11 mg/dL) and Day 84 (0.3 ± 0.15 vs. 0.3 ± 0.20 mg/dL). Source: PMC5215647.
text: A study found that total bilirubin levels were similar between biosimilar adalimumab and reference adalimumab at screening and Day 84 (PMC5215647). Thus, biosimilar adalimumab has a similar effect on bilirubin as reference adalimumab.

memory: A 12-week trial found no significant cognitive improvement with MSDC-0160 on ADAS-Cog, global cognition, or executive function z-scores. However, it significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin (p<0.001), suggesting improved insulin sensitivity. Trends in hs-CRP and FFA indicated possible benefits, though not statistically significant. Source: [PMC4153084].
text: MSDC-0160 did not significantly improve cognitive test battery global cognitive scores compared to control in a 12-week trial (PMC4153084). However, it increased high molecular weight adiponectin, suggesting improved insulin sensitivity.
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: JQJT tablets reduced pre-diabetes progression to diabetes by 0.58-fold (HR 0.58, P=0.010) compared to placebo in 400 patients over 12 months (ITT: 16.5% vs. 28.9%).
text: JinqiJiangtang tablets reduced the risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes by 0.58-fold (HR 0.58, P=0.010) compared to placebo in 400 patients over 12 months (ITT: 16.5% vs. 28.9%).
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
outcome: risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes

memory: Group A (non-selective clopidogrel) had 3.5% bleeding vs. Group B (selective) 1.4% (P=0.025). Adjusted OR=3.03 (95% CI 1.14–8.10; P=0.027). Female gender and GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors were also significant risk factors.
text: Group A (non-selective clopidogrel) had a higher bleeding risk (3.5%) compared to Group B (selective, 1.4%) (P=0.025). Adjusted OR=3.03 (95% CI 1.14–8.10; P=0.027), indicating non-selective use increases bleeding complications. Female gender and GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors also increased risk.
intervention: group A ('non-selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG;
comparator: group B ('selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg in the cath-lab after CAG, only in case of PCI;

memory: Source [PMC4812817]: DKT significantly reduced GSRS indigestion/constipation scores (ANOVA P < 0.001) and VAS bloating (76→30, P=0.005). Abdominal pain and bloating face scales improved (P=0.039, 0.008). No changes in bowel frequency or stool form. 40% SIBO positive.
text: Daikenchuto significantly reduced indigestion and constipation scores compared to control (ANOVA P < 0.001) and improved bloating and abdominal pain (P=0.005, 0.039). Source: [PMC4812817].

memory: In a study comparing α-MSH to controls, urine output was significantly lower in the α-MSH group during a 10-hour follow-up (p<0.05), with no animals anuric. α-MSH also tended to impair GFR recovery compared to controls (Figure 3A). Source: PMC3984270.
text: α-MSH significantly reduced urine output compared to controls over 10 hours (p<0.05), with no animals anuric, and tended to impair GFR recovery. Source: PMC3984270.

memory: TCC vs usual care showed higher CPAP use (78% ±22% vs 60% ±32% nights, P=.07) with no significant efficacy, mask leak, or AHI differences. TCC patients had higher CPAP continuation likelihood (P<.05). Similar satisfaction and low concern about data monitoring in both groups. Source: PMC1874716.
text: Telemonitored clinical care (TCC) was associated with a higher likelihood of CPAP continuation compared to usual care (P<.05), though CPAP use differences were not statistically significant (P=.07). Source: PMC1874716.
outcome: Patients rated their likelihood to continue using CPAP

memory: Both usual care and manual therapy significantly improved outcomes such as headache frequency, pain intensity, and absenteeism, with no group differences. Low recruitment limited study power. Source: PMC2758835.
text: Both usual care and manual therapy significantly improved headache frequency, pain intensity, and absenteeism, with no group differences. Low recruitment limited study power. Source: PMC2758835.
outcome: Reduction in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and use of additional professional help (secondary outcomes)

memory: A study compared frovatriptan and rizatriptan for menstrually related migraine. Frovatriptan showed a significantly lower (p < 0.01) cumulative hazard of recurrence (10% vs. 32% at 24 h), as shown in Fig. 1 [PMC3208043].
text: Frovatriptan significantly reduced the cumulative hazard of recurrence during follow-up for menstrually related migraine compared to rizatriptan (10% vs. 32% at 24 h, p < 0.01) [PMC3208043].
outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine

memory: A study compared video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) to standard consultations (UNN). Overall, durations were similar (p = 0.60). However, for patients needing casting (11% of consultations), RMC took longer (29.0 min vs. 22.6 min, p = 0.0063). All RMC patients had planned operations. Source: PMC5017045.
text: Video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) took significantly longer than standard consultations (UNN) for patients requiring casting (29.0 min vs. 22.6 min, p = 0.0063). Source: PMC5017045.
outcome: The mean consultation duration in the subgroup patients who required casting

memory: Pro Taper Universal retreatment (PR) removed more filling material (12.96%) than Mani NRT-GPR (MR, 24.26%, P=0.0056). PR also caused greater dentin removal (5.02% vs. 1.36%, P=0.0028). Neither system fully removed filling material. Source: [PMC5911298].
text: Mani NRT-GPR removed more filling material (24.26%) than Pro Taper Universal retreatment (12.96%, P=0.0056). However, neither system fully removed filling material. Source: [PMC5911298].

memory: A study compared prostaglandin gel with and without hygroscopic cervical dilators. Combined therapy improved Bishop score (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) and reduced induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hours, P=0.085), but increased infection rates (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003).
text: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators significantly improved Bishop score changes after 6 hours compared to prostaglandin gel alone (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007).
intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours

memory: Sonas program vs. control showed significant MMSE differences at baseline (p=0.026) and T0 (p=0.011), T1 (p=0.044) for 0–10 and 11–20 scores. No overall group difference. Focus on interest, humor, and knowledge, not memory or communication. Source: PMC5425769.
text: The Sonas program showed significant differences in MMSE scores compared to control at baseline and follow-ups (p < 0.05), but no overall group difference. The program influenced interest, humor, and knowledge, not memory or communication. Source: PMC5425769.

memory: RFA vs resection for liver metastases showed 5-year OS 14.3% vs 34.6% (P=0.330), DFS 6.4% vs 16.2% (P=0.037). For solitary metastases, RFA 47.6% vs resection 56.0% (P=0.308).
text: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) compared with hepatic resection shows a lower 5-year disease-free survival (DFS) rate (6.4% vs 16.2%, P=0.037). For solitary metastases, DFS was 47.6% for RFA vs 56.0% for resection (P=0.308). Source: Study on RFA vs resection for liver metastases.

memory: 13 subjects completed PJ trial with 5.8 mg anthocyanin/100 ml. SBP reduced 7% (P=0.013), DBP 6% (P=0.010). FMD change 20% (P=0.172). Source: [PMC3933059].
text: Pomegranate juice significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (7%, P=0.013) and diastolic blood pressure (6%, P=0.010) compared to baseline in 13 subjects. Source: [PMC3933059].
outcome: Systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP)

memory: r-FSH + rLH vs. r-FSH + HMG showed no significant differences in follicles, oocytes, or fetus quality (p>0.05). r-FSH + HMG had higher total fetuses (p=0.02) and better fertility outcomes, including live birth, chemical pregnancy, and clinical pregnancy rates (p<0.05). Source: PMC5601935.
text: No significant differences were found in the number of oocytes or M2 oocytes between r-FSH + rLH and r-FSH + HMG (p>0.05). However, r-FSH + HMG showed better fertility outcomes, including higher total fetuses and improved live birth rates (p<0.05). Source: PMC5601935.
intervention: Recombinant- follicle stimulating hormone (r-FSH) plus recombinant-luteinizing hormone (rLH)
outcome: Number of oocytes or M2 oocytes

memory: Source [PMC5698974]: Endobutton showed higher satisfaction (89±4.3 vs 85±2.9, P=0.006) and better sports ability (85.2±4.6 vs 80.5±4, P=0.006) than Rigidfix. No difference in last month symptoms (P=0.34).
text: The Endobutton showed higher satisfaction scores (89±4.3) compared to Rigidfix (85±2.9, P=0.006) according to the IKDC 2000 questionnaire. No significant difference was found in last month symptoms (P=0.34). Source: PMC5698974.
outcome: the mean scores of satisfaction with surgery by using a subjective questionnaire IKDC 2000

memory: Recruitment substudy halted due to funding. Telephone (n=332, 69% contacted) vs. mail follow-up. Similar age (mean 55.7±6.1 vs. 55.6±6.3). 18.1% (n=60) ineligible for SCOPE trial due to recent colorectal screening. Source: [PMC3599938].
text: The effect of "Follow-up invitation by telephone" compared with "Follow-up invitation by mail" on "Age of the participants" was minimal, as both groups had similar mean ages (55.7±6.1 vs. 55.6±6.3). Source: [PMC3599938].

memory: A study compared implants placed immediately after extraction (Group A, n=68) with those in healed sites (Group B, n=76). text: Implants placed immediately after extraction (Group A) showed higher maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3 compared to healed sites (Group B, p<0.05), according to [PMC4048120]. No significant differences in plaque levels were observed.
comparator: implants were placed in healed sites
outcome: maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3

memory: Misoprostol+celecoxib reduced potassium excretion at day 3 compared to baseline (0.09±0.03 vs. 0.23±0.02 μmol/min/100g, p=0.0011) and vehicle+vehicle (0.09±0.03 vs. 0.18±0.04, p=0.0267).
text: Misoprostol + celecoxib significantly reduced potassium excretion at day 3 compared to baseline (p=0.0011) and vehicle alone (p=0.0267).

memory: Group A (neuromuscular blocking agent) vs. Group B (atracurium infusion): Group B had higher post-operative heart rate 30 min post-extubation (P=0.02). text: Group B (atracurium infusion) was associated with a higher heart rate 30 minutes post-extubation compared to Group A (neuromuscular blocking agent) (P=0.02). Other parameters were similar (P=0.27). Source: [PMC5296807].

memory: ALTPOMx vs. ALTPLAC increased VO2 at 5 min into TTE100% by +3.8 ml/min/kg (p=0.001, ES=0.6), no submaximal VO2 effect. SEAPOMx vs. SEAPLAC showed no change. Source: [PMC5452353].

intervention: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx)
comparator: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Placebo (ALTPLAC)

memory: In a study comparing self-management intervention to treatment as usual, 2 (1.9%) of 103 intervention participants relapsed (re-hospitalizations) over 30 months, versus 14 (14.3%) of 98 control participants (X²=8.83, p=0.003).
text: The self-management group had a significantly lower rate of re-hospitalizations (1.9%) compared to treatment as usual (14.3%) over 30 months (X²=8.83, p=0.003).

memory: Source [PMC5595267]: Single vs. multiple dose artificial tears showed no significant difference in OSDI score reduction (p=0.440) or TBUT improvement (p=0.497). Both groups had significant pre- vs. post-intervention OSDI decreases (p<0.001). No product-type by time interaction (p=0.468).
text: A single dose of artificial tears had no significant difference compared to multiple doses in reducing OSDI scores (p=0.440). Both showed significant OSDI decreases (p<0.001) with no interaction effect (p=0.468). Source: PMC5595267.

memory: A 10-week telephone intervention for pregnant women reduced 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose levels compared to three monitoring calls at 28 weeks (123±18 vs. 137.5±25.7 mg/dl, p=0.008). Other meal times showed non-significant differences. Source: [PMC4715405].
text: A 10-week telephone intervention significantly reduced 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose levels compared to three monitoring calls (123±18 vs. 137.5±25.7 mg/dl, p=0.008) at 28 weeks of pregnancy. Other meal times showed no significant differences. Source: [PMC4715405].
intervention: telephone intervention was performed for 10 weeks
comparator: three times of telephone call was established to record blood sugar levels

memory: Study [PMC5434251] found text message feedback had minimal, nonsignificant effects on PHQ-9 scores. Post-hoc analyses showed small differences in perseverative thinking, mindfulness, and exercise. Symptom measures favored the intervention, while FMI and SCS-D favored control.
text: Text message–based feedback had minimal, nonsignificant effects on PHQ-9 scores (PMC5434251). Post-hoc analyses showed small differences in perseverative thinking, mindfulness, and exercise, with symptom measures favoring the intervention.
comparator: Patients not receiving text message assistance during follow-up

memory: Bio-GroTM did not significantly differ from placebo in metabolic panel or resting hemodynamic measures (HR, SBP, DBP). Time effects were observed for BUN, sodium, and chloride, but no group × time interactions (p > 0.05). Source: [PMC4595235].
text: The bio-active peptide supplement (Bio-GroTM) did not significantly affect heart rate compared to placebo, as no group × time interactions were observed (p > 0.05). Source: [PMC4595235].

text: Providing written information about electrodiagnostic testing reduces anxiety compared to control. Study [PMC5951568] showed a significant decrease in anxiety scores (14.53±2.44mm vs. 21.28±2.86mm; p=0.04).
intervention: provided with written information about the electrodiagnostic testing

memory: A study compared cefepime (C), cefepime with amikacin (C-A), and cefepime with levofloxacin (C-L). ICU length of stay post-infection was similar (medians 15, 16, and 14 days). Ventilator-free days within 28 days showed no significant differences (p > 0.05).
text: The effect of cefepime (C), cefepime with amikacin (C-A), and cefepime with levofloxacin (C-L) on ICU length of stay after infection showed similar medians (15, 16, and 14 days, respectively). No significant differences were found in ventilator-free days within 28 days (p > 0.05).
intervention: cefepime (C group), cefepime with amikacin (C-A group)
outcome: length of stay in the intensive care unit after infection

memory: ILF showed higher grade 3/4 GI toxicity (18% diarrhoea) compared to none in ELF. ELF had higher neutropenia (57%) and alopecia (28%) vs ILF (5% alopecia). It also decreased Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices completion time (p = 0.026) and increased sleep duration (p = 0.039). fMRI showed increased activity in the right angular gyrus and left lingual gyrus. text: Singing Training significantly reduced Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores (p = 0.042) compared to Control [PMC4608626]. memory: A study compared Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine (RCF) with Ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) and Ropivacaine-clonidine (RC) on hemodynamic parameters. No significant differences in MAP or HR were observed between groups (P>0.05). Analgesic effects were similar across groups. RCF significantly reduced side effects: nausea/vomiting (10% vs. 40% in RF, P<0.05), sedation (5% vs. 30% in RF, P<0.05), and dry mouth (P<0.05). Other side effects were comparable. Patient comfort improved in the RCF group due to fewer adverse effects. Source: [PMC4173331].
text: The combination of Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine (RCF) compared to Ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) showed no significant differences in hemodynamic parameters like MAP or HR. However, RCF significantly reduced side effects such as nausea/vomiting, sedation, and dry mouth. Source: [PMC4173331].

memory: Low GI intervention significantly reduced glycemic response (GR) after lunch (p=0.02) compared to high GI. Lower daily AUC was also observed with low GI (p=0.03). text: A low glycemic index intervention significantly reduces glycemic response after lunch compared to a high glycemic index intervention (p=0.02). Source: PMC5684963.

memory: Source [PMC4141382]: Caudal Sufentanil + neostigmine (CSuNeo) reduced dipyrone doses (P < 0.005) and prolonged time to first dipyrone (10-11 h vs. 3-4 h, P < 0.05) compared to Caudal Sufentanil (CSu). text: Caudal Sufentanil + neostigmine reduces dipyrone needed compared to Caudal Sufentanil (P < 0.005), delays first dipyrone use (10-11 h vs. 3-4 h, P < 0.05), and lowers rescue analgesic use (P < 0.005). Source: PMC4141382.

memory: In a study comparing PLMA and ETT, cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation were significantly elevated compared to baseline (p = 0.001). The PLMA group had lower cortisol levels than the ETT group (p = 0.024). No significant differences were observed in adrenalin, noradrenalin, or dopamine. text: Both PLMA and ETT significantly increased cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation compared to baseline (p = 0.001). However, PLMA caused a less intense stress response than ETT (p = 0.024). Source: PMC3525032.
outcome: cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation

memory: A study compared an Enhanced and Basic weight loss maintenance program in 227 participants (n=114 Basic, n=113 Enhanced). No significant differences were found in attrition (18.4% vs. 23.9%, p=0.31) or weight rebound (1.3% vs. 1.5%) after 12 months. Both groups showed minimal weight rebound (Basic −0.5 (1.9) kg/m2, Enhanced −0.5 (1.6) kg/m2, p > 0.05). text: The Enhanced weight loss maintenance program did not significantly reduce weight rebound compared to the Basic program after 12 months (1.3% vs. 1.5%, p > 0.05). Both showed minimal rebound, suggesting the Basic program is as effective. Source: [PMC5746685].

memory: Source [PMC5343026] compares classic cigarettes with two e-cigarette types on craving. Spices in the curry did not significantly affect systemic and forearm hemodynamics or biochemical parameters, including oxidative stress markers.
text: A single serving of curry meal significantly increased postprandial flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal (P = 0.002). Source: [PMC4082484].

memory: Infliximab had higher total health service costs than Ciclosporin over 30 months (£5632 higher; 95% CI 2773–8305), mainly due to higher acquisition costs (p=0.001). Both treatments showed similar effectiveness with no significant difference in quality-adjusted life-years (0.021; 95% CI −0.032 to 0.096; p=0.350). Three deaths occurred, all in the Infliximab group. No significant differences were found in colectomy rates, adverse reactions, or quality-adjusted survival. Source: [PMC4994668].
text: Infliximab incurred higher total health service costs than Ciclosporin over 30 months (£5632 higher; 95% CI 2773–8305), mainly due to higher acquisition costs (p=0.001). Both showed similar effectiveness in quality-adjusted life-years (p=0.350). Source: [PMC4994668].

memory: A study compared NBUVB (9 J/cm2 for 6 weeks) with prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in generalized lichen planus, focusing on disease duration. Baseline disease duration was similar between groups (p = 0.910). NBUVB showed significantly better treatment efficacy (p = 0.008) and higher patient satisfaction (p = 0.012) compared to prednisolone. No significant side effects were reported in either group. The findings suggest NBUVB may be more effective than systemic steroids for this condition. Source: PMC3434899.
text: NBUVB (9 J/cm2 for 6 weeks) significantly reduced disease duration more effectively than prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in generalized lichen planus (p = 0.008). Source: PMC3434899.

memory: Source article [PMC5827302] found that the exercise group had significantly lower BAI scores than the control group (5.6±3.9 vs 0.1±2.3, p=0.02) with a very large within-group effect size (1.40). No significant group differences were observed for PDSS (p=0.41) or BDI-II (p=0.09), though the exercise group showed a large within-group effect size for BDI-II (1.06). The exercise group also had a significant increase in SUDS post-intervention compared to baseline (p=0.04) and after 10 minutes of resting (p=0.003), but no significant group differences for SUDS.
text: Exercise significantly reduced Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scores compared to control (5.6±3.9 vs 0.1±2.3, p=0.02) with a very large effect size (1.40) [PMC5827302].

memory: Study [PMC3546023] reported that smokers had lower NK cell percentages than nonsmokers at baseline and after 200 mg/day palmvitee (p < 0.0001). Subgroup analysis confirmed these findings. Smokers also exhibited higher cotinine and α1-antitrypsin levels (p < 0.05). Palmvitee increased tocopherol and tocotrienol levels in both smokers and nonsmokers but did not change NK cell percentages in either group. The treatment effect on NK cells was similar between smokers and nonsmokers.
text: The effect of 200 mg/day palmvitee on NK cell percentage was similar in smokers and nonsmokers (p < 0.0001). Smokers had lower NK cell percentages than nonsmokers at baseline and after treatment, but palmvitee did not alter NK cell percentages in either group (PMC3546023).

memory: The ABC group showed a significant decrease in total GLP-1 (p = 0.003) compared to baseline, while the control group did not. This was linked to metabolic improvements, including lower insulin, BAs, and metabolic syndrome markers. ABC also enhanced blood pressure, lipid profiles, and glucose control. Total BA levels, especially glycine and taurine conjugated BAs, and specific BA fractions (CDCA, CA, UDCA), were significantly reduced. These effects were not observed in the control group. Source: [PMC4958948].
text: "Active Body Control" significantly reduced total GLP-1 (p = 0.003) compared to baseline, linked to metabolic improvements, while the control group showed no change. Source: [PMC4958948].

memory: Source [PMC4990415]: GSLiM led to greater weight loss (19.6% vs. 4.1%) and improved physical discomfort, negative emotions, and quality of life compared to dietary counseling. Retention rates were similar (83.5% vs. 82.5%). No significant differences in systolic or diastolic blood pressure between groups.
text: GSLiM significantly improved physical discomfort more than dietary counseling, along with greater weight loss and better quality of life (PMC4990415).

memory: Notes: A study compared an Intensified anticipatory guidance program with a Routine program on baseline characteristics in 323 participants. Mean age was 26.5 years, 61% single, 68% Hispanic, 44% without a high school diploma, and 33% primiparous. No significant differences in baseline characteristics (age, race/ethnicity, education, marital status, number of children) were found between groups. Follow-up survey completion was low (44% and 40% in intervention and control groups, respectively). No significant differences in nonurgent ED visits (p=0.12) or knowledge score changes were observed. Source: [PMC4860224]
text: The intensified anticipatory guidance program did not significantly differ from the routine program in baseline characteristics (age, race/ethnicity, education, marital status, children) [PMC4860224].

memory: Notes: A study compared Gallium maltolate (GaM) with clarithromycin + rifampin (CLR+R) in foals with Rhodococcus equi pneumonia, focusing on lesion resolution ≥27 mm. Resolution rates were similar (GaM: 70%; CLR+R: 74%), but noninferiority of GaM was not conclusively proven. Stratified by lesion size, GaM had a lower resolution rate than CLR+R, though not statistically significant. Logistic regression considered treatment, lesion size, and their interaction. Four foals died, all from R. equi infection. Noninferiority of GaM was supported when excluding a noncompliant farm. Source: [PMC4895420].
text: A study found similar lesion resolution rates (GaM: 70%; CLR+R: 74%) for resolving lesions >27 mm in foals with Rhodococcus equi pneumonia, though noninferiority of GaM was not conclusively proven. Source: [PMC4895420].

memory: The study compared group A (mini-open anterior approach) with group B (conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach), both combined with posterior internal fixation in period I, on anal exsufflation time. Group A had significantly shorter anal exsufflation time (1.21±0.48 day) than group B (2.12±0.82 day; p<0.05). Operation time was longer in group A, while blood loss and hospitalization time were lower, though not statistically significant. VAS scores improved significantly in both groups, with group A showing better scores than group B (p<0.05). Cobb angle and ESR showed no significant differences. Source: [PMC5586978].
text: The mini-open anterior approach (group A) significantly reduced anal exsufflation time (1.21±0.48 day) compared to the conventional approach (group B: 2.12±0.82 day; p<0.05) [PMC5586978].
intervention: The mini-open anterior approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group A
comparator: conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group B

memory: In a study [PMC2650992], 100 patients undergoing breast lumpectomy and axillary dissection were randomized into a fibrin glue group (N=50) and a control group (N=50). Both groups had similar overall outcomes in drainage duration, drain output, and seroma incidence. However, subgroup analysis showed that fibrin glue significantly reduced drainage duration (3.5 vs. 4.7 days; p=0.0006) and overall drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255) in patients with level II or III axillary dissection. These findings suggest that fibrin glue may be effective in reducing drainage duration and output in patients undergoing more extensive axillary dissection.
text: In a study (PMC2650992), fibrin glue significantly reduced overall drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255) compared to the control group in patients with level II or III axillary dissection, though both groups had similar overall outcomes.
intervention: fibrin glue group (glue sprayed onto the axillary dissection site)

memory: In a pediatric study, plasma exchange (PE) was linked to shorter mechanical ventilation duration than IVIG (median 11 vs. 13 days, p=0.037). A significant negative correlation between CSF protein and ventilation duration was observed only in the PE group (p=0.037), not in IVIG (p=0.132). No baseline differences or adverse effects were noted. PE also showed a trend for shorter PICU stays (p=0.094). Source: [PMC3387601].
text: Plasma exchange (PE) was associated with a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation compared to IVIG (median 11 vs. 13 days, p=0.037). A significant negative correlation between CSF protein and ventilation duration was observed only in the PE group (p=0.037), not in IVIG (p=0.132). Source: [PMC3387601].
outcome: negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation

memory: Positive psychology-based intervention significantly improved children's subjective well-being, positive emotions (F=10.93, p=0.001), life satisfaction (F=9.68, p=0.002), and empathy (F=8.65, p=0.004) compared to wait-list control, with moderate to large effect sizes (d=0.38, 0.67, 0.34). Parental reports confirmed enhanced well-being and positive learning behaviors. No changes in negative emotions or mental health difficulties were observed. The findings suggest positive psychology interventions may effectively boost well-being in young children. Source: PMC5662620.
text: A positive psychology-based intervention significantly improved children's subjective well-being compared to a wait-list control (F=10.93, p=0.001), with moderate to large effect sizes. Source: PMC5662620.

memory: The GHSH intervention significantly increased MVPA by 24.16 minutes/week (95% CI: 5.07, 43.25, P=.007) at 6 months compared to no continued contact. text: The "Get Healthy, Stay Healthy" (GHSH) intervention significantly increased accelerometer-assessed MVPA by 24.16 minutes/week (95% CI: 5.07, 43.25, P=.007) at 6 months compared to no continued contact (Source: [PMC4879328]).
outcome: accelerometer-assessed moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA)

memory: In-sequence computer tutorials significantly improved ORS topic knowledge (19% higher post-test scores, 95% CI +7% to +31%, Cohen's-d 0.85) compared to out-of-sequence tutorials. Pre-test scores were similar. In-sequence tutorials also correlated with higher z-scores (1.1 vs. 0.52, 95% CI +0.16 to +0.93). Time spent was longer in the in-sequence group (12.1 vs. 10.5 min, 95% CI -1.2 to +4.5 min), though not statistically significant. Source: [PMC3517358]
text: In-sequence computer tutorials significantly improved ORS topic knowledge (19% higher post-test scores, 95% CI +7% to +31%) compared to out-of-sequence tutorials. Source: [PMC3517358]

memory: Cinacalcet vs. Control on iPTH target (150–300 pg/ml). Source: [PMC3669111]. Median iPTH decreased by 42.3% (cinacalcet) vs. 30.7% (control), P = 0.483. Proportion achieving iPTH target was 24.3% vs. 18.2%, P = 0.764. Primary endpoint (30% iPTH reduction) reached by 48.5% vs. 51.5%, P = 1.000. No significant difference between groups. text: Cinacalcet showed a greater median iPTH decrease (42.3%) compared to control (30.7%), but differences were not statistically significant (P=0.483). The proportion achieving the iPTH target (150–300 pg/ml) was 24.3% vs. 18.2% (P=0.764), with no significant difference. Source: [PMC3669111].

memory: A study compared Aequasyal® with DC161-DP0292 regarding safety. No clinically relevant abnormalities in systemic or local exams were found. No serious adverse events or treatment discontinuations occurred. Both products had one gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse event each. No significant differences in adverse event incidence or type were observed between the two. Source: [PMC5839221].
text: Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 showed similar safety profiles, with no serious adverse events or discontinuations. Both had one gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse event each, and no significant differences in adverse event incidence or type were observed. Source: [PMC5839221].

memory: Study [PMC5656562] reported higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios in CYP3A4 Intermediate metabolizers (CYP3A4*22 carriers) than Extensive metabolizers at weeks 12 and 24 (P=0.045, adjusted for age, BMI, ancestry PCs). However, this did not meet the corrected significance threshold (P<0.0167). In Caucasians, CYP2C9 and CYP3A5 associations were significant after correction (P=0.0165). CYP3A5 poor metabolizers showed higher concentrations but not significantly overall (P>0.14). An exploratory analysis suggested higher sildenafil levels with lower predicted CYP3A4/3A5 capacity (F test P=0.0238).
text: CYP3A4 Intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios than Extensive metabolizers (P=0.045), though not statistically significant after correction. Exploratory analysis linked lower CYP3A4/3A5 capacity with higher sildenafil levels (P=0.0238). Source: PMC5656562.

memory: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations did not induce ADCC-mediating antibody responses, as none of the four unprimed vaccinees developed such responses post-immunization [PMC4871571]. However, they significantly increased CN54rgp140-specific IgG concentrations, with median titers rising from 0.861 to 17.75 μg/ml after two doses (p<0.001). Binding IgG responses to subtype C CN54rgp140 were significantly higher after first and second immunizations compared to after HIV-MVA immunization (p<0.0001). Adverse events were mild or moderate, with no HIV infections reported. One participant experienced severe, asymptomatic hypoglycaemia.
text: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations did not induce ADCC-mediating antibody responses [PMC4871571]. However, they significantly increased CN54rgp140-specific IgG concentrations (p<0.001). No HIV infections were reported, though one participant had asymptomatic hypoglycaemia.

memory: Source [PMC5215647]: Biosimilar adalimumab showed no significant difference from reference adalimumab in ACR20, ACR50, or ACR70. Bilirubin levels were similar between groups at Day 84: 0.3 ± 0.15 (test) vs. 0.3 ± 0.20 (reference). No persistent lab changes or drug-related adverse events. text: Biosimilar adalimumab had no significant effect on bilirubin levels compared to reference adalimumab (0.3 ± 0.15 vs. 0.3 ± 0.20 at Day 84; Source: PMC5215647).

memory: A 12-week trial in non-diabetic mild AD patients (N=16 MSDC-0160, N=13 control) found no significant difference in cognitive test battery global cognitive score changes between MSDC-0160 and control. Cognitive outcomes, including the 19-item cognitive test battery global cognitive summary z-score, were assessed at baseline, 12 weeks, and 4 weeks post-treatment. MSDC-0160 significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin (p<0.001), suggesting improved insulin sensitivity, but had no effect on hs-CRP or FFA. No significant group differences were observed in cognitive measures during the short trial. The results suggest MSDC-0160 may not significantly impact cognitive function in this population, though it may improve metabolic markers. Source: [PMC4153084].
text: A 12-week trial found no significant difference in cognitive test battery global cognitive score changes between MSDC-0160 and control in non-diabetic mild AD patients. MSDC-0160 increased high molecular weight adiponectin but had no effect on cognitive measures. Source: [PMC4153084].
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: JQJT tablets reduced the risk of progressing from pre-diabetes to diabetes compared to placebo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P=0.010), with 16.5% versus 28.9% developing diabetes after 12 months (P=0.005). JQJT also showed a 1.41-fold higher normalized blood glucose (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.002-1.996, P=0.0049). Adverse events were similar between groups (2.8% vs. 1.7%, P=0.501). Source: [PMC5593818].
text: JinqiJiangtang tablets reduced the risk of progressing from pre-diabetes to diabetes compared to placebo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P=0.010) after 12 months. Source: [PMC5593818].
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
