memory: In a study [PMC3984270], α-MSH was linked to significantly lower urine output compared to controls over 10 hours (p<0.05). It also impaired GFR recovery and reduced sodium excretion at 10 hours post-reperfusion (p<0.05). No anuria was observed. α-MSH did not reduce renal inflammation or improve short-term graft function post-DBD kidney transplant, likely due to hemodynamic effects. Trends showed lower mean arterial blood pressure and higher heart rate with α-MSH.
text: α-MSH significantly reduced urine output compared to controls over 10 hours (p<0.05) and impaired GFR recovery, likely due to hemodynamic effects. It also decreased sodium excretion but did not affect renal inflammation or graft function.

memory: A study found that patients receiving telemonitored clinical care (TCC) were more likely to continue using CPAP than those receiving usual care (P < .05). TCC patients used CPAP 4.1 ± 1.8 hours per night, compared to 2.8 ± 2.2 hours in usual care (P = .07), a 46% increase. TCC also showed a trend for higher CPAP use nights (78% ± 22% vs. 60% ± 32%; P = .07). No significant differences were found in CPAP efficacy measures like mask leak or AHI reduction (P = .32). Both groups were satisfied with care, and patients were not concerned about data monitoring. Source: [PMC1874716].
text: Patients receiving telemonitored clinical care (TCC) were more likely to continue using CPAP than those receiving usual care (P < .05). TCC also showed a trend for higher CPAP use nights (P = .07). Source: [PMC1874716].
outcome: Patients rated their likelihood to continue using CPAP

memory: Both Usual care and Manual therapy led to similar improvements in primary and secondary outcomes, including headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and use of additional professional help. No significant differences were found between the groups (n=19 vs. n=18). Baseline headache characteristics were comparable. Follow-up assessments showed no differences in global perceived effect or Headache Impact Test scores. The small sample size may limit the reliability of these findings.
text: Both Usual care and Manual therapy showed similar improvements in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication use, absenteeism, and professional help utilization. No significant differences were found between the groups (n=19 vs. n=18). The small sample size may limit the reliability of these findings.
outcome: Reduction in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and use of additional professional help (secondary outcomes)

memory: A study (PMC3208043) found frovatriptan significantly reduced the cumulative hazard of recurrence (p < 0.01) compared to rizatriptan in menstrually related migraine. At 24 h, recurrence was 10% with frovatriptan versus 32% with rizatriptan. Pain relief at 2 h and 24 h was similar (p = NS). Frovatriptan provided comparable immediate pain relief but better sustained effect with fewer recurrences. The study included 49 frovatriptan-treated and 59 rizatriptan-treated attacks.
text: Frovatriptan significantly reduced the cumulative hazard of recurrence (10% at 24 h) compared to rizatriptan (32% at 24 h) in menstrually related migraine (PMC3208043). Both provided similar immediate pain relief, but frovatriptan offered better sustained effect.
outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine

text: In patients requiring casting, video-assisted remote consultations had a significantly longer mean duration (29.0 min) than standard consultations (22.6 min, p = 0.0063). Source: [PMC5017045]

PR showed significantly less residual filling material (12.96% vs. 24.26%, P=0.0056) and caused more dentin removal (5.02% vs. 1.36%, P=0.0028). No complications were reported. text: Pro Taper Universal retreatment (PR) removed significantly more remaining filling material (12.96%) compared to Mani NRT-GPR (24.26%, P=0.0056), but caused more dentin removal (5.02% vs. 1.36%, P=0.0028). Neither system fully removed filling material. Source: [PMC5911298].

memory: A study found that combining prostaglandin gel with hygroscopic cervical dilators led to a greater increase in Bishop score after 6 hours (3.6 vs. 2.1, P = 0.007) compared to prostaglandin gel alone. There was a trend toward shorter induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hours, P = 0.085). However, the combined therapy was associated with a significantly higher infection rate (59% vs. 12%, P = 0.003). The study included 17 patients in the prostaglandin-only group and 23 in the combined group, with no demographic differences. While the combination improved cervical ripening and induction time, the increased infection risk may limit its use. Source: PMC1784771.
text: Combining prostaglandin gel with hygroscopic cervical dilators significantly increases Bishop score after 6 hours (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) compared to prostaglandin gel alone. However, this combination raises infection risk (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003). Source: PMC1784771.
intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours

memory: Source [PMC3204557]: RFA and resection showed similar 5-year DFS for small solitary CRLM (P=0.980). RFA had lower DFS for larger solitary CRLM (23.1% vs 36.6%, P=0.01). In metachronous liver metastases, DFS was similar between RFA (32.2%) and resection (34.0%, P=0.164). For multiple metastases, no OS differences (P=0.330). text: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) shows similar 5-year disease-free survival (DFS) to hepatic resection for small solitary CRLM (P=0.980) and metachronous liver metastases (P=0.164). However, RFA has lower DFS for larger solitary CRLM (23.1% vs 36.6%, P=0.01) and multiple metastases (6.4% vs 16.2%, P=0.037). Source: [PMC3204557].

memory: A study with 13 participants showed that pomegranate juice (PJ) significantly lowered systolic blood pressure (SBP) by 7% (P = 0.013) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) by 6% (P = 0.010) compared to baseline. text: Pomegranate juice significantly reduced SBP by 7% (P = 0.013) and DBP by 6% (P = 0.010) compared to baseline in a study of 13 participants [PMC3933059].
outcome: Systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP)

text: The effect of r-FSH + rLH compared with HMG + r-FSH on the number of oocytes or M2 oocytes showed no significant difference (p > 0.05). Source: PMC5601935.
intervention: Recombinant- follicle stimulating hormone (r-FSH) plus recombinant-luteinizing hormone (rLH)

memory: The study compared Endobutton and Rigidfix using the IKDC 2000 questionnaire to evaluate patient satisfaction. text: The Endobutton showed higher patient satisfaction scores (89 ± 4.3) compared to Rigidfix (85 ± 2.9; P = 0.006) using the IKDC 2000 questionnaire. Source: [PMC5698974].

memory: A study compared telephone and mail follow-up invitations and found similar baseline ages between groups (telephone: mean 55.7 years, SD 6.1; mail: mean 55.6 years, SD 6.3). Telephone follow-up improved screening attendance (17.5% vs. 9.1%) and RCT enrollment (12.3% vs. 7.4%). However, the impact of follow-up method on participant age was not directly assessed. Age similarity was noted at baseline, but no analysis on age changes due to follow-up method was conducted. Source: [PMC3599938].
text: The study found similar baseline ages between participants invited by telephone (mean 55.7 years) and mail (mean 55.6 years). However, it did not assess the effect of follow-up method on age changes. Source: [PMC3599938].

memory: Study [PMC4048120] evaluated immediate vs. delayed implant placement on maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3. 144 implants (76 delayed, 68 immediate) were analyzed. Immediate implants had higher mean CFV at all time points, with significant differences at time points 2 and 3 (Table 2). No significant differences in bone loss (0.54 vs. 0.66 mm, p=0.201) or other peri-implant parameters at 12 months. Findings suggest immediate placement may affect maxillary CFV during early follow-up, but not long-term bone loss or other clinical parameters.
text: Immediate implant placement after extraction was associated with significantly higher maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3 compared to implants placed in healed sites (PMC4048120). However, no significant differences in bone loss or other peri-implant parameters were observed at 12 months.
comparator: implants were placed in healed sites
outcome: maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3

memory: Study [PMC5595267] found no significant difference between single-dose and multiple-dose artificial tears in improving OSDI (p = 0.440). Both showed significant OSDI improvement (p < 0.001). memory: A study compared a 10-week telephone intervention with three calls to monitor blood sugar levels on 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose at 28 weeks of pregnancy. text: The 10-week telephone intervention significantly reduced mean 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose levels at 28 weeks of pregnancy compared to three monitoring calls (123±18 vs. 137.5±25.7 mg/dl; p=0.008). Source: [PMC4715405].

memory: In [PMC5434251], text message–based feedback had near-zero to small, nonsignificant effects on PHQ-9 scores, suggesting limited impact on depressive symptoms. Similar nonsignificant results were found for PTQ, FFA, and SCS-D. While PHQ-9 and PTQ showed slight favor toward the intervention, FFA and SCS-D favored the control. Overall, the study indicates text message feedback has limited effectiveness on primary depressive symptom outcomes.
text: Patients receiving text message–based feedback showed near-zero to small, nonsignificant effects on PHQ-9 scores compared to those not receiving it, indicating limited impact on depressive symptoms (PMC5434251).
comparator: Patients not receiving text message assistance during follow-up

memory: A study [PMC4595235] found no significant group or group × time interaction effects on heart rate (HR) when comparing Bio-active peptide supplement with Placebo (p > 0.05). Although significant time effects were observed for HR (p < 0.05), they were not associated with the supplement. No specific effects of the supplement on HR, systolic or diastolic blood pressure were noted. Group effects were observed for creatinine, eGFR, and RBC, but these were unrelated to HR. The supplement had no significant impact on metabolic, blood chemistry, or complete blood count variables. Thus, the supplement does not appear to influence HR or related cardiovascular measures.
text: A study found no significant effect of "Bio-active peptide supplement" on heart rate compared to "Placebo" (p > 0.05). While time effects were observed for heart rate, they were not linked to the supplement. The supplement also did not influence related cardiovascular measures. Source: [PMC4595235].

memory: In a phase II trial of 114 metastatic gastric cancer patients, ILF showed higher grade 3/4 digestive toxicities (18% diarrhea) compared to ELF (no reports). memory: The study evaluated intensive sound masking therapy's impact on tinnitus using THI scores in effective and non-effective subgroups compared to baseline. Post-intervention, no significant group differences in THI scores were observed. However, significant pre-post THI score changes were found (19.10 vs 0.98, t=12.54, P<0.001). THI scores significantly decreased in the effective group (t=−14.07, P<0.001), while no significant reduction was found in the non-effective group (t=−1.98, P=0.054). Pre-intervention THI scores were significantly lower in the non-effective group (t=4.11, P<0.001). Logistic regression identified predictive factors for effectiveness, with audiometric configuration analyzed in four sub-groups.
text: Intensive sound masking therapy significantly reduced THI scores in the effective subgroup (t=−14.07, P<0.001) compared to baseline, while no significant improvement was observed in the non-effective subgroup (t=−1.98, P=0.054).
intervention: intensive sound masking therapy on tinnitus in effective subgroup

memory: Source: [PMC4869362]. TCA and KOH improved skin hydration and texture initially. TCA showed better texture improvement at D7 (p=0.00). memory: A study with 40 children (mean age 11.5 ± 1.175 years) examined vitamin D supplements versus placebo on HDL-C and vitamin D levels. Vitamin D supplementation significantly increased HDL-C (P = 0.007) and vitamin D levels (P < 0.001), while the placebo group showed slight HDL-C decreases (P = 0.27). Initially, no between-group differences were significant (P = 0.11 for HDL-C; P = 0.20 for vitamin D). text: Vitamin D supplementation significantly increased HDL-C (P = 0.007) and vitamin D levels (P < 0.001) compared to placebo in children. After adjustment, the vitamin D group had higher HDL-C (P = 0.04) and vitamin D levels (P < 0.001) than the placebo group. Source: [PMC5045666]
outcome: Baseline levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and vitamin D

text: The effect of "DCS D-cycloserine first" compared with "PCB placebo first" on "duration of illness (schizophrenia patients)" showed no significant differences [PMC5508614].

text: Adding physiological-dose steroids to standard sepsis therapy for 10 days did not significantly affect 28-day mortality compared to standard therapy alone (40% vs. 60%, P = 0.343). Other outcomes were also similar. Source: [PMC125315].

memory: The study evaluated the effect of SRP with amoxicillin + metronidazole versus SRP alone on TIMP-1/MMP-1 balance. Both groups showed significant MMP-1 decreases at 3 and 6 months (P < 0.05). intervention: scaling and root planning (SRP) in combination with amoxicillin plus metronidazole

memory: In a study of 90 low-to-moderate cardiac risk patients, both home-based training with telemonitoring and centre-based training improved peakVO2 significantly from baseline to discharge (+11% vs +15%) and at one-year follow-up (+16% vs +17%), with no between-group differences (p = 0.25 and p = 0.89). text: Both home-based training with telemonitoring and centre-based training similarly improved peakVO2 at discharge and one-year follow-up (p = 0.25 and p = 0.89). Source: [PMC5518918].

text: Linagliptin reduced urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) by 32% at 24 weeks compared to control (P < 0.05). The between-group difference was -28% (P = 0.0357). Baseline UACR was similar, and the effect was evident by 12 weeks. Source: PMC3816860.

memory: Study [PMC5791397] found that transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath (Group 1) resulted in a significantly shorter hospital stay (1.17 ± 0.47 days) compared to conventional PCCL (Group 2: 2.12 ± 0.35 days, P=0.000). memory: A study found no significant difference in PIVC failure rates per 1000 hours between 10 mL and 3 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flushes (4.84 vs. 7.44, p=0.06). text: A study found no significant difference in PIVC failure rates per 1000 hours between 10 mL and 3 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flushes (4.84 vs. 7.44, p=0.06). Source: [PMC4960789].

text: Face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) significantly reduced anxious symptoms (STAI trait subscale) compared to placebo (F(2,112) = 3.3, p = .05), with sustained effects at follow-up (t(15) = 2.4, p = .03). memory: In an experimental model of mild extrapulmonary ALI with IAH, PSV improved lung function, reduced alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, and DAD score compared to PCV. memory: A study compared Alfentanil (10 μg/kg, 1 μg/kg/min infusion) and Remifentanil (0.5 μg/kg, 0.1 μg/kg/min infusion) in 40 patients. Both groups had no respiratory issues, but Remifentanil was associated with higher nausea and vomiting (6 vs. 1 patients, P<0.05). Demographics and baseline parameters were comparable between groups.
text: No significant differences were found between Alfentanil and Remifentanil in time to eye opening, verbal response, or discharge from recovery (PMC3591547). Remifentanil was linked to higher nausea and vomiting.
intervention: 10 μg/kg of Alfentanil, infusion of Alfentanil 1 μg/kg/min
comparator: Remifentanil 0.5 μg/kg, infusion of Remifentanil 0.1 μg/kg/min

memory: DHP + PQ vs DHP: Faster gametocyte clearance with DHP + PQ (median 1 vs 12 days, HR 7.3, p=0.01). By day 7, 2.1% vs 15% had patent gametocytes (PR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02–0.9, p=0.03). text: Dihydroartemisin-piperaquine + primaquine significantly reduces gametocyte carriage compared to dihydroartemisin-piperaquine alone, with faster clearance (median 1 vs 12 days, HR 7.3, p=0.01) and lower prevalence by day 7 (2.1% vs 15%, PR 0.12, p=0.03). Source: [PMC5462369].

memory: Source [PMC5350209] indicates that "Visual warning (text)" significantly reduces the speed of alcohol consumption compared to "No warning" (p < .001). text: Visual warning (text) significantly reduces the speed of alcohol consumption compared to no warning (p < .001). Text and image warnings had similar effects (p = .76). The presence of warnings, not message format, mainly affects consumption speed (PMC5350209).

memory: Proximal-release pellets significantly increased plasma lithium levels compared to distal-release pellets (P = 0.001), as shown by AUC data. Proximal pellets also increased uric acid by ~50% vs. placebo (P = 0.003), whereas distal pellets had no effect. ATP-containing proximal pellets showed lower lithium AUC than placebo (P = 0.001). text: Administration via proximal-release pellets significantly increases plasma lithium levels compared to distal-release pellets (P = 0.001). Source: [PMC3441280].

memory: A study found that Pap smear at enrollment significantly increased IL-10 levels in cervicovaginal lavages (CVLs) compared to no intervention (p = 0.0003). No significant changes were observed in IL-8, IL-1β, or IL-6. IL-12 p70 and TNF-α also increased in the Pap smear group. Total protein concentrations remained unchanged. The study included 41 intervention and 39 control participants with no baseline differences. CVL samples were collected at enrollment and 2 weeks later. text: Pap smear at enrollment significantly increased IL-10 levels in cervicovaginal lavages compared to no intervention (p = 0.0003). This effect was observed without changes in proinflammatory cytokines. Source: [PMC1868022].

memory: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, demonstrated therapeutic equivalence to etanercept (ETN) in RA patients on methotrexate (MTX) at week 24. ACR20 response was 78.1% (SB4) vs 80.3% (ETN), with 95% CI within −15% to 15% (PMC5264222). ACR50: 46.6% vs 42.3%; ACR70: 25.5% vs 22.6% (PPS). text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, is therapeutically equivalent to etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate, with similar ACR20, ACR50, and ACR70 responses (PMC5264222). outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

text: The new formula (NF) showed a significantly higher soft stool frequency (17% vs 0%, p=0.046) compared to standard formula (SF), though no significant difference in weekly defecation frequency (p=0.38). [PMC1852321]

memory: In the DPP/DPPOS study, continuous antidepressant use (ADM) was associated with increased diabetes risk in both the placebo (HR 2.34 [1.32–4.15]) and lifestyle (HR 2.48 [1.45–4.22]) arms, but not in the metformin arm (HR 0.55 [0.25–1.19]). text: Antidepressant users had a significantly increased diabetes risk in the lifestyle arm (HR 2.48 [1.45–4.22]) of the DPP/DPPOS study compared to non-users, but not in the metformin arm. This association remained consistent after excluding weight-gain-prone antidepressants (PMC2992187).

memory: In a study [PMC3856598], BMDMC therapy in CLP mice reduced alveolar collapse compared to controls. It improved survival (70% vs. 40% at day 7), reduced lung elastance, cellularity, collagen, and IL-1β. Chemokine expression (KC, MCP-1) and adhesion molecules (ICAM-1, VCAM-1) increased. These findings suggest BMDMC may mitigate alveolar collapse in ARDS models.
text: BMDMC therapy in CLP mice reduced alveolar collapse compared to controls [PMC3856598]. It improved survival, reduced lung elastance, and inflammatory markers, suggesting a protective effect against alveolar collapse in ARDS models.
intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)

memory: Source [PMC5282794] indicates plastic caps reduced pain responses in infants during vaginal operative delivery compared to metal cups (p < 0.001), with low pain responses and full recovery within 72 hours. text: Plastic caps reduced pain responses in infants during vaginal operative delivery compared to metal cups (p < 0.001), with full recovery within 72 hours. Metal cups caused more scalp trauma (13.2% vs. 6.6%), though not statistically significant. Pain scores (EDIN ≥ 5) showed no significant difference (p = 0.8). Source: [PMC5282794].

memory: In a phase 2a trial, synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) was compared to placebo on the Dependence Scale. Responders showed less decline (p=0.033) and reduced decline on the Disability Assessment for Dementia scale (p=0.015). Sustained anti-AN1792 titers were found in 17 of 19 responders, while non-responders had no detectable antibodies. MRI showed similar brain volume loss between responders and placebo. A 20.2% less decline on the CDR-SOB scale was noted in responders, though not statistically significant (p=0.185). Source: [PMC2825665].
text: Synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) showed less decline on the Dependence Scale compared to placebo (p=0.033) in a phase 2a trial. This effect was associated with sustained anti-AN1792 titers in responders. Source: [PMC2825665].

memory: Study [PMC4973627] compared "Physical activity + Healthy eating" with "Control" on "Cardiovascular mortality." The combined intervention (PA+/HE+) had a 15% mortality rate (76/502) with a relative risk of 0.49 (0.36–0.66; P < 0.001) versus control. text: The combination of physical activity and healthy eating significantly reduces cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.36–0.66; P < 0.001) compared to control, more effectively than either intervention alone (PA+ only: RR 0.56; P < 0.001). Source: [PMC4973627].

memory: Web-based CME, feedback, and tools showed no significant incremental benefit over control on medication intensification for glucose, BP, or LDL control in diabetic patients (p=0.948). text: The intervention showed no significant incremental benefit over the control group (p=0.948) in medication intensification for glucose, BP, or LDL control in diabetic patients. Source: [PMC3467590].
intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

text: Cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day orally for 8 weeks) reduced nitro-oxidative stress compared to placebo, as shown by lower NT immunoreactivity and improved markers of oxidative stress in diabetic myocardium (PMC4628236).
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

intervention: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF)

text: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) significantly reduced the 25/PT ratio compared to saline (3 ml) (P < 0.05), suggesting improved expiratory flow dynamics. Saline had no effect. Source: [PMC111183].

memory: In the GENRES Study [PMC4330076], bisoprolol was compared to losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide in males with moderate hypertension (mean BP 152/100 mm Hg) and elevated BMI. Bisoprolol showed greater BP reduction (11.1/8.3 mm Hg). Genome-wide analysis identified three SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) significantly associated with ASBP response to bisoprolol (P≤1×10−5). text: Bisoprolol showed greater BP reduction than losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide in hypertensive males. SNPs rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037 on chromosome 11 (ACY3 gene) were significantly associated with ASBP response to bisoprolol (P≤1×10−5), suggesting genetic factors influence treatment efficacy (GENRES Study, PMC4330076).
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

memory: At week 26, 18.18% (8/44) of patients on metformin + alogliptin achieved HbA1c ≤7.0%, compared to 10.81% (4/37) on metformin alone, with no statistically significant difference (P > 0.05) [PMC5370803]. text: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) significantly reduced felt stigma after treatment compared to individual support (B = −0.44, p = 0.02). This effect was maintained six months post-treatment, though not statistically significant (B = −0.45, p = 0.12). Source: [PMC5808396].

memory: Lixisenatide reduced infarct size in isolated rat hearts compared to placebo (162 ± 12 mm² vs. 98 ± 9 mm², p < 0.05). Left ventricular risk area was slightly lower with lixisenatide (288 ± 5 mm²) than placebo (306 ± 9 mm²), though not statistically significant. The infarct-to-risk area ratio decreased by 36% in the lixisenatide group. No significant differences were observed in left ventricular total area or wall thickness. Source: [PMC3637243].
text: Lixisenatide reduced left ventricular risk area compared to control in isolated rat hearts (288 ± 5 mm² vs. 306 ± 9 mm²), though not statistically significant. Source: [PMC3637243].

text: An 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction significantly increased longus colli thickness compared to 10% MVIC during concurrent masticatory muscle contraction (p<0.05), according to [PMC4681902]. This effect was context-dependent and not observed in sternocleidomastoid thickness.

memory: A study of 176 patients found no significant difference in median hospitalization duration (4 days, IQR: 4-4, p=0.09) between Ampicillin/sulbactam and Cefuroxime. Postoperative infection rates were 7.4% with no group differences (p=0.6). Post-cesarean endometritis rates were 2.3% and 2.4% for Ampicillin/sulbactam and Cefuroxime, respectively (p=1). text: Ampicillin/sulbactam and Cefuroxime showed no significant difference in hospitalization duration (median 4 days, p=0.09) in a study of 176 patients. Other outcomes also showed no significant differences. Source: [PMC3009979].

memory: Source [PMC3112403]: Flaxseed significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose (5.92 ± 0.31 mmol/L) compared to wheat bran (4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L). Wheat bran reduced fasting insulin but not glucose. No significant differences in BMI, waist circumference, or inflammatory markers (IL-6, TNF-α, hs-CRP) between groups. Energy and nutrient intake were similar. Flaxseed had no significant effect on insulin, while wheat bran reduced insulin compared to baseline.
text: Flaxseed significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose compared to wheat bran (5.92 ± 0.31 vs. 4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L) (PMC3112403). Wheat bran reduced insulin but not glucose. No significant differences in BMI or inflammatory markers were observed.

memory: In study [PMC4301837], LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration at 12 h by 49–63% (P < 0.001) compared to placebo, with effects returning to baseline by 24 h. No additional benefit was seen with the 10 mg dose. LCI699 also reduced aldosterone on Days 7 and 14. Eplerenone 100 mg increased pre-ACTH aldosterone by 29% and ACTH-stimulated aldosterone by 63%. LCI699 increased 11-deoxycortisol at higher doses, indicating possible off-target effects.
text: LCI699 significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration at 12 h by 49–63% (P < 0.001) compared to placebo in study [PMC4301837]. Effects returned to baseline by 24 h, with no additional benefit at 10 mg.

memory: The study compared system-oriented therapy with reference intervention regarding completed follow-up. The reference group had higher non-completion (15/40 vs. 4/30, P=0.017). System-oriented therapy achieved 43% standard fulfillment in the hospital. No significant differences were found in average bed days or hospitalization duration. Compliance trends favored system-oriented therapy but were not statistically significant. Higher attrition in the reference group may affect effect estimates.
text: System-oriented therapy showed better completion rates compared to reference intervention (4/30 vs. 15/40, P=0.017). However, no significant differences were found in average bed days or hospitalization duration. Compliance trends favored system-oriented therapy, though not statistically significant. Higher attrition in the reference group may impact effect estimates.

memory: A study evaluated IPE (4g/day) vs. placebo in diabetic patients (median baseline A1c = 6.8%). No significant changes in fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR were found in all subgroups. Baseline hsCRP was higher in total and less-controlled diabetes groups. IPE significantly improved lipid parameters across all groups, with greater hsCRP and Apo B reductions in less-controlled diabetes. Source: [PMC3718763] Abstract > Results.
text: IPE (4g/day) did not significantly affect fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR in diabetic patients, regardless of baseline A1c levels (PMC3718763). However, it improved lipid parameters, with greater reductions in hsCRP and Apo B in less-controlled diabetes.
outcome: fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or homeostasis model assessment-estimated insulin total (all subjects with diabetes—overall median baseline glycosylated hemoglobin A1c [A1c] = 6.8%), better-controlled diabetes (below median baseline A1c), and less-controlled diabetes (above median baseline A1c).

memory: In a 12-week trial, Dextromethorphan (DM60) demonstrated significantly better treatment retention compared to Placebo (PMC4540107). The DM60 group exhibited lower plasma morphine and TNF-α levels. No significant differences were observed in plasma cytokine levels, BDNF, or methadone dose requirements. These results suggest DM60 may enhance treatment retention without affecting methadone needs or other biomarkers.
text: Dextromethorphan (DM60) significantly improved treatment retention compared to placebo in a 12-week trial (PMC4540107). The DM60 group showed lower plasma morphine and TNF-α levels, suggesting a potential benefit in enhancing treatment retention without affecting methadone requirements or other biomarkers.

memory: A study compared Agave-derived fructans with formula and breast milk on C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels in infants. No statistically significant differences were found in initial or final CRP levels between groups (Wilcoxon test p = 0.05; Fisher Student T-Test p > 0.05), as shown in Table 3 (PMC4663570). Serum ferritin levels also showed no significant differences. Analysis based on delivery type (cesarean vs. vaginal) did not reveal significant variations in CRP or ferritin. Salivary IgA levels showed group differences (p < 0.05; p < 0.01), but these were not associated with CRP levels. Source: nutrients-07-05442-t003_Table 3.
text: Agave-derived fructans had no significant effect on C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels compared to formula (p > 0.05). No differences were observed in initial or final CRP levels between groups (PMC4663570).

memory: In CKD patients with low vitamin D, Vitamin D + Calcium supplementation compared to Calcium alone showed no significant effect on pro-inflammatory markers like IL-6 and hs-CRP, except in non-diabetics. However, Vitamin D + Calcium maintained serum IL-10 levels (p = 0.06), while the Calcium group showed significant reductions at weeks 6 and 12, suggesting calcitriol may stabilize anti-inflammatory IL-10. These effects were independent of serum vitamin D levels. Serum 25-OHD levels increased significantly in the Vitamin D + Calcium group (p = 0.001). The study highlights the need to monitor serum calcium levels. Findings align with prior research in chronic heart failure patients, where Vitamin D3 + Calcium similarly preserved IL-10. Source: PMC4440033.
text: In CKD patients with low vitamin D, "Vitamin D + Calcium" compared to "Calcium" alone maintained serum IL-10 levels (p = 0.06), while the Calcium group showed significant reductions. This suggests calcitriol may stabilize anti-inflammatory IL-10. Source: PMC4440033.

memory: Study [PMC4092926] found no significant differences (p>0.05) in body weight at slaughter (21.78 kg), hot and cold carcass weights, carcass yields, or rib eye area (7.73 cm²) when sunflower cake replaced soybean meal at 0, 33, 66, and 100% DM levels. Muscle:fat and muscle:bone ratios were unchanged, indicating no effect on commercial value. Consistent body weights across treatments suggest similar carcass and rib eye area measurements. The study concluded that sunflower cake can fully replace soybean meal without affecting carcass traits in goats.
text: A study found no significant differences (p>0.05) in body weight, carcass yields, or rib eye area when sunflower cake replaced soybean meal in goats. Sunflower cake can fully replace soybean meal without affecting carcass traits.
outcome: Weights, carcass yields, rib eye area of goats

memory: Source [PMC2911596]: MAC and SE values before fentanyl boluses were similar between sevoflurane-fentanyl and isoflurane-fentanyl anesthesia (MAC: 0.74 ± 0.12 vs 0.77 ± 0.17, P = .32; SE: 43.5 ± 8.1 vs 45.2 ± 8.3, P = .47). Fentanyl boluses decreased SSI similarly in both groups, though SSI values were higher in the sevoflurane group. Pre-bolus HR differed (70.6 ± 13.0 vs 64.9 ± 11.8, P < .01). text: Sevoflurane-fentanyl and isoflurane-fentanyl anesthesia showed similar MAC and SE values before fentanyl boluses (P = .32 and P = .47, respectively) according to [PMC2911596].
outcome: MAC and SE values before fentanyl boluses

memory: Source [PMC5986505]: VOO (p=0.037) and OVOO (p=0.002) increased fasting plasma triacylglycerol levels, while FOO had no effect. Baseline triacylglycerol was 78 ± 5 mg/dL. FOO increased total cholesterol (p=0.021), but LDLc was unchanged. SBP decreased after VOO (p=0.019) and increased after FOO (p=0.004). HDLc increased only after OVOO (p=0.041) in females. No changes in daily energy intake, BMI, waist circumference, or fasting glucose were observed.
text: Virgin olive oil (VOO) and Optimized virgin olive oil (OVOO) increased fasting plasma triacylglycerol levels (p=0.037 and p=0.002, respectively), while Functional olive oil (FOO) had no effect (PMC5986505).
intervention: Virgin olive oil (VOO) and Optimized virgin olive oil (OVOO)

memory: Source [PMC4007144] shows that the "Intimate partner prevention intervention" significantly improved men's ability to control hostility and manage conflicts (ARR 1.3, 95% CI 1.06-1.58). It also reduced intentions to use physical IPV (ARR 0.83, 95% CI 0.66-1.06) and improved attitudes toward sexual IPV (ARR 1.21, 95% CI 0.77-1.91). However, effects on actual physical and sexual IPV levels were not significant (ARR 0.52, 95% CI 0.18-1.51). text: The "Intimate partner prevention intervention" significantly improved men's ability to control hostility and manage conflicts (ARR 1.3, 95% CI 1.06-1.58) compared to control, according to [PMC4007144].

memory: Source [PMC5447816]: High E scores correlate with faster suturing test completion time (β = −418.2, P = 0.0118). memory: Erlotinib vs. placebo showed no significant difference in quality of life scores at 1 or 2 months (all P ≥ .40) [PMC4112798]. Median OS was 2.9 months (placebo) vs. 3.4 months (erlotinib), HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.58-1.55; P = .83). No difference in neurological progression-free survival (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.59-1.54; P = .84). text: Erlotinib showed no significant difference from placebo in quality of life scores at 1 or 2 months (all P ≥ .40) [PMC4112798]. Other outcomes also showed no significant differences.

text: Yogic intervention combined with medication significantly improved positive well-being (P<0.01) and vitality (P<0.02) compared to medication alone at six months (PMC4794540). No significant differences were found in self-control.

memory: Source [PMC4727391] found no significant differences in adverse effects between laryngeal mask (LM) and endotracheal intubation (ETI) (LM, n=3; ETI, n=4). text: A study (PMC4727391) found no significant differences in adverse effects between laryngeal mask ventilation and endotracheal intubation. Both methods showed similar safety and effectiveness in terms of insertion success, time, and resuscitation outcomes.

text: Diet intervention significantly reduced LDL cholesterol (P = 0.003) at 12 weeks, with effects sustained at 1 year, compared to control (PMC3917884).

text: Both the underwater treadmill and control groups showed significant reductions in anteroposterior, mediolateral, and total postural sway compared to baseline (p<0.05). memory: A study found that lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg improved symptom control more than lanreotide microparticles 30 mg, with significant reductions in hyperhidrosis (P < 0.001) and headache (P < 0.001). Symptom intensity was mild to moderate. Both treatments showed similar hormonal control, but Autogel® achieved better GH suppression (3.8 vs 4.3 ng/ml, P < 0.001). IGF-1 levels remained largely unchanged, with similar normalization rates (55% and 56%). Patient acceptance was good for both treatments.
text: Lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg improved symptom control compared to lanreotide microparticles 30 mg, with significant reductions in hyperhidrosis and headache (P < 0.001). Both provided similar hormonal control, but Autogel® achieved better GH suppression. Patient acceptance was good for both treatments.

memory: Perindopril vs. placebo on FMD after 6 months: FMD increased from 2.6% to 3.3% in perindopril (n=256) and 2.8% to 3.0% in placebo. Change in FMD after 36 months was 0.55% higher in perindopril (95% CI −0.36, 1.47; p=0.23). Rate of change per 6 months: 0.14% (p=0.02) in perindopril vs. 0.02% (p=0.74) in placebo (difference 0.12%, p=0.07). No difference in nitroglycerine response. Source: PMC2039813.
text: After 6 months, Perindopril showed a greater increase in flow-mediated vasodilatation (FMD) compared to placebo (0.14% vs. 0.02%, p=0.07). However, this difference was not statistically significant. Source: PMC2039813.

memory: A 6-week study compared 100g of instant oat cereal with 100g of wheat flour-based noodles. The oat group showed significant reductions in waist circumference (p=0.002), total cholesterol (p=0.015), and LDL-C (p=0.028), with increased HDL-C (p=0.017). No significant differences were found in blood pressure or other anthropometric/laboratory parameters. The oat group had higher dietary fiber intake. These findings suggest that instant oat cereal may be more beneficial than wheat flour-based noodles in reducing waist circumference and improving lipid profiles.
text: A 6-week study found that 100g of instant oat cereal significantly reduced waist circumference (p=0.002) compared to 100g of wheat flour-based noodles, along with improvements in lipid profiles.

memory: In a study of 200 patients, Diazepam + chlorpheniramine (5 mg + 4 mg) premedication was associated with increased local pain (30%) compared to control (16%; P = 0.018). text: Diazepam + chlorpheniramine premedication was associated with increased local pain (30% vs. 16%; P = 0.018) compared to control. Source: [PMC5358282].

intervention: 4 weeks before Ramadan while performing the Islamic fasting for 1 week (baseline fasting) (BLF) or during the second week of Ramadan while fasting (Ramadan)

memory: Source [PMC5689110]: In an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, high-dose aripiprazole had a higher discontinuation rate (35.7%) than placebo (16.7%), with a hazard ratio of 5.51 (p=0.0278). text: High-dose aripiprazole significantly increased discontinuation rate (35.7%) compared to placebo (16.7%) (HR 5.51, p=0.0278) in an 8-week trial. Low-dose aripiprazole showed no significant difference from placebo (HR 1.05, p=0.9576). Source: [PMC5689110].

memory: At extubation readiness, respiratory physiotherapy–driven weaning led to significantly lower PSV (5 vs. 8 cmH2O; p=0.015) and PEEP (5 vs. 8 cmH2O; p<0.001) compared to progressive discontinuation of PSV with SmartCare™. memory: Source [PMC2853089]: In a breast cancer trial on Trastuzumab, the Internet group (received invitation letter) showed significantly better understanding of trial results (18.8% vs 5.6%, P=0.039) compared to the control group. text: The Internet group showed significantly better understanding of trial results (18.8% vs 5.6%, P=0.039) compared to the control group in a breast cancer Trastuzumab trial (PMC2853089).
intervention: Internet group (who received the letter of invitation)
comparator: control group (who did not receive it)

memory: Study [PMC4636858] compared "Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone" with "No treatment" in 71 MS patients. MRI plaque counts slightly decreased during treatment (2.29 vs. 2.17), but differences were not significant (P = 0.782). Post-treatment, both groups showed similar plaque count increases (P = 0.611). EDSS scores also showed no significant changes. The study found no added benefit of methylprednisolone when combined with mitoxantrone compared to mitoxantrone alone. The combination did not significantly reduce plaques or disability compared to no treatment.
text: A study found that "Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone" did not significantly reduce multiple sclerosis plaques compared to no treatment (P = 0.782). Plaque counts and EDSS scores showed no significant changes, indicating no added benefit of methylprednisolone with mitoxantrone. Source: [PMC4636858].

memory: Artesunate monotherapy (2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily) resulted in a faster median FCT (17.9–19.1 h) compared to quinine + doxycycline (29.3 h; P=0.001). PCT was also quicker in artesunate groups (29.5–29.8 h) vs quinine + doxycycline (43.1 h; P<0.001). Parasite reduction ratios at 12 and 24 h were similar between groups (P<0.001). Cure rates were 97.8%, 100%, and 100% for the three arms. No serious adverse events; all groups well tolerated. Source: [PMC3525560].
text: Artesunate monotherapy (2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily) significantly reduced median FCT (17.9–19.1 h) compared to quinine + doxycycline (29.3 h; P=0.001). Source: [PMC3525560].
intervention: artesunate monotherapy with 2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily
comparator: quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days

memory: Source [PMC5079604]: Metformin 1,000 mg + sitagliptin 100 mg daily significantly improved hyperglycemia relapse-free survival vs. placebo (P = 0.015), with a mean time to relapse of 480 vs. 305 days (P = 0.004). text: Metformin 1,000 mg + sitagliptin 100 mg daily significantly improved hyperglycemia relapse-free survival compared to placebo (P = 0.015), with a mean time to relapse of 480 vs. 305 days (P = 0.004). Source: [PMC5079604].
intervention: metformin 1,000 mg daily, sitagliptin 100 mg daily

memory: A 12-week trial with 101 participants showed isomaltulose significantly reduced triglycerides compared to sucrose (b: 34.01 [6.59–61.44], P = 0.016). Triglycerides increased in the sucrose group (P = 0.023), while they decreased in the isomaltulose group. memory: A study compared 8 cm and 4 cm pillows during tracheal intubation on discomfort scores. memory: A study compared telemonitored clinical care (TCC) to usual care on patients’ likelihood to continue using CPAP. text: Frovatriptan significantly reduced the cumulative hazard of recurrence during follow-up for menstrually related migraine compared to rizatriptan (p < 0.01). After 24 hours, recurrence rates were 10% for frovatriptan versus 32% for rizatriptan [PMC3208043].
outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine

memory: Source article [PMC1784771]: Compared "Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators" with "Prostaglandin gel" on "Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours." 17 patients received prostaglandin alone, 23 received prostaglandin plus dilators. No demographic differences. After 6 hours, the combined group had a greater Bishop score change (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007). Combined therapy also showed a trend toward shorter induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hours, P=0.085). However, the combined group had a significantly higher infection rate (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003). Conclusion: Combined therapy offers more effective cervical ripening and faster induction but with increased infection risk.
text: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators resulted in a greater Bishop score change (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) compared to prostaglandin gel alone after 6 hours (PMC1784771). However, this combination increased infection risk (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003).
intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours

memory: In a study comparing ILF (Irinotecan with high-dose 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin) and ELF (Etoposide with 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin), grade 3/4 digestive system toxic events were more common with ILF. Specifically, 18% of ILF patients experienced grade 3/4 diarrhoea, while no such events were reported in the ELF group. Withdrawals due to toxicity were similar (5 ILF, 3 ELF), though not directly linked to digestive toxicity. Haematological toxicities were low, except for neutropenia (57% in ELF). Alopecia was more frequent in ELF (28%) compared to ILF (5%). Source: [PMC2361806].
text: The ILF regimen was associated with a higher incidence of grade 3/4 digestive system toxic events, particularly diarrhoea (18% vs. 0% in ELF). Source: [PMC2361806].

Source: [PMC4610775]  
Intervention: Urinary kallidinogenase (UK) vs. Control.  
Outcome: Amyloid betas 1-40 (Aβ1-40).  
At 4 weeks, UK reduced Aβ1-40 serum levels with improved cognition, while Aβ1-42 remained stable. memory: Source [PMC4869362] evaluated TCA and KOH for skin texture improvement. Both improved hydration and texture over time, though TCA showed reduced hydration and texture at D14. KOH improved elasticity, while TCA caused reduced elasticity. At D7, TCA significantly outperformed KOH in texture (p = 0.00). Callus surface area decreased in both by D14 and D21, except for TCA at D7. Plantar skin showed increased hydration and texture but decreased elasticity over time. No significant differences in hydration or elasticity were found between groups at each time point.
text: Both Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) and Potassium hydroxide (KOH) improved skin texture and hydration over time. At D7, TCA significantly outperformed KOH in texture (p = 0.00). However, TCA showed reduced hydration and elasticity compared to KOH. Source: [PMC4869362].

memory: The study compared FEC (4–6 cycles) and PE regimens in neoadjuvant chemotherapy, focusing on neutropenia frequency. intervention: receive 4–6 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy with tri-weekly 5-fluorouracil–epirubicin–cyclophosphamide (FEC) regimen

memory: In study [PMC4628236], cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic mice compared to placebo. These findings suggest that cinaciguat mitigates nitro-oxidative stress and restores antioxidant enzyme expression in diabetic myocardium.

memory: Study [PMC1468428] evaluated 1 litre saline enema vs. no enema on puerperal and neonatal infection rates. No significant differences were observed: puerperal infection was 22% with enema vs. 14% without (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43–1.03); neonatal infection was 20% with enema vs. 22% without (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76–1.66). Labour time and episiorraphy dehiscence rates were similar. Follow-up was 86% at one month.
text: A 1 litre saline enema did not significantly affect puerperal or neonatal infection rates compared to no enema (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43–1.03 for puerperal; RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76–1.66 for neonatal) [PMC1468428].

memory: Source [PMC3648394]: A 10-week yoga program significantly improved flexibility (sit & reach test) in the experimental group compared to control (p < 0.001). text: A 10-week yoga program significantly improved flexibility (sit & reach test) compared to control (p < 0.001) [PMC3648394].

memory: A study found no significant difference between Istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg in their effect on daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia. text: No significant difference was found between Istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg on daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia. memory: Oral liarozole (150 mg) significantly improved 'daily activities' (P = 0.008), 'leisure' (P = 0.026), and 'symptoms and feelings' (P = 0.023) compared to placebo, as reported in [PMC4232915]. text: Oral liarozole (150 mg) significantly improved 'daily activities' (P = 0.008), 'leisure' (P = 0.026), and 'symptoms and feelings' (P = 0.023) compared to placebo, as reported in [PMC4232915]. These results indicate a positive impact on patients' functioning and quality of life.

memory: A study compared 15-pulse ATP with eight-pulse ATP in 14 patients with FVT episodes, evaluating syncope and near-syncope as secondary endpoints. text: A study found no significant difference in syncope and near-syncope episodes between 15-pulse and eight-pulse ATP (p = 0.690). Source: [PMC2836470].

memory: Prednisolone 30 mg once daily reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis by 34 ± 6% compared to placebo (PMC3131514), while 7.5 mg reduced it by 11 ± 5%. text: Prednisolone 30 mg once daily reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis by 34 ± 6% compared to placebo (PMC3131514), while 7.5 mg reduced it by 11 ± 5%. Both doses showed a similar trend in decreasing fasted-state lipolysis (p = 0.062).

memory: The study compared online and mailed paper questionnaires among married participants. Married individuals were more common in the online group (P=.043). text: Married subjects were more prevalent in the online group (P=.043). The study found no significant difference in return rates between online and mailed questionnaires after adjusting for marital status and asthma. Source: [PMC1550608].

memory: A study found no significant differences in subjective stress markers between using one's own Facebook profile and quietly reading at any time point (p < 0.05) [PMC5610684]. text: Using one's own Facebook profile had no significant effect on subjective stress markers compared to quietly reading (p < 0.05) [PMC5610684]. Both conditions showed comparable stress responses, including cortisol levels, indicating no difference in stress recovery.

memory: Source [PMC4823408]: Compared 8 cm vs. 4 cm pillows during tracheal intubation. No difference in laryngeal view or number of trials. Discomfort score was higher in the 8 cm group during sequence I. text: Using an 8 cm pillow during tracheal intubation resulted in a higher discomfort score compared to a 4 cm pillow (PMC4823408). No differences were found in laryngeal view or number of trials, but one patient needed to switch to the 4 cm pillow after failed attempts.

memory: Source [PMC4947329]: Daily prednisone significantly reduced Procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP) compared to placebo in a dose- and time-dependent manner. text: Daily prednisone significantly reduced Procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP) compared to placebo in a dose- and time-dependent manner, with greater reductions observed at higher doses (Source: PMC4947329).

memory: In a study comparing 1,800 mg and 1,000 mg doses of gepotidacin in healthy volunteers, 64% of subjects experienced moderate adverse events with the higher dose versus 46% with the lower dose. text: The 1,800 mg dose of gepotidacin in healthy volunteers was associated with a higher incidence of moderate adverse events (64%) compared to the 1,000 mg dose (46%). Events included vomiting, nausea, throat tightness, and dizziness. Source: [PMC5404516].

memory: A study compared facial affect training (FAT) with treatment as usual (TAU) in schizophrenia patients using 20 daily 1-hour sessions. memory: A study found music therapy improved cognitive performance, as indicated by reduced completion time on the Japanese Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (p = 0.026), and improved behavioral outcomes with decreased Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores (p = 0.042). memory: A study compared RCF with RF and RC. Groups were similar in demographics and block characteristics. RCF showed no significant differences in analgesic effects or hemodynamic parameters compared to RF and RC (P>0.05). However, RCF significantly reduced side effects (P<0.05), enhancing patient comfort. Nausea/vomiting was 40% in RF, 15% in RC, and 10% in RCF. Sedation rates were 30% in RF, 10% in RC, and 5% in RCF. Dry mouth was more common in RC. Other side effects were comparable. Vital parameters and side effects were detailed in figures and tables.
text: The effect of Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine compared to Ropivacaine-fentanyl on hemodynamic parameters showed no significant differences (P>0.05). Source: Study comparing RCF with RF and RC.

memory: Low GI reduced post-meal glycemic response (GR) (p=0.02 for breakfast, lunch; p=0.05 for dinner) and daily AUC (p=0.03). memory: A study compared laryngeal mask (PLMA) and endotracheal intubation (ETT) and found no significant differences in demographic, hemodynamic, or respiratory parameters (p > 0.05). Adrenalin, noradrenalin, and dopamine levels also showed no significant differences between or within groups. However, serum cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation were significantly lower in the PLMA group compared to ETT (p = 0.024). Within groups, cortisol levels after CO2 insufflation were significantly higher than after anaesthesia induction (p = 0.001). These results suggest PLMA may induce a less pronounced stress response compared to ETT, as indicated by cortisol levels. Data in Tables 4 and 5. Source: [PMC3525032].
text: Compared to baseline, both PLMA and ETT increased cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation (p = 0.001). However, PLMA resulted in significantly lower cortisol levels than ETT (p = 0.024), suggesting a reduced stress response. Source: [PMC3525032].
outcome: cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation

memory: A study [PMC4776564] compared hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs to no intervention. The intervention group showed significantly higher quality of life (QOL) scores in satisfaction and importance immediately post-intervention (70.7 vs. 59.2, 73.6 vs. 65.7) and 1 month later (75.2 vs. 59.4, 76.3 vs. 66.8) (P < 0.05). Baseline demographics and QOL scores were similar between groups. Post-intervention, significant differences in QOL scores were observed in the study group across multiple dimensions (performance, health, socioeconomic, psychological, spiritual, familial) and areas of satisfaction and importance (P < 0.05). Repeated measures ANOVA also showed significant changes in the control group over time.
text: The study [PMC4776564] found that baseline characteristics, including demographics and QOL scores, were similar between the hope-promoting religious intervention group and the no-intervention group.
intervention: Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs

memory: Butoconazole (Gynazole-1) demonstrated faster symptom relief than fluconazole (Diflucan) for vaginal infections. Median time to first relief was 17.5 h (butoconazole) vs. 22.9 h (fluconazole; p < 0.001). At 75% relief, times were 24.5 h vs. 46.3 h (p < 0.001). By 24 h, 72.8% of patients on butoconazole vs. 55.7% on fluconazole achieved relief (p = 0.024). No significant differences in total relief or 30-day reinfection rates. Butoconazole had fewer adverse events, with common side effects including pruritus and burning.
text: Butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream provides faster relief of symptoms compared to oral fluconazole 150 mg tablets. The median time to first relief was 17.5 hours (butoconazole) versus 22.9 hours (fluconazole; p < 0.001).
intervention: butoconazole nitrate 2% Site Release vaginal cream (Gynazole-1)
outcome: The median time to first relief of symptoms

memory: Green tea ingestion significantly increased post-exercise (p < 0.01) and resting (p < 0.05) fat oxidation compared to placebo. Pre-exercise fat oxidation rose by 20% in both trained and untrained groups (p < 0.01), while post-exercise fat oxidation increased by 15% (p < 0.01). Plasma epinephrine levels were higher during and after exercise under green tea conditions. Plasma glycerol levels increased significantly in both groups, with higher levels in untrained individuals (p < 0.05). Norepinephrine levels were significantly higher in untrained individuals during and after exercise (p < 0.05).
text: Green tea significantly increases post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo (p < 0.01). It also elevates plasma epinephrine and glycerol levels, suggesting enhanced lipolysis. This effect is consistent in both trained and untrained individuals.

memory: A 2001–2002 trial compared artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) and mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) in 490 patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria. Both regimens had similar PCR-adjusted cure rates by day 42 (98.8% vs. 96.3%). MAS3 caused a greater decrease in haematocrit at day 7 (9.3% vs. 6.7%, P=0.023) and fewer P. vivax cases (29 vs. 90, P<0.001). Adverse events were similar, with no serious events reported. New P. falciparum infections were comparable (27 vs. 24, P>0.05). [PMC1261533]
text: In a 2001–2002 trial, artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) was associated with more P. vivax parasitaemia cases during follow-up compared to mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) (90 vs. 29, P<0.001). [PMC1261533]
outcome: P. vivax parasitaemia diagnosed during follow up

memory: Robotic BABA thyroidectomy had longer operative time (118.8 ± 16.5 vs. 90.7 ± 10.3 min, P < 0.05) compared to conventional open. No significant differences in blood loss, hospital stay, lymph nodes removed, thyroglobulin, or complications (P > 0.05). Robotic group showed better VAS (2.1 ± 1.0 vs. 3.8 ± 1.2, P < 0.05) and NSS (8.9 ± 0.8 vs. 4.8 ± 1.7, P < 0.05) scores. Subclinical central lymph node metastasis rate was 35%, with no conversion to open surgery. Cosmetic outcomes were satisfactory in robotic group. No iatrogenic implantation or metastasis in either group. Complication rates were similar between groups.
text: Thyroidectomy via BABA showed better Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores (2.1 ± 1.0 vs. 3.8 ± 1.2, P < 0.05) compared to conventional open thyroidectomy, indicating less postoperative pain.

memory: In a study comparing intubation methods, the WEI JET group had significantly longer intubation times (110.8±18.3 s) than the lightwand-only (LW) group (63.3±27.5 s, p=0.000) and direct laryngoscopy (DL) group (66.7±29.4 s, p=0.000). WEI JET showed higher lowest SpO2 compared to other groups. WEI JET also had fewer successful intubation attempts than LW (1.0±0 vs. 1.21±0.4, p=0.043). No differences in intubation time or attempts were found between LW and DL groups. Source: [PMC4372550].
text: The "lightwand only" method had a higher number of successful tracheal intubation attempts compared to "lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy" (1.21±0.4 vs. 1.0±0, p=0.043). Source: [PMC4372550].
comparator: lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy

memory: A 48-week trial compared VitD/Cal to placebo, finding no significant differences in glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, BMI, or metabolic syndrome prevalence. Both groups showed increased total and HDL cholesterol, with no inter-group differences. LDL cholesterol increased in the placebo group at week 24 but not week 48. VitD/Cal significantly elevated 25(OH)D levels at both timepoints, while placebo showed no change. Waist circumference increased in the placebo group but not in VitD/Cal, though differences were not significant. Low HDL prevalence decreased, while elevated TG prevalence increased over time.
text: Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation significantly increased 25(OH)D levels compared to placebo at both 24 and 48 weeks (source: 48-week trial).

memory: A study compared cilostazol (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks) to placebo and found that cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, 95% CI 10.65 to 199.71; P = 0.0003). No significant changes were observed in baPWV (mean difference 31.42 cm/sec, 95% CI −55.67 to 118.5) or other markers such as hsCRP, adiponectin, IL-6, TNF-α, MCP-1, and sICAM-1. Source: [PMC3733748].
text: Cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to placebo (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, 95% CI 10.65 to 199.71; P = 0.0003). No significant changes were observed in other markers. Source: [PMC3733748].
intervention: cilostazol group (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks)
outcome: soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) level

memory: A study compared computer-assisted learning (CAL) with an information leaflet, revealing that CAL significantly improved retention performance (p=0.02, effect size=0.8) and enjoyment (p=0.04, effect size=0.7) compared to the control group. No significant difference was found in confidence to identify autism (p=0.39, effect size=-0.3). CAL also enhanced retention in co-morbidities (p=0.02, effect size=0.9) and treatment (p=0.003, effect size=1.2) subcategories. These findings are from source article [PMC2652457].
text: Computer-assisted learning significantly increased the level of enjoyment compared to the control group (p=0.04, effect size=0.7) according to [PMC2652457].

memory: Spiromax outperformed Easyhaler and Turbuhaler in most features (p<0.001), except 'inhaling procedure' where no significant difference was found. Turbuhaler had better PIL instructions than Easyhaler (p<0.003), while Easyhaler had clearer dose counter (p<0.015). Spiromax showed higher device mastery (93.3%) compared to Easyhaler (58.3%) and Turbuhaler (76.7%) after reading PIL (p<0.001). Mastery was high with all devices after HCP instructions. No significant differences were found between Easyhaler and Turbuhaler for most features. Source: [PMC4809147].
text: Spiromax showed better overall ease of use, preparing the dose, and device mastery compared to Easyhaler and Turbuhaler (p<0.001). Turbuhaler had better PIL instructions than Easyhaler (p<0.003), while Easyhaler had clearer dose counter (p<0.015). No significant differences were found between Easyhaler and Turbuhaler for most features. Source: [PMC4809147].
outcome: ‘overall ease of use’, ‘quality of PIL instructions’, ‘preparing the dose’,  ‘clarity of dose counter’

memory: Cingal showed greater pain reduction than Monovisc and saline (P < .05) in the anteromedial subgroup at 3 weeks, with no difference between Monovisc and saline (P > .05). At 1 week, Cingal improved function vs. saline only in the anteromedial subgroup. No significant differences in stiffness scores at 26 weeks. Cingal's pain reduction was significant only in the anteromedial subgroup. Anteromedial and anterolateral injection techniques showed greater pain reduction than lateral midpatellar at 18 and 26 weeks across all therapies. Post hoc power at 12 weeks: 55% (AL), 38% (AM), 43% (LM) [PMC5560514].
text: Monovisc showed no significant difference from saline in pain reduction up to 3 weeks in the anteromedial subgroup (P > .05). Cingal demonstrated greater pain reduction than both Monovisc and saline in this subgroup (P < .05). Source: PMC5560514.
outcome: pain reduction up to 3 weeks in patients with knee osteoarthritis - anteromedial subgroup

memory: The phone calls group had fewer treatment discontinuations (4 vs. 30; p<0.0094) compared to the no phone calls group. No significant difference in controlled BP (<140/90 mmHg) between groups. BP control improved by the end of treatment (74%), with 80% in uncomplicated and 67% in complicated groups (p<0.000001). Only 29% achieved <120/80 mmHg. At visit 7, 90% (uncomplicated) and 66% (complicated) had BP <140/90 mmHg. The phone calls group showed better BP control (80%) vs. no phone calls (71%), though not statistically significant.
text: The "phone calls" group had fewer treatment discontinuations (4 vs. 30; p<0.0094) compared to the "no phone calls" group.

memory: A study (n=31 vs. n=33) compared skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding with no contact. Skin-to-skin contact was associated with significantly shorter median time to latching-on (2.0 vs. 4.7 weeks, p=0.020) and higher Breastfeeding Emotional Scale scores (69.2 vs. 62.4, p=0.022). No significant differences were found in latching-on proportions (75% vs. 86%, p=0.217) or median age at latching-on (7.7 vs. 7.1 weeks, p=0.919). Source: PMC3606616.
text: Skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding is associated with a significantly shorter median time to latching-on (2.0 vs. 4.7 weeks, p=0.020) compared to no contact (PMC3606616).
comparator: no skin-to-skin contact during the breastfeeding
outcome: registered time when infants began latching on

memory: [PMC3785973] IBSM improved asthma-related quality of life (AQLQ) at 12 months (0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.61) and 30 months (0.29, 95% CI 0.01-0.57). Asthma control improved at 12 months (-0.57, 95% CI -0.88 to -0.26) and 30 months (-0.33, 95% CI -0.61 to -0.05). No changes in FEV1 or inhaled corticosteroid use. Greater ACQ score improvements were seen in engaged participants (0.43 vs. 0.34).
text: Internet-based self-management support did not significantly affect inhaled corticosteroid dosage (PMC3785973).

memory: A 12-month study compared Basic and Enhanced web-based weight loss maintenance (WLM) programs in 227 adults (mean age 42.3, BMI 30.4). No significant differences in attrition (18.4% vs. 23.9%, p=0.31) or BMI change (−0.5 kg/m², p=0.93) were found between groups. Both showed minimal weight rebound (1.3% and 1.5%, respectively). The Enhanced program included personalized e-feedback but offered limited additional benefits over the Basic program. The web-based WLM was effective in preventing weight regain, with no significant between-group differences in primary or secondary outcomes. Source: PMC5746685.
text: The Enhanced weight loss maintenance program did not significantly differ from the Basic program in preventing weight rebound after 12 months (1.3% vs. 1.5%, p=0.93). Both programs showed minimal weight regain, with no significant between-group differences. Source: PMC5746685.

memory: Single sustained inflation (SI) increased carotid blood flow (CaBF) more rapidly than conventional ventilation and multiple SI (p = 0.01), but CaBF dropped below other groups by 10 minutes due to higher cerebral oxygen delivery (p = 0.01). Single SI also increased blood-brain barrier disruption, evidenced by more plasma protein extravasation in cerebral cortex blood vessel profiles (p = 0.001). No differences in CaBF or cerebral oxygen delivery were found between multiple SI and no SI groups. Source: [PMC4713062].
text: Single sustained inflation (SI) significantly increased plasma protein extravasation in cerebral cortex blood vessel profiles compared to conventional ventilation and multiple SI (p = 0.001). Source: [PMC4713062].
outcome: numbers of blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation

memory: Source: [PMC5539943]. MI knowledge increased significantly (b=0.111, p<0.001) with no condition differences (p=0.186). MI-LEAF had lower sustain talk (ST) reflections than MI-AU (b=-0.257, p=0.025), but change talk (CT) did not differ (p=0.703). At 3-month follow-up, MI-LEAF showed significantly lower client ST (b=-0.1008, p<0.001), while CT remained similar (p=0.355). Across time points, ST was lower in MI-LEAF (b=-0.175, p=0.046), but CT did not differ (p=0.781).
text: The MI-LEAF condition significantly reduced sustain talk (ST) compared to baseline (b=-0.1008, p<0.001) and MI-AU (b=-0.257, p=0.025) at follow-up, with lower ST across time points (b=-0.175, p=0.046). Change talk (CT) did not differ significantly. Source: [PMC5539943].
intervention: Language Enhanced Attention and Focus MI training condition (MI-LEAF)

memory: Source [PMC3658388]: LLLT vs. placebo showed no significant differences in TEOAE PTA (F(2,31)=0.133, P=0.876) or HFA (F(2,31)=0.20, P=0.819) via ANOVA. Kruskal-Wallis also found no median differences for TEOAE HFA (Kw(2)=4.04, P=0.133). For PTA and HFA, ANOVA results were non-significant (F(2,57)=0.09, P=0.913; F(2,57)=1.33, P=0.274). Assumptions: third met, fourth likely violated. Results detailed in Tables 2, 3, 6, 7.
text: Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) showed no significant effect compared to placebo on TEOAE PTA (F(2,31)=0.09, P=0.913) (PMC3658388).

memory: Vildagliptin vs. placebo: HGP suppression similar (42.2% vs. 54.7%, P = .89). ALT decreased with vildagliptin (27.2 to 20.3 IU/L, P = .0007), correlating with liver fat (r = 0.83). HbA1c dropped −0.5% (P < .0001) vs. +0.2% in placebo (P = .14). Liver triglycerides fell 27% (7.3% to 5.3%, P = .013). Fasting plasma glucose decreased −1.0 mmol/L (P = .018), correlating with liver triglycerides (r = 0.47–0.44). Placebo showed no significant changes.
text: Vildagliptin significantly reduced HbA1c by −0.5% (P < .0001) compared to placebo, where HbA1c increased by +0.2% (P = .14). This indicates a beneficial effect of vildagliptin on glycated hemoglobin.

memory: Both PAR and CAL reduced bone turnover markers (osteocalcin, bone alkaline phosphatase, C-terminal telopeptide) after 6 months, with no group differences. FGF23 decreased in both, with a greater reduction in CAL. BMD remained unchanged. PAR significantly lowered serum iPTH (76 ± 55 vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036). ≥30% iPTH reduction rates were 95.1% (PAR) vs. 88.4% (CAL; P = 0.26). Fewer PAR patients had iPTH >110 pg/ml (19.6% vs. 36.2%; P = 0.07), with a significant difference in per-protocol analysis (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008).
text: Paricalcitol significantly reduced serum iPTH levels compared to Calcifediol (76 ± 55 vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036). Fewer PAR patients had iPTH >110 pg/ml (19.6% vs. 36.2%; P = 0.07), with a significant difference in per-protocol analysis (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008).

memory: A VH-IVUS study compared nebivolol and atenolol. Nebivolol increased plaque area (P<0.001), while atenolol showed plaque regression (P=0.047), though the difference between groups was not significant (P=0.27). Nebivolol had lower EEM (P=0.02) and lumen areas (P=0.004) than atenolol. Plaque components and TCFAs were similar. Serial remodeling differed significantly (P=0.002), with nebivolol showing more constrictive remodeling (73% vs. 46%) and less excessive expansive remodeling (16% vs. 39%). Static remodeling was similar. Source: [PMC4859395]
text: Nebivolol and atenolol had similar effects on plaque components and TCFAs per vessel. Source: [PMC4859395].
outcome: plaque components and number of TCFAs per vessel

memory: In a study comparing tetraplegic patients (with and without 2 mg melatonin for 4 days) to able-bodied men, circadian F1+2 showed increased variation in tetraplegic groups (P=0.01 and P<0.001), while D-dimer patterns were similar (P>0.05). Absolute F1+2 and D-dimer concentrations were similar across groups (P>0.05). Activated FVII was higher in able-bodied subjects (P<0.05), with no melatonin effect. Circadian PAI-1 and TFPI variations were not significantly different (P>0.05). Melatonin did not alter sleep duration or quality in tetraplegic patients.
text: Tetraplegic patients exhibited increased circadian variation of F1+2 compared to able-bodied men (P=0.01 and P<0.001), with no effect of 2 mg melatonin over 4 days.
intervention: 2 mg of melatonin given 4 days for tetraplegic patients and placebo for tetraplegic patients

memory: Baseline MRDR values were similar between intervention (0.032, 0.025–0.038) and control (0.031, 0.024–0.038) groups. Post-intervention, TBS (436 vs. 434 μmol) and liver retinol (0.82 vs. 0.79 μmol/g) were comparable, indicating adequate vitamin A reserves. No significant differences in anthropometric indices or anemia rates (23.5% vs. 31.6%) were observed between groups. Source: [PMC4780150].
text: The effect of "Sachets of 'Sprinkles' with vitamin A" compared to those without on baseline MRDR values showed no significant difference, as baseline MRDR values were similar between groups (0.032 vs. 0.031). Source: [PMC4780150].

memory: Study [PMC3480782] evaluated Ciclesonide (CIC) and Fluticasone propionate (FLP) in 58% male patients, median age 32, with 24-month symptom duration. Patients preferred FLP over CIC for sensory attributes (55.41% vs. 25.68%, P=0.007), primarily due to less nasal irritation (1.35% vs. 28.38%, P=0.002) and fewer sneezing urges (1.35% vs. 13.51%). CIC showed less immediate taste, aftertaste, run down to throat, and run off from nose, but these differences were not statistically significant. No significant efficacy differences were observed between the treatments.
text: Patients preferred Fluticasone propionate (FLP) over Ciclesonide (CIC) as a preferred intranasal corticosteroid due to less nasal irritation and sneezing urges (PMC3480782). No significant efficacy differences were observed between the two.

memory: A 36-month study compared Superion® and X-STOP® for moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis. Superion® showed a higher success rate (52.5% vs. 38.0%, P=0.023) and consistent performance across primary endpoints (81–91%). X-STOP® exhibited a modest decline in clinical success between 24 and 36 months. Superion® demonstrated better durability in pain severity and functional outcomes, with significant improvement in leg pain. X-STOP® had higher rates of reoperations, revisions, and removals. Overall, Superion® provided more sustained clinical success and fewer complications over 36 months.
text: Superion® (52.5%) showed a higher success rate than X-STOP® (38.0%, P=0.023) in achieving the primary composite endpoint for moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis over 36 months, with better durability and fewer complications.
outcome: subjects achieving the primary composite endpoint - moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis.

memory: [PMC5897859] Vonoprazan 10/20 mg showed similar safety profiles to lansoprazole 15 mg (AEs: 10.4%/10.3% vs 11.4%). EE recurrence at 24 weeks was 16.8% (lansoprazole), 5.1% (vonoprazan 10 mg), 2.0% (vonoprazan 20 mg). Vonoprazan was non-inferior to lansoprazole (P < 0.0001). No significant difference in EE recurrence between vonoprazan doses (P = 0.1090). No clinically significant changes in labs, ECG, or vital signs. Baseline characteristics were well-matched across groups. Compliance >97% in all groups.
text: Vonoprazan 10 mg and 20 mg showed lower erosive esophagitis (EE) recurrence rates (5.1% and 2.0%) compared to lansoprazole 15 mg (16.8%) after 24 weeks (P < 0.0001). No significant difference between vonoprazan doses (P = 0.1090). Safety profiles were similar. [PMC5897859]
outcome: Erosive esophagitis recurrence rate after 24 weeks

memory: In study A, FBC and SFC increased FEV1 by 0.22 L and 0.25 L, respectively (p < 0.001) vs. placebo. In study B, FEV1 decline slopes were -16.0 ml/hr (SFC) and -14.2 ml/hr (FBC), with 24-hr AUC of 0.21 and 0.22 Lxmin. Morning PEF improved by 25 L/min for both. Median days without relief medication were 63% (SFC) and 61% (FBC); nights were 93% (SFC) and 89% (FBC). No significant differences between SFC and FBC for these parameters (PMC1570354).
text: Formoterol/budesonide (FBC) and salmeterol/fluticasone propionate (SFC) showed similar effects on the median number of days with no use of relief medication (61% vs. 63%, respectively; PMC1570354). No significant differences were observed between the two treatments.
outcome: the median number of days with no use of relief medication

memory: A study compared Andrographis paniculata to placebo in patients, showing a significant 44% reduction in Fatigue Severity Scores (FSS) at 12 months. No significant differences were observed in relapse rate, EDSS, or inflammatory markers, though a trend toward fewer new lesions was noted in the A. paniculata group. One patient had a mild, transient skin rash managed with anti-histamines for three weeks. Source: [PMC4877819]
text: Andrographis paniculata significantly reduced Fatigue Severity Scores by 44% compared to placebo after 12 months, with no major adverse effects. Source: [PMC4877819]

memory: Source: [PMC4731690]. Extensive hyperacute stroke (HAS) was associated with worse 6-month outcomes (OHS; OR 0.61, p=0.027) and poor outcomes (OR 0.66, p<0.001). Alteplase improved HAS shrinkage (OR 0.77, p=0.006), with no effect from HAS location (p=0.516) or extent (p=0.580). Age correlated with HAS growth (OR 1.01, p=0.013). No interaction between HAS presence and alteplase benefit on OHS (p=0.167).
text: More extensive hyperdense artery sign (HAS) was associated with worse 6-month outcomes (OHS; OR 0.61, p=0.027) compared to less extensive HAS, according to [PMC4731690].

memory: Study [PMC5426232] compared DEB + BMS vs ZES in 180 patients. Follow-up angiography at 298 days showed 81.1% completion. Baseline characteristics were similar. DEB + BMS had significantly higher late luminal loss (LL) (0.50 ± 0.46 vs 0.21 ± 0.44 mm; P < 0.001). Mean LL difference was 0.31 mm (CI: 0.15–0.48), exceeding non-inferiority margin (0.19 mm). Non-inferiority not met (P = 0.138). Binary restenosis rate higher in DEB + BMS (not statistically significant). Minimal luminal diameter and acute gain were lower in DEB + BMS. Clinical outcomes not significantly different.
text: In a study of 180 patients, DEB + BMS showed higher late luminal loss and minimal luminal diameter compared to ZES, with a mean LL difference exceeding the non-inferiority margin (P = 0.138). Binary restenosis rates were not statistically different (PMC5426232).

memory: A study compared nutrition psychoeducation (NPC), motivational interviewing (MIC), and usual care (UC). NPC significantly reduced BDI scores (p=0.009 vs UC) and lowered triglycerides (p=0.008). MIC showed no significant differences from UC in BDI or triglycerides. Both NPC and MIC had higher satisfaction scores (p<.0005) and were delivered as intended. At 3-month follow-up, BDI scores trended toward significance (p=.057) and weight loss (≥5%) was similar between NPC and MIC. High fidelity and adherence were observed, with adherence correlating with weight loss. No significant differences were found between MIC and UC in BDI or triglycerides.
text: Nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) significantly lowers triglyceride levels compared to usual care (p=0.008). Motivational interviewing (MIC) showed no significant effect on triglycerides.

memory: Two groups compared: 10-mm transumbilical vs. 5-mm transabdominal. No complications; all patients discharged on POD 1 with 3-month follow-up. Similar satisfaction (9.2±0.6 vs. 9.5±0.6, P=0.69) and cosmetic outcomes (9.6±0.5 vs. 9.8±0.4, P=0.74). Transumbilical group had shorter specimen retrieval time (43.5±14.5 s vs. 69.4±20.5 s, P<0.001). Rescue analgesia needed in 4 vs. 3 patients. Intact tubes found in 18 vs. 3 cases (P<0.001, OR: 51.0). No intraoperative retrieval bag rupture.
text: The 10-mm transumbilical group had significantly more intact tubes (18 vs. 3, P<0.001, OR: 51.0) compared to the 5-mm transabdominal group.

memory: A study compared Stracos titanium rib fixation with a control group, finding no significant differences in injury severity scores. The surgical group showed significantly reduced ventilator time (142 ± 224 vs. 74 ± 125 hours, P = 0.026) and hospital stay (P = 0.026) after adjusting for prognostic scores. There was a trend toward shorter ICU stay (12.3 ± 8.5 vs. 9.0 ± 4.3 days, P = 0.076). Surgery was performed within 48 hours. Conclusion: Stracos rib fixation is feasible and reduces ventilator time and hospital stay. Source: [PMC4331314].
