text: Specially designed molding titanium clips (Stracos) reduced ventilator time (P = 0.026) and hospital stay (P = 0.026) compared to control, after adjusting for prognostic scores. Source: [PMC4331314].
outcome: Ventilator time and overall hospital stay

memory: A study compared CIMT combined with gait training to gait training alone. Groups were similar at baseline except for age. The CIMT group showed significant improvements in dynamic balance (28.6% increase on TIS) and paretic side movement distances (34.3% increase on LOS), which were greater than the control group showing no significant balance improvements. These results suggest CIMT enhances balance outcomes compared to gait training alone. Source: PMC4395675.
text: Gait training with CIMT significantly improves dynamic balance (28.6% increase on TIS) compared to gait training alone, which showed no significant improvements. CIMT also enhanced paretic side movement distances (34.3% increase on LOS). Source: PMC4395675.
intervention: Gait training with constrained induced movement therapy

memory: Apremilast 20/30 mg BID showed greater pruritus VAS reduction (P≤0.005) and higher rates of ≥MCID achievement (60.9-63.6%) vs. placebo (44.3%). MCS scores improved significantly (P<0.05) across 10/20/30 mg BID, exceeding MCID. DLQI scores improved more with 20/30 mg BID (-5.9/-4.4) vs. placebo (1.9; P≤0.005). PCS scores showed non-significant improvements. Baseline MCS scores were 0.5 SD below US norms.
text: Apremilast 20/30 mg BID significantly reduced pruritus VAS scores (P≤0.005) and improved MCID achievement (60.9-63.6%) compared to placebo (44.3%). MCS and DLQI scores also improved more with apremilast than placebo.

memory: Aprepitant triple regimen (aprepitant + tropisetron + dexamethasone) vs. standard (tropisetron + dexamethasone) showed higher complete response (CR) in overall phase (OP, 80.0% vs. 56.0%, P=0.018) and delay phase (DP, 80.0% vs. 56.0%, P=0.018). Acute phase (AP) CR rates were similar (98.0% in both, P=1.000). Male aprepitant group had higher CR (93.1%) than female (61.9%, P=0.011). Primary endpoint: OP CR. Secondary endpoints: AP and DP CR. Quality of life assessed via FLIE. Source: PMC5851005.
text: The aprepitant regimen (aprepitant + tropisetron + dexamethasone) showed a higher complete response (CR) in the delay phase (DP) compared to the standard regimen (tropisetron + dexamethasone) (80.0% vs. 56.0%, P=0.018). Source: PMC5851005.
intervention: the aprepitant regimen (aprepitant plus tropisetron and dexamethasone)
outcome: complete response (CR) in the delay phase (DP)

memory: [PMC4747995] Ch14.18-UTC and ch14.18-NCI showed comparable PK parameters (AUCinf 0.96 [0.88–1.04], Cmax 1.04 [0.98–1.11]), meeting bioequivalence criteria. Adverse events were similar, with pain-related TRAEs common: pain (59% UTC vs. 44% NCI), abdominal pain (48% vs. 41%), and extremity pain (33% vs. 41%). Most pain events occurred in cycles 1, 2, and 4.
text: Ch14.18-UTC and ch14.18-NCI had similar adverse event profiles (PMC4747995). Pain-related treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were common in both, with higher pain incidence in UTC (59% vs. 44%). Abdominal and extremity pain also showed comparable rates.

memory: Baseline vaginal practices showed 12.6% no practices, 31.8% one, 56.6% ≥2, with no group differences in washing, wiping, or insertion. Johannesburg had the highest washing (86.7%), while Zimbabwe had more wiping (68.0%). The intervention (diaphragm + gel) increased washing (AOR 1.35), wiping (AOR 1.14), and soap/water use (AOR 1.23) during follow-up vs. control. All practices decreased over time. Washing, wiping, and insertion were inversely associated with diaphragm/gel and condom use. Cultural context may influence interventions.
text: At baseline, there were no group differences in vaginal practices between Johannesburg and Durban/Harare. Johannesburg had the highest washing rate (86.7%), but no significant differences in wiping or insertion. (Source: Working notes)

memory: A study compared CHG dressings to transparent dressings, finding CRBSI rates of 3 vs. 14 per 1,000 patients (highly significant, non-overlapping 95% CIs). ICU-days, days before discharge, and mortality were similar. The CRBSI ratio favored CHG 1:5. The mean cost difference per patient was €141 (95% CI: [€-975; €1,258], not statistically significant). The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was €12,046 per CRBSI prevented, with an incremental net monetary benefit of €344.88 per patient. Source: PMC4472776.
text: Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) dressings significantly reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) compared to transparent dressings (3 vs. 14 per 1,000 patients, PMC4472776). ICU-days, discharge timing, and mortality were similar, but CHG dressings showed better cost-effectiveness with an incremental net monetary benefit of €344.88 per patient.

memory: NIV vs. PSV in ICU showed no significant differences in MV duration (6.20 vs. 7.47 days, P>0.05), weaning duration (35.17 vs. 47.05 hours, P>0.05), or ICU stay (8.47 vs. 10.80 days, P>0.05). VAP occurred in 5 PSV vs. 1 NIV patients. ICU mortality was 3 (20%) NIV vs. 5 (33.33%) PSV; 30-day mortality was 5 vs. 9, P>0.05. Source: [PMC2856148].
text: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) compared with pressure support ventilation (PSV) showed no significant difference in weaning duration (35.17 vs. 47.05 hours, P>0.05). Source: [PMC2856148].

memory: A study compared case-based discussions (intervention) with standardized patient cases (control). No significant differences were found in total scores between groups (13.4 vs. 14.4, p = 0.12). Both groups scored higher in the third rotation compared to the first (13.6 vs. 15, p = 0.038). Analysis of 13 technology items showed no differences between intervention and control groups (7.5 vs. 7.9, p = 0.25) or between first and third rotation groups (7.3 vs. 8.3, p = 0.08). Source: [PMC1420296].
text: No significant effect was found of case-based discussions compared to standardized patient cases on total scores in the third rotation (13.4 vs. 14.4, p = 0.12). Source: [PMC1420296].
outcome: total scores in the third rotation scored

memory: An 18-patient study compared hydrodistension plus RTX to hydrodistension alone in interstitial cystitis (IC) patients. Both groups showed significant improvements in pain, frequency, and bladder capacity at 3 months. RTX did not enhance voiding symptoms or uroflowmetry. Baseline symptoms were similar, with all patients having prior ineffective treatments. Median age was 55.8±6.9 years, and symptom duration was 3.6±1.6 years. Source: [PMC3321403].
text: A study found that hydrodistension plus RTX did not improve voiding symptoms more than hydrodistension alone in IC patients. Both groups showed similar improvements in pain, frequency, and bladder capacity. Source: [PMC3321403].

memory: PVB group showed lower NRS pain scores at rest and during movement (P<0.05) within 24 hours post-op. They used less tramadol (200 mg vs. 300 mg, P=0.003) and no nurse-administered morphine compared to control (2.5 mg, P=0.001). First analgesic request was delayed in PVB (120 min vs. 30 min, P<0.05). No differences in BP, HR, RR, or SpO2 (P>0.05). Demographics showed similar gender distribution, with higher ASA I in PVB (26%) vs. control (40%).
text: Paravertebral block (PVB) significantly reduced NRS pain scores at rest and during movement post-op (P<0.05) compared to control. PVB also delayed first analgesic request and reduced tramadol use (200 mg vs. 300 mg, P=0.003). No differences in vital signs were observed. Source: Study comparing PVB and control.

memory: Home Monitoring (HM ON) reduced scheduled follow-up visits (3.79 vs. 5.53; P < 0.001) but increased unscheduled visits (0.95 vs. 0.62; P < 0.005) and non-office-based contacts (1.95 vs. 1.01; P < 0.001). It also increased in-clinic discussions (1.84 vs. 1.28; P < 0.03) and Internet sessions (11.02 vs. 0.06; P < 0.001). Actionable visits were higher in HM ON (32.0% vs. 26.8%; P < 0.05). No significant cost difference in follow-up was found. Finland's small sample size (two patients per group) limited monetary analysis.
text: Home Monitoring facilitated follow-up (HM ON) reduced scheduled visits (3.79 vs. 5.53; P < 0.001) but increased unscheduled visits and non-office contacts. It also enhanced in-clinic discussions and internet sessions. No significant cost difference was found. Source: Finland study.

memory: [PMC2928344] In a T1D trial, calcitriol vs. placebo showed no differences in A1C, insulin requirement, or C-peptide at 6, 12, or 24 months. C-peptide decreased similarly in both groups (P < 0.001). Fasting C-peptide decline after 12 months: 17.7% (calcitriol) vs. 28.4% (placebo). 47% had vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/ml). 25OHD levels increased slightly in calcitriol (+3.9%) and decreased in placebo (−8.0%). No adverse events. AUC0–120 min C-peptide not significantly different at baseline or 12 months. Vitamin D status did not affect β-cell function. Calcium and phosphate levels remained normal.
text: In a T1D trial, calcitriol showed no adverse events compared to placebo (PMC2928344). Both groups had similar safety profiles, with no significant differences in adverse events reported.

memory: Two studies (CaMEWS, D&Cancer) compared Vitamin D + Calcium vs. Calcium or Placebo. Baseline demographics and serum 25(OH)D, calcium were similar (P > 0.05). Vitamin D + Calcium significantly increased serum 25(OH)D by +24.31 and +31.92 nmol/L in CaMEWS and D&Cancer, respectively. Calcium only showed minimal changes (-1.02 and +0.36 nmol/L). Placebo changes mirrored Calcium. P < 0.0001 for Vitamin D + Calcium vs. others. Baseline 25(OH)D ranged 24.2-144.6 nmol/L (CaMEWS) and 13.3-225.8 nmol/L (D&Cancer).
text: Vitamin D + Calcium significantly increased serum 25(OH)D levels compared to Placebo or Calcium alone (CaMEWS: +24.31 nmol/L; D&Cancer: +31.92 nmol/L; P < 0.0001).

memory: Source: PMC5343026. A study compared classic cigarettes (C) with two e-cigarette types (H: 24 mg nicotine disposable; E: 24 mg liquid nicotine Ego C). Craving increased over time in C and H groups, while E group showed increased craving up to T3. Cognitive performance was unaffected by product type. Craving and smoking gestures were associated with ritualistic behavior. E-cigarettes may help reduce relapse by replacing smoking rituals. Trial: NCT01735487.
text: Classic cigarettes (C) and high-nicotine e-cigarettes (H) increased craving over time, while low-nicotine e-cigarettes (E) showed increased craving only up to T3 (PMC5343026). E-cigarettes may reduce relapse by replacing smoking rituals.

memory: A 28-day trial in T2DM patients showed that SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) reduced body weight by 0.93 kg (p=0.0236) but increased HbA1c by 0.48% (p=0.004). Bradykinin-induced vasodilatation was reduced (mean diff −1.291, p=0.012). No significant changes were seen in lipid profiles, platelet-monocyte activation, or responses to acetylcholine or sodium nitroprusside (p>0.05). Source: [PMC5588958].
text: In T2DM patients, 28 days of oral SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) reduced body weight by 0.93 kg (p=0.0236) compared to placebo, but increased HbA1c by 0.48% (p=0.004). Source: [PMC5588958].
outcome: body weight in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)

memory: [PMC5448649] showed that PPV/CPA (cyclophosphamide) induced stronger T cell responses and improved progression-free survival (6.1 vs 2.9 mo; HR: 0.427; P=0.008) and overall survival (12.1 vs 5.9 mo; HR: 0.376; P=0.004) compared to PPV alone. PPV alone increased plasma IL-6 post-vaccination, which correlated with reduced T cell responses (Spearman r=-0.703; P=0.007). No differences in IgG or IFN-γ spot numbers were observed. Elevated IL-6 in PPV alone may suppress antigen-specific T cells, suggesting low-dose CPA may counteract this immune suppression in aBTC patients.
text: Cyclophosphamide (CPA) improved progression-free survival compared to control (6.1 vs 2.9 months; HR: 0.427; P=0.008) in aBTC patients, according to [PMC5448649]. This effect may be due to enhanced T cell responses and reduced IL-6-mediated suppression.

memory: Study [PMC3258705] compared oestradiol (N=47) and progesterone-only (N=51) groups in IVF. No significant differences in oocyte retrieval, embryos transferred, or pregnancy rates. Oestradiol group had higher progesterone levels on days 7, 10, 12 post-transfer, but not statistically significant. Mean infertility duration was 5.98 vs 7.81 years, not significant. No significant LH differences. Higher serum progesterone/estradiol ratio in oestradiol group, but not significant. Of 25 oestradiol group patients with positive βhCG, 23 had intrauterine gestational sacs, 1 ectopic, 1 blighted ovum.
text: The study [PMC3258705] found no significant difference in mean infertility duration (5.98 vs. 7.81 years) between the oestradiol plus progesterone group and the progesterone-only group. Other outcomes like pregnancy rates were also not significantly different.
intervention: oestradiol group, 2 mg of oestradiol valerate was initiated orally with progesterone
comparator: the control group received vaginal administration of progesterone supplementation alone starting on the day after oocyte retrieval and continued until the tenth week if the chemical pregnancy test was positive

memory: A study of 22 premature infants randomized to paracetamol or ibuprofen found no significant differences in mortality, primary closure rates, or short-term neonatal outcomes. Sepsis occurred in 7 and 4 cases (p=0.664), surfactant therapy in 9 and 6 cases (p=0.898), and pulmonary hemorrhage in 1 case each (p=0.783). Results suggest comparable safety and efficacy between paracetamol and ibuprofen in this population. Source: PMC5971505.
text: A study found no significant difference between paracetamol and ibuprofen in surfactant therapy use in premature infants (p=0.898). Both drugs showed comparable safety and efficacy. Source: PMC5971505.

memory: Speed endurance training (SET) and small-sided games (SSG) did not alter PFK activity. Both increased α1 Na+–K+ ATPase (19% and 37%, P < 0.05), with a trend for greater change in SSG (P = 0.07). HAD activity rose 24% in both (P < 0.05). CS activity increased only in SET (18%, P < 0.05). MCT4 increased by 30% (SET) and 61% (SSG). SOD2 increased by 28% (SET) and 37% (SSG). GLUT-4 rose by 40% only in SSG. SET improved Yo–Yo IR2 by 39% more than SSG (P < 0.05).
text: Speed endurance training increased citrate synthase maximal activity by 18% (P < 0.05), while small-sided games did not. This suggests SET is more effective than SSG in enhancing CS activity. (Source: Working notes)

memory: rTMS (real or sham) significantly reduced cravings [F(1,9)=15.91, p=0.003], with no main effect of condition [F(1,9)=1.13, ns] or time-by-condition interaction [F(1,9)=0.13, ns]. No difference in hours since last meal between conditions [t(9)=0.52, ns]. Controlling for meal time, no effects on cravings [F(1,8)=2.97, ns; F(1,8)=1.94, ns; F(1,8)=2.07, ns]. Sham-TMS showed slightly larger craving reduction (d=0.09). Participants correctly guessed only 40% of sessions (p=0.27), suggesting sham condition matched real rTMS for face/scalp sensations.
text: Prefrontal rTMS and sham rTMS had similar effects on face and scalp sensations, as participants correctly guessed only 40% of sessions (p=0.27), indicating sham condition was effective in matching real rTMS for these sensations.

memory: A study compared haloperidol (H1: 1 mg, H2: 2 mg) with saline (H0) for PONV prevention. PONV incidence was 22% (H1) and 20% (H2) versus 42% (H0), with significant reduction in both haloperidol groups (P = 0.003), though H1 and H2 showed no significant difference. Sedation scores in the PACU over 2 hours were higher in H2 than in H1 and H0 (P < 0.001), with no difference between H1 and H0. Three H2 patients experienced hypotension (systolic 75–80/diastolic 50–55 mmHg) requiring ephedrine. Findings are presented in Table 2 and Fig. 2.
text: Both haloperidol doses (1 mg and 2 mg) significantly reduced PONV incidence compared to saline (22% vs. 42%, P=0.003). No difference was found between the two haloperidol doses. However, the 2 mg dose caused more sedation and hypotension. Source: Table 2 and Fig. 2.
outcome: the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV)

memory: A study evaluated sipuleucel-T with or without pTVG-HP DNA vaccine in 18 patients (11 completed). Th1-biased PAP-specific T-cell responses were similar between arms, but Arm 2 (pTVG-HP + sipuleucel-T) showed higher PAP antibody titers. Median time to progression was <6 months, with no inter-arm differences. Median overall survival was 715 days (Arm 1) vs. 901 days (Arm 2), not statistically significant. Two Arm 2 patients progressed at month 3 but stabilized until months 9–12. No differences in PSA kinetics or doubling times were observed; pre-treatment PSA doubling time was 2.55 months, unchanged post-treatment. The trial was underpowered to detect survival or progression differences.
text: In a small study, sipuleucel-T with pTVG-HP DNA vaccine showed a trend toward improved overall survival (715 vs. 901 days) compared to sipuleucel-T alone, but the difference was not statistically significant. The trial was underpowered to detect survival differences.
intervention: sipuleucel-T alone followed by intradermal immunization with pTVG-HP DNA vaccine

memory: In a study comparing selenium (Se) supplementation to placebo, Se significantly reduced sFlt-1 concentration (P=0.039) and halved the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio (P=0.066) in participants in the lowest quartile of baseline Se status. These effects were not observed in all participants combined. No significant differences were found in PlGF levels between Se and placebo (95% CI: 0.78–1.21, P=0.801). The results suggest Se may have a targeted effect on sFlt-1 and its ratio with PlGF in individuals with low baseline Se status. Data from Table 3 and the Results section support these findings.
text: Selenium supplementation significantly reduced sFlt-1 concentration (P=0.039) and halved the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio (P=0.066) in participants with low baseline selenium status, but not in all participants combined. No significant changes in PlGF levels were observed.
outcome: Soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (Overall)

memory: A study compared natural childbirth preparation with standard antenatal education, finding no significant differences in spontaneous vaginal delivery (66% in both groups; RR 1.0), emergency Caesarean (14% vs. 15%; RR 0.9), elective Caesarean (6% vs. 6%; RR 0.9), or childbirth experience or parental stress. Epidural use was 52% in both groups. More women in the natural childbirth group used psychoprophylaxis (70% vs. 37%), but this did not influence main outcomes. Source: PMC2759981.
text: A study found no significant difference between natural childbirth preparation and standard antenatal education on elective Caesarean rates (6% vs. 6%; RR 0.9). Source: PMC2759981.

memory: SP-based scenarios improved post-test scores compared to mannequin-based scenarios (4.53/5 vs 3.69/5, P=0.01), except for acute bacterial meningitis. SP scenarios showed greater score improvement (1.8/5 vs 1.2/5, P=0.01), with the highest gain in calcium channel blocker overdose (2.4/5 vs 1.3/5, P=0.03). SP scenarios also had higher realism scores (4.73/5 vs 2.00/5, P=0.002). Pre-test scores were similar between groups (2.56/5 vs 2.53/5). Nine residents completed mannequin scenarios, 10 SP scenarios. Results were significant in three of four scenarios (P=0.01).
text: SP-based scenarios significantly improved realism scores compared to mannequin-based scenarios (4.73/5 vs 2.00/5, P=0.002).

memory: In a trial of 2,793 women, SPAZ (SP+AZ) reduced low birthweight (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.60–0.91, P=0.005; ARR 4.5%), preterm delivery (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43–0.89, P=0.010), and maternal parasitaemia (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35–0.95, P=0.029), while increasing mean birthweight by 41.9 g (95% CI 0.2–83.6, P=0.049). No serious adverse events were treatment-related. [PMC4305224]
text: In a trial of 2,793 women, Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + azithromycin (SPAZ) reduced the risk of active placental malaria, as indicated by lower maternal parasitaemia (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35–0.95, P=0.029) compared to control. [PMC4305224]

memory: A study compared anesthetic interventions and their effects on postoperative nausea and vomiting. Nausea within 24 h was 55% in group I (sevoflurane alone), 42.5% in group II, 30% in groups III and V, and 27.5% in group IV. Groups III and V showed significantly lower nausea rates than group I (P < 0.05). Vomiting was lower in groups II (17.5%), IV (7.5%), and VI (10%) compared to group I (55%) and others (P < 0.05). Propofol alone or combined with sevoflurane reduced both vomiting and nausea compared to sevoflurane alone. Ondansetron reduced vomiting but not nausea across all anesthetic types. Source: [PMC3633335].
text: Sevoflurane + ondansetron significantly reduces vomiting compared to sevoflurane alone (7.5% vs. 55%, P < 0.05). Ondansetron alone reduces vomiting but not nausea. Source: [PMC3633335].

memory: A study compared PLTR and BLTR surgeries. No difference in intraoperative pain (p=0.84), but BLTR caused more post-op pain until suture removal (OR 1.46, p=0.004). BLTR had higher under-correction at 12 months (p<0.0001) and greater recurrence (22% vs 13%, OR 1.96, p=0.0001). No significant differences in satisfaction for trichiasis treatment (p=0.20) or cosmetic appearance (p=0.64). PLTR was faster (15 min 33 s vs 16 min 39 s). No effect modification by surgeon or other factors observed.
text: BLTR caused more post-operative pain until suture removal compared to PLTR (OR 1.46, p=0.004). No difference in intraoperative pain.
outcome: Pain between surgery and stitches removal

memory: Dovitinib had higher AE-related discontinuation (38.3% vs 8.0%) than placebo. Common discontinuation AEs included diarrhea (6.4% vs 0%), ALT increase (4.3% vs 2.0%), AST increase (4.3% vs 2.0%), and rash (4.3% vs 0%). Two on-treatment deaths occurred in the dovitinib group: one from breast cancer progression and one from suspected pulmonary embolism. Overall mortality was 29.8% in the dovitinib group vs 36.0% in the placebo group. Most dovitinib patients required dose reductions or interruptions (74.5% vs 26.0%). Source: PMC5301372.
text: Dovitinib caused higher discontinuation due to rash (4.3%) compared to placebo (0%) (PMC5301372).

memory: No serious adverse events; no significant differences in adverse events between vitamin D groups (DD, DP) and placebo (PP). Two cases of primary hyperparathyroidism excluded, one with elevated serum calcium (2.62 mmol/L). Four had transient calcium increases >2.59 mmol/L. Baseline 25(OH)D: 58 nmol/L; increased to 141 and 100 nmol/L in DD and DP groups. No significant changes in BMD (lumbar spine, hip), serum OPG, or RANKL after one year. PTH decreased in DD and DP groups. One PP subject had 11.3% BMD increase, one DD had 11.5% decrease. Most subjects showed no changes outside "least significant change." [PMC2818614]
text: No significant differences in adverse events were found between the vitamin D groups (DD, DP) and placebo (PP). No serious adverse events occurred, though some transient calcium increases were observed. [PMC2818614]
intervention: Vitamin D3 40.000 IU (DD group) or Vitamin D3 20.000 IU (DP group)

memory: A study compared LIPUS with standard implant treatment, showing significant FD-mesial increases after six months: 0.132 (control) vs. 0.342 (intervention), with effect sizes of 2.64 vs. 4.85. FD-distal also improved more in the intervention group. Post-surgery, FD and RF values were similar between groups, confirming randomization. RF values increased by 7.4 units in the intervention group (Cohen's d = 7.4), vs. 2.25 in the control. LIPUS enhanced implant outcomes with greater effect sizes over time. Source: PMC5925011.
text: The intervention group with added low-intensity power ultrasound treatment (LIPUS) showed significantly greater FD mesial values after six months (0.342) compared to the standard implant protocol (0.132), with a larger effect size (4.85 vs. 2.64). Source: PMC5925011.
intervention: intervention group with added low-intensity power ultrasound treatment (LIPUS)
outcome: FD mesial values after six months of follow-up

memory: A study compared postprandial flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) after a single serving of curry versus a spice-free control meal. The control meal led to a slight decrease in FMD (5.8 ± 2.4% to 5.1 ± 2.3%, P = 0.039), whereas the curry meal increased FMD (5.2 ± 2.5% to 6.6 ± 2.0%, P = 0.001). FMD was significantly higher after the curry meal compared to the control (P = 0.002). Spices in the curry did not significantly affect systemic and forearm hemodynamics or biochemical parameters, including oxidative stress markers (Source: PMC4082484).
text: A single serving of curry meal significantly increases flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal (P = 0.002). The control meal caused a slight decrease in FMD, while the curry meal improved it (Source: PMC4082484).

memory: Infliximab vs. ciclosporin in IBD showed no significant differences in quality-adjusted survival (CUCQ AUC: 564 vs 587; p=0.603), colectomy rates (OR 1.35; p=0.223), or time to colectomy (HR 1.23; p=0.251). Infliximab was more costly (£5632; p=0.001) but similar in effectiveness. No significant differences in serious adverse events (event ratio 0.938; p=0.788). Three infliximab-related deaths occurred, including two from sepsis and one from cancer. Renal impairment was more common with ciclosporin. No significant difference in quality-adjusted life-years (0.021; p=0.350).
text: Infliximab was more costly than ciclosporin (£5632; p=0.001) but showed similar effectiveness in treating IBD. No significant differences were found in colectomy rates, time to colectomy, or quality-adjusted survival. Renal impairment was more common with ciclosporin, while infliximab had more serious adverse events.

memory: A study compared NBUVB (9 J/cm² for 6 weeks) and prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in generalized lichen planus. Baseline disease duration was similar (p = 0.910). NBUVB demonstrated significantly better efficacy (p = 0.008) and higher patient satisfaction (p = 0.012) compared to systemic steroids. No significant side effects were reported in either group. Chi-square tests and ANOVA were used for statistical analysis, with results presented in Tables 1-3.
text: NBUVB (9 J/cm² for 6 weeks) significantly reduced disease duration compared to prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in generalized lichen planus (p = 0.008). NBUVB also showed higher patient satisfaction (p = 0.012) with no significant side effects.

memory: Exercise group showed significant increases in SUDS post-intervention (3.8±0.8 vs baseline 2.4±1.1; p=0.04) and post-rest (1.6±0.5; p=0.003), with no differences vs control. No significant PDSS changes (p=0.41). BAI scores decreased more in the exercise group (5.6±3.9 vs 0.1±2.3; p=0.02, ES=1.40). BDI-II scores also decreased significantly in the exercise group post-intervention (15.8±9.4 vs baseline 21.6±10.7; p=0.01), though no between-group differences were found (p=0.09). All data from [PMC5827302].
text: Exercise significantly reduced BAI scores compared to control (p=0.02, ES=1.40) [PMC5827302].

memory: In a study [PMC3546023], smokers exhibited higher urine cotinine and serum α1-antitrypsin levels than nonsmokers (p < 0.05). Both groups showed increased lymphocyte proliferation with 200 mg/day palmvitee. Smokers had lower NK cells and higher CD4+ and B cells compared to nonsmokers, with B cells increasing in nonsmokers on palmvitee. The CD4+/CD8+ ratio was higher in smokers. NK cells remained lower in smokers compared to nonsmokers at baseline and post-supplementation (p < 0.0001). Plasma tocopherol and tocotrienol levels increased in both groups after 12 weeks of palmvitee. Smokers had significantly higher urinary cotinine and α1-antitrypsin than nonsmokers (p < 0.05).
text: Smokers taking 200 mg/day palmvitee had lower NK cell percentages compared to nonsmokers (p < 0.0001), with no significant change post-supplementation. [PMC3546023]

memory: Lifestyle-induced weight loss in the ABC arm significantly reduced total BAs (−34.59%, p=0.007), CDCA (−52.38%, p=0.001), CA (−31.49%, p=0.018), and UDCA (−49.37%, p=0.002), primarily due to lower glycine/taurine conjugated BAs. Total GLP-1 decreased (p=0.003), correlating with metabolic improvements. The control arm showed no changes in BAs, GLP-1, or FGF-19. ABC improved BP, triglycerides, cholesterol, HbA1c, fasting glucose, insulin, and HOMA-I, while HDL increased. No MetS progression or T2D cases occurred.
text: Active Body Control significantly reduced total GLP-1 compared to baseline (p=0.003), correlating with metabolic improvements. Baseline showed no changes in GLP-1.

memory: A study compared Group Support Lifestyle Modification (GSLiM) to dietary counseling for weight loss. GSLiM participants had greater weight loss (6% vs. 4.1%; RR 4.75; 95% CI: 1.68, 13.45) with similar retention (83.5% vs. 82.5% at 24 weeks). GSLiM improved weight self-efficacy, negative emotions, physical discomfort, MDPSS friend subscale, and quality of life. The comparison group showed reduced negative self-thoughts. No significant differences were found in blood pressure, physical activity, or psychological scores over time. Source: [PMC4990415].
text: The Group Support Lifestyle Modification (GSLiM) had a greater effect on reducing physical discomfort compared to dietary counseling, as reported in the study [PMC4990415].

memory: A study compared an intensified anticipatory guidance program (intervention) with routine guidance (control) in pregnant women, evaluating nonurgent ED visits (NUC) in newborns during the first month of life. 24% of infants had at least one NUC visit, with 21% in the intervention group and 27% in the control group (p=0.12), showing no significant difference. Subgroup analyses also found no significant differences. Participants were mostly Hispanic (68%), single (61%), and had incomplete high school education (44%), with no significant demographic differences between groups. Knowledge scores showed no significant changes. Follow-up data was missing for 44% and 40% of the intervention and control groups, respectively.
text: The intensified anticipatory guidance program did not significantly affect baseline characteristics compared to the routine program (p=0.12). Demographics, knowledge scores, and nonurgent ED visits showed no significant differences between groups.

memory: A study compared Gallium maltolate (GaM) to clarithromycin + rifampin (CLR+R) in foals with R. equi infection. Similar mortality rates were observed, with four foals dying from R. equi-related complications. GaM showed a 70% resolution rate, similar to 74% in CLR+R, though noninferiority for GaM was not conclusively demonstrated. Excluding noncompliant farms, GaM was noninferior. Both groups had similar resolution rates for smaller lesions (<27 mm), while GaM had a lower, non-significant resolution rate for larger lesions (≥27 mm). Logistic regression considered treatment and lesion size interaction.
text: Gallium maltolate showed a non-significantly lower resolution rate than clarithromycin + rifampin for lesions >27 mm. Noninferiority of GaM was not conclusively demonstrated, though similar overall resolution rates were observed. (Source: Study on foals with R. equi infection)

memory: A study compared mini-open anterior approach (Group A) with conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach (Group B). Both groups showed significant postoperative improvement in VAS scores (p<0.01) and Frankel classification (p<0.01). Group A had better VAS scores than Group B (p<0.05). One week post-surgery, VAS scores improved significantly in Group A (p<0.05), but not in Group B (p>0.05). No significant differences were found in Cobb angle or ESR between groups. Group A had shorter hospitalization and less blood loss, though not statistically significant. Anal exsufflation time was significantly shorter in Group A (1.21±0.48 days) than in Group B (2.12±0.82 days, p<0.05).
text: The mini-open anterior approach (Group A) significantly reduced anal exsufflation time compared to the conventional extraperitoneal approach (Group B) (1.21±0.48 vs. 2.12±0.82 days, p<0.05).
intervention: The mini-open anterior approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group A
comparator: conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group B

memory: In a study [PMC2650992], 100 breast cancer patients undergoing lumpectomy and axillary dissection were randomized into a fibrin glue group (N=50) or a control group (N=50). Both groups had similar outcomes in drainage duration, drain output, and seroma incidence overall. However, subgroup analysis showed that fibrin glue significantly reduced drainage duration (3.5 vs. 4.7 days; p=0.0006) and overall drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255) in patients undergoing level II or III axillary dissection. Thus, fibrin glue use was associated with reduced drainage duration and drain output in breast cancer patients undergoing lumpectomy and level II or III axillary dissection.
text: In a study [PMC2650992], fibrin glue significantly reduced overall drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255) compared to the control group in patients undergoing level II or III axillary dissection. Drainage duration was also shorter in the fibrin glue group.
intervention: fibrin glue group (glue sprayed onto the axillary dissection site)

memory: A pediatric study compared plasma exchange (PE) and IVIG. PE showed a shorter median mechanical ventilation duration (11 vs. 13 days, p=0.037) and a trend for shorter PICU stays (p=0.094). Recovery of unaided walking within four weeks was similar (95.2% vs. 90%, p=0.606). No significant treatment-related side effects were reported. PE had a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and MV duration (p=0.037), not observed in IVIG (p=0.132). Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
text: Plasma exchange (PE) showed a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and mechanical ventilation duration (p=0.037), unlike IVIG (p=0.132). PE also reduced median ventilation duration (11 vs. 13 days, p=0.037).
outcome: negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation

memory: A positive psychology intervention significantly enhanced children's positive emotions (F=10.93, p=0.001), life satisfaction (F=9.68, p=0.002), empathy (F=8.65, p=0.004), and prosocial behavior (F=7.29, p=0.004) compared to a wait-list control group, with no changes in negative emotions or total mental health difficulties. Subjective well-being and positive learning behaviors also improved in the intervention group. Age was a covariate for conduct problems. Cohen's d ranged from 0.38 to 0.81 for positive outcomes. No significant changes were observed in the control group. Source: PMC5662620.
text: A positive psychology-based intervention significantly improved subjective well-being compared to a wait-list control, as evidenced by enhanced positive emotions, life satisfaction, and prosocial behavior (PMC5662620).

memory: The GHSH intervention led to significant weight loss (−1.35 kg, 95% CI: −2.24, −0.46, P=.003) and increased weekly moderate physical activity (0.56 sessions/week, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.96, P=.008) compared to controls. Accelerometer-assessed MVPA also increased (24.16 minutes/week, 95% CI: 5.07, 43.25, P=.007). Waist circumference differences were not significant (P=.115). Dietary outcomes showed small, significant improvements in fiber and total FFBQ indices in the intervention group, while controls saw declines in fruit and vegetable intake. Other dietary and physical activity outcomes did not differ significantly between groups.
text: The GHSH intervention significantly increased accelerometer-assessed MVPA by 24.16 minutes/week compared to no continued contact (P=.007).
outcome: accelerometer-assessed moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA)

memory: A study compared "in sequence" and "out of sequence" computer tutorials. The in sequence group had higher post-test scores (z-score 1.1 vs. 0.52; 95% CI +0.16, +0.93). For the ORS topic, in sequence resulted in a 19% higher score (95% CI +7%, +31%) with a large effect size (Cohen's-d 0.85). For FWS, the in sequence group scored 6% higher (95% CI -3%, +16%), but this was not statistically significant (Cohen's-d 0.38). Time spent on tutorials was longer for in sequence (12.1 min vs. 10.5 min), though not statistically significant. Pre-test scores were similar between groups.
text: The "in sequence" computer tutorial significantly improved ORS topic scores by 19% (95% CI +7%, +31%) compared to "out of sequence," with a large effect size (Cohen's-d 0.85).

memory: Cinacalcet and control showed similar efficacy in reducing iPTH. Median iPTH decreased by 42.3% (cinacalcet) vs. 30.7% (control), P = 0.483. Primary endpoint (≥30% iPTH reduction) was achieved by 48.5% vs. 51.5%, P = 1.000. iPTH target (150–300 pg/ml) achieved by 24.3% vs. 18.2%, P = 0.764. Baseline iPTH was 729 pg/ml (cinacalcet) and 649 pg/ml (control), decreasing to 421 pg/ml and 441 pg/ml, respectively. No significant differences in outcomes between groups. Figure 2 presents mineral metabolic parameters.
text: Cinacalcet and control had similar efficacy in achieving the iPTH target (150–300 pg/ml), with 24.3% vs. 18.2% achieving it (P = 0.764). Both groups showed comparable reductions in iPTH levels, with no significant differences in outcomes.

memory: A study with 24 subjects evaluated the safety of four products (Aequasyal®, DC161‐DP0291, DC161‐DP0292, DC161‐DP0293). No clinically relevant systemic or local abnormalities were observed. No serious adverse events, discontinuations, or withdrawals occurred. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mainly gastrointestinal, reported once each for DC161‐DP0292 and the comparator. No significant differences in adverse event incidence or type were found between products.
text: Aequasyal® had a safety profile similar to DC161‐DP0292, with no significant differences in adverse event incidence or type. No serious adverse events or discontinuations occurred. Both products showed mainly mild, gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse events. Source: Study with 24 subjects.

memory: A study found that CYP2C9 intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentrations than extensive metabolizers in Caucasians (P = 0.0165, adjusted). CYP3A5 poor metabolizers showed higher concentrations, though not significantly. CYP3A4 intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios (P = 0.045). Age and BMI significantly influenced sildenafil ratios. Exploratory analyses showed higher predicted CYP3A4/3A5 metabolizing capacity correlated with lower sildenafil concentrations (F test P = 0.0238). Results were adjusted for age, BMI, and genetic ancestry PCs. Associations were not significant in the overall population.
text: CYP3A4 intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios than extensive metabolizers (P = 0.045). However, associations were not significant in the overall population.

memory: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations induced robust subtype C CN54rgp140-specific IgG responses (median titers 8100, 24300 post-doses 1, 2) with rising concentrations (0.861→9.866→17.75 μg/ml). ADCC responses were absent despite neutralizing activity in one participant; only 1/4 unprimed vaccinees developed neutralizing activity. Adverse events were mild (15% with 8 non-solicited events, no HIV infections). Responses were higher after CN54rgp140/GLA-AF than HIV-MVA (p<0.0001). Subtype B gp160 antibodies were detected in 87% after prior vaccinations. Mann-Whitney test used for comparisons.
text: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations significantly enhanced ADCC-mediating antibody responses compared to baseline, with higher IgG titers and concentrations. However, ADCC responses were absent in most participants despite neutralizing activity in one. Source: Working notes.

memory: A study comparing biosimilar and reference adalimumab found no significant differences in ACR20, ACR50, or ACR70 responses (Table 3). Adverse events were mild, unrelated to the study drug, and fully resolved, with no persistent lab changes (Table 5). Two cases of pallor were noted in the reference group at Visit 3, but no other systemic abnormalities were observed. Bilirubin levels remained stable, with no significant group differences at screening and Day 84. Musculoskeletal disorders were comparable between treatment groups.
text: A study found no significant differences in bilirubin levels between biosimilar and reference adalimumab, with stable levels observed at screening and Day 84. No persistent lab changes were reported.

memory: A 12-week trial compared MSDC-0160 (N=16) and placebo (N=13) in non-diabetic mild AD patients. No significant differences in glucose metabolism were observed in pre-defined regions when referenced to the pons or whole brain. However, glucose metabolism referenced to the cerebellum was maintained in MSDC-0160-treated participants, while it declined in placebo patients in several brain regions. Voxel-based FDG-PET analyses showed additional differences. Cognitive tests (ADAS-Cog, 19-item cognitive battery, and 7-item Executive Function battery) showed no significant group differences over 12 weeks. MSDC-0160 significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin levels (p<0.001), indicating improved insulin sensitivity, though hs-CRP and FFA levels did not change significantly, though trends suggested expected decreases. Source: [PMC4153084].
text: The study found no significant differences between MSDC-0160 and control on cognitive test battery global cognitive scores over 12 weeks. Source: [PMC4153084].
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: JQJT tablets (n=400) vs. placebo in pre-diabetes patients over 24 months showed reduced diabetes risk (HR 0.58, P=0.010) and higher normalized blood glucose (HR 1.41, P=0.0049). At 12 months, diabetes incidence was 16.5% vs. 28.9% (P=0.005). Adverse events were 2.8% vs. 1.7% (P=0.501). Mean age was higher in JQJT group (55.5 vs. 53.5, P=0.036).
text: JinqiJiangtang tablets reduced the risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes compared to placebo (HR 0.58, P=0.010) over 24 months, with lower diabetes incidence at 12 months (16.5% vs. 28.9%, P=0.005).
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
outcome: risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes

memory: Source [PMC2429977]: Group A (non-selective clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG) vs. Group B (selective clopidogrel in cath-lab after CAG, only if PCI). In PCI subgroup: 8.4% vs. 11.9% troponin elevation (P=0.316), 7.1% vs. 0.7% bleeding (P=0.006). All patients: 2.6% vs. 3.3% troponin elevation (P=0.475), 3.5% vs. 1.4% bleeding (P=0.025; OR=3.03). Adjusted for covariates, Group A had higher bleeding risk. Female gender and GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors also increased bleeding risk.
text: Group A (non-selective clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG) had a higher risk of bleeding complications compared to Group B (selective clopidogrel in cath-lab after CAG, only if PCI) (OR=3.03, P=0.025). This was adjusted for covariates, with female gender and GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors also increasing bleeding risk. Source: PMC2429977.
intervention: group A ('non-selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG;
comparator: group B ('selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg in the cath-lab after CAG, only in case of PCI;

memory: In a study [PMC4812817], 40% of patients had SIBO confirmed by GBT. DKT treatment significantly reduced median total GSRS scores (P < 0.001), especially in indigestion and constipation. Abdominal bloating (VAS) decreased from 76 to 30 (P = 0.005), and overall treatment effect scores improved from 13 to 51 (P = 0.005). Face scale assessments showed significant reductions in bloating (P = 0.008) and abdominal pain (P = 0.039). No significant changes were noted in acid reflex, diarrhea, or abdominal pain subscales. DKT had no effect on bowel movement frequency or stool form.
text: Daikenchuto significantly reduced indigestion and constipation scores compared to control (P < 0.001). It improved overall treatment effect scores and reduced bloating (P = 0.005), but had no effect on bowel movement frequency or stool form. Source: [PMC4812817].

memory: In a porcine DBD kidney transplant model, α-MSH treatment led to reduced urine output (p<0.05) and impaired GFR recovery at 10 hours post-reperfusion (13.3 vs. 19 ml/min; p<0.05). Sodium excretion was lower in the α-MSH group (4.5 vs. 5.8 mmol/min; p<0.05). No improvement in inflammation or short-term graft function was observed, possibly due to hemodynamic effects. No anuria was reported. Source: [PMC3984270].
text: α-MSH compared with controls in a porcine kidney transplant model resulted in reduced urine flow (p<0.05) and impaired GFR recovery. Sodium excretion was also lower in the α-MSH group (p<0.05). Source: [PMC3984270].

memory: TCC group used CPAP 4.1 ± 1.8 hours/night vs. 2.8 ± 2.2 hours/night in UCC (P = .07), 46% increase. TCC had 78% ± 22% CPAP use nights vs. 60% ± 32% (P = .07). TCC patients rated CPAP continuation higher. AHI was 7.9 ± 4.1 in TCC vs. 5.0 ± 4.0 in UCC (P = .04), but change in AHI (baseline - intervention mean) was not significantly different (TCC: 38.1 ± 18.4; UCC: 32.2 ± 14.8; P = .32). No significant differences in mask leak. Both groups satisfied with care, not concerned about data monitoring.
text: Telemonitored clinical care (TCC) was associated with higher patient-reported likelihood to continue using CPAP compared to usual clinical care (UCC). TCC users had greater CPAP usage hours and nights, though differences were not statistically significant (P = .07). AHI improved similarly in both groups.
outcome: Patients rated their likelihood to continue using CPAP

memory: A study compared usual care (UC) and manual therapy (UCMT) for headache management. Both groups showed significant improvements in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication use, absenteeism, and professional help utilization. No significant differences were found between groups in primary outcomes like global perceived effect (GPE) or Headache Impact Test (HIT-6) scores, though both groups showed significant improvements from baseline in HIT-6. Baseline characteristics were similar. However, the small sample size (UC n=19, UCMT n=18) may limit the study's power to detect differences. Results are based on data from [PMC2758835].
text: Both usual care and manual therapy led to significant improvements in secondary outcomes like headache frequency, pain intensity, and medication use. No significant differences were found between the groups, possibly due to the small sample size. Source: [PMC2758835].
outcome: Reduction in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and use of additional professional help (secondary outcomes)

memory: Frovatriptan and rizatriptan were compared for menstrually related migraine, with 49 vs. 59 attacks. At 2h, pain relief was 58% vs. 64% (p=NS), and pain-free rates were 31% vs. 34% (p=NS). At 24h, pain relief was 81% vs. 74% (p=NS), and pain-free rates were 67% vs. 61% (p=NS). Recurrence at 24h was 10% vs. 32% (p<0.01). Frovatriptan had a lower cumulative hazard of recurrence (p<0.01) and a more favorable sustained effect. Source: PMC3208043.
text: Frovatriptan had a lower cumulative hazard of recurrence during follow-up for menstrually related migraine compared to rizatriptan (p<0.01), with a more favorable sustained effect. Source: PMC3208043.
outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine

memory: A study compared video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) to standard in-person consultations (UNN). No significant difference was found in the number of operated patients (p = 0.432). RMC consultations for patients requiring casting were longer (29.0 min vs. 22.6 min, p = 0.0063). No significant differences were observed in discharged patients or referrals within two years (p = 0.858), nor in the number of consultations per patient. Patient-reported outcomes at 3 and 12 months were similar between groups. The findings suggest that video-assisted consultations are not inferior to standard care.
text: Video-assisted remote consultations resulted in longer mean consultation durations (29.0 min) compared to standard consultations (22.6 min) for patients requiring casting (p = 0.0063). Otherwise, outcomes were similar. Source: Study comparing RMC to standard care.
outcome: The mean consultation duration in the subgroup patients who required casting

memory: A study compared Pro Taper Universal retreatment (PR) and Mani NRT-GPR (MR). PR resulted in significantly less remaining filling material (12.96% vs. 24.26%, P=0.0056) and greater dentin removal (5.02% vs. 1.36%, P=0.0028). No complications, such as perforations, ledges, obstructions, or instrument fractures, were observed in either group. Neither system completely removed filling material from canals.
text: Pro Taper Universal retreatment significantly reduces remaining filling material compared to Mani NRT-GPR (12.96% vs. 24.26%, P=0.0056). Both systems had no complications but failed to completely remove filling material.

memory: A study compared prostaglandin gel alone (n=17) with a combination of prostaglandin gel and hygroscopic cervical dilators (n=23). After six hours, the combination group showed a greater Bishop score change (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) and a trend toward shorter induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hours, P=0.085). However, the combination group had a significantly higher infection rate (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003). Conclusion: Combination therapy enhances cervical ripening and induction speed but increases infection risk. Source: PMC1784771.
text: The combination of prostaglandin gel and hygroscopic cervical dilators resulted in a greater Bishop score change after 6 hours (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) compared to prostaglandin gel alone, according to PMC1784771.
intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours

memory: The Sonas programme showed no overall improvement in communication (Holden Communication Scale) but improved communication compared to the reading group (p=0.019) and control group (p=0.001), with HCS scores decreasing over time (T0 to T2). In severe dementia, Sonas outperformed the reading group at 12 weeks (T1) but not at 24 weeks (T2). MMSE scores showed differences in interest in past events and humor between Sonas and reading groups, but no significant cognitive differences in memory or speech. The reading group controlled for attention effects. Data was collected at baseline (T0), 12 weeks (T1), and 24 weeks (T2).
text: The Sonas programme did not significantly improve MMSE scores compared to the control group. There were no significant cognitive differences in memory or speech, though some differences in interest and humor were noted.

memory: In CRLM, RFA and resection had similar OS and DFS for lesions <3 cm (P=0.962, 0.980) in 226 patients. For ≥3 cm lesions, RFA showed worse DFS (23.1% vs 36.6%, P=0.01) in 70 patients. Five-year OS was similar (RFA 51.1%, resection 51.2%), but DFS was lower for RFA (33.6% vs 31.6%). In multiple metastases, OS was similar (P=0.330), but RFA DFS was lower than resection/combination (P=0.037). Source: PMC3204557.
text: For lesions <3 cm, RFA and resection show similar 5-year DFS (P=0.980). For ≥3 cm lesions, RFA has worse DFS (23.1% vs 36.6%, P=0.01). In multiple metastases, RFA also shows lower DFS than resection/combination (P=0.037). Source: PMC3204557.

memory: A trial with 13 subjects consuming pomegranate juice containing 5.8 mg anthocyanin/100 ml showed significant reductions in SBP (7%, P=0.013) and DBP (6%, P=0.010). FMD increased by 20% (P=0.172, not significant). No significant changes were observed in CRP (P=0.263), ICAM-1 (P=0.248), VCAM-1 (P=0.657), E-selectin (P=0.182), or IL-6 (P=0.763). Source: PMC3933059.
text: Pomegranate juice significantly reduced SBP by 7% (P=0.013) and DBP by 6% (P=0.010) compared to baseline in a trial of 13 subjects. Source: PMC3933059.
outcome: Systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP)

memory: A study compared r-FSH + rLH with rFSH + HMG in follicular development and fertility outcomes. No significant differences were found in follicle count, total oocytes, M2 oocytes, or fetal quality (p > 0.05). However, the rFSH + HMG group had a significantly higher total number of fetuses (p = 0.02). Fertility outcomes, including live birth rate, chemical pregnancy, and clinical pregnancy rate, were significantly better in the rFSH + HMG group compared to the rFSH + rLH group (p < 0.05). Source: [PMC5601935].
text: The effect of r-FSH + rLH compared to rFSH + HMG on the number of oocytes or M2 oocytes showed no significant differences (p > 0.05). Source: [PMC5601935].
intervention: Recombinant- follicle stimulating hormone (r-FSH) plus recombinant-luteinizing hormone (rLH)
outcome: Number of oocytes or M2 oocytes

memory: Source [PMC5698974]: Endobutton and Rigidfix showed no significant differences in knee stability (P=0.99) or tibial displacement (P=0.46). Knee range of motion was 135.73±2.63 vs 129.87±7.14 (P=0.06). Pain frequency was 2.5±1.4 vs 3.4±1.4 (P=0.08). Endobutton had higher patient satisfaction (89±4.3 vs 85±2.9, P=0.006) and better sports ability (85.2±4.6 vs 80.5±4, P=0.006). No significant difference in last month symptoms (P=0.34).
text: The Endobutton showed higher patient satisfaction scores compared to Rigidfix (89±4.3 vs 85±2.9, P=0.006) based on the IKDC 2000 questionnaire. No significant differences were found in knee stability or tibial displacement. (Source: PMC5698974)
outcome: the mean scores of satisfaction with surgery by using a subjective questionnaire IKDC 2000

memory: A study compared telephone vs. mail follow-up for RCT enrollment. Telephone follow-up increased eligibility screening attendance (17.5% vs. 9.1%, RR 1.92, 95% CI 1.36-2.71, P<0.001) and enrollment (12.3% vs. 7.4%, RR 1.66, 95% CI 1.11-2.47, P=0.01). Participants were similar in age (mean 55.7 vs. 55.6 years). Telephone contact was achieved with 332 (69%) of 480 participants; 60 (18.1%) were ineligible due to recent colorectal screening. The study stopped early due to lack of funding. Initial mail invitations enrolled 104 patients in the RCT.
text: The effect of "Follow-up invitation by telephone" compared with "Follow-up invitation by mail" on "Age of the participants" was minimal, as participants were similar in age (mean 55.7 vs. 55.6 years). Source: Study comparing telephone vs. mail follow-up for RCT enrollment.

memory: A study compared immediate vs. delayed implant placement in 144 implants (76 healed, 68 immediate). At 12 months, no significant differences in implant success, marginal bone loss, or peri-implant health were observed. Immediate implants had higher mean CFV at all time points, with significant differences in maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3. Initial differences in keratinized mucosa and probing depth at prosthetic loading disappeared after 6 and 12 months. Bone loss was 0.54 ± 0.39 mm for immediate and 0.66 ± 0.25 mm for delayed implants (p=0.201). No implant failures occurred. Source: [PMC4048120].
text: Implants placed immediately after extraction showed higher maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3 compared to healed sites (PMC4048120). No significant differences in success or bone loss were observed between groups.
comparator: implants were placed in healed sites
outcome: maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3

memory: In a study comparing misoprostol+celecoxib to vehicle+celecoxib, diastolic (p=0.0071) and mean blood pressure (p=0.0153) were significantly higher in the misoprostol+celecoxib group. Potassium excretion was significantly lower in misoprostol+celecoxib compared to baseline (p=0.0011) and vehicle+vehicle (p=0.0267). No significant differences were observed in aldosterone levels (p=0.8269) or Kidney Injury Molecule-1 (p=0.6624) between the groups. All treatments caused tubular dilatation/necrosis, but no significant myocardial changes were noted, though three animals had pericarditis. Source: PMC3931696.
text: Misoprostol + celecoxib significantly reduced potassium excretion compared to vehicle alone (p=0.0267). Source: PMC3931696.

memory: In a study comparing a neuromuscular blocking agent (Group A) with atracurium infusion (Group B), intraoperative heart rates were similar. Post-operative heart rate remained higher in Group B for 30 minutes after extubation (P = 0.02). Mean arterial pressure and brain relaxation scores were not significantly different (P = 0.27). Tracheal extubation time, orientation time, and time to achieve Aldrete score ≥9 were comparable between groups. Recovery characteristics, including hemodynamic parameters and surgical conditions, showed no significant differences between the groups.
text: Group A (neuromuscular blocking agent) had a lower heart rate 30 minutes after extubation compared to Group B (atracurium infusion) (P = 0.02). Other hemodynamic parameters were similar.

memory: POMx vs. PLAC: SBP trend increased (+3.9 bpm, p=0.08); NO3− increased (+10.3 μmol, p<0.04). ALTPOMx vs. ALTPLAC: VO2 max increased (+3.8 ml/min/kg, p=0.001). SEAPOMx vs. SEAPLAC: no VO2 change. ALT vs. SEA: performance decreased (−4.1 min, p<0.02). Submaximal VO2 unaffected by POMx (p≥0.05).
text: Exercise at 1657 m with pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx) significantly increased VO2 max by +3.8 ml/min/kg (p=0.001) compared to placebo (ALTPLAC). Submaximal VO2 was unaffected.
intervention: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx)
comparator: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Placebo (ALTPLAC)
outcome: Level of VO2 max after 5 minutes into cycling time trial to exhaustion at 100%VO2max

memory: A study compared a self-management intervention to treatment as usual in individuals with chronic mental illness (mean illness duration 17.4 years). Baseline scores on the Medication Adherence Questionnaire (MAQ) and Scale to Assess Understanding of Mental Disorder (SAUMD) were similar between groups. After 30 months, the self-management group showed significantly better medication compliance, greater insight, and higher self-reported antipsychotic dosages. They also had significantly higher MAQ and SAUMD scores. Re-hospitalization rates were lower in the intervention group (1.9% vs. 14.3%, p=0.003). Baseline demographics, age of onset, duration of illness, and hospitalization history were comparable.
text: The self-management group had a significantly lower re-hospitalization rate (1.9%) compared to treatment as usual (14.3%, p=0.003) after 30 months. This suggests that self-management interventions may reduce re-hospitalizations in individuals with chronic mental illness. Source: Study on self-management vs. treatment as usual.

memory: Two groups (A and B) with similar baseline demographics (age 44.08 ± 6.29 vs. 45.83 ± 8.42 years) received single or multiple artificial tear doses. No pre-intervention differences in OSDI, TBUT, staining, or Schirmer scores (p > 0.05). After 4 weeks, both groups showed significant improvements in OSDI, conjunctival, and corneal staining scores (p < 0.001). TBUT improved slightly (p = 0.013–0.027), but not significantly. Schirmer scores increased non-significantly (p = 0.115–0.129). No significant differences in efficacy between single and multiple dose products (p > 0.05).
text: Both single and multiple dose artificial tears significantly improved OSDI scores (p < 0.001) after 4 weeks, with no significant difference in efficacy between the two (p > 0.05). (Source: Study comparing single vs. multiple dose artificial tears)

memory: A 10-week telephone intervention in pregnant women (n=?) showed significantly lower 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose at 28 weeks (123±18 vs. 137.5±25.7 mg/dl, p=0.008) and lower pre-sleep glucose (113.2±15.8 vs. 124.7±13.9 mg/dl, p=0.1) compared to 3 calls for blood sugar monitoring. The intervention group had significantly higher increases in fasting blood glucose from 28 to 32 weeks and 28 to 36 weeks (p<0.05). Postpartum glucose screening rates were significantly higher in the intervention group (p<0.001). Data from [PMC4715405].
text: The 10-week telephone intervention significantly reduced 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose at 28 weeks (123±18 vs. 137.5±25.7 mg/dl, p=0.008) compared to three monitoring calls. Source: [PMC4715405].
intervention: telephone intervention was performed for 10 weeks
comparator: three times of telephone call was established to record blood sugar levels
outcome: mean level of blood glucose, 2 hours after lunch at 28 weeks of pregnancy

memory: A study compared text message–based feedback with no feedback, assessing mindfulness practice and four outcomes (PHQ-9, PTQ, FFA, SCS-D). Post-hoc analyses found near-zero to small, nonsignificant effect sizes across all measures. Symptom measures (PTQ, PHQ) showed slight positive effect sizes favoring the intervention, while FFA and SCS-D favored the control. The largest differences, still small, were in perseverative thinking, self-reported mindfulness, and exercise frequency. No significant differences were found in primary outcomes, suggesting limited impact of the intervention on depressive symptoms or mindfulness outcomes (Table 2).
text: Patients receiving text message–based feedback showed near-zero to small, nonsignificant improvements in PHQ-9 scores compared to those without feedback, suggesting limited impact on depressive symptoms (Table 2).
comparator: Patients not receiving text message assistance during follow-up

memory: [PMC4595235] Bio-GroTM vs. placebo showed no group × time interactions for metabolic panel (BUN, BUN/creatinine, sodium, chloride, CO2, calcium, albumin, alka phosphate), hemodynamics (HR, SBP, DBP), or blood chemistry (RBC, MCV, MCHC). Significant time effects for MCV, MCHC, and metabolic panel variables (p < 0.05). Group effects for creatinine, eGFR, BUN/creatinine (p < 0.05). No specific effects of supplementation on metabolic or hemodynamic variables.
text: The "Bio-active peptide supplement" had no significant effect on heart rate compared to placebo. The study found no group × time interactions for hemodynamic variables, including heart rate. Source: [PMC4595235].

memory: A study compared an intervention group receiving written information about electrodiagnostic testing to a control group. Anxiety scores were significantly lower in the intervention group (14.53±2.44mm) compared to the control group (21.28±2.86mm; p=0.04). Pain scores were not significantly different between groups (intervention: 20.91±2.33mm; control: 25.30±2.44mm; p=0.15). Subgroup analysis by gender found no significant differences in pain scores among males (intervention: 22.56±3.03mm; control: 21.85±3.74mm; p=0.71). Source: PMC5951568.
text: Provided with written information about electrodiagnostic testing significantly reduced overall anxiety scores compared to control (14.53±2.44mm vs. 21.28±2.86mm; p=0.04). Source: PMC5951568.
intervention: provided with written information about the electrodiagnostic testing

memory: Study [PMC1550875] evaluated C, C-A, and C-L in VAP patients. ICU stay medians: 15 (C), 16 (C-A), 14 (C-L) days. No significant differences in ICU stay, ventilator-free days (C: 16.1 ± 8.3, C-A: 12.6 ± 8.1, C-L: 12.6 ± 10.4; p > 0.05), temperature, leukocytosis, CRP, or mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no difference in mechanical ventilation duration. VAP confirmed in 84% (59/70). All regimens had similar clinical outcomes.
text: A study (PMC1550875) found no significant differences in ICU length of stay between cefepime (C), cefepime with amikacin (C-A), or cefepime with levofloxacin (C-L) in VAP patients. Median ICU stays were 15, 16, and 14 days, respectively. All regimens had similar clinical outcomes.
intervention: cefepime (C group), cefepime with amikacin (C-A group)
outcome: length of stay in the intensive care unit after infection

memory: A phase II trial compared ILF and ELF in 56 and 58 patients with metastatic gastric cancer (median age 62, Karnofsky 90%). At 14 weeks, response rates were 30% (ILF) vs 17% (ELF; RR 0.57, P=0.0766), with overall response rates of 43% vs 24% (RR 0.56, P=0.0467). Median progression-free survival was 4.5 vs 2.3 months, and overall survival was 10.8 vs 8.3 months (P=0.2818). ILF had higher grade 3/4 diarrhea (18%) compared to ELF’s neutropenia (57%). ILF demonstrated better response rates and should be further investigated for metastatic gastric cancer.
text: The ILF regimen was associated with a higher incidence of grade 3/4 diarrhea (18%) compared to ELF’s grade 3/4 neutropenia (57%). Thus, ILF had a more favorable profile for digestive system toxic events. Source: phase II trial in metastatic gastric cancer.

memory: Maraviroc intensification improved FMD by +0.73% (p=0.049) vs. control (-0.42%) in 21 HIV patients on cART. CCR5 expression increased in CD4+ (2.4%, p=0.010) and CD8+ (14.0%, p=0.002) T cells. No significant changes in D-dimer, hsCRP, or immune activation markers. FMD change correlated with ΔD-dimer (β -22.70, p=0.011) and ΔCD95+ CD4+ T cells (β -0.16, p=0.013). Carry-over effect noted in C2. Source: PMC5019971.
text: Maraviroc intensification increased CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells by 14.0% (p=0.002) compared to unchanged cART in 21 HIV patients. Source: PMC5019971.
outcome: CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells

memory: A study assessed intensive sound masking therapy for tinnitus using THI scores. The effective group showed significant THI reduction post-intervention (t = −14.07, P < 0.001), while the non-effective group had no significant change (t = −1.98, P = 0.054). Pre-intervention THI scores were lower in the non-effective group (t = 4.11, P < 0.001). Pre-post THI changes differed significantly between groups (19.10 vs 0.98, t = 12.54, P < 0.001). Logistic regression identified predictive factors for treatment effectiveness, with audiometric sub-groups considered.
text: Intensive sound masking therapy significantly reduced THI scores in the effective subgroup compared to baseline (t = −14.07, P < 0.001). The non-effective subgroup showed no significant THI change (t = −1.98, P = 0.054). Pre-intervention THI scores were lower in the non-effective group (t = 4.11, P < 0.001), and pre-post changes differed significantly between groups (t = 12.54, P < 0.001).
intervention: intensive sound masking therapy on tinnitus in effective subgroup

memory: A study compared LNG-IUS and oral NET for treating endometrial hyperplasia. Regression rates were significantly higher with LNG-IUS at 3 months (67.8% vs. 47.5%), 6 months (79.7% vs. 60.7%), and 12 months (88.1% vs. 55.7%; p<0.001). Median time to regression was similar between groups (3 months; p=0.697). Hysterectomy rates were significantly higher in the NET group (57.4% vs. 22%; p<0.001). Six LNG-IUS users underwent hysterectomy for persistent bleeding, but histology confirmed hyperplasia regression.
text: The Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) showed a higher regression rate at 3 months compared to oral norethisterone acetate (NET) (67.8% vs. 47.5%, p<0.001).

memory: A study compared calcium carbonate + calcitriol to calcitriol alone over 8 weeks. No significant changes in serum PTH or 25(OH)D levels were observed. Serum calcium and phosphorus levels remained unchanged. Serum FGF23 levels increased significantly in both groups, with a trend toward greater increase in the combination group (ΔFGF23 [%] =68.9%±58.8% vs. 35.1%±39.1%, P=0.097). Source: PMC5565373.
text: The combination of calcium carbonate and calcitriol did not significantly affect serum calcium levels compared to calcitriol alone (PMC5565373).
intervention: a combination of calcium carbonate and calcitriol group

memory: MgSO4 (30, 40, 50 mg/kg) vs. normal saline in intubation showed no significant HR differences (P>0.30). MgSO4 groups had significantly lower SBP, DBP, and MAP at 1, 3, 5 min post-intubation compared to control. SBP changes <20% or >20% of baseline were not significantly different at 10 min post-laryngoscopy (P<0.05 for Group III vs. control). No differences in extubation time or incidence of hypertension, hypotension, tachycardia, bradycardia, or arrhythmias across groups. Source: [PMC4418140].
text: MgSO4 (30, 40, 50 mg/kg) significantly reduced SBP at 1, 3, and 5 minutes post-intubation compared to normal saline (P<0.05). No significant differences in heart rate or adverse events were observed. Source: [PMC4418140].
intervention: MgSO4 - Group I, II, III: 30. 40/ 50 mg/kg
comparator: normal saline as a control group (S)
outcome: (SBP) systolic blood pressures at 1, 3, and 5 minutes after intubation

memory: A study comparing tranexamic acid (TXA) to placebo found no significant differences in mortality [RR = 0.69 (95% CI 0.35 to 1.39)] or unfavorable Glasgow Outcome Scale results [RR = 0.76 (95% CI 0.46 to 1.27)]. Progressive intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 18% (21/120) of TXA patients and 27% (32/118) of placebo patients, with no statistically significant difference [RR = 0.65 (95% CI 0.40 to 1.05)]. No increased risk of thromboembolic events was observed in TXA patients. Source: PMC4221638.
text: Tranexamic acid did not significantly reduce the risk of unfavorable Glasgow Outcome Scale results compared to placebo (RR = 0.76, 95% CI 0.46 to 1.27). Source: PMC4221638.
outcome: Risk of unfavorable outcome on the Glasgow Outcome Score

memory: In a study [PMC4610775], urinary kallidinogenase (UK) treatment improved cognitive function in patients at 4 weeks, linked to reduced serum Aβ1-40 levels, with no change in Aβ1-42. By 8 weeks, cognitive benefits persisted, and both Aβ1-40 and Aβ1-42 levels significantly decreased. These results suggest UK may enhance cognition while reducing amyloid-beta levels, initially affecting Aβ1-40 and later Aβ1-42.
text: Urinary kallidinogenase (UK) reduces Amyloid beta 1-40 levels compared to control, as shown in [PMC4610775]. Initially, UK lowered Aβ1-40 at 4 weeks, with both Aβ1-40 and Aβ1-42 decreasing by 8 weeks, suggesting a progressive amyloid-lowering effect.

memory: In a study [PMC4153077], Bifidobacterium lactis (probiotic) significantly increased monocyte phagocytic activity compared to maltodextrin (P < 0.001) and galacto-oligosaccharides (prebiotic) (P < 0.001). Galacto-oligosaccharides did not significantly affect monocyte or granulocyte phagocytosis compared to maltodextrin. Monocyte phagocytosis was higher in the probiotic group than the prebiotic group (P = 0.005).
text: "Bifidobacterium lactis" significantly enhances monocyte phagocytosis compared to "Galacto-oligosaccharides" (P = 0.005). The study [PMC4153077] shows that "Bifidobacterium lactis" increases phagocytic activity more than both maltodextrin and "Galacto-oligosaccharides."

memory: Study [PMC5019463] assessed navigator assistance versus usual care in 71.2±10.0-year-old patients, mostly female (65.8%) and African-American (71.6%). Groups G1, G2, G3 had mean follow-up visits of 1.3, 1.6, 1.3 (P=0.48). Adherence (≥1 visit): 69.8%, 82.5%, 73.3% (P=0.28). Subanalysis (≥2 visits): 91.3%, 74.3%, 66.7% (P=0.11). Most were single/divorced/widowed (73.3%), 54.5% lived alone, and 77.8% had ≥12 years education.
text: The study [PMC5019463] found no statistically significant difference in adherence rates (≥2 follow-up visits) between assistance from a patient navigator and usual care (P=0.11).
outcome: adherence rates for patients who attended two or more follow-up appointments

memory: A study compared podiatry, TCA, and KOH for callus treatment. TCA and KOH showed gradual improvements in hydration and texture, though KOH had reduced hydration by D14, and TCA had deteriorated texture. Skin elasticity improved with KOH but declined with TCA. At D7, TCA significantly improved texture over KOH (p=0.00). By D21, no significant differences were observed between TCA and KOH for hydration, elasticity, or texture. Both treatments reduced callus surface area by D7, D14, and D21, except TCA at D7. Podiatry showed similar trends in hydration and texture but decreased elasticity. By D21, no significant differences were found between groups for any outcome measures.
text: Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) initially showed better skin texture improvement than potassium hydroxide (KOH) at D7 (p=0.00), but by D21, both had similar effects. KOH improved elasticity, while TCA caused texture deterioration. Both reduced callus surface area over time, with no significant differences by D21. Source: Study on callus treatment.

memory: In a trial (PMC5340016), 293 patients received FEC or PE regimens. PE showed higher clinical response rates (76.06% vs. 59.95%, P=0.001) and lower post-chemotherapy pathologic T/N stages (P<0.001). FEC had lower neutropenia (5.96% vs. 11.97%, P=0.031). pCR rates were similar (10.61% vs. 12.31%, P=0.665), with no significant differences in breast or lymph node pCR rates (P=0.460, 0.463). FEC allowed more breast-conserving surgeries (27.27% vs. 35.28%).
text: The FEC regimen is associated with a lower frequency of neutropenia compared to the PE regimen (5.96% vs. 11.97%, P=0.031) (PMC5340016).
intervention: receive 4–6 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy with tri-weekly 5-fluorouracil–epirubicin–cyclophosphamide (FEC) regimen

memory: Bimatoprost 0.03% PF and standard bimatoprost both significantly reduced IOP (p<0.001), with mean changes of -7.49 to -5.93 mm Hg and -7.77 to -6.06 mm Hg, respectively. Between-group IOP differences were <0.4 mm Hg and not significant. Both were well tolerated, with AEs in 40.5% (PF) and 44.1% (standard), primarily mild conjunctival hyperaemia. Iris color change occurred in 0.3% (PF) and 1.0% (standard). No significant differences were observed in cup/disc ratio, visual acuity, visual field, or vital signs.
text: Both bimatoprost 0.03% preservative-free and standard bimatoprost significantly reduced intraocular pressure, with minimal differences (p<0.001). Adverse events were similar, with no significant differences in other outcomes.

memory: T-EO and Af-EO similarly reduced BV below baseline up to 7 h post-rinse (P < 0.001). After 4 days, both decreased BV, thickness, and CG of PL-biofilm compared to water (P < 0.001). Af-EO showed better reduction in thickness (7.90 vs. 9.92 μm, P = 0.012) and CG (33.36 vs. 46.61%, P = 0.001). Neither significantly reduced 48 h PL-biofilm thickness after a single rinse. Both displayed strong antibacterial and antiplaque effects, with Af-EO performing better in biofilm reduction. Outer layers had higher BV than inner layers (PMC5703870).
text: Both T-EO and Af-EO formulations significantly reduced BV, thickness, and CG of PL-biofilm compared to sterile water after 4 days (P < 0.001). Af-EO showed better reduction in thickness and CG than T-EO (P = 0.012 and P = 0.001, respectively). (PMC5703870)

memory: A study involving 40 children (mean age 11.5 ± 1.175 years) randomized to vitamin D or placebo found that the vitamin D group had significant increases in HDL-C (P=0.007) and vitamin D levels (P<0.001) post-intervention, while the placebo group showed slight decreases (P=0.27). However, no significant group differences were observed in HDL-C (P=0.11) or vitamin D (P=0.20) post-intervention. Adjusted analysis revealed significantly higher HDL-C (P=0.04) and vitamin D (P<0.001) in the vitamin D group. Source: [PMC5045666]
text: In children, vitamin D supplementation significantly increased HDL-C (P=0.04) and vitamin D levels (P<0.001) compared to placebo, though baseline differences were not significant. Source: [PMC5045666].
outcome: Baseline levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and vitamin D

memory: A study found no significant differences in coagulation parameters between nanoparticle exposure and placebo [PMC5588713]. One participant experienced mild fever and chest pain after 10 μg carbon nanoparticle exposure, with no serious complications. Dose-dependent increases in neutrophils (p = 0.0468) and a trend in leukocytes (p = 0.061) were observed, with the highest dose (100 μg) showing a significant rise in neutrophil percentage (p = 0.05). These findings are supported by Figure 2 and Table 2 from the source article. No significant adverse events were reported overall.
text: Exposure to nanoparticles showed a dose-dependent increase in neutrophils (p = 0.0468) compared to placebo, with the highest dose (100 μg) significantly raising neutrophil percentage (p = 0.05) [PMC5588713]. No significant adverse events were reported.

memory: Source [PMC4467206] found significant baseline differences (p = .001) between treatment groups in SF-36 MCS and SOC. CT had worse MCS and SOC values than TA and IT (all p = .001), with no differences between IT and TA. Large effect sizes were observed for MCS (ES = 1.12; CI = .64–1.58) and moderate for SOC (ES = .82; CI = .36–1.27) when comparing IT and TA to CT.
text: Compared to conventional treatment (CT), both salutogenic dialogue (IT) and therapeutic acupuncture (TA) significantly improved SF-36 MCS and SOC scores (PMC4467206). IT and TA showed similar effects, with large and moderate effect sizes for MCS and SOC, respectively.
outcome: SF-36 mental component summary (MCS), sense of coherence (SOC)

memory: Oral glutamine (10g/1000ml water) administered 2h pre-radiation reduced grade 3/4 mucositis (14.29% vs 37.14%, P=0.02; 2.86% vs 17.14%, P=0.04) and delayed onset (P<0.001) compared to control. In patients >60 years, glutamine reduced grade 3/4 mucositis (20.83% vs 52%, P=0.01). Chemoradiation patients also showed benefit (17.39% vs 41.67%, P<0.05). Glutamine reduced mean duration of grade 3+ mucositis (6.6 vs 9.2 days, P<0.001). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups.
text: Oral glutamine suspension (10g/1000ml water) given 2h before radiation significantly reduced the mean duration of grade 3+ mucositis (6.6 vs 9.2 days, P<0.001) compared to baseline. It also reduced incidence (14.29% vs 37.14%, P=0.02) and delayed onset (P<0.001).
intervention: oral glutamine suspension daily 2h before radiation in the study arm (10 g in 1000 ml of water)
outcome: The mean duration of grade 3 mucositis or worse (grade 3 and grade 4)

memory: A study comparing D-cycloserine (DCS) and placebo (PCB) in schizophrenia patients found no significant differences in age, age at onset, illness duration, or CPZ equivalents between groups. DCS showed no improvement in positive or negative symptoms or cognitive dysfunction. Subgroup analysis suggested DCS may worsen negative symptoms in early-onset schizophrenia. Findings from [PMC5508614].
text: The effect of "DCS D-cycloserine first" compared with "PCB placebo first" on "duration of illness (schizophrenia patients)" shows no significant difference, according to [PMC5508614].

memory: A 10-day steroid therapy in sepsis showed no significant differences compared to standard therapy in outcomes. SOFA score changes were 43.1 ± 26.5% vs. 45.4 ± 12.7% (P=0.624).
