Organ dysfunction on admission was 40% vs. 45%. Median hospital stay was 14 vs. 13 days (P=0.406). 28-day mortality was 40% vs. 60% (P=0.343). Source: PMC125315.
text: The addition of 10-day physiological-dose steroid therapy to standard sepsis treatment did not significantly affect 28-day mortality compared to standard therapy alone (40% vs. 60%, P=0.343). Source: PMC125315.
intervention: received standard therapy for sepsis and physiological-dose steroid therapy for 10 days;
comparator: received only standard therapy for sepsis

memory: SRP with amoxicillin/metronidazole vs SRP alone showed no significant differences in PD, CAL, or GI at 3/6 months (P > 0.05). The test group had better reduction in PD ≥7 mm (P < 0.05). At 6 months, the test group showed improved TIMP-1/MMP-1 balance (P < 0.05). Both groups had significantly reduced MMP-1 levels at 3/6 months (P < 0.05). TIMP-1 levels increased in the test group but not significantly (P > 0.05). Source: PMC4319300.
text: SRP combined with amoxicillin/metronidazole showed improved TIMP-1/MMP-1 balance at 6 months (P < 0.05) compared to SRP alone, despite no significant differences in PD, CAL, or GI. Source: PMC4319300.
intervention: scaling and root planning (SRP) in combination with amoxicillin plus metronidazole

memory: A study compared AIT, MVIT, and walking. AIT improved VO2max more than walking (p = 0.03, ITT) and significantly increased L/min (p = 0.01, ITT; p = 0.04, PP). MVIT showed no significant differences from walking. No changes in body mass or calorie intake were observed, but waist circumference and body fat decreased. Blood pressure and total cholesterol improved, though blood pressure changes might reflect a reverse Hawthorne effect. Walking had the lowest adherence (116 min/week).
text: Aerobic interval training (AIT) significantly improves VO2max more than walking (p = 0.03, ITT). Walking had lower adherence and showed no significant VO2max improvement compared to AIT or MVIT.

memory: Study [PMC3622020] evaluated 0%, 1%, and 5% glucose acetated Ringer’s infusion during cesarean delivery. Neonatal minimum blood glucose within 8h was 35.7 ± 9.6 (0% group), 49.8 ± 10.8 (1% group), and 29.2 ± 7.5 (5% group). The 5% group had the highest umbilical blood glucose (181.8 ± 22.2 mg/dL). Maternal glucose significantly increased post-infusion in the 1% and 5% groups. Neonatal hypoglycemia treatment was needed for 6 (0%), 3 (1%), and 9 (5%) infants.
text: Infusing 5% glucose acetated Ringer’s during cesarean delivery significantly increases maternal blood glucose levels compared to 0% or 1% (PMC3622020). The 5% group had the highest umbilical blood glucose, and more infants required hypoglycemia treatment.
intervention: 5 %  glucose acetated Ringer’s solution infusion during cesarean delivery
comparator: 0 % or 1 %, glucose acetated Ringer’s solution infusion during cesarean delivery

memory: ESWT and TPI+TENS showed no significant difference in neck ROM (p>0.05), but both were effective. Time effect was significant (p<0.05) except for extension. ESWT had a higher pain threshold (12.57±0.72) compared to TPI+TENS (9.60±2.19) post-therapy (p=0.045). VAS scores improved more in ESWT (1.86±0.69) than in TPI+TENS (2.80±0.84) (p=0.010). No significant differences were found in the McGill pain questionnaire (p=0.816) or pain rating scale (p=0.644). Source: PMC3503942.
text: ESWT showed greater improvement in VAS scores (1.86±0.69) compared to TPI+TENS (2.80±0.84) (p=0.010). Both treatments were effective, but ESWT had a higher pain threshold. Source: PMC3503942.
comparator: trigger point injections (TPI)+transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS)
outcome: The changes in visual analog scale

memory: A 4-week WBV training program (15 min, 5x/week) was compared to control and baseline. No significant differences in average velocity or total path length of COP sway were found between intervention and control groups. However, the WBV group showed significantly greater anterior, non-paretic, and paretic reach post-intervention (p<0.05). No significant changes in COP parameters were observed from baseline.
text: The task-oriented WBV training program did not significantly affect average velocity or total path length of COP compared to control or baseline. No significant changes in COP parameters were observed from baseline.
intervention: task-oriented training program with WBV, which was performed for 15 minutes, five times per week, for four weeks and control
outcome: average velocity and total path length of COP

memory: A trial comparing immediate vs. delayed treatment in metastatic colorectal cancer found no significant differences in quality of life (QoL), progression-free survival, or time to disease progression (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.72–1.41). Median survival was 13.0 vs. 11.0 months (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.79–1.47), with no survival benefit for immediate treatment. QoL scores, assessed using multiple scales, were similar across groups at all time points. Risk factors did not significantly influence survival or progression. A pooled meta-analysis showed no benefit of early treatment (P=0.5 for survival, P=0.047 for progression). The trial was suspended due to low accrual. Source: [PMC2361520].
text: A trial found no significant difference in overall QoL between immediate and delayed treatment in metastatic colorectal cancer. QoL scores were similar across groups at all time points. Source: [PMC2361520].

memory: A study [PMC4280732] assessed the impact of an educational workshop on maternal and spousal attitudes and delivery preferences. Post-intervention, knowledge and attitude scores significantly improved (P < 0.0001). Normal vaginal delivery was most preferred (P = 0.017). Pre-intervention, no significant differences in attitude scores were found between groups (P = 0.120 for women, P = 0.112 for men), but post-intervention differences emerged (P < 0.0001). Age differences were not significant (P = 0.968 for mothers, P = 0.612 for spouses), but couples had higher education levels. The intervention positively influenced delivery preferences and attitudes.
text: The couples' educational workshop significantly increased preference for normal vaginal delivery (P = 0.017) compared to the control group. This effect was observed post-intervention, alongside improved knowledge and attitudes (P < 0.0001). Source: [PMC4280732].
outcome: Most preferred method; normal vaginal delivery

memory: Liraglutide 1.8 mg (n=35) vs. placebo (n=33) showed higher discontinuation (31% vs. 18%, P=0.26). Continued use led to greater weight loss (6.8 vs. 3.3 kg, P<0.001). Liraglutide improved SSPG (−3.2 vs. 0.2 mmol/L, P<0.001), reduced systolic BP (−8.1 vs. −2.6 mmHg), fasting glucose (−0.5 vs. 0 mmol/L), and triglycerides (−0.4 vs. −0.1 mmol/L, P≤0.04). Pulse increased (6.4 vs. −0.9 bpm, P=0.001). Inflammatory markers remained unchanged.
text: Liraglutide 1.8 mg significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (−8.1 vs. −2.6 mmHg), fasting glucose (−0.5 vs. 0 mmol/L), and triglycerides (−0.4 vs. −0.1 mmol/L) compared to placebo, with P≤0.04. These findings suggest beneficial metabolic effects of liraglutide.
outcome: systolic blood pressure, fasting glucose , and triglyceride

memory: Study [PMC5518918] evaluated home-based vs. centre-based cardiac rehab in 90 low-to-moderate risk patients. Both groups showed similar improvements in peakVO2 at discharge (+11% vs. +15%, p=0.25) and at one-year follow-up (+16% vs. +17%, p=0.89). No differences were observed in physical fitness, activity levels, or quality of life. Home-based rehab was linked to higher patient satisfaction (p=0.02) and lower healthcare costs (€437, p=0.39). Societal cost-effectiveness showed a non-significant €3160 advantage for home-based (p=0.09). Home-based training appears equally effective but more satisfying and potentially more cost-effective.
text: Home-based training with telemonitoring shows similar improvements in peakVO2 compared to centre-based training (+11% vs. +15% at discharge, p=0.25). Both methods are equally effective in improving physical fitness, but home-based training is more satisfying and may reduce healthcare costs (€437, p=0.39). (Source: PMC5518918)

memory: Vaccine group had higher HIV-1 incidence (4.7%, 95% CI 3.7-5.8%) vs placebo (3.0%, 95% CI 2.3-3.9%, p=0.01) in combined follow-up (HVTN 503-S: 19 vs 17 infections). Enrollment differences significant in Soweto (p=0.045), Cape Town (p=0.03), and circumcised men (p=0.054). Men had higher risk (HR 2.46, 1.22-4.93, p=0.01); women HR 1.42 (0.85-2.35, p=0.18). No significant differences in condom use or sexual partners. Source: PMC4569275.
text: The vaccine group had a higher estimated infection hazard ratio (HR 2.46, 1.22-4.93, p=0.01) compared to the placebo group in men, indicating increased HIV-1 incidence. Source: PMC4569275.
outcome: Estimated infection hazard ratios for men

memory: Linagliptin showed similar overall AE rates (63.0% vs. 63.6%) but higher drug-related AEs (14.2% vs. 7.3%) compared to control. It significantly reduced HbA1c by −0.61% (P < 0.0001) and FPG by −25.1 mg/dL (P = 0.0003). UACR decreased by 32% (P < 0.05) at 24 weeks and 29% at 12 weeks (P < 0.05), with similar baseline UACR (73.8 vs. 80.5 mg/g Cr). The albuminuria-lowering effect was not influenced by race or baseline HbA1c/SBP. Source: [PMC3816860]
text: Linagliptin significantly reduced urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) by 32% at 24 weeks compared to control (P < 0.05). This effect was consistent across races and baseline HbA1c/SBP levels. Source: [PMC3816860]

memory: A study compared transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath (Group 1) with conventional percutaneous cystolithotripsy (Group 2). No significant differences were found in transurethral access number (1.2 vs. 1.28, P = 0.643) or operative time (32.73 vs. 34.31 minutes, P = 0.428). Group 2 had a significantly longer hospital stay (2.12 vs. 1.17 days, P = 0.000). Patient age (53.3 vs. 49.9 years) and stone size (3.2 vs. 3.2 cm) were similar between groups. All patients achieved 100% stone clearance. Source: [PMC5791397].
text: The transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath significantly reduces hospital stay compared to conventional percutaneous cystolithotripsy (2.12 vs. 1.17 days, P = 0.000). Source: [PMC5791397].
intervention: transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath

memory: A study evaluated PIVC failure rates (per 1000 hours) based on flush volume (3 mL vs. 10 mL) and frequency (every 24 vs. 6 hours), with an average dwell time of 3.1 days. Failure rates were 4.84 (3 mL) vs. 7.44 (10 mL), p=0.06, and 5.06 (24 hours) vs. 7.34 (6 hours), p=0.05. Cox regression found no significant association between interventions and failure (p=0.21 for interaction), with consistent results across univariable and multivariable analyses. No significant interaction between volume and frequency was observed, and no intervention significantly reduced failure rates. Source: [PMC4960789]
text: The study found no significant difference in PIVC failure rates between 3 mL and 10 mL sodium chloride flushes (p=0.06). Neither flush volume nor frequency significantly reduced failure rates (p=0.21 for interaction). Source: [PMC4960789].
outcome: Peripheral intravenous catheter failure rates per 1000 hours

memory: A study compared Aloe cream and Calendula ointment for diaper dermatitis. Baseline characteristics (age, gender, diaper care frequency) were similar between groups (Table 1). Both treatments significantly improved rash severity (P < 0.001), but Calendula ointment showed fewer rash sites (P = 0.001). No adverse effects were reported. Past medical conditions like diarrhea, immunodeficiency, and allergies were similarly distributed between groups (P > 0.05) (Table 2).
text: The study found no significant difference in baseline characteristics between Aloe cream and Calendula ointment groups. Age, gender, diaper care frequency, and past medical conditions were similarly distributed (P > 0.05).

memory: A study compared the mobiletype program (monitoring mood, stress, and daily activities) to an attention-control group (monitoring only daily activities). GPs found the mobiletype program significantly more helpful in medication decisions (p = .013, d = 0.55) and referrals (p = .012, d = 0.56). It also improved diagnosis (p = .002, d = 0.69) and communication (p = .031, d = 0.47), as well as identification of medical (p = .023, d = 0.52) and mental health problems (p = .011, d = 0.56). However, after adjusting for baseline confidence scores, the difference in post-test confidence was not significant (β = 1.05, p = .131).
text: The intervention group showed greater improvements in diagnosis, communication, and identification of medical and mental health problems compared to the attention-comparison group (p < .05). The mobiletype program was more helpful for GPs in medication decisions and referrals. Source: Study data.
intervention: intervention group (where mood, stress and daily activities were monitored with program mobiletype)
comparator: attention-comparison group (where only daily activities were monitored)
outcome: helping to diagnosed and communication, specific medical and mental health problems

memory: A study compared meditation awareness training (MAT) with a control group on workaholism and job performance. Baseline scores for BWAS, AJIGS, DASS, RBPS, work engagement, and work involvement were similar (p > 0.05). MAT participants showed significant improvements in workaholism, job satisfaction, work engagement, and psychological distress, with reduced work hours without decreased job performance. The study aimed to evaluate MAT’s therapeutic effects on workaholism, with secondary outcomes including job performance and psychological distress. Results supported MAT's efficacy in reducing workaholism and improving work-related outcomes. Source: PMC5520118.
text: Meditation Awareness Training (MAT) significantly reduces workaholism symptomatology compared to a control group, as shown in a study (PMC5520118). MAT improved work engagement, job satisfaction, and psychological distress without compromising job performance.

memory: A study compared neonatal resuscitation + oral antibiotics (intervention) with routine care (control). Early fetal loss rates were similar (61 vs 63 per 1000; RR 0.97, p=0.60). Facility births and skilled attendants did not differ significantly (53% vs 54%; 54% vs 56%). Intervention clusters had more home deliveries attended by LHWs (14% vs 1%; p<0.0001) and higher use of clean delivery kits (p<0.0001). Neonatal mortality was lower in the intervention group (42 vs 55 per 1000; RR 0.80, p=0.005). Stillbirth rates showed no significant difference (RR 0.89, p=0.13).
text: The effect of neonatal bag and mask resuscitation and oral antibiotic therapy compared with routine care on early fetal loss rates showed no significant difference (RR 0.97, p=0.60).
intervention: neonatal bag and mask resuscitation and oral antibiotic therapy
comparator: routine care through the existing national programme

memory: A study [PMC3504298] found that face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) reduced depressive and anxious symptoms (BDI, HRSD, STAI) compared to placebo, with sustained effects at follow-up. It also reduced cortisol awakening response, a recurrence risk marker. Word-based ABM showed no significant symptom reduction. While word-based ABM altered attentional bias differently than placebo, no difference was found between face- and word-based ABM groups in attentional function. Face-based ABM showed more consistent benefits across outcomes.
text: Face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) reduces anxious symptoms more effectively than placebo, with sustained benefits and reduced cortisol awakening response, according to [PMC3504298]. Word-based ABM showed no significant symptom reduction.

memory: In an IAH-induced ALI model, PSV reduced mean airway pressure and mRNA levels of IL-6 and type III procollagen compared to PCV, suggesting anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects. PSV improved oxygenation, decreased alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, and DAD, and increased surfactant protein B expression. In nIAP animals, no significant differences were observed between PSV and PCV in alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, septal thickening, or DAD scores. These findings indicate PSV may offer protective benefits in IAH-associated ALI. Source: PMC5444773.
text: In IAH-induced ALI, PSV reduced alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, and DAD compared to PCV, with anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects (PMC5444773). No significant differences were found in nIAP animals.
outcome: Alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, or DAD score in animals with IAH

memory: A study compared Alfentanil (10 μg/kg, 1 μg/kg/min infusion) and Remifentanil (0.5 μg/kg, 0.1 μg/kg/min infusion) in 40 patients with similar baseline characteristics. Alfentanil showed a shorter average respiration return time (2 min) compared to Remifentanil (3.3 min), though the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.08). No significant differences were observed in time to eye opening, verbal response, or discharge from recovery. Nausea and vomiting were more frequent in the Remifentanil group (n=6) than in the Alfentanil group (n=1; P<0.05). No respiratory issues were reported during recovery. Source: PMC3591547.
text: The effect of Alfentanil compared to Remifentanil on stopping anesthesia drugs, eye opening, verbal response, and discharge showed no significant differences (P>0.05). However, Alfentanil had a shorter respiration return time (2 vs. 3.3 min, P=0.08). Remifentanil was associated with more nausea and vomiting (P<0.05). Source: PMC3591547.
intervention: 10 μg/kg of Alfentanil, infusion of Alfentanil 1 μg/kg/min
comparator: Remifentanil 0.5 μg/kg, infusion of Remifentanil 0.1 μg/kg/min
outcome: stopping the anesthesia drugs up to opening eyes, return to verbal response, and discharge from the recovery

memory: Primaquine added to DHP reduced gametocyte clearance time (1 vs. 12 days; HR 7.3, p=0.01) and decreased day 7 patent gametocyte prevalence (2.1% vs. 15%, p=0.03). Hemoglobin drop was greater with primaquine (24.8% vs. 7.1%, p=0.14). Baseline gametocyte prevalence was 9% by microscopy, 46% by PCR. Post-dosing, 12% had gametocytemia; by day 7, only 1/4 of day-2 gametocytemic subjects remained positive, all negative by day 14. Five subjects with severe G6PD deficiency were excluded; 8 had mild/moderate deficiency (Excerpt [PMC5462369]).
text: Adding primaquine to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine significantly reduced gametocyte clearance time (HR 7.3, p=0.01) and day 7 gametocyte prevalence (2.1% vs. 15%, p=0.03) (Excerpt [PMC5462369]).

memory: Source [PMC5350209]: Health warning labels (text or image) significantly reduced alcohol acceptance (p = .002) compared to no warning, with no difference between text and image warnings. Both warning types slowed drinking speed compared to no warning (p < .001), with no difference between text and image. The presence of a warning, not its type, affected consumption speed.
text: Visual warning (text) significantly slows the speed of alcohol consumption compared to no warning (p < .001). However, there is no difference in consumption speed between text and image warnings. The presence of any warning, not its type, affects drinking speed (Source: PMC5350209).

memory: Raloxifene (RAL) treatment in ZDSD rats reduced type 2 diabetes incidence compared to vehicle (VEH)-treated rats, with lower blood glucose levels than both diabetic and non-diabetic VEH groups. Although cumulative blood glucose (AUC) was lower in RAL-treated rats (p=0.048), endpoint values were not significantly different. RAL improved femoral toughness through increased energy absorption in the post-yield region and enhanced structural mechanical properties, including energy-to-failure, post-yield energy-to-failure, and post-yield displacement. No significant differences were found in DXA or μCT measures of L4 vertebrae or pQCT measures of femoral midshaft. In the distal femur, VEH-D rats exhibited lower trabecular thickness and number, higher separation, and a more rod-like structure compared to RAL-treated rats.
text: Raloxifene improved femoral toughness in ZDSD rats compared to control, as evidenced by increased energy absorption and structural mechanical properties (p=0.048). This effect was independent of changes in bone density or microstructure. Source: Study on RAL-treated ZDSD rats.

memory: No significant differences in pain (P=0.22), visual acuity (P=0.08, 0.36), refractive error (P=0.23), or complication rates between alcohol-assisted and mechanical epithelial removal. Alcohol-assisted removal was faster (96±18 vs 118±26 s, P=0.035). Re-epithelialization time was similar (P=0.75). Sample sizes: 658 and 592 eyes. Spherical equivalent: −4.37±2.3 D vs −3.8±1.3 D (P=0.78).
text: No significant difference in mean spherical equivalent between alcohol-assisted and mechanical epithelial removal (P=0.78). Other outcomes, including pain, visual acuity, and re-epithelialization time, were also similar. Alcohol-assisted removal was faster.

memory: A study compared ATP delivery via proximal- vs. distal-release pellets and naso-duodenal tube. Proximal-release pellets and naso-duodenal tube increased uric acid by ~50% vs. placebo (P=0.003 and P=0.001), while distal-release pellets did not. Blood ATP levels did not rise. Proximal-release pellets caused higher plasma lithium levels than distal-release pellets (P=0.001), with lower lithium AUC compared to placebo (P=0.001). Release profiles were confirmed using plasma lithium measurements over 7 hours. Results indicate ATP absorption and metabolism depend on gastrointestinal release timing, with proximal release leading to higher uric acid and lithium levels.
text: Administration via proximal-release pellets increases plasma lithium levels compared to distal-release pellets (P=0.001). This effect was confirmed through plasma lithium measurements over 7 hours, showing higher lithium concentrations with proximal release.

memory: Study [PMC1868022] evaluated Pap smear (n=41) vs. no intervention (n=39) on cervicovaginal lavage inflammatory markers. No baseline differences were noted. Post-intervention, the Pap group showed significant increases in TNF-α (p=0.025), IL-12 p70 (p=0.0016), and IL-10 (p=0.0003), but no changes in total protein, IL-8, IL-1β, or IL-6. Four participants in each group had abnormal Pap smears (p=0.95). Results suggest Pap smear elevates Th1 and regulatory cytokines without affecting proinflammatory markers.
text: The Pap smear at enrollment significantly increased IL-10 levels compared to no intervention (p=0.0003), according to Study [PMC1868022]. This suggests that Pap smear elevates regulatory cytokines like IL-10 without affecting other proinflammatory markers.

memory: SB4 (etanercept biosimilar) demonstrated therapeutic equivalence to ETN in RA patients on MTX. At week 24, ACR50 (46.6% vs 42.3%) and ACR70 (25.5% vs 22.6%) were comparable in PPS. ACR20 response rates were 78.1% (SB4) vs 80.3% (ETN), with 95% CI within −15% to 15%. ADA incidence was significantly lower in SB4 (0.7%) vs ETN (13.1%). ADAs in ETN had neutralizing capacity, while most resolved by week 12. Source: PMC5264222.
text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, showed therapeutic equivalence to etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate, with comparable ACR50 and ACR70 responses at week 24. ACR20 response rates were similar, and SB4 had a significantly lower ADA incidence (0.7% vs 13.1%) (PMC5264222).
outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: Robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) showed higher acute circumferential extent (94% vs. 88%, P=0.03) and LGE encirclement (72% vs. 60%, P=0.002) than standard navigation. Late imaging showed LGE encirclement of 56% vs. 45% (P=0.04). At 6 months, arrhythmia-free patients had similar LGE (64% vs. 60%, P=0.45), but those with recurrences had higher LGE in the robotic group (43% vs. 30%, P=0.001). At 3 years, the robotic group required fewer procedures (1.3 vs. 1.9, P<0.001) with higher success rates (80% vs. 75%).
text: Robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) showed greater mean LGE encirclement at 6 months compared to standard navigation (64% vs. 60%, P=0.45). However, among patients with arrhythmia recurrence, the robotic group had higher LGE (43% vs. 30%, P=0.001).
outcome: mean LGE encirclement at 6 months follow-up

memory: Paracetamol 250 mg reduced fever ≥38°C in infants (efficacy 43.0%, 95% CI: 17.4, 61.2) but not in toddlers (15.9%, 95% CI: -19.9, 41.3). It significantly reduced fever >39°C in toddlers (efficacy 79%, 95% CI: 3.9, 97.7) in PP population. Systemic reactions were less frequent in the paracetamol group, with significant decreases in activity (p=0.005) and other symptoms after infant doses (all p<0.05). No serious adverse events were reported. Source: PMC3698010.
text: Paracetamol 250 mg significantly reduced fever in infants and toddlers, with notable efficacy in toddlers for fever >39°C. It also decreased activity (p=0.005) and other symptoms in infants. Source: PMC3698010.

memory: A crossover study with 24 infants compared Nutrilon Omneo (NF) to standard formula (SF). Defecation frequency was similar between NF (5.5/week) and SF (5.9/week) (p = 0.38). Soft stools were more frequent with NF (17%) than SF (0%) (p = 0.046). Pre- to post-treatment, defecation frequency increased for both formulas (NF: 3.5 to 5.6/week; SF: 3.6 to 4.9/week), but the difference was not significant (p = 0.36). Improvement in stool consistency was more common with NF (90%) than SF (50%), but not statistically significant (p = 0.14). Painful defecation and abdominal/rectal masses decreased in both groups, with no significant differences between formulas.
text: The new formula (NF) increased soft stool frequency compared to standard formula (SF) (17% vs. 0%, p=0.046). Defecation frequency was similar between groups. Stool consistency improved more with NF (90% vs. 50%), though not significantly. Painful defecation and masses decreased in both groups without significant differences. (Source: crossover study with 24 infants)

memory: Kegel exercises significantly improved pulmonary function parameters compared to control, including FVC, FEV1, PER, FEF 25–75%, IC, and MVV (PMC4668172). The control group showed no improvement in these parameters. However, changes in the FEV1/FVC ratio were not statistically significant.
text: A Kegel exercises program significantly improved peak expiratory flow (PER) compared to control (PMC4668172). The control group showed no improvement in PER.

memory: Peramivir and oseltamivir showed no significant differences in symptom disappearance time (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65) or total symptom scores (P = .69) [PMC5534217]. Fever alleviation times were 40.0 vs. 37.8 hours (P = .69). Virus titer reduction was similar (P = .51). No significant intergroup differences were found in primary outcomes. Censored cases and missing data were noted.
text: A study found no significant difference between peramivir and oseltamivir in the number of days required for influenza symptoms to disappear (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65) [PMC5534217].
outcome: The numbers of days required for the disappearance of influenza symptoms

memory: Telemonitoring for hypertension increased total costs by £115.32/patient (CI £83.49-£146.63; p<0.001), primarily due to service, training, and consultations. Medication costs were slightly higher but not clinically significant. Hospital admission costs were £287.01 vs. £181.54 (diff £105.47; p=0.424), with no significant difference in accident and emergency visits (p=0.286). Systolic BP reduction cost £25.56/mm Hg (CI £16.06-£46.89).
text: Hypertension telemonitoring increased total costs by £115.32/patient compared to control, mainly due to service and consultations. There was no significant difference in accident and emergency visits costs (p=0.286). Source: Working notes.

memory: In a study [PMC2992187], continuous antidepressant (ADM) use was linked to higher diabetes risk in the placebo (HR 2.34 [1.32–4.15]) and lifestyle (2.48 [1.45–4.22]) arms of the DPP/DPPOS trial, but not in the metformin arm (0.55 [0.25–1.19]). Intermittent ADM use showed a trend toward increased risk in the placebo arm (1.34 [0.99–1.81]). The ADM-diabetes risk association differed significantly between lifestyle and metformin arms. Excluding weight-gain linked ADMs (tricyclic/tetracyclic agents) did not alter results. Findings were consistent across placebo and lifestyle arms but not in metformin.
text: Antidepressant use (ADM) is associated with increased diabetes risk in the lifestyle arm (HR 2.48 [1.45–4.22]) of the DPP/DPPOS trial, similar to the placebo arm but distinct from the metformin arm. This association remains consistent even after excluding weight-gain linked antidepressants.

memory: In a study using CLP and LPS-induced ARDS models, BMDMC therapy improved survival in CLP groups (70% at day 7 vs. 40% in controls, P < 0.05). It reduced lung elastance, alveolar collapse, tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage cellularity, collagen fiber content, and interleukin-1β. BMDMC also increased chemokine expression (keratinocyte-derived chemokine and monocyte chemotactic protein-1) in lung tissue regardless of ARDS model. Intercellular adhesion molecule-1 and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 expression increased post-cell therapy, depending on the insult (LPS or CLP). Survival rates were 100% in sham, C, LPS-SAL, and LPS-BMDMC groups at day 7. (Source: PMC3856598)
text: BMDMC therapy reduced alveolar collapse in CLP-induced ARDS compared to controls (P < 0.05), improving survival and lung function. (Source: PMC3856598)
intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)

memory: A study compared plastic cap and metal cup ventouse delivery in vaginal operative deliveries. Infants showed lower pain responses with plastic caps (p < 0.001), though pain was mild and resolved within 72 hours. Scalp trauma was higher with metal cups (13.2%) than plastic (6.6%), but not statistically significant (p = 0.51). Air aspiration occurred in 10% of metal cup cases. Plastic cups had two detachment incidents (6.7%), while metal cups had none. No severe complications like subgaleal or intracranial haemorrhage were reported. Pain scores (EDIN ≥ 5) showed no significant differences between groups. Maternal analgesia effects could not be evaluated due to uneven distribution.
text: Plastic caps reduced infant pain response compared to metal cups (p < 0.001), though pain was mild and resolved within 72 hours. Metal cups had higher scalp trauma (13.2% vs. 6.6%) but not statistically significant. No severe complications were reported. Pain scores (EDIN ≥ 5) did not differ significantly between groups.

memory: In a phase 2a study, AN1792 (Aβ42) antibody responders showed significantly less decline on the Disability Assessment for Dementia (p=0.015) and Dependence Scale (p=0.033) compared to placebo after 4.6 years. Low but sustained anti-AN1792 titers were detected in 17 of 19 responder samples, while non-responders had no detectable antibodies. Responders had 20.2% less decline on the CDR-SOB, though not statistically significant (p=0.185). MRI follow-up showed similar brain volume loss between responders and placebo.
text: Synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) showed a statistically significant reduction in decline on the Dependence Scale compared to placebo (p=0.033) in a phase 2a study after 4.6 years. This effect was observed in responders who developed sustained anti-AN1792 titers.

memory: Levamisole added to IM/ID HB vaccinations increased antibody titers (514.2 IU/L, p=0.001; 176.1 IU/L, p=0.01) and improved seroconversion (90%) compared to baseline. Six months post-vaccination, titers declined less in IM+Levamisole (30% drop) versus others (50% drop). IM 40 μg HB vaccine showed lower titers (28.9 ±7 IU/L) and seroconversion (60%) compared to ID 20 μg (121.1 ±82.3 IU/L, 70%), though differences were not statistically significant. Source: [PMC1540413]
text: The IM 40 μg HB vaccine had a lower seroconversion rate (60%) compared to ID 20 μg (70%), though differences were not statistically significant. Source: [PMC1540413].

memory: [PMC4973627] PA+HE− (n=992) had 17% cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.56, 0.44–0.73, P<0.001). PA−HE+ (n=162) showed 61% general mortality (HR 0.90, 0.71–1.13, P=0.358). PA+HE+ (n=502) had 44% general mortality (HR 0.53, 0.44–0.63, P<0.001) and 15% cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.49, 0.36–0.66, P<0.001).
text: The combination of physical activity and healthy eating significantly reduces cardiovascular mortality compared to control (HR 0.49, 0.36–0.66, P<0.001) [PMC4973627].

memory: A web-based CME, performance feedback, and quality improvement tools intervention did not significantly improve medication intensification for glucose, BP, or LDL control in rural diabetic patients (p=0.948). Unadjusted results showed increased A1c intensification in both intervention (26.4% to 32.6%) and control groups (24.8% to 31.1%). For A1c >9%, both groups showed increased intensification (intervention: 34.8% to 62.5%; control: 35.7% to 61.4%). No significant differences were found for BP or LDL intensification. Adjusted analyses confirmed no intervention effect (p=0.948, 0.216, 0.995). Source: PMC3467590.
text: The intervention of web-based CME, performance feedback, and quality improvement tools did not significantly improve incremental benefit in medication intensification for glucose, BP, or LDL control in rural diabetic patients compared to the control group (p=0.948). Source: PMC3467590.
intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

memory: In a study [PMC4628236], diabetic rats exhibited elevated myocardial nitro-oxidative stress, indicated by increased NT immunoreactivity, which was reduced by cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) over 8 weeks. Cinaciguat normalized HSP70a1 and glutathione-reductase mRNA expression, improved PKG signaling (increased p-VASP/VASP ratio), and decreased PDE-5 expression. It enhanced cardiac function by increasing PRSW and trending Ees, while improving diastolic function through reduced Tau (14.9 ± 0.6 ms) and a flatter EDPVR slope. These effects were absent in non-diabetic rats.
text: Cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic rats, as shown by decreased NT immunoreactivity, compared to placebo. This effect was accompanied by improved cardiac function and signaling pathways.
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

memory: Lemon verbena extract showed a trend in increasing GPxP activity (p=0.0681) and a time effect (p=0.0624) vs. placebo. Exercise-induced CK was not significantly different (p=0.9412), though lemon verbena had significant CK elevation only at 24 h, while placebo showed elevations at all timepoints. IL-6 showed no group differences (p=0.5824). Trends favored lemon verbena for movement-induced pain (p=0.0788) and reduced muscle strength loss (p=0.0311). MVC fully recovered in the lemon verbena group by 48 h, not in placebo. Source: [PMC5781260].
text: Lemon verbena extract showed a trend toward reduced muscle strength loss (p=0.0311) and faster recovery of MVC compared to placebo. Source: [PMC5781260].

memory: Arformoterol vs. placebo showed greater improvements in trough FEV1 (0.051 L, P = .030) and FVC (0.075 L, P = .018), and quality of life (P < .05). Risk of first respiratory serious adverse event was 50% lower with arformoterol (P = .003). Overall AE incidence was similar (72.9% vs. 68.2%), but fewer COPD exacerbation hospitalizations (9.0% vs. 14.3%). Nonrespiratory AEs ≥5%: headache, nausea, UTI. Numerically more cardiac SAEs with arformoterol (3.1% vs. 2.4%), but no significant difference in time-to-first event. Mortality rates were similar (2.9% vs. 2.4%).
text: Arformoterol showed greater improvements in quality of life compared to placebo (P < .05). It also improved lung function and reduced respiratory serious adverse events. Overall AE incidence was similar, with fewer hospitalizations for COPD exacerbations.
outcome: improvements in quality of life (overall St. George's Hospital Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire)

memory: In a rat diet study, GF and GIF diets improved calcium absorption and bone strength compared to control (GC), while isoflavone alone (GI) had no effect on bone strength. GX decreased these parameters. GF and GIF prevented bone fragility (p<0.05). Serum analysis showed no difference in genistein between GI and GIF, but daidzein was lower and equol higher in GIF (p<0.05). FOS diets (GF, GIF) improved calcium absorption and bone strength compared to control, though isoflavone alone did not enhance bone strength.
text: The Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF) improved femur bone strength compared to the Control diet (GC), while isoflavone alone (GI) did not. GF and GIF enhanced calcium absorption and prevented bone fragility (p<0.05).
intervention: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF)

memory: A study compared nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) to saline (3 ml) in asthma patients. Both significantly increased peak tidal expiratory flow (PTEF) with no group difference (P = 0.6). Albuterol significantly reduced TEF10 and the 25/PT ratio (P < 0.05), while VPTEF/VE and tPTEF/tE were unchanged. Baseline demographics were balanced except for gender. No significant changes were seen in heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, or wheeze score post-treatment. Other variables were unaffected by aerosol administration. Results from Table 1, 2, and 3 of [PMC111183].
text: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) significantly reduced the 25/PT ratio compared to saline (3 ml) in asthma patients (P < 0.05), while both increased PTEF with no group difference (P = 0.6). Source: [PMC111183].
intervention: nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline)
outcome: ratio of the tidal expiratory flow at 25% of the remaining tidal volume to PTEF (25/PT)

memory: GENRES Study: Male patients with moderate hypertension (mean OBP 152/100 mm Hg) and slightly elevated BMI (<32 kg/m²), no diabetes or reduced kidney function. Bisoprolol showed the highest BP reduction (11.1/8.3 mm Hg) compared to losartan, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. A genome-wide analysis identified 3 SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) significantly associated with bisoprolol's ASBP response, located in the ACY3 gene regions. Additionally, 42 SNPs in 31 regions were associated with treatment response at P≤1×10−5.
text: Bisoprolol showed greater systolic blood pressure reduction than losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide in hypertensive males. Genome-wide analysis identified three SNPs (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) on chromosome 11, in ACY3 gene regions, significantly associated with bisoprolol's ASBP response (GENRES Study).
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

memory: Intervention: metformin (500 mg, bid po) + alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) vs. metformin (1000 mg, bid po). Week 26: HbA1c ≤7.0% higher in intervention (18.18%) vs. controls (10.81%), P > 0.05. Intervention showed greater TC, LDL-C, and TG reductions (P < 0.05). BMI and WC declines similar (P > 0.05). Pulmonary function (VC%, FEV1%, MVV%, TLC%) no differences (P > 0.05). Headaches more common in intervention (12.7%) vs. controls (2.0%, P < 0.05). No serious AEs. Oxidative/antioxidative balance correlated with pulmonary function.
text: At week 26, the combination of metformin (500 mg, bid po) and alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) showed a higher proportion of patients with HbA1c ≤7.0% (18.18%) compared to metformin alone (10.81%), though the difference was not statistically significant (P > 0.05).
intervention: metformin (500 mg, bid po) combined with alogliptin (25 mg, qd po)
outcome: proportion of patients with glycosylated hemoglobinA1c (HbA1c) ≤7.0%

memory: In a study comparing FAST and SLOW treatments, FAST significantly increased pulse rate (P = 0.022) and mean arterial pressure (MAP), systolic blood pressure (sBP), and diastolic blood pressure (dBP) (P = 0.035; P = 0.046; P = 0.035) during resuscitation. No significant differences were found in cardiac index (CI), systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI), oxygen delivery (DO2), or biochemical parameters like oxygen saturation, venous blood gas, or Nt-BNP between groups. However, CI paradoxically declined in 89% of FAST-treated participants during the last quarter of the resuscitation phase. No significant differences in DO2 were observed across time points or after adjusting for confounders.
text: FAST treatment significantly increased pulse rate, MAP, sBP, and dBP compared to SLOW treatment during resuscitation (P < 0.05). However, CI paradoxically declined in 89% of FAST-treated participants later in resuscitation, with no significant differences in DO2 or other hemodynamic or biochemical parameters. (Source: Study)

memory: Desmopressin vs. placebo in surgery showed no significant difference in bleeding rate (359.3 ± 266.2 vs. 406.3 ± 341.6; P = 0.208) or complications. Hb levels significantly decreased post-surgery (P = 0.0001), with no group difference (P = 0.134). Pre-surgery platelet levels were similar (P = 0.802), but post-surgery thrombocytopenia was higher in the control group (P = 0.012), with significant platelet changes between groups (P = 0.038). Source: [PMC5101425].
text: Desmopressin did not significantly affect thrombocytopenia rate compared to placebo (P = 0.012). Source: [PMC5101425].

memory: Resistance exercise (SR + RT) increased fat-free leg mass compared to control (9332 ± 254 vs. 9206 ± 258, P < 0.05). No significant changes were observed in femoral artery diameter, leg blood flow, or mean arterial pressure (Table 3). Heart rate was higher in the fed state (P < 0.0001), but no leg differences in blood flow timing. Plasma and intracellular free phenylalanine enrichments showed no significant differences across time (P = 0.07, P = 0.22) or between legs (P = 0.40). Source: [PMC4562579].
text: Resistance exercise (SR + RT) did not significantly affect leg blood flow compared to control, as no changes were observed in femoral artery diameter, leg blood flow, or mean arterial pressure (P > 0.05). Source: [PMC4562579].

memory: In a phase III trial, trametinib (2 mg daily) significantly improved PFS (4.8 vs. 1.5 months, HR 0.45, P < 0.001) and 6-month OS (81% vs. 67%, HR 0.54, P = 0.01) over chemotherapy in advanced BRAF-mutant melanoma [67]. A phase II trial showed selumetinib (75 mg twice daily) with docetaxel improved PFS (5.3 vs. 2.1 months) but no significant OS difference (9.4 vs. 5.2 months, HR 0.8, p = 0.21) in K-Ras mutant NSCLC [83].
text: Oral trametinib (2 mg daily) significantly improved 6-month overall survival (81% vs. 67%, HR 0.54, P = 0.01) compared to intravenous chemotherapy (dacarbazine or paclitaxel) in advanced BRAF-mutant melanoma [67].
comparator: intravenous chemotherapy consisting of either dacarbazine (1000mg/m2) or paclitaxel (175mg/m2), every 3weeks
outcome: At 6 months, the rate of overall survival

memory: A study compared Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) to placebo in adults with postprandial intestinal gas-related symptoms. GD showed significant improvements in GSRS abdominal pain subscore (p=0.046) and total score (p=0.048), with a trend for abdominal distension (p=0.061). Other endpoints, including SF-36v2 MCS and VAS-Gas, did not reach statistical significance, likely due to a strong placebo effect. The results suggest GD may offer some benefit for gastrointestinal symptoms, though broader efficacy remains inconclusive. Source: [PMC2784472].
text: The Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) group showed no significant improvement in GSRS VAS-Gas score compared to the placebo group (p>0.05). However, GD showed significant improvements in GSRS abdominal pain subscore (p=0.046) and total score (p=0.048). Source: [PMC2784472].
intervention: Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) group
outcome: Improvement in GSRS (Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale) VAS-Gas score - in adults with post prandial intestinal gas-related symptoms and no GI diagnoses

memory: D-serine administration significantly reduced legal errors on the Groton Maze Learning test (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03), with the most significant effect in the second trial (t = −3.13, p = 0.003). No change in illegal errors (p = 0.82) suggests improved performance was not due to test comprehension. Higher plasma D-serine levels correlated with better test performance (r² = −0.19, p = 0.009). D-serine had no significant effect on mood or other cognitive tests, including n-back working memory (p > 0.1), Set-Shifting task (p = 0.47), or visual attention (p > 0.7). Results are summarized in Table 2 of [PMC4914255].
text: D-serine significantly reduced legal errors on the Groton Maze Learning Test compared to control (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03), with the most significant effect in the second trial (t = −3.13, p = 0.003). This improvement was not due to test comprehension, as illegal errors remained unchanged (p = 0.82). Higher plasma D-serine levels correlated with better performance (r² = −0.19, p = 0.009). Source: [PMC4914255].
outcome: Groton Maze Learning Test legal errors

memory: A study [PMC5706318] compared C. gigantea extract, Listerine, and Chlorhexidine mouth rinses for reducing salivary Streptococcus mutans. All three significantly reduced S. mutans levels compared to a control group. Although there were numerical differences between the interventions, no statistically significant differences were found, suggesting similar efficacy among the mouth rinses in reducing S. mutans.
text: Chlorhexidine mouth rinse significantly reduces Streptococcus mutans count compared to control, as shown in a study (PMC5706318). However, it was similarly effective as other mouth rinses like Listerine and C. gigantea extract in reducing S. mutans levels.

memory: A study compared septal deviation patients who had septoplasty with healthy controls. Post-surgery, total nasal resistance (TNR) significantly decreased in patients (P=0.001), but no significant TNR differences were found between groups post-operatively. Voice parameters showed no significant group differences post-surgery, except for NHR (P=0.017), which was not linked to TNR changes. Analysis of /n/ and /a/ showed no significant pre/post or group differences, except for some formant frequencies (F3, F4) in /n/ (P=0.022, P=0.024, P=0.017), which were not clinically relevant. Most patients (61%) reported no change in voice quality post-surgery.
text: Septoplasty did not significantly improve "a" vowel quality compared to controls. While some formant frequencies in /n/ showed minor changes, they were not clinically relevant. Voice parameters, including NHR, showed no significant improvement in "a" vowel production post-surgery. (Source: study described)

memory: A phlebotomy training program was evaluated at four sites (CHC A, CHC B, CDC C, CDC D) against a control group. Pre-training sample rejection rates were 0.79%, 1.13%, 1.64%, and 1.36%, respectively. Post-training rates showed no significant change (p > 0.05). Preanalytical errors, including unaccountable errors (46 vs. 51, p = 0.73) and request form errors (25 vs. 26, p = 0.85), also remained unchanged. However, phlebotomy questionnaire scores improved significantly at all sites (p < 0.05). Source: PMC5419060.
text: The phlebotomy training program significantly improved phlebotomy questionnaire scores compared to the control (p < 0.05). However, it did not reduce sample rejection rates or preanalytical errors. Source: PMC5419060.

memory: OSS improved treatment appropriateness in the No-IMID subgroup for emergency patients (aRRR=1.98, p<0.001) and emergency/priority admissions (aRRR=2.12, p=0.006). In IMID-MLP, OSS enhanced malaria treatment (aRRR=1.26, p=0.005) and AFB-negative acute respiratory treatment (aRRR=2.04, p=0.005). It also reduced antimalarial prescriptions for negative tests (aRRR=0.49, p=0.004 in IMID-MLP; aRRR=0.65, p=0.006 overall). Overall, OSS improved three facility performance indicators. Source: [PMC4972969].
text: In IMID-MLP groups, OSS reduced antimalarial prescriptions for negative malaria tests (aRRR=0.49, p=0.004). Source: [PMC4972969].
outcome: proportion of patients with a negative malaria test result prescribed an antimalarial in integrated management of infectious diseases (IMID)- mid-level practitioners (MLP) group

memory: Aerobic exercise (75, 150, or 225 min/wk) improved cardiorespiratory fitness and cognitive functions, including Simple Attention and Visuospatial Processing, in a dose-dependent manner in per-protocol analyses. Simple Attention improved equivalently across all exercise groups versus controls. Visuospatial Processing showed a dose-response trend, with greater benefits in 150 and 225 min/wk groups. Adverse events were more common in 150 and 225 min/wk groups, mostly mild (e.g., musculoskeletal pain), with no severe AEs. Verbal Memory and Reasoning improved similarly across groups, suggesting practice effects. Intent-to-treat analyses showed dose-dependent improvements in fitness and disability, but limited cognitive benefits. Source: [PMC4497726].
text: Aerobic exercise (150 or 225 min/wk) significantly improved VO2 peak compared to no exercise, with greater improvements at higher doses. Source: [PMC4497726].

memory: Anemia (54%) and growth issues were similar between TSC and control groups. TSC improved sanitation coverage by 19 pp (41.4% vs 22.6%) and any IHL by 20 pp (44.1% vs 24.2%). Open defecation was lower in TSC villages for adults (mean diff: 9.5–10%) and children (<5 years: 5%), though 41% of TSC households with improved facilities still practiced open defecation. E. coli contamination in drinking water was slightly lower in TSC villages (77% vs 82%; p=0.050). Helminth infections showed no significant difference (p=0.001).
text: The Total Sanitation Campaign reduced open defecation compared to control, with lower rates among adults and children under 5, though 41% of TSC households with improved facilities still practiced it. (Source: Working notes)

memory: Group II (CHX + H2O2 1.5%) showed significantly lower stain intensity and plaque than Group I (CHX 0.2%) at 14 and 21 days (P < 0.05), with less plaque at all time points (P < 0.001). Group II had less stain than Group III (H2O2 + CHX) at 2-3 weeks, though not significant (P > 0.05). Group III had less plaque than Group I at 1-2 weeks (P < 0.05), but not at 3 weeks (P = 0.104). Stain intensity in Group III was lower than Group I but not significant. Source: PMC3800406.
text: Group III (H2O2 + CHX) showed less plaque than Group I (CHX 0.2%) at 1-2 weeks (P < 0.05), but not at 3 weeks (P = 0.104). Group II (CHX + H2O2 1.5%) had significantly lower plaque than Group I at 14 and 21 days (P < 0.05). Source: PMC3800406.
intervention: group III used hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) 1.5% followed by chlorhexidine (CHX)
comparator: group I rinsed with chlorhexidine (CHX) 0.2% alone
outcome: amount of plaque formed at end of week 3

memory: In CKD children, paricalcitol showed higher rates of achieving iPTH within KDOQI range (33.3% vs. 11.1%; P=0.128) and greater iPTH reduction (27.8% vs. 0%; P=0.045) compared to control. Mean iPTH decreased by -72.4 pg/mL (P<0.001). Placebo had higher adverse events (88.9% vs. 38.9%; P=0.005). No significant differences in calcium or phosphorus levels. Among stage 5 CKD patients, 61.5% achieved ≥30% iPTH reduction, with 21% experiencing hypercalcemia. Source: PMC5440538.
text: Paricalcitol did not significantly affect calcium levels compared to control in CKD children (PMC5440538). However, it reduced iPTH more effectively and was associated with higher adverse events in placebo group.

memory: A 24-week trial [PMC4749757] showed PR-fampridine (n=132) improved MSWS-12, TUG speed, and BBS scores vs. placebo (p < 0.05). More PR-fampridine patients (46%) reported PGIC improvement than placebo (26%, p=0.023). Adverse events were similar (77% vs. 75%), with UTIs more common in placebo and falls more in placebo. Balance disorder, gait disturbance, and dizziness were more frequent with PR-fampridine. No significant differences in EQ-5D-5L. PR-fampridine was well tolerated.
text: Prolonged-release fampridine significantly improved TUG speed compared to placebo over 24 weeks (p < 0.05) [PMC4749757]. Adverse events were similar, though PR-fampridine had more reports of balance issues and dizziness.
outcome: Improvement in Timed Up and Go (TUG) speed during 24 weeks

memory: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced mean SMPR vs. placebo (P=0.004), driven by fewer radiotherapy/surgery events (P<0.001, P=0.037). No significant fracture difference (P=0.195). Urinary CTx decreased by −77.3% vs. +11.0% (P<0.001). Risk of skeletal events reduced by 38% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001). Mean events and measurement periods with events were lower (P=0.008, 0.015). Median time to first event was 90.3 vs. 64.9 weeks (P=0.089). [PMC2409647]
text: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced the risk of skeletal events by 38% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001) compared to placebo, with fewer radiotherapy/surgery events. No significant difference in fracture rates was observed (P=0.195). [PMC2409647]
outcome: risk reduction for a skeletal event

memory: 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% significantly improved TSQM satisfaction and effectiveness (P < 0.01) at 8 weeks vs. vehicle. CCC was higher with 5-FU (49.5% vs. 18.2%, P=0.0006), and more patients achieved PC (69.5% vs. 34.6%, P < 0.0001). However, 5-FU had higher adverse event rates (99.1% vs. 83.6%). No significant differences in TSQM convenience or side effect scores. DLQI total score improved more with vehicle due to 5-FU-related skin reactions.
text: The 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% combination significantly increased treatment-emergent adverse events (99.1% vs. 83.6%) compared to vehicle, likely due to higher skin reactions, as indicated by greater DLQI improvements with vehicle.

memory: Bupropion, NRT, and their combination show similar smoking cessation effectiveness with behavioral support (27.9%, 24.2%, 24.2%; OR = 1.21, 95% CI = 0.883–1.67). Bupropion may be more effective for depressed smokers (29.8% vs. 18.5%). NRT success rates were similar across product types (26.9% for patches). No significant differences in effectiveness were found across sites or between direct and GP-prescribed bupropion. Bupropion was associated with more unwanted symptoms.
text: Bupropion and NRT have similar effectiveness for smoking cessation with behavioral support (27.9% vs. 24.2%). Bupropion may be more effective for depressed smokers. NRT success rates were similar across product types. Bupropion was linked to more unwanted symptoms.

memory: The 11-week FIFA 11 for Health programme (IG) showed greater reductions in systolic blood pressure (−3.5 vs 0.9 mm Hg), mean arterial blood pressure (−1.9 vs 0.4 mm Hg), BMI (−0.02 vs 0.13 kg/m²), and body fat percentage (−0.83% vs −0.04%) compared to control (CG) (p<0.05). IG also improved 20 m sprint time (4.09±0.29 to 4.06±0.28 s) and YYIR1C performance (852±464 to 896±517 m), but these changes were not significantly different from CG. Balance and jump performance remained unchanged in both groups (PMC5136709).
text: The FIFA 11 for Health programme significantly reduced body fat percentage (−0.83%) compared to control (−0.04%) (p<0.05) (PMC5136709).

memory: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) vs. placebo showed no significant microbiota differences at 6 months. By 18 months, LGG increased butyrate-producing Anaerostipes caccae et rel (2.89% vs. 1.18%, p=0.03) and Eubacterium ventriosum et rel (0.17% vs. 0.11%, p=0.04). Placebo had higher Clostridium difficile et rel (1.19% vs. 0.78%, p=0.047). Source: PMC3563445, Analysis Of The Intestinal Microbiota Composition In Relation To The Health Status.
text: At 18 months, LGG vs. placebo showed higher butyrate-producing microbes but lower Clostridium difficile et rel (1.19% vs. 0.78%, p=0.047). Source: PMC3563445.
outcome: Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age

memory: In a study [PMC5761719], 30.1% of 531 patients were classified as minimal-risk using the PROMISE tool compared to the CADC model. PROMISE patients had lower pre-test obstructive CAD probability (30.0% vs 47.0%, p < 0.001) and fewer typical angina symptoms (24.1% vs 42.6%, p < 0.001). PROMISE showed improved discrimination (c-statistic 0.785 vs 0.730, p < 0.001) and better calibration (χ2 5.6, HL p = 0.692) after revision, while CADC had poor calibration (χ2 1010.1, HL p < 0.001).
text: Patients classified as minimal-risk using the PROMISE tool had a lower pre-test probability of obstructive CAD (30.0%) compared to the remainder of the cohort (47.0%, p < 0.001) [PMC5761719].

memory: A study compared partial matrix excision (Group I) and segmental phenolization (Group II). Moderate postoperative pain occurred in 3 Group I and 2 Group II patients, managed with analgesics for 3 days; pain differences were not significant (P > 0.05). No soft tissue infections were reported. Recurrence and complication rates also showed no significant difference (P = 0.688). Group II had a significantly shorter time to return to normal daily activities (P < 0.05), which was the primary success criterion.
text: Partial matrix excision and segmental phenolization showed no significant difference in postoperative complications (P > 0.05). However, segmental phenolization allowed a faster return to daily activities (P < 0.05).

memory: KOS nasal treatment significantly reduced pain compared to placebo, with VAS scores decreasing from 5.5 to 1.2 (active) vs. 4.9 to 3.9 (placebo), a 3.3-point difference (P < .001). The effect was significant at 5 minutes (1.9 points, P = .007) and 2 hours post-treatment (3.7 points, P < .001). Over 2 months, migraine days decreased slightly in the active group but not significantly compared to placebo (P = .39, .53). Trends indicated lower pain intensity and duration in the active group, though not statistically significant (P = .42, .37). Source: PMC4312979.
text: Kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity significantly reduced pain scores compared to placebo, with a 3.3-point decrease in VAS scores (P < .001). The effect was significant at 5 minutes and 2 hours post-treatment. Source: PMC4312979.
intervention: kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity

memory: A community-based intervention study found no significant difference in SF-12 PCS at 6 months compared to usual care. The intervention group showed significant improvements in SF-12 MCS, general health subdomain, and SDSCA. No significant differences in total costs were observed, though some cost categories favored the intervention. Multiple imputation confirmed complete-case findings. No significant changes were noted in CES-D, GAD-7, or self-efficacy. Source: [PMC5836873].
text: A community-based intervention showed no significant difference in SF-12 PCS compared to usual care but improved SF-12 MCS and SDSCA. No significant changes were found in CES-D, GAD-7, or self-efficacy. Source: [PMC5836873].
outcome: 12‐item Short‐Form Health Survey (SF‐12), Mental Component Summary (MCS), Summary of Diabetes Self‐Care Activities (SDSCA)

memory: Study [PMC2721929] evaluated bladder training (BT), tolterodine (To), and their combination (Co) for overactive bladder (OAB). All groups showed reduced frequency and nocturia, with Co showing the greatest improvement (33.5% and 66.3% decrease, p<0.05). Urgency scores improved by 44.8% (BT), 62.2% (To), and 60.2% (Co), with To and Co outperforming BT (p<0.05). No difference between To and Co in urgency improvement. Satisfaction scores were 1.5 (BT), 1.4 (To), and 1.3 (Co), with higher improvement in Co. Combination therapy was more effective than monotherapies, though To alone may be first-line.
text: Bladder training plus tolterodine (Co) significantly reduced micturition frequency more than tolterodine alone (To) (33.5% vs. no specific To improvement noted, p<0.05). Co also showed greater improvement in nocturia and patient satisfaction. (Source: PMC2721929)

memory: A study compared remifentanil 0.3 (RH), remifentanil 0.05 (RL), and remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5 (KRH). Demographics and anesthetic parameters were similar, except RL had higher end-tidal desflurane. RH showed increased analgesic consumption, higher NRS scores at 6 and 24 hours, and greater cumulative fentanyl use compared to other groups. Touch-Test sensory evaluation was more negative in RH. No dropouts occurred, and PACU ketorolac use was higher in RH than in RL.
text: Remifentanil 0.3 (RH) resulted in more negative Touch-Test sensory evaluations compared to remifentanil 0.05 (RL) and remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5 (KRH). RH also showed higher analgesic consumption and NRS scores, suggesting less effective postoperative sensory recovery (source: study).
comparator: Remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5 (group KRH) or remifentanil 0.05 (Group RL)
outcome: Value of the Touch-Test sensory evaluation after surgery

memory: A study comparing exercise training to control found no significant differences in BP, HDL cholesterol, or CRP changes. However, LDL cholesterol increased in the exercise group compared to controls (p = 0.020). Among patients with carotid plaques, LDL cholesterol increased in the exercise group [0.20 mmol/L (0.00 to 0.41) vs −0.13 mmol/L (−0.37 to 0.12), p = 0.044], but not in those without plaques (p = 0.40). Source: PMC4724125.
text: Exercise training did not significantly affect HDL cholesterol compared to control. Source: PMC4724125.

memory: Heated infusions reduced spontaneous breath time (4.06 vs 4.47 min, P=0.042), eye opening (6.72 vs 8.66 min, P<0.001), consciousness recovery (9.91 vs 11.19 min, P=0.004), and extubation time (10.09 vs 11.13 min, P=0.015) compared to control. No difference in hospital stay. Operation time was longer in the control group (3.094 vs 2.925 min, P<0.05). Source: PMC5380277.
text: Heated infusions significantly reduced consciousness recovery time compared to control (9.91 vs 11.19 min, P=0.004). Source: PMC5380277.

memory: A study compared Charité artificial disc (intervention) with ALIF using BAK cages (control). Infection rates were higher in the intervention group (12.7% vs. 8.1%), with superficial wound infections 3 times higher (6.3% vs. 2.0%), though not statistically significant (P = .103). No deep infections were reported. The control group had 3.0% iliac crest donor site infections. Major neurological complications were similar (4.4% vs. 4.0%). Approach-related complications were 9.8% in the intervention group and 10.1% in the control. Pseudarthrosis occurred in 9.1% of the control group. Retrograde ejaculation was 3.3% in the intervention group and 5.5% in the control (P = .515).
text: The Charité artificial disc was associated with a higher rate of superficial wound infection compared to ALIF with BAK cages (6.3% vs. 2.0%), though not statistically significant (P = .103).

memory: In E2, GBB increased by 12.7% (p=0.044) within normal range; in ET, GBB decreased 2.3–1.8 mm (p=0.007), with no group difference at end. GBB maintained femoral neck BMD (+1.3% vs. placebo, p=0.007) and increased Ward's triangle BMD (+2.3% vs. −1.1%, p<0.05). No significant ECG or vital sign changes. Source: PMC3549413.
text: The placebo group showed a decrease in BMD at 6 months, while the treatment group maintained femoral neck BMD (+1.3% vs. placebo, p=0.007) and increased Ward's triangle BMD (+2.3% vs. −1.1%, p<0.05). Source: PMC3549413.
outcome: bone mineral density (BMD) At the 6-month time point

memory: A study compared 1200 mg cranberry extract (6 weeks) with a placebo. Exercise significantly increased IL-6 post-exercise, which normalized after 24 hours (p < 0.001). Cranberry had no significant effect on IL-6 (p = 0.051). TAC was influenced by both exercise and cranberry; the cranberry group had higher TAC at rest, post-exercise, and post-recovery compared to placebo. However, both groups showed a post-exercise TAC decrease at Trial II. Cranberry had no effect on serum iron (p = 0.516), though exercise increased it in both groups. Myoglobin levels were only affected by exercise (p < 0.001). Source: PMC5330006.
text: Receiving 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks significantly increased total antioxidant capacity (TAC) at rest, post-exercise, and post-recovery compared to placebo (PMC5330006).
intervention: receiving 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks

memory: A study compared Propolis gel, Triamcinolone acetonide, and no treatment for pain and erythema. All interventions significantly reduced pain and erythema scores from baseline to second follow-up compared to no treatment (P = 0.000). No significant difference was found between Propolis gel and Triamcinolone acetonide (P = 0.255). None of the interventions outperformed the others significantly. Source: PMC5863413.
text: Propolis gel significantly reduced pain compared to no treatment (P = 0.000). It showed similar efficacy to Triamcinolone acetonide, with no significant difference between them (P = 0.255). Source: PMC5863413.

memory: A study compared ESM-I (6 weeks ESM + weekly feedback) with ESM without feedback and treatment as usual. At 32 weeks, HDRS scores were 3 units lower in ESM-I compared to comparator groups (B = −3.1, p = 0.051, intention-to-treat), though not statistically significant. No significant differences in symptomatic remission were found between ESM-I and comparator groups (OR = 2.65, p = 0.12; OR = 1.84, p = 0.29). ESM-I also showed no difference compared to pseudo-intervention (B = −1.13, p = 0.47). Source: [PMC5747107].
text: The study found no significant effect of ESM-I (6 weeks ESM + weekly feedback) on the rate of symptomatic remission compared to ESM without feedback (OR = 2.65, p = 0.12) or pseudo-intervention (B = −1.13, p = 0.47). Source: [PMC5747107].
intervention: ESM-I consisting of six weeks of ESM combined with weekly feedback regarding the individual’s positive affective experiences
comparator: (ii) six weeks of ESM without feedback,

memory: In a study comparing hyaluronic acid (HA) to a control, HA showed significantly longer bleeding times (7.17±1.36 vs. 5.64±1.46 min, p<0.05). No significant differences in swelling (pre-op, 1 hour, 7th day) or pain (MIO and VAS) were observed between groups, though HA showed increased swelling on day 3 (p<0.05). Salivary TF levels in the HA group were significantly lower after 1 week compared to baseline (p<0.05), with T2 showing lower TF than T0 and T1. Control group TF levels remained stable across time points.
text: Hyaluronic acid (HA) significantly reduced salivary tissue factor (TF) levels after 1 week compared to baseline (p<0.05), with lower TF at T2 than T0 and T1. Control group TF levels remained stable over time.

memory: Source [PMC4045368]: A study (n=41, 13.4-month follow-up) compared locking vs. nonlocking plates for tibial plateau fractures. No significant differences were found in fracture types (Schatzker/AO), follow-up duration, or range of motion (P=0.219). Locking plates showed better knee scores (80.20 vs. 72.52, P=0.039), lower VAS pain scores (4.45 vs. 6.00, P=0.046), and improved functional scores (77.26 vs. 69.55, P=0.026). No significant differences in infection rates or fracture severity classifications were observed.
text: Locking plate fixation results in better mean knee scores at follow-up compared to nonlocking plate fixation (80.20 vs. 72.52, P=0.039) according to a study with a 13.4-month follow-up (PMC4045368).

memory: A study found that Ashwagandha (KSM-66) improved Quality of Life (QOL) subdomains more than placebo at 12 weeks (P < 0.05), with environmental impact showing significant improvement at 12 weeks (P < 0.01), not at 8 weeks. Vital signs remained stable in both groups. Ashwagandha also increased mean VO2 max significantly more than placebo at 8 weeks (4.91 vs. 1.42) and 12 weeks (5.67 vs. 1.86; P < 0.0001). These results suggest Ashwagandha enhances QOL and cardiorespiratory fitness over 12 weeks. Source: [PMC4687242].
text: Ashwagandha (KSM-66) significantly increased mean VO2 max more than placebo after 8 weeks (4.91 vs. 1.42; P < 0.0001). Source: [PMC4687242].
outcome: Increase from baseline in the mean VO2 max after 8 weeks

memory: A 12-week study compared sitagliptin and voglibose, finding both improved ΔFMD similarly after adjusting for baseline FMD, age, sex, smoking, diabetes duration, and BMI. No group differences were observed in HbA1c, GIP, GLP-1, C-peptide, lipid profile, oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, or eGFR. Sitagliptin significantly increased circulating CD34 levels (endothelial progenitor cell marker) compared to voglibose (P < 0.05). These results are from Table 3 and Figure 3 of [PMC4149239].
text: Sitagliptin and voglibose had similar effects on gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) levels, with no significant group differences observed in GIP or other markers. This is based on a 12-week study (PMC4149239).

memory: PBF showed higher job satisfaction than C1 and C2, though not as high as expected. C1 had 8.64% (p < 0.05) lower compensation satisfaction than PBF, while C2 had 3.88% (p < 0.1) lower than C1. PBF had 4.75% (p < 0.05) higher overall job satisfaction than C2, and C1 had 10.31% (p < 0.05) higher than C2. PBF had 0.10 (p < 0.05) fewer administrators leaving than C1 and 0.14 (p < 0.05) fewer nurses than C2. No significant differences in compensation or attrition between C1 and C2. Source: PMC5331731.
text: Performance-based financing (PBF) was associated with 0.10 (p < 0.05) fewer administrators leaving health centers compared to control 1 (C1). Source: PMC5331731.
outcome: administrators on average who left health centers

memory: In a study [PMC5808396], women with moderate baseline felt stigma (mean = 1.98) were randomized to Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) or individual support (IS). CPT led to significantly greater stigma reduction at treatment end (B = −0.44, p = 0.02) and a sustained advantage at 6 months (B = −0.45, p = 0.12). Both groups showed stigma reduction over time. Results suggest CPT is more effective than IS in reducing felt stigma, with effects lasting at least six months. Table 2 supports these findings.
text: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) is more effective than individual support in reducing felt stigma, with significant reductions at treatment end (B = −0.44, p = 0.02) and sustained advantages at 6 months (B = −0.45, p = 0.12) [PMC5808396].

memory: In a study on ischemia-reperfusion injury in isolated rat hearts, lixisenatide significantly reduced infarct size compared to placebo (98 ± 9 mm² vs. 162 ± 12 mm², p < 0.05, n=10-11), with a 36% reduction in the infarct area to risk area ratio. Left ventricular total area and risk area were not significantly different between groups. Right ventricular wall thickness normalized to sham values with lixisenatide, while left-ventricular wall thickness was unaffected. No changes in rate pressure product, coronary flow, cardiac dilatation, or septal wall thickness were observed. Source: [PMC3637243].
text: Lixisenatide significantly reduced infarct size compared to control in isolated rat hearts, decreasing the infarct area to risk area ratio by 36% (p < 0.05). Left ventricular risk area was not significantly different between groups. Source: [PMC3637243].

memory: A study compared PEG-lactulose (20-30g lactulose + 280g PEG in 4L water, single dose) with lactulose alone (oral, nasogastric, or rectal enema) for improving HESA scores. PEG-lactulose showed greater improvement after 24 hours (p=0.04), with 20 vs. 14 patients showing at least a 1-point decrease (p=0.05). No significant difference in blood ammonia levels (p=0.858). PEG-lactulose reduced hospital stay overall (p=0.03), with a significant effect in women (p=0.01). Source: [PMC5308129].
text: The PEG–lactulose group showed no significant difference in blood ammonia levels compared to lactulose alone (p=0.858). Source: [PMC5308129].
intervention: PEG–lactulose group received the 20-30 grams of lactulose of oral or rectal lactulose, plus 280 grams of PEG in 4 liters of water orally as a single dose in 30-120 minutes
comparator: 20-30 grams of lactulose orally or by a nasogastric tube, or 200 grams of lactulose enema by a rectal tube

memory: A study assessed SCM and LC thickness during maximal voluntary isometric contractions at 10%, 50%, and 80% intensity. SCM thickness did not significantly change across intensities (p>0.05). LC thickness significantly increased with higher masticatory muscle contraction intensity (80% vs. 10%) during concurrent training compared to deep cervical flexor training alone (p<0.05).
text: An 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction significantly increases longus colli thickness compared to 10% (p<0.05), while SCM thickness remains unchanged across intensities (p>0.05).

memory: A study of 176 patients (median age 28) compared ampicillin/sulbactam with cefuroxime. No significant differences were observed in postoperative infections (7.4% total; 5.9% with cefuroxime, 8.8% with ampicillin/sulbactam, p=0.6) or post-cesarean endometritis (2.3% vs. 2.4%, p=1). Hospitalization duration was similar between groups (median 4 days, IQR 4-4). Source: [PMC3009979].
text: Ampicillin/sulbactam and cefuroxime had similar effects on hospitalization duration (median 4 days, IQR 4-4) in a study of 176 patients. No significant differences were observed. Source: [PMC3009979].

memory: A study compared flaxseed and wheat bran supplementation, finding no significant changes in BMI, body weight, or waist circumference. Flaxseed significantly lowered fasting plasma glucose (5.92 ± 0.31 vs. 4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L) compared to wheat bran. Wheat bran significantly reduced plasma insulin (p = 0.026). No differences were observed in inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, TNF-α, hs-CRP) or nutrient intake. Baseline energy intake was 1875 ± 798 kcal/d, with 17%, 38%, and 45% from protein, fat, and carbohydrates, respectively. No significant relationships were found between weight change and glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, or inflammatory markers.
text: Flaxseed significantly lowers fasting plasma glucose compared to wheat bran (5.92 ± 0.31 vs. 4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L). Wheat bran reduced plasma insulin (p = 0.026), but no differences were observed in inflammatory markers or nutrient intake.

memory: LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) significantly reduced ACTH-stimulated aldosterone by 41–64% vs. 7% with placebo (P < 0.001), unlike eplerenone 100 mg, which increased it by 63%. LCI699 increased 11-deoxycortisol by 942–584% at ≥100 mg. At 0.5–3 mg, it reduced plasma aldosterone by 47–63% at 12 h (P < 0.001). 24-h urinary cortisol decreased 34–42% with 30–200 mg LCI699 (P ≤ 0.001). No dose-dependence in aldosterone effects was observed.
text: LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration at 12 h by 47–63% compared to placebo (P < 0.001). This effect was not dose-dependent.

memory: A 12-month study compared system-oriented therapy to a reference intervention, finding no significant differences in average bed days or hospitalization duration. System-oriented therapy showed non-significant trends toward improved compliance and PANSS scores. It significantly prolonged time to readmission (P=0.049). Attrition was higher in the reference group (15/40 vs 4/30, P=0.017). Only 43% of system-oriented interventions met standards. Adverse events and time to first readmission differed significantly between groups. Compliance was measured using a project-specific scale with multiple imputation for missing values.
text: System-oriented therapy showed a significant prolongation of time to readmission (P=0.049) compared to reference intervention, with higher retention (P=0.017). However, no significant differences were found in bed days or hospitalization duration. Compliance and PANSS scores showed non-significant trends toward improvement.

memory: A study compared IPE (4g/day) to placebo in diabetic patients (median baseline A1c 6.8%) and found IPE significantly reduced multiple lipid and inflammatory markers, including TG, non-HDL-C, VLDL-C, lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2, Apo B, total cholesterol, HDL-C, VLDL-TG, oxidized LDL, and remnant-like particle cholesterol across all diabetes groups. LDL-C decreased in the total diabetes group, and hsCRP decreased in total and less-controlled diabetes groups, with greater reductions in hsCRP and Apo B in less-controlled diabetes. No significant increases in fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR were observed. Baseline hsCRP was higher in total and less-controlled diabetes groups.
text: IPE (4g/day) did not significantly increase fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR in diabetic patients compared to placebo, suggesting it is safe regarding glycemic control. The study showed significant reductions in lipid and inflammatory markers, with greater effects in less-controlled diabetes. Source: Study cited in working notes.
outcome: fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or homeostasis model assessment-estimated insulin total (all subjects with diabetes—overall median baseline glycosylated hemoglobin A1c [A1c] = 6.8%), better-controlled diabetes (below median baseline A1c), and less-controlled diabetes (above median baseline A1c).

memory: rtfMRI-nf from left amygdala (LA) vs. HIPS showed greater happiness (t=2.33, p=0.01) and reduced anxiety (t=2.58, p=0.03) in the experimental group. LA group had reduced POMS depression (t=2.12, p=0.025) and increased VAS happiness (t=3.04, p=0.005), along with reduced anger, trait/state anxiety, restlessness, and irritability (ps<0.05). Whole brain analysis revealed increased activity in left superior temporal gyrus, temporal polar cortex, and right thalamus during transfer run. No other ratings changed significantly. Source: PMC3921228.
text: rtfMRI-nf from left amygdala (LA) showed greater happiness and reduced state anxiety compared to HIPS (t=2.58, p=0.03). LA also reduced depression, anger, and irritability (ps<0.05). Source: PMC3921228.
comparator: rtfMRI-nf from the horizontal segment of the intraparietal sulcus (HIPS

memory: A 12-week study found that dextromethorphan (DM60) improved treatment retention and reduced plasma morphine levels compared to placebo. TNF-α levels were significantly lower in the DM60 group. No significant differences were observed in plasma cytokine levels, BDNF levels, or methadone dose requirements between groups. Results remained consistent across study sections.
text: Dextromethorphan (DM60) improved treatment retention and reduced plasma morphine levels compared to placebo in a 12-week study. TNF-α levels were significantly lower in the DM60 group, with no significant differences in other measured parameters.
