memory: No significant differences in C-reactive protein or serum ferritin levels between Agave fructans, formula, and breast milk groups (Wilcoxon p=0.05; Fisher T-Test p>0.05; Table 3). Salivary IgA showed significant differences between Agave fructans and formula groups (p<0.05; p<0.01). Source: nutrients-07-05442-t003_Table 3.
text: There is no significant effect of Agave derived fructans compared with Formula on C-Reactive Protein (Wilcoxon p=0.05; Fisher T-Test p>0.05). Source: nutrients-07-05442-t003_Table 3.

memory: A 12-week study in CKD patients with low vitamin D found that calcitriol + calcium did not significantly reduce pro-inflammatory markers (IL-6, hs-CRP) compared to calcium alone, except for non-diabetics showing reduced IL-6. Calcitriol helped stabilize anti-inflammatory IL-10 levels (p=0.06), while the calcium group experienced significant IL-10 reduction. Serum 25-OHD levels increased in the Vitamin D + C group (p=0.001). Serum calcium levels were elevated but within normal ranges. Anti-inflammatory effects were independent of serum vitamin D levels. Diabetic CKD patients benefited from calcium with or without calcitriol, while non-diabetics needed calcitriol for added benefit. Findings align with previous studies in chronic heart failure patients.
text: In CKD patients, "Vitamin D + Calcium" did not significantly alter serum IL-10 compared to "Calcium" alone. However, "Calcium" alone caused a significant reduction in IL-10, while "Vitamin D + Calcium" stabilized IL-10 levels (p=0.06). Source: 12-week study in CKD patients.

memory: A study [PMC4092926] replaced soybean meal with sunflower cake in diets of 1/2 Boer goats at 0, 33, 66, and 100% DM substitution levels. Slaughter results showed no significant differences (p>0.05) in body weight, carcass weights, yields, rib eye area, or other carcass traits across treatments. Substitution up to 100% did not affect quantitative carcass parameters, suggesting it could be recommended without altering these traits. Muscle:fat and muscle:bone ratios, key for commercial value, were also unaffected. Muscle growth was isometric, while fat deposition occurred later, suggesting younger animals may have better muscle:fat ratios. Consistent body weights across treatments indicated uniform carcass characteristics.
text: A study found no significant differences (p>0.05) in body weight, carcass yields, or rib eye area when sunflower cake replaced soybean meal in goat diets up to 100% substitution. Carcass traits remained unaffected, suggesting sunflower cake can replace soybean meal without altering these parameters.
outcome: Weights, carcass yields, rib eye area of goats

memory: Sevoflurane-fentanyl vs. isoflurane-fentanyl anesthesia: Fentanyl boluses (1.5 μg/kg) every 30–40 min similarly reduced SSI in both groups, though SSI remained higher in the sevoflurane group. Nociceptive stimuli increased SSI. Pre-fentanyl, MAC and SE were similar (MAC: 0.74 vs. 0.77; SE: 43.5 vs. 45.2), but HR differed (70.6 vs. 64.9, P < .01). Post-fentanyl, HR, SE changes were similar, and MAC remained stable. Source: PMC2911596.
text: Before fentanyl boluses, MAC and SE values were similar between sevoflurane-fentanyl and isoflurane-fentanyl anesthesia (MAC: 0.74 vs. 0.77; SE: 43.5 vs. 45.2). Source: PMC2911596.
outcome: MAC and SE values before fentanyl boluses

memory: A study compared VOO, OVOO, and FOO on lipid and blood pressure profiles. VOO increased fasting plasma triacylglycerol (p=0.037) and decreased SBP (p=0.019). OVOO increased triacylglycerol (p=0.002) and significantly raised HDLc (p=0.041), particularly in females (p=0.005). FOO increased total cholesterol (p=0.021) and raised SBP (p=0.004). LDLc remained unchanged across all groups. No differences in energy or nutrient intake were noted. All biomarkers stayed within normal ranges.
text: Both VOO and OVOO increased fasting plasma triacylglycerol levels (p=0.037 and p=0.002, respectively), while FOO had no significant effect on triacylglycerol.
intervention: Virgin olive oil (VOO) and Optimized virgin olive oil (OVOO)

memory: Intervention: Intimate partner prevention vs. control. Outcomes: Partner sexual violence (ARR 0.52, 95% CI 0.18-1.51, not significant); decreased intentions to use physical IPV (ARR 0.83, 95% CI 0.66-1.06); improved attitudes toward sexual IPV (ARR 1.21, 95% CI 0.77-1.91). Believing a woman can refuse sex in all circumstances: 27% vs. 24% (1.26, 0.83-1.91). Participation in household tasks: ARR 2.47 (1.24-4.90). Hostility management: ARR 1.3 (1.06-1.58). Source: [PMC4007144].
text: The "Intimate partner prevention intervention" was associated with improved hostility management compared to the control group (ARR 1.3, 95% CI 1.06-1.58). Source: [PMC4007144].

memory: Source: PMC5447816. High E scores correlated with faster suturing test completion (β = -418.2, P = 0.0118). Low A scores showed a non-significant trend for faster completion (β = -290.9, P = 0.057). Simulator-learning group had significantly better length scores on NUMSAS (P = 0.02673) compared to video-learning, though overall NUMSAS scores were not significantly different (P = 0.11287). Simulator group completed tasks significantly faster than video group. No significant relationships found between N, O, and C traits and suturing performance.
text: High E scores correlate with faster suturing test completion (β = -418.2, P = 0.0118) compared to average E scores, according to PMC5447816. No significant effects were found for low A scores or other personality traits on completion time.

memory: Erlotinib vs. placebo in a clinical trial [PMC4112798]. Neurological progression-free survival (nPFS): HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.59–1.54; P=0.84), median 1.6 months in both arms. Overall survival (OS): median 2.9 vs. 3.4 months, HR 0.95 (0.58–1.55; P=0.83). No quality of life differences (P≥0.40). Low EGFR mutation rate (2.9%). Adverse events were similar (70%), except for rash (20% vs. 5%) and fatigue (17.5% vs. 35%).
text: A clinical trial [PMC4112798] found no significant differences in quality of life between Erlotinib and placebo (P≥0.40). Other outcomes, including neurological progression-free survival and overall survival, also showed no significant differences. Adverse events were similar, except for rash and fatigue.

memory: Source: PMC4794540. A six-month yogic intervention combined with medication significantly improved anxiety (P<0.01), depression (P<0.02), positive well-being (P<0.01), general health (P<0.04), and vitality (P<0.02) compared to medication alone. No significant difference in self-control was found between the intervention and control groups. Results from Table 3.
text: A six-month yogic intervention combined with medication significantly improved positive well-being and vitality scores (P<0.01 and P<0.02, respectively) compared to prescribed medication alone, according to PMC4794540.

memory: A study compared laryngeal mask (LM) and endotracheal intubation (ETI) in ventilation. No significant differences were found in first attempt success rate (LM, 94.4% vs. ETI, 90.6%), insertion time (LM, 7.58 ± 1.16 s vs. ETI, 7.89 ± 1.52 s), Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes, response time, ventilation time, or adverse events (LM, n=3 vs. ETI, n=4). However, LM had a lower successful resuscitation rate (86.1% vs. 96.9%). These findings are from the Abstract > Results section of [PMC4727391].
text: A study found no significant differences in adverse events between laryngeal mask (LM) and endotracheal intubation (ETI) ventilation. Both had similar rates of adverse events (LM, n=3 vs. ETI, n=4). Source: [PMC4727391].

memory: A diet intervention (D) significantly reduced waist circumference (P=0.001), total cholesterol (P=0.007), LDL-cholesterol (P=0.003), and fasting insulin (P=0.042) at 12 weeks, with sustained waist circumference reduction (P<0.001), insulin decrease (P=0.024), and increased HDL-cholesterol (P=0.005) at 1 year. No significant changes were observed for the exercise intervention (E) on VO2 max, blood lipids, glucose, or inflammation markers. No interaction effects between D and E were found for cardiovascular risk outcomes. D had no effect on systolic or diastolic blood pressure or IGF-1. Source: PMC3917884.
text: The diet intervention significantly reduced LDL cholesterol (P=0.003) compared to control. Source: PMC3917884.

memory: ZA10 (zhibitai 480 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg) had similar adverse events (abdominal distension, nausea, vomiting, hunger) as A20 and A40 (P > 0.05). No significant differences in creatine kinase (CK) levels or myopathy incidence among groups (P > 0.05). CT-1 and hs-CRP significantly decreased after 4 and 8 weeks in all groups (P < 0.01 or 0.05), with no group differences (P > 0.05). Triglycerides, TC, LDL-C, and ApoB100 decreased similarly in ZA10 and A40 (P > 0.05). Source: PMC5319516.
text: The ZA10 group showed no significant differences in creatine kinase levels or myopathy incidence compared to A20 or A40 groups (P > 0.05). Source: PMC5319516.
comparator: atorvastatin 20 mg (A20 group) or atorvastatin 40 mg (A40 group)

memory: A study assessed p-synephrine (50 mg) and flavonoid combinations (naringin, hesperidin) against placebo. P-synephrine alone increased RMR by 65 kcal. Adding 600 mg naringin raised RMR to 129 kcal, and 100 mg hesperidin further increased it to 183 kcal (p<0.02). However, 1000 mg hesperidin only increased RMR by 79 kcal. No significant changes in heart rate, blood pressure, or symptoms were observed. The combination of p-synephrine, naringin, and 100 mg hesperidin increased RMR without physiological stress, suggesting potential as a weight control agent, though long-term studies are needed.
text: P-synephrine (50 mg) alone increased RMR by 65 kcal compared to placebo (p<0.02). No significant changes in heart rate, blood pressure, or symptoms were observed.

memory: In a study comparing 2 g YM to placebo, YM showed higher total TEE AUC (85.60 vs. 82.13, p < 0.001) with no HR differences. YM increased FAO during 30-min exercise (p = 0.037). YM reduced Hunger (p = 0.019) and Prospective eating (p = 0.022) scores, with a trend for reduced desire to eat (p = 0.079), but no effect on fullness. Time effects were significant for TEE and FAO but not satiety measures. No YM-time interaction was found for satiety. Resting data showed a slight reduction in prospective eating with YM (p = 0.046).
text: 2 g YM reduced prospective eating scores compared to placebo (p = 0.022), with a trend for reduced desire to eat (p = 0.079). This effect was observed during exercise and at rest (p = 0.046).

memory: A study compared an underwater treadmill group to a control group, both showing significant post-intervention reductions in anteroposterior, mediolateral, and total postural sway (p<0.05), with no significant group differences. Static and dynamic balance improved significantly in both groups (p<0.05), though no between-group differences were observed. Baseline comparisons also revealed significant improvements in dynamic balance and reductions in postural sway for both groups.
text: Both the underwater treadmill group and control group showed significant reductions in anteroposterior, mediolateral, and total postural sway compared to baseline (p<0.05). No significant differences were found between the groups.
outcome: anteroposterior, mediolateral and total postural sway

memory: A study compared Lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg (Lan ATG) and lanreotide microparticles 30 mg (Lan MP) in acromegaly patients. Lan ATG demonstrated superior symptom control, with significant improvements in hyperhidrosis (P < 0.001) and headache (P < 0.001). At treatment end, 40% of Lan ATG patients achieved both GH < 2.5 ng/ml and normalized IGF-1, compared to 35% with Lan MP. GH levels were lower with Lan ATG (3.8 ng/ml) than with Lan MP (4.3 ng/ml; P < 0.001). Plasma IGF-1 levels showed no significant changes. Lan ATG also had better treatment acceptance and symptom control.
text: Lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg showed superior symptom control compared to lanreotide microparticles, with significant improvements in hyperhidrosis and headache (P < 0.001). It also achieved better GH suppression and higher rates of normalized IGF-1.

memory: Perindopril vs. placebo: FMD increased from 2.6% to 3.3% over 36 months in perindopril, compared to 2.8% to 3.0% in placebo (0.55% higher, p=0.23). The rate of change per 6 months was 0.14% (p=0.02) in perindopril vs. 0.02% (p=0.74) in placebo, a 0.12% difference (p=0.07). Mean FMD change was 0.91% (SD 3.77) vs. 0.35% (SD 3.63). No significant difference in nitroglycerine response (8.2% vs. 8.8%). Analysis based on 256 participants.
text: After 6 months, Perindopril showed a 0.12% greater increase in flow-mediated vasodilatation (FMD) compared to placebo (p=0.07), though not statistically significant. The rate of change per 6 months was higher in Perindopril (0.14%) than in placebo (0.02%, p=0.02). No significant difference was found in nitroglycerine response. (Source: Analysis based on 256 participants.)

memory: A 6-week study compared 100g of instant oat cereal to 100g of wheat flour-based noodles. The oat group showed significant reductions in total cholesterol (p=0.015), LDL-C (p=0.028), and waist circumference (p=0.002) compared to the control. HDL-C was significantly higher in the oat group (p=0.017). Dietary fiber intake increased significantly in the oat group. No significant changes in blood pressure or other anthropometric or lab measures were observed between groups.
text: Consuming 100 grams of instant oat cereal for 6 weeks significantly reduced waist circumference (p=0.002) compared to 100 grams of wheat flour-based noodles, along with improvements in cholesterol levels.

memory: In a study of 200 patients, premedication with diazepam (5 mg) and chlorpheniramine (4 mg) 60 minutes before procedures showed no significant differences in periprocedural pain (31% vs. 29%; P = 0.75) or anxiety (59% vs. 50%; P = 0.2) compared to controls. However, local pain was more common in the premedicated group (30% vs. 16%; P = 0.018). Catheter-induced spasms occurred in 4% of the premedicated group versus 0% in controls (P = 0.04), while non-catheter-induced spasms were similar (1% in both; P = NS). No contrast-related reactions were observed in either group.
text: The combination of diazepam and chlorpheniramine increased local pain compared to control (30% vs. 16%; P = 0.018) (Source: study of 200 patients).

memory: Study [PMC3751553] compared sleep patterns during Ramadan fasting (Ramadan) with baseline fasting (BLF) and non-fasting baseline (BL). Bedtime and wake-up times significantly delayed during Ramadan (p < 0.05), with no changes in BL/BLF. REM sleep % was lower in BLF (17.7 ± 8.1%) and Ramadan (18.6 ± 10.7%) vs BL (25.6 ± 4.8%) (p < 0.05). Serum glucose at 15:30 h showed no differences: BL 6.2 ± 0.4, BLF 5.6 ± 0.5, Ramadan 5.7 ± 0.5 mmol/L. No significant differences in JDS scores, blink duration, or MRT across BL, BLF, and Ramadan.
text: Both BLF and Ramadan conditions significantly reduced REM sleep percentages compared to BL (p < 0.05). REM sleep was lower in BLF (17.7 ± 8.1%) and Ramadan (18.6 ± 10.7%) than BL (25.6 ± 4.8%). Source: [PMC3751553].
intervention: 4 weeks before Ramadan while performing the Islamic fasting for 1 week (baseline fasting) (BLF) or during the second week of Ramadan while fasting (Ramadan)

memory: Aripiprazole low- and high-dose significantly improved YGTSS-TTS vs. placebo (p=0.002 and p<0.0001), with high-dose showing greater improvement. At week 8, low-dose reduced YGTSS total motor tic score by -6.7 (0.9) and high-dose by -8.0 (0.9). Response rates were 40.5% (low-dose) and 57.1% (high-dose) vs. 16.7% (placebo). Discontinuation rates were higher for high-dose (10/30) compared to low-dose (2/30) and placebo (2/30). Randomization was stratified by region and weight.
text: High-dose aripiprazole was associated with a higher discontinuation rate (10/30) compared to low-dose (2/30) and placebo (2/30).

memory: Source [PMC4511442]: A trial compared SmartCare™-driven PSV weaning with physiotherapy-driven weaning. No differences were found in pre-weaning Pimax, Pemax, FVC, or RSBI. At extubation readiness, the physiotherapy group had higher PSV (8 vs. 5 cmH2O; p=0.015) and PEEP (8 vs. 5 cmH2O; p<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration (3.5 vs. 4.1 days; p=0.467) and extubation failure rates (2 vs. 2; p=1.00) were similar. Weaning duration was significantly shorter in the physiotherapy group (60 vs. 110 minutes; p<0.001).
text: The progressive discontinuation of PSV with SmartCare™ did not significantly differ from physiotherapy-driven weaning in PSV and PEEP at extubation readiness, except physiotherapy showed higher PSV and PEEP (p<0.001). Source: [PMC4511442].
intervention: progressive discontinuation of pressure support ventilation (PSV) with SmartCare™
outcome: pressure support ventilation (PSV)  and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)

memory: In a breast cancer trial on Trastuzumab, Internet and control groups had similar expectations (P>0.468). The Internet group more often found the platform 'perfectly suitable' (43.5% vs 17.6%, P=0.006), though preferred face-to-face or mail. 72% had Internet access, and 97.2% found results useful. The Internet group showed higher uptake (47.1% vs 33.9%, P=0.166) and better understanding (18.8% vs 5.6%, P=0.039). Oncologists were the top information source. Both groups preferred systematic access to trial results (45.7%) via patient request (41.0%) or physician discretion (13.3%).
text: The Internet group showed better understanding of trial results (18.8% vs 5.6%, P=0.039) compared to the control group. They also had higher uptake (47.1% vs 33.9%, P=0.166), though differences were not statistically significant. Source: Working notes.
intervention: Internet group (who received the letter of invitation)
comparator: control group (who did not receive it)
outcome: accurately understanding the results - Breast cancer patients participating in a trial on the efficacy of Trastuzumab

memory: Vegetable intake did not differ significantly across groups (P=.10). The plus intervention (environmental + individual) significantly increased fruit intake compared to control (ES=0.25, P=.01; ES=0.37, P=.001) and basic interventions. Both basic and plus interventions reduced high-energy snack intake more than control (ES=–0.30, –0.29 vs. control). In risk groups, plus intervention showed greater fruit intake increases (ES=0.25, 0.37) and greater reductions in high-energy snacks (ES=–0.38, –0.32) compared to control. Plus intervention was more effective for high-educated participants. No group differences in vegetable intake changes.
text: The "Individual cognition and self-regulation processes intervention" significantly reduced high-energy snack intake compared to control (ES=–0.30, –0.29). The plus intervention showed greater reductions (ES=–0.38, –0.32) in risk groups and was more effective for high-educated participants.
intervention: Individual cognition and self-regulation processes intervention

memory: CGM Sensor On vs Off: HbA1c lower by -0.43% (p < 0.001). Sensor On had fewer time <3.9 mmol/l (19 vs 31 min/day, p=0.009). Daily boluses increased (6.8 vs 5.8, p < 0.0001), as did temporary basal rates (0.75 vs 0.26, p < 0.0001) and manual insulin suspend (0.91 vs 0.70, p < 0.018). Sensor On had lower average glucose (8.82 vs 9.44 mmol/l, p < 0.001). Severe hypoglycaemia events: 4 vs 2 (p=0.40). Source: PMC3483098.
text: The CGM Sensor On arm was associated with an increase in the mean number of daily boluses (6.8 vs 5.8, p < 0.0001) compared to the Sensor Off arm. Source: PMC3483098.
comparator: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) Sensor Off arm
outcome: The mean number of daily boluses

memory: Study [PMC4636858] compared Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone with Mitoxantrone alone and no treatment in 71 MS patients. MRI plaque counts decreased during treatment in both groups (2.29 vs. 2.17, P = 0.782), with similar increases at 6 months (0.72 vs. 0.77, P = 0.611). EDSS improved significantly at treatment end (0.79 vs. 0.53, P = 0.953), but worsened similarly at 6 months (0.35 vs. 0.43, P = 0.624). No significant differences were found between groups in any outcomes.
text: The combination of Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone did not significantly differ from no treatment in reducing multiple sclerosis plaques (P = 0.782) or improving EDSS scores (P = 0.953) according to [PMC4636858]. Both groups showed similar plaque count changes and EDSS outcomes at 6 months.

memory: Artesunate (2 or 4 mg/kg/day) showed similar median parasite clearance times (29.8 and 29.5 h) compared to quinine+doxycycline (43.1 h; P<0.001). Faster median fever clearance times were observed in artesunate groups (17.9–19.1 h) versus 29.3 h (P=0.001). 28/42-day cure rates were 97.8%, 100%, and 100% for arms 1–3. No serious adverse events were reported; 61.5% of 78 events were drug-related. Median parasite reduction ratios at 12/24 h were lower in artesunate groups (P<0.001).
text: Artesunate monotherapy (2 or 4 mg/kg/day) significantly reduced median fever clearance time (17.9–19.1 h) compared to quinine+doxycycline (29.3 h; P=0.001). Median parasite clearance times were also faster with artesunate (29.5–29.8 h) versus quinine+doxycycline (43.1 h; P<0.001).
intervention: artesunate monotherapy with 2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily
comparator: quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days

memory: In a study (PMC5079604), metformin (1,000 mg) and sitagliptin (100 mg) both significantly reduced hyperglycemia relapse risk compared to placebo (HR 0.28 and 0.31, respectively). Relapse-free survival was higher in both treatment groups (P = 0.015), with a longer time to relapse (480 vs. 305 days, P = 0.004). No difference in relapse-free survival was observed between metformin and sitagliptin (P = 0.75). Patients who achieved remission had higher DI (P = 0.02) and AUCi (P < 0.001) compared to those who relapsed.
text: Metformin 1,000 mg daily and sitagliptin 100 mg daily both significantly improved hyperglycemia relapse-free survival compared to placebo (HR 0.28 and 0.31, respectively; P = 0.015). No difference in relapse-free survival was observed between metformin and sitagliptin (P = 0.75). (PMC5079604)
intervention: metformin 1,000 mg daily, sitagliptin 100 mg daily

memory: A study in 101 patients compared isomaltulose and sucrose. No significant difference in HbA1c was found (sucrose: 7.39 ± 0.78%; isomaltulose: 7.24 ± 0.76%; P = 0.844). Triglycerides were significantly lower in the isomaltulose group (b: 34.01 [6.59–61.44], P = 0.016). Sucrose showed a significant increase in triglycerides over time (P = 0.023), while isomaltulose showed a trend toward reduction. No significant differences were observed for insulin, fasting glucose, fructosamine, proinsulin, C-peptide, or HOMA-IR between groups. Source: [PMC3357231].
text: Isomaltulose significantly lowers triglycerides compared to sucrose (P = 0.016). Sucrose increased triglycerides over time (P = 0.023), while isomaltulose showed a trend toward reduction. Source: [PMC3357231].

memory: In a study of 42 OA dogs, CCOT (Curcuminoids, Collagen, Green Tea) supplementation showed no significant overall change in PI (p=0.063). However, it improved ability to rise from lying down (p=0.029) and PS (p=0.009). No significant differences were found in lameness, pain at palpation, or joint mobility. PVF for the most affected limb showed no significant change at T0 or T3. CCOT was well tolerated, with no significant body weight changes or side effects; mild, transient diarrhea occurred in 3 CCOT and 2 control dogs.
text: The experimental diet with CCOT did not significantly affect pain interference (p=0.063) in OA dogs. However, it improved rising ability (p=0.029) and pain score (p=0.009). No significant changes were observed in lameness, joint mobility, or PVF. CCOT was well tolerated with minimal side effects. Source: Study of 42 OA dogs.
intervention: an experimental diet supplemented with Curcuminoids extract, hydrolyzed COllagen and green Tea extract (CCOT)

memory: In a clinical study [PMC4391304], 100 g of fermented milk (FM) containing Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055) was compared to FM without LG2055. Fecal fat levels significantly increased in the active group post-FM intake, not observed in the control group. LG2055 dose-dependently enhanced fat emulsion droplet size and lipase activity more than other strains. No significant differences in wet fecal weight were found before or after FM intake. The change in fecal fat levels between pre- and post-FM intake was higher in the active group, though not statistically significant (P = 0.086).
text: The addition of Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 to fermented milk significantly increased fecal fat levels compared to FM alone (PMC4391304). This effect was dose-dependent, with enhanced lipase activity and fat droplet size. However, the change in fecal fat levels between pre- and post-intake was not statistically significant (P = 0.086).
intervention: 100&amp;nbsp;g of fermented milk (FM) + Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055)

memory: [PMC1468428] 1L saline enema vs no enema showed no significant difference in episiorraphy dehiscence (12% vs 17%, P=0.30). Puerperal infection rates were 22% vs 14% (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43-1.03). Neonatal infection rates were 20% vs 22% (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76-1.66). Median labour time was similar (515 vs 585 min, P=0.24). Follow-up rate was 86%. No significant differences in other outcomes.
text: A 1L saline enema compared with no enema showed no significant difference in neonatal infection rates (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76-1.66) or puerperal infection rates (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43-1.03) [PMC1468428].

memory: A 10-week yoga program improved flexibility (sit & reach, p < 0.001) but had minimal effects on HRV, with only LF:HF increasing (p = 0.04) and pNN50 decreasing (p = 0.04) compared to control. Post hoc analysis of high adherers (≥70% attendance) showed reduced state anxiety (p = 0.02) and RMSSD (p = 0.05), with a trend toward better push-up performance (p = 0.07). No significant changes in quality of life domains or group × time interactions for anxiety were observed (all p > 0.05). Results partially contradicted hypotheses.
text: A 10-week yoga program significantly improved flexibility (sit & reach, p < 0.001) compared to control. Minimal effects on HRV were noted, with no significant changes in quality of life or anxiety domains (all p > 0.05).

memory: Istradefylline (20 mg/day and 40 mg/day) reduced daily OFF time by −0.99 and −0.96 hours, respectively, compared to −0.23 hours with placebo (P < .003) in Japanese PD patients, with no significant dose difference. Both doses increased daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia by 1.09 and 1.08 hours (P < .004). Dyskinesia was more common with istradefylline (13.0%, 12.1%) than with placebo (4.0%). UPDRS Part II (OFF state) improved more with istradefylline (−1.4, −1.7) than with placebo (−0.6). No increase in ON time with troublesome dyskinesia. Source: PMC3842830.
text: Both 20 mg and 40 mg istradefylline increased daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia by ~1.09 hours compared to placebo, with no significant dose difference. Neither dose increased ON time with problematic dyskinesia. Source: PMC3842830.
outcome: Daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia

memory: Liarozole (150, 75 mg) vs. placebo showed no significant difference in adverse events (P ≥ 0.062). The 150 mg dose significantly improved daily activities (P=0.008), leisure (P=0.026), and symptoms/feelings (P=0.023). DLQI showed no significant change for 150 mg (P=0.06), but 75 mg demonstrated significant improvement (P=0.014).
text: Oral liarozole 150 mg significantly improved daily activities (P=0.008), leisure (P=0.026), and symptoms/feelings (P=0.023) compared to placebo, though DLQI showed no significant change (P=0.06).

memory: A study compared 15-pulse vs. eight-pulse anti-tachycardia pacing (ATP) for treating fascicular ventricular tachycardia (FVT). No significant differences were observed in the number of shocks required (p = 0.907). ATP efficacy in terminating FVT episodes was 64% for eight-pulse and 70% for 15-pulse (p = 0.504). FVT acceleration occurred in 3.9% of episodes in both groups (p = 0.993), with no correlation to syncope or near-syncope. Syncope and near-syncope occurred in 1.7% and 1.8% of patients, respectively, with no significant differences between groups (p = 0.690). Results suggest similar effectiveness and safety profiles between the two ATP configurations.
text: A study found no significant difference between 15-pulse and eight-pulse ATP in reducing syncope and near-syncope episodes (p = 0.690). Both configurations showed similar effectiveness and safety profiles in managing FVT.

memory: A study compared prednisolone (7.5 mg and 30 mg daily) to placebo, showing prednisolone reduced insulin's suppression of endogenous glucose production (17 ± 6% and 46 ± 7%, respectively). Only the 30 mg dose reduced peripheral glucose uptake (34 ± 6%, p < 0.0001). Both doses decreased insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis (11 ± 5% and 34 ± 6%, respectively). Prednisolone tended to lower fasted-state lipolysis (p = 0.062) and increased whole-body proteolysis during hyperinsulinaemia, with the 30 mg dose showing a stronger trend (5 ± 2%, p = 0.06). No side effects were reported, and all participants completed the study.
text: Both prednisolone doses (7.5 mg and 30 mg) reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis compared to placebo (11 ± 5% and 34 ± 6%, respectively). The 30 mg dose showed a stronger effect. Source: Study cited in working notes.
intervention: prednisolone 30 mg once daily and  prednisolone 7,5 mg once daily

memory: A study compared online and mailed paper questionnaires. Trends were noted for shortness of breath (p=.074, p=.081) and higher asthma levels in mailed responses (p=.096). After ANCOVAs adjusting for asthma and demographics, asthma differences were not significant (p=.254). Slight trends existed for ER visits (p=.146) and health distress (p=.116), though ER visits were skewed (Wilcoxon p=.330). Health distress trends remained (p=.111, p=.193). Internet respondents were more likely to be married (p=.043). All variables were covariates. No other outcomes reached significance.
text: The study found no significant effect of "questionnaires online" versus "mailed paper-and-pencil versions" on married subjects. Internet respondents were more likely to be married (p=.043), but no other outcomes reached significance after adjusting for covariates.

memory: A study compared Facebook use with quiet reading during stress recovery. Despite 79% of participants reporting Facebook affected their well-being, both groups showed similar changes in tension, anxiety, and well-being (p > 0.05). Control participants (quiet reading) had significantly greater cortisol reduction from 20 to 45 min post-stressor (F(1, 84) = 5.03, p = 0.03, η2 = 0.06). Female participants with high Facebook engagement showed smaller cortisol reductions. No significant differences were found in subjective stress markers between conditions (p < 0.05). Source: PMC5610684.
text: Using their own Facebook profile did not significantly affect subjective stress markers compared to quietly reading (p > 0.05). However, quiet reading led to greater cortisol reduction. Source: PMC5610684.

memory: A study compared 8 cm vs. 4 cm pillows during tracheal intubation, finding no differences in laryngeal view, intubation success rate, or alignment of laryngeal, pharyngeal, and oral axes. However, discomfort scores were higher with the 8 cm pillow during sequential head elevation (4 cm first, then 8 cm). Objective angles from the horizontal line to the laryngeal, pharyngeal, and oral axes were greater in the 8 cm group, though angular differences between adjacent axes were similar. One patient failed intubation with the 8 cm pillow but succeeded on first attempt with the 4 cm pillow. Source: [PMC4823408].
text: Using an 8 cm pillow during tracheal intubation resulted in higher discomfort scores compared to a 4 cm pillow [PMC4823408]. No differences were found in laryngeal view, success rate, or axis alignment.

memory: A study compared prednisone (various doses) to placebo, showing minimal effects on glucose and insulin after 6 days, with no significant differences post-OGTT. Prednisone 60 mg significantly increased uNTX/uCr from Day 2, with dose-dependent increases up to Day 8. Plasma osteocalcin (OC) decreased significantly from 2 hours post-dose on Day 1, with continued dose- and time-dependent reductions through Day 8. Procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP) was significantly reduced with prednisone ≥20 mg on Day 1, showing dose- and time-dependent decreases until Day 8. These results indicate prednisone has a more pronounced effect on bone metabolism markers than on glucose metabolism markers.
text: Daily prednisone significantly reduces procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP) in a dose- and time-dependent manner compared to placebo, with effects observed as early as Day 1 and persisting through Day 8 (source: study).

memory: A study compared Gutta-percha with AH26, MTA, and a new endodontic cement (NEC) in terms of apical and coronal dye penetration. No significant differences in apical sealing were found between groups (LGP/AH26, SGP/MTA, SGP/NEC). However, the SGP/NEC group showed significantly less coronal dye penetration (P<0.001), indicating better coronal seal compared to others. All groups exhibited similar apical sealing, but NEC provided superior coronal sealing. Source: PMC3712263.
text: The use of Gutta-percha with a new endodontic cement significantly reduces coronal dye penetration compared to Gutta-percha with AH26, indicating a better coronal seal (PMC3712263).

memory: Intermediate addition multifocals showed significant differences compared to full bifocals in vertical toe clearance on ascent (χ²=6.9, p=0.009), variability of vertical toe clearance (χ²=12.0, p=0.0005), ascent duration (χ²=12.7, p<0.0001), and heel clearance on descent (χ²=8.7, p=0.003). Intermediate PALs showed no significant differences compared to distance single vision lenses across all gait parameters (p>0.05) and performed similarly to participants' own spectacles. Intermediate bifocals had poorer gait safety than intermediate PALs or distance single vision lenses.
text: Intermediate progressive addition lenses (PALs) had no significant effect on ascent vertical toe clearance compared to distance single vision lenses (p>0.05). They performed similarly to participants' own spectacles. Intermediate bifocals, however, showed poorer gait safety. Source: Working notes.

memory: Behavioral lifestyle intervention in children significantly improved BMI-SDS (P=0.02), WC-SDS (P=0.03), and VO2peak-SDS (P<0.01) at 1 year, with BMI-SDS reduction sustained at 2 years (P=0.02). Adiposity decreased by 10% and WC-SDS by 19% at 1 year. VO2peak-SDS-kg increased by 20% in the intervention group compared to an 18% reduction in controls. HOMA-SDS improved (P=0.04), but no changes in lipid profile, CRP, or adiponectin. Attendance varied, with some missing meetings. No change in Borg scores. Source: [PMC3302141]
text: Behavioral lifestyle intervention significantly reduced waist circumference (WC-SDS by 19%) compared to control at 1 year (P=0.03). Source: [PMC3302141]

memory: Participants consumed energy intakes above national averages (8672 kJ) before and after the 4.5-month intervention (±1.1 months). Discretionary foods contributed 34.6% of total energy. Macronutrient intake remained stable and aligned with national averages, with minor group differences. Saturated fat intake, measured by FFQ, showed no significant change, though dietary habits suggested possible reductions via meat choices. The dietary model combined Mediterranean and portfolio patterns, but baseline diets were less aligned, characterized by higher discretionary food intake. Core food energy intake at baseline was 63 ± 10%, with no difference between completers and non-completers. Source: [PMC4555162].
text: Before intervention, participants had higher energy intakes (8672 kJ) than the national average, with 34.6% from discretionary foods. Macronutrient intake aligned with national averages, though core food energy was 63 ± 10%. Source: [PMC4555162].

memory: ES10/20 and R10 showed no significant differences in apoA-I, LDL-P, or other lipid markers (NS). Both significantly reduced PLAC and Lp-PLA2 compared to doubling the statin dose (P<0.05). ES10/20 reduced LDL-P more than doubling the dose, with results comparable to R10 (P>0.05). Both ES10/20 and R10 increased apoA-I more than doubling the dose (P<0.05). No significant changes in triglycerides, HDL-C, or hsCRP. LDL-P changes correlated with sLDL-P reductions (P<0.0001). Source: PMC4845107.
text: ES10/20 and R10 had no significant differences in LDL-P (P>0.05). Both reduced LDL-P more than doubling the statin dose. ES10/20’s LDL-P reduction was comparable to R10. Source: PMC4845107.

memory: Weight management intervention (diet + PA + usual care) vs usual care increased fiber intake (+5.7 g/day, p < .001) at 4 and 12 months, but not fat consumption (−2.3 g/day, p = 0.13). Fiber intake predicted weight loss at 4 months (−1.98 kg, p < .01) and 12 months (−1.85 kg, p = 0.1). At 12 months, unadjusted weight loss not significant (−3.7 vs −1.9 kg, p = 0.13), but adjusted for co-interventions and morbidities, difference was significant (−2.9 kg, p = 0.014). No significant PA changes. Behavioral mediators like self-efficacy and coping planning supported dietary changes. Source: [PMC4304200].
text: The weight management intervention (diet + PA + usual care) increased fiber intake by +5.7 g/day at 12 months compared to usual care (p < .001). This effect was not observed for fat consumption. Source: [PMC4304200].
intervention: weight management intervention targeting diet and physical activity plus usual care

memory: In a study comparing escalating tamsulosin dose (0.4 mg/d) to maintaining 0.2 mg/d, IIEF-5 scores showed no significant difference (p=0.859) in 15 patients with no LUTS improvement. However, in 35 patients with improved LUTS, escalators had a significantly higher IIEF-5 increase (4.6 vs. 1.7, p=0.002). At week 4, nonescalators showed slightly better but non-significant improvements in IPSS-total (-4.8 vs. -2.8, p>0.05) and IPSS-voiding (-3.7 vs. -1.8, p>0.05) scores compared to escalators. Source: PMC3580298.
text: In patients with no improvement in LUTS, maintaining 0.2 mg/d tamsulosin showed no significant difference in IIEF-5 scores compared to escalating to 0.4 mg/d (p=0.859). Source: PMC3580298.
comparator: increase their dose to 0.4 mg once daily (escalators)
outcome: International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5)  in patients who showed no improvement of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)

memory: A study on gepotidacin showed that 1,800-mg doses caused higher adverse events (64%) compared to 1,000-mg (46%), including vomiting (15%), nausea (8%), throat tightness (2%), and dizziness (2%). Nine percent discontinued due to adverse events, including C. difficile infections. QTc prolongation peaked at 22.2 ms, decreasing to 21.4 ms when excluding vomiting. QTc prolongation correlated linearly with plasma concentration (1.45 ms/μg/ml). Heart rate increased by ~10-13 bpm post-infusion. Adverse events were mostly mild to moderate, with cholinergic effects like salivary hypersecretion being mild. These findings support understanding dose-related QT prolongation and safety profiles.
text: The 1,800 mg dose of gepotidacin in healthy volunteers resulted in a higher incidence of moderate adverse events (64%) compared to 1,000 mg (46%), including vomiting, nausea, and dizziness. These findings suggest a dose-related increase in moderate adverse events. (Source: Study on gepotidacin)

memory: Propofol (midazolam-based) showed higher rates of cardiopulmonary adverse events (72.6% vs. 54.8%, P = .040), vital sign fluctuation (50.0% vs. 27.4%, P = .010), and transient hypotension (41.9% vs. 24.2%, P = .036) compared to etomidate. Etomidate had more procedure-disturbing events (25.8% vs. 8.1%, P = .008) and myoclonus (16.1% vs. 1.6%, P = .004). No major adverse events were reported in either group. Baseline and procedural characteristics were similar, with no significant differences in induction, procedure, or awake times.
text: Etomidate is associated with a higher incidence rate of myoclonus (16.1%) compared to propofol based on midazolam (1.6%, P = .004).

memory: [PMC4469426] ALM (85g/day) vs CON diet showed no significant changes in lipid profiles (TC, HDL-C, LDL-C, TG, small dense LDL-C, Apo-B100, Apo-AI) or inflammation markers (CRP, TNFα, IL-6). ALM increased vitamin E intake by 103%, raising plasma α-tocopherol by 5.8% (10.2% vs CON, P=0.0065) and decreasing γ-tocopherol by 15.4% (16.5% vs CON, P=0.047). Endothelial function biomarkers (E-selectin, VCAM-1, NO) were not reported.
text: The CON diet with almonds (85 g/day) increased plasma α-tocopherol by 5.8% compared to the CON diet (P=0.0065) [PMC4469426].

memory: A study compared a computerised diabetes register with a standard system, with intervention costs of £27,885 for guidelines, software, and education. No significant differences in average cost per patient, HbA1c, BP, or patient-reported outcomes (SF36, DCSQ) were found. However, cholesterol levels were significantly lower in the intervention group (-0.15 mmol/l, 95% CI -0.25, -0.06). Intervention patients had higher odds of attending diabetes appointments, foot checks, receiving dietary advice, and BP recordings. Economic data and outcomes are detailed in Table 5 and Table 4, respectively.
text: The computerised diabetes register increased the frequency of diabetes appointments, foot checks, dietary advice, and BP recordings compared to the standard system (p<0.05). No significant differences were found in HbA1c, BP, or patient-reported outcomes, though cholesterol levels were significantly lower in the intervention group.
intervention: area-wide, computerised diabetes register incorporating a full structured recall and individualised patient management system
comparator: standard structured and recall management system
outcome: Frequency of at least one diabetes appointment, a foot check, receiving dietary advice, recording of blood pressure

memory: A study [PMC4215531] found that facial affect training (FAT) over 20 daily 1-hour sessions led to a significant Time effect (F(1,18) = 5.61, p = .03), with increased alpha power during the pre-recognition period of the FAR criterion task post-training. No significant Emotion effects were observed. The alpha power increase was noted in the FAT group during the prestimulus baseline, suggesting FAT may influence neural activity related to emotional processing.
text: Facial affect training (FAT) in 20 daily 1-hour sessions significantly increased alpha power during the pre-recognition period of the FAR criterion task compared to baseline (F(1,18) = 5.61, p = .03) [PMC4215531]. This suggests FAT may influence neural activity related to emotional processing.
intervention: facial affect training (FAT) in 20 daily 1-hour sessions

memory: In a study [PMC4608626], singing training (music therapy) was compared to a control group. Results showed a significant reduction in time to complete the Japanese Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (p=0.026). Caregiver interviews indicated a significant decrease in Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores (p=0.042) and longer patient sleep duration (p=0.039). fMRI findings revealed increased activity in the right angular gyrus and left lingual gyrus pre- to post-intervention.
text: Singing training significantly reduced Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores compared to control (p=0.042) [PMC4608626].

memory: A study compared RCF (Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine), RF (Ropivacaine-fentanyl), and RC (Ropivacaine-clonidine). Demographics and block characteristics were similar across groups. Adding clonidine to ropivacaine-fentanyl did not significantly affect analgesic effects or hemodynamics (P>0.05). However, the RCF group experienced significantly fewer side effects (P<0.05), leading to improved patient comfort. Source: [PMC4173331].
text: Adding clonidine to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RCF) did not significantly affect hemodynamic parameters compared to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) (P>0.05). Source: [PMC4173331].

memory: A study (PMC5684963) found that a low GI diet significantly reduced glycemic response (GR) after lunch (p=0.02), breakfast (p=0.02), and dinner (p=0.05), along with a decrease in daily area under the curve (AUC) (p=0.03). A significant reduction in incremental AUC (IAUC) was observed after low GI breakfast compared to high GI breakfast (p=0.03).
text: A low glycemic index intervention significantly reduces glycemic response after lunch compared to a high glycemic index intervention (p=0.02). This is supported by a study (PMC5684963) showing decreased glycemic response and daily AUC with low GI diets.

memory: In a study comparing caudal sufentanil with and without neostigmine, groups receiving caudal sufentanil alone (Group IVSu, Group CSu, Group CSuAdr) showed similar postoperative dipyrone doses within 24 hours (P > 0.05). Groups with both caudal sufentanil and neostigmine (Group CSuNeo and Group CSuNeoAdr) required fewer dipyrone doses (P < 0.005). Facial pain VAS scores at analgesic administration were similar across all groups (5-6 cm, P > 0.05). The incidence of postoperative nausea or vomiting was also similar among groups. Source: [PMC4141382]
text: Caudal sufentanil + neostigmine reduces dipyrone needed compared to caudal sufentanil alone (P < 0.005). Source: [PMC4141382]

memory: A study compared transillumination-assisted (T) and midline approach (R) intubation techniques. First, second, and third attempt success rates and average intubation time were similar between groups (P > 0.05). However, in cases of successful intubation on the second attempt, the T group had longer intubation times (P = 0.0006). The T group also experienced higher rates of dry throat, sore throat, and hoarseness (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in overall intubation success rates or total intubation time between the T and R groups (P > 0.05).
text: The intubation success rates at first, second, and third attempts were similar between the T and R groups (P > 0.05). However, the T group had longer intubation times when successful on the second attempt (P = 0.0006).
outcome: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempt

Source: [PMC3525032]  
Intervention: PLMA vs. ETT. Outcome: cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation. PLMA group had significantly lower cortisol than ETT group (p=0.024). Within groups, cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation were significantly higher than after anaesthesia induction (p=0.001). text: The laryngeal mask (PLMA) significantly reduces cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation compared to endotracheal intubation (ETT) (p=0.024). Both groups showed increased cortisol from anaesthesia induction (p=0.001). No differences were found in other catecholamines. Source: [PMC3525032].

memory: Source [PMC4776564]: A study compared hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs with no intervention. Baseline demographics and pre-intervention QOL scores in performance/health, socioeconomic, psychological, spiritual, familial dimensions, and satisfaction/improvement areas were similar between groups. Post-intervention and 1-month follow-up showed significant QOL score differences (P < 0.05). Repeated measures ANOVA indicated significant QOL score changes over time in the control group across four dimensions and two areas.
text: The study found no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs and the no-intervention group. Source: [PMC4776564].
intervention: Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs

memory: A study compared butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream (Gynazole-1) with oral fluconazole 150 mg (Diflucan). Median time to first symptom relief was 17.5 hours for butoconazole versus 22.9 hours for fluconazole (p < 0.001). At the 75th percentile, relief occurred at 24.5 hours for butoconazole and 46.3 hours for fluconazole (p < 0.001). Secondary outcomes included overall symptom relief and 30-day reinfection rates. Safety was evaluated through adverse event reports.
text: Butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream provides faster relief of symptoms compared to oral fluconazole 150 mg. The median time to first relief was 17.5 hours versus 22.9 hours (p < 0.001).
intervention: butoconazole nitrate 2% Site Release vaginal cream (Gynazole-1)
outcome: The median time to first relief of symptoms

memory: Vit D (50,000 IU/week) vs. placebo showed no significant differences in FBS, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP (P>0.05). Pre-study proteinuria: case 962.62±885.99 vs. control 755.71±640.94 (P=0.70). Post-study: 892.24±879.40 vs. 971.60±940.24 (P=0.48). Change in proteinuria: case -70.38±553.71 vs. control -215.89±451.44 (P=0.028). Source: PMC5106877.
text: Vitamin D (50,000 IU/week) did not significantly affect FBS, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP compared to placebo (P>0.05). Source: PMC5106877.
outcome: fasting blood sugar (FBS), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1C), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels

memory: A study compared lifestyle physical activity (LPA) with fibromyalgia education (FME). LPA involved 30 minutes of moderate-intensity activity, 5–7 days/week. Baseline measures (FIQ, pain, fatigue, depression, tender points, BMI, six-minute walk) were similar between groups. Post-intervention, LPA significantly reduced FIQ (P = .032; d = .53) and pain (P = .006; d = .67) compared to FME. The six-minute walk test approached significance (P = .067; d = .53). No differences were found in BMI, fatigue, depression, or tender points. Source: [PMC2888205].
text: LPA significantly reduced pain (P = .006; d = .67) compared to FME. Source: [PMC2888205].
intervention: lifestyle physical activity (LPA) - 30 minutes of self-selected moderate-intensity LPA, five to seven days per week
comparator: fibromyalgia (FM) education control (FME) group - received information and support

memory: A study found green tea significantly increased resting and post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01). Plasma glycerol levels rose after green tea consumption in both trained and untrained groups, with higher levels in untrained individuals (p < 0.05). Green tea also elevated plasma epinephrine during and after exercise in both groups, while norepinephrine increases were significant only in untrained individuals (p < 0.05). Source: [PMC4899895].
text: Green tea significantly increases post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo (p < 0.05). It also raises plasma glycerol and epinephrine levels, with greater effects in untrained individuals. Source: [PMC4899895].

memory: Experiment 1 used red/blue cursors to indicate curl field directions, assessing performance via MPE and force compensation during clamp trials. MPE significantly decreased over time (F1,5 = 58.220; P = 0.001), but force compensation did not improve (F1,5 = 0.223; P = 0.657). Postexposure, no trajectory deviations were observed, indicating no learned field-specific compensation. Source: PMC3653044.
text: The initial trial showed a significant decrease in MPE over time (F1,5 = 58.220; P = 0.001), but no improvement in force compensation. The final trial did not demonstrate learned field-specific compensation, as no trajectory deviations were observed postexposure. Source: PMC3653044.
outcome: over the course of the exposure period maximum perpendicular error (MPE) decrease - cursor color (red or blue)

memory: In SMART-1, SMART-2, and SMART-5, BZA/CE (20 mg/0.45 mg or 20 mg/0.625 mg) showed no significant difference in breast tenderness compared to placebo, raloxifene, or BZA alone. In SMART-5, BZA/CE had significantly lower breast tenderness than CE/MPA (P < 0.001). BZA/CE showed non-inferiority to placebo in mammographic breast density, unlike CE/MPA, which increased breast density. BZA/CE did not alter age-related breast density changes during menopause. Source: [PMC3743641].
text: In clinical trials, BZA/CE showed no significant difference in breast tenderness compared to placebo. It also demonstrated lower breast tenderness than CE/MPA (P < 0.001) and maintained non-inferiority to placebo in mammographic breast density. Source: [PMC3743641].
intervention: BZA/CE combines bazedoxifene (BZA), a selective estrogen receptor modulator, with conjugated estrogens (CE),

memory: In a study [PMC5126873], the UPBEAT intervention (diet and physical activity) significantly reduced Processed (−0.14; 95% CI −0.19, −0.08, P <0.0001) and Snacks (−0.24; 95% CI −0.31, −0.17, P <0.0001) dietary pattern scores at 28 weeks, with effects maintained at 36 weeks. No changes were observed in Fruit and vegetables or African/Caribbean dietary patterns between intervention and control groups at 28 and 36 weeks gestation.
text: The effect of "Diet and physical activity" compared with "Control" on "African/Caribbean food intake" showed no significant changes in dietary patterns at 28 and 36 weeks gestation (PMC5126873).

memory: A study (n=5 each group) compared resveratrol to placebo in assessing ibuprofen use. The resveratrol group had a mean ibuprofen dose of 1200 mg (SD 848), versus 5640 mg (SD 328) in the placebo group. No statistically significant difference was found (p=0.09). Source: PMC5686687.
text: A study found no statistically significant difference (p=0.09) in the need for ibuprofen between resveratrol (mean dose 1200 mg) and placebo (mean dose 5640 mg) groups (n=5 each). Source: PMC5686687.

memory: A study compared regular activity breaks (RAB) with prolonged sitting (SIT) on appetite and food intake over two days. Linear mixed models found no significant differences in appetite AUC between RAB and SIT on Day 1 (standardized effect: 0.11; 95% CI: −0.28, 0.06; p = 0.212) or Day 2 (standardized effect: 0.04; 95% CI: −0.15, 0.24; p = 0.648). Energy intake at an ad libitum lunch on Day 2 also did not differ significantly. The results suggest that RAB do not acutely impact appetite or food consumption, despite increased energy expenditure. Source: PMC5852701.
text: Regular activity breaks did not significantly affect appetite AUC on Day 1 compared to prolonged sitting (standardized effect: 0.11; 95% CI: −0.28, 0.06; p = 0.212). Source: PMC5852701.
outcome: Appetite area under the curve at day 1

memory: A study compared artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) and mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) in 452 patients. P. vivax parasitaemia occurred in 119 patients during follow-up, with MAS3 showing significantly fewer cases (29 of 227) than ALN (90 of 225; P < 0.001). The median time to parasitaemia was longer in the MAS3 group (40 days; range 13–43) compared to ALN (28 days; range 14–43; P < 0.001). Source: [PMC1261533].
text: Mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) significantly reduced P. vivax parasitaemia during follow-up compared to artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) (29/227 vs. 90/225; P < 0.001). The median time to parasitaemia was longer with MAS3 (40 days) than ALN (28 days; P < 0.001). Source: [PMC1261533].
outcome: P. vivax parasitaemia diagnosed during follow up

memory: Source [PMC5022334]: Compared BABA and open thyroidectomy. Subclinical central lymph node metastasis rate was 35%. Robotic group had longer operative time (118.8 ± 16.5 vs. 90.7 ± 10.3 min, P < 0.05). Open group showed better postoperative outcomes with lower VAS (2.1 ± 1.0 vs. 3.8 ± 1.2, P < 0.05) and NSS (8.9 ± 0.8 vs. 4.8 ± 1.7, P < 0.05). No significant differences in blood loss, hospital stay, lymph node count, thyroglobulin, or complications (all P > 0.05). No iatrogenic implantation or metastasis in either group.
text: Conventional open thyroidectomy resulted in lower postoperative Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores (2.1 ± 1.0) compared to Thyroidectomy via BABA (3.8 ± 1.2, P < 0.05) according to [PMC5022334].

memory: In a study comparing intubation methods, the WEI JET group had significantly longer intubation times (110.8±18.3 s) than the lightwand (LW) group (63.3±27.5 s) and direct laryngoscopy (DL) group (66.7±29.4 s, p=0.000). text: The "lightwand only" method had shorter intubation times and more successful attempts compared to "lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy" (p=0.000 and p=0.043, respectively). No significant difference was found between lightwand and direct laryngoscopy. Source: [PMC4372550]
comparator: lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy

memory: Baseline 25(OH)D levels were balanced between the VitD/Cal and placebo groups. text: Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation significantly increased 25(OH)D levels compared to placebo over 48 weeks (P < .001). The VitD/Cal group showed increases of +27.5 ng/mL at 24 weeks and +24.2 ng/mL at 48 weeks, while the placebo group showed minimal changes. Source: [PMC5726464].

memory: A study compared cilostazol (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks) to placebo and found that cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, 95% CI 10.65 to 199.71) (Table 3). text: Cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to placebo (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, 95% CI 10.65 to 199.71) (PMC3733748). No significant differences were observed in other markers.
intervention: cilostazol group (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks)
outcome: soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) level

memory: A study compared computer-assisted learning (CAL) with an information leaflet in students. CAL significantly improved retention performance (p = 0.02, 95% CI = 0.83–12.19, effect size = 0.8) and enjoyment (p = 0.04, 95% CI = 0.03–2.75, effect size = 0.7) compared to the control group. text: Computer-assisted learning significantly increased the level of enjoyment compared to the control group (p = 0.04, effect size = 0.7). Source: PMC2652457.

memory: In a study comparing Spiromax, Easyhaler, and Turbuhaler, Spiromax was rated significantly higher than both Easyhaler and Turbuhaler for overall ease of use, quality of PIL instructions, preparing the dose, and clarity of dose counter (p<0.001 for all). text: Spiromax showed significantly higher ratings than Easyhaler and Turbuhaler for overall ease of use, quality of PIL instructions, preparing the dose, and clarity of dose counter (p<0.001). Turbuhaler scored higher than Easyhaler for PIL instructions, while Easyhaler outperformed Turbuhaler in clarity of dose counter. Source: [PMC4809147].
outcome: ‘overall ease of use’, ‘quality of PIL instructions’, ‘preparing the dose’,  ‘clarity of dose counter’

memory: In a study comparing Monovisc, saline, and Cingal for knee osteoarthritis pain reduction in the anteromedial subgroup, Cingal showed significantly greater pain reduction than both Monovisc (P = .0449) and saline (P = .0231) at 3 weeks, with no significant difference between Monovisc and saline (P = .4782). text: Monovisc showed no significant difference from saline in pain reduction up to 3 weeks in the anteromedial subgroup (P = .4782). Cingal was more effective than both. Source: [PMC5560514].
outcome: pain reduction up to 3 weeks in patients with knee osteoarthritis - anteromedial subgroup

memory: A study compared a "phone calls" intervention group with a "no phone calls" comparator group, finding significantly fewer patients discontinued treatment in the phone calls group (4 vs. 30; p<0.0094). This suggests the phone calls intervention may improve treatment adherence. Source: [PMC2974815].
text: Patients in the "phone calls" group had significantly fewer treatment discontinuations (4) compared to the "no phone calls" group (30; p<0.0094), suggesting phone calls improve treatment adherence. Source: [PMC2974815].

memory: A study compared skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding (n=31) with no contact (n=33). Infants with skin-to-skin contact latched on significantly sooner, with a median time of 2.0 weeks (Q1=1.0, Q3=3.7) versus 4.7 weeks (Q1=2.0, Q3=8.0) in the control group (p=0.020). A Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed this trend (p=0.017, Peto-Peto-Wilcoxon test). These findings suggest that skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding may promote earlier latching and suckling. Source: [PMC3606616].
text: Skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding significantly reduces the time infants begin latching compared to no contact (median 2.0 vs. 4.7 weeks, p=0.020). This effect was confirmed by Kaplan-Meier analysis (p=0.017). Source: [PMC3606616].
comparator: no skin-to-skin contact during the breastfeeding
outcome: registered time when infants began latching on

memory: At 30 months post-baseline, internet-based self-management (IBSM) significantly improved asthma-related quality of life (0.29; 95% CI 0.01-0.57) and asthma control (-0.33; 95% CI -0.61 to -0.05) compared to control. No significant changes were observed in inhaled corticosteroid dosage or lung function (FEV1). Source: PMC3785973.
text: Internet-based self-management support did not significantly affect inhaled corticosteroid dosage compared to control (PMC3785973).

memory: Study [PMC5746685] assessed 227 adults (44% male, mean age 42.3 ± 10.1 years, BMI 30.4 ± 4.1 kg/m2) randomized to basic or enhanced web-based weight loss maintenance (WLM) programs. The primary outcome was weight rebound after 12 months, with minimal rebound in both groups (basic 1.3%, enhanced 1.5%). No significant differences in BMI change were found (basic −0.5 (1.9) kg/m2, enhanced −0.5 (1.6) kg/m2, p = 0.93). Secondary outcomes showed limited change. Intention-to-treat analysis with last observation carried forward imputation was used. The study concluded that a web-based WLM program effectively prevents weight regain over one year following weight loss.
text: The enhanced weight loss maintenance program did not significantly reduce weight rebound compared to the basic program after 12 months (basic 1.3%, enhanced 1.5%; p = 0.93). Both programs similarly prevented weight regain. (Source: PMC5746685)

text: The MI-LEAF training condition significantly reduced "sustain talk" (ST) compared to baseline (b = −0.1008, SE = 0.0179, p < 0.001), supporting the hypothesis, though this effect was less strong over time. Source: [PMC5539943].
intervention: Language Enhanced Attention and Focus MI training condition (MI-LEAF)

memory: A study compared LLLT to placebo by evaluating changes in TEOAE PTA and HFA. ANOVA found no significant differences between groups for TEOAE PTA (F(2,31) = 0.133, P = 0.876) or TEOAE HFA (F(2,31) = 0.20, P = 0.819). Kruskal-Wallis test also showed no significant difference in TEOAE HFA medians (Kw(2) = 4.04, P = 0.133). Results are detailed in Tables 6 and 7 of [PMC3658388].
text: A study found no significant effect of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) compared to placebo on TEOAE pure-tone average (PTA) (F(2,31) = 0.133, P = 0.876). Results are from [PMC3658388].

memory: In a study comparing vildagliptin to placebo, vildagliptin significantly reduced HbA1c by −0.5 ± 0.1% (P < .0001) from a baseline of 6.5 ± 0.1%. The placebo group showed a small increase of 0.2 ± 0.1% (P = .14) from a baseline of 6.4 ± 0.1%. The between-group difference was −0.7 ± 0.1% (P < .001), indicating vildagliptin improved glycemic control more than placebo. Source: [PMC4399299].
text: Vildagliptin significantly reduced glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) by −0.5 ± 0.1% compared to a small increase of 0.2 ± 0.1% with placebo (P < .001). This indicates vildagliptin improves glycemic control more effectively than placebo. Source: [PMC4399299].

memory: In a per-protocol analysis (2 vs. 12 patients), PAR significantly reduced serum iPTH levels compared to CAL at 6 months (76 ± 55 pg/ml vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036), with a greater reduction rate (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008). No significant difference was found in the proportion of patients with ≥30% iPTH reduction (95.1% vs. 88.4%; P = 0.26). The proportion of patients with iPTH between 70-110 pg/ml was 14.6% (PAR) vs. 25.6% (CAL; P = 0.056). Source: PMC5762965.
text: Paricalcitol significantly reduced serum iPTH levels compared to Calcifediol at 6 months (P = 0.0036), with a greater reduction rate (P = 0.008). However, no significant difference was found in the proportion of patients achieving ≥30% iPTH reduction (P = 0.26). Source: PMC5762965.

memory: A study comparing nebivolol and atenolol using VH-IVUS found that nebivolol segments had significantly reduced EEM area (P=0.02) and lumen area (P=0.004) compared to atenolol, with no significant differences in plaque components or TCFAs. At follow-up, nebivolol showed increased plaque area (P<0.001), whereas atenolol showed plaque regression (P=0.047). However, the difference between the two groups was not significant (P=0.27). Source: [PMC4859395].
text: A study found no significant differences between nebivolol and atenolol in plaque components or TCFAs per vessel. However, nebivolol showed increased plaque area, while atenolol showed regression, though the difference between groups was not significant (P=0.27). Source: [PMC4859395].
outcome: plaque components and number of TCFAs per vessel

memory: A study compared tetraplegic patients (with and without 2 mg melatonin for 4 days) to able-bodied men, assessing circadian patterns of F1+2 and D-dimer. Tetraplegic groups showed increased F1+2 circadian variation (P=0.01 and P<0.001) compared to able-bodied individuals, with no difference between melatonin and placebo groups. D-dimer patterns were similar across all groups, and plasma concentrations of F1+2 and D-dimer were comparable. No significant differences in circadian variation of FVIIa were observed. Source: PMC5399146.
text: Tetraplegic patients exhibited increased circadian variation of F1+2 compared to able-bodied men (P=0.01 and P<0.001), with no effect of 2 mg melatonin over 4 days. Source: PMC5399146.
intervention: 2 mg of melatonin given 4 days for tetraplegic patients and placebo for tetraplegic patients

memory: Baseline MRDR values were similar between vitamin A intervention and control groups (0.032 vs. 0.031, 95% CI). Post-intervention, total body stores (TBS) and liver retinol concentrations did not differ significantly: TBS was 436 (SD 303) vs. 434 (SD 186) μmol, and liver concentrations were 0.82 (SD 0.53) vs. 0.79 (SD 0.36) μmol/g liver. text: The effect of "Sprinkles" with vitamin A versus without vitamin A on baseline MRDR values was negligible, as values were similar between groups (0.032 vs. 0.031). Post-intervention, no significant differences were found in total body stores or liver retinol concentrations, indicating adequate vitamin A reserves in all children. Source: [PMC4780150].

memory: A study compared Ciclesonide (CIC) and Fluticasone propionate (FLP) nasal sprays in 58% male patients, median age 32, with 24 months of symptoms. Patients preferred FLP over CIC (55.41% vs. 25.68%, P=0.007), citing better scent, soothing feel, and less nasal irritation. No significant difference in immediate efficacy was observed. Adverse effects were mild, with two CIC patients reporting headache, and three FLP patients experiencing headache, one dizziness, and one nasal congestion. Source: [PMC3480782].
text: Patients preferred Fluticasone propionate (FLP) over Ciclesonide (CIC) as a preferred intranasal corticosteroid (55.41% vs. 25.68%, P=0.007), citing better scent, soothing feel, and less nasal irritation, though both showed similar immediate efficacy. Source: [PMC3480782].

memory: A 3-year study compared Superion® and X-STOP® in patients with moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis. A higher proportion of Superion® patients (52.5%, 63/120) met the primary composite endpoint compared to X-STOP® (38.0%, 49/129; P=0.023). Superion® success rates for each component of the primary endpoint exceeded 80% (81%–91%). Both groups showed sustained improvements in back and leg pain and functional outcomes through 36 months. Source: [PMC4599047].
text: Superion® (52.5%, 63/120) showed a higher proportion of subjects achieving the primary composite endpoint compared to X-STOP® (38.0%, 49/129; P=0.023) in patients with moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis. Source: [PMC4599047].
outcome: subjects achieving the primary composite endpoint - moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis.

memory: A 24-week study compared vonoprazan 10 mg and 20 mg to lansoprazole 15 mg for EE recurrence (PMC5897859). Vonoprazan doses showed lower recurrence rates (5.1% and 2.0%) compared to lansoprazole (16.8%). Vonoprazan was non-inferior to lansoprazole (P < 0.0001), with both doses significantly reducing recurrence (P = 0.0002 and P < 0.0001). No significant difference in recurrence was found between the two vonoprazan doses (P = 0.1090). Safety profiles were similar, with treatment-related adverse events in 11.4%, 10.4%, and 10.3% of patients, respectively.
text: Vonoprazan 10 mg and 20 mg significantly reduced erosive esophagitis recurrence rates (5.1% and 2.0%) compared to lansoprazole 15 mg (16.8%) after 24 weeks (PMC5897859). Both vonoprazan doses were non-inferior to lansoprazole, with no significant difference between the vonoprazan doses. Safety profiles were similar across all groups.
outcome: Erosive esophagitis recurrence rate after 24 weeks

text: In Study B [PMC1570354], FBC and SFC showed similar effects on the median number of days with no use of relief medication, with SFC having a slightly higher median percentage (63% vs. 61%), though differences were not statistically significant.
outcome: the median number of days with no use of relief medication

memory: A study [PMC4877819] found that patients treated with Andrographis paniculata showed a 44% reduction in Fatigue Severity Scores (FSS) compared to placebo after 12 months. No significant differences were observed in relapse rate, EDSS, or inflammatory markers, though a trend toward fewer new lesions was noted in the A. paniculata group. One patient experienced a mild, transient skin rash, managed with anti-histamines for three weeks.
text: Andrographis paniculata significantly reduced Fatigue Severity Scores by 44% compared to placebo after 12 months (PMC4877819). No major adverse effects were reported.

memory: A study compared DEB + BMS with Zotarolimus-eluting stents, showing higher binary restenosis in the DEB + BMS group, though not statistically significant. text: The "Drug-eluting balloon + bare metal stent" may have a higher risk of binary restenosis compared to "Zotarolimus-eluting stent," though the difference was not statistically significant [PMC5426232].

memory: A study found a significant time-by-condition interaction (F(2,85)=3.92, p=.024, partial η²=.084) in triglyceride levels between nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) and usual care (UC). Post-hoc analysis showed significantly lower triglycerides in the NPC group compared to UC (p=0.008), with a trend for MIC vs. UC (p=0.057). No difference was observed between MIC and UC (p=0.423). text: Nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) significantly lowers triglyceride levels compared to usual care (UC) (p=0.008), with a trend for MIC vs. UC (p=0.057). No difference was found between MIC and UC (p=0.423). Source: [PMC4236282].

memory: A study compared 10-mm transumbilical and 5-mm transabdominal approaches. Rescue analgesia was needed in 4 transumbilical and 3 transabdominal cases. No intra-operative retrieval bag rupture occurred. Post-removal evaluation showed intact tubes in 18 transumbilical cases versus 3 transabdominal (P < 0.001, OR: 51.0, 95% CI: 7.56-343.73). No surgical complications were reported, with all patients discharged on postoperative day 1. Three-month follow-up showed uneventful recovery without complications such as post-side herniation. Source: [PMC3872586].
text: The 10-mm transumbilical group had significantly higher intact tube rates (18/22) compared to the 5-mm transabdominal group (3/22; P < 0.001, OR: 51.0). No surgical complications were reported. Source: [PMC3872586].

memory: Source [PMC4331314]: A study compared titanium clip surgery with a control group, adjusting for injury severity and prognostic factors. text: The use of specially designed molding titanium clips significantly reduced ventilator time (P = 0.026) and overall hospital stay (P = 0.026) compared to control, according to [PMC4331314].
outcome: Ventilator time and overall hospital stay

memory: A study [PMC4395675] found that CIMT combined with gait training significantly improved dynamic balance (28.6% increase in TIS) and paretic side movement (34.3% increase in LOS) compared to gait training alone. The control group showed no significant balance improvement. These results suggest that CIMT enhances the outcomes of gait training in patients.
text: Gait training with constrained induced movement therapy (CIMT) significantly improves dynamic balance compared to gait training alone, with a 28.6% increase in TIS (PMC4395675). CIMT enhances gait training outcomes by promoting paretic side movement and balance improvement.
intervention: Gait training with constrained induced movement therapy

memory: In a study [PMC3661377], apremilast 20 mg BID and 30 mg BID significantly reduced pruritus VAS scores at week 16 compared to placebo (P=0.005 and P<0.001, respectively), while 10 mg BID did not (P=0.366). text: Apremilast 20 mg or 30 mg BID significantly reduced pruritus VAS scores at week 16 compared to placebo (P=0.005 and P<0.001). A higher proportion of patients on 20 mg (60.9%) or 30 mg (63.6%) reported pruritus improvements ≥MCID versus placebo (44.3%) [PMC3661377].

memory: A study compared vaginal practices (washing, wiping, insertion) across three sites: Johannesburg, Durban, and Harare. text: At baseline, vaginal washing was most common in Johannesburg (86.7%) compared to Durban (77.9%) and Harare (84.1%) (P < 0.0001). Source: [PMC2865639].

memory: A study compared chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) dressings to transparent dressings for reducing catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs). The CHG group had 1–5 times fewer CRBSIs, with 3 out of 1,000 patients developing infections, versus 14 out of 1,000 in the non-CHG group (PMC4472776). The difference was highly statistically significant, with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals. ICU-days and days before discharge or death were similar between groups.
text: Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) dressings significantly reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs) compared to transparent dressings (PMC4472776). The CHG group had 3 vs. 14 infections per 1,000 patients, with highly significant, non-overlapping confidence intervals. ICU-days and time to discharge/death were similar.

memory: A study compared home monitoring (HM ON) with regular in-office follow-up (HM OFF). memory: In advanced biliary tract cancer (aBTC), CPA combined with PPV improved progression-free survival (median 6.1 vs 2.9 months; HR 0.427; P=0.008) and overall survival (median 12.1 vs 5.9 months; HR 0.376; P=0.004) compared to PPV alone. memory: In a trial comparing sipuleucel-T alone (Arm 1) with sipuleucel-T plus pTVG-HP DNA vaccine (Arm 2), two Arm 2 patients (ID010, ID015) progressed at month 3 but remained progression-free until months 9 and 12, respectively. memory: A study compared sevoflurane with and without ondansetron. memory: In the dovitinib arm, 38.3% of patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events (AEs), compared to 8.0% in the placebo arm. memory: In a study [PMC4082484], participants consumed either a curry meal or a spice-free control meal. FMD decreased after the control meal (5.8 ± 2.4% to 5.1 ± 2.3%, P = 0.039), while it increased after the curry meal (5.2 ± 2.5% to 6.6 ± 2.0%, P = 0.001). text: A single serving of curry meal significantly increased flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal (P = 0.002). FMD decreased after the control meal, while it increased after the curry meal, suggesting a beneficial vascular effect of curry. Source: [PMC4082484].

memory: A study compared infliximab and ciclosporin, noting three deaths after infliximab: two from septic pneumonia (20 and 65 days post-treatment, both with diabetes and comorbidities) and one from disseminated colorectal cancer (278 days post-treatment, 20 years post-ulcerative colitis diagnosis). A cost-utility analysis found infliximab increased total health service costs by £5632 (95% CI 2773–8305) over 30 months (p=0.001), mainly due to higher acquisition costs. Effectiveness was similar, with no significant difference in quality-adjusted life-years (0.021; 95% CI −0.032 to 0.096; p=0.350).
text: Infliximab increases total health service costs by £5632 (95% CI 2773–8305) over 30 months compared with ciclosporin, primarily due to higher acquisition costs, with similar effectiveness (p=0.350). Source: Study cited.
