memory: A short-term trial compared MSDC-0160 to control for cognitive effects, measuring ADAS-Cog total score, 19-item cognitive battery z-score, and 7-item Executive Function battery z-score at baseline, 12 weeks, and 4-week follow-up. No significant cognitive differences were observed between groups. MSDC-0160 significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin levels (p<0.001), indicating improved insulin sensitivity. Circulating hs-CRP and FFA levels showed a downward trend, consistent with insulin sensitizer effects, though not statistically significant. Source: [PMC4153084].
text: MSDC-0160 did not significantly affect cognitive test battery global cognitive scores compared to control in a short-term trial (PMC4153084). However, it improved insulin sensitivity markers like adiponectin.
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: In a 12-month trial (ChiCTR-PRC-09000401) with 400 pre-diabetic patients, JinqiJiangtang (JQJT) tablets were compared to placebo. JQJT reduced diabetes progression risk by 42% (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P=0.010) and increased normalized blood glucose achievement by 41% (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.002-1.996, P=0.0049). Intention-to-treat analysis showed 16.5% diabetes incidence in the JQJT group versus 28.9% in the placebo group.
text: In a 12-month trial, JinqiJiangtang tablets reduced the risk of progressing from pre-diabetes to diabetes by 42% compared to placebo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P=0.010). The diabetes incidence was 16.5% in the JQJT group versus 28.9% in the placebo group.
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
outcome: risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes

memory: A study compared two clopidogrel administration strategies before coronary angiography (CAG). Group A received 600 mg >6 h before CAG, while Group B received it only if PCI was performed. Bleeding complications were 3.5% in Group A vs. 1.4% in Group B (P = 0.025). Adjusted analysis showed Group A had a 3.03-fold higher bleeding risk (95% CI 1.14–8.10; P = 0.027). Female gender (P = 0.001) and GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors (P = 0.027) were also significant bleeding risk factors. Low platelet counts approached significance (P = 0.091). Source: [PMC2429977].
text: Group A (non-selective clopidogrel) had a higher bleeding risk (3.5%) compared to Group B (selective clopidogrel, 1.4%; P = 0.025). Adjusted analysis showed a 3.03-fold increased risk in Group A (95% CI 1.14–8.10; P = 0.027). Source: [PMC2429977].
intervention: group A ('non-selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG;
comparator: group B ('selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg in the cath-lab after CAG, only in case of PCI;

memory: In a study [PMC4812817], 40% of patients had SIBO confirmed by GBT. DKT treatment did not alter bowel movement frequency or stool form. It significantly reduced median total GSRS scores (P < 0.001) and subscales for indigestion and constipation (ANOVA P < 0.001), but not acid reflux, diarrhea, or abdominal pain. Median VAS scores for abdominal bloating decreased from 76 to 30 (P = 0.005), and the overall treatment effect score increased from 13 to 51 (P = 0.005). Face scale assessments showed significant reductions in abdominal pain (P = 0.039) and bloating (P = 0.008).
text: Daikenchuto significantly reduced indigestion and constipation scores compared to control (ANOVA P < 0.001). It also decreased abdominal bloating (P = 0.005) and improved overall treatment effect (P = 0.005). Source: [PMC4812817].

memory: In a study comparing α-MSH to controls, α-MSH was linked with significantly reduced urine output over ten hours (p<0.05), with no animals becoming anuric. There was also a trend toward impaired recovery of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) compared to controls. Source: PMC3984270.
text: α-MSH significantly reduced urine output over ten hours compared to controls (p<0.05), without causing anuria. There was also a trend toward impaired recovery of GFR. Source: PMC3984270.

memory: A study compared telemonitored clinical care (TCC) to usual care for CPAP use. Telemonitored patients used CPAP on 78% ± 22% of nights, compared to 60% ± 32% in usual care (P = .07). No significant differences were found in CPAP efficacy measures, including mask leak or Apnea-Hypopnea Index. Telemonitored patients were more likely to continue CPAP use. Both groups reported high satisfaction with care and were "not concerned" about wireless data monitoring. Source: PMC1874716.
text: Telemonitored clinical care (TCC) was associated with a higher likelihood of patients continuing CPAP use compared to usual care (P = .07). No significant differences were found in CPAP efficacy measures. Source: PMC1874716.
outcome: Patients rated their likelihood to continue using CPAP

memory: A study compared manual therapy with usual care for headache management. Both groups showed significant improvements in primary and secondary outcomes, including reduced headache frequency, pain intensity, medication use, absenteeism, and professional help utilization. No significant differences were found between the two treatment groups. Recruitment was challenging, leading to a low participant number despite multiple strategies. Source: PMC2758835.
text: Both "Usual care" and "Manual therapy" significantly improved secondary outcomes like headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and professional help use. No significant differences were found between the two treatments. Source: PMC2758835.
outcome: Reduction in headache frequency, pain intensity, medication intake, absenteeism, and use of additional professional help (secondary outcomes)

memory: A study compared frovatriptan and rizatriptan for menstrually related migraine. Frovatriptan significantly reduced migraine recurrence at 24 hours (10% vs. 32%, p < 0.01) and had a lower cumulative hazard of recurrence (p < 0.01), as shown in Fig. 1. These findings suggest frovatriptan is more effective than rizatriptan in reducing migraine recurrence in this population. Source: [PMC3208043]
text: Frovatriptan significantly reduced the cumulative hazard of recurrence during follow-up for menstrually related migraine compared to rizatriptan (p < 0.01). Source: [PMC3208043]
outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine

memory: A study compared video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) to in-person consultations (UNN). Overall, consultation duration was not significantly different (p = 0.60). However, in the subgroup of patients requiring casting (11% of consultations), RMC had significantly longer mean consultation times (29.0 min) compared to UNN (22.6 min, p = 0.0063). All RMC patients underwent planned operations. Source: [PMC5017045]
text: In patients requiring casting, video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) had significantly longer mean consultation durations (29.0 min) compared to standard in-person consultations (22.6 min, p = 0.0063). Source: [PMC5017045]
outcome: The mean consultation duration in the subgroup patients who required casting

memory: A study compared Pro Taper Universal Retreatment (PR) and Mani NRT-GPR (MR) in canal retreatment. PR removed significantly less filling material (12.96%) than MR (24.26%) (P=0.0056). However, PR caused greater dentin removal (5.02%) compared to MR (1.36%) (P=0.0028). Neither system fully removed filling material from canals. Source: [PMC5911298].
text: Pro Taper Universal Retreatment removes significantly less remaining filling material (12.96%) compared to Mani NRT-GPR (24.26%) (P=0.0056), but causes more dentin removal (5.02% vs. 1.36%, P=0.0028). Neither system fully removes filling material. Source: [PMC5911298].

memory: A study compared prostaglandin gel with hygroscopic cervical dilators (n=17) to prostaglandin gel alone (n=23). No demographic differences were observed. After six hours, the combined group showed greater Bishop score improvement (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) and a trend toward shorter induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hours, P=0.085). However, the combined group had a significantly higher infection rate (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003). While combined therapy improved cervical ripening and induction speed, the increased infection risk is a major concern. Source: [PMC1784771].
text: The combination of prostaglandin gel with hygroscopic cervical dilators resulted in greater Bishop score improvement after 6 hours (3.6 vs. 2.1, P=0.007) compared to prostaglandin gel alone, though it was associated with a higher infection rate (59% vs. 12%, P=0.003) [PMC1784771].
intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours

memory: The Sonas programme improved interest in past events, humor, and general knowledge compared to control, but did not affect memory or communication. In MMSE-stratified analysis, Sonas showed significant differences from the reading group at baseline (p = 0.026) and follow-up (p = 0.011 and p = 0.044) for MMSE 0–10. For MMSE 11–20, a baseline difference was found between Sonas and reading (p = 0.026). No differences were observed between Sonas and control groups. Source: [PMC5425769].
text: The Sonas programme did not significantly improve MMSE scores compared to control groups. While it enhanced interest, humor, and general knowledge, it had no effect on memory or communication. No differences in MMSE scores were observed between Sonas and control groups. Source: [PMC5425769].

memory: A study compared RFA, hepatic resection, and combination therapy for liver metastases. The 5-year OS rates were 14.3% (RFA), 34.6% (resection), and 22.9% (combination), with no significant differences (P = 0.330). DFS was significantly lower in the RFA group (6.4%) than in resection (16.2%) and combination (18.4%) groups (P = 0.037). For 148 patients with solitary liver metastases, 5-year OS was 47.6% (RFA) and 56.0% (resection), with no significant difference (P = 0.308). Source: [PMC3204557].
text: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) had a lower 5-year disease-free survival (DFS) rate (6.4%) compared to hepatic resection (16.2%) and combination therapy (18.4%) in patients with liver metastases (P = 0.037). Source: [PMC3204557].

memory: A study with 13 subjects found that pomegranate juice containing 5.8 mg/100 ml anthocyanin significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (SBP) by 7% (P = 0.013) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) by 6% (P = 0.010) from baseline. However, improvements in flow-mediated dilation (FMD) of 20% were not statistically significant (P = 0.172). Source: [PMC3933059].
text: Pomegranate juice significantly reduced SBP by 7% (P = 0.013) and DBP by 6% (P = 0.010) compared to baseline in a study of 13 subjects. Source: [PMC3933059].
outcome: Systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP)

memory: A study compared r-FSH + rLH with r-FSH + HMG. No significant differences were found in follicle count, oocyte number, or M2 oocyte yield (p>0.05). However, the r-FSH + HMG group had significantly more total fetuses (p=0.02). Fertility outcomes, including live birth rate, chemical pregnancy, and clinical pregnancy rate, were significantly better in the r-FSH + HMG group (p<0.05). Source: [PMC5601935].
text: A study found no significant differences in oocyte or M2 oocyte yield between r-FSH + rLH and r-FSH + HMG (p>0.05). However, r-FSH + HMG showed better fertility outcomes, including higher live birth and pregnancy rates (p<0.05). Source: [PMC5601935].
intervention: Recombinant- follicle stimulating hormone (r-FSH) plus recombinant-luteinizing hormone (rLH)
outcome: Number of oocytes or M2 oocytes

memory: A study comparing Endobutton and Rigidfix showed that the Endobutton group had significantly higher mean IKDC 2000 satisfaction scores (89 ± 4.3 vs. 85 ± 2.9; P = 0.006). Last month symptoms scores were not significantly different (Endobutton: 89.8 ± 4.6; Rigidfix: 88.1 ± 5.2; P = 0.34). Endobutton also demonstrated significantly better ability to perform sports activities (85.2 ± 4.6 vs. 80.5 ± 4; P = 0.006). Source: [PMC5698974].
text: The Endobutton showed a significantly higher mean IKDC 2000 satisfaction score compared to Rigidfix (89 ± 4.3 vs. 85 ± 2.9; P = 0.006). Source: [PMC5698974].
outcome: the mean scores of satisfaction with surgery by using a subjective questionnaire IKDC 2000

memory: The SCOPE trial recruitment substudy was halted due to funding issues. Of 481 participants, 332 (69%) were contacted via telephone or mail, with similar mean ages (55.7 and 55.6, SD ~6.1). Among those contacted, 60 (18.1%) were ineligible due to recent colorectal screening: 18 had fecal occult blood testing, 39 had optical colonoscopy, 1 had virtual colonoscopy, and 2 were unspecified. Study flow is presented in Figure 1. Source: [PMC3599938].
text: The effect of "Follow-up invitation by telephone" compared with "Follow-up invitation by mail" on "Age of the participants" was minimal, as both groups had similar mean ages (55.7 and 55.6, SD ~6.1). Source: [PMC3599938].

memory: A study compared implants placed immediately after extraction (Group A, n=68) with those in healed sites (Group B, n=76). Group A showed higher mean peri-implant crevicular fluid volume (CFV) at all time points, with significant differences in maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3 (Table 2). Overall CFV differences were not statistically significant. Plaque levels increased over time but did not differ significantly between groups (p≥0.05, Mann-Whitney U-test). Marginal bone levels were assessed (Table 2). Source: PMC4048120.
text: Implants placed immediately after extraction (Group A) showed significantly higher maxillary CFV at time points 2 and 3 compared to healed sites (Group B) (PMC4048120).

text: Misoprostol + celecoxib significantly reduced potassium excretion on day 3 compared to baseline (p=0.0011) and the vehicle group (p=0.0267) [PMC3931696].

memory: A study compared a neuromuscular blocking agent (Group A) with atracurium infusion (Group B). Post-extubation heart rate was higher in Group B (P = 0.02), while mean arterial pressure and intraoperative heart rate were similar. Brain relaxation scores did not differ significantly (P = 0.27). Tracheal extubation time, orientation time, and time to achieve Aldrete score ≥9 were not significantly different between groups. Source: [PMC5296807].
text: Group B (Atracurium infusion) had a higher heart rate 30 minutes after extubation compared to Group A (Neuromuscular blocking agent) (P = 0.02). Other parameters like mean arterial pressure and intraoperative heart rate were similar. Source: [PMC5296807].

memory: A study compared ALTPOMx (pomegranate extract at altitude) with ALTPLAC (placebo at altitude) and found ALTPOMx significantly increased VO2 at 5 minutes into a cycling time trial to exhaustion at 100% VO2max (+3.8 ml·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹, 95% CI −5.7 to 9.5, F1,7 = 29.2, p = 0.001, ES = 0.6) compared to ALTPLAC. text: Exercise at 1657 m with pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx) significantly increased VO2 max at 5 minutes into a cycling time trial to exhaustion (+3.8 ml·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹, p = 0.001) compared to placebo (ALTPLAC). This effect was not observed at sea level. Source: PMC5452353.
intervention: Exercise at 1657 m of altitude plus Pomegranate extract (ALTPOMx)

memory: A study compared a self-management intervention to treatment as usual (TAU) and found that the self-management group had a significantly lower re-hospitalization rate. Over 30 months, 2 (1.9%) of 103 participants in the self-management group relapsed, compared to 14 (14.3%) of 98 in the TAU group. The difference was statistically significant (X²=8.83, p=0.003). The outcome was measured as the rate of re-hospitalizations.
text: The self-management group had a significantly lower re-hospitalization rate (1.9%) compared to treatment as usual (14.3%), with a statistically significant difference (X²=8.83, p=0.003).

memory: A study compared single-dose and multiple-dose artificial tears, finding both groups showed significant improvements in OSDI scores (p < 0.001). No significant difference in efficacy between the products was observed (p = 0.440), nor was there an interaction effect between product type and time (p = 0.468). TBUT also improved significantly in both groups (Group A: p = 0.027; Group B: p = 0.013), though the difference between products was not statistically significant (p = 0.497). These results are based on data from Table 1 and Table 2 of the source article [PMC5595267].
text: Both single-dose and multiple-dose artificial tears significantly improved OSDI scores (p < 0.001), with no significant difference in efficacy between them (p = 0.440). TBUT also improved significantly in both groups, but no significant difference was found between products (p = 0.497) [PMC5595267].

memory: Source: [PMC4715405]. A 10-week telephone intervention in pregnant women resulted in significantly lower 2-hour post-lunch blood glucose levels in the intervention group (123±18 mg/dl) compared to control (137.5±25.7 mg/dl; p=0.008). The intervention group demonstrated better post-lunch glucose control, suggesting potential benefits of the telephone intervention in managing blood sugar during pregnancy.

intervention: telephone intervention was performed for 10 weeks

memory: A study compared text message feedback with no feedback on mindfulness home practice, finding near-zero to small, nonsignificant effect sizes on outcomes (PHQ-9, PTQ, FFA, SCS-D). intervention: provided with written information about the electrodiagnostic testing

memory: A study compared cefepime (C), cefepime with amikacin (C-A), and cefepime with levofloxacin (C-L) in ICU patients. ICU length of stay after infection was similar across groups, with medians of 15 (7.5–24.75), 16 (9–21), and 14 (9.5–21.5) days, respectively. No significant differences were found in ventilator-free days (VFDs) within 28 days post-infection: 16.1 ± 8.3, 12.6 ± 8.1, and 12.6 ± 10.4 VFDs for C, C-A, and C-L groups (p > 0.05). text: The effect of cefepime (C), cefepime with amikacin (C-A), and cefepime with levofloxacin (C-L) on ICU length of stay after infection was similar, with no significant differences observed (p > 0.05). Source: PMC1550875.
intervention: cefepime (C group), cefepime with amikacin (C-A group)
outcome: length of stay in the intensive care unit after infection

memory: A study compared Irinotecan plus high-dose 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin (ILF) to Etoposide plus 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin (ELF). ILF caused more grade 3/4 gastrointestinal toxicities, especially diarrhoea (18% vs. 0% in ELF). Haematological toxicities were generally low, except for neutropenia, which occurred in 57% of ELF patients. Grade 3/4 alopecia was more common in ELF (28%) than ILF (5%). Five patients in each group withdrew or refused treatment, with only one case due to toxicity. Source: PMC2361806.
text: The ILF regimen caused more grade 3/4 digestive toxicities, particularly diarrhoea (18% vs. 0% in ELF). Source: PMC2361806.

memory: [PMC5019971] reported that maraviroc intensification compared to unchanged cART resulted in a 1.15% increase in FMD (p=0.079). Due to maraviroc’s 13h half-life, no washout period was used. A carry-over effect was observed in control period 2 (C2), with CD8+ CCR5+ expression rising from 8.3% to 16.3% (p=0.021). Subsequent analysis compared intervention (INT1 + INT2) to C1 (pre-maraviroc control).
text: Maraviroc intensification increased CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells compared to unchanged cART (from 8.3% to 16.3%, p=0.021). This effect was observed in the control period following maraviroc use, suggesting a carry-over impact. Source: [PMC5019971].
outcome: CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells

text: Intensive sound masking therapy significantly reduced THI scores in the effective subgroup (t=−14.07, P<0.001) compared to baseline, while the non-effective subgroup showed no significant reduction (t=−1.98, P=0.054) (PMC5695311).
intervention: intensive sound masking therapy on tinnitus in effective subgroup

memory: A study compared LNG-IUS and oral NET for fibroid regression, showing higher regression rates with LNG-IUS at 3 (67.8% vs. 47.5%, RR 1.42), 6 (79.7% vs. 60.7%, RR 1.31), and 12 months (88.1% vs. 55.7%, RR 1.58). text: The Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) shows a higher regression rate at 3 months compared to oral norethisterone acetate (NET) (67.8% vs. 47.5%, RR 1.42). Source: PMC3644688.

memory: In a study comparing calcium carbonate + calcitriol to calcitriol alone, serum calcium levels remained stable over 8 weeks in the calcitriol-only group (baseline: 9.6±0.5 mg/dL; 8 weeks: 9.6±0.5 mg/dL, P=0.77). text: The combination of calcium carbonate and calcitriol does not significantly affect serum calcium levels compared to calcitriol alone (ΔCa %: 2.6%±2.2% vs. 0.5%±4.6%, P=0.075). Serum calcium levels remained stable in both groups over 8 weeks. Source: PMC5565373.
intervention: a combination of calcium carbonate and calcitriol group

intervention: MgSO4 - Group I, II, III: 30. 40/ 50 mg/kg

memory: A study compared tranexamic acid (TXA) to placebo in patients with intracranial hemorrhage. Progressive hemorrhage occurred in 18% (21/120) of TXA patients versus 27% (32/118) in the placebo group, with no significant difference [RR = 0.65 (95% CI 0.40–1.05)]. memory: Study [PMC4610775] found that urinary kallidinogenase (UK) treatment improved cognitive status in patients at 4 weeks, linked to reduced serum Aβ1-40 levels, with no change in Aβ1-42. By 8 weeks, cognitive benefits remained, and both Aβ1-40 and Aβ1-42 levels significantly decreased. These results suggest UK may influence amyloid-beta metabolism, initially affecting Aβ1-40 and later Aβ1-42 over time.
text: Urinary kallidinogenase (UK) reduces Amyloid beta 1-40 levels compared to control, as shown in a study (PMC4610775). Initially, it lowered Aβ1-40 at 4 weeks, with both Aβ1-40 and Aβ1-42 decreasing by 8 weeks, suggesting a time-dependent effect on amyloid-beta metabolism.

memory: Study PMC4153077 showed that Bifidobacterium lactis significantly enhanced monocyte phagocytic activity compared to maltodextrin (P < 0.001) and galacto-oligosaccharides (prebiotic) groups (P < 0.001), indicating its potential superiority in boosting monocyte phagocytosis.
text: Bifidobacterium lactis significantly enhances monocyte phagocytosis compared to galacto-oligosaccharides (P < 0.001), suggesting it is more effective in boosting this immune function. (Source: PMC4153077)

memory: Source [PMC5019463]: A study compared a patient navigator intervention (G1) with usual care (G2, G3) on adherence, defined as ≥1 follow-up visit (69.8% G1, 82.5% G2, 73.3% G3; P=0.28) and ≥2 visits (91.3% G1, 74.3% G2, 66.7% G3; P=0.11). text: The study found no statistically significant difference in adherence rates (≥2 follow-up visits) between the patient navigator group (91.3%) and usual care groups (74.3% and 66.7%; P=0.11). Source: [PMC5019463].

memory: A study compared TCA and KOH for skin texture improvement. Both showed gradual hydration and texture improvement over time. At D14, KOH had reduced hydration, while TCA showed texture deterioration. Skin elasticity improved in the KOH group but decreased in the TCA group. At D7, TCA significantly improved skin texture compared to KOH (p = 0.00). Plantar skin showed increased hydration and texture but decreased elasticity over time. Callus surface area reduced by D7, D14, and D21 for both groups, except D7 in the TCA group. No significant differences in hydration and elasticity were observed between groups at each time point. memory: In a study [PMC3961877], patients received oral glutamine suspension (10g in 1000ml water) 2 hours before radiation or no intervention. memory: In a study [PMC3504298], face-based attention bias modification (ABM) was tested against placebo for reducing anxiety and depressive symptoms. Trait anxiety (STAI) showed a significant ABM type × ABM stimuli × time interaction (F(2,112) = 3.3, p = .05). Post hoc tests indicated that positive face ABM reduced anxiety during follow-up (F(1,28) = 5.2, p = .03; t(15) = 2.4, p = .03). Depressive symptoms (HRSD) showed similar trends but only reached a trend level (F(1,28) = 2.9, p = .09). The results suggest that positive face ABM may be beneficial for reducing anxiety symptoms, with less clear evidence for depression.
text: Face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) showed a significant reduction in anxious symptoms compared to placebo, as indicated by a significant interaction effect (F(2,112) = 3.3, p = .05) and post hoc tests (t(15) = 2.4, p = .03). This suggests ABM may be beneficial for reducing anxiety symptoms. (Source: PMC3504298)

memory: In a study [PMC4171519], raloxifene reduced type 2 diabetes incidence and blood glucose levels in ZDSD rats compared to vehicle-treated controls, both diabetic and non-diabetic. memory: In a study [PMC1868022], 39 women underwent cervical vault lavage (CVL) at enrollment and 2 weeks later, with a control group receiving no intervention. memory: In a study [PMC5264222], 596 RA patients on MTX were randomized to SB4 (etanercept biosimilar) or etanercept. At week 24, ACR20 response rates were 78.1% (SB4) and 80.3% (ETN), with an adjusted difference of -9.41% to 4.98% (95% CI), within the -15% to 15% equivalence margin, confirming therapeutic equivalence. Efficacy and pharmacokinetic endpoints were comparable. Adverse events were similar (55.2% vs 58.2%), but antidrug antibodies were lower in SB4 (0.7% vs 13.1%).
text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, is therapeutically equivalent to etanercept in RA patients on MTX, as shown by similar ACR20 response rates (78.1% vs. 80.3%) within the -15% to 15% equivalence margin [PMC5264222]. Efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and adverse events were comparable, with lower antidrug antibodies in SB4.
outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: A study compared robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) with standard navigation in cardiac ablation. High-dose aripiprazole significantly improved LS mean changes in all SNAP-IV rating subscales at week 8. Source: [PMC5689110].

memory: In a clinical study [PMC4391304], participants consumed either 100 g of fermented milk (FM) with Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055) or FM alone. memory: In a study [PMC3131514], prednisolone (7.5 mg and 30 mg daily) was compared to placebo, assessing effects on insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis. Prednisolone 30 mg significantly reduced insulin suppression of endogenous glucose production (46 ± 7%) and peripheral glucose uptake (34 ± 6%) compared to placebo. memory: A study compared daily prednisone to placebo, assessing bone metabolism markers. Plasma osteocalcin (OC) significantly decreased from 2 hours post-dose on Day 1, with dose-dependent reductions up to 12 hours post-dose. Procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP) was significantly reduced with prednisone ≥20 mg on Day 1, increased slightly on Day 2, then decreased dose- and time-dependently until Day 8. memory: Study [PMC4215531] evaluated the impact of 20 daily 1-hour sessions of facial affect training (FAT) versus baseline on alpha power. A significant Intervention × Time interaction (F(1,36) = 4.78, p = .04) showed greater alpha power improvement in the FAT group compared to a nonsignificant decline in the treatment-as-usual (TAU) group. However, no main effect of Intervention was found. Within the FAT group, a main effect of Time (F(1,18) = 5.61, p = .03) indicated increased alpha power during the pre-recognition period of the FAR criterion task post-training. On neuropsychological outcomes, the MCCB performance improved over time, with a Domain × Time interaction (F(6,324) = 4.05, p = .001), showing gains in Processing Speed, Attentional Vigilance, and Visual Learning. A Time × Intervention effect (F(2,54) = 3.70, p = .03) revealed improved Reasoning performance after cognitive enhancement (CE) but not after FAT or TAU. No Time × Intervention × Domain interaction was found (F(12, 324) = 1.28, p > .1). The findings suggest that FAT may enhance alpha power and certain cognitive domains, though effects vary by outcome measure and intervention type.
text: Facial affect training (FAT) in 20 daily 1-hour sessions showed a significant Intervention × Time interaction (F(1,36) = 4.78, p = .04), indicating greater alpha power improvement compared to baseline. Within the FAT group, alpha power increased during the pre-recognition period post-training (F(1,18) = 5.61, p = .03). (Source: PMC4215531)
intervention: facial affect training (FAT) in 20 daily 1-hour sessions

Source: [PMC4608626]  
Intervention: Singing Training vs. Control  
Outcome: Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) score  

Singing Training was associated with a significant decrease in NPI scores (p = 0.042), indicating reduced neuropsychiatric symptoms. Caregiver interviews supported these results with reports of improved behavior and mood. Additional findings included a significant reduction in time to complete the Japanese Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (p = 0.026) and increased sleep duration (p = 0.039). Functional MRI data showed increased brain activity in the right angular gyrus and left lingual gyrus. The Dementia Behavior Disturbance (DAD) score significantly decreased (p = 0.002), suggesting reduced behavioral disturbances. The Barthel Index score, which evaluates activities of daily living, did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.064), though a trend toward decline was noted. These results suggest that singing training may have beneficial effects on neuropsychiatric symptoms and behavior in patients, with potential cognitive and functional improvements, although functional outcomes were not statistically significant.
text: Singing Training significantly reduced Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) scores compared to Control (p = 0.042), indicating improved neuropsychiatric symptoms. This was supported by caregiver reports of better behavior and mood. Source: [PMC4608626].

memory: A study evaluated the effect of Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine (RCF) compared to Ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) and Ropivacaine-clonidine (RC) on hemodynamic parameters. No significant differences were observed in intraoperative and postoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) or heart rate (HR) between RCF, RF, and RC groups (P>0.05). Demographic and block characteristics were similar across all groups. Although RCF showed a significant reduction in side effects compared to RF and RC (P<0.05), this did not affect hemodynamic stability. Nausea/vomiting was more frequent in the RF group (40%) than in RCF (10%) and RC (15%). Sedation was higher in RF (30%) than in RCF (5%) and RC (10%). Dry mouth was more common in the RC group (P<0.05). Other side effects, such as shivering, headache, urinary retention, and respiratory depression, were comparable across groups. Analgesic properties were similar among the groups. The addition of clonidine and fentanyl to ropivacaine did not significantly alter hemodynamic parameters but improved patient comfort by reducing adverse effects. Source: [PMC4173331]
text: The addition of clonidine to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RCF) compared to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) did not significantly alter hemodynamic parameters like mean arterial pressure or heart rate. However, RCF reduced side effects such as nausea, sedation, and dry mouth, improving patient comfort. Source: [PMC4173331].

memory: Source [PMC5684963]: Low glycemic index (LGI) intervention significantly reduced glycemic response (GR) after lunch compared to high glycemic index (HGI) (p = 0.02). LGI also led to a lower area under the curve (AUC) for daily glucose response (p = 0.03). HGI caused an increased GR incremental area under the curve (IAUC) overnight (p = 0.003) and higher mean amplitude of glycemic excursion (MAGE) over 48 h (p = 0.03). Energy intake at lunch was greater with HGI (1041.6 ± 258.9 kcal) than LGI (840.7 ± 404.8 kcal; p = 0.02). No significant difference in MAGE was observed between days for LGI or HGI. Fasting glucose at 0600 h was higher with HGI on day 2 (p = 0.04).
text: A low glycemic index (LGI) intervention significantly reduces glycemic response (GR) after lunch compared to high glycemic index (HGI) (p = 0.02) and lowers daily glucose AUC (p = 0.03). HGI increases overnight GR IAUC (p = 0.003) and 48-h MAGE (p = 0.03). Source: [PMC5684963].

Source: [PMC4141382]  
Research question: Effect of "Caudal Sufentanil + neostigmine" vs. "Caudal Sufentanil" on "Dipyrone needed."  
Intervention: Caudal Sufentanil + neostigmine (Groups CSuNeo and CSuNeoAdr) vs. Caudal Sufentanil (Groups CSu and CSuAdr).  
Outcome: Dipyrone needed (number of postoperative doses in 24 h).  

Results: Patients receiving caudal sufentanil plus neostigmine required significantly fewer dipyrone doses in 24 h compared to those receiving caudal sufentanil alone or with adrenaline (P < 0.005). The number of dipyrone doses administered by a trained nurse was similar among Group IVSu, Group CSu, and Group CSuAdr (P > 0.05). The time to first dipyrone administration was similar among Group IVSu, Group CSu, and Group CSuAdr (3-4 h), but significantly delayed in Group CSuNeo and Group CSuNeoAdr (10-11 h) (P < 0.05). VAS for sedation at reversal time was similar among Group IVSu, Group CSu, and Group CSuAdr (P > 0.05), but lower in Group CSuNeo and Group CSuNeoAdr (P < 0.005). Isoflurane consumption was similar among Group IVSu, Group CSuNeo, and Group CSuNeoAdr but lower than Group CSu and Group CSuAdr (P < 0.02). The incidence of postoperative nausea or vomiting was similar across all groups.
text: Caudal sufentanil plus neostigmine significantly reduced dipyrone doses needed (P < 0.005) compared to caudal sufentanil alone or with adrenaline. Source: [PMC4141382].

memory: A study compared the transillumination-assisted technique group (T group) with the midline approach technique group (R group) in terms of intubation success rates at first, second, and third attempts. No significant differences were found between the groups in success rates at any attempt or overall success rate (P > 0.05). However, in patients who succeeded on the second attempt, the T group had significantly longer intubation times compared to the R group (P = 0.0006), although overall intubation time was not significantly different (P > 0.05). In the R group, first, second, and third attempt success rates were 78.0% (195/250), 14.4% (36/242), and 4.4% (11/242), respectively, with 3.2% (8/250) failing after three attempts. The T group experienced higher rates of dry throat (52.2% vs. 40.4%, P = 0.020), sore throat (26.8% vs. 16.8%, P = 0.009), and hoarseness (14% vs. 8%, P = 0.045) compared to the R group. These findings were reported in a study sourced from [PMC5320759].
text: The transillumination-assisted technique group (T group) showed no significant difference in intubation success rates at first, second, or third attempts compared to the midline approach technique group (R group) (P > 0.05). However, T group had longer intubation times for second-attempt successes (P = 0.0006). Source: [PMC5320759].
outcome: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempt

memory: The study evaluated the effect of laryngeal mask (PLMA) or endotracheal intubation (ETT) compared with baseline on cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation. Serum cortisol levels were significantly higher after CO2 insufflation than after anaesthesia induction in both the PLMA and ETT groups (p = 0.001). The PLMA group exhibited significantly lower cortisol levels than the ETT group (p = 0.024). No significant differences were observed between groups in terms of age, BMI, gender, ASA status, or operation time (p > 0.05). Adrenalin, noradrenalin, and dopamine levels showed no significant differences between or within groups. Hemodynamic and respiratory parameters remained stable across groups (p > 0.05). These findings suggest that both PLMA and ETT lead to elevated cortisol levels compared to baseline following CO2 insufflation, with PLMA associated with a reduced cortisol response compared to ETT. Supporting data are presented in Table 4 (group comparisons of stress hormones) and Table 5 (within-group comparisons of stress hormones) from the source article [PMC3525032].
text: Both PLMA and ETT significantly increase cortisol levels compared to baseline after CO2 insufflation (p = 0.001). PLMA shows a lower cortisol response than ETT (p = 0.024). [PMC3525032]
outcome: cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation

memory: The study evaluated the effect of hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs compared to no interventions on baseline characteristics. Baseline demographic data, including age, gender, marital status, employment status, educational level, duration of heart disease, hospitalizations, and other chronic diseases, were similar between the two groups, as presented in Tables 1 and 2 of the source article [PMC4776564]. Independent t-tests revealed no significant differences in baseline quality of life (QOL) scores across performance, health, socioeconomic, psychological, spiritual, and familial dimensions, as well as in satisfaction and importance areas. The intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in QOL scores in these areas immediately after and one month post-intervention compared to the control group (P < 0.05). These changes were supported by repeated measures ANOVA, which also identified significant changes over time in the control group. The comparable baseline characteristics between groups suggest that the observed differences in QOL outcomes were likely due to the intervention rather than pre-existing differences. This supports the internal validity of the study and strengthens the conclusion that the intervention had a positive effect on QOL.
text: The effect of hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs compared to no interventions on baseline characteristics showed no significant differences. Demographics, QOL scores, and other baseline factors were similar between groups (PMC4776564). Thus, the intervention likely caused the observed QOL improvements.
intervention: Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs

memory: In a study comparing butoconazole nitrate 2% Site Release vaginal cream (Gynazole-1) with oral fluconazole 150 mg tablets (Diflucan), butoconazole demonstrated a significantly shorter median time to first relief of symptoms (17.5 h vs. 22.9 h, p < 0.001). At 75% relief, butoconazole achieved this faster (24.5 h vs. 46.3 h, p < 0.001). By 12 h post-treatment, 44.4% of butoconazole patients reported relief, compared to 29.1% of fluconazole patients (p = 0.044), and by 24 h, 72.8% of butoconazole patients experienced relief versus 55.7% of fluconazole patients (p = 0.024). Among those with relief within 48 h, the median time was also shorter with butoconazole (12.9 h vs. 20.7 h, p = 0.048). However, no significant differences were observed in time to total relief of symptoms or recurrence of infection within 30 days. Butoconazole was associated with fewer adverse events, with the most common being vulvovaginal pruritus and burning. Source: PMC1784583.
text: Butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream significantly reduced the median time to first symptom relief compared to oral fluconazole 150 mg (17.5 h vs. 22.9 h, p < 0.001). Source: PMC1784583.
intervention: butoconazole nitrate 2% Site Release vaginal cream (Gynazole-1)
outcome: The median time to first relief of symptoms

memory: A study compared "Vit D as 50 000 IU/week" with "placebo" on fasting blood sugar (FBS), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1C), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP). Serum Vit D levels significantly increased in the Vit D group compared to baseline, while no change was observed in the placebo group. Proteinuria levels were not significantly different between groups at baseline or post-intervention (P=0.70 and P=0.48, respectively). However, the change in proteinuria over time was significantly different between groups (P=0.028), suggesting greater stability in the Vit D group. Regarding the primary outcomes—FBS, HbA1C, ESR, and CRP—no significant differences were found between the groups (P>0.05). This indicates that Vit D supplementation did not significantly impact metabolic or inflammatory markers. While the intervention successfully raised serum Vit D levels and showed a trend toward stabilizing proteinuria, it did not lead to improvements in the studied clinical outcomes. These findings are based on data from [PMC5106877].
text: Vit D (50,000 IU/week) did not significantly affect FBS, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP compared to placebo (P>0.05). Although it increased serum Vit D levels and showed a trend toward stabilizing proteinuria, it had no significant impact on metabolic or inflammatory markers [PMC5106877].
outcome: fasting blood sugar (FBS), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1C), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels

memory: A study compared the effect of lifestyle physical activity (LPA)—30 minutes of self-selected moderate-intensity activity, five to seven days per week—with a fibromyalgia education control (FME) group on pain in individuals with fibromyalgia. Baseline pain levels were similar between groups. After the intervention, the LPA group showed significantly reduced pain compared to the FME group (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67). Additionally, the LPA group had significant improvements in the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) score (P = .032; Cohen's d = .53). The six-minute walk test showed a trend toward significance (P = .067; Cohen's d = .53). No significant differences were observed between the groups in BMI, fatigue, depression, or number of tender points. The Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) showed no significant differences post-intervention (P = .888). The number of tender points also showed no significant differences (P = .172). Similarly, BMI showed no significant differences at post-intervention (P = .575). Fatigue severity scale scores also showed no significant differences between groups (P = .727). The study suggests that LPA may be more effective than FME in reducing pain and improving FIQ scores in individuals with fibromyalgia. Source: PMC2888205.
text: Lifestyle physical activity (LPA) significantly reduced pain compared to fibromyalgia education (FME) (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67) and improved FIQ scores (P = .032; Cohen's d = .53). No significant differences were found in BMI, fatigue, depression, or tender points. Source: PMC2888205.
intervention: lifestyle physical activity (LPA) - 30 minutes of self-selected moderate-intensity LPA, five to seven days per week
comparator: fibromyalgia (FM) education control (FME) group - received information and support

memory: Source article [PMC4899895] found that green tea significantly increases post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo (p < 0.01). Fat oxidation was also higher at rest after green tea ingestion (p < 0.05). Plasma glycerol levels increased significantly in both groups after green tea consumption, with higher levels in the untrained group compared to the trained group (p < 0.05). Plasma epinephrine levels were significantly higher during and after exercise in the green tea condition compared to placebo for both groups, while norepinephrine levels were only significantly greater in the untrained group (p < 0.05). Pre-exercise fat oxidation increased by 20% in both untrained and trained groups after green tea ingestion compared to placebo (p < 0.01). During the post-exercise period (minutes 30 to 75), fat oxidation rate was 15% higher in the green tea condition compared to placebo (p < 0.01). The respiratory exchange ratio (RER) was significantly lower from minutes 30 to 75 post-exercise in the green tea condition compared to placebo (p < 0.01). These findings suggest that green tea enhances fat oxidation both before and after exercise, potentially due to increased epinephrine and altered RER, indicating a shift toward fat utilization. The effect was consistent across trained and untrained individuals, though some differences were observed in glycerol and norepinephrine responses.
text: Green tea significantly increases post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo (p < 0.01). It also enhances pre-exercise fat oxidation by 20% and maintains higher fat oxidation rates during post-exercise (minutes 30–75) by 15% (p < 0.01). These effects are likely due to increased epinephrine levels and lower RER, indicating greater fat utilization. (Source: PMC4899895)

memory: In experiment 1, cursor color (red or blue) was linked to specific curl field directions. Over the exposure period, maximum perpendicular error (MPE) decreased significantly (F1,5 = 58.220; P = 0.001), but no significant increase in force compensation was observed between initial and final trials (F1,5 = 0.223; P = 0.657). Postexposure, no trajectory deviations were seen, suggesting no specific compensation was learned for the opposing force fields. In experiment 2, with no visual contextual cues, MPE decreased slightly (F1,5 = 12.560; P = 0.016), but again no significant increase in force compensation (F1,5 = 1.623; P = 0.259). Postexposure, no trajectory deviations were observed, indicating no learned compensation. In experiment 3, with movement in different workspace locations, MPE decreased significantly (F1,5 = 82.295; P < 0.001), and a significant increase in force compensation was found (F1,5 = 55.284; P = 0.001). Postexposure, strong trajectory deviations in the opposite direction were observed, suggesting learned compensation for field directions. In experiment 1, MPE decreased over the exposure period (F1,5 = 58.220; P = 0.001), but no significant increase in force compensation was observed (F1,5 = 0.223; P = 0.657). Postexposure, no trajectory deviations were observed, suggesting no specific compensation was learned for the two opposing force fields.
text: The initial trial showed a significant decrease in MPE over the exposure period (F1,5 = 58.220; P = 0.001), but no significant increase in force compensation compared to the final trial (F1,5 = 0.223; P = 0.657). Postexposure, no trajectory deviations were observed, suggesting no learned compensation.
outcome: over the course of the exposure period maximum perpendicular error (MPE) decrease - cursor color (red or blue)

memory: The effect of BZA/CE (bazedoxifene + conjugated estrogens) on breast tenderness compared to placebo was analyzed in multiple trials (SMART-1, SMART-2, SMART-5). Breast pain/tenderness was assessed using daily diaries. Results indicated no significant difference in the incidence of breast tenderness between BZA/CE groups (BZA 20 mg/CE 0.45 mg and BZA 20 mg/CE 0.625 mg) and placebo, raloxifene 60 mg, or BZA 20 mg alone. In SMART-5, BZA/CE showed significantly lower breast tenderness compared with CE 0.45 mg/MPA 1.5 mg (P < 0.001). BZA/CE did not influence age-related changes in mammographic breast density, unlike CE 0.45 mg/MPA 1.5 mg, which increased breast density compared to placebo. The incidence of breast tenderness in BZA/CE groups was consistent with adverse event rates and discontinuation rates due to breast pain in SMART trials. BZA/CE had an acceptable safety profile, with no increased risk of serious adverse events like venous thromboembolism, cardiovascular events, endometrial cancer, or breast cancer. These findings suggest that BZA/CE does not significantly increase breast tenderness compared to placebo, supporting its use in non-hysterectomized, symptomatic postmenopausal women.
text: BZA/CE does not significantly increase breast tenderness compared to placebo, based on trials like SMART-1, SMART-2, and SMART-5. Results showed no significant difference in breast tenderness incidence between BZA/CE groups and placebo.
intervention: BZA/CE combines bazedoxifene (BZA), a selective estrogen receptor modulator, with conjugated estrogens (CE),

memory: The study [PMC5126873] examined the impact of a "Diet and physical activity" intervention (UPBEAT) compared to a "Control" group on dietary patterns in pregnant women. The intervention was evaluated at 28 and 36 weeks gestation. Results showed significant reductions in "Processed" (−0.14; 95% CI −0.19, −0.08, P < 0.0001) and "Snacks" (−0.24; 95% CI −0.31, −0.17, P < 0.0001) dietary pattern scores in the intervention group, with these improvements maintained at 36 weeks. However, no significant differences were observed in "Fruit and vegetables" or "African/Caribbean" dietary pattern scores between the intervention and control groups at either 28 or 36 weeks. The data, presented in Table 2 of the source article, includes baseline, post-intervention, and late gestation dietary pattern scores. These findings suggest that the UPBEAT intervention effectively reduced consumption of processed and snack foods but did not significantly influence African/Caribbean food intake compared to the control group.
text: The "Diet and physical activity" intervention (UPBEAT) did not significantly affect "African/Caribbean food intake" compared to the control group (PMC5126873).

memory: Source article [PMC5686687]: A study compared Resveratrol to Placebo in terms of need for Ibuprofen. The mean Ibuprofen dose required was 1200 (848) mg [n=5] in the Resveratrol group and 5640 (328) mg [n=5] in the Placebo group, with P = 0.09, indicating a non-significant trend toward lower Ibuprofen use in the Resveratrol group. Pain scores were measured in 44 subjects, with no significant difference between groups post-treatment (P = 0.7; Mann-Whitney U test). The median difference in pain scores between groups was 0.75 (–1.6 to 2.3). The study was conducted between 18 June and 6 November 2015.
text: A study (PMC5686687) found a non-significant trend toward lower Ibuprofen use with Resveratrol (mean dose 1200 mg) compared to Placebo (5640 mg), P = 0.09. Pain scores showed no significant difference between groups.

memory: Source article [PMC5852701] evaluated the effect of "Regular activity breaks" (RAB) versus "Prolonged sitting" (SIT) on "Appetite area under the curve at day 1." Using linear mixed models, no significant difference in appetite AUC was found between RAB and SIT on Day 1 (standardised AUC difference: 0.11 S.D., 95% CI: −0.28, 0.06; p = 0.212). Similar results were observed on Day 2 (standardised AUC difference: 0.04 S.D., 95% CI: −0.15, 0.24; p = 0.648). Appetite scores before lunch predicted food consumption (β = −2.4 mm; 95% CI: 0.8 mm, 3.9 mm; p = 0.003), but no significant differences in food intake or energy consumption were found between RAB and SIT on Day 2. The study included 35 participants, with average appetite scores across days and interventions shown in Figure 3. Table 3 further confirms no significant changes in appetite response with RAB compared to SIT. The conclusion indicates that interrupting prolonged sitting with regular activity breaks does not acutely affect appetite or food consumption, despite increased energy expenditure. Findings suggest that RAB does not significantly alter appetite AUC on Day 1 or Day 2.
text: Regular activity breaks (RAB) did not significantly affect appetite area under the curve (AUC) on Day 1 compared to prolonged sitting (SIT) (standardised AUC difference: 0.11 S.D., 95% CI: −0.28, 0.06; p = 0.212). Findings suggest RAB does not acutely alter appetite or food consumption (PMC5852701).
outcome: Appetite area under the curve at day 1

memory: In a study comparing artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) with mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) in 490 patients with P. falciparum malaria, P. vivax parasitaemia was detected during follow-up in 26.3% of patients. The MAS3 group had significantly fewer cases of vivax malaria (29 of 227) compared to the ALN group (90 of 225) (P < 0.001). The median time to appearance of P. vivax parasitaemia was longer in the MAS3 group (40 days) than in the ALN group (28 days) (P < 0.001). Both regimens showed high PCR-adjusted cure rates by day 42, with 98.8% (95% CI, 96.4–99.6%) for ALN and 96.3% (95% CI, 93.1–98.0%) for MAS3 (P = 0.08). The mean decrease in haematocrit at day 7 was greater in the MAS3 group (9.3%) than in the ALN group (6.7%) (P = 0.023). The incidence of new P. falciparum infections during the 42-day follow-up was similar between the groups (27 in ALN and 24 in MAS3; P > 0.05). Adverse events were more common in the MAS3 group but not statistically significant. The most common adverse events included gastrointestinal and central nervous system effects. Source: [PMC1261533].
text: Mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) significantly reduced P. vivax parasitaemia during follow-up compared to artemether-lumefantrine (ALN) (29/227 vs. 90/225, P < 0.001). The median time to parasitaemia was longer in the MAS3 group (40 days vs. 28 days). Source: [PMC1261533].
outcome: P. vivax parasitaemia diagnosed during follow up

Source: [PMC5022334]  
Research question: Effect of "Thyroidectomy via BABA" vs. "Conventional open thyroidectomy" on "Visual analogue scale".  
Key findings: Robotic BABA thyroidectomy resulted in significantly lower VAS scores (2.1 ± 1.0) compared to conventional open thyroidectomy (3.8 ± 1.2; P < 0.05), indicating reduced postoperative pain. However, operative time was longer in the robotic group (118.8 ± 16.5 min vs. 90.7 ± 10.3 min; P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in intraoperative blood loss, hospital stay, number of lymph nodes removed, thyroglobulin levels, or complications (all P > 0.05). Cosmetic outcomes were better in the robotic group. Subclinical central lymph node metastasis rate was 35%, with no effect on staging. Complications such as hypoparathyroidism, RLN paralysis, and seroma were not significantly different between groups. No iatrogenic implantation or metastasis was found in punctured channels or chest wall. The robotic group had more patients with lymph node metastasis (19 vs. 16), but this did not affect staging (P > 0.05). No conversions to open or endoscopic surgery occurred in the robotic group. NSS scores were significantly higher in the robotic group (8.9 ± 0.8 vs. 4.8 ± 1.7; P < 0.05).
text: Thyroidectomy via BABA resulted in significantly lower VAS scores (2.1 ± 1.0) compared to conventional open thyroidectomy (3.8 ± 1.2; P < 0.05), indicating reduced postoperative pain (PMC5022334).

memory: In a study comparing "lightwand only" with "lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy," the WEI JET group had a significantly lower rate of successful tracheal intubation attempts compared to the lightwand-only group (1.0±0 vs. 1.21±0.4, p = 0.043). Intubation time was significantly longer in the WEI JET group (110.8±18.3 s) compared to both the lightwand-only group (63.3±27.5 s) and the direct laryngoscopy group (66.7±29.4 s, p = 0.000). However, the lowest SpO2 levels were significantly higher in the WEI JET group compared to the other two groups. No significant differences were observed in intubation time or the number of attempts between the lightwand-only and direct laryngoscopy groups. The findings suggest that the addition of WEI JET to the lightwand may negatively impact the success rate of tracheal intubation attempts, despite improvements in oxygen saturation. Source: [PMC4372550].
text: The "lightwand only" method had a higher successful tracheal intubation rate compared to "lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy" (1.21±0.4 vs. 1.0±0, p=0.043). Intubation time was longer with WEI JET (110.8±18.3 s). Source: [PMC4372550].
comparator: lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy

memory: The study evaluated the effect of "Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation" versus "Placebo" on "25(OH)D levels" over 48 weeks. Baseline 25(OH)D levels were comparable between groups. At week 24, the VitD/Cal group showed a median increase of 27.5 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = 15.0, 38.0 ng/mL) from baseline (P < .001), and this increased to 24.2 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = 14.6, 37.8 ng/mL) by week 48 (P < .001). In contrast, the placebo group exhibited negligible and non-significant changes: –0.8 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = –5.9, 4.9 ng/mL) at week 24 and 0.6 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = –6.1, 4.3 ng/mL) at week 48. Additional outcomes included glucose metabolism, lipid profile, and body composition. Insulin levels increased in the placebo group at week 24 but not in the VitD/Cal group, with no differences observed at week 48. Total and HDL cholesterol levels increased in both groups, but no significant intergroup differences were found. Waist circumference increased in the placebo group but not in the VitD/Cal group, though these differences were not statistically significant. Metabolic syndrome prevalence remained stable in both groups. The results confirm that "Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation" significantly elevates 25(OH)D levels compared to "Placebo" over 48 weeks (source article [PMC5726464]).
text: Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation significantly increases 25(OH)D levels compared to placebo over 48 weeks (P < .001 at weeks 24 and 48). Placebo showed negligible, non-significant changes. Source: [PMC5726464].

memory: A study compared cilostazol (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks) with placebo and found that cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to placebo (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, 95% CI 10.65 to 199.71; P = 0.0003). The sVCAM-1 level decreased from 1288.7 ± 285.6 ng/dL to 1168.2 ± 252.3 ng/dL in the cilostazol group. No significant differences were observed between the groups in other outcomes, including baPWV, hsCRP, adiponectin, IL-6, TNF-α, MCP-1, and sICAM-1. The mean difference in baPWV was 31.42 cm/sec (95% CI −55.67 to 118.5), indicating no improvement in this parameter with cilostazol treatment. These results suggest that cilostazol may specifically reduce sVCAM-1 without affecting other inflammatory or vascular markers. Source: [PMC3733748].
text: Cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to placebo (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, P = 0.0003). No significant changes were observed in other markers. Source: [PMC3733748].
intervention: cilostazol group (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks)
outcome: soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) level

memory: Source article [PMC2652457] found that "Computer assisted learning" (CAL) significantly increased "Level of enjoyment" compared to a "Control" group receiving an information leaflet (p = 0.04, 95% CI = 0.03–2.75, effect size = 0.7), with students using CAL reporting higher enjoyment levels. This result is supported in the Abstract and Results sections. CAL also showed better retention performance percentage scores (p = 0.02, 95% CI = 0.83–12.19, effect size = 0.8). However, no significant difference was observed in "Level of confidence to identify a child with autism" (p = 0.39, 95% CI = -1.80–0.72, effect size = -0.3). Additional findings indicated significant improvements in co-morbidities (p = 0.02, 95% CI = 1.96–23.03, effect size = 0.9) and treatment retention performance percentage scores (p = 0.003, 95% CI = 4.70–20.30, effect size = 1.2) with CAL. These results suggest that CAL enhances both knowledge retention and enjoyment compared to traditional control methods.
text: Computer-assisted learning (CAL) significantly increased the level of enjoyment compared to a control group (p = 0.04, effect size = 0.7) [PMC2652457]. Students using CAL reported higher enjoyment levels than those receiving an information leaflet.

memory: In the study [PMC5560514], Monovisc and saline were compared for pain reduction up to 3 weeks in the anteromedial subgroup of patients with knee osteoarthritis. Cingal showed significantly greater pain reduction than both Monovisc (P = .0168) and saline (P = .0458), while no significant difference was found between Monovisc and saline (P = .9154). A second analysis confirmed Cingal's superiority over Monovisc (P = .0449) and saline (P = .0231), with no difference between Monovisc and saline (P = .4782). These results suggest that Monovisc and saline had similar effects on pain reduction in this subgroup. Post hoc power analysis at 12 weeks indicated low power across all groups. In secondary outcomes, Cingal showed significant functional improvement over saline at 1 week in the anteromedial subgroup, but not over Monovisc. No significant differences in stiffness scores were found between treatment arms at 26 weeks. The study reanalyzed prior data to evaluate injection techniques, finding Cingal's pain reduction was significant only in the anteromedial subgroup. Anteromedial and anterolateral injection techniques demonstrated greater pain reduction than the lateral midpatellar approach at 18 and 26 weeks. The study highlights the lack of consensus on optimal injection technique and suggests that anteromedial and anterolateral approaches may be more effective than the lateral midpatellar approach.
text: Monovisc and saline had similar effects on pain reduction up to 3 weeks in the anteromedial subgroup (P = .9154). Cingal showed greater pain reduction than both. The study suggests no significant difference between Monovisc and saline in this subgroup. Source: [PMC5560514].
outcome: pain reduction up to 3 weeks in patients with knee osteoarthritis - anteromedial subgroup

memory: Source article [PMC2974815] reported that the "phone calls" group had significantly fewer patients discontinuing treatment compared to the "no phone calls" group (4 vs. 30; p<0.0094), indicating a lower rate of treatment discontinuation in the intervention group. This difference was statistically significant, suggesting that phone calls may positively influence patient adherence to treatment. The study did not report other outcomes related to treatment discontinuation. Regarding blood pressure control, no significant difference was found between the "phone calls" and "no phone calls" groups. However, "uncomplicated" and "complicated" groups showed significant differences in the percentage of patients with controlled blood pressure (<140/90 mmHg) (80% vs. 67%, respectively; p<0.000001). These findings suggest that while phone calls may not significantly affect blood pressure control, they do have a positive impact on reducing treatment discontinuation.

memory: In a study comparing skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding with no skin-to-skin contact, infants in the skin-to-skin group began latching on significantly earlier, with a median time of 2.0 weeks (Q1 = 1.0, Q3 = 3.7) compared to 4.7 weeks (Q1 = 2.0, Q3 = 8.0) in the control group (p = 0.020; Peto-Peto-Wilcoxon test, p = 0.017). A Kaplan-Meier curve illustrated this difference. However, the proportion of infants who started latching-on and suckling did not differ significantly between the groups (75% vs. 86%, p = 0.217). Additionally, the median age when infants started latching-on and suckling regularly was not significantly different (7.7 weeks vs. 7.1 weeks, p = 0.919). The experimental group also showed higher mean scores on the Breastfeeding Emotional Scale (mean 69.2 vs. 62.4, p = 0.022). The study included 31 infants in the experimental group and 33 in the control group for the latching-on time analysis. Source: [PMC3606616].

memory: Source article [PMC3785973] evaluated the effect of Internet-based self-management support (IBSM) versus control (UC) on inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) dosage in asthma patients. Outcomes were measured at 12 and 30 months post-baseline. At 12 months, IBSM improved asthma-related quality of life (AQLQ) and asthma control, but no significant changes in ICS dosage or FEV1 were observed. At 30 months, IBSM continued to show significant improvements in AQLQ (0.29; 95% CI 0.01–0.57) and asthma control (-0.33; 95% CI -0.61 to -0.05). No significant differences were found in ICS dosage or FEV1 at either time point. The findings suggest that IBSM enhances asthma-related quality of life and control but does not significantly alter ICS dosage. The study highlights the potential of IBSM in improving clinical outcomes related to asthma management, though it does not lead to changes in medication use as measured by ICS dosage. These results are important for understanding the role of digital health interventions in asthma care.
text: Internet-based self-management support (IBSM) did not significantly affect inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) dosage compared to control in asthma patients, according to [PMC3785973]. While IBSM improved quality of life and asthma control at 12 and 30 months, ICS dosage remained unchanged.

memory: In a randomized trial with 227 adults (mean age 42.3 ± 10.1 years, BMI 30.4 ± 4.1 kg/m²), participants were assigned to either a Basic or Enhanced weight loss maintenance (WLM) program. The Enhanced program included additional support compared to the Basic version. The primary outcome was BMI change after 12 months, and secondary outcomes included weight rebound and attrition. Attrition rates were 18.4% for the Basic group and 23.9% for the Enhanced group, with no significant difference (p = 0.31). Both groups showed minimal weight rebound (Basic: 1.3%, Enhanced: 1.5%) and no significant differences in BMI change (Basic: −0.5 (1.9) kg/m², Enhanced: −0.5 (1.6) kg/m², p = 0.93). The study used an intention-to-treat analysis with last observation carried forward imputation. No significant between-group differences were found for primary or secondary outcomes. The conclusion was that the web-based WLM program was effective in preventing weight regain over one year, but the addition of personalized e-feedback in the Enhanced program provided limited additional benefits compared to the Basic program. The study suggests both programs are similarly effective in maintaining weight loss over 12 months. Source: [PMC5746685]

memory: A study compared single sustained inflation (SI) with conventional ventilation and consecutive sustained inflation (SI) in terms of their effects on blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation in the cerebral cortex. Single SI was associated with a significant increase in these profiles (p = 0.001), indicating greater blood-brain barrier disruption, as reported in the Abstract > Results section of the source article [PMC4713062]. During single SI, carotid blood flow (CaBF) increased more rapidly and to a greater extent (p = 0.01) compared to other groups. However, by 10 minutes, CaBF decreased below levels in other groups due to higher cerebral oxygen delivery (p = 0.01). In contrast, no differences in CaBF or cerebral oxygen delivery were found between multiple SI and no SI groups. The increased cerebral oxygen delivery during single SI may have contributed to the observed blood-brain barrier disruption. The study suggests that the effect on blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation is specific to single SI compared to conventional ventilation and consecutive SI. These findings highlight potential adverse effects of single SI on cerebral vascular integrity, as indicated by plasma protein extravasation. The results may have implications for clinical practices involving sustained inflation in neonatal or critical care settings.

This effect is specific to single SI, suggesting potential adverse impacts on cerebral vascular integrity. Source: [PMC4713062].
outcome: numbers of blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation

memory: The study evaluated the effect of the Language Enhanced Attention and Focus MI training condition (MI-LEAF) compared to baseline and MI-AU on "sustain talk" (ST). Results indicated that MI-LEAF significantly reduced client ST at 3-month follow-up compared to baseline (b = −0.1008, SE = 0.0179, p < 0.001), supporting the hypothesis. Additionally, MI-LEAF showed a significant reduction in ST compared to MI-AU (b = −0.175, SE = 0.087, p = 0.046). Reflections of ST were also significantly lower in the MI-LEAF group compared to MI-AU (b = −0.257, SE = 0.114, p = 0.025). No significant differences were observed in client collaborative talk (CT) frequency when comparing MI-LEAF to baseline (b = −0.0857, SE = 0.0923, p = 0.355) or MI-AU (b = −0.018, SE = 0.064, p = 0.781). MI knowledge improved significantly post-training (b = 0.111, SE = 0.015, p < 0.001), with no differences between training conditions (b = −0.041, SE = 0.031, p = 0.186). These findings suggest that MI-LEAF training effectively reduces client ST compared to both baseline and MI-AU, though CT was not significantly affected. Source: [PMC5539943].

memory: The study evaluated the effect of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) versus placebo on Transient-Evoked Otoacoustic Emissions (TEOAE) pure-tone average (PTA) and high-frequency average (HFA). Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to assess group mean differences for changes in TEOAE PTA (F(2,31) = 0.133, P = 0.876) and HFA (F(2,31) = 0.20, P = 0.819), with no significant differences found. A Kruskal-Wallis test was also performed to assess group medians for changes in TEOAE HFA (Kw(2) = 4.04, P = 0.133), again revealing no significant differences. For PTA, ANOVA showed no differences between group means (F(2,57) = 0.09, P = 0.913) or for HFA (F(2,57) = 1.33, P = 0.274). The study noted that the third assumption was assumed to be met, while the fourth assumption was likely violated. Results are summarized in Tables 2, 3, 6, and 7. Overall, the findings indicate no statistically significant differences between LLLT and placebo in their effect on TEOAE PTA or HFA. Source: [PMC3658388].

memory: Vildagliptin significantly reduced HbA1c compared to placebo (−0.5 ± 0.1% vs. +0.2 ± 0.1%; P < .001), indicating improved glycemic control. Fasting plasma glucose also decreased by −1.0 mmol/L with vildagliptin (P = .018). Additionally, liver triglycerides decreased by 27% (7.3% to 5.3%) in the vildagliptin group, while no change was observed in the placebo group (P = .013). ALT levels decreased in the vildagliptin group (27.2 ± 2.8 to 20.3 ± 1.4 IU/L; P = .0007), and this reduction was strongly correlated with the decrease in liver triglycerides (r = 0.83; P < .0001). Hepatic glucose production suppression was similar between the vildagliptin and placebo groups (P = .89 and P = .42, respectively). These findings suggest that vildagliptin not only improves glycemic control but also has beneficial effects on liver metabolism. Source: [PMC4399299].

memory: In a study comparing Paricalcitol (PAR) and Calcifediol (CAL), serum iPTH levels were significantly lower in the PAR group at 6 months (76 ± 55 pg/ml vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036). However, the proportion of patients achieving a ≥30% reduction in iPTH was not significantly different between groups (95.1% vs. 88.4%; P = 0.26). The proportion of patients with iPTH between 70 and 110 pg/ml was lower in the PAR group (14.6% vs. 25.6%; P = 0.056). In the per-protocol population, a significant difference was observed in the number of patients with iPTH >110 pg/ml (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008). However, in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, this difference was not statistically significant (19.6% vs. 36.2%; P = 0.07). No significant differences were found between groups in other bone turnover markers, such as osteocalcin and bone alkaline phosphatase, or in BMD at the femoral neck and lumbar spine. FGF23 levels decreased in both groups, with lower values observed in the CAL group at 6 months. These findings suggest that while PAR may lead to lower iPTH levels, the clinical significance of this difference remains unclear, and further analysis is warranted. Source: PMC5762965.
text: Paricalcitol significantly reduced serum iPTH levels compared to Calcifediol at 6 months (P = 0.0036), but the clinical significance remains unclear. Source: PMC5762965.

memory: A study compared nebivolol and atenolol using VH-IVUS to evaluate their effects on plaque components and TCFAs per vessel. Both drugs showed similar changes in these parameters (Table 2). However, nebivolol was associated with increased plaque area at follow-up (P<0.001), whereas atenolol showed plaque regression (P=0.047). The difference between the two groups was not statistically significant (P=0.27). Nebivolol also resulted in significantly reduced EEM area (P=0.02) and lumen area (P=0.004) compared to atenolol. Static remodeling indices were similar, but serial remodeling differed significantly (P=0.002). Nebivolol was linked with more constrictive remodeling (73% vs. 46%) and less excessive expansive remodeling (16% vs. 39%) compared to atenolol. These findings were illustrated in Figure 6, which shows serial arterial remodeling by β-blocker at 1-year follow-up. The P value represents the comparison of the frequency of three remodeling groups across the two β-blocker categories. The study also reported a P value for the comparison of WSS categories across the two β-blockers.

memory: A study examined the effect of 2 mg melatonin over 4 days in tetraplegic patients (and placebo) compared to able-bodied men with no intervention, focusing on circadian variation of F1+2, a marker of thrombin generation. No significant differences were found in F1+2 circadian patterns between tetraplegic groups receiving melatonin or placebo (P>0.05). However, both tetraplegic groups showed significantly increased circadian variation of F1+2 compared to able-bodied men (P=0.01 and P<0.001). D-dimer circadian patterns were similar across all groups (P>0.05), and absolute concentrations of F1+2 and D-dimer were comparable in all groups (P>0.05). Tetraplegic patients had distinct 24-h profiles of prothrombin fragment 1+2 and von Willebrand factor compared to able-bodied subjects (P<0.05), while activated FVII levels were higher in able-bodied men (P<0.05). Melatonin had no significant effect on these markers. Plasma concentrations of PAI-1 and free TFPI showed no significant differences across groups in terms of circadian variation or absolute levels (P>0.05). Sleep duration and quality remained unchanged in tetraplegic patients with or without melatonin. The study concluded that melatonin supplementation in tetraplegic patients mimicked endogenous circadian variation without significantly altering hemostatic markers. Source: [PMC5399146]

memory: The study compared the effect of "Sachets of 'Sprinkles' with vitamin A" versus "Sachets of 'Sprinkles' without vitamin A" on baseline MRDR values. At baseline, MRDR values were similar between the intervention and control groups, with values of 0.032 (SD 0.018) (95% CI: 0.025–0.038) and 0.031 (SD 0.018) (95% CI: 0.024–0.038), respectively. No significant differences were found in total body stores (TBS) of vitamin A or liver retinol concentrations after the intervention, with TBS values of 436 (SD 303) and 434 (SD 186) μmol, and liver retinol concentrations of 0.82 (SD 0.53) and 0.79 (SD 0.36) μmol/g liver, respectively. Additionally, no significant differences were observed in anthropometric indices, including weight, height, and z-scores, between the intervention and control groups at baseline and endline. Although a tendency for higher anemia rates was observed in the control group at the end of the supplementation period (31.6%) compared to the intervention group (23.5%), this difference was not statistically significant. The results suggest that baseline MRDR values were similar in both groups, and the intervention did not significantly affect vitamin A stores or other measured outcomes. Source: [PMC4780150].

memory: In a study comparing Ciclesonide (CIC) and Fluticasone propionate (FLP) as preferred intranasal corticosteroids, Fluticasone propionate (FLP) was significantly preferred over Ciclesonide (CIC) (55.41% vs. 25.68%, P = 0.007), primarily due to better sensory attributes. Patients favored FLP for its more satisfying scent (50% vs. 8.11%, P < 0.001) and more soothing feel (56.76% vs. 20.27%, P < 0.001). FLP also caused less nasal irritation (1.35% vs. 28.38%, P = 0.002). Although FLP was associated with less urge to sneeze (1.35% vs. 13.51%), this difference was not statistically significant. Taste-related issues were less frequent with CIC, but this difference was also not significant. No significant difference in immediate efficacy was observed between the two medications. Side effects included mild headache (2 with CIC first, 3 with FLP first), dizziness, and nasal congestion. The study highlights FLP's superior sensory profile, particularly in reducing nasal irritation and improving patient preference, despite similar efficacy. Source: PMC3480782.

memory: At 36 months, a higher proportion of subjects implanted with Superion® (63/120, 52.5%) achieved the primary composite endpoint compared to X-STOP® (49/129, 38.0%) (P=0.023). Superion® showed sustained clinical success from 24 months (53%), while X-STOP® experienced a slight decline from 50% at 24 months. Superion® success rates for individual components of the primary endpoint exceeded 80%, with rates of 88%, 81%, 91%, and 87% for improvement in two of three ZCQ domains, no reoperations at the index level, no major implant/procedure-related complications, and no clinically significant confounding treatments, respectively. Five of six comparisons favored Superion®, with only leg pain results reaching statistical significance. Line graphs showed the durability of Superion® outcomes and a modest decline in X-STOP® results between 24 and 36 months for ZCQ, back and leg pain severity, and back function. X-STOP® had more reoperations, revisions, and removals (15/44) compared to Superion® (11/49). Superion® maintained improvements in back and leg pain severity and functional outcomes through 36 months. Source: [PMC4599047]

memory: In Study B [PMC1570354], the median number of days with no use of relief medication was 63% for the salmeterol/fluticasone propionate (SFC, Seretide™, GSK, UK) group and 61% for the formoterol/budesonide (FBC, Symbicort™, AstraZeneca, UK) group.
