Source: [PMC4731690]  
Research question: Effect of more vs less extensive hyperdense artery sign (HAS) on 6-month Oxford Handicap Scale (OHS).  
Key findings:  
- More extensive HAS independently predicted worse 6-month outcome (higher OHS score) (OR 0.61, p = 0.027).  
- HAS presence (vs absence) was also linked to worse outcome (OR 0.66, p < 0.001).  
- No significant difference in outcome between proximal vs distal HAS (p = 0.420).  
- Alteplase treatment increased HAS shrinkage/disappearance (OR 0.77, p = 0.006).  
- Alteplase effect on HAS shrinkage was not significantly different based on HAS location (p = 0.516) or extent (p = 0.580).  
- No interaction between HAS presence and alteplase benefit on OHS (p = 0.167).  
- Increasing age was associated with more HAS growth at follow-up (OR 1.01, p = 0.013).  
Conclusion: More extensive HAS is associated with worse 6-month outcome, independent of alteplase treatment or HAS location. Alteplase improves HAS shrinkage but does not differentially affect outcome based on HAS extent or location.
text: More extensive hyperdense artery sign (HAS) independently predicts worse 6-month Oxford Handicap Scale (OHS) outcomes (OR 0.61, p = 0.027). This association remains regardless of alteplase treatment or HAS location.

memory: A study compared "Drug-eluting balloon + bare metal stent" (DEB + BMS) with "Zotarolimus-eluting stent" (ZES) in 180 patients for the outcome of "Binary restenosis." Patients were divided into two groups: 72 received DEB + BMS, and 74 received ZES. Angiographic follow-up occurred at 298 days post-procedure, with an 81.1% follow-up rate. Baseline characteristics, including minimal lumen diameter, reference diameter, percentage diameter stenosis, and lesion length, were similar between groups. Post-procedure, DEB + BMS showed significantly lower minimal luminal diameter and less acute gain compared to ZES. Late luminal loss (LL) was significantly higher in the DEB + BMS group (0.50 ± 0.46 mm) compared to ZES (0.21 ± 0.44 mm; P < 0.001). The mean difference in LL was 0.31 mm (95% CI: 0.15–0.48), exceeding the non-inferiority margin of 0.19 mm (P for non-inferiority = 0.138). Although binary restenosis rate was higher in the DEB + BMS group, the difference was not statistically significant. The study concluded that DEB + BMS was not non-inferior to ZES in terms of LL, indicating a potential disadvantage in restenosis risk. Source: [PMC5426232].
text: The "Drug-eluting balloon + bare metal stent" showed a higher late luminal loss (0.50 ± 0.46 mm) compared to "Zotarolimus-eluting stent" (0.21 ± 0.44 mm; P < 0.001), exceeding the non-inferiority margin. Although binary restenosis rates were higher in the DEB + BMS group, the difference was not statistically significant. Source: [PMC5426232].

memory: A study compared nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) with usual care (UC) and motivational interviewing (MIC) on triglyceride levels. A significant time-by-condition interaction was found (F(2,85)=3.92, p=.024, partial eta2=.084). Post-hoc analyses showed significantly lower triglyceride levels in the NPC group compared to UC (p=0.008) and a trend toward significance compared to MIC (p=0.057). No significant differences were observed between MIC and UC (p=0.423). Triglyceride levels, along with weight and depression scores, decreased significantly in NPC compared to UC but not MIC. These results were maintained at 3-month follow-up, with approximately 25% of MIC and NPC patients achieving at least 5% weight loss, regardless of BED status. Fidelity ratings were high, and treatment adherence was associated with weight loss. Psychologically, NPC led to significantly lower BDI scores compared to UC at post-treatment (p=0.009), though not compared to MIC (p=0.195). No significant differences were found between MIC and UC in BDI scores (p=0.168). Participants in NPC and MIC reported higher satisfaction with treatment compared to UC (p<.0005). Source: [PMC4236282]
text: Nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) significantly reduced triglyceride levels compared to usual care (UC) (p=0.008) but not compared to motivational interviewing (MIC) (p=0.057). Source: [PMC4236282].

memory: The study compared the 10-mm transumbilical group with the 5-mm transabdominal group in terms of intact tubes. Post-operative evaluation showed 18 intact tubes in the transumbilical group versus 3 in the transabdominal group (P < 0.001, OR: 51.0, 95% CI: 7.56-343.73), indicating a significantly higher rate of intact tubes in the transumbilical group. No intra-operative rupture of the retrieval bag was observed during specimen extraction. Baseline characteristics, such as age, BMI, obstetric history, hospital stay, and tubal size, were similar between the groups. The transumbilical group had a significantly shorter specimen retrieval time (43.5 ± 14.5 s) compared to the transabdominal group (69.4 ± 20.5 s, P < 0.001). Both groups reported similar overall satisfaction with surgery (9.2 ± 0.6 vs. 9.5 ± 0.6, P = 0.69) and cosmetic results (9.6 ± 0.5 vs. 9.8 ± 0.4, P = 0.74). Rescue analgesia was required for four patients in the transumbilical group and three in the transabdominal group. No surgical complications were reported, and all patients were discharged on postoperative day 1. A three-month follow-up showed uneventful recovery with no complications, such as post-side herniation. Source: [PMC3872586].
text: The 10-mm transumbilical group had significantly more intact tubes (18) compared to the 5-mm transabdominal group (3; P < 0.001, OR: 51.0). Other outcomes, such as satisfaction and recovery, were similar. Source: [PMC3872586].

memory: A study compared "specially designed molding titanium clips" (intervention) with a control on ventilator time and hospital stay. No differences were found in injury severity score, revised trauma score, or trauma injury severity score between groups. After adjusting for these scores, ventilator time was significantly lower in the surgical group (142 ± 224 hours vs. 74 ± 125 hours, P = 0.026). Similarly, overall hospital stay was significantly lower in the surgical group (142 ± 224 hours vs. 74 ± 125 hours, P = 0.026). There was a trend toward shorter ICU stay for operative patients (12.3 ± 8.5 days vs. 9.0 ± 4.3 days, P = 0.076), though not statistically significant. Surgery was performed within the first 48 hours. The study concluded that rib fixation using titanium clips is feasible and associated with reduced ventilator time and hospital stay. Adjusted results suggest the intervention may have a beneficial effect on these outcomes. Source: PMC4331314.

memory: A study evaluated the effect of "Gait training with constrained induced movement therapy" (experimental group) versus "Gait training alone" (control group) on dynamic balance improvement. Dynamic balance was assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test and Limits of Stability (LOS) test. Participants had comparable baseline characteristics except for age. The experimental group demonstrated a 28.6% improvement in TUG scores and a 34.3% increase in paretic side movement distances on the LOS test. In contrast, the control group did not show significant improvements in balance ability following gait training alone. These findings suggest that incorporating constrained induced movement therapy into gait training leads to significantly greater dynamic balance improvements. This implies that combined therapies may enhance balance outcomes in patients undergoing gait training. Source: [PMC4395675].

memory: A study compared the aprepitant regimen (aprepitant plus tropisetron and dexamethasone) with the standard regimen (tropisetron and dexamethasone) on complete response (CR) in the delay phase (DP). The aprepitant regimen significantly improved CR during DP (80.0% vs. 56.0%, P = 0.018), with similar results observed in the overall phase (OP) (80.0% vs. 56.0%, P = 0.018). No difference was found in the acute phase (AP), where both groups achieved identical CR rates (98.0%, P = 1.000). CR in the OP was the primary endpoint, while CR in the AP and DP were secondary endpoints. The study also used Kaplan–Meier curves to evaluate the first time of vomiting and the FLIE to assess the impact of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) on quality of life. Within the aprepitant group, males had a higher CR rate compared to females (93.1% vs. 61.9%, P = 0.011). These findings suggest that adding aprepitant to the standard regimen enhances CR in DP and OP, with no effect in AP. Source: PMC5851005.
text: The aprepitant regimen (aprepitant plus tropisetron and dexamethasone) significantly improved complete response (CR) in the delay phase (DP) compared to the standard regimen (tropisetron and dexamethasone) (80.0% vs. 56.0%, P = 0.018). Source: PMC5851005.

memory: No significant differences in treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were observed between ch14.18-UTC and ch14.18-NCI [PMC4747995]. The overall incidence of TRAEs was similar between the two formulations, despite variations in specific adverse events. Pain was the most common TRAE, reported in 59% of ch14.18-UTC recipients and 44% of ch14.18-NCI recipients, followed by abdominal pain (48% vs. 41%) and pain in extremity (33% vs. 41%). Pain-related TRAEs were most frequently reported during cycles 1, 2, and 4 (93%, 74%, and 71%, respectively). The adverse event profiles of both products were consistent with previously reported findings, indicating similar safety profiles. These results suggest that ch14.18-UTC and ch14.18-NCI have comparable safety profiles in terms of TRAEs, with no significant differences in overall incidence or major categories of adverse events. The findings support the use of both products with similar risk profiles, though individual patient experiences may vary. The data highlight the importance of monitoring for pain-related events during early treatment cycles. The adverse event data align with prior studies, reinforcing that the safety profile of these ch14.18-based products is well-characterized.
text: No significant differences in adverse events were observed between ch14.18-UTC and ch14.18-NCI [PMC4747995]. Both had similar overall incidence of treatment-related adverse events, with pain being the most common. Safety profiles were comparable, supporting similar risk profiles for both formulations.

memory: Source article [PMC4472776] evaluated Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) dressings versus transparent dressings for preventing catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI). In a study with 1,000 patients per group, CRBSI occurred in 3 patients in the CHG group and 14 in the transparent group, showing a statistically significant difference with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals. The CRBSI ratio between groups was 1:5. ICU days and time to discharge or death were similar between groups. The number needed to treat (NNT) with CHG to prevent one CRBSI was 85. The mean cost per patient for CHG was €141 higher than for transparent dressings, but this was not statistically significant (95% CI: [€-975; €1,258]). The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was €12,046 per CRBSI prevented, and the incremental net monetary benefit per patient was €344.88. These findings indicate that CHG dressings are more effective in preventing CRBSIs, though their cost-effectiveness is moderate.
text: Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) dressings significantly reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) compared to transparent dressings (3 vs. 14 cases, ratio 1:5, p<0.05). The NNT to prevent one CRBSI is 85. While more costly (€141), the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio is €12,046 per CRBSI prevented, indicating moderate cost-effectiveness. Source: [PMC4472776].

memory: Source article [PMC2856148] evaluated noninvasive ventilation (NIV) versus pressure support ventilation (PSV) in terms of weaning duration and related outcomes. The study groups were comparable in demographics, disease severity, and clinical profiles. No significant difference was observed in duration of mechanical ventilation (6.20 ± 5.20 days vs. 7.47 ± 6.38 days, P > 0.05), weaning duration (35.17 ± 16.98 hours vs. 47.05 ± 20.98 hours, P > 0.05), or ICU stay (8.47 ± 4.79 days vs. 10.80 ± 5.28 days, P > 0.05). Although NIV showed a trend toward shorter ICU stays (about 2 days less), this was not statistically significant. The NIV group had fewer cases of ventilator-associated pneumonia (1 vs. 5) and lower mortality rates at ICU discharge (3 vs. 5) and at 30 days (5 vs. 9), but these differences were also not statistically significant (P > 0.05). The findings suggest that while NIV may offer potential clinical benefits, including reduced VAP and lower mortality trends, there is no significant difference between NIV and PSV regarding weaning duration or ICU stay.

NIV showed trends toward shorter ICU stays and lower mortality but these were not statistically significant. Thus, NIV does not significantly affect weaning duration compared to PSV (PMC2856148).

memory: In a study of 18 patients with an average age of 55.8±6.9 years and symptom duration of 3.6±1.6 years, the effect of "Hydrodistension plus intravesical resiniferatoxin (RTX)" versus "Hydrodistension only" on voiding symptoms was assessed. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in voiding frequency, functional bladder capacity, and pain scores (measured on a 5-point scale) at 3 months post-treatment. However, no significant differences were observed between the two groups in terms of voiding symptom improvement or uroflowmetry outcomes. Baseline interstitial cystitis (IC) symptom severity was comparable, and no clinically meaningful differences were noted. All patients had previously failed other treatments. The study suggests that while RTX combined with hydrodistension may provide pain relief, it does not lead to significant improvements in voiding symptoms or urodynamic parameters compared to hydrodistension alone. These findings indicate that adding RTX may not offer additional benefits for improving voiding function in patients with IC. Source: [PMC3321403].

memory: PVB significantly reduced NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing/movement compared to control (P<0.05) [PMC5513842]. PVB was associated with lower tramadol consumption (200 mg vs 300 mg, P=0.003) and reduced nurse-administered morphine use (0 mg vs 2.5 mg, P=0.001). The time to first analgesic request was significantly longer in the PVB group (120 min vs 30 min, P<0.05). No significant differences were found in postoperative vital signs between groups (P>0.05). Patient demographics showed similar gender distribution (PVB 84% female, control 80% female) and comparable ASA classifications (PVB 26% ASA I, control 40% ASA I). These results suggest PVB provides effective pain relief and reduces opioid use compared to control. The absence of adverse effects on vital signs supports PVB's safety profile. Similar baseline characteristics between groups enhance the validity of the comparison. These findings indicate a potential benefit of PVB in postoperative pain management. However, further research in larger and more diverse populations is needed to confirm these results. The study highlights the potential of PVB as an effective alternative to control in managing postoperative pain with minimal side effects.
text: Paravertebral block (PVB) significantly reduces NRS pain scores at rest and during movement compared to control (P<0.05) [PMC5513842]. It also decreases opioid consumption and delays the first analgesic request, suggesting PVB offers effective, safe postoperative pain relief.

Intervention: Home Monitoring facilitated FU (HM ON) vs. regular in-office FU (HM OFF)  
Outcome: Follow-up (FU) visits  

HM ON significantly reduced scheduled in-office FU visits compared to HM OFF (3.79 ± 1.67 vs. 5.53 ± 2.32; P < 0.001). Although HM ON had more unscheduled in-office visits (0.95 ± 1.50 vs. 0.62 ± 1.25; P < 0.005), the total number of FU visits was still significantly lower. HM ON involved more non-office-based contacts (e.g., phone calls) and internal staff discussions. No significant differences were observed in other healthcare service utilization, though there were numerically fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations and shorter hospital stays in the HM ON group. Additionally, a higher percentage of in-office visits in the HM ON group resulted in clinically relevant findings or actions (32.0% vs. 26.8%; P < 0.05). The total FU cost for providers was not significantly different between the groups. Patient demographics included an average age of 62.4 ± 13.1 years, with 81% male, 39% receiving a DDD system, and 51% having a prophylactic ICD.

memory: A study compared calcitriol with placebo and found no adverse events in any patients during the follow-up period [PMC2928344]. The study evaluated multiple outcomes, including adverse events, A1C levels, insulin requirements, and C-peptide response. No significant differences were observed between the calcitriol and placebo groups in A1C levels, insulin requirements, or C-peptide response at 6, 12, and 24 months. Calcium and phosphate levels remained within normal ranges throughout the study. Although fasting C-peptide levels declined significantly in both groups, the decline was less pronounced in the calcitriol group (17.7%) compared to the placebo group (28.4%) after 12 months. However, no significant difference was found in the area under the curve of C-peptide response between the groups at baseline or after 12 months. Vitamin D deficiency at diagnosis was not linked to lower residual β-cell function at 24 months. At baseline, 47% of participants had significant vitamin D deficiency, with 25OHD levels increasing slightly in the calcitriol group and decreasing in the placebo group over time. Overall, the absence of adverse events indicates that calcitriol was well-tolerated compared to placebo.
text: A study found no adverse events in patients treated with calcitriol compared to placebo [PMC2928344]. Calcitriol was well-tolerated, with no significant differences in adverse events between groups during follow-up.

memory: The study evaluated the effect of "Vitamin D + Calcium" versus "Placebo" on serum 25(OH)D levels using data from the CaMEWS and D&Cancer trials. Participants in both studies had comparable baseline characteristics, including age, BMI, and initial serum 25(OH)D and calcium levels (all P > 0.05). The "Vitamin D + Calcium" group demonstrated significantly greater increases in serum 25(OH)D compared to both the Calcium-only group and the Placebo group (P < 0.0001). In CaMEWS, the mean serum 25(OH)D change was +24.31 nmol/L, while in D&Cancer, it was +31.92 nmol/L. In contrast, the Calcium-only group in CaMEWS had a minimal increase of −1.02 nmol/L, and the Placebo group in D&Cancer showed a negligible change of 0.36 nmol/L. Baseline serum 25(OH)D levels ranged from 24.2 to 144.6 nmol/L in CaMEWS and from 13.3 to 225.8 nmol/L in D&Cancer. These results suggest that the combination of Vitamin D and Calcium significantly elevates serum 25(OH)D levels compared to Placebo or Calcium-only interventions. Source: [PMC5228186].
text: The combination of Vitamin D + Calcium significantly increases serum 25(OH)D levels compared to Placebo (P < 0.0001). Source: [PMC5228186].

memory: A study compared classic cigarettes (group C) with two e-cigarette types (group H: disposable cigalike e-cigarette with 24 mg nicotine; group E: second-generation e-cigarette with 24 mg nicotine) on craving levels over time. Craving increased significantly in group C from T1 to T6, and similarly in group H from T1 to T6, while in group E, craving increased only up to T3. This suggests that craving increases more persistently with classic cigarettes compared to either e-cigarette type. The study found no effect of the products or gender on cognitive performance, including attention, executive function, and working memory. The research highlights the role of smoking-related gestures and rituals in tobacco addiction, noting that e-cigarettes may replace some of these rituals, potentially aiding in smoking cessation. Second-generation e-cigarettes can deliver nicotine levels comparable to classic cigarettes, but craving persistence differs. The trial was registered under ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01735487). Findings suggest that factors beyond nicotine, such as the ritual of smoking, may influence smoking dependence and relapse.
text: Classic cigarettes caused a more persistent increase in craving over time compared to both e-cigarette types. Craving in e-cigarette users (H and E) increased only up to T3, suggesting that factors beyond nicotine, such as smoking rituals, may influence craving persistence. Source: NCT01735487.

memory: [PMC5588958] A 28-day trial of SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) in T2DM patients showed a statistically significant reduction in body weight by 0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) compared to placebo. However, HbA1c increased by 0.48% (95% CI 0.26% to 0.70%, p=0.004) and fructosamine rose by 33.41 μmol/L (95% CI 20.24 to 46.58, p<0.001), indicating potential adverse metabolic effects. Bradykinin-induced vasodilatation was reduced (mean diff −1.291, 95% CI −2.296 to −0.285, p=0.012), while acetylcholine- and sodium nitroprusside-induced vasodilatation remained unchanged. No significant changes were observed in lipid profile or platelet-monocyte activation (p>0.05). SRT2104 also reduced plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 antigen release (mean diff −38.89 ng/100 mL tissue/min, 95% CI −75.47 to –2.305, p=0.038), with no differences in other fibrinolytic factors. The findings suggest a modest weight loss benefit but raise concerns about glycemic control and vascular function. Further studies are needed to evaluate the clinical significance of these effects.
text: A 28-day trial found that SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) significantly reduced body weight by 0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) compared to placebo in T2DM patients. However, it worsened glycemic control (HbA1c +0.48%, p=0.004) and reduced bradykinin-induced vasodilation (p=0.012). (Source: PMC5588958)

memory: In a study on advanced biliary tract cancer (aBTC), Cyclophosphamide (CPA) combined with Peptide-based Vaccination (PPV) showed improved progression-free survival (PFS) compared to PPV alone. The median PFS was 6.1 months in the PPV/CPA group versus 2.9 months in the PPV-only group (HR: 0.427; P = 0.008). The addition of CPA was associated with enhanced T cell responses to vaccinated peptides, though no significant differences in peptide-specific IgG levels were observed. Plasma IL-6 levels increased significantly after PPV in the PPV-alone group but not in the PPV/CPA group, suggesting CPA may reduce IL-6-driven immune suppression. IL-6 changes were negatively correlated with T cell responses (Spearman r = -0.703; P = 0.007). IFN-γ spot numbers showed increased T cell responses in both arms over time, but no significant differences were observed between them. The study suggests that low-dose CPA combined with PPV may offer clinical benefits in aBTC patients by enhancing antigen-specific T cell responses and mitigating IL-6-mediated immune suppression. Source: [PMC5448649].
text: Cyclophosphamide (CPA) combined with Peptide-based Vaccination (PPV) improved progression-free survival (PFS) in advanced biliary tract cancer compared to PPV alone (median PFS 6.1 vs. 2.9 months; HR: 0.427; P = 0.008). Source: [PMC5448649].

memory: A study compared an oestradiol group (N=47) receiving 2 mg of oestradiol valerate orally with progesterone to a control group (N=51) receiving vaginal progesterone supplementation alone, starting after oocyte retrieval and continuing until the tenth week if a chemical pregnancy was confirmed. The primary outcome was the mean duration of infertility, which was 5.98 ±0.55 years in the control group and 7.81 ±1.37 years in the oestradiol group, with no statistically significant difference (P > 0.05). Additional outcomes, including serum progesterone and oestradiol levels, were higher in the oestradiol group but not statistically significant (P > 0.05). LH levels were measured on different days, with no significant differences observed between the groups. The study also found no significant differences in the mean number of retrieved oocytes, number of transferred embryos, or chemical and clinical pregnancy rates between the two groups. Among the oestradiol group participants with a positive β hCG test (25 out of 47), 23 had a detectable intrauterine gestational sac with fetal heart activity, while one had an ectopic pregnancy and another had a blighted ovum. The study provides data on the lack of significant differences in key reproductive outcomes between the two treatment groups. Source: PMC3258705.

memory: Source article [PMC5971505] evaluated the effect of Paracetamol versus Ibuprofen on Surfactant therapy in 22 premature infants. A randomized study assigned 9 infants to Paracetamol and 6 to Ibuprofen. No significant differences were found between the groups in outcomes related to Surfactant therapy (p=0.898), mortality, primary closure rates, or short-term neonatal outcomes. Sepsis occurred in 7 infants in the Paracetamol group and 4 in the Ibuprofen group, but this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.664). Pulmonary hemorrhage was reported in 1 infant in each group (p=0.783). The study concluded that there was no significant difference between Paracetamol and Ibuprofen in terms of mortality, primary closure rates, or short-term neonatal outcomes. The results suggest that both drugs may be similarly effective in the context of Surfactant therapy for premature infants, though larger studies may be needed to confirm these findings.

memory: Source article [PMC5754420] found that speed endurance training (SET) increased citrate synthase (CS) maximal activity by 18%, significantly more than the small-sided game (SSG) group. No changes in phosphofructokinase (PFK) maximal activity were observed in either group. HAD maximal activity increased by 24% in both groups, with no between-group differences. Na+–K+ ATPase α1 subunit protein expression increased by 19% in SET and 37% in SSG, with a trend toward greater change in SSG. No differences were found in α2, β1, and FXYD1 subunits. MCT4 protein expression increased by 30% in SET and 61% in SSG. SOD2 protein expression increased by 28% in SET and 37% in SSG. GLUT-4 expression increased by 40% in SSG only. SET also showed a 39% greater improvement in Yo–Yo IR2 performance compared to SSG. These findings indicate that SET is more effective than SSG in enhancing CS maximal activity, a key indicator of mitochondrial enzyme capacity, while both interventions elicited some adaptations in other markers of muscle metabolism and performance.
text: Speed endurance training (SET) increased citrate synthase maximal activity by 18%, significantly more than small-sided games (SSG) [PMC5754420]. Thus, SET is more effective than SSG in enhancing CS maximal activity.

A study evaluated the effect of prefrontal rTMS versus sham rTMS on face and scalp sensations. Participants could not reliably differentiate between real and sham sessions, with only 40% guessing correctly (p = 0.27), suggesting that the sham condition effectively mimicked the sensory experience of real rTMS, supporting its validity in replicating face and scalp sensations.

Regarding cravings, both real and sham rTMS led to significant reductions [F(1,9) = 15.91, p = 0.003]. However, no significant difference was found between real and sham conditions [F(1,9) = 1.13, ns], nor was there a significant time by condition interaction [F(1,9) = 0.13, ns]. Adjusting for hours since last meal, no significant effects were observed for time [F(1,8) = 2.97, ns], condition [F(1,8) = 1.94, ns], or the time by condition interaction [F(1,8) = 2.07, ns]. Although the change in cravings was slightly greater in the sham-TMS group, the effect size was minimal (d = 0.09), favoring sham-TMS. These results suggest that the reduction in cravings was not specific to real rTMS and may be attributed to placebo effects or the sham condition itself.
text: Prefrontal rTMS and sham rTMS had similar effects on face and scalp sensations, as participants could not reliably distinguish between the two (40% correct guess, p = 0.27). Both conditions led to comparable reductions in cravings, with no significant differences between them. These findings suggest that the sensory and craving effects may be attributable to placebo or sham condition factors rather than specific rTMS effects.

memory: In a study comparing haloperidol 1 mg (H1), haloperidol 2 mg (H2), and saline (H0), the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) was evaluated within 24 hours postoperatively. Both H1 and H2 showed significantly lower PONV incidence compared to H0 (29% vs. 54% and 24% vs. 54%, respectively; P = 0.003). In the ward (2–24 h), PONV rates remained lower for H1 (22%) and H2 (20%) compared to H0 (42%), with no significant difference between H1 and H2. Sedation scores in the PACU over 2 hours showed that H2 had higher sedation than H1 and H0 (P < 0.001), with no difference between H1 and H0. Three patients in the H2 group required ephedrine due to hypotension (systolic 75–80 mmHg, diastolic 50–55 mmHg) in the PACU. These findings suggest that both haloperidol doses reduced PONV compared to saline, but no significant difference in PONV incidence was observed between H1 and H2. Source: [PMC4493951].
text: Both H1 (haloperidol 1 mg) and H2 (haloperidol 2 mg) significantly reduced PONV incidence compared to H0 (saline) within 24 hours postoperatively (29% vs. 54% and 24% vs. 54%, P = 0.003). No significant difference in PONV incidence was observed between H1 and H2. Source: [PMC4493951].
outcome: the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV)

memory: In a study comparing "sipuleucel-T alone followed by intradermal immunization with pTVG-HP DNA vaccine" to "sipuleucel-T alone" on overall survival, 18 patients were followed for a median of 24 months. Th1-biased PAP-specific T-cell responses were observed in 11/18 patients, with no significant differences between treatment arms. Patients receiving the DNA vaccine showed higher antibody titers against PAP. Median time to progression was less than 6 months, with no statistical differences between groups. Median overall survival was 715 days (24 months) in the sipuleucel-T alone group versus 901 days (30 months) in the sipuleucel-T + DNA vaccine group, though the difference was not statistically significant (Fig. 6b). PSA doubling times remained similar before and after treatment (2.55 months), with no significant differences between arms. Time to radiographic progression was also not significantly different (median 161 days in Arm 1 vs. 164 days in Arm 2). Two patients in the DNA vaccine group experienced early progression at month 3 but remained progression-free until months 9 and 12, respectively. The trial was not adequately powered to detect differences in overall survival or time to progression. Source: [PMC5850960]
text: The combination of sipuleucel-T with pTVG-HP DNA vaccine showed a trend toward improved overall survival (901 vs. 715 days) compared to sipuleucel-T alone, but the difference was not statistically significant. The trial was underpowered to detect such differences. Source: [PMC5850960].

memory: In a study comparing selenium (Se) supplementation with placebo, the impact on soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (sFlt-1) was assessed. Among participants with the lowest baseline selenium status (n=50), Se treatment significantly reduced sFlt-1 concentrations (P=0.039) and halved the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio (P=0.066, not significant). However, when considering all participants (n=233), Se did not significantly influence sFlt-1, PlGF, or the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio. The relative risk of Se on PlGF was 0.97 (95% CI: 0.78–1.21, P=0.801). These results suggest that the positive effects of Se on sFlt-1 and the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio are confined to individuals with low baseline selenium levels. Source: [PMC4054662].
text: Selenium supplementation significantly reduced soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (sFlt-1) concentrations (P=0.039) only in participants with low baseline selenium status (n=50), but not in the overall group (n=233). Source: [PMC4054662].

memory: A study compared "Natural childbirth preparation" with "Standard antenatal education" on elective Caesarean rates. No significant difference was found between the groups: 6% (29/484) in the Natural group and 6% (31/514) in the Standard group (relative risk [RR] 0.9, 95% CI: 0.6 to 1.6, p = 0.8). Spontaneous vaginal delivery rates were also similar, at 66% in both groups (RR: 1.0, 95% CI: 0.9 to 1.1, p = 1.0). Emergency Caesarean rates were 14% in the Natural group and 15% in the Standard group (RR: 0.9, 95% CI: 0.7 to 1.2, p = 0.5). Parental stress and childbirth experience were not significantly different between the groups. Notably, 70% of women in the Natural group used psychoprophylaxis during labour, compared to 37% in the Standard group. Subgroup analysis excluding psychoprophylaxis users did not change the main findings. Epidural use was similar in both groups at 52%. The study suggests that neither intervention significantly affects elective or emergency Caesarean rates or maternal outcomes. Source: [PMC2759981].
text: A study found no significant difference between "Natural childbirth preparation" and "Standard antenatal education" on elective Caesarean rates (6% vs. 6%, RR 0.9, 95% CI: 0.6 to 1.6, p = 0.8). Both groups had similar outcomes for spontaneous vaginal delivery, emergency Caesarean rates, and maternal stress. Source: [PMC2759981].

memory: A study compared SP-based scenarios with mannequin-based scenarios on realism scores, finding SP-based scenarios significantly higher (4.73/5 vs 2.00/5, P=0.002). The study included 19 residents, with 9 in the mannequin group and 10 in the SP group. Pre-test scores were similar (2.56/5 vs 2.53/5). Post-test scores were significantly higher in the SP group (4.53/5 vs 3.69/5, P=0.01), with improvement in all scenarios except acute bacterial meningitis. The SP group showed greater improvement in post-test scores compared to the mannequin group (1.8/5 vs 1.2/5, P=0.01). In the calcium channel blocker overdose scenario, the SP group had a 2.4/5 (48%) improvement, while the mannequin group had 1.3/5 (26%) improvement (P=0.03). SP-based scenarios also led to significantly higher post-test scores in three of four scenarios (P=0.01). The realism score was notably higher in SP-based scenarios, indicating a more realistic simulation experience. Results were consistent across multiple scenarios, including severe asthma exacerbation and severe sepsis. The study suggests that SP-based scenarios may enhance both learning outcomes and perceived realism compared to mannequin-based scenarios. Source: [PMC5524701]
text: SP-based scenarios significantly improved realism scores compared to mannequin-based scenarios (4.73/5 vs 2.00/5, P=0.002). Source: [PMC5524701].

memory: Study [PMC4305224] assessed the impact of "Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + azithromycin" (SPAZ) versus control on the risk of active placental malaria in 2,021 women. SPAZ significantly reduced active placental malaria (RR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47–0.98, P=0.037) and maternal parasitaemia (RR: 0.57, 95% CI: 0.35–0.95, P=0.029). No serious adverse events (SAEs) were linked to SPAZ, with similar rates between groups (13.1% vs. 12.7%, P=0.712). Adverse events (AEs) were also comparable (10.5% vs. 10.8%, P=0.737). Additional benefits included lower risk of low birthweight (RR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.60–0.91, P=0.005) and preterm delivery (RR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.43–0.89, P=0.010), along with a 41.9 g increase in mean birthweight (95% CI: 0.2–83.6, P=0.049). The findings suggest that SPAZ may offer protective effects against placental malaria and improve perinatal outcomes without increasing the risk of serious adverse events.
text: Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + azithromycin significantly reduces the risk of active placental malaria (RR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47–0.98, P=0.037) compared to control, with no increased serious adverse events (PMC4305224).

memory:
Source: [PMC3633335]  
Research question: Effect of "Sevoflurane + Ondansetron" vs. "Sevoflurane alone" on "Vomiting".  
Key findings:  
- Vomiting incidence was significantly lower in groups receiving Sevoflurane + Ondansetron (group II: 17.5%, group IV: 7.5%, group VI: 10%) compared to groups receiving Sevoflurane alone (group I: 55%, group III: 27.5%, group V: 30%) (P < 0.05).  
- Groups III and V had lower vomiting rates than group I (P < 0.05).  
- Ondansetron reduced vomiting incidence but not nausea across all three types of general anesthesia.  
- Nausea incidence was 55% in group I, 42.5% in group II, 30% in group III, 27.5% in group IV, 30% in group V, and 30% in group VI. Groups III and V had lower nausea rates than group I (P < 0.05).  
- No significant difference in vomiting was found between groups II, IV, and VI.  
- No significant difference in vomiting was found between group II vs. group I, group IV vs. group III, and group VI vs. group V.  
Conclusion: Sevoflurane combined with ondansetron reduced vomiting compared to sevoflurane alone.
text: Sevoflurane + ondansetron significantly reduces vomiting compared to sevoflurane alone (PMC3633335). Groups receiving the combination had vomiting rates of 17.5%, 7.5%, and 10%, versus 55%, 27.5%, and 30% for sevoflurane alone (P < 0.05). Ondansetron did not affect nausea rates.

memory: A study compared Posterior lamellar tarsal rotation (PLTR) surgery with Bilamellar tarsal rotation (BLTR) surgery, focusing on pain between surgery and stitches removal. No significant difference in pain during surgery was found (p=0.84). However, BLTR surgery was associated with significantly more pain and discomfort during the early recovery phase (OR 1.46 [95% CI 1.12–1.89]; p=0.004). PLTR surgery was quicker (15 min 33 s vs 16 min 39 s; p<0.0001). No significant differences in patient satisfaction for trichiasis treatment or cosmetic appearance were observed (p=0.20 and p=0.64). BLTR was also associated with a higher risk of recurrent trichiasis at 12 months (OR 1.96 [95% CI 1.40–2.75]; p=0.0001). No evidence of effect modification by other factors on the primary outcome was found. Source: [PMC5075282].
text: Posterior lamellar tarsal rotation (PLTR) surgery caused less pain during early recovery compared to bilamellar tarsal rotation (BLTR) surgery (OR 1.46, p=0.004). PLTR was also quicker (p<0.0001). No significant difference in pain during surgery was found (p=0.84). Source: [PMC5075282].
outcome: Pain between surgery and stitches removal

memory: In a study comparing Dovitinib to Placebo, discontinuation due to rash occurred more frequently in the Dovitinib group (4.3%) than in the Placebo group (0%) [PMC5301372]. Rash, along with diarrhea (6.4% vs 0%), alanine aminotransferase increase (4.3% vs 2.0%), and aspartate aminotransferase increase (4.3% vs 2.0%), were the most common adverse events (≥3%) leading to discontinuation [Additional file 2: Table S2]. Dovitinib was associated with a higher frequency of dose reductions (74.5% vs 26.0%) and dose changes (57.4% vs 8.0%) due to adverse events compared to Placebo. Overall, discontinuation due to adverse events was significantly higher in the Dovitinib group (21.3%) compared to Placebo (2.0%). Other reasons for discontinuation included progressive disease (55.3% vs 80.0%), patient or guardian decision (10.6% vs 0%), termination by sponsor (8.5% vs 16.0%), death (2.1% vs 2.0%), and nonadherence (2.1% vs 0%). Four on-treatment deaths were reported, with two in each group. One death in the Dovitinib arm was attributed to breast cancer progression, and another was suspected to be due to a pulmonary embolism related to treatment.
text: Dovitinib was associated with a higher rate of discontinuation due to rash (4.3%) compared to Placebo (0%) [PMC5301372].

memory: No significant differences in adverse event rates between Vitamin D3 groups (DD: 40,000 IU, DP: 20,000 IU) and placebo (PP) [PMC2818614]. No serious adverse events were reported. Serum 25(OH)D levels increased in both DD and DP groups but did not significantly affect BMD, OPG, or RANKL. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels decreased in both Vitamin D3 groups. text: No significant differences in adverse event rates were found between Vitamin D3 groups (40,000 IU or 20,000 IU) and placebo [PMC2818614]. No serious adverse events were reported.

These results indicate that adding LIPUS significantly enhances FD and RF values over time, with a more pronounced effect in the intervention group. The findings support the effectiveness of LIPUS as an adjunct to standard implant protocols in promoting favorable outcomes. Source: PMC5925011.
text: Adding low-intensity power ultrasound (LIPUS) to the standard implant protocol significantly increases FD mesial values after six months (0.342 vs. 0.132 units, Cohen's d = 4.85) compared to standard treatment (PMC5925011).

memory: Source article [PMC4082484] found that a single serving of curry meal significantly increased postprandial flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal. FMD decreased after the control meal (from 5.8 ± 2.4% to 5.1 ± 2.3%, P = 0.039), whereas it increased after the curry meal (from 5.2 ± 2.5% to 6.6 ± 2.0%, P = 0.001). Postprandial FMD after the curry meal was significantly higher than after the control meal (P = 0.002). The study found that spices in the curry did not significantly affect systemic or forearm hemodynamics or biochemical parameters like oxidative stress markers. These results suggest that curry improves endothelial function as measured by FMD, independent of systemic or biochemical changes. The control meal had a neutral or slightly negative effect on FMD. This evidence supports the potential role of curry in enhancing vascular function, possibly through bioactive compounds in spices. The study provides a foundation for further research into specific curry components that may improve endothelial function.
text: A single serving of curry meal significantly increases postprandial flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal (P = 0.002). The control meal slightly decreased FMD, while curry improved endothelial function, independent of systemic or biochemical changes (PMC4082484).

Infliximab compared to Ciclosporin in Crohn's/UC showed significantly higher costs (£5632 more, 95% CI 2773–8305) over 30 months, primarily due to higher acquisition costs (p=0.001). No significant differences were observed in quality-adjusted survival (p=0.603), AUC per day (p=0.129), or effectiveness (QALY difference: 0.021, p=0.350). Colectomy rates and time to colectomy were not significantly different (OR 1.350, p=0.223; HR 1.234, p=0.251). Serious adverse events were similar (event ratio 0.938, p=0.788), as were overall adverse events (1.075, p=0.807). Three deaths were reported in the infliximab group (pneumonia, sepsis, cancer), while 11 ciclosporin patients had renal impairment, only one of which was serious. No significant differences in use of other immunosuppressants or adverse event types were observed.
text: Infliximab is significantly more costly than Ciclosporin (£5632 more over 30 months, 95% CI 2773–8305) due to higher acquisition costs (p=0.001). No significant differences were found in effectiveness, quality-adjusted survival, or adverse events. [PMC4994668]

memory: The study compared NBUVB (9 J/cm2 for 6 weeks) with prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in treating generalized lichen planus, with a focus on disease duration. Baseline disease duration was similar between the two groups (p = 0.910). NBUVB showed significantly better treatment outcomes than prednisolone (p = 0.008), and patient satisfaction was higher in the NBUVB group (p = 0.012). No significant side effects were reported in either group. The study found no significant association between sex and disease duration (p = 0.763 for females, p = 0.738 for males). Although the specific effect of the treatments on disease duration was not directly measured, the results suggest that NBUVB may be more effective and better tolerated than systemic steroids for generalized lichen planus. Source: [PMC3434899].
text: The study suggests NBUVB (9 J/cm2 for 6 weeks) may be more effective than prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in treating generalized lichen planus, with better treatment outcomes and higher patient satisfaction, though disease duration was not directly measured. Source: [PMC3434899].

memory: Source article [PMC5827302] reported that Exercise significantly reduced Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scores compared to Control (Exercise Group=5.6±3.9 vs Control Group=0.1±2.3, p=0.02), with a very large within-group effect size (1.40). No between-group differences were found for PDSS (p=0.41). For SUDS, the Exercise group had significant increases post-intervention (Post-0=3.8±0.8 vs Baseline=2.4±1.1, p=0.04) and after 10 minutes of resting (Post-10=1.6±0.5, p=0.003), though no between-group differences were observed. Regarding BDI-II, the Exercise group showed a significant decrease post-intervention (M±SD=15.8±9.4 vs Baseline=21.6±10.7, p=0.01), but no significant between-group differences (p=0.09). Only the Exercise group had a large within-group effect size (1.06). Descriptive data for all outcomes are presented in Table 2.
text: Exercise significantly reduced Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scores compared to Control (p=0.02) with a very large within-group effect size (1.40), according to [PMC5827302].

memory: Study [PMC3546023] evaluated the effect of 200 mg/day palmvitee on NK cell percentages in smokers and nonsmokers. At baseline, smokers had significantly lower NK cell percentages than nonsmokers (p < 0.0001), with significance across subgroups (S1: p < 0.05, S2: p < 0.005, S3: p < 0.01). This difference remained after palmvitee supplementation, as shown in Table 8 and Table 9. Supplementation did not significantly alter NK cell percentages in either group. Smokers had higher urinary cotinine and serum α1-antitrypsin levels (p < 0.05), indicating greater tobacco exposure. Both groups showed increased plasma tocopherol and tocotrienol levels after supplementation (p < 0.05), but these did not influence NK cell percentages. Smokers also had higher CD4+ and B cell percentages compared to nonsmokers, with B cell percentages increasing in nonsmokers on palmvitee compared to placebo. The CD4+/CD8+ ratio was higher in smokers. Despite increased vitamin E levels in both groups, NK cell percentages remained unaffected by palmvitee. The results suggest that palmvitee does not alter NK cell percentages in smokers or nonsmokers, and baseline differences in NK cell levels between the groups persisted throughout the study.
text: Palmvitee supplementation (200 mg/day) did not significantly alter NK cell percentages in smokers or nonsmokers (PMC3546023). Baseline differences in NK cell levels between smokers and nonsmokers persisted throughout the study.

memory: Source article [PMC4958948] found that Active Body Control (ABC) significantly reduced total GLP-1 levels (p = 0.003) after lifestyle-induced weight loss, unlike the baseline group. This GLP-1 reduction was associated with metabolic improvements, such as decreased blood pressure, triglycerides, cholesterol, HbA1c, fasting glucose, and insulin, and increased HDL cholesterol. ABC also significantly lowered total bile acid (BA) levels by −34.59% (p = 0.007), especially glycine and taurine conjugated BAs like CDCA, CA, and UDCA. GLP-1 changes correlated with insulin, BAs, and other metabolic syndrome markers. FGF-19 levels remained unchanged in both ABC and baseline groups. The findings suggest that ABC-induced weight loss alters metabolic and BA profiles, with GLP-1 serving as a key indicator of these changes.
text: Active Body Control significantly reduced total GLP-1 compared to baseline (p = 0.003) after weight loss, associated with metabolic improvements. This effect was linked to changes in bile acids and insulin, highlighting GLP-1 as a key metabolic marker. Source: [PMC4958948].

memory: Source article [PMC4990415] evaluated the impact of Group Support Lifestyle Modification (GSLiM) versus dietary counseling on physical discomfort. GSLiM participants showed greater improvement in physical discomfort subscales compared to dietary counseling (Abstract > Results). At 24 weeks, retention rates were 83.5% for GSLiM and 82.5% for dietary counseling. A higher percentage of GSLiM participants achieved 6% weight loss (19.6%) compared to dietary counseling (4.1%), with a risk ratio of 4.75 (95% CI: 1.68, 13.45). GSLiM also improved weight self-efficacy, negative emotions, and quality of life. GSLiM participants experienced significant improvements in negative emotions compared to the dietary counseling group (Abstract > Results). The dietary counseling group saw a reduction in negative self-thoughts. No significant differences were found between groups for systolic and diastolic blood pressure at any time intervals (Between Group Differences). Tables 6 and 7 summarize obesity, cardiovascular measures, and psychological scores across time intervals.
text: Group Support Lifestyle Modification (GSLiM) significantly improved physical discomfort compared to dietary counseling (PMC4990415). GSLiM participants had greater weight loss, improved weight self-efficacy, and reduced negative emotions. No significant differences were found in blood pressure between groups.

memory: A study compared an "Intensified anticipatory guidance program" with a "Routine anticipatory guidance program" on baseline characteristics. The sample included 323 participants, mostly Hispanic (68%), single (61%), primiparous (39%), and with no high school diploma (44%), with a mean age of 26.5 years. The intervention group (n=170) and control group (n=153) had no statistically significant differences in baseline characteristics, including age, race/ethnicity, education, marital status, or number of children. Nonurgent ED visits occurred in 24% of newborns, with 21% in the intervention group and 27% in the control group (p=0.12), but this difference was not statistically significant. Subgroup analyses by marital status, education, maternal age, ethnicity, and number of children also showed no significant differences in ED visits. Knowledge scores showed no significant within-subject changes between groups. A high follow-up loss rate (44% in the intervention group and 40% in the control group) may affect generalizability. Overall, the baseline characteristics were well balanced, and the intervention did not significantly affect nonurgent ED visits or knowledge scores. Source: PMC4860224.
text: The "Intensified anticipatory guidance program" did not significantly affect baseline characteristics compared to the "Routine anticipatory guidance program." Both groups were well-balanced in age, race/ethnicity, education, marital status, and number of children (PMC4860224).

memory: In a study comparing Gallium maltolate (GaM) to clarithromycin + rifampin (CLR+R) for resolving lesions >27 mm in foals with Rhodococcus equi infection, GaM-treated foals had a lower resolution rate than CLR+R-treated foals, though the difference was not statistically significant. Lesion size was stratified at 27 mm, the median from initial ultrasound. For smaller lesions (<27 mm), resolution rates were similar between groups. For larger lesions (≥27 mm), GaM showed a lower resolution rate, but again, the difference was not significant. Logistic regression modeling treatment, lesion size, and their interaction did not find a significant interaction, indicating consistent treatment effects across lesion sizes. GaM was noninferior to CLR+R when results from a noncompliant farm were excluded, but noninferiority could not be conclusively demonstrated overall. Mortality due to R. equi was similar between groups (P = .47). Limitations included potential bias from excluded foals and variability in lesion size, which may have influenced outcomes. Source: [PMC4895420].
text: Gallium maltolate showed a lower resolution rate than clarithromycin + rifampin for lesions >27 mm in foals with Rhodococcus equi infection, though the difference was not statistically significant (PMC4895420). Noninferiority could not be conclusively demonstrated.

memory: The study compared the effect of "The mini-open anterior approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group A" with "conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group B" on "anal exsufflation time." As per source article [PMC5586978], group A showed a significantly shorter anal exsufflation time (1.21±0.48 day) compared to group B (2.12±0.82 day) (p<0.05), suggesting that the mini-open anterior approach may be more effective in reducing this parameter. Both groups showed improvements in VAS scores, Cobb angle, and ESR post-surgery, but no significant differences were found between the two groups for these outcomes. Operation time was slightly longer in group A, while blood loss and hospitalization time were reduced, although these differences were not statistically significant. The Frankel classification showed significant improvements in both groups from pre-surgery to the last follow-up (p<0.01), with no significant differences between group A and group B (p>0.05). These results indicate that both surgical approaches are effective in improving postoperative nerve compression symptoms and clinical outcomes, but the mini-open anterior approach may offer advantages in reducing anal exsufflation time.
text: The mini-open anterior approach (Group A) significantly reduced anal exsufflation time (1.21±0.48 day) compared to the conventional approach (Group B: 2.12±0.82 day) (p<0.05) [PMC5586978].
intervention: The mini-open anterior approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group A
comparator: conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group B

memory: In a study [PMC2650992], 100 patients undergoing breast lumpectomy and axillary dissection were randomized into a fibrin glue group (N=50; glue sprayed onto the axillary dissection site) and a control group (N=50). Outcome measures included drainage duration, overall drain output, and seroma incidence. Overall, no significant differences were found between the fibrin glue and control groups in drainage duration, overall drain output, or seroma incidence. However, subgroup analysis revealed that in patients undergoing level II or III axillary dissection, fibrin glue significantly reduced drainage duration (3.5 vs. 4.7 days; p=0.0006) and overall drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255). These findings suggest that fibrin glue may be more effective in reducing drainage duration and overall drain output in patients with more extensive axillary dissection (level II or III). The study indicates that fibrin glue could offer benefits in this specific subgroup of breast cancer patients undergoing lumpectomy and level II or III axillary dissection.
text: In a study [PMC2650992], fibrin glue did not significantly affect overall drain output in all patients. However, in those undergoing level II or III axillary dissection, fibrin glue significantly reduced overall drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255).
intervention: fibrin glue group (glue sprayed onto the axillary dissection site)

memory: In a study comparing plasma exchange (PE) with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in children, the PE group had a shorter median duration of mechanical ventilation (MV) (11 days) compared to the IVIG group (13 days; p = 0.037). A significant negative correlation between CSF protein levels and MV duration was observed in the PE group (p = 0.037), but not in the IVIG group (p = 0.132). Combined data from all patients also showed a statistically significant negative correlation between CSF protein and MV duration (p = 0.024). The PE group showed a trend toward shorter PICU stay (p = 0.094), though not statistically significant. No significant side effects were reported for either treatment. Baseline characteristics, including age, weight, duration of illness prior to MV, preceding diarrhea, cranial nerve involvement, MRC sum score, and CSF protein levels, were comparable between the groups. The proportion of children who could walk unaided within four weeks after PICU discharge was similar between groups (95.2% in PE vs. 90% in IVIG; p = 0.606). These findings suggest that PE may be associated with a shorter duration of MV and a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and MV duration, which was not observed with IVIG. Source: [PMC3387601]
text: Plasma exchange (PE) was associated with a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation (11 days vs. 13 days, p=0.037) and a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and MV duration (p=0.037), unlike IVIG (p=0.132). Source: [PMC3387601]
outcome: negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation

memory: Positive psychology-based intervention vs. wait-list control on subjective well-being: Source [PMC5662620]. Results showed significant intervention × time interaction effects on positive emotions (F=10.93, p=0.001), life satisfaction (F=9.68, p=0.002), and empathy (F=8.65, p=0.004). No significant effect on negative emotions (F=1.83, p=0.18). Post-hoc t-tests indicated significant increases in positive emotions (d=0.38), life satisfaction (d=0.67), and empathy (d=0.34) in the intervention group, not in the control group. Subjective well-being and positive learning behaviors increased significantly in the intervention group, with no changes in the control group. Prosocial behavior also increased significantly in the intervention group (F=7.29, p=0.004, d=0.66), with no change in the control group. No significant differences between groups in negative emotions or total mental health difficulties. A main effect of time on total mental health difficulties (F=7.52, p=0.002) showed decreases in both groups. Age was used as a covariate in the analyses.
text: A positive psychology-based intervention significantly improved subjective well-being (life satisfaction, positive emotions) compared to a wait-list control (PMC5662620). No significant effects on negative emotions were observed.

memory: The study evaluated the effect of the "Get Healthy, Stay Healthy" (GHSH) intervention compared to "no continued contact" on accelerometer-assessed moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA). At 6 months, the GHSH group had a significant increase in MVPA of 24.16 minutes/week (95% CI: 5.07, 43.25; P=.007) compared to the control group. Additionally, the GHSH group experienced significant weight loss (−1.35 kg, 95% CI: −2.24, −0.46; P=.003) and an increase in weekly moderate physical activity sessions (0.56 sessions/week, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.96; P=.008). No significant differences were observed between groups for waist circumference or other physical activity outcomes. The GHSH intervention also led to small but significant improvements in dietary outcomes, including higher fiber intake and total FFBQ Index Scores, while the control group showed declines in fruit and vegetable consumption. These results indicate that GHSH positively influenced MVPA and other health behaviors, although it did not significantly affect waist circumference. The findings suggest that continued contact interventions may be effective in promoting physical activity and healthier behaviors. Source: PMC4879328.
text: The "Get Healthy, Stay Healthy" (GHSH) intervention significantly increased accelerometer-assessed MVPA by 24.16 minutes/week (95% CI: 5.07, 43.25; P=.007) compared to no continued contact at 6 months (Source: PMC4879328).
outcome: accelerometer-assessed moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA)

memory: A study investigated the impact of a relevant computer tutorial ("in sequence") versus a non-relevant one ("out of sequence") on knowledge gain regarding Oral Rehydration Solutions (ORS). The "in sequence" group showed a statistically significant 19% higher post-test score (95% CI +7%, +31%) with a large effect size (Cohen's-d = 0.85, 95% CI 0.25, 1.5), indicating substantial knowledge improvement for the ORS topic. In contrast, for the Fever Without Source (FWS) topic, the "in sequence" group had a non-significant 6% higher score (95% CI -3%, +16%) and a smaller effect size (0.38, 95% CI -0.20, +0.97). Overall, the "in sequence" group had higher post-test scores (z-score 1.1 vs. 0.52; 95% CI +0.16, +0.93). Although students spent more time on in-sequence tutorials (12.1 min vs. 10.5 min), this was not statistically significant (95% CI -1.2, +4.5). Pre-test scores were similar between groups. The study included 92 participants, with 41 in the "in sequence" group. The results suggest that the relevance and sequence of the tutorial significantly enhance knowledge gain for specific topics like ORS. Source: PMC3517358.
text: A relevant computer tutorial ("in sequence") significantly improves knowledge of ORS compared to a non-relevant one ("out of sequence"), with a 19% higher post-test score (95% CI +7%, +31%) and a large effect size (Cohen's-d = 0.85). Source: PMC3517358.

memory: In a study comparing Cinacalcet with Control on iPTH target (150 to 300 pg/ml), the median iPTH decreased by 42.3% in the Cinacalcet group and by 30.7% in the Control group (P = 0.483). The proportion of patients achieving a 30% reduction in mean iPTH from baseline was similar between groups (48.5% vs. 51.5%, P = 1.000). The proportion of patients achieving iPTH within the target range (150 to 300 pg/ml) during the efficacy phase was also similar (24.3% vs. 18.2%, P = 0.764). Baseline median iPTH levels were 729 pg/ml (518, 1424 pg/ml) in the Cinacalcet group and 649 pg/ml (490, 1143 pg/ml) in the Control group. During the efficacy phase, median iPTH levels were 421 pg/ml (267, 753 pg/ml) in the Cinacalcet group and 441 pg/ml (317, 663 pg/ml) in the Control group. While Cinacalcet led to a greater reduction in iPTH, the difference was not statistically significant, and there was no significant difference in the proportion of patients achieving the iPTH target range. These results were visualized in Figure 2A, which shows iPTH levels at each scheduled visit for both groups. Source: [PMC3669111].
text: Cinacalcet resulted in a greater reduction in iPTH (42.3%) compared to Control (30.7%), but the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.483). The proportion of patients achieving iPTH within the target range (150–300 pg/ml) was similar between groups (24.3% vs. 18.2%, P = 0.764). Source: [PMC3669111].

memory: In a study with 24 subjects, Aequasyal® and multiple DC161 formulations, including DC161-DP0292, were compared for safety. No clinically relevant abnormalities were observed in systemic or local examinations, and no serious adverse events, product discontinuations, or premature withdrawals were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were primarily gastrointestinal, with one event each following application of DC161-DP0292 and its comparator. No significant differences in the incidence or type of TEAEs were found between Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 or other DC161 formulations. All tested products were well-tolerated, and no major safety concerns were identified. The study suggests that Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 have comparable safety profiles. Source: [PMC5839221].
text: Aequasyal® and DC161-DP0292 show comparable safety profiles, with no serious adverse events or major safety concerns. Both had similar, primarily gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse events. Source: [PMC5839221].

memory: Source article [PMC5656562] examined the effect of CYP3A4 Intermediate metabolizers (IM) versus Extensive metabolizers (EM) on sildenafil levels in 85 patients. Sildenafil concentration:dose ratios were significantly associated with age and BMI (P < 0.0001). CYP3A4 IM showed higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios than EM at weeks 12 and 24 (P = 0.045 for repeated measures analysis, adjusted for age, BMI, and genetic ancestry PCs), though this did not reach the corrected significance threshold of 0.0167. All CYP3A4 IM patients carried the CYP3A4*22 allele. An exploratory analysis combining CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 phenotypes found that higher predicted metabolizing capacity correlated with lower dose-adjusted sildenafil concentrations (F test P = 0.0238). Other CYP-related comparisons (CYP2C9, CYP3A5) did not show significant associations after multiple comparison correction, though trends were observed in the more homogeneous Caucasian subgroup.
text: CYP3A4 Intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios than Extensive metabolizers at weeks 12 and 24 (P=0.045), though not significant after correction. Source: [PMC5656562].

memory: In a study assessing the effect of two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations compared to baseline on ADCC-mediating antibody response, no ADCC-mediating antibody responses were observed post-immunization. However, one participant exhibited neutralizing activity against CM235 CRF01_AE. Statistical analysis was conducted using the Mann-Whitney test. Safety data indicated only mild or moderate adverse events, with no serious vaccine-related events. Binding IgG responses were significantly higher following two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations compared to HIV-MVA immunizations (p<0.0001). CN54rgp140-specific IgG concentrations increased significantly after each CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunization compared to HIV-DNA and HIV-MVA vaccinations (p<0.001). The increase in IgG titers between the two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations was also statistically significant (p=0.012). After three HIV-DNA and two HIV-MVA vaccinations, 87% of evaluable participants had detectable antibodies to subtype B gp160, with a median titer of 400. Source: [PMC4871571].
text: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations did not induce ADCC-mediating antibody responses compared to baseline (PMC4871571). However, they significantly increased binding IgG responses (p<0.0001).

memory: In a study comparing biosimilar adalimumab with reference adalimumab, total bilirubin levels were comparable between the two groups at screening and at Visit 5 (Day 84). At screening, bilirubin levels were 0.3 ± 0.18 mg/dL in the biosimilar group and 0.3 ± 0.11 mg/dL in the reference group. At Visit 5, levels were 0.3 ± 0.15 mg/dL for the biosimilar and 0.3 ± 0.20 mg/dL for the reference. No persistent changes in hemoglobin or other laboratory parameters were observed. Adverse events were mild, unrelated to the study drug, and fully resolved. Pallor was noted in two cases in the reference group at Visit 3, but no other systemic abnormalities were reported. These findings suggest that biosimilar adalimumab does not significantly affect bilirubin levels compared to reference adalimumab. Source: [PMC5215647]
text: Biosimilar adalimumab had no significant effect on bilirubin levels compared to reference adalimumab, as levels were comparable at screening and Visit 5 (Day 84). Source: [PMC5215647].

memory: In a study [PMC4153084], MSDC-0160, an mTOT modulating insulin sensitizer, was compared to control (placebo) in non-diabetic patients with mild Alzheimer's disease (AD) on cognitive outcomes. After 12 weeks, no significant differences were observed between groups in the 19-item cognitive test battery global cognitive summary z-score. Additional cognitive measures, including ADAS-Cog total score and Executive Function battery score, also showed no significant group differences. The trial was not powered to detect cognitive changes in this short timeframe. However, MSDC-0160 significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin levels (p<0.001), indicating improved insulin sensitivity. Trends were observed for hs-CRP and FFA levels, though not statistically significant. Glucose metabolism, as measured by FDG-PET, showed no significant differences in pre-defined regions when referenced to the pons or whole brain. However, when referenced to the cerebellum, MSDC-0160 treatment maintained glucose metabolism in several brain regions, while it declined in the placebo group. Voxel-based analyses also identified FDG-PET differences associated with MSDC-0160 treatment. While the study suggests MSDC-0160 may enhance insulin sensitivity, it did not significantly affect cognitive test battery global cognitive scores in this short-term trial.
text: In a 12-week trial [PMC4153084], MSDC-0160 showed no significant effect compared to control on cognitive test battery global cognitive scores in mild AD patients. The study was not powered to detect cognitive changes in this short timeframe.
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: JQJT tablets (n=400) were compared with placebo in pre-diabetes patients over 12-month treatment and 12-month follow-up. The primary endpoint was the incidence of diabetes. JQJT significantly reduced the risk of progression to diabetes (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P=0.010). At 12 months, diabetes incidence was 16.5% (JQJT) vs. 28.9% (placebo). At 24 months, this remained significant (20.3% vs. 32.8%, P=0.007). JQJT also showed a higher probability of normalized blood glucose (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.002-1.996, P=0.0049), with 41.8% vs. 27.8% achieving normalization at 12 months. Adverse events were similar (2.8% placebo vs. 1.7% JQJT, P=0.501). Baseline age was slightly higher in the JQJT group (55.49 vs. 53.49 years, P=0.036). The study supports the potential of JQJT in delaying diabetes onset in pre-diabetic individuals. Source: PMC5593818.
text: JinqiJiangtang tablets significantly reduced the risk of pre-diabetes progressing to diabetes compared to placebo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P=0.010) over 12 months, with this effect sustained at 24 months. Source: PMC5593818.
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
outcome: risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes

memory: A study compared group A (non-selective clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG) with group B (selective clopidogrel 600 mg in the cath-lab after CAG, only if PCI was performed) regarding bleeding complications. Bleeding occurred in 3.5% of group A versus 1.4% of group B (P = 0.025). After adjusting for covariates, group A had a significantly higher risk of bleeding (OR = 3.03; 95% CI 1.14–8.10; P = 0.027). Female gender (P = 0.001) and use of GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors (P = 0.027) were additional significant risk factors. Low thrombocyte levels showed a trend toward significance (P = 0.091). In the subgroup of patients undergoing PCI, bleeding rates were 7.1% in group A and 0.7% in group B (P = 0.006). Other outcomes like periprocedural troponin elevation, TIMI-flow post-PCI, and re-intervention within 7 days showed no significant differences between groups. The primary endpoint (death, MI, stroke, or re-intervention) was not significantly different. The findings suggest that non-selective clopidogrel administration before CAG increases bleeding risk compared to selective administration after CAG in PCI patients. Source: [PMC2429977].
text: Non-selective clopidogrel administration before CAG (group A) was associated with a higher risk of bleeding complications (3.5%) compared to selective administration after CAG in PCI patients (group B, 1.4%; OR = 3.03; P = 0.027). Source: [PMC2429977].
intervention: group A ('non-selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG;
