Excerpts from source article [PMC3856598]:
- [Intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC) | Comparator: Control mice | Outcome: alveolar collapse | Section: Abstract > Results] BMDMC therapy significantly reduced alveolar collapse in CLP mice compared to control mice. This effect was observed regardless of the ARDS model used (LPS or CLP). The therapy also improved survival, reduced lung elastance, tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellularity, and collagen fiber content, while decreasing interleukin-1β levels and increasing chemokine expression in lung tissue. Additionally, intercellular adhesion molecule-1 and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 expression increased in lung tissue after cell therapy, depending on the type of insult (LPS or CLP).
text: BMDMC therapy significantly reduced alveolar collapse in CLP mice compared to control mice, as shown in the study (PMC3856598). This effect was consistent across different ARDS models and was accompanied by improved survival and reduced inflammation.
intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)

memory: Source article [PMC5282794] examined the effect of "plastic cap" versus "metal cup" on "pain response" in infants during vaginal operative delivery. Infants with ventouse delivery using a plastic cap showed significantly lower pain responses than those with a metal cup (p < 0.001), although overall pain responses were lower than anticipated, with full recovery within 72 hours. Scalp trauma occurred more frequently with metal cups (13.2%, 12/90) than with plastic cups (6.6%, 2/30), though this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.51). Plastic cups had a 6.7% (2/30) detachment rate, while metal cups had none. No subgaleal or intracranial hemorrhage or skull fractures were reported. Pain scores were not significantly influenced by suppository use, with no significant difference in EDIN ≥ 5 between metal/placebo and plastic/placebo groups. The study could not assess the impact of maternal analgesia on EDIN scores due to imbalances in analgesia types.
text: Infants undergoing vaginal operative delivery with a plastic cap showed significantly lower pain responses than those with a metal cup (p < 0.001). Plastic caps also had a lower scalp trauma rate, though not statistically significant. Source: PMC5282794.

memory: In a phase 2a trial, synthetic amyloid-β peptide (Aβ42) (AN1792) was compared to placebo for its effect on the Dependence Scale. Among antibody responders, there was a statistically significant reduction in decline on the Dependence Scale compared to placebo (p=0.033). This was consistent with findings from the Disability Assessment for Dementia (DAD) scale, which also showed significantly less decline in antibody responders (p=0.015) over 4.6 years. Anti-AN1792 antibodies were detected in 17 out of 19 responders, while no detectable antibodies were found in non-responders. Although CDR-SOB ratings showed a 20.2% less decline in responders, this was not statistically significant (p=0.185). MRI data showed no significant differences in brain volume loss between groups. The results suggest that the efficacy of AN1792 may be limited to individuals who developed an immune response, as indicated by the presence of anti-AN1792 antibodies. These findings support the potential of AN1792 in slowing disease progression in responders, but further studies are needed to validate these results and explore underlying mechanisms. Source: [PMC2825665]
text: In a phase 2a trial, synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) showed a statistically significant reduction in decline on the Dependence Scale compared to placebo (p=0.033) among antibody responders. This effect was consistent with findings on the DAD scale (p=0.015). Source: [PMC2825665]

memory: In a study comparing "40 μg HB vaccine intramuscularly" (group A) to "20 μg HB vaccine intradermally" (group B), group A had a lower HB antibody titer (28.9 ± 7 IU/L) compared to group B (121.1 ± 82.3 IU/L, p = 0.04). The seroconversion rate was also lower in group A (60%) than in group B (70%), though the difference was not statistically significant. Groups C (IM + Levamisole) and D (ID + Levamisole) had similar seroconversion rates (90%) and higher antibody titers (541.1 ± 494.4 IU/L and 297.2 ± 9 IU/L, respectively; p = 0.6). Levamisole addition significantly increased antibody titers in both IM and ID groups (p = 0.001 and p = 0.01). Six months post-vaccination, antibody titers declined in all groups, but the decline was less in groups C and D. In groups A, B, and C, titers were approximately halved, while in group D, the decrease was only 30%. Source: [PMC1540413]
text: The "40 μg HB vaccine intramuscularly" had a lower seroconversion rate (60%) compared to "20 μg HB vaccine intradermally" (70%), though the difference was not statistically significant. Source: [PMC1540413].

memory: Study [PMC4973627] assessed the effect of "Physical activity + Healthy eating" (PA+/HE+) versus "Control" on "Cardiovascular mortality." In the PA+/HE+ group (n=502), cardiovascular mortality was 15% (76), with a relative risk (RR) of 0.49 (95% CI: 0.36–0.66; P < 0.001) compared to control, indicating a significant reduction. Another analysis of the same group showed an RR of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.42–0.78; P < 0.001), reinforcing this finding. The PA+/HE− group (n=992) had a cardiovascular mortality rate of 17% (169), with an RR of 0.56 (95% CI: 0.44–0.73; P < 0.001) and 0.59 (95% CI: 0.46–0.77; P < 0.001), also showing a significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality. However, the PA−/HE+ group (n=162) had a higher general mortality rate of 61% (98), but no significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality was observed. These findings suggest that combining physical activity with healthy eating is effective in reducing cardiovascular mortality compared to control. The results highlight the importance of integrating both lifestyle factors for cardiovascular benefit, while indicating that healthy eating alone may not significantly reduce cardiovascular mortality in this context.
text: Combining physical activity and healthy eating significantly reduces cardiovascular mortality compared to control (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.36–0.66; P < 0.001). Healthy eating alone did not show a significant reduction. Source: PMC4973627.

memory: A study [PMC3467590] assessed the impact of a web-based CME program, performance feedback, and quality improvement tools on medication intensification in diabetes management among rural physicians compared to a control group. The intervention did not demonstrate a significant incremental benefit for medication intensification in glucose, blood pressure, or lipid control. Both groups showed increased medication intensification for A1c control, particularly in patients with worse glucose control (A1c >9%), but no significant differences were observed between the intervention and control groups for BP or LDL control. Adjusted analyses also found no significant effect of the intervention on medication intensification measures. The group-by-time interaction for incremental benefit was not statistically significant (p=0.948). Although the intervention group showed a trend toward greater medication intensification for A1c control, this was not significantly different from the control group. The study concluded that the multicomponent web-based intervention did not provide a significant incremental benefit over standard care for improving medication intensification in diabetes management.
text: A study (PMC3467590) found no significant incremental benefit of web-based CME, feedback, and quality tools over control in improving medication intensification for diabetes management. Both groups showed similar improvements, with no significant differences in glucose, BP, or LDL control.
intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

memory: In a study [PMC4628236], cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks was compared to placebo in diabetic animals. Cinaciguat significantly reduced myocardial nitro-oxidative stress, as indicated by decreased nitrotyrosine (NT) immunoreactivity in the left ventricular myocardium (Fig. 2a, b). Diabetes mellitus (DM) increased antioxidant enzyme expression, including HSP70a1, catalase, glutathione-reductase, and thioredoxin-1 (Fig. 2c). Cinaciguat normalized HSP70a1 and glutathione-reductase mRNA expression to levels observed in healthy controls (Fig. 2c). Regarding PKG activity, DM was associated with elevated PDE-5 and PKG protein expression but reduced PKG activity, as shown by a decreased p-VASP/VASP ratio (Fig. 3a). Cinaciguat treatment reduced PDE-5 expression and increased PKG activity, as demonstrated by an elevated p-VASP/VASP ratio (Fig. 3a). PKG expression levels were similar between diabetic groups (Fig. 3a). These findings suggest that cinaciguat alleviates DM-induced nitro-oxidative stress and restores PKG signaling.
text: Cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks significantly reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic animals compared to placebo, as shown by decreased nitrotyrosine immunoreactivity and normalization of antioxidant enzyme expression (PMC4628236).
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

memory: A study found that lemon verbena extract may reduce exercise-induced muscle strength loss compared to placebo. Participants taking lemon verbena showed significantly less reduction in maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) post-exercise (p = 0.0311), with a significant time effect (p = 0.0051). Muscle strength in the lemon verbena group returned to baseline after 48 hours, whereas the placebo group still exhibited reduced strength at that time. The lemon verbena group also experienced less movement-induced pain (p = 0.0788, trend) and showed a trend toward improved glutathione peroxidase (GPxP) activity (p = 0.0681, trend). Creatine kinase (CK) levels were not significantly different between groups (p = 0.9412), although CK elevation occurred only at 24 hours post-exercise in the lemon verbena group, while the placebo group had significant CK increases at all time points. Interleukin 6 (IL-6) levels did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.5824). These results suggest that lemon verbena extract may reduce muscle damage and enhance recovery following exercise compared to placebo. However, some outcomes only showed trends toward significance. Source: [PMC5781260]
text: Lemon verbena extract reduces exercise-related muscle strength loss compared to placebo, with less reduction in maximal voluntary contraction (p = 0.0311) and faster recovery. Source: [PMC5781260]

memory: Arformoterol showed significant improvements in quality of life compared to placebo, as measured by the overall St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) and Clinical COPD Questionnaire (P < .05). Additional benefits included greater improvements in trough FEV1 (0.051 L, P = .030) and FVC (0.075 L, P = .018). Patients on arformoterol had a 50% lower risk for the first respiratory serious adverse event (P = .003). Fewer patients on arformoterol experienced COPD exacerbation-related hospitalizations (9.0% vs 14.3%). Adverse events (AEs) were similar between groups (72.9% vs 68.2%), but COPD exacerbation or worsening was less common with arformoterol (23.3% vs 28.0%). Nonrespiratory AEs ≥5% included headache, nausea, and urinary tract infection. Cardiac serious AEs were numerically higher with arformoterol (3.1% vs 2.4%), though time-to-first event was not significantly different. Mortality rates were similar between groups (2.9% vs 2.4%).
text: Arformoterol significantly improved quality of life compared to placebo, as measured by SGRQ and Clinical COPD Questionnaire (P < .05). It also showed better lung function and lower risk of serious respiratory events.
outcome: improvements in quality of life (overall St. George's Hospital Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire)

memory: In the study [PMC3432828], GF and GIF diets were compared to GC on femur bone strength. Results indicated that GX caused a significant decrease in bone breaking force, which was prevented by both GF and GIF diets (p<0.05). However, isoflavone alone (GI) did not prevent the decline. Additionally, calcium absorption decreased after GX, but GF and GIF diets significantly improved calcium absorption compared to GC (p<0.05), with no significant difference between GC and GI groups. The study also found that GIF led to lower daidzein and higher equol concentrations compared to GI (p<0.05), while genistein levels were similar between GI and GIF. These findings suggest that FOS diets may enhance bone strength and calcium absorption more effectively than the control diet or isoflavone alone. The protective effect of FOS on bone strength appears independent of isoflavone.
text: The GF and GIF diets significantly improved femur bone strength and calcium absorption compared to the GC diet (p<0.05). The protective effect of FOS on bone strength was independent of isoflavone, as GI did not prevent bone strength decline. Source: [PMC3432828].
intervention: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF)

memory: In a study comparing nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) to saline (3 ml), the effect on the tidal expiratory flow ratio at 25% of the remaining tidal volume to PTEF (25/PT) was assessed. Both treatments led to a significant post-administration decrease in 25/PT (P < 0.05), but no significant difference was observed between albuterol and saline. Albuterol significantly reduced TEF10, while saline had no such effect. PTEF increased significantly after both interventions, though the difference between groups was not statistically significant (P = 0.6). No significant changes were noted in VPTEF/VE or tPTEF/tE. Baseline characteristics were similar, except for gender distribution. Other parameters such as heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and wheeze score remained unaffected. The results indicate that while both treatments improved PTEF, only albuterol significantly impacted 25/PT and TEF10. Source: [PMC111183].
text: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) and saline (3 ml) both significantly decreased 25/PT (P < 0.05), with no significant difference between groups. Albuterol uniquely reduced TEF10, while saline had no effect. PTEF increased after both, but group differences were not significant (P = 0.6). Source: [PMC111183].
intervention: nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline)
outcome: ratio of the tidal expiratory flow at 25% of the remaining tidal volume to PTEF (25/PT)

memory: The GENRES Study [PMC4330076] assessed the impact of bisoprolol versus losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide on antihypertensive response in male patients with moderate hypertension (mean OBP 152/100 mm Hg) and slightly elevated BMI. No participants had diabetes or reduced kidney function. BP reductions ranged from 4.8/1.7 mm Hg (hydrochlorothiazide) to 11.1/8.3 mm Hg (bisoprolol). A genome-wide association study identified three SNPs on chromosome 11—rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037—reaching genome-wide significance for ASBP response to bisoprolol. These SNPs are located in the ACY3 gene, which encodes aminoacylase III. Additionally, the study found 42 SNPs across 31 genomic regions associated with treatment response at P≤1×10⁻⁵. These findings suggest that genetic factors, particularly in the ACY3 gene, influence ASBP response to bisoprolol, potentially supporting personalized antihypertensive therapy.
text: Bisoprolol showed greater systolic blood pressure reduction than losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide in hypertensive males. SNPs rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037 on chromosome 11 (ACY3 gene) were significantly associated with ASBP response to bisoprolol (GENRES Study, PMC4330076).
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

memory: The study evaluated the effect of metformin (500 mg, bid po) combined with alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) compared to metformin (1000 mg, bid po) on the proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤7.0%. At week 26, 18.18% (8/44) in the intervention group met the target versus 10.81% (4/37) in the control group, but the difference was not statistically significant (P > 0.05). The intervention group showed greater improvements in lipid profiles: lower total cholesterol (−4.27 mg/dL vs. −1.59 mg/dL), LDL-C (−2.36 mg/dL vs. −0.16 mg/dL), triglycerides (−6.23 mg/dL vs. −2.78 mg/dL), and higher HDL-C (1.00 mg/dL vs. 0.24 mg/dL). BMI decreased more in the intervention group (−2.07 kg/m²) than in the control group (−1.78 kg/m²), though not significantly (P > 0.05). Pulmonary function parameters showed no significant differences (P > 0.05). Adverse events were more frequent in the intervention group, including higher rates of headaches (12.7% vs. 2.0%) and pruritic events (12.7% vs. 4.0%), but no serious cutaneous adverse events or hypoglycemia were reported. Source: [PMC5370803].
text: The combination of metformin (500 mg, bid po) and alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) did not significantly improve the proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤7.0% compared to metformin (1000 mg, bid po) at week 26 (18.18% vs. 10.81%, P > 0.05). Source: [PMC5370803].
intervention: metformin (500 mg, bid po) combined with alogliptin (25 mg, qd po)

memory: FAST treatment significantly increased MAP (P = 0.035), sBP (P = 0.046), and dBP (P = 0.035) compared to SLOW treatment. Pulse rate was also higher in the FAST group (P = 0.022). No significant differences were observed in CI, SVRI, or DO2 between the two treatments. Biochemistry, oxygen saturation, venous blood gas, and BNP-NT values showed no significant changes. During resuscitation, FAST treatment led to a uniform rise in pulse rate, whereas SLOW treatment increased pulse rate in less than 50% of participants. text: FAST treatment significantly increased MAP, sBP, dBP, and pulse rate compared to SLOW treatment (P < 0.05). However, no significant differences were observed in CI, SVRI, or DO2. Source: [PMC4957966].

memory: In a study comparing Desmopressin with Placebo, pre-surgery platelet levels were similar between groups (P = 0.802). Post-surgery, the Placebo group had a significantly higher rate of thrombocytopenia (P = 0.012), and mean platelet levels were also significantly lower in the Placebo group (P = 0.038), indicating a protective effect of Desmopressin on platelet levels. Bleeding rates post-surgery were not significantly different between groups (Desmopressin: 359.3 ± 266.2 vs. Placebo: 406.3 ± 341.6; P = 0.208). Hemoglobin levels decreased significantly in both groups post-surgery (P = 0.0001), but there was no significant difference between groups (P = 0.134). Demographic and procedural variables, including age, gender, pump time, clamp time, duration of surgery, and complications, were not significantly different between groups (P > 0.05). These findings suggest that Desmopressin may help maintain platelet levels post-surgery compared to Placebo, though it does not significantly affect bleeding rates or hemoglobin levels. Source: [PMC5101425].
text: Desmopressin reduces thrombocytopenia rate compared to Placebo post-surgery (P = 0.012), with higher platelet levels in the Desmopressin group (P = 0.038). Bleeding rates and hemoglobin levels were not significantly different. Source: [PMC5101425].

memory: The study [PMC4562579] examined the effect of resistance exercise (SR + RT) compared to a control condition on leg blood flow. Results from the Vascular Measures section showed no significant changes in leg blood flow, femoral artery diameter, or mean arterial pressure due to SR or SR + RT. Although heart rate was higher in the fed state compared to the fasted state (P < 0.0001), no differences were found in leg blood flow measurements across time or between legs. Additionally, plasma enrichment of 13C6 phenylalanine did not differ across time (P = 0.07), and intracellular free phenylalanine enrichments showed no differences between legs or across time (P = 0.40 and P = 0.22, respectively). These findings, as summarized in Table 3, suggest that resistance exercise did not significantly affect leg blood flow or related vascular parameters when compared to the control condition.
text: Resistance exercise (SR + RT) did not significantly affect leg blood flow compared to control [PMC4562579]. No changes were observed in femoral artery diameter or mean arterial pressure. Heart rate differences were noted, but leg blood flow remained unaffected across conditions and time.

memory: In a phase III trial [PMC3626705], 322 previously treated advanced melanoma patients with V600E or V600K B-Raf mutations were randomized 2:1 to receive oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) or intravenous chemotherapy (dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² or paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every 3 weeks). At 6 months, the overall survival rate was 81% in the trametinib group versus 67% in the chemotherapy group (HR 0.54; P = 0.01). The median progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly longer in the trametinib group (4.8 months) compared to the chemotherapy group (1.5 months; HR 0.45; P < 0.001). Another trial in K-Ras mutant NSCLC evaluated selumetinib in combination with docetaxel but found no statistically significant improvement in median overall survival (9.4 months vs 5.2 months; HR 0.8, p = 0.21). This information supports the comparison between trametinib and chemotherapy for overall survival at 6 months in melanoma patients. The source article [PMC3626705] provides the key data for this comparison.
text: At 6 months, oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) significantly improved overall survival compared to intravenous chemotherapy (dacarbazine or paclitaxel) in advanced melanoma patients with BRAF mutations (81% vs 67%, HR 0.54; P = 0.01). Source: [PMC3626705].
comparator: intravenous chemotherapy consisting of either dacarbazine (1000mg/m2) or paclitaxel (175mg/m2), every 3weeks
outcome: At 6 months, the rate of overall survival

memory: In a study comparing the Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) group with a Placebo group in adults with postprandial intestinal gas-related symptoms and no GI diagnoses, the effect on the GSRS VAS-Gas score was not statistically significant [PMC2784472]. However, the GD group showed a trend toward greater improvement compared to the placebo, as noted in the Results and Discussion section of the source article. While the VAS-Gas score did not reach statistical significance, other efficacy endpoints, such as the GSRS abdominal pain subscore (p = 0.046) and the GSRS total score (p = 0.048), showed significant improvements in the GD group. The abdominal distension subscore also showed a strong trend toward improvement (p = 0.061). The lack of statistical significance for many endpoints, including the VAS-Gas score, was attributed to a strong placebo effect observed in the study. The findings suggest that while the GD group demonstrated a beneficial trend in VAS-Gas score, the results were not statistically significant, possibly due to the pronounced placebo effect. These results were consistent across multiple outcome measures and were discussed in the context of the study’s overall findings.

memory: D-serine significantly reduced legal errors on the Groton Maze Learning Test (GML) compared to control (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03), with the most significant difference observed in the second trial (t = −3.13, p = 0.003). No significant changes were found in illegal errors (F(3, 38) = 0.05, p = 0.82), suggesting the effect was not due to test comprehension. Performance improvements correlated with higher plasma D-serine levels (r² = −0.19, p = 0.009). However, D-serine had no significant impact on other cognitive tests, including the n-back working memory test (p > 0.1), Set-Shifting task (p = 0.47), or visual attention test (p > 0.7). Mood was also unaffected (p > 0.4). These results suggest that D-serine may specifically enhance spatial memory, learning, and problem-solving abilities, as reflected in the reduction of legal errors on the GML. The study indicates a targeted cognitive benefit of D-serine on the GML without broad cognitive or mood effects. Source: PMC4914255.

memory: Study [PMC5706318] found that Chlorhexidine mouth rinse significantly reduced Streptococcus mutans counts compared to a control group. The study also evaluated Listerine and C. gigantea extract mouth rinses, both of which also showed significant reductions in S. mutans. However, pairwise comparisons between Chlorhexidine, Listerine, and C. gigantea extract did not reveal statistically significant differences in their effectiveness, despite some numerical variations. Specifically, no significant difference was found between Chlorhexidine and C. gigantea extract or between Listerine and C. gigantea extract. The results indicate that all three mouth rinses are similarly effective in reducing S. mutans counts. While Chlorhexidine is effective compared to control, it is not significantly more effective than the other tested mouth rinses. The study supports the use of these mouth rinses for reducing S. mutans but does not identify one as superior to the others. These findings suggest that Chlorhexidine is as effective as other tested mouth rinses in reducing S. mutans counts, though further studies may be needed to confirm these findings in different populations or conditions.
text: Chlorhexidine mouth rinse significantly reduces Streptococcus mutans counts compared to control (PMC5706318). However, it is not significantly more effective than Listerine or C. gigantea extract, which also show significant reductions. All three rinses are similarly effective in reducing S. mutans counts.

memory: A study evaluated the effect of Septoplasty versus a Control group on "a" vowel improvement. Post-septoplasty, total nasal resistance (TNR) significantly decreased (P=0.001), but no significant changes were observed in /a/ vowel parameters between pre- and post-surgery assessments at 1 and 3 months (Table 3). No significant differences in /a/ vowel parameters were found between the Septoplasty and control groups, except for NHR (P=0.017), which was not linked to TNR changes. Subjectively, 61% of patients reported no change in voice quality, 36% noted improvement, and 3% reported deterioration. The study concluded that Septoplasty did not result in significant objective or subjective improvements in "a" vowel production compared to the control group. Although TNR improved, this did not lead to meaningful changes in vowel parameters. No significant differences were found in /n/ nasal consonant parameters, except for some non-clinically significant formant frequency differences. The findings suggest that Septoplasty may have limited clinical impact on "a" vowel improvement in patients with septal deviation. Source: PMC4996097.
text: Septoplasty did not significantly improve "a" vowel parameters compared to control (PMC4996097). Although total nasal resistance decreased, no meaningful changes in vowel production were observed. Subjectively, most patients reported no improvement. Thus, septoplasty has limited clinical impact on "a" vowel improvement in patients with septal deviation.

memory: The study evaluated the effect of a "Phlebotomy training programme" versus a "Control" on "Phlebotomy questionnaire score" among healthcare professionals. Pre- and post-training assessments showed significant improvements in questionnaire scores at multiple centers: CHC A (63% to 96%, p = 0.039), CHC B (58% to 93%, p = 0.006), CDC C (60% to 97%, p = 0.001), and CDC D (63% to 97%, p = 0.001). These results indicate a positive impact of the training programme on knowledge or skills related to phlebotomy. However, no significant changes were observed in sample rejection rates (p > 0.05), and other outcomes such as preanalytical errors and request-form errors did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. The data were sourced from the abstract and results section concerning the phlebotomy questionnaire score, with additional outcomes extracted from other sections (PMC5419060).
text: The phlebotomy training programme significantly improved phlebotomy questionnaire scores compared to the control (p < 0.05 across multiple centers). However, it did not affect sample rejection rates or other preanalytical errors (PMC5419060).

memory: The study [PMC4497726] evaluated the impact of aerobic exercise (75, 150, or 225 min/wk) versus no exercise on VO2 peak and cognitive outcomes. A dose-response relationship was found for VO2 peak, with higher exercise volumes associated with greater improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness, particularly in per-protocol analyses. All exercise groups showed improvements compared to no exercise. Cognitive outcomes showed improvements in Simple Attention across all exercise groups, while Visuospatial Processing improved in a dose-dependent manner, with the greatest benefits at 225 min/wk. Verbal Memory and Reasoning improved in all groups, but these gains may not be specific to exercise and could reflect practice effects. Adverse events were more common in the 150 and 225 min/wk groups compared to the 75 min/wk group, though most were mild (e.g., musculoskeletal pain), with no severe adverse events reported. The study suggests that even lower exercise doses improve cognitive function, with potential greater benefits in visuospatial processing at higher volumes. Results were consistent in both intent-to-treat and per-protocol analyses, with more robust findings in the latter. These findings support the positive effects of aerobic exercise on both cardiovascular fitness and cognitive function, with dose-related benefits in some domains.
text: Aerobic exercise (150 or 225 min/wk) significantly improves VO2 peak compared to no exercise, with greater improvements at higher volumes, as shown in [PMC4497726].

memory: The Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) significantly reduced open defecation compared to the control group, with greater reductions observed in adult men (75% vs. 84%, p=0.001), adult women (73% vs. 83%, p<0.001), and children under 5 (84% vs. 89%, p=0.014). Despite these improvements, the decline in open defecation was less than the rise in improved sanitation facility (IHL) availability. Among households with improved IHLs, 41% in the TSC group still practiced open defecation, compared to 28% in the control group. The TSC increased coverage of JMP-defined improved sanitation facilities by 19 percentage points (p<0.001) and any IHLs by 20 percentage points (p<0.001) compared to the control. However, a gap remains between facility availability and actual behavioral change. No significant differences were found in anemia prevalence or growth outcomes between groups. TSC did not significantly affect E. coli contamination in household water samples (p=0.050 for household samples; p=0.143 for water source samples). Helminth infection data showed a statistically significant difference (p=0.001), though the effect size was small. These findings suggest that while TSC improved sanitation infrastructure, it did not fully translate into behavioral change, highlighting the complex relationship between sanitation infrastructure and open defecation practices. Source: PMC4144850.
text: The Total Sanitation Campaign significantly reduced open defecation compared to control (p<0.001), with greater reductions in adult men, women, and children under 5. However, a gap remained between improved sanitation facility availability and actual behavioral change, as 41% of TSC households still practiced open defecation. Source: PMC4144850.

memory: A study evaluated the effect of using hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) 1.5% followed by chlorhexidine (CHX) 0.2% (group III) compared to CHX 0.2% alone (group I) on plaque formation after 3 weeks. At week 3, group III showed less plaque than group I, but the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.104). Group II, which used CHX followed by H2O2 1.5%, had significantly less plaque than group I at all time points (P < 0.001) and also showed significantly less plaque than group III at weeks 2 and 3 (P = 0.002 and 0.008, respectively). Group III had significantly less plaque than group I at weeks 1 (P = 0.000) and 2 (P = 0.017), but not at week 3. These results suggest that both group II and group III had reduced plaque compared to group I, but group II was more effective in plaque reduction at weeks 2 and 3. The findings highlight the potential benefit of combining H2O2 with CHX in reducing plaque formation, though the sequence of application appears to influence effectiveness, with the CHX followed by H2O2 order (group II) being more effective than H2O2 followed by CHX (group III). Source: [PMC3800406]
text: Using H2O2 1.5% followed by CHX 0.2% (group III) showed less plaque than CHX alone (group I) at weeks 1 and 2, but not week 3 (P = 0.104). Source: [PMC3800406]
intervention: group III used hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) 1.5% followed by chlorhexidine (CHX)
comparator: group I rinsed with chlorhexidine (CHX) 0.2% alone
outcome: amount of plaque formed at end of week 3

memory: In a 12-week double-blind trial with 36 children with stage 3/4 CKD, paricalcitol did not show a statistically significant effect compared to control (placebo) on achieving calcium levels within KDOQI target ranges or on changes in calcium levels during the study. However, paricalcitol significantly reduced intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) levels compared to control, with a mean between-group change of −72.4 pg/mL (P < 0.001). Additionally, 27.8% of the paricalcitol group achieved two consecutive iPTH reductions of ≥30% from baseline, compared to none in the placebo group (P = 0.045). Adverse events were more frequent in the placebo group (88.9%) than in the paricalcitol group (38.9%; P = 0.005). However, 21% of children in the paricalcitol group experienced clinically meaningful hypercalcemia. The study included participants with stage 3/4 and stage 5 CKD. These findings suggest that while paricalcitol significantly lowers iPTH levels, it does not significantly impact calcium levels compared to control. The results indicate that paricalcitol may not be effective for managing calcium levels in children with CKD, though it may have benefits in reducing iPTH. (Source: PMC5440538)
text: Paricalcitol did not significantly affect calcium levels compared to control in children with CKD (PMC5440538). However, it significantly reduced iPTH levels. Adverse events were more common in the placebo group, but 21% of the paricalcitol group experienced hypercalcemia.

memory: In a 24-week trial with 132 patients across 24 sites in six countries, PR-fampridine showed greater median improvements from baseline compared to placebo in TUG speed, MSWS-12 score, and BBS total score. A higher proportion of PR-fampridine patients achieved ≥10% (p=0.0021) and ≥15% (p=0.0262) improvements in TUG speed. The drug was well tolerated, with similar AE rates (77% placebo vs. 75% PR-fampridine). Common AEs included nasopharyngitis in PR-fampridine and urinary tract infections in placebo. Falls were more frequent in the placebo group, while balance disorder, gait disturbance, and dizziness were more common in PR-fampridine. EQ-5D-5L results showed no significant differences between groups, with median treatment differences of 0.00 (–4.17, 4.67) for VAS and 0.00 (–0.04, 0.04) for utility index. A post hoc analysis found a significantly greater proportion of PR-fampridine patients (46%) reported improvement on PGIC at week 2 compared to placebo (26%) (p=0.023). Improvements in MSIS-29 PHYS scores were also greater with PR-fampridine versus placebo. These benefits were sustained throughout the 24-week trial. Source: [PMC4749757]
text: Prolonged-release fampridine significantly improved TUG speed compared to placebo (p=0.0021 for ≥10% improvement) over 24 weeks. Benefits were sustained, with greater improvements in MSWS-12, BBS, and MSIS-29 PHYS scores. Source: [PMC4749757]
outcome: Improvement in Timed Up and Go (TUG) speed during 24 weeks

memory: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced the mean skeletal morbidity period rate (SMPR) for all new bone events compared with placebo (P=0.004). The reduction was mainly due to fewer bone events requiring radiotherapy (P<0.001) or surgery (P=0.037). No significant difference was observed in skeletal fractures between groups (P=0.195). Multivariate Poisson regression analysis showed a 38% risk reduction for skeletal events in the ibandronate group (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001). The median time to first bone event was 90.3 weeks with ibandronate and 64.9 weeks with placebo (P=0.089). Ibandronate also significantly reduced urinary CTx from baseline over 96 weeks compared with placebo (median change −77.3% vs +11.0%, P<0.001). The mean number of events and measurement periods with events per patient were significantly lower in the ibandronate group (P=0.008 and 0.015). The effect of ibandronate on overall SMPR and events requiring radiotherapy remained significant even when including events from the first 12 weeks (Table 2). Source: [PMC2409647].
text: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced the risk of skeletal events compared to placebo, with a 38% risk reduction (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001). This effect was mainly due to fewer events requiring radiotherapy or surgery. No significant difference in skeletal fractures was observed. Source: [PMC2409647].

memory: Source article [PMC5336430] evaluated the effect of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% versus vehicle on treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in 166 patients. 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% led to a significantly higher rate of TEAEs (99.1%) compared to vehicle (83.6%), primarily due to application- and administration-site reactions. TSQM side effect domain scores were similar between groups (92.4 vs. 96.4), but the DLQI total score showed greater improvement with vehicle, likely due to fewer local skin reactions. The study found that 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% was more effective in achieving complete clinical clearance (CCC) and complete clearance of lesions (PC), with higher odds ratios and statistically significant differences. However, this efficacy was accompanied by increased TEAEs. No significant differences were observed in the convenience domain of TSQM. The findings suggest a trade-off between efficacy and increased local adverse events with 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% compared to vehicle.
text: The use of 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% resulted in a significantly higher rate of treatment-emergent adverse events (99.1%) compared to vehicle (83.6%), primarily local skin reactions (PMC5336430).

memory: Source article [PMC4282128] found that bupropion and nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) had similar smoking cessation effectiveness (27.9% vs. 24.2%) when combined with behavioural support, with an odds ratio of 1.21 (95% CI: 0.883–1.67). Combining bupropion and NRT did not significantly improve cessation rates compared to either treatment alone (24.2%). There was a trend suggesting bupropion may be more effective for smokers with a history of depression (29.8% vs. 18.5%), but this difference was not statistically significant (χ2 = 2.86, P = 0.091). Bupropion was associated with more unwanted symptoms than NRT. No significant heterogeneity in treatment effects was observed across study sites (χ2(3) = 1.24, P = 0.745). NRT success rates were similar across product types (26.9% for patch users vs. 26.7% for bupropion). Overall, the study indicates that bupropion and NRT are similarly effective for smoking cessation in clinical practice, with a potential advantage of bupropion for individuals with a history of depression.
text: Bupropion and NRT show similar smoking cessation effectiveness (27.9% vs. 24.2%) with behavioural support (PMC4282128). Bupropion may have a trend toward better efficacy in those with depression history, though not statistically significant. Bupropion is associated with more side effects. No significant difference in success rates between NRT types.

memory: An 11-week study assessed the impact of the "FIFA 11 for Health" programme on body fat percentage compared to a control group. The intervention group (IG) experienced a significantly greater reduction in body fat percentage (−0.83%) than the control group (CG) (−0.04%, p<0.05). Additional cardiovascular and physical fitness parameters improved more in the IG, including reductions in systolic blood pressure (−3.5 vs 0.9 mm Hg), mean arterial blood pressure (−1.9 vs 0.4 mm Hg), and BMI (−0.02 vs 0.13 kg/m2), all with p<0.05. However, no significant differences were found between groups in 20 m sprint time, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery level 1 performance, balance, or jump performance. The findings suggest that the "FIFA 11 for Health" programme is effective in reducing body fat and improving certain cardiovascular and physical fitness parameters compared to a control group. This conclusion is based on the study published in the PMC5136709 article.
text: The "FIFA 11 for Health" programme significantly reduced body fat percentage (−0.83%) compared to control (−0.04%, p<0.05). It also improved cardiovascular parameters but had no effect on sprint, balance, or jump performance (PMC5136709).

memory: In a study comparing Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG with placebo, no significant differences in microbiota composition were observed at 6 months. At 18 months, however, L. rhamnosus GG supplementation showed effects on three genus-like bacterial groups. Children in the LGG group had higher levels of butyrate-producing bacteria, including Anaerostipes caccae et rel (2.89 ± 2.13% vs. 1.18 ± 0.91%, p=0.03) and Eubacterium ventriosum et rel (0.17 ± 0.11% vs. 0.11 ± 0.07%, p=0.04), compared to the placebo group. Additionally, the placebo group had higher levels of Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age (1.19 ± 0.85% vs. 0.78 ± 0.60%, p=0.047). These findings suggest a potential protective effect of L. rhamnosus GG against Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age. Detailed microbiota data and p-values are provided in Additional files 7, 8, and 9 of the source article [PMC3563445].
text: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG was associated with lower levels of Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months compared to placebo (1.19 ± 0.85% vs. 0.78 ± 0.60%, p=0.047), suggesting a potential protective effect [PMC3563445].
outcome: Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age

memory: In a study [PMC5761719], 30.1% (531/1765) of patients were classified as minimal-risk using the PROMISE minimal-risk tool, showing a significantly lower pre-test probability of obstructive CAD compared to the remainder of the cohort (30.0% vs. 47.0%, p < 0.001), with consistency across study sections. Minimal-risk patients were also less likely to have typical angina (24.1% vs. 42.6%, p < 0.001). The PROMISE tool outperformed the CADC model in discrimination (c-statistic 0.785 vs. 0.730, p < 0.001), with further improvement after re-estimating covariate coefficients (c-statistic 0.805, p < 0.001). Initial calibration of the PROMISE tool was poor (χ2 197.6, HL p < 0.001), with overestimation of minimal risk, but this improved significantly after adjusting the intercept and coefficients (χ2 5.6, HL p = 0.692). The CADC model also showed poor goodness-of-fit (χ2 1010.1, HL p < 0.001). HDL-C was imputed in 28.7% of patients, which could affect risk estimates. Overall, the PROMISE minimal-risk tool better differentiates minimal-risk patients from the remainder of the cohort in terms of pre-test probability of obstructive CAD.
text: Patients classified as minimal-risk using the PROMISE tool had a significantly lower pre-test probability of obstructive CAD (30.0%) compared to the remainder of the cohort (47.0%, p < 0.001) [PMC5761719].

memory: Source article [PMC3726903] evaluated "Partial matrix excision" (Group I) versus "Segmental phenolization" (Group II) in terms of postoperative complications. Both groups showed comparable complication profiles, with 3 patients in Group I and 2 in Group II experiencing moderate pain requiring analgesics for 3 days, with no statistically significant difference (P > 0.05). No soft tissue infections were reported in either group. Postoperative complication and recurrence rates were also not significantly different (P = 0.688). However, Group II (Segmental phenolization) showed a significantly shorter time to return to normal daily activities compared to Group I (P < 0.05). The results indicate that both procedures have similar complication rates, but Segmental phenolization may offer a faster recovery. This suggests that while neither technique is superior in terms of complications, recovery time could be an important factor in clinical decision-making. The study provides useful insights for selecting between these procedures based on patient recovery needs.
text: Both "Partial matrix excision" and "Segmental phenolization" have comparable postoperative complication rates (P > 0.05), with no significant differences in pain or infection. However, Segmental phenolization allows a faster return to daily activities (P < 0.05). Thus, neither procedure is superior in complications, but recovery time may influence clinical choice (PMC3726903).

memory: KOS in the nasal cavity significantly reduced pain scores compared to placebo (P < .001), with a 3.3-point reduction in VAS scores (95% CI: 2.3, 4.4). The active group's VAS scores decreased from 5.5 to 1.2, while the placebo group decreased from 4.9 to 3.9. The effect was rapid, showing significance at 5 minutes (1.9 points, P = .007) and remained significant at 2 hours post-treatment (3.7 points, P < .001). Secondary outcomes showed a trend toward fewer migraine days in the active group during the 2-month follow-up, but the difference was not statistically significant (P = .39 and P = .53). Pain intensity and attack duration also tended to decrease in the active group during the first month, though differences were not statistically significant (P = .42 and P = .37). text: Kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity significantly reduced pain scores compared to placebo (P < .001), with a 3.3-point reduction in VAS scores (95% CI: 2.3, 4.4). The effect was rapid and sustained. Source: [PMC4312979].
intervention: kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity

memory: Community-based intervention showed no significant difference compared to usual care on SF-12 Physical Component Summary (PCS) at 6 months. However, it significantly improved SF-12 Mental Component Summary (MCS) (mean difference = 2.74, 95% CI = 0.28–5.19, P = .03) and the SF-12 general health subdomain (mean difference = 3.11, 95% CI = 0.05–5.71, P = .02), both favoring the intervention. Additionally, the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities (SDSCA) significantly improved in the intervention group (mean difference = 3.74, 95% CI = 0.9–6.57, P = .01). These results were confirmed by multiple imputation analyses. No significant differences were observed between groups on CES-D, GAD-7, or self-efficacy. Cost analyses showed no significant overall difference between groups, though some services had cost reductions in the intervention group. The mean group difference in total cost change excluding hospital costs was $236.92, favoring the intervention but not statistically significant. Source: [PMC5836873]
text: Community-based intervention significantly improved SF-12 MCS (MD=2.74, 95% CI 0.28–5.19, P=.03) and SDSCA (MD=3.74, 95% CI 0.9–6.57, P=.01) compared to usual care, but not PCS. General health subdomain also improved (MD=3.11, 95% CI 0.05–5.71, P=.02). Source: [PMC5836873].
outcome: 12‐item Short‐Form Health Survey (SF‐12), Mental Component Summary (MCS), Summary of Diabetes Self‐Care Activities (SDSCA)

memory: A study compared the effect of bladder training plus tolterodine (Co) with tolterodine only (To) on micturition frequency. Both Co and To groups showed significant reductions in micturition frequency compared to bladder training alone (BT). The Co group experienced a 33.5% decrease in micturition frequency, which was significantly greater than the 25.9% decrease in the BT group (p<0.05). The To group had a 30.2% decrease in frequency, which was not significantly different from the Co group. Urgency scores also improved significantly in both To and Co groups compared to BT (p<0.05 each), with no difference between To and Co. Although Co showed greater improvement in frequency compared to BT, it was not significantly better than To. The study concluded that combination therapy was more effective than either method alone in controlling overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms, but tolterodine alone may be a viable first-line therapy. Source: [PMC2721929]
text: Bladder training plus tolterodine (Co) reduced micturition frequency by 33.5%, significantly more than bladder training alone (p<0.05). Tolterodine alone (To) reduced frequency by 30.2%, not significantly different from Co. Both Co and To were more effective than bladder training alone. Source: [PMC2721929]

memory: In a study comparing Remifentanil 0.3 (group RH), Remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5 (group KRH), and Remifentanil 0.05 (group RL), Touch-Test sensory evaluation after surgery showed significantly higher negative values in group RH compared to groups KRH and RL (source: PMC4610927, Abstract > Results). Groups KRH and RL had similar sensory outcomes. No significant differences were found in demographic or anesthetic parameters, except for end-tidal desflurane concentration, which was higher in group RL. Group RH had significantly higher additional analgesic consumption, NRS scores at 6 and 24 hours post-surgery, and cumulative fentanyl dose compared to groups KRH and RL. Pain scores, as measured by the NRS, were also significantly higher in group RH than in the other groups. Additional analgesic consumption during the PACU stay was significantly higher in group RH compared to group RL. The study had no dropouts, and all groups were comparable in age, body weight, baseline blood pressure, heart rate, anesthesia duration, input/output, and time to extubation. The results suggest that group RH experienced greater sensory impairment and required more analgesic support post-surgery compared to groups KRH and RL.
text: Remifentanil 0.3 (group RH) showed significantly higher negative Touch-Test sensory values post-surgery compared to groups KRH and RL (PMC4610927). Groups KRH and RL had similar sensory outcomes.
comparator: Remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5 (group KRH) or remifentanil 0.05 (Group RL)
outcome: Value of the Touch-Test sensory evaluation after surgery

memory: Source article [PMC4724125] evaluated the impact of "Exercise training" versus "Control" on "High density lipoprotein" (HDL). No significant differences were observed between groups in changes in HDL cholesterol levels. Additionally, no significant differences were found in changes of blood pressure (BP) or C-reactive protein (CRP). However, LDL cholesterol increased in the exercise group compared to controls. In patients with carotid plaques, LDL cholesterol levels increased significantly in the exercise group compared to controls [0.20 mmol/L (0.00 to 0.41) vs −0.13 mmol/L (−0.37 to 0.12), p = 0.044], while no such difference was found in patients without plaques (p = 0.40). In a table, LDL cholesterol levels were reported as 2.0 (1.6, 2.6) for the exercise group and 1.9 (1.6, 2.5) for the control group, with a p-value of 0.020, indicating a significant difference in LDL levels between the groups. The study does not show a significant effect of exercise training on HDL cholesterol levels when compared with control.
text: Exercise training did not significantly affect HDL cholesterol levels compared to control (PMC4724125). However, LDL cholesterol increased in the exercise group. No significant changes in BP or CRP were observed.

memory: Heated infusions were associated with faster postoperative recovery compared to control (room temperature infusions). Consciousness recovery time was significantly shorter in the heated infusion group (9.91 ± 1.91 minutes) compared to the control group (11.19 ± 1.49 minutes, P = 0.004). Eye opening time was also significantly reduced in the heated infusion group (6.72 ± 1.73 minutes vs 8.66 ± 2.03 minutes, P < 0.001). Spontaneous breath time was shorter in the heated group (4.06 ± 0.72 minutes vs 4.47 ± 0.84 minutes, P = 0.042), and extubation time was significantly reduced (10.09 ± 1.91 minutes vs 11.13 ± 1.34 minutes, P = 0.015). No significant differences were observed in hospital stay duration. Intraoperatively, blood loss, transfusion volume, and operation time were not significantly different, except for a significantly shorter operation time in the heated infusion group (2.925 ± 0.216 minutes vs 3.094 ± 0.254 minutes, P < 0.05). Source: [PMC5380277].
text: Heated infusions significantly reduced consciousness recovery time compared to control (9.91 ± 1.91 vs. 11.19 ± 1.49 minutes, P = 0.004). Source: [PMC5380277].

memory: Source article [PMC4365564] found a superficial wound infection rate of 6.3% in the Charité artificial disc group and 2.0% in the ALIF with BAK cages group, with no statistically significant difference (P = .103). No deep wound infections were reported in either group. The overall infection rate was higher in the Charité group (12.7%) compared to the ALIF group (8.1%). Major neurological complications were similar between groups (4.4% vs. 4.0%). The Charité group had a higher superficial wound infection rate, but no deep infections were observed. Iliac crest donor site infection occurred in 3.0% of the control group. Pseudarthrosis occurred in 9.1% of the control group. Retrograde ejaculation occurred in 3.3% of the investigational group and 5.5% of the control group, with no significant difference (P = .515).
text: The Charité artificial disc had a higher superficial wound infection rate (6.3%) compared to ALIF with BAK cages (2.0%), but the difference was not statistically significant (P = .103).

memory: Source article [PMC3549413] investigates the effect of "placebo" compared with "baseline" on "bone mineral density (BMD) at the 6-month time point." The study includes a placebo group (n=28) and compares it with the geniVidaTM bone blend (GBB) and calcium-only groups. At 6 months, the placebo group showed a significant decrease in BMD at the femoral neck (p=0.007) and Ward's triangle (p<0.05). The BMD decrease in the placebo group was 1.3% less than in the GBB group at the femoral neck and 2.3% greater than the GBB group at Ward's triangle. However, the study does not provide a direct comparison of the placebo group's BMD at 6 months with its own baseline values. Instead, it focuses on inter-group differences, particularly between the GBB and placebo groups, rather than intra-group changes over time. The placebo group’s BMD decreased compared to GBB, which maintained BMD levels. Supporting evidence includes p-values and percentage differences between groups. The absence of baseline-to-placebo comparisons limits the ability to determine whether the observed BMD changes in the placebo group are due to natural progression or the placebo effect. Therefore, the study does not directly address the effect of "placebo" compared with "baseline" on BMD at 6 months. No other relevant data is provided in the excerpts.
text: The study does not directly compare "placebo" with "baseline" for BMD at 6 months. It focuses on inter-group differences between placebo and GBB, not intra-group changes. Thus, the effect of placebo compared with baseline on BMD at 6 months cannot be determined from this source (PMC3549413).
outcome: bone mineral density (BMD) At the 6-month time point

memory: A study examined the effect of 1200 mg cranberry extract over 6 weeks versus a placebo on total antioxidant capacity (TAC). Results indicated that both cranberry supplementation and physical exercise significantly influenced TAC levels (p < 0.001). In Trial I, both groups experienced a significant post-exercise drop in serum TAC. In Trial II, the cranberry group showed significantly higher resting, post-exercise, and post-recovery TAC levels compared to the placebo group. However, the cranberry group still experienced a significant post-exercise decline in TAC, suggesting that while cranberry extract may enhance antioxidant capacity, it does not fully prevent exercise-induced TAC reduction. These findings are presented in Fig. 1 of the source article [PMC5330006]. Additional outcomes, such as interleukin 6 and serum iron levels, were not significantly affected by cranberry supplementation. The study suggests that cranberry extract may support antioxidant status in athletes, though further research is necessary to confirm these results and explore underlying mechanisms.
text: Receiving 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks significantly increased total antioxidant capacity (TAC) compared to placebo (p < 0.001), particularly at rest, post-exercise, and post-recovery, though both groups still showed post-exercise TAC decline. Source: [PMC5330006].
intervention: receiving 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks

Source: [PMC5863413]  
Research question: Effect of "Propolis gel" vs "No treatment" on "Pain".  
The study found that Propolis gel and no treatment both significantly reduced pain scores from baseline to second follow-up (P = 0.000 for both). However, the difference in pain reduction between Propolis gel and no treatment was not statistically significant (P = 0.255), indicating no significant advantage of Propolis gel over no treatment. The study also compared Propolis gel with Triamcinolone acetonide, finding both interventions significantly reduced pain (P = 0.000), with no significant difference between them (P = 0.255). Similarly, Triamcinolone acetonide and no treatment showed significant pain reduction (P = 0.000), with no significant difference in effectiveness (P = 0.255). Overall, all three interventions—Propolis gel, Triamcinolone acetonide, and no treatment—were effective in reducing pain, but no statistically significant differences were found between them. The results suggest that while each intervention was effective, there was no significant difference in their effectiveness in reducing pain.
text: Propolis gel and no treatment both significantly reduced pain (P = 0.000), but no significant difference was found between them (P = 0.255). Thus, Propolis gel does not show a significant advantage over no treatment in pain reduction [PMC5863413].

memory: A study evaluated the effect of ESM-I (six weeks of Ecological Momentary Assessment with weekly feedback on positive affect) compared to two groups: (ii) ESM without feedback and (iii) treatment as usual, on the rate of symptomatic remission. The primary outcome was measured using HDRS scores and remission rates. At 32 weeks, ESM-I showed a non-significant reduction in HDRS scores compared to the control group (B = −3.1, p = 0.051, intention-to-treat), and no significant differences were found between ESM-I and the pseudo-intervention group (B = −1.13, p = 0.47). Additionally, no significant differences in remission rates were observed between ESM-I and the control group (OR = 2.65, p = 0.12) or between ESM-I and the pseudo-intervention group (OR = 1.84, p = 0.29). The results suggest that ESM-I did not significantly improve symptomatic remission rates compared to either comparator group. The findings were consistent across analyses and showed no evidence of a clinically meaningful effect on remission. Source: [PMC5747107].
text: The study found no significant effect of ESM-I with feedback on remission rates compared to ESM without feedback (OR = 1.84, p = 0.29) or treatment as usual (OR = 2.65, p = 0.12). Source: [PMC5747107].
intervention: ESM-I consisting of six weeks of ESM combined with weekly feedback regarding the individual’s positive affective experiences

memory: Source article [PMC5393542]: Hyaluronic acid (HA) intervention showed a significant decrease in Salivary TF levels at 1 week post-intervention (T2) compared to baseline (T0) and 1 week post-intervention (T1), as determined by One-Way ANOVA for Repeated Measurements (p<0.05). memory: Study [PMC4045368] evaluated locking plate fixation (n=20) versus nonlocking plate fixation in tibial plateau fractures, with a follow-up of 13.4 months (10–17 months). Groups were comparable in follow-up duration (P = 0.158) and fracture severity (Schatzker/AO classifications; P > 0.25). The locking plate group had significantly higher mean knee scores (80.20 ± 10.21 vs. 72.52 ± 14.75, P = 0.039) and functional scores (77.26 ± 9.95 vs. 69.55 ± 10.22, P = 0.026). Pain scores, as measured by VAS, were also lower in the locking group (4.45 ± 2.50 vs. 6.00 ± 2.59, P = 0.046). A greater proportion of patients in the locking group achieved excellent knee scores (65.0% vs. 33.3%). No significant differences were found in range of motion (122.35 ± 12.93° vs. 115.71 ± 20.14°, P = 0.219) or complication rates (e.g., infection, nonunion). These findings suggest that locking plate fixation may offer better knee function and pain relief compared to nonlocking fixation in tibial plateau fractures.
text: Locking plate fixation improves mean knee scores at follow-up compared to nonlocking fixation (80.20 vs. 72.52, P = 0.039) in tibial plateau fractures, according to [PMC4045368]. It also enhances functional scores and reduces pain, though range of motion and complication rates are similar.

memory: A study assessed the effect of Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera [L.] Dunal) versus placebo on the increase from baseline in mean VO2 max after 8 weeks. The trial included 24 participants in the Ashwagandha group and 25 in the placebo group. At 8 weeks, Ashwagandha showed a significantly greater increase in VO2 max compared to placebo (4.91 vs. 1.42, P < 0.0001). This improvement was even more pronounced at 12 weeks (5.67 vs. 1.86, P < 0.0001). The results suggest that Ashwagandha significantly enhances VO2 max compared to placebo, with the effect increasing over time. At 8 weeks, Ashwagandha also improved most quality of life (QOL) sub-domain scores compared to placebo, except for environmental impact (P > 0.05). By 12 weeks, all QOL sub-domains were significantly improved (P < 0.01). No changes in vital parameters such as pulse rate, blood pressure, or respiratory function at rest were observed in either group. These findings indicate that Ashwagandha may improve cardiovascular endurance and overall quality of life, with the most significant effects observed at 12 weeks. The study supports the use of Ashwagandha as a beneficial supplement for enhancing physical performance and well-being, though further research is needed to confirm long-term effects. Source: [PMC4687242].
text: Ashwagandha significantly increased VO2 max more than placebo after 8 weeks (4.91 vs. 1.42, P < 0.0001). Source: [PMC4687242].
outcome: Increase from baseline in the mean VO2 max after 8 weeks

memory: A study compared sitagliptin and voglibose in diabetic patients, assessing their impact on gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP). The primary outcome, flow-mediated dilatation (FMD), improved significantly in both groups after 12 weeks, with no significant difference between the two. For GIP, no significant differences were observed in changes between sitagliptin and voglibose. Secondary efficacy measures, including HbA1c, GIP, GLP-1, C-peptide, lipid profile, oxidative stress markers, inflammatory markers, and eGFR, showed no significant differences between the groups. Although sitagliptin increased circulating CD34 compared to voglibose, this was not linked to changes in GIP. The analysis used ANCOVA adjusted for baseline FMD, age, sex, smoking, diabetes duration, and BMI to compute least square means (95% CI). The results suggest both drugs have similar effects on GIP levels. These findings were supported by statistical analysis and presented in Table 3. Source: [PMC4149239].
text: Sitagliptin and voglibose have similar effects on gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) levels in diabetic patients, with no significant differences observed in changes between the two drugs (PMC4149239).

memory: In the study [PMC5331731], PBF was compared with C1 (enhanced financing) on administrator attrition. Results showed that PBF led to 0.10 fewer administrators leaving health centers on average compared to C1 (p < 0.05), indicating a statistically significant reduction in administrator turnover under PBF. This finding is based on data from Table 6, which outlines the estimated effects of PBF and enhanced financing on attrition. The PBF vs. C1 comparison included 448 participants. While PBF also showed lower nurse turnover compared to C2 (pure control), with 0.14 fewer nurses leaving (p < 0.05), the specific difference in administrator attrition between PBF and C2 was not explicitly provided. The C1 vs. C2 comparison involved 345 participants, and the PBF vs. C2 comparison included 462 participants. Overall, the results suggest that PBF may be more effective in retaining administrators than C1. However, further analysis is needed to fully assess the magnitude of this effect.
text: Performance-based financing (PBF) was associated with 0.10 fewer administrators leaving health centers compared to control 1 (C1; enhanced financing) (p < 0.05), indicating a statistically significant reduction in administrator turnover under PBF [PMC5331731].
outcome: administrators on average who left health centers

memory: Source article [PMC5808396] evaluated the impact of Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) versus individual support (IS) on felt stigma after treatment. At baseline, felt stigma was moderate (mean = 1.98). After treatment, the IS group showed significantly higher levels of felt stigma compared to the CPT group (B = −0.44, p = 0.02). This difference remained at six months post-treatment, although it was no longer statistically significant (B = −0.45, p = 0.12). Both groups experienced a reduction in stigma over time, but CPT was associated with a greater decline. The results indicate that CPT is more effective than IS in reducing felt stigma, with benefits persisting beyond treatment, though the statistical significance weakened by six months. These findings suggest that CPT may be a more effective intervention for reducing stigma in this population, despite the diminishing statistical significance over time. The study supports the use of CPT as a potential treatment for stigma reduction in clinical settings.
text: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) is more effective than individual support in reducing felt stigma after treatment, with greater decline observed in the CPT group (B = −0.44, p = 0.02). This benefit persisted at six months, though it became non-significant (B = −0.45, p = 0.12). Source: [PMC5808396].

memory: In a study [PMC3637243], lixisenatide was compared to control in isolated rat hearts undergoing ischemia-reperfusion injury. Lixisenatide reduced infarct size when administered 10 minutes before reperfusion (98 ± 9 mm² vs. 162 ± 12 mm²; p < 0.05). However, no significant differences were observed in left ventricular total area (control: 543 ± 16 mm²; lixisenatide: 505 ± 7 mm²) or left ventricular risk area (control: 306 ± 9 mm²; lixisenatide: 288 ± 5 mm²). The infarct area to risk area ratio was reduced by 36% with lixisenatide. Rate pressure product (LVP x HR) and coronary flow were not significantly altered during reperfusion. In long-term injury models, lixisenatide did not significantly change left ventricular wall thickness but normalized slightly increased right ventricular wall thickness in control animals. No cardiac dilatation was observed using the expansion index. These findings suggest that lixisenatide reduces infarct size without significantly affecting left ventricular total or risk area in acute ischemia-reperfusion injury models.
text: In a study [PMC3637243], lixisenatide did not significantly affect left ventricular risk area compared to control in ischemia-reperfusion injury models. However, it reduced infarct size and the infarct-to-risk area ratio.

memory: A study evaluated the effect of PEG-lactulose (20-30 g lactulose, oral or rectal, plus 280 g PEG in 4 L water orally as a single dose over 30-120 min) versus lactulose alone (20-30 g orally or via nasogastric tube, or 200 g enema via rectal tube) on blood ammonia levels. No significant difference in blood ammonia levels was observed between the two groups after 24 hours (p = 0.858). However, PEG-lactulose was associated with better improvement in HESA scores (p = 0.04) and a reduction in hospital stay (p = 0.03), with the latter being significant only in women (p = 0.01). Although both treatments had similar effects on blood ammonia levels, PEG-lactulose may provide clinical benefits in terms of symptom improvement and shorter hospitalization, especially in women. Source: [PMC5308129].
text: The PEG–lactulose group showed no significant difference in blood ammonia levels compared to lactulose alone (p = 0.858). However, PEG–lactulose improved HESA scores (p = 0.04) and reduced hospital stay (p = 0.03), particularly in women (p = 0.01). Source: [PMC5308129].
intervention: PEG–lactulose group received the 20-30 grams of lactulose of oral or rectal lactulose, plus 280 grams of PEG in 4 liters of water orally as a single dose in 30-120 minutes
comparator: 20-30 grams of lactulose orally or by a nasogastric tube, or 200 grams of lactulose enema by a rectal tube

memory: Study [PMC4681902] assessed the impact of 80% and 10% maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC) on longus colli thickness. Results showed that during concurrent masticatory muscle contraction, longus colli thickness significantly increased with 80% MVIC compared to 10% MVIC (p<0.05). In contrast, no significant differences were observed in sternocleidomastoid thickness between 80% and 10% MVIC (p>0.05), nor between 50% and 10% MVIC (p>0.05). The findings suggest that longus colli thickness is sensitive to contraction intensity, particularly when masticatory muscles are engaged, whereas sternocleidomastoid thickness remains relatively unchanged across different contraction intensities. These results indicate that cervical muscles may respond differently to varying levels of isometric contraction, with longus colli being more responsive to higher contraction intensities. This highlights the importance of considering muscle-specific responses when evaluating the effects of isometric contractions on cervical muscle thickness.
text: An 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction significantly increased longus colli thickness compared to 10% (p<0.05), while sternocleidomastoid thickness remained unchanged (p>0.05). This suggests longus colli is more responsive to higher contraction intensities (PMC4681902).

memory: A study compared ampicillin/sulbactam with cefuroxime in 176 patients (median age 28 years, IQR: 24-32) regarding hospitalization duration. Both groups had a median hospital stay of 4 days (IQR: 4-4), with no statistically significant difference (p=0.09). Postoperative infection rates were similar overall (7.4%), with 5.9% in the cefuroxime group and 8.8% in the ampicillin/sulbactam group (p=0.6). There were 10 postoperative surgical site infections (SSIs): 6 in the ampicillin/sulbactam group and 4 in the cefuroxime group (p=0.7). SSIs included 5 superficial incisional and 5 organ/space infections, with 4 cases of post-cesarean endometritis and 1 intrabdominal collection. Post-cesarean endometritis occurred in 2.3% of the ampicillin/sulbactam group and 2.4% of the cefuroxime group (p=1). No significant differences were found in hospitalization duration or secondary outcomes, including postoperative infections or endometritis. Source: [PMC3009979].
text: Ampicillin/sulbactam and cefuroxime had similar effects on hospitalization duration (median 4 days, p=0.09) in a study of 176 patients. No significant differences were observed in postoperative infections or secondary outcomes. Source: [PMC3009979].

memory: Source article [PMC3112403] found that flaxseed supplementation significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose compared to baseline and to wheat bran (5.92 ± 0.31 vs. 4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L). Wheat bran showed no significant change in fasting plasma glucose (5.67 ± 0.14 vs. 5.73 ± 0.35 mmol/L). Flaxseed had no significant effect on fasting plasma insulin, while wheat bran significantly reduced plasma insulin compared to baseline (p = 0.026). Body weight, BMI, and waist circumference remained unchanged in both groups over the 12-week study. No significant differences in weight change were observed between groups or in relation to glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, or inflammatory biomarkers. Inflammation markers like IL-6, TNF-α, and hs-CRP showed no significant changes after either intervention, with no differences between flaxseed and wheat bran groups. Dietary intake of energy and nutrients did not differ significantly between groups. Software limitations hindered analysis of α-linolenic acid and fiber intake. Antioxidant intake from food was also not significantly different between groups.
text: Flaxseed significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose compared to wheat bran (4.79 ± 0.17 vs. 5.92 ± 0.31 mmol/L) in a 12-week study (PMC3112403). Wheat bran showed no significant change in fasting plasma glucose.

memory: [PMC4301837] LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration at 12 h compared to placebo (–49% to –63%; P < 0.001). Placebo increased aldosterone by 37% at 12 h. Aldosterone returned to baseline after 24 h. No further reduction observed with 10 mg LCI699. On Days 7 and 14, LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) reduced aldosterone from pre-dose baseline. ACTH-stimulated aldosterone levels showed 41–64% inhibition with LCI699 vs 7% with placebo (P < 0.001). Eplerenone 100 mg increased pre-ACTH aldosterone by 29% (P ≤ 0.01) and caused a 63% increase in ACTH-stimulated aldosterone. LCI699 ≥ 100 mg increased 11-deoxycortisol (942% and 584% at 100 mg and 200 mg, P < 0.001 vs placebo), likely due to off-target inhibition. Single LCI699 doses ≥ 30 mg showed no dose-dependent aldosterone effect, leading to evaluation of 0.5–10 mg in multiple-dose phase. 24-h urinary cortisol decreased 34–42% with 30–200 mg LCI699 (P ≤ 0.001 vs placebo), while 200 mg LCI699 reduced plasma cortisol by 19% (P = 0.029).
text: LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration at 12 h compared to placebo (–49% to –63%; P < 0.001), while placebo increased aldosterone by 37% (PMC4301837).

memory: A study compared system-oriented therapy with a reference intervention in patients with schizophrenia, focusing on completed follow-up. The system-oriented group had a lower non-completion rate (4/30) compared to the reference group (15/40; P = 0.017), suggesting better follow-up completion with system-oriented therapy. However, higher attrition in the reference group may have influenced effect estimates. System-oriented therapy achieved a 43% fulfillment of standards in the hospital, while the reference group received an average of 3 sessions (SD 2.1) and no booster sessions (SD 0.7). Although compliance and PANSS scores showed a trend toward improvement in favor of system-oriented therapy, the results were not statistically significant. There was a significant difference in time to first readmission, with the system-oriented group experiencing a longer time to readmission (P = 0.049). No significant differences were found in duration of index hospitalization or average bed day consumption over 12 months. In conclusion, system-oriented therapy may improve follow-up completion and reduce readmission rates, but evidence for its effect on compliance and other outcomes remains inconclusive. Source: [PMC4060171].
text: System-oriented therapy showed a lower non-completion rate (4/30) compared to reference intervention (15/40; P = 0.017), suggesting better follow-up completion. It also delayed time to first readmission (P = 0.049). However, evidence for other outcomes remains inconclusive. Source: [PMC4060171].

memory: In a study comparing IPE (4g/day) to placebo in individuals with diabetes (overall median baseline A1c = 6.8%), no significant changes were observed in fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR across all groups, including those with better-controlled (below median A1c) and less-controlled (above median A1c) diabetes. memory: In a 12-week trial (PMC4540107), Dextromethorphan (DM60) was compared with Placebo in opioid maintenance therapy, focusing on treatment retention. The DM60 group demonstrated significantly longer treatment retention, indicating better adherence to the program. Plasma morphine levels were lower in the DM60 group, and there was a significant reduction in plasma TNF-α levels, suggesting possible anti-inflammatory properties. However, no significant differences were observed between groups regarding changes in plasma cytokine levels, BDNF levels, or methadone dose requirements. These results imply that DM60 may enhance treatment retention and modulate inflammatory markers without affecting other key biomarkers or methadone dosing. The findings support the potential of DM60 as an adjunct in opioid maintenance therapy to improve adherence. Further research is required to better understand the mechanisms behind DM60's effects on retention and inflammation. This study offers preliminary evidence that DM60 could be beneficial in treatment programs aiming to improve patient retention and manage inflammation.

memory: The study evaluated the effect of "Agave derived fructans" versus "Formula" on "C-Reactive Protein" (CRP) in infants. CRP levels were measured at baseline (approximately 20 days old) and at three months of age. No significant differences in CRP levels were found between the Agave derived fructans and Formula groups (Wilcoxon test p = 0.05). Similarly, no significant differences were observed in CRP concentrations between cesarean and vaginal delivery groups (Fisher Student T-Test: p > 0.05). The results remained consistent when comparing Agave derived fructans with Breast milk and Formula, with non-significant differences also noted in serum ferritin levels across groups. The Agave derived fructans group included 27 participants, with an initial median CRP level of 0.290 mg/dL. Statistical methods used included Wilcoxon and Fisher Student T-Test, with p-values indicating no significant differences in CRP concentrations across the groups. Other outcomes, such as IgA in saliva, were assessed but were not relevant to the CRP comparison. Overall, the study suggests that Agave derived fructans did not significantly alter CRP levels compared to Formula or Breast milk. The findings are presented in Table 3 of the source article [PMC4663570]: nutrients-07-05442-t003_Table 3.
