A 48-week trial compared vitamin D plus calcium (VitD/Cal) with placebo, finding no significant differences in glucose metabolism, insulin resistance, or lipid profiles between groups. Insulin levels rose in the placebo group at week 24 but not in the VitD/Cal group, though these differences were not statistically significant (P > .05). HOMA-IR increases were modest and not significantly different between arms. Fasting total and HDL cholesterol levels increased significantly in both groups, with no between-group differences. LDL cholesterol increased in the placebo group at week 24 but not at week 48. Triglyceride changes were not significant in either group. 

Baseline 25(OH)D levels were balanced, but the VitD/Cal group showed significant increases at weeks 24 and 48 (median 27.5 and 24.2 ng/mL, respectively, P < .001), while the placebo group had minimal changes. Waist circumference increased in the placebo group but not in the VitD/Cal group at weeks 24 and 48, though differences were not significant. BMI changes were not significant in either group over 48 weeks. Metabolic syndrome prevalence was 12% at baseline and 14% at week 48, with no significant differences between arms. Low HDL prevalence decreased from 45% to 26%, while elevated triglyceride prevalence increased from 14% to 22%. Source: PMC5726464.
text: Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation significantly increased 25(OH)D levels compared to placebo (P < .001) at weeks 24 and 48. Source: PMC5726464.

memory: In a clinical study comparing cilostazol (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks) to placebo, cilostazol significantly reduced soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) levels compared to placebo (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, 95% CI 10.65 to 199.71; P = 0.0003). sVCAM-1 levels decreased from 1288.7 ± 285.6 ng/dL to 1168.2 ± 252.3 ng/dL in the cilostazol group. No significant differences were observed between the cilostazol and placebo groups in brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) (mean difference 31.42 cm/sec, 95% CI −55.67 to 118.5). Cilostazol did not significantly affect other biochemical markers, including lipid profiles, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), adiponectin, interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), monocyte chemotactic protein-1 (MCP-1), or soluble intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (sICAM-1). The results suggest that cilostazol may have a specific effect on reducing sVCAM-1 levels but does not influence other cardiovascular or inflammatory markers in this study population. Source: PMC3733748.
text: Cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to placebo (mean difference 105.18 ng/dL, P=0.0003). No significant changes were observed in other markers. Source: PMC3733748.
intervention: cilostazol group (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks)
outcome: soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) level

memory: A study compared computer-assisted learning (CAL) with a control group using an information leaflet. memory: Source: PMC3785973. A study compared internet-based self-management (IBSM) support with usual care (UC) in asthma patients. At 12 months, IBSM significantly improved asthma-related quality of life (AQLQ) by 0.37 (95% CI 0.14-0.61) and asthma control (ACQ) by -0.57 (95% CI -0.88 to -0.26). These benefits were sustained at 30 months, with AQLQ improvements of 0.29 (95% CI 0.01-0.57) and ACQ improvements of -0.33 (95% CI -0.61 to -0.05). Both IBSM and UC groups showed improvements in ACQ over time, with IBSM participants improving by 0.43 (95% CI 0.21-0.66) and UC participants by 0.34 (95% CI 0.06-0.61). No significant differences were observed in inhaled corticosteroid use or FEV1. The study suggests that IBSM enhances asthma-related quality of life and asthma control, with sustained benefits up to 30 months, without affecting lung function or medication use.
text: The effect of Internet-based self-management support compared with control on inhaled corticosteroid dosage shows no significant difference (PMC3785973).

memory: A study evaluated two web-based weight loss maintenance (WLM) programs—Basic and Enhanced—in 227 adults (mean age 42.3 ± 10.1 years, mean BMI 30.4 ± 4.1 kg/m², 44% male) over 12 months. The Enhanced program included additional support features compared to the Basic program. Attrition rates were 18.4% for the Basic group and 23.9% for the Enhanced group, with no significant difference (p = 0.31). Both groups showed minimal weight regain (Basic: 1.3%, Enhanced: 1.5%) and no significant differences in the primary outcome of BMI change (Basic: −0.5 (1.9) kg/m², Enhanced: −0.5 (1.6) kg/m², p = 0.93). Secondary outcomes also showed limited differences between groups. The study concluded that a web-based WLM program was effective in preventing weight regain over one year, but the Enhanced program provided limited additional benefits compared to the Basic program. The analysis used an intention-to-treat approach with last observation carried forward imputation. Participants were predominantly Australian-born (95%), and no significant between-group differences were found for any primary or secondary outcomes.
text: The Enhanced weight loss maintenance program showed no significant additional benefit over the Basic program in preventing weight rebound after 12 months (p = 0.93). Both programs resulted in minimal weight regain.

memory: In a study comparing single sustained inflation (SI) with conventional ventilation and multiple SI, single SI significantly increased carotid blood flow (CaBF) more rapidly and to a greater extent (p = 0.01), though this effect diminished by 10 minutes, likely due to higher cerebral oxygen delivery (p = 0.01). Single SI also caused increased blood-brain barrier disruption, as indicated by a higher number of blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation in the cerebral cortex (p = 0.001). No differences in CaBF or cerebral oxygen delivery were found between multiple SI and no SI groups. These findings were reported in the Abstract > Results section of the source article [PMC4713062].
text: Single sustained inflation (SI) significantly increased blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation in the cerebral cortex compared to conventional ventilation and multiple SI (p = 0.001). Source: [PMC4713062].
outcome: numbers of blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation

memory: In a study comparing vildagliptin to placebo, suppression of fasting hepatic glucose production (HGP) during hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp was similar between groups at baseline and endpoint (vildagliptin: 42.2% vs 42.8%; placebo: 54.7% vs 48.4%; P > 0.42). Vildagliptin significantly reduced fasting liver triglycerides by 27% (7.3% to 5.3%; P = 0.013), while no change was observed in the placebo group. Mean fasting plasma glucose decreased by 1.0 mmol/L in the vildagliptin group compared to placebo (P = 0.018), with a positive correlation between glucose reduction and liver triglyceride levels (r = 0.47 at 3 months, r = 0.44 at 6 months; P < 0.05). HbA1c decreased by −0.5% (P < 0.0001) in the vildagliptin group, compared to a small increase in the placebo group (P = 0.14), with a significant between-group difference (−0.7%; P < 0.001). Plasma ALT levels fell significantly in the vildagliptin group (27.2 to 20.3 IU/L; P = 0.0007) but remained stable in the placebo group. A strong positive correlation was observed between the fall in ALT and reduction in liver fat (r = 0.83; P < 0.0001), which remained significant after excluding an outlier (r = 0.64; P = 0.003).
text: Vildagliptin significantly reduced HbA1c by −0.5% (P < 0.0001) compared to placebo, with a between-group difference of −0.7% (P < 0.001).

Both paricalcitol (PAR) and calcifediol (CAL) significantly reduced bone turnover markers (osteocalcin, bone alkaline phosphatase, and C-terminal telopeptide) at 6 months compared to baseline, with no group differences. FGF23 levels decreased in both groups, with lower values in the CAL group at 6 months. No significant differences were observed in femoral neck or lumbar spine BMD between the two treatments.

PAR led to significantly lower serum intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) levels compared to CAL (76 ± 55 pg/ml vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036). The proportion of patients with iPTH between 70 and 110 pg/ml was lower in the PAR group (14.6%) compared to CAL (25.6%; P = 0.056). In the per-protocol population, the proportion of patients achieving iPTH ≤110 pg/ml was significantly higher in the PAR group (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008). In the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, the number of patients with iPTH >110 pg/ml at 6 months was lower in the PAR group (19.6% vs. 36.2%; P = 0.07), though not statistically significant.
text: Paricalcitol significantly reduced serum iPTH levels compared to calcifediol (76 ± 55 vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036). However, the proportion achieving ≥30% reduction was not significantly different (P = 0.26).

In a study comparing nebivolol and atenolol, VH-IVUS findings revealed that nebivolol segments had significantly reduced external elastic membrane (EEM) area (P=0.02) and lumen area (P=0.004) compared to atenolol. No significant differences were observed in plaque components or thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFAs) per vessel. At follow-up, nebivolol was associated with increased plaque area (P<0.001), while atenolol showed plaque regression (P=0.047). However, the difference between the two groups was not statistically significant (P=0.27). 

Regarding arterial remodeling, static remodeling (remodeling index) was similar between the groups. However, serial remodeling showed significant differences (P=0.002). Nebivolol segments exhibited more constrictive remodeling (73% vs. 46%) and less excessive expansive remodeling (16% vs. 39%) compared to atenolol. These findings were visualized in Figure 6, which depicts serial arterial remodeling by β-blocker at 1-year follow-up. The P values represent comparisons of the frequency of three remodeling groups across the two β-blocker categories.
text: Nebivolol and atenolol showed no significant differences in plaque components or TCFAs per vessel. However, nebivolol was linked to increased plaque area, while atenolol showed plaque regression, though the difference between groups was not statistically significant (P=0.27).
outcome: plaque components and number of TCFAs per vessel

memory: In a study comparing tetraplegic patients (with and without 2 mg melatonin for 4 days) to able-bodied men, circadian patterns of F1+2 and D-dimer showed no differences between tetraplegic groups regardless of melatonin (P>0.05). Tetraplegic groups exhibited increased circadian variation in F1+2 compared to able-bodied controls (P=0.01 and P<0.001), while D-dimer patterns were similar across all groups (P>0.05). Absolute plasma concentrations of F1+2 and D-dimer were similar in all groups (P>0.05). The 24-h profiles of prothrombin fragment 1+2 and von Willebrand factor differed between tetraplegic and able-bodied subjects (P<0.05), with higher activated FVII levels in able-bodied individuals (P<0.05). Melatonin had no impact on these findings. Free TFPI and PAI-1 concentrations did not differ significantly between groups regarding circadian variation or absolute levels (P>0.05). Tetraplegic patients reported unchanged sleep duration and quality with or without melatonin. Supplementation of melatonin in tetraplegia mimicked its endogenous circadian variation, but did not alter the observed hemostatic markers. No significant changes were observed in the circadian variation of FVIIa among the three study groups.
text: Tetraplegic patients, with or without 2 mg melatonin for 4 days, showed increased circadian variation of F1+2 compared to able-bodied men (P=0.01 and P<0.001). Melatonin had no effect on this variation.
intervention: 2 mg of melatonin given 4 days for tetraplegic patients and placebo for tetraplegic patients

memory: In a study comparing Ciclesonide (CIC) and Fluticasone propionate (FLP) nasal sprays, patients (58% male, median age 32 years, median symptom duration 24 months) showed a significant preference for FLP over CIC (55.41% vs. 25.68%, P = 0.007), primarily due to sensory attributes. FLP was preferred for scent (50% vs. 8.11%, P < 0.001), soothing feel (56.76% vs. 20.27%, P < 0.001), and lower nasal irritation (1.35% vs. 28.38%, P = 0.002). Although urge to sneeze was less with FLP (1.35% vs. 13.51%), this difference was not statistically significant. No significant differences in immediate efficacy were observed between the two sprays. Adverse events were mild: two patients experienced headache with CIC, while three had headache, one dizziness, and one nasal congestion with FLP. CIC was associated with fewer reports of immediate taste, aftertaste, run down to throat, and run off from nose, but these differences were not statistically significant. The study suggests a strong patient preference for FLP based on sensory characteristics, despite comparable efficacy.
text: Patients showed a significant preference for Fluticasone propionate (FLP) over Ciclesonide (CIC) as a preferred intranasal corticosteroid, primarily due to better sensory attributes like scent, soothing feel, and lower nasal irritation (P < 0.001). Efficacy was comparable, with no significant differences in immediate effectiveness. (Source: Study comparing CIC and FLP nasal sprays)

memory: A 36-month study compared Superion® and X-STOP® in treating moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis. Superion® demonstrated a higher success rate for the primary composite endpoint (52.5% vs. 36.0%, P=0.023). It maintained clinical success from 24 to 36 months, while X-STOP® showed a decline. At 36 months, Superion® exceeded 80% in individual components of the primary endpoint: 88% for ZCQ improvement in two of three domains, 81% for no reoperations, 91% for no major implant-related complications, and 87% for no clinically significant confounding treatments. Five of six comparisons for pain severity and functional outcomes favored Superion®, with only leg pain showing statistical significance. Line graphs illustrated the durability of Superion® results and the degradation of X-STOP® results over time for ZCQ, back and leg pain severity, and back function. X-STOP® had higher rates of reoperations, revisions, and removals (15 out of 44) compared to Superion® (11 out of 49). Superion® sustained improvements in back and leg pain severity and functional outcomes through 36 months.
text: Superion® showed a higher success rate (52.5% vs. 38.0%, P=0.023) in achieving the primary composite endpoint for moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis compared to X-STOP®. It maintained clinical success longer and had fewer reoperations and complications.
outcome: subjects achieving the primary composite endpoint - moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis.

A 24-week study compared vonoprazan (10 mg and 20 mg) to lansoprazole 15 mg for maintaining healed erosive esophagitis (EE). Both vonoprazan doses showed non-inferiority to lansoprazole in preventing EE recurrence (P < 0.0001). Recurrence rates were 16.8% for lansoprazole 15 mg, 5.1% for vonoprazan 10 mg, and 2.0% for vonoprazan 20 mg. Post-hoc analysis confirmed significant reductions in recurrence with both vonoprazan doses compared to lansoprazole (P = 0.0002 and P < 0.0001, respectively). No significant difference in recurrence was observed between the two vonoprazan doses (P = 0.1090). 

Safety profiles were similar across groups, with treatment-related adverse events (AEs) reported in 11.4%, 10.4%, and 10.3% of patients for lansoprazole 15 mg, vonoprazan 10 mg, and vonoprazan 20 mg, respectively. No clinically significant changes were observed in vital signs, ECG findings, or laboratory test values. Baseline characteristics were well-matched across groups, with similar demographics, EE severity, and medical histories. Mean treatment compliance exceeded 97% in all groups.
text: Vonoprazan 10 mg and 20 mg showed non-inferiority to lansoprazole 15 mg in preventing erosive esophagitis recurrence over 24 weeks (P < 0.0001). Recurrence rates were 5.1% and 2.0% for vonoprazan 10 mg and 20 mg, respectively, versus 16.8% for lansoprazole. No significant difference was found between the two vonoprazan doses (P = 0.1090).
outcome: Erosive esophagitis recurrence rate after 24 weeks

memory: In a study comparing Drug-eluting balloon + bare metal stent (DEB + BMS) with Zotarolimus-eluting stent (ZES), 180 patients were enrolled, with 72 and 74 undergoing 9-month follow-up angiography, respectively. The angiographic follow-up rate was 81.1%, conducted at 298 days post-PCI. Baseline characteristics, including minimal lumen diameter, reference diameter, percentage diameter stenosis, and lesion length, were comparable between the two groups. After PCI, DEB + BMS showed significantly lower acute gain and minimal luminal diameter compared to ZES. Late luminal loss (LL), the primary endpoint, was significantly higher in DEB + BMS (0.50 ± 0.46 mm) than in ZES (0.21 ± 0.44 mm; P < 0.001). The mean LL difference was 0.31 mm (95% CI: 0.15–0.48), exceeding the prespecified non-inferiority margin of 0.19 mm (P for non-inferiority = 0.138). Binary restenosis rates were higher in the DEB + BMS group, though not statistically significant. Clinical outcomes were not significantly different between the groups. Findings suggest DEB + BMS may be inferior to ZES in terms of LL and acute gain, despite similar baseline characteristics. Source: PMC5426232.
text: The "Drug-eluting balloon + bare metal stent" showed higher late luminal loss and lower acute gain compared to "Zotarolimus-eluting stent," suggesting potential inferiority in preventing binary restenosis (PMC5426232).

memory: A study compared nutrition psychoeducation (NPC), motivational interviewing (MIC), and usual care (UC) on depression (BDI scores), triglycerides, weight loss, and satisfaction. NPC significantly reduced BDI scores post-treatment compared to UC (p=0.009), but not MIC (p=0.195), with no difference between MIC and UC (p=0.168). At 3-month follow-up, BDI scores showed a trend toward significance (p=0.057). For triglycerides, NPC significantly reduced levels compared to UC (p=0.008) and trended lower than MIC (p=0.057), with no difference between MIC and UC (p=0.423). Weight loss was achieved by ~25% of MIC and NPC participants, with no difference by BED status. Satisfaction scores were significantly higher in NPC (M=75.2, SD=5.3) and MIC (M=73.3, SD=6.6) compared to UC (M=66.0, SD=11.1), with no difference between NPC and MIC (p=0.393). Both NPC and MIC were delivered as intended, with treatment adherence linked to weight loss. These findings suggest that NPC and MIC are more effective than UC in improving depression and triglyceride levels, with high satisfaction and fidelity.
text: Nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) significantly reduced triglyceride levels compared to usual care (UC) (p=0.008). No significant difference was found between NPC and motivational interviewing (MIC) (p=0.057).

memory: A study compared 10-mm transumbilical and 5-mm transabdominal approaches in surgery, with no complications reported. All patients were discharged on postoperative day 1 and followed up at 3 months with no post-side herniation. Surgical satisfaction was similar between groups (9.2 ± 0.6 vs. 9.5 ± 0.6, P = 0.69), as were cosmetic outcomes (9.6 ± 0.5 vs. 9.8 ± 0.4, P = 0.74). Baseline characteristics, including age, BMI, obstetric history, hospital stay, and tubal size, were comparable. The transumbilical group had significantly shorter specimen retrieval time (43.5 ± 14.5 s) than the transabdominal group (69.4 ± 20.5 s, P < 0.001). Rescue analgesia was needed for four patients in the transumbilical group and three in the transabdominal group. No intra-operative retrieval bag ruptures were observed. Post-removal evaluation showed intact tubes in 18 of 20 cases in the transumbilical group versus 3 of 20 in the transabdominal group (P < 0.001, OR: 51.0, 95% CI: 7.56-343.73). VAS scores on postoperative days 0 and 1 were similar between the groups.
text: The 10-mm transumbilical group had significantly higher intact tube rates (18/20) compared to the 5-mm transabdominal group (3/20, P < 0.001, OR: 51.0). No complications were reported, and other outcomes were similar between groups.

memory: [PMC3661377] Apremilast 20 mg BID and 30 mg BID significantly reduced pruritus VAS scores at week 16 (P=0.005 and P<0.001), with 60.9% and 63.6% of patients achieving ≥MCID improvement. A clinical study compared an aprepitant triple regimen (aprepitant + tropisetron + dexamethasone) with a standard regimen (tropisetron + dexamethasone) for managing chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV). The primary endpoint was complete response (CR) during the overall phase (OP, 0–120 h). The aprepitant group showed a significantly higher CR rate (80.0%, 40/50) compared to the standard group (56.0%, 28/50; P = 0.018). This improvement was also observed during the delay phase (DP, 25–120 h), with CR rates of 80.0% and 56.0%, respectively (P = 0.018). However, during the acute phase (AP, 0–24 h), both groups had identical CR rates (98.0%, P = 1.000). 

Secondary outcomes included CR in the AP and DP, the first time of vomiting (assessed by Kaplan–Meier curves), and the impact of CINV on quality of life using the Functional Living Index-Emesis (FLIE). Within the aprepitant group, males had a higher CR rate (93.1%, 27/29) compared to females (61.9%, 13/21; P = 0.011). The study highlights the effectiveness of the aprepitant regimen in improving CR during the OP and DP, with no significant difference in the AP. Source: PMC5851005.
text: The aprepitant regimen (aprepitant + tropisetron + dexamethasone) significantly improved complete response (CR) in the delay phase (DP) compared to the standard regimen (tropisetron + dexamethasone) (80.0% vs. 56.0%, P = 0.018). Source: PMC5851005.

memory: A study compared ch14.18-UTC and ch14.18-NCI and found similar pharmacokinetic parameters to previously published data for ch14.18-NCI, with comparable profiles between the two products. Systemic exposures were similar, with 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the ratio of AUCinf (0.96; 90% CI 0.88–1.04) and Cmax (1.04; 90% CI 0.98–1.11) falling within standard bioequivalence bounds (0.80–1.25). Adverse events (AEs) were similar between the two products, with no notable differences in treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) by manufacturer, either overall or specifically attributable to ch14.18. Pain-related TRAEs were most commonly reported during cycles 1, 2, and 4 (93%, 74%, and 71%, respectively).

A multi-site study in Johannesburg, Durban, and Harare found that at baseline, 12.6% of women reported no vaginal practices, 31.8% reported one, and 56.6% reported ≥2. Washing was most common in Johannesburg (86.7%), while wiping was more frequent in Harare (68.0%) than in Durban (40.9%) or Johannesburg (51.3%). No differences in practices were found between randomization groups, but site differences were significant.

During follow-up, the intervention group (diaphragm with lubricant gel, MIRA) showed a modest but significant increase in reporting washing (AOR 1.35; 95% CI 1.22–1.50), wiping (AOR 1.14; 95% CI 1.05–1.24), and use of soap and water (AOR 1.23; 95% CI 1.07–1.41) compared to the control group. However, no differences were found in insertion practices or use of water or other products. All practices decreased over time, with a significant time effect (P < 0.0001) across groups.

Baseline vaginal practices were common: washing (82.77%), wiping (56.47%), and insertion (20.58%). These were inversely associated with consistent diaphragm and gel use and condom use. Socio-cultural context of these practices may influence educational strategies and future HIV prevention interventions.
text: At baseline, vaginal practices differed by site: washing was most common in Johannesburg (86.7%), while wiping was more frequent in Harare (68.0%) than in Durban (40.9%) or Johannesburg (51.3%). No differences were found between randomization groups, but site differences were significant (source: study in Johannesburg, Durban, and Harare).

memory: A study compared chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) dressings with transparent dressings in reducing central line-associated bloodstream infection (CRBSI) rates. The CHG group had a significantly lower CRBSI rate (3 per 1,000 patients) compared to the non-CHG group (14 per 1,000 patients), with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals, indicating statistical significance. ICU-days and days before discharge or death were comparable between groups, as was the number of patients reaching absorbing states (discharge or death). The study reported a 1:5 CRBSI ratio between the CHG and non-CHG groups. The mean cost difference per patient was €141, not statistically significant (95% CI: [€-975; €1,258]). The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was €12,046 per CRBSI prevented, with an incremental net monetary benefit of €344.88 per patient. The number needed to treat was 85 patients to prevent 11.8 infections per 1,000 patients (95% CI: [3.85; 19.64]). These results were derived from a base case scenario using 1,000 NH-MCMC simulations of 1,000 patients in each group (Table 3).
text: Chlorhexidine gluconate dressings significantly reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections compared to transparent dressings (3 vs. 14 per 1,000 patients). The study showed a 1:5 CRBSI ratio, with a number needed to treat of 85.

memory: A study compared noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and pressure support ventilation (PSV) in patients with similar demographics, disease severity, and clinical profiles. No statistically significant differences were found in the duration of mechanical ventilation (6.20 ± 5.20 days vs. 7.47 ± 6.38 days, P > 0.05), duration of weaning (35.17 ± 16.98 hours vs. 47.05 ± 20.98 hours, P > 0.05), or ICU stay (8.47 ± 4.79 days vs. 10.80 ± 5.28 days, P > 0.05). However, the NIV group had a shorter ICU stay by nearly 2 days compared to the PSV group, though not statistically significant. The PSV group had a higher incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) (5 cases) compared to the NIV group (1 case). Regarding mortality, the NIV group had fewer deaths at ICU discharge (3 vs. 5 patients) and at 30 days (5 vs. 9 patients), but these differences were not statistically significant (P > 0.05). The study suggests a potential benefit of NIV in terms of reduced ICU stay and lower VAP incidence, though further research is needed to confirm these findings. Source: [PMC2856148].
text: A study found no statistically significant difference in duration of weaning between NIV and PSV (P > 0.05). However, NIV showed a trend toward shorter ICU stays and lower VAP incidence, though not significant. Source: [PMC2856148].

memory: A clinical study evaluated the efficacy of hydrodistension combined with intravesical resiniferatoxin (RTX) versus hydrodistension alone in 18 patients (mean age 55.8±6.9 years, mean symptom duration 3.6±1.6 years) with interstitial cystitis (IC) who had failed prior treatments. Both interventions resulted in significant improvements in frequency, functional bladder capacity, and pain scores (5-point scale) at 3 months post-treatment. However, the addition of RTX did not significantly affect voiding symptoms or uroflowmetry outcomes compared to hydrodistension alone. Pain scores showed a significant improvement with RTX plus hydrodistension. Baseline symptom severity was comparable between groups. memory: A study compared paravertebral block (PVB) with a control group and found that PVB was associated with significantly lower Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores at rest and during coughing/movement within 24 postoperative hours (P<0.05). The PVB group had lower median tramadol consumption (200 mg [150–250]) compared to the control group (300 mg [200–350], P=0.003) and lower nurse-administered morphine consumption (0 mg [0–2] vs. 2.5 mg [2–4], P=0.001). Additionally, the first analgesic request time was significantly longer in the PVB group (120 minutes [60–120]) compared to the control group (30 minutes [27.5–30], P<0.05). No significant differences were found between groups in postoperative mean arterial blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation (P>0.05). Demographic data showed 84% females in the PVB group and 80% in the control group, with no significant differences in ASA physical status distribution. These results suggest that PVB may offer improved postoperative analgesia with reduced opioid consumption and delayed analgesic requirement, without adverse effects on vital signs. Source: [PMC5513842]
text: Paravertebral block (PVB) significantly reduces Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores at rest and during movement/coughing within 24 hours postoperatively compared to control (P<0.05). Source: [PMC5513842].

memory: In a study comparing calcitriol to placebo in patients with type 1 diabetes, vitamin D status at diagnosis did not correlate with residual β-cell function at 24 months, as C-peptide levels were similar between participants with 25OHD levels <20 ng/ml and >20 ng/ml (P = 0.408). No adverse events were reported, and calcium and phosphate levels remained normal throughout the study. A1C levels and insulin requirements did not differ between the calcitriol and placebo groups at 6, 12, and 24 months. C-peptide levels decreased significantly (P < 0.001) in both groups over time, with no significant difference in decline between groups at any time point. The area under the curve of the C-peptide response (AUC0–120 min) was also not significantly different between groups at baseline or after 12 months (P = 0.658 and P = 0.845, respectively). Fasting C-peptide levels dropped significantly in both groups during follow-up (P < 0.001), though the calcitriol group showed a slower rate of decline (17.7%) compared to the placebo group (28.4%) after 12 months. Vitamin D deficiency was present in 47% of participants at baseline, with calcitriol leading to a slight increase in 25OHD levels (+3.9%) and a decrease in the placebo group (−8.0%). Source: PMC2928344.
text: In a study comparing calcitriol to placebo in type 1 diabetes patients, no adverse events were reported. Calcium and phosphate levels remained normal, and there were no significant differences in A1C, insulin requirements, or C-peptide decline between groups. Source: PMC2928344.

memory: Two studies (CaMEWS and D&Cancer) assessed the effects of Vitamin D + Calcium, Calcium only, and Placebo on serum 25(OH)D levels. Baseline characteristics, including age, height, weight, BMI, serum 25(OH)D, and calcium levels, were similar across groups (P > 0.05). The Vitamin D + Calcium groups showed significantly greater increases in serum 25(OH)D compared to Calcium only and Placebo groups (P < 0.0001). In CaMEWS, the mean serum 25(OH)D change was +24.31 nmol/L for the Vitamin D + Calcium group, while the Calcium only group had a mean change of −1.02 nmol/L. In D&Cancer, the mean serum 25(OH)D change was +31.92 nmol/L for the Vitamin D + Calcium group, compared to +0.36 nmol/L for the Calcium only group. Baseline serum 25(OH)D levels ranged from 24.2 to 144.6 nmol/L in CaMEWS and 13.3 to 225.8 nmol/L in D&Cancer. Source: PMC5228186.
text: Vitamin D + Calcium significantly increased serum 25(OH)D levels compared to Placebo (P < 0.0001), with mean changes of +24.31 nmol/L (CaMEWS) and +31.92 nmol/L (D&Cancer). Source: PMC5228186.

A study compared classic cigarettes with two e-cigarette types (disposable cigalike and second-gen Ego C), all with 24 mg nicotine. Craving increased over time in all groups, but was higher and more prolonged in the classic cigarette group. E-cigarette users experienced less pronounced increases in craving, especially from T1 to T3. Cognitive performance (attention, executive function, working memory) was not affected by e-cigarette use or gender, suggesting e-cigarettes may support smoking cessation without impairing cognitive function. The study indicates that craving and withdrawal are not solely nicotine-dependent, pointing to the role of smoking rituals in dependence and relapse. E-cigarettes mimic smoking gestures, offering a potential coping mechanism for conditioned smoking cues. Participants reported satisfaction with e-cigarettes, which may help replace ritualistic aspects of smoking such as tactile sensations and predictable actions. This suggests e-cigarettes could help reduce relapse by substituting these rituals, though further research is needed on the impact of behavioral factors on smoking cessation. Trial registration: NCT01735487.
text: Classic cigarettes caused higher and more prolonged craving compared to two e-cigarette types (disposable cigalike and Ego C). E-cigarettes led to less pronounced craving increases, suggesting they may help reduce relapse by substituting smoking rituals. Source: [PMC5343026].

memory: [PMC5588958] A 28-day trial of oral SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) in T2DM showed a significant 0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) reduction in body weight. However, HbA1c increased by 0.48% (95% CI 0.26% to 0.70%, p=0.004), and plasma fructosamine rose by 33.41 μmol/L (95% CI 20.24 to 46.58 μmol/L, p<0.001). Bradykinin-induced vasodilatation was significantly reduced in the SRT2104 group compared to placebo (mean difference=−1.291, 95% CI −2.296 to −0.285, p=0.012), but acetylcholine (p=0.318) and sodium nitroprusside (p=0.083) responses were not significantly different. Lipid profile and platelet-monocyte activation showed no significant differences (p>0.05). The estimated net plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 antigen release was reduced in the SRT2104 group compared to placebo (mean difference=−38.89 ng/100 mL tissue/min, 95% CI −75.47 to –2.305, p=0.038). No significant differences were observed in other plasma fibrinolytic factors (p>0.05).
text: Oral SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) for 28 days significantly reduced body weight by 0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) in T2DM patients compared to placebo, but increased HbA1c and fructosamine levels (PMC5588958).

memory: [PMC5448649] PPV/CPA (peptide vaccine + low-dose cyclophosphamide) improved progression-free survival (6.1 vs 2.9 mo; HR 0.427; P=0.008) and overall survival (12.1 vs 5.9 mo; HR 0.376; P=0.004) compared to PPV alone. T cell responses were stronger in the PPV/CPA group. PPV alone increased plasma IL-6 levels at 6th (P=0.010) and 12th (P=0.006) months, which correlated negatively with T cell responses (r=-0.703; P=0.007). No significant changes in peptide-specific IgG levels were observed between treatment arms. IFN-γ spot numbers increased over time in both arms, but no differences were seen between groups. The rise in IL-6 with PPV alone may suppress antigen-specific T cell responses, while low-dose CPA may counteract this immune suppression in aBTC patients.
text: Cyclophosphamide (CPA) combined with peptide vaccine (PPV) improved progression-free survival (6.1 vs 2.9 mo; HR 0.427; P=0.008) compared to PPV alone [PMC5448649].

memory: Study [PMC3258705] evaluated the addition of 2 mg oral oestradiol valerate to vaginal progesterone (N=47) versus vaginal progesterone alone (N=51) in a reproductive context. Outcomes included oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, pregnancy rates, and hormone levels. No significant differences were found in the mean number of retrieved oocytes, transferred embryos, or pregnancy rates between groups. Serum progesterone levels were higher in the oestradiol group on days 7, 10, and 12 post-embryo transfer, but these differences were not statistically significant. Similarly, serum oestradiol and progesterone levels were higher in the oestradiol group, though not significantly different from the control. LH levels showed no significant differences between groups. The mean duration of infertility was 5.98 ±0.55 years in the control group and 7.81 ±1.37 years in the oestradiol group, with no significant difference. Among 25 oestradiol group participants with positive β hCG tests, 23 had intrauterine gestational sacs with detectable fetal heart, while one had an ectopic pregnancy and another had a blighted ovum. The study concluded that adding oral oestradiol valerate did not significantly improve pregnancy outcomes compared to vaginal progesterone alone.
text: The addition of oral oestradiol valerate to vaginal progesterone did not significantly affect the mean duration of infertility compared to vaginal progesterone alone (Study [PMC3258705]).
intervention: oestradiol group, 2 mg of oestradiol valerate was initiated orally with progesterone
comparator: the control group received vaginal administration of progesterone supplementation alone starting on the day after oocyte retrieval and continued until the tenth week if the chemical pregnancy test was positive

memory: A clinical study involving 120 premature infants compared the effects of paracetamol and ibuprofen on primary closure rates and other neonatal outcomes. Of these, 34 met treatment criteria, and 22 were randomized. No significant differences were observed between the groups in terms of mortality, primary closure rates, or short-term neonatal outcomes. Additional data showed no significant differences in sepsis (7 vs. 4, p=0.664), surfactant therapy (9 vs. 6, p=0.898), or pulmonary hemorrhage (1 vs. 1, p=0.783) between the paracetamol and ibuprofen groups. These results suggest that both drugs may have comparable effects on the studied outcomes in premature infants. The study underscores the lack of significant differences in key clinical outcomes between paracetamol and ibuprofen in this population. The findings contribute to the understanding of potential therapeutic equivalency between these two medications in the context of neonatal care.
text: A clinical study found no significant difference between paracetamol and ibuprofen in surfactant therapy use in premature infants (9 vs. 6, p=0.898). Both drugs showed comparable effects on key neonatal outcomes.

memory: A study compared prefrontal rTMS with sham rTMS in reducing food cravings. Both real and sham interventions led to significant reductions in cravings [F(1,9) = 15.91, p = 0.003], but no significant differences were found between real and sham conditions [F(1,9) = 1.13, ns] or in the time by condition interaction [F(1,9) = 0.13, ns]. Controlling for hours since last meal, no significant effects were found for time [F(1,8) = 2.97, ns], condition [F(1,8) = 1.94, ns], or the time by condition interaction [F(1,8) = 2.07, ns]. Cravings decreased slightly more in the sham group, but the effect size was minimal (d = 0.09). Hours since last meal did not differ significantly between conditions [t(9) = 0.52, ns]. The sham rTMS system was validated by participants’ ability to identify the real session, with only 40% correct identification (p = 0.27), suggesting good blinding. These results indicate that both real and sham rTMS produced similar reductions in food cravings, and the sham condition was effective in mimicking the real intervention in terms of participant perception.
text: The study found no significant difference between prefrontal rTMS and sham rTMS in reducing face and scalp sensations, as both led to similar reductions in food cravings. The sham condition effectively mimicked the real intervention, with minimal effect size (d = 0.09).

memory: A clinical study compared haloperidol (H1: 1 mg, H2: 2 mg) with saline (H0) for postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) prevention. Both haloperidol doses reduced PONV incidence compared to saline. Within 24 hours postoperatively, PONV rates were 29% (H1), 24% (H2), and 54% (H0), with a statistically significant difference (P = 0.003). In the ward (2–24 h), PONV incidence was 22% (H1), 20% (H2), and 42% (H0), with no significant difference between H1 and H2. Sedation scores in the PACU over 2 h were significantly higher in group H2 compared to H1 and H0 (P < 0.001), with no difference between H1 and H0. Three patients in group H2 required ephedrine for hypotension (systolic 75–80 mmHg, diastolic 50–55 mmHg) in the PACU. These results are presented in Table 2 and Fig. 2 of the source article [PMC4493951].
text: Both haloperidol doses (H1: 1 mg, H2: 2 mg) significantly reduced PONV incidence compared to saline (H0), with 29% and 24% vs. 54% (P = 0.003). No significant difference was found between H1 and H2. Source: [PMC4493951].
outcome: the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV)

In a study comparing sipuleucel-T alone (Arm 1) with sipuleucel-T plus intradermal pTVG-HP DNA vaccine (Arm 2), 18 patients were followed for a median of 24 months. Eleven completed treatment as per protocol, with no treatment-related events above grade 2. Th1-biased PAP-specific T-cell responses were detected in 11/18 patients, with no differences between arms. Patients in Arm 2 showed higher antibody titers to PAP. Median time to progression was less than 6 months, with no differences between arms.

Overall survival was 715 days (24 months) in Arm 1 and 901 days (30 months) in Arm 2, though the trial was not powered to detect survival differences. No significant differences in PSA kinetics were observed. Pre-treatment PSA doubling time was 2.55 months (2.8 in Arm 1, 2.2 in Arm 2). Post-treatment PSA doubling times remained similar (2.6 months overall, 2.5 in Arm 1, 2.6 in Arm 2).

Radiographic progression occurred at a median of 161 days in Arm 1 and 164 days in Arm 2. Two Arm 2 patients showed progression at month 3 but remained stable until months 9 and 12 before further progression. Other patients with progression at month 3 progressed by month 6. The study used month 3 scans as baseline to account for delayed treatment effects. No significant differences in clinical outcomes were observed between the study arms.
text: The combination of sipuleucel-T with pTVG-HP DNA vaccine showed a non-significant trend toward improved overall survival (901 vs. 715 days) compared to sipuleucel-T alone, though the trial was not powered to detect survival differences. No significant differences in progression or PSA kinetics were observed.
intervention: sipuleucel-T alone followed by intradermal immunization with pTVG-HP DNA vaccine

memory: In a study comparing selenium (Se) supplementation to placebo, the effects on sFlt-1, PlGF, and their ratio were analyzed. In participants with the lowest quartile of baseline Se status (n=50), Se treatment significantly reduced sFlt-1 concentrations (P=0.039) and halved the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio (P=0.066, not quite significant). However, in all participants combined (n=233), Se had no significant effect on sFlt-1, PlGF, or their ratio. For PlGF specifically, the data showed a 0.97 ratio (95% CI: 0.78–1.21, P=0.801) in all participants, indicating no significant difference between Se and placebo. The results suggest that Se may have a more pronounced effect on sFlt-1 and its ratio in individuals with lower baseline Se levels, but not in the general population. These findings were derived from Table 3 of the source article [PMC4054662], which details the outcomes at 35 weeks of gestation.
text: In participants with low baseline selenium status, selenium supplementation significantly reduced sFlt-1 concentrations (P=0.039) and trended toward lowering the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio (P=0.066). However, in all participants combined, selenium had no significant effect on sFlt-1, PlGF, or their ratio (PMC4054662).

memory: A study compared Natural childbirth preparation with Standard antenatal education and found no significant differences in key delivery outcomes. Spontaneous vaginal delivery rates were 66% in both groups (RR 1.0, 95% CI 0.9 to 1.1). Emergency Caesarean rates were similar: 14% in the Natural group and 15% in the Standard group (RR 0.9, 95% CI 0.7 to 1.2). Elective Caesarean rates were also comparable at 6% in both groups (RR 0.9, 95% CI 0.6 to 1.6). Epidural use was similar, with 52% in both groups. Parental stress and childbirth experience were not significantly different between the groups, despite higher use of psychoprophylaxis in the Natural group (70% vs. 37% in Standard). Subgroup analysis excluding psychoprophylaxis users did not change the main findings. The study suggests that Natural childbirth preparation does not significantly differ from Standard antenatal education in terms of delivery outcomes or parental stress. Source: [PMC2759981].
text: A study found no significant difference between Natural childbirth preparation and Standard antenatal education on elective Caesarean rates (6% in both groups, RR 0.9, 95% CI 0.6 to 1.6). Source: [PMC2759981].

memory: Residents in SP-based scenarios scored higher on post-tests than those in mannequin-based scenarios (4.53/5 [90%] vs 3.69/5 [73%], P=0.01), with significant improvement in all scenarios except acute bacterial meningitis. In the calcium channel blocker overdose scenario, SP group scores improved by 2.4/5 (48%) compared to 1.3/5 (26%) in the mannequin group (P=0.03). Overall, SP group post-test improvement was 1.8/5 (36%) versus 1.2/5 (24%) in the mannequin group (P=0.01). SP scenarios were rated significantly higher in realism (4.73/5 vs 2.00/5, P=0.002), with higher realism scores also noted in severe asthma exacerbation and severe sepsis scenarios. Both groups showed post-test score improvements, but SP simulations achieved significantly higher scores in three of four scenarios (P=0.01). Pre-test scores were equivalent between groups (2.56/5 [51%] in mannequin group vs 2.53/5 [50%] in SP group). Nine residents completed mannequin-based scenarios, while 10 completed SP-based scenarios. Source: [PMC5524701]
text: SP-based scenarios significantly improved realism scores compared to mannequin-based scenarios (4.73/5 vs 2.00/5, P=0.002). Source: [PMC5524701]

memory: Study [PMC4305224] assessed sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + azithromycin (SPAZ) versus control in 2,793 pregnant women, with primary analysis on 2,021 (72.4%) participants. SPAZ significantly reduced low birthweight (RR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.60–0.91, P=0.005; ARR: 4.5%, NNT: 22) and preterm delivery (RR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.43–0.89, P=0.010). Birthweight increased by 41.9 g (95% CI: 0.2–83.6, P=0.049). SPAZ also decreased maternal parasitaemia (RR: 0.57, 95% CI: 0.35–0.95, P=0.029) and active placental malaria (RR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47–0.98, P=0.037). Gonorrhoea carriage was reduced (RR: 0.66, 95% CI: 0.44–0.99, P=0.041). No treatment-related serious adverse events (SAEs) were observed; SAE rates were similar between groups (intervention: 13.1%, control: 12.7%, P=0.712). Adverse event (AE) rates were also comparable (intervention: 10.5%, control: 10.8%, P=0.737).
text: Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + azithromycin significantly reduced the risk of active placental malaria (RR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47–0.98, P=0.037) compared with control in pregnant women (PMC4305224).

memory: In a clinical trial comparing dovitinib to placebo, the most common adverse events (AEs) leading to discontinuation were diarrhea (6.4% dovitinib vs 0% placebo), alanine aminotransferase increase (4.3% vs 2.0%), aspartate aminotransferase increase (4.3% vs 2.0%), and rash (4.3% vs 0%). AEs led to discontinuation in 38.3% of dovitinib patients versus 8.0% of placebo patients. Discontinuation reasons included progressive disease (55.3% vs 80.0%), AEs (21.3% vs 2.0%), patient or guardian decision (10.6% vs 0%), termination by sponsor (8.5% vs 16.0%), death (2.1% vs 2.0%), and nonadherence (2.1% vs 0%). Most dovitinib patients required dose reductions, interruptions, or changes (74.5% vs 26.0% for placebo), primarily due to AEs. Four on-treatment deaths were reported, two in each arm. In the dovitinib group, one death was due to breast cancer progression and another due to a suspected pulmonary embolism related to treatment. Overall, 29.8% of dovitinib and 36.0% of placebo patients died during the study period. These findings highlight the higher incidence of AEs and discontinuations in the dovitinib arm, with specific emphasis on diarrhea, rash, and liver enzyme elevations as key factors. (Source: PMC5301372)
text: Dovitinib significantly increased discontinuation due to rash compared to placebo (4.3% vs 0%). Source: PMC5301372.

memory: A clinical study compared high-dose Vitamin D3 (40,000 IU, DD group; 20,000 IU, DP group) with placebo (PP group). No serious adverse events were reported, and no significant differences in adverse events were observed between groups. Two participants had primary hyperparathyroidism, and one experienced elevated serum calcium (2.62 mmol/L), leading to exclusion. Four others had transient calcium increases (>2.59 mmol/L) but remained in the study. Baseline serum 25(OH)D was 58 nmol/L, rising to 141 nmol/L in the DD group and 100 nmol/L in the DP group. Vitamin D supplementation significantly reduced serum PTH levels, but no significant changes in weight or serum calcium were observed. Regarding bone mineral density (BMD), no significant differences were found between groups in changes at the lumbar spine (L2-L4) or hip after one year, even when combining DD and DP groups or analyzing only those with low baseline 25(OH)D (<45 nmol/L). Minor BMD changes were noted in two subjects (11.3% increase in PP group, 11.5% decrease in DD group), but these were within the "least significant change" range. No significant differences were found in serum osteoprotegrin (OPG) or receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappaB ligand (RANKL) changes across the groups after one year.
text: The study found no significant differences in adverse events between the Vitamin D3 groups (40,000 IU or 20,000 IU) and the placebo group. No serious adverse events were reported, though some transient increases in serum calcium were observed.
intervention: Vitamin D3 40.000 IU (DD group) or Vitamin D3 20.000 IU (DP group)

memory: A study assessed the effect of adding low-intensity power ultrasound (LIPUS) to standard implant treatment compared to standard treatment alone. Immediately post-surgery, no significant differences were found in FD mesial values (1.338 vs. 1.319) or RF values (55.3% vs. 53.2%). However, at six months post-surgery, FD-mesial values showed greater improvement in the LIPUS group (increase of 0.342 units) compared to the control group (0.132 units), with a very strong effect size (Cohen's d = 4.85 vs. 2.64). FD-distal values also improved more in the LIPUS group, though to a lesser extent. RF values increased by 7.4 units in the LIPUS group, corresponding to a very strong effect size (Cohen's d = 7.4) compared to the control group (Cohen's d = 2.25). The effect sizes for FD and RF improvements were significantly higher in the LIPUS group, suggesting enhanced long-term outcomes of dental implants. These results were consistent across follow-up assessments at three and six months post-surgery. Source: [PMC5925011].
text: The intervention group with added LIPUS showed significantly greater improvement in FD mesial values after six months (increase of 0.342 units) compared to standard treatment (0.132 units), with a very strong effect size (Cohen's d = 4.85). Source: [PMC5925011].
intervention: intervention group with added low-intensity power ultrasound treatment (LIPUS)

memory: A study investigated the effect of a single serving of curry meal versus a spice-free control meal on postprandial flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD). The control meal resulted in a decrease in FMD from 5.8 ± 2.4% to 5.1 ± 2.3% (P = 0.039). In contrast, the curry meal increased FMD from 5.2 ± 2.5% to 6.6 ± 2.0% (P = 0.001). Postprandial FMD following the curry meal was significantly higher than that following the control meal (P = 0.002). The presence of spices in the curry meal did not significantly influence systemic and forearm hemodynamics or biochemical parameters, including oxidative stress markers. These results suggest that the curry meal, likely due to its spices, may improve endothelial function as indicated by enhanced FMD, without affecting other hemodynamic or biochemical parameters.
text: A single serving of curry meal significantly improves flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) compared to a spice-free control meal (P = 0.002). The curry meal increased FMD from 5.2 ± 2.5% to 6.6 ± 2.0%, while the control meal decreased it from 5.8 ± 2.4% to 5.1 ± 2.3% (P = 0.039). This suggests that curry's spices may enhance endothelial function without affecting other hemodynamic or biochemical parameters.

memory: [PMC4994668] A trial comparing infliximab and ciclosporin in IBD found no significant difference in quality-adjusted survival (CUCQ AUC: 564.0 vs 587.0; p=0.603) or colectomy rates (41% vs 48%; OR 1.350; p=0.223). Infliximab had higher total health service costs (£5632 more; p=0.001) but similar effectiveness (QALY difference: 0.021; p=0.350). Three deaths occurred in the infliximab group: 2 from sepsis, 1 from cancer. No significant difference in serious adverse reactions (16 vs 10; p=0.788) or serious adverse events (21 vs 25; p=0.807). Renal impairment was noted in 11 ciclosporin patients, mostly non-serious. No significant difference in steroid use duration (5.32 vs 5.43 days; p=0.603) or use of immunosuppressants (azathioprine, 6-MP, methotrexate). One infliximab patient received oral ciclosporin at 3 months. No significant difference in time to colectomy (811 vs 744 days; p=0.251). Malignancies: 2 in infliximab (basal cell, colorectal), 1 in ciclosporin (endometrial).
text: Infliximab had higher total health service costs (£5632 more; p=0.001) than ciclosporin in IBD, with no significant difference in effectiveness or colectomy rates (PMC4994668).

memory: A clinical study compared NBUVB (9 J/cm² for 6 weeks) with systemic prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in treating generalized lichen planus. Baseline disease duration was similar between groups (p = 0.910). Sex did not significantly affect disease duration (p = 0.763 for females, p = 0.738 for males). Treatment efficacy, evaluated via chi-square test, showed NBUVB was significantly more effective than systemic steroids (p = 0.008). Patient satisfaction was also significantly higher in the NBUVB group compared to the systemic corticosteroid group (p = 0.012). No significant side effects were reported in either group. These results are detailed in Tables 1, 2, and 3 of the source article [PMC3434899].
text: NBUVB (9 J/cm² for 6 weeks) significantly reduced disease duration compared to prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg for 6 weeks) in generalized lichen planus (p = 0.008). NBUVB also showed higher patient satisfaction (p = 0.012). Source: [PMC3434899].

memory: In a study comparing Group Support Lifestyle Modification (GSLiM) to dietary counseling, GSLiM participants achieved significantly higher weight loss (19.6%) compared to the dietary counseling group (4.1%) at 6%, with a risk ratio of 4.75 (95% CI: 1.68, 13.45). Retention rates were similar at 24 weeks (83.5% for GSLiM and 82.5% for the comparison group). GSLiM was associated with significant improvements in total weight self-efficacy, negative emotions, physical discomfort, MDPSS friend subscale, and all domains of quality of life. The comparison group experienced a reduction in negative self-thoughts. No significant between-group differences were found for systolic or diastolic blood pressure at any of the time intervals assessed (baseline to 12th week, 13th to 24th week, baseline to 24th week, and 25th week to 36th week). Physical activity, psychological, and quality of life scores were measured from baseline to 24th week and from 25th week to 36th week, but no other significant mean differences between groups were observed during these periods. The results suggest that GSLiM may be more effective than dietary counseling in promoting weight loss and improving certain psychological and quality of life outcomes. Source: [PMC4990415]
text: Group Support Lifestyle Modification (GSLiM) significantly reduces physical discomfort more than dietary counseling, as shown in a study (PMC4990415). GSLiM also led to greater weight loss and improvements in psychological and quality of life outcomes.

memory:
A study compared an intensified anticipatory guidance program with a routine program to assess their impact on nonurgent emergency department (ED) visits and knowledge scores in newborns during the first month of life. Of 323 participants, 24% had at least one nonurgent ED visit. The intervention group (n=170) had 21% (35/170) of such visits, while the control group (n=153) had 27% (41/153), with no statistically significant difference (p=0.12). Subgroup analyses based on marital status, education, maternal age, ethnicity, and number of children also showed no significant differences (data not shown). 

Participants were predominantly Hispanic (68%), single (61%), had incomplete high school education (44%), and 39% were primiparous. There was no statistically significant difference in within-subject changes in knowledge scores between the two groups. Follow-up data were incomplete, with 44% (n=74) of the intervention group and 40% (n=61) of the control group not contacted. The study concludes that nonurgent ED visits for newborns are common and that the intensified anticipatory guidance program did not significantly reduce these visits or improve knowledge scores compared to routine guidance.
text: The intensified anticipatory guidance program did not significantly affect baseline characteristics compared to the routine program (p=0.12). No differences were found in demographics, education, or other factors.

memory: A study compared Gallium maltolate (GaM) to clarithromycin + rifampin (CLR+R) in foals with Rhodococcus equi infection. Mortality was similar between groups, with four foals dying from R. equi-related complications. One GaM-treated foal died from septic mesenteric lymphadenitis and intestinal entrapment after 15 days, while one CLR+R-treated foal died during anesthesia from respiratory failure due to pneumonia, and another CLR+R-treated foal died after 21 days from severe pneumonia and enteritis. GaM-treated foals had a 70% resolution rate (14/20), compared to 74% (25/34) for CLR+R, but noninferiority of GaM was not conclusively demonstrated. However, excluding results from a noncompliant farm showed GaM was noninferior to CLR+R. Lesion size was analyzed as a binary variable (≥27 mm or <27 mm), with similar resolution rates in both groups for smaller lesions. For larger lesions, GaM-treated foals had a lower resolution rate than CLR+R-treated foals, though the difference was not statistically significant. Logistic regression was used to assess the interaction between treatment and lesion size, with lesion size categorized as a binary variable due to non-linear association in the logit model.
text: Gallium maltolate showed a noninferior resolution rate (70%) compared to clarithromycin + rifampin (74%) for resolving lesions >27 mm in foals with Rhodococcus equi infection, though the difference was not statistically significant. Noninferiority was suggested when excluding noncompliant farms. (Source: Study on GaM vs CLR+R in R. equi-infected foals)

memory: A study compared two surgical approaches for focal cleaning with posterior internal fixation in period I: group A (mini-open anterior approach) and group B (conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach). Both groups showed significant improvement in VAS scores from preoperative to last follow-up (p<0.01), with group A demonstrating better postoperative VAS scores than group B (p<0.05). No significant differences were found between groups in Cobb angle or ESR. Frankel classification improved significantly in both groups (p<0.01), but no difference was observed between the groups (p>0.05). At one week post-surgery, VAS scores improved significantly in group A compared to preoperative scores (p<0.05), but not in group B (p>0.05). Both groups had significantly lower Cobb angles and ESR at one week post-surgery and at last follow-up compared to preoperative values (p<0.01). Group A had shorter hospitalization time and reduced blood loss compared to group B, though these differences were not statistically significant. Anal exsufflation time was significantly shorter in group A (1.21±0.48 days) compared to group B (2.12±0.82 days) (p<0.05). Liver function improved following adjustments and liver treatment.
text: The mini-open anterior approach (group A) significantly reduced anal exsufflation time compared to the conventional extraperitoneal approach (group B) (1.21±0.48 vs. 2.12±0.82 days, p<0.05).
intervention: The mini-open anterior approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group A
comparator: conventional anterior extraperitoneal approach focal cleaning combined with posterior internal fixation in period I - group B

memory: In a study [PMC2650992], 100 patients undergoing breast lumpectomy with axillary dissection were randomized into a fibrin glue group (N=50) and a control group (N=50). Primary outcomes included drainage duration, total drain output, and seroma incidence. No significant differences were found overall between the groups. However, a subgroup analysis showed that in patients undergoing level II or III axillary dissection, fibrin glue significantly reduced drainage duration (3.5 vs. 4.7 days; p=0.0006) and total drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255). No significant difference in seroma incidence was observed between the groups. These findings suggest that fibrin glue may offer benefits in reducing drainage duration and total drain output in patients undergoing more extensive axillary dissection (level II or III) during breast lumpectomy. The study highlights the potential role of fibrin glue in specific subpopulations undergoing more extensive procedures, though it did not show overall efficacy across all patients.
text: In a study (PMC2650992), fibrin glue did not significantly affect overall drain output in all patients. However, in those undergoing level II or III axillary dissection, fibrin glue significantly reduced total drain output (196 vs. 278 mL; p=0.0255).
intervention: fibrin glue group (glue sprayed onto the axillary dissection site)

memory: In a study comparing plasma exchange (PE) and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in children, the PE group had a shorter median duration of mechanical ventilation (MV) (11 days, IQR 11.0–13.0) compared to the IVIG group (13 days, IQR 11.3–14.5; p = 0.037). There was a trend toward shorter PICU stays in the PE group (p = 0.094), though not statistically significant. Recovery of unaided walking within four weeks after PICU discharge was similar between groups (95.2% in PE vs. 90% in IVIG; p = 0.606). Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups. A significant negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of MV was observed in the PE group (p = 0.037), but not in the IVIG group (p = 0.132). No significant treatment-related side effects were reported. The hospital stay was shorter in the PE group, though not statistically significant. Overall, a statistically significant negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of MV was observed (p = 0.024). Source: PMC3387601.
text: Plasma exchange (PE) showed a significant negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation (p = 0.037), unlike IVIG (p = 0.132). PE also reduced median ventilation duration (11 vs. 13 days; p = 0.037). Source: PMC3387601.
outcome: negative correlation between CSF protein and duration of mechanical ventilation

memory: A positive psychology-based intervention was compared to a wait-list control group in a study assessing its impact on children's emotional and behavioral outcomes. Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significant intervention × time interactions for positive emotions (F(1,313)=10.93, p=0.001), life satisfaction (F(1,313)=9.68, p=0.002), and empathy (F(1,313)=8.65, p=0.004). The intervention group showed significant improvements in positive emotions (d=0.38), life satisfaction (d=0.67), and empathy (d=0.34) from pre- to post-intervention, with no changes in the control group. Prosocial behavior also increased significantly in the intervention group (F(1,171)=7.29, p=0.004, d=0.66). Parent-reported data showed significant increases in positive emotions (F(1,171)=9.11, p=0.004, d=0.81). Subjective well-being and positive learning behaviors improved in the intervention group, while the control group showed no changes. No significant effects were observed for negative emotions or total mental health difficulties. A main effect of time was found for total mental health difficulties, with decreases in both groups. Age was included as a covariate due to its significant correlation with conduct problems. No significant interaction effects were found for negative emotions or total mental health difficulties. The study suggests that positive psychology interventions may enhance emotional well-being and prosocial behaviors in young children.
text: A positive psychology-based intervention significantly improved subjective well-being (life satisfaction, positive emotions) compared to a wait-list control (p<0.005, d=0.38–0.67). The control group showed no changes.

The GHSH intervention resulted in significant weight loss compared to no continued contact at 6 months (−1.35 kg, 95% CI: −2.24, −0.46, P=.003) and increased weekly moderate physical activity (0.56 sessions/week, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.96, P=.008). Accelerometer-assessed MVPA also increased significantly (24.16 minutes/week, 95% CI: 5.07, 43.25, P=.007). However, waist circumference differences were not statistically significant between groups (P=.115). 

Within the intervention group, significant reductions in body weight (−0.89 kg, 95% CI: −1.53, −0.25) and waist circumference (−1.34 cm, 95% CI: −2.31, −0.36) were observed from baseline. Dietary outcomes showed small but significant improvements in the intervention group for the FFBQ Fiber and Total Indices, while the control group experienced declines in vegetable and fruit intake. Other dietary outcomes remained stable in both groups.

Overall, the GHSH intervention led to favorable changes in weight, physical activity, and some dietary behaviors. However, waist circumference and other physical activity and dietary outcomes did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups.
text: The GHSH intervention significantly increased accelerometer-assessed MVPA by 24.16 minutes/week compared to no continued contact (P=.007). It also improved weight loss and moderate physical activity levels, though waist circumference differences were not significant.

memory: A study compared the effect of completing a computer tutorial in sequence (relevant) versus out of sequence (non-relevant) on student post-test scores. Students who completed the tutorial in sequence had significantly higher post-test scores overall (z-score 1.1 vs. 0.52; 95% CI +0.16, +0.93). For the Oral Rehydration Solutions (ORS) topic, students in the in-sequence group scored 19% higher (95% CI +7%, +31%) with a large Cohen's-d of 0.85 (95% CI 0.25, 1.5). However, for the Fever Without Source (FWS) topic, the improvement was only 6% (95% CI -3%, +16%) with a Cohen's-d of 0.38 (95% CI -0.20, +0.97), which was not statistically significant. The overall results indicate that the in-sequence condition had a consistent benefit, though not uniformly significant across topics. Students spent slightly more time on in-sequence tutorials (12.1 min vs. 10.5 min), but this difference was not statistically significant (95% CI -1.2, +4.5). Pre-test scores were not significantly different between groups. The study involved 92 students, with 41 in the in-sequence group. These findings suggest that the sequence of tutorials may influence knowledge gain, particularly for certain topics. Source: [PMC3517358]
text: Students who completed the ORS tutorial in sequence scored 19% higher (95% CI +7%, +31%) than those who did it out of sequence, with a large effect size (Cohen's-d = 0.85). Source: [PMC3517358]

memory: In a study comparing cinacalcet to control, the median intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) decreased by 42.3% in the cinacalcet group and 30.7% in the control group (P = 0.483). The proportion of patients achieving a 30% reduction in mean iPTH from baseline was similar between groups (48.5% vs. 51.5%, P = 1.000). Additionally, the proportion of patients reaching an iPTH target of 150–300 pg/ml during the efficacy assessment phase was not statistically different (24.3% vs. 18.2%, P = 0.764). Baseline iPTH levels were 729 pg/ml (518, 1424 pg/ml) in the cinacalcet group and 649 pg/ml (490, 1143 pg/ml) in the control group. During the efficacy assessment phase, iPTH levels were 421 pg/ml (267, 753 pg/ml) and 441 pg/ml (317, 663 pg/ml), respectively. These findings were presented in the context of mineral metabolic parameters, including calcium-phosphorus product, calcium, and phosphorus levels, as shown in Figure 2. No significant differences were found between the groups for these biochemical parameters.
text: Cinacalcet did not significantly differ from control in achieving the iPTH target of 150–300 pg/ml (24.3% vs. 18.2%, P = 0.764). Both groups showed similar reductions in iPTH levels, with no significant differences in mineral metabolic parameters.

memory: A clinical study involving 24 subjects evaluated the safety of Aequasyal® compared to three formulations (DC161-DP0291, DC161-DP0292, DC161-DP0293). All participants were included in the safety analysis. No clinically relevant abnormalities were observed during systemic or local examinations. No serious adverse events, discontinuations, or premature withdrawals were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were primarily gastrointestinal, with one occurrence each following application of DC161-DP0292 and its comparator. No significant differences in the incidence or type of TEAEs were observed between the products. The safety profile was consistent across all product comparisons, indicating no relevant differences in safety outcomes.
text: Aequasyal® demonstrated a safety profile comparable to DC161-DP0292, with no significant differences in treatment-emergent adverse events. No serious adverse events or discontinuations were reported, and all subjects completed the study.

memory: A study investigated sildenafil concentrations in relation to CYP2C9 and CYP3A4/3A5 phenotypes. Among CYP2C9 intermediate and poor metabolizers, significant associations with sildenafil levels were observed in Caucasians after adjusting for age, BMI, and ancestry PCs (P = 0.0165), but not in the overall population. No significant associations were found between CYP2C9 inferred phenotype and sildenafil concentration:dose ratio. CYP3A5 poor metabolizers showed higher sildenafil concentrations in Caucasians, though not statistically significant (P > 0.14). An exploratory analysis grouped Caucasians by CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 phenotypes, revealing that higher predicted metabolizing capacity correlated with lower sildenafil dose-adjusted concentrations (F test P = 0.0238). CYP3A4 intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios than extensive metabolizers at weeks 12 and 24 (P = 0.045), though not meeting corrected significance thresholds. All CYP3A4 intermediate metabolizers carried CYP3A4*22. Age and BMI were strongly associated with sildenafil concentration:dose ratios (P < 0.0001). Results were consistent across multiple timepoints and adjusted for covariates. Source: [PMC5656562].
text: CYP3A4 intermediate metabolizers had higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios than extensive metabolizers at weeks 12 and 24 (P = 0.045), though not meeting corrected significance thresholds. Source: [PMC5656562].

Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations induced strong IgG responses to subtype C CN54rgp140, with median titers rising from 900 (after HIV-DNA/MVA) to 8100 (after first CN54rgp140/GLA-AF) and 24,300 (after second CN54rgp140/GLA-AF). CN54rgp140-specific IgG concentrations increased significantly, from 0.861 μg/ml to 9.866 μg/ml after the first dose and 17.75 μg/ml after the second. These responses were significantly higher than those after HIV-MVA (p<0.0001). Among unprimed vaccinees, 2 of 5 developed responses after the first CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunization. No ADCC-mediating antibody responses were detected after two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations, despite one participant showing neutralizing activity against CM235 CRF01_AE.

Safety profile: Only 15% of participants (6/40) reported 8 non-solicited adverse events, all mild or moderate and unrelated to vaccination. One participant experienced severe but asymptomatic hypoglycaemia (glucose <2.24 mmol/L) seven days after the first CN54rgp140/GLA immunization. No HIV infections occurred during the 12-week observation period.
text: Two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations significantly increased IgG responses compared to baseline (p<0.0001), but no ADCC-mediating antibody responses were detected (PMC4871571).

Intervention: Biosimilar adalimumab vs. reference adalimumab.  
Efficacy: No statistically significant differences in ACR20, ACR50, or ACR70 responses between groups (Table 3). 95% confidence intervals provided for both groups.

text: Biosimilar adalimumab had no significant effect on bilirubin levels compared to reference adalimumab (PMC5215647). Total bilirubin remained stable in both groups, with no persistent changes observed.

memory:
In a study [PMC4153084], non-diabetic patients with mild Alzheimer's disease (AD) were treated with MSDC-0160 (150 mg/day, N=16) or placebo (N=13) for 12 weeks. The primary outcome was glucose metabolism measured by FDG-PET. No significant differences were found in pre-defined regions when referenced to the pons or whole brain. However, glucose metabolism referenced to the cerebellum was maintained in MSDC-0160-treated participants, while it declined significantly in placebo patients in regions including anterior and posterior cingulate, and parietal, lateral temporal, and medial temporal cortices. Voxel-based analyses revealed additional FDG-PET differences related to MSDC-0160 treatment. 

Secondary outcomes included cognitive assessments: ADAS-Cog total score, 19-item cognitive test battery global cognitive summary z-score, and 7-item Executive Function battery summary z-score. No significant differences were observed between groups over the 12-week period. However, MSDC-0160 significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin levels (p<0.001), suggesting improved insulin sensitivity. Circulating hs-CRP and FFA levels decreased, though not significantly, consistent with the drug's pharmacology. 

The study did not detect significant cognitive improvements in the short term, but MSDC-0160 showed metabolic and metabolic marker benefits.
text: MSDC-0160 did not significantly improve cognitive test battery global cognitive scores compared to control in mild AD patients over 12 weeks [PMC4153084]. However, it showed metabolic benefits, including maintained glucose metabolism and increased adiponectin levels.
outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score

memory: In a 24-month randomized controlled trial (ChiCTR-PRC-09000401) involving 400 pre-diabetic patients, JinqiJiangtang (JQJT) tablets were evaluated for diabetes prevention compared to a placebo. At 12 months, the diabetes incidence was 16.5% in the JQJT group versus 28.9% in the placebo group (P=0.005). This benefit was sustained at 24 months, with 20.3% versus 32.8% incidence (P=0.007). The hazard ratio (HR) for progression to diabetes was 0.58 (95% CI 0.384–0.876, P=0.010), suggesting a 42% lower risk in the JQJT group. At 12 months, 41.8% of JQJT patients achieved normalized blood glucose compared to 27.8% in the placebo group, with an HR of 1.41 (95% CI 1.002–1.996, P=0.0049). Safety data showed 8 adverse events overall (5 in placebo, 3 in JQJT), with no significant difference in incidence (2.8% vs. 1.7%, P=0.501). Baseline characteristics were generally balanced, except for a slightly younger mean age in the JQJT group (55.49 vs. 53.49 years, P=0.036). The study indicates that JQJT may be effective in reducing diabetes progression in pre-diabetic individuals, with a favorable safety profile.
text: JinqiJiangtang tablets significantly reduced the risk of pre-diabetes progressing to diabetes compared to placebo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384–0.876, P=0.010) over 24 months. This effect was sustained, with lower diabetes incidence at both 12 and 24 months. Safety was comparable between groups. (Source: ChiCTR-PRC-09000401)
intervention: JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT tablets, a traditional Chinese patent medicine)
outcome: risk of converting from pre-diabetes to diabetes

memory: A study compared two clopidogrel administration strategies: group A (600 mg >6 h before CAG) and group B (600 mg in cath-lab after CAG, if PCI was performed). Periprocedural troponin elevation was 2.6% (group A) vs. 3.3% (group B; P = 0.475). Bleeding complications were higher in group A (3.5%) vs. group B (1.4%; P = 0.025), with an adjusted OR of 3.03 (95% CI 1.14–8.10; P = 0.027). Female gender (P = 0.001) and use of GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors (P = 0.027) were significant bleeding risk factors, with low platelet count near significance (P = 0.091). In PCI patients, bleeding complications were 7.1% (group A) vs. 0.7% (group B; P = 0.006). Periprocedural troponin elevation in PCI patients was 8.4% (group A) vs. 11.9% (group B; P = 0.316), and TIMI-flow <3 after PCI was 1.3% (group A) vs. 0% (group B; P = 0.499). Re-intervention within 7 days occurred in 0.7% (group A) vs. 1.4% (group B; P = 0.515). No significant differences were observed in the primary endpoint (periprocedural MI, death, stroke, or re-intervention) between groups.
text: Group A (clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG) had higher bleeding complications (3.5%) compared to group B (1.4%; P=0.025). In PCI patients, bleeding was 7.1% vs. 0.7% (P=0.006). Adjusted OR for bleeding was 3.03 (95% CI 1.14–8.10; P=0.027).
intervention: group A ('non-selective'—clopidogrel 600 mg >6 h before CAG;

In a study, four patients (40%) tested positive for SIBO via GBT. DKT did not affect bowel movement frequency or stool form. However, it significantly reduced the median total GSRS score (P < 0.001), as well as the indigestion and constipation subscales (P < 0.001). The overall treatment effect score improved significantly from 13 to 51 (P = 0.005).
