comparator: lightwand with WEI JET under direct laryngoscopy

memory: In a clinical study comparing Vitamin D plus calcium (VitD/Cal) with a placebo, baseline 25(OH)D levels were balanced between groups. Over 48 weeks, the VitD/Cal group showed significant increases in 25(OH)D levels, while the placebo group showed no significant changes. At week 24, the median 25(OH)D concentration in the VitD/Cal group increased by 27.5 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = 15.0, 38.0 ng/mL) from baseline (P < .001). By week 48, the increase was 24.2 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = 14.6, 37.8 ng/mL) (P < .001). In contrast, the placebo group had minimal changes: –0.8 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = –5.9, 4.9 ng/mL) at week 24 and 0.6 ng/mL (Q1, Q3 = –6.1, 4.3 ng/mL) at week 48. These results demonstrate the efficacy of VitD/Cal in significantly raising 25(OH)D levels over time compared to the placebo. Source: [PMC5726464] (Results > Baseline Demographics, Table 2).
text: Vitamin D plus calcium supplementation significantly increases 25(OH)D levels compared to placebo. At week 24, the median increase was 27.5 ng/mL (P < .001), and at week 48, 24.2 ng/mL (P < .001). Placebo showed minimal changes. Source: [PMC5726464].

memory: In a clinical study comparing cilostazol to a placebo, participants received 50 mg of cilostazol for 2 weeks, followed by 100 mg for 6 weeks. The primary outcome was the level of soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1). Cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to the placebo, with a mean difference of 105.18 ng/dL (95% CI 10.65 to 199.71), as reported in Table 3 of the source article [PMC3733748]. No significant differences were found between the cilostazol and placebo groups for other outcomes, including brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), adiponectin, interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and soluble intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (sICAM-1). These results suggest that cilostazol specifically reduces sVCAM-1 levels without affecting other inflammatory or vascular markers.
text: Cilostazol significantly reduced sVCAM-1 levels compared to placebo by 105.18 ng/dL (95% CI 10.65 to 199.71), as reported in [PMC3733748]. No other markers were significantly affected.
intervention: cilostazol group (50 mg for 2 weeks, 100 mg for 6 weeks)
outcome: soluble vascular cellular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) level

memory: Source article [PMC2652457] evaluated Computer Assisted Learning (CAL) against an information leaflet for autism identification training in students. The CAL group demonstrated significantly higher retention performance scores (p = 0.02, 95% CI = 0.83–12.19, effect size = 0.8) and greater enjoyment (p = 0.04, 95% CI = 0.03–2.75, effect size = 0.7) compared to the control group. However, no significant difference was found in confidence levels for identifying children with autism (p = 0.39, 95% CI = -1.80–0.72, effect size = -0.3). The study suggests that CAL improves knowledge retention and enjoyment in autism identification training but does not significantly enhance confidence in identification. These results indicate that CAL may be beneficial in educational settings for improving engagement and knowledge retention. However, further research is needed to explore its impact on confidence in autism identification.
text: Computer-assisted learning (CAL) significantly increases the level of enjoyment compared to control (p = 0.04, effect size = 0.7) [PMC2652457].

memory: In a study comparing the Spiromax inhaler with Easyhaler and Turbuhaler, participants assessed their satisfaction with five device features: 'overall ease of use', 'quality of PIL instructions', 'preparing the dose', 'inhaling procedure', and 'clarity of dose counter'. Spiromax was rated significantly higher than both Easyhaler and Turbuhaler for all features except 'inhaling procedure', where no significant differences were found between the devices. Turbuhaler scored significantly higher than Easyhaler for 'quality of PIL instructions' (p<0.003), while Easyhaler was rated significantly higher than Turbuhaler for 'clarity of dose counter' (p<0.015). These findings were reported in the 'Device Preference And Satisfaction' section of the source article [PMC4809147].
text: Spiromax was rated significantly higher than Easyhaler and Turbuhaler for 'overall ease of use', 'quality of PIL instructions', 'preparing the dose', and 'clarity of dose counter', except for 'inhaling procedure' where no differences were found. Turbuhaler scored higher than Easyhaler for 'quality of PIL instructions', while Easyhaler scored higher for 'clarity of dose counter' [PMC4809147].

memory: Source: PMC5560514. A clinical study compared Monovisc, Cingal, and saline for knee osteoarthritis, with a focus on the anteromedial subgroup over 3 weeks. memory: A clinical study investigated the effect of phone calls as an intervention to reduce treatment discontinuation. Participants were divided into two groups: one received phone calls, and the other did not. The group that received phone calls had significantly fewer patients discontinue treatment (4 patients) compared to the group that did not receive calls (30 patients), with a p-value of less than 0.0094. These results suggest that the phone call intervention may be effective in improving treatment adherence. The findings are detailed in the source article [PMC2974815].
text: The "phone calls" group had significantly fewer discontinued treatments (4 patients) compared to the "no phone calls" group (30 patients), with a p-value < 0.0094, suggesting phone calls may improve treatment adherence [PMC2974815].

memory: A study compared skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding (intervention) with no skin-to-skin contact (control) to assess the time for infants to begin latching on. The intervention group (n=31) had a median latching time of 2.0 weeks (Q1 = 1.0, Q3 = 3.7), while the control group (n=33) had a median latching time of 4.7 weeks (Q1 = 2.0, Q3 = 8.0). The difference in latching time between the two groups was statistically significant (p-value = 0.020). A Kaplan-Meier time-to-event curve further illustrated the group differences, with a Peto-Peto-Wilcoxon test yielding a p-value of 0.017. These results indicate that skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding is associated with a significantly shorter time to latching on in infants. Source: PMC3606616.
text: Skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding significantly reduces the time infants begin latching on compared to no contact (p=0.020; Peto-Peto-Wilcoxon p=0.017). The median latching time was 2.0 weeks vs. 4.7 weeks. Source: PMC3606616.
comparator: no skin-to-skin contact during the breastfeeding
outcome: registered time when infants began latching on

memory: At 30 months post-baseline, the Internet-based self-management (IBSM) group demonstrated significant improvements in asthma-related quality of life (difference of 0.29; 95% CI 0.01–0.57) and better asthma control (difference of -0.33; 95% CI -0.61 to -0.05) compared to the control group. These positive outcomes were sustained over time. However, no significant differences were found between the IBSM group and the control group regarding inhaled corticosteroid dosage or lung function, as measured by forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1). The results indicate that IBSM may offer long-term benefits for asthma-related quality of life and control but does not appear to influence medication use or lung function metrics. Source: PMC3785973.
text: Internet-based self-management support did not significantly affect inhaled corticosteroid dosage compared to control (PMC3785973).

memory:
Source: [PMC5746685]  
A 12-month RCT compared a basic and enhanced web-based weight loss maintenance (WLM) program in 227 adults (44% male, mean age 42.3 ± 10.1 years, mean BMI 30.4 ± 4.1 kg/m²). Participants were randomized and followed using intention-to-treat analysis with last observation carried forward. The primary outcome was weight rebound, with no significant difference between the basic (1.3%) and enhanced (1.5%) groups. BMI change was also similar between groups (basic: −0.5 (1.9) kg/m², enhanced: −0.5 (1.6) kg/m², p = 0.93). Secondary outcomes showed minimal differences. The study concluded that both programs were effective in preventing weight regain over one year, with no added benefit from the enhanced program.
text: A 12-month RCT (PMC5746685) found no significant difference in weight rebound between enhanced and basic web-based weight loss maintenance programs. Both groups had similar BMI changes, suggesting both programs are equally effective in preventing weight regain over one year.

Intervention: Single sustained inflation (SI) compared to conventional ventilation and consecutive SI.  
Outcome: Cerebral cortex blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation.  
Results: Single SI caused a more rapid and greater increase in cerebral blood flow (CaBF) (p = 0.01) but decreased below other groups by 10 minutes, potentially due to higher cerebral oxygen delivery (p = 0.01). Single SI was associated with increased blood-brain barrier disruption, as indicated by a higher number of blood vessel profiles showing plasma protein extravasation (p = 0.001). No differences in CaBF or cerebral oxygen delivery were observed between multiple SI and no SI groups.
text: Single sustained inflation (SI) significantly increased blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation compared to conventional ventilation and consecutive SI (p = 0.001) [PMC4713062].
outcome: numbers of blood vessel profiles with plasma protein extravasation

memory: In a study comparing the Language Enhanced Attention and Focus MI training condition (MI-LEAF) to baseline, the effect of training condition on client CT frequency in treatment sessions was not significant at the 3-month follow-up (b = −0.0857, SE = 0.0923, 95% CI [0.765, 1.102), T = −0.929, p = 0.355), contradicting the hypothesis. text: The MI-LEAF training condition significantly reduced "sustain talk" (ST) compared to baseline at 3-month follow-up (b = −0.1008, p < 0.001), consistent with hypotheses. This effect remained notable when combining all time points. Source: [PMC5539943]
intervention: Language Enhanced Attention and Focus MI training condition (MI-LEAF)

memory: A study assessed the impact of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) versus a placebo on Transient-Evoked Otoacoustic Emissions (TEOAE), focusing on changes in pure-tone average (PTA) and harmonic frequency analysis (HFA). Data were analyzed using ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis tests. ANOVA results revealed no significant differences between groups for changes in TEOAE PTA (F(2,31) = 0.133, P = 0.876) or TEOAE HFA (F(2,31) = 0.20, P = 0.819), as detailed in Tables 6 and 7 of the source article. The Kruskal-Wallis test, used to evaluate group medians for changes in TEOAE HFA, also found no significant differences (Kw(2) = 4.04, P = 0.133). These results indicate that neither LLLT nor the placebo had a statistically significant effect on TEOAE PTA or HFA in this study. Source: PMC3658388.
text: A study found no significant effect of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) compared to placebo on TEOAE pure-tone average (PTA) (F(2,31) = 0.133, P = 0.876). Source: PMC3658388.

memory: In a clinical study comparing vildagliptin to placebo, vildagliptin significantly reduced HbA1c levels compared to placebo. The vildagliptin group had a mean decrease of −0.5 ± 0.1% (P < .0001) from a baseline of 6.5 ± 0.1%. In contrast, the placebo group showed a small numerical increase of 0.2 ± 0.1% from a baseline of 6.4 ± 0.1% (P = .14). The between-group difference was significant, with vildagliptin outperforming placebo by −0.7 ± 0.1% (P < .001). These results indicate that vildagliptin effectively lowers HbA1c levels compared to placebo. Source: [PMC4399299].
text: Vildagliptin significantly reduces glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) compared to placebo. The vildagliptin group showed a mean decrease of −0.5 ± 0.1% (P < .0001), while the placebo group had a slight increase of 0.2 ± 0.1% (P = .14). The between-group difference was −0.7 ± 0.1% (P < .001). Source: [PMC4399299].

memory: In a study comparing paricalcitol (PAR) and calcifediol (CAL), serum iPTH levels were significantly lower in the PAR group at 6 months (76 ± 55 pg/ml vs. 101 ± 55 pg/ml; P = 0.0036). A per-protocol analysis showed a statistically significant difference in the proportion of patients with a reduction in iPTH levels (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008). However, no significant difference was found in the proportion of patients with ≥30% reduction in iPTH levels (95.1% vs. 88.4%; P = 0.26). Additionally, a higher proportion of patients in the PAR group had iPTH levels within the target range of 70–110 pg/ml (14.6% vs. 25.6% in the CAL group; P = 0.056). These findings suggest PAR may be more effective in reducing serum iPTH levels compared to CAL, though differences in achieving ≥30% reduction and target range were not statistically significant. Source: PMC5762965.
text: Paricalcitol significantly reduced serum iPTH levels compared to calcifediol at 6 months (P = 0.0036). A higher proportion of patients in the paricalcitol group had reduced iPTH levels (6.9% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.008). However, differences in ≥30% reduction and target range were not significant. memory: In a study comparing nebivolol and atenolol, VH-IVUS results indicated that nebivolol significantly reduced external elastic membrane (EEM) area (P=0.02) and lumen area (P=0.004) compared to atenolol. No significant differences were observed between the two β-blockers in plaque composition or the number of thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFAs) per vessel (PMC4859395). Over time, nebivolol was associated with an increase in plaque area (P<0.001), while atenolol showed plaque regression (P=0.047). However, the difference in plaque area changes between the two groups was not statistically significant (P=0.27). The P values also relate to comparisons of three wall shear stress (WSS) categories between the β-blockers, reflecting mechanical stress on the vessel wall from blood flow. These findings suggest that both β-blockers influence vascular remodeling, but through different mechanisms: nebivolol may promote plaque progression, whereas atenolol favors plaque regression, though the overall difference remains non-significant.

memory: A 24-week study compared vonoprazan (10 mg and 20 mg) to lansoprazole 15 mg for maintaining healed erosive esophagitis (EE). memory: A study compared 10-mm transumbilical and 5-mm transabdominal approaches in a clinical setting. Intact tube detection was significantly higher in the transumbilical group (18 cases) compared to the transabdominal group (3 cases), with a P-value < 0.001 and an odds ratio of 51.0 (95% CI: 7.56-343.73). No intra-operative rupture of the homemade retrieval bag was observed during specimen extraction. Rescue analgesia was required for four patients in the transumbilical group and three in the transabdominal group. No surgical complications were reported, and all patients were discharged on postoperative day 1. At three months post-surgery, all patients were followed up at the clinic and had recovered without complications such as post-side herniation. The findings suggest that the transumbilical approach may offer advantages in terms of intact tube detection, although both approaches were associated with minimal complications and similar recovery profiles.

SRT2104 resulted in a modest body weight reduction of 0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236), with a trend for treatment-by-period interaction (p=0.080). However, HbA1c levels increased by 0.48% (95% CI 0.26% to 0.70%, p=0.004), and plasma fructosamine levels rose by 33.41 μmol/L (95% CI 20.24 to 46.58 μmol/L, p<0.001). memory: In a study [PMC5448649], advanced biliary tract cancer (aBTC) patients received a peptide vaccine (PPV) alone or with low-dose cyclophosphamide (CPA). Peptides were selected based on pre-existing IgG responses and delivered subcutaneously. The PPV/CPA group showed stronger T cell responses compared to PPV alone. Progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly longer in the PPV/CPA group (median 6.1 months vs. 2.9 months; HR: 0.427; P = 0.008), as was overall survival (OS) (median 12.1 months vs. 5.9 months; HR: 0.376; P = 0.004). In the PPV-only group, increased plasma IL-6 levels post-vaccination were observed, potentially suppressing antigen-specific T cell responses. The addition of low-dose CPA to PPV appears to enhance clinical outcomes in aBTC patients, likely by mitigating IL-6-driven immune suppression.

memory: In a study comparing real prefrontal rTMS with sham rTMS, participants were asked to identify which session was real and which was sham [Source: PMC3089991]. Only 40% correctly identified the real session (p = 0.27), indicating that the sham rTMS condition was effectively indistinguishable from the real one in terms of face and scalp sensations. This suggests that the sham-TMS system successfully mimics the sensory experience of real rTMS, reducing placebo effects related to sensory perception. The result supports the internal validity of the study by ensuring that any observed effects are more likely due to the rTMS intervention itself rather than differences in sensory experience between conditions. This finding is important for interpreting outcomes related to sensory responses and for ensuring the reliability of rTMS studies that use sham controls.

memory: In a study comparing lifestyle-induced weight loss (Intervention: Active Body Control) to a baseline (Comparator: baseline), the effect on metabolic parameters was analyzed. Lifestyle-induced weight loss did not alter circulating FGF-19 levels, as shown in Fig. 2a. However, total GLP-1 levels decreased significantly (p = 0.003; Fig. 2b). memory: In a sub-study of 85 patients, 77 had sildenafil concentration measurements at week 12 (n = 71) and week 24 (n = 66). CYP3A4 intermediate metabolizers (IM), all of whom were CYP3A4*22 carriers, showed higher sildenafil concentration:dose ratios compared to extensive metabolizers (EM) at both week 12 and week 24. The difference between IM and EM was statistically significant in repeated measures analysis (P = 0.045) after adjusting for age, BMI, and genetic ancestry principal components. memory: In a study [PMC4871571], vaccinees who received two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations were evaluated for ADCC-mediating antibody responses compared to baseline. Results indicated that none of the unprimed volunteers who received two immunizations developed ADCC-mediating antibody responses. However, one of four unprimed volunteers exhibited neutralizing activity against CM235 CRF01_AE following the second immunization, as measured by the IMC/PBMC assay. Statistical analysis was conducted using the Mann-Whitney test. Colored dots represent unprimed vaccinees who received only two immunizations, while black dots represent those who received seven vaccinations. The data suggest that two CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations in unprimed individuals do not elicit ADCC responses, although some neutralizing activity was observed.

memory: A clinical trial evaluated MSDC-0160's effect on cognitive function compared to a control, using ADAS-Cog total score, a 19-item cognitive test battery global cognitive summary z-score, and a 7-item Executive Function battery summary z-score at baseline, 12 weeks of treatment, and a 4-week follow-up. No significant differences in cognitive performance were observed between groups over the short time frame, as anticipated due to the trial's duration [24]. However, MSDC-0160 treatment significantly increased high molecular weight adiponectin levels (p<0.001), indicating improved insulin sensitivity. Trends toward decreased high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and free fatty acid (FFA) levels were also noted, consistent with the expected effects of an insulin sensitizer [24]. The study's results suggest that while cognitive changes were not detected, MSDC-0160 had beneficial metabolic effects.

memory: A 12-month trial (ChiCTR-PRC-09000401) evaluated JinqiJiangtang (JQJT) tablets for diabetes prevention in 400 pre-diabetic patients across five centers. The primary endpoint was the incidence rate of diabetes mellitus. JQJT significantly reduced the risk of progressing from pre-diabetes to diabetes compared to placebo, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.384, 0.876; P = 0.010). Additionally, JQJT increased the probability of achieving normalized blood glucose by 1.41-fold (HR: 1.41; 95% CI: 1.002, 1.996; P = 0.0049). An intention-to-treat analysis showed that 16.5% of patients in the JQJT group developed diabetes, compared to 28.9% in the placebo group. These results suggest JQJT may have a preventative effect in reducing the progression of pre-diabetes to diabetes. Source: PMC5593818.

memory: A study compared two groups of patients receiving clopidogrel before or during coronary angiography (CAG). Group A (non-selective) received 600 mg clopidogrel more than 6 hours prior to CAG, while Group B (selective) received 600 mg only in the cath-lab if PCI was performed. The primary outcome was bleeding complications, which occurred in 3.5% of Group A versus 1.4% of Group B (P = 0.025). memory: In a study evaluating Daikenchuto (DKT) for gastrointestinal symptoms, 40% of participants had small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) confirmed via glucose breath test (GBT). DKT did not significantly alter bowel movement frequency or stool form. However, it significantly reduced the median total Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) score (P < 0.001), with notable improvements in the indigestion and constipation subscales (ANOVA P < 0.001). No significant changes were observed in acid reflux, diarrhea, or abdominal pain subscales. The median Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score for abdominal bloating decreased significantly from 76 to 30 (P = 0.005). The overall treatment effect score increased significantly from 13 to 51 (P = 0.005). Additionally, abdominal pain and bloating severity, as measured by a face scale, showed significant decreases (P = 0.039 and P = 0.008, respectively). These findings suggest that DKT may be effective in alleviating symptoms of indigestion, constipation, and bloating, even in patients with SIBO.
text: Daikenchuto significantly reduced indigestion and constipation scores compared to control (ANOVA P < 0.001). It also improved bloating and overall treatment effect scores, suggesting efficacy in alleviating these symptoms, even in SIBO patients.

memory: In a study comparing α-MSH treatment to controls, urine output was significantly lower in the α-MSH group during a ten-hour follow-up (p<0.05), as shown in Figure 2. No animals in either group became anuric. α-MSH also appeared to impair the recovery of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) during the same period, as indicated in Figure 3A. These findings suggest that α-MSH may negatively affect renal function parameters, specifically urine flow and GFR recovery, compared to control conditions. The results are derived from the "Results > Effect On Clinical Parameters" section of the source article [PMC3984270].

memory: A study compared telemonitored clinical care (TCC) with usual clinical care for CPAP use. Telemonitored patients used CPAP on 78% ± 22% of possible nights, while usual care patients used it on 60% ± 32% (P = .07). Although the difference in CPAP use was not statistically significant, telemonitored patients were significantly more likely to report continued CPAP use. No significant differences were found between groups in CPAP efficacy measures, including mask leak and the Apnea-Hypopnea Index. Both groups expressed high satisfaction with the care received, and patients in both groups rated themselves as “not concerned” about the wireless monitoring of their CPAP data (Source: PMC1874716, Abstract > Results).

memory: A clinical study [PMC2758835] compared manual therapy with usual care in reducing headache frequency, pain intensity, medication use, absenteeism, and need for additional professional help. Both interventions demonstrated significant improvements in primary and secondary outcomes, with no statistically significant differences between groups, suggesting similar effectiveness. However, the study faced recruitment challenges, resulting in a small sample size, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. Despite this limitation, the results suggest that both usual care and manual therapy are effective in managing headache-related outcomes. The small sample size should be considered when interpreting the study's conclusions.

memory: In a clinical study comparing frovatriptan and rizatriptan for the treatment of menstrually related migraine, frovatriptan showed superior efficacy in reducing migraine recurrence. At 24 hours post-treatment, the recurrence rate was significantly lower with frovatriptan (10%) compared to rizatriptan (32%), with a p-value < 0.01, indicating a statistically significant difference. Additionally, the cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up period was significantly lower for frovatriptan, as illustrated in Figure 1 of the source article. These findings suggest that frovatriptan may be more effective than rizatriptan in preventing migraine recurrence in patients with menstrually related migraine. The results were reported in the "Results > Overall Efficacy Of Study Drugs" section of the source article, referenced as [PMC3208043].

memory: A clinical study compared the efficacy of prostaglandin gel alone (n=17) with prostaglandin gel combined with hygroscopic cervical dilators (n=23) for cervical ripening. No significant demographic differences were observed between the groups. After six hours, the combined therapy group showed a significantly greater change in Bishop score (3.6 vs. 2.1, P = 0.007) and a trend toward shorter induction time (21.7 vs. 26.4 hours, P = 0.085). memory: The Sonas programme showed significant improvements compared to the control group in aspects such as interest in past events, humour, and general knowledge, but no significant differences were observed in higher-level cognitive functions like remembering names, speech, communication success, or interest in objects. When stratified by MMSE scores (moderate and severe; cut-off of 10 points), the Sonas group demonstrated significant differences compared to the reading group at baseline (p = 0.026) and at follow-up (T0, p = 0.011; T1, p = 0.044) for those with MMSE scores of 0–10. memory: A study compared radiofrequency ablation (RFA), hepatic resection, and combination therapy in patients with metachronous liver metastases. No statistically significant differences in overall survival (OS) were observed between the groups (P = 0.330). Five-year OS rates were 14.3% for RFA, 34.6% for resection, and 22.9% for combination therapy. Disease-free survival (DFS) was significantly lower in the RFA group compared to the other groups (P = 0.037), with 5-year DFS rates of 6.4% for RFA, 16.2% for resection, and 18.4% for combination therapy. Among 148 patients with solitary liver metastases, 103 underwent RFA and 45 had resection. The 5-year OS rate was 47.6% in the RFA group and 56.0% in the resection group, though this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.308). These findings suggest that while RFA may offer comparable OS to resection in some subgroups, it is associated with worse DFS outcomes. Source: [PMC3204557]
text: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is associated with worse 5-year disease-free survival (DFS) compared to hepatic resection (6.4% vs. 16.2%, P = 0.037). Source: [PMC3204557].

memory: A clinical study with 13 participants evaluated the effects of pomegranate juice (PJ) on blood pressure and vascular function. The PJ used contained 5.8 mg of anthocyanins per 100 ml. The study found a significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (SBP) by approximately 7% (P = 0.013) and a decrease in diastolic blood pressure (DBP) by about 6% (P = 0.010) following the intervention compared to baseline measurements. However, flow-mediated dilation (FMD), a marker of vascular function, showed a 20% change that was not statistically significant (P = 0.172). These results indicate that pomegranate juice may help reduce blood pressure, but its effect on vascular function remains inconclusive based on this study. Source: [PMC3933059]

memory: A clinical study compared the efficacy of recombinant follicle-stimulating hormone (r-FSH) combined with recombinant luteinizing hormone (rLH) versus r-FSH combined with human menopausal gonadotropin (HMG) in reproductive outcomes. The findings showed no significant differences between the groups in follicle count, total oocytes retrieved, or M2 oocytes (p > 0.05), and fetal quality was similar. However, the rFSH + HMG group had a significantly higher total number of fetuses compared to the rFSH + rLH group (p = 0.02). Fertility outcomes, including live birth rate, chemical pregnancy rate, and clinical pregnancy rate, were significantly better in the rFSH + HMG group (p < 0.05). These results suggest that while both treatment regimens yield comparable follicular and oocyte outcomes, rFSH + HMG may be more effective in achieving successful pregnancy and live birth outcomes. The study was published in the PMC database under reference [PMC5601935].
text: The effect of r-FSH + rLH versus r-FSH + HMG on the number of oocytes or M2 oocytes showed no significant difference (p > 0.05). However, r-FSH + HMG resulted in better pregnancy outcomes. Source: [PMC5601935].
intervention: Recombinant- follicle stimulating hormone (r-FSH) plus recombinant-luteinizing hormone (rLH)

memory: In a study [PMC3931696], the effect of Misoprostol + Celecoxib on potassium excretion was compared to a vehicle alone. memory: In a clinical study comparing Irinotecan with high-dose 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin (ILF) to Etoposide with 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin (ELF), differences in toxicity were observed. Withdrawals due to treatment-related toxicity were minimal, with only one patient from each group withdrawing. However, five patients on ILF and three on ELF withdrew consent or refused further treatment. Haematological toxicities were generally low, except for neutropenia, which was reported in 57% of ELF recipients. Gastrointestinal toxic events were more common with ILF, particularly diarrhoea, affecting 18% of patients, compared to none in the ELF group. Alopecia was more frequently reported in the ELF group, with 28% experiencing grade 3/4 alopecia, versus only 5% in the ILF group. These findings are from the Safety section of the Results in source article [PMC2361806].

memory: In a study [PMC5019971], maraviroc intensification was compared to an unchanged cART regimen, with CD8+ T cell CCR5 expression as the primary outcome. After 8 weeks of maraviroc treatment, FMD increased by 1.15% (IQR −0.25 to 1.70) in the intervention group, compared to −0.42% (IQR −1.41 to 0.56) in the control group (p = 0.079). Due to maraviroc's 13-hour half-life, the study omitted a washout period. A carry-over effect was observed, with CD8+ CCR5+ T cell expression in control period 2 (C2) showing a significant difference between week 16 and baseline (16.3 vs. 8.3; p = 0.021). To address this, the analysis compared intervention periods (INT1 + INT2) to control period C1, where patients had not yet received maraviroc, to minimize bias from carry-over. The study design focused on comparing the intervention effect against a control period prior to maraviroc exposure.

outcome: CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells

memory: Source article [PMC5695311] evaluated the efficacy of intensive sound masking therapy for tinnitus using the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) as the primary outcome. The study compared an effective subgroup receiving the intervention with a baseline comparator group. Although no significant difference in THI scores was found post-intervention between the groups, pre- and post-intervention THI score changes were significantly different (19.10 vs 0.98, t=12.54, P<0.001). The effective group showed a significant reduction in THI scores (t=−14.07, P<0.001), while the non-effective group did not (t=−1.98, P=0.054). To identify predictors of treatment effectiveness, variables significant between effective and non-effective groups were analyzed using logistic regression. Due to audiometric configuration being divided into four sub-groups, pair comparisons were conducted to estimate these factors. The study aimed to determine which factors could predict a positive response to sound masking therapy for tinnitus.
text: Intensive sound masking therapy significantly reduced THI scores in the effective subgroup compared to baseline (t=−14.07, P<0.001), while the non-effective subgroup showed no significant change (t=−1.98, P=0.054). Source: PMC5695311.

memory: A clinical study compared the Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) with oral norethisterone acetate (NET) in terms of regression rates and hysterectomy rates. At 3 months, the regression rate was significantly higher in the LNG-IUS group (67.8%) compared to the NET group (47.5%), with a relative risk (RR) of 1.42. This trend continued at 6 months (79.7% vs. 60.7%, RR 1.31) and 12 months (88.1% vs. 55.7%, RR 1.58), as assessed by intention-to-treat analysis. Although the regression rates were higher for LNG-IUS, the median time to regression was similar between the groups, with both reaching regression at 3 months. However, the hysterectomy rate during the follow-up period was significantly higher in the NET group (57.4%) compared to the LNG-IUS group (22%), with a p-value < 0.001. These findings indicate that the LNG-IUS may be more effective in achieving regression and reducing the need for hysterectomy compared to oral NET. Source: PMC3644688.

memory: A study compared T-EO and Af-EO formulations to sterile water (control) in reducing BV levels after 4 days of treatment [PMC5703870]. Both essential oil treatments significantly reduced BV levels compared to the control (P < 0.001). The 4D-T-EO group had BV levels of 26.27 ± 14.61%, and the 4D-Af-EO group showed 31.08 ± 16.52%, compared to 51.35 ± 5.38% in the 4D-WATER group. These results indicate that both T-EO and Af-EO were more effective than the control in reducing BV levels. Additionally, BV levels were consistently higher in outer layers than in inner layers across all groups, suggesting differences in formulation distribution across tissue layers. This may be relevant to their efficacy and penetration characteristics. The findings support the potential of both essential oil formulations as effective treatments for reducing BV levels. Further research is needed to explore their mechanisms of action and layer-specific effects.

memory: A study compared home-based training with telemonitoring to centre-based training in cardiac rehabilitation (CR). memory: In a clinical study comparing linagliptin to a control group, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) was measured at 24 weeks. Baseline median UACR was similar between groups: 73.8 mg/g Cr (range 30.1–2,534.4) for linagliptin and 80.5 mg/g Cr (range 30.9–1,538.2) for placebo. After 24 weeks, adjusted geometric mean UACR showed a significantly greater reduction in the linagliptin group (−32% [95% CI −42 to −21]; P < 0.05) compared to placebo (−6% [95% CI −27 to +23]). The between-group difference was −28% (95% CI −47 to −2; P = 0.0357). The albuminuria-lowering effect of linagliptin was evident as early as 12 weeks, with a −29% reduction (95% CI −40 to −17; P < 0.05) compared to a −6% reduction in the placebo group. However, the between-group difference at 12 weeks was not statistically significant (−25% [95% CI −46 to +3]; P = 0.0750). These results suggest that linagliptin has a beneficial effect on reducing albuminuria compared to control.

memory: A study compared a mobiletype program, which monitors mood, stress, and daily activities, to an attention-control group monitoring only daily activities. memory: A study investigated the impact of face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) on residual depressive and anxiety symptoms compared to a placebo. Observer-reported depressive symptoms, measured using the Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD), showed a significant ABM type × ABM stimuli × time interaction (F(2,112) = 3.4, p = .04). Post hoc tests indicated a trend for face training effects (F(1,28) = 2.9, p = .09). Anxiety symptoms, assessed via the trait subscale of the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), demonstrated a similar specific effect of positive face ABM as observed for depressive symptoms (F(2,112) = 3.3, p = .05). Notably, the beneficial impact of positive face ABM was evident during follow-up (F(1,28) = 5.2, p = .03), with a significant reduction in anxious symptoms in the positive face ABM group (t(15) = 2.4, p = .03). memory: In an experimental model of mild extrapulmonary acute lung injury (ALI) with intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH), pressure support ventilation (PSV) was compared to pressure-controlled ventilation (PCV). PSV resulted in lower mean airway pressure than PCV, with no differences in peak airway or transpulmonary pressures. PSV reduced mRNA expression of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and type III procollagen, markers of inflammation and fibrogenesis, regardless of IAH presence. In the presence of IAH, PSV improved oxygenation and decreased alveolar collapse, interstitial edema, and diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) compared to PCV. PSV also increased surfactant protein B expression, important for alveolar stability. Additionally, PSV was associated with better lung function and morphology and reduced type 2 epithelial cell damage compared to PCV in the experimental model of ALI with IAH. These findings suggest that PSV may be a more beneficial ventilation strategy in ALI with IAH due to its anti-inflammatory effects and improved lung protection. Source: PMC5444773.

memory: A study assessed the effect of adding primaquine (PQ) to Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHP) on gametocyte prevalence. Gametocytemia was measured using both microscopy and Pfs25 RT-PCR. At baseline, 9% of participants had gametocytemia by microscopy, while 46% were positive by RT-PCR. Microscopic gametocytemia increased to 12% prior to PQ dosing on day 2. By day 7 post-treatment, the DHP + PQ group had a significantly lower rate of gametocyte carriage (2.1%) compared to the DHP-only group (15%), with a prevalence ratio of 0.12 (95% CI 0.02–0.9, p = 0.03). In the DHP + PQ group, only one of four individuals with gametocytemia on day 2 remained positive on day 7, and all were gametocyte-free by day 14. These findings suggest that adding PQ to DHP significantly reduces gametocyte carriage. Source: [PMC5462369]

memory: A study examined the effect of health warnings on alcohol consumption speed, comparing a text-based warning condition with a no-warning condition. The primary outcome was the duration of drinking. Results indicated that the 'no health warning' condition resulted in significantly faster consumption compared to both the text and pictorial warning conditions (p < .001). No significant difference in consumption speed was found between the text and pictorial warning conditions (p = .76). These findings suggest that the presence of a health warning label influences the rate of alcohol consumption more than the specific type of warning (text versus pictorial). The data are visualized in Fig. 1, which displays the mean duration of drinking as a function of the health-warning label.
text: The "Visual warning (text)" significantly reduces the speed of alcohol consumption compared to "No warning" (p < .001). There is no significant difference in consumption speed between text and pictorial warnings (p = .76).

memory: In a study using ZDSD rats, raloxifene was evaluated for its effects on diabetes prevention and bone properties compared to a vehicle-treated control group. Raloxifene-treated rats exhibited a reduced incidence of type 2 diabetes and significantly lower blood glucose levels than both diabetic and non-diabetic vehicle-treated rats. Regarding bone properties, raloxifene improved femoral toughness, likely due to enhanced energy absorption in the post-yield region of the stress-strain curve. Structural mechanical properties, including energy-to-failure, post-yield energy-to-failure, and post-yield displacement, were also improved in raloxifene-treated rats compared to both diabetic and non-diabetic vehicle-treated groups. These results suggest that raloxifene may help prevent diabetes onset and enhance bone material properties in diabetes-prone ZDSD rats. Source: PMC4171519.
text: Raloxifene improves femoral toughness compared to control in ZDSD rats, as evidenced by enhanced energy absorption and structural mechanical properties. This effect was observed alongside reduced diabetes incidence and lower blood glucose levels. Source: PMC4171519.

memory: A study (PMC3441280) assessed lithium release from proximal- and distal-release pellets and measured plasma lithium concentrations over 7 hours post-administration. Proximal-release pellets led to significantly higher lithium AUC compared to distal-release pellets (P = 0.001). Furthermore, proximal-release pellets containing ATP showed significantly lower lithium AUC than placebo-containing proximal-release pellets (P = 0.001). These findings suggest that the site of pellet disintegration in the gastrointestinal tract affects lithium absorption, with proximal placement resulting in higher plasma lithium levels. Supporting evidence includes individual plasma lithium concentration profiles provided in Additional file 2: Figure S2. The results emphasize the importance of pellet placement in influencing drug absorption and plasma drug concentrations.
text: Administration via proximal-release pellets significantly increases plasma lithium levels compared to distal-release pellets (P = 0.001). This highlights the impact of pellet placement on lithium absorption.

memory: In a study [PMC1868022], 39 women were divided into a control group with no intervention, and cervical vault lavage (CVL) samples were collected at enrollment and 2 weeks later. Inflammatory markers in CVL specimens, including IL-12 p70, TNF-α, IL-8, IL-6, IL-10, and IL-1β, were measured. Following a Pap smear, levels of IL-8, IL-1β, and IL-6 remained unchanged. However, markers of cell-mediated immunity (IL-12 p70 and TNF-α) and T cell regulation (IL-10) showed significant elevation. These results suggest that Pap smear procedures may influence specific inflammatory and immunoregulatory cytokine levels in cervical secretions, without affecting others. The findings highlight the potential impact of the procedure on immune responses in this context.
text: A Pap smear at enrollment significantly increases IL-10 levels compared to no intervention, as shown in a study (PMC1868022). This suggests the procedure influences immunoregulatory responses in cervical secretions.

memory: In a study involving 596 RA patients inadequately responding to methotrexate, SB4 (etanercept biosimilar) was compared to etanercept (ETN) [PMC5264222]. Patients were randomized into two groups: SB4 (N=299) and ETN (N=297). The primary endpoint was therapeutic equivalence, assessed by ACR20 response at week 24. In the per-protocol set, ACR20 response rates were 78.1% for SB4 and 80.3% for ETN. The 95% CI for the adjusted treatment difference was -9.41% to 4.98%, within the predefined equivalence margin of -15% to 15%, confirming therapeutic equivalence. Efficacy and pharmacokinetic outcomes were comparable between groups. Adverse events were similar, with 55.2% of SB4-treated and 58.2% of ETN-treated patients experiencing treatment-emergent adverse events. Notably, the development of antidrug antibodies up to week 24 was significantly lower in the SB4 group (0.7%) compared to the ETN group (13.1%). These results suggest SB4 is therapeutically equivalent to ETN in efficacy and safety, with a potential benefit in reducing antidrug antibody formation.
text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, is therapeutically equivalent to etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate, with similar ACR20 response rates (78.1% vs. 80.3%) and adverse events. SB4 showed a lower incidence of antidrug antibodies (0.7% vs. 13.1%) [PMC5264222].
outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: A study compared robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) with standard navigation in evaluating late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) encirclement at 6-month follow-up. Both groups showed T2W signal resolution to baseline, with LGE being the predominant signal. The robotic group had higher LGE encirclement (56% vs. 45%, P = 0.04) compared to the standard group. However, among arrhythmia-free patients, LGE encirclement was similar between groups (robotic 64% vs. standard 60%, P = 0.45). In patients with recurrences, LGE was significantly higher in the robotic group (43% vs. 30%, P = 0.001). At a mean 3-year follow-up, the robotic group required fewer procedures (1.3 vs. 1.9, P < 0.001) and had a higher success rate (80% vs. 75%). These findings suggest that robotic-assisted navigation may be associated with higher LGE encirclement in patients with recurrences, yet it leads to fewer long-term procedures. Source: [PMC4535555] Abstract > Methods And Results.

memory: In a crossover study involving 24 infants, the frequency of soft stools was compared between Nutrilon Omneo (new formula; NF) and standard formula (SF). Weekly defecation frequency was similar between the two formulas, with a mean of 5.5/week for NF and 5.9/week for SF (difference of means, -0.5; 95% CI, -1.6 to 0.6; p = 0.38). memory: A study [PMC4668172] found that Kegel exercises significantly improved pulmonary function parameters compared to a control group. The experimental group showed improvements in forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), peak expiratory flow (PEF), forced expiratory flow between 25% and 75% of FVC (FEF 25–75%), inspiratory capacity (IC), and maximum voluntary ventilation (MVV). These improvements were not observed in the control group. The intervention involved a Kegel exercises program, and outcomes were measured using pulmonary function tests. The results suggest that Kegel exercises may enhance respiratory function, indicating potential benefits for individuals with respiratory conditions. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings and explore their broader applicability. The study provides preliminary evidence that Kegel exercises could positively impact respiratory function, but additional studies are required to validate these results and understand their potential clinical implications.
text: A study (PMC4668172) found that Kegel exercises significantly improved peak expiratory flow (PEF) compared to a control group. The intervention enhanced various pulmonary function parameters, suggesting potential benefits for respiratory function. Further research is needed to confirm these findings.

memory: A clinical study compared peramivir (Rapiacta) and oseltamivir (Tamiflu) in treating influenza, focusing on days to symptom disappearance. The study included 43 participants in the oseltamivir group and an unspecified number in the peramivir group, with four censored cases in each group. The mean days for symptom disappearance were 5.26 ± 0.15 for peramivir and 5.38 ± 0.16 for oseltamivir, with no statistically significant difference (log-rank test, P = .65; χ² = 0.204). Total Symptom Scores (TSSs) were also evaluated. On day 2, TSSs were −2.5 for peramivir and −1.3 for oseltamivir, decreasing to −7.1 and −5.9 by day 5, respectively. However, no significant intergroup differences were found for TSSs (log-rank test, P = .69). The results indicate that both treatments had similar efficacy in reducing symptoms over time. Source: [PMC5534217].

memory: A study investigated diabetes risk in antidepressant users (ADM) compared to non-users across three groups: placebo, lifestyle intervention, and metformin. After adjusting for diabetes risk factors, continuous antidepressant use was associated with an increased risk of diabetes in the placebo (aHR 2.34, 95% CI 1.32–4.15) and lifestyle arms (aHR 2.48, 95% CI 1.45–4.22). In contrast, no significant association was found in the metformin group (aHR 0.55, 95% CI 0.25–1.19). These results suggest that antidepressant use may raise diabetes risk in individuals receiving either placebo or lifestyle interventions but not when metformin is used. The study was controlled, and the results are derived from the abstract's results section of the source article [PMC2992187].
text: Antidepressant use (ADM) is associated with increased diabetes risk in placebo and lifestyle arms (aHR 2.34 and 2.48, respectively), but not in metformin users (aHR 0.55). This suggests ADM may elevate diabetes risk in non-metformin groups. Source: [PMC2992187].

memory: In a study using cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) as an intervention, bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC) were administered to mice and compared with control mice. The primary outcomes included alveolar collapse and other lung-related parameters. BMDMC therapy improved survival in the CLP group and reduced lung elastance, alveolar collapse, tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellularity, and collagen fiber content. It also decreased interleukin-1β levels while increasing keratinocyte-derived chemokine and monocyte chemotactic protein-1 expression in lung tissue. These protective effects were observed across different ARDS models. However, BMDMC therapy increased the expression of intercellular adhesion molecule-1 and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 in lung tissue, with the response depending on the type of insult—LPS or CLP. The findings suggest that BMDMC therapy offers protective benefits in ARDS models, though adhesion molecule responses vary based on the injury type. Source: PMC3856598.
text: BMDMC therapy reduced alveolar collapse in CLP-induced ARDS models compared to control mice, improving survival and lung function. Source: PMC3856598.

Source: PMC5282794  
Intervention: Plastic cap  
Comparator: Metal cup  
Outcome: Pain response  
Section: Abstract > Results  

Infants born via vaginal operative delivery exhibited a significantly lower pain response when exposed to a plastic cap compared to a metal cup during ventouse delivery (p < 0.001). The pain response was lower than expected, and all infants fully recovered within 72 hours. These findings suggest that the type of delivery device may influence the perceived pain response in neonates. The results highlight the potential impact of non-invasive interventions on pain management in this population.
text: Infants undergoing vaginal operative delivery showed a significantly lower pain response with a plastic cap compared to a metal cup (p < 0.001). This suggests that the type of delivery device may influence neonatal pain perception.

memory: In a phase 2a trial, patients treated with the synthetic amyloid-β peptide (Aβ42) intervention AN1792 showed significantly less decline on the Disability Assessment for Dementia scale compared to those on placebo (p=0.015) after 4.6 years. memory: Source article [PMC4973627]: A study compared an intervention group (Physical activity + Healthy eating, n=502) with a control group and found that the intervention was associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality. memory: A study (PMC3467590) evaluated a web-based CME intervention with performance feedback and quality improvement tools compared to a control group, examining effects on clinical outcomes. The intervention did not show incremental benefit over time (group-by-time interaction, p=0.948). However, both groups demonstrated significant increases in care intensification for patients with poor glucose control (A1c >9%). In the intervention group, care intensification rates increased from 34.8% pre-intervention to 62.5% post-intervention (p=0.002). In the control group, intensification increased from 35.7% pre-intervention to 61.4% post-intervention (p=0.008). These results suggest that while the intervention did not offer additional benefit overall, both groups achieved meaningful improvements in care intensification for patients with poor glucose control. The study highlights the potential for general improvements in this subgroup, regardless of the intervention used.

memory: In a study [PMC4628236], diabetic mice showed elevated nitrotyrosine (NT) immunoreactivity in the left ventricular (LV) myocardium, indicating increased nitro-oxidative stress. Treatment with the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day, oral, 8 weeks) significantly reduced NT levels, normalizing them compared to placebo-treated diabetic mice. This suggests that cinaciguat mitigates nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic myocardium. Diabetic mice also exhibited increased expression of antioxidant enzymes, including HSP70a1, catalase, glutathione-reductase, and thioredoxin-1. However, in the cinaciguat-treated diabetic group (DiabCin), HSP70a1 and glutathione-reductase mRNA levels returned to those seen in healthy controls, indicating normalization of antioxidant enzyme expression. These results imply that cinaciguat not only reduces oxidative stress markers but also restores antioxidant pathways in diabetic hearts.
text: Cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks significantly reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic mice, as evidenced by decreased nitrotyrosine levels and normalization of antioxidant enzyme expression, compared to placebo [PMC4628236].
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

memory: In a clinical study comparing arformoterol to placebo in COPD patients, arformoterol demonstrated significant improvements in lung function and quality of life. Trough FEV1 and FVC improvements were greater with arformoterol compared to placebo, with least-squares mean changes from baseline of 0.051 L (P = .030) and 0.075 L (P = .018), respectively. Quality of life improvements were observed, with significant results in both the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire (P < .05). Regarding safety, a numerically higher percentage of patients on arformoterol (3.1%) experienced cardiac serious adverse events compared to placebo (2.4%), although the time-to-first cardiac serious adverse event was not significantly different between groups. These findings suggest that arformoterol provides clinical benefits in terms of lung function and quality of life for COPD patients, though its safety profile requires further investigation. memory: A study assessed the impact of diets containing Fructooligosaccharides (FOS) and Isoflavone + FOS on femoral bone strength, measured by bone breaking force. The intervention groups included a FOS diet (GF) and an Isoflavone + FOS diet (GIF), with a control group (GC) receiving a standard diet. The control group experienced a significant decrease in bone breaking force (p<0.05). Both FOS-based diets (GF and GIF) effectively prevented this decline, preserving bone strength (Fig. 2C; p<0.05). However, the addition of isoflavone to the FOS diet (GIF) did not provide any additional benefit over the FOS diet alone (GF) in terms of bone breaking force preservation. These findings suggest that FOS plays a key role in maintaining femoral bone strength under these dietary conditions, while isoflavone did not enhance this effect. The study highlights the potential protective role of FOS in preventing bone fragility. Source: [PMC3432828].

memory: Source article [PMC4330076] describes a study comparing antihypertensive responses to bisoprolol with losartan, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. A GWAS of ~630,000 SNPs identified three SNPs on chromosome 11—rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037—significantly associated with ASBP response to bisoprolol. memory: A clinical study compared desmopressin (group D) to placebo (group P) in terms of post-surgical bleeding and platelet changes. No significant difference was observed in post-surgical bleeding rates between the groups (359.3 ± 266.2 in group D vs. 406.3 ± 341.6 in group P; P = 0.208). memory: A clinical trial compared oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) with intravenous chemotherapy (dacarbazine or paclitaxel) in patients with advanced melanoma. memory: In a study published in [PMC4914255], D-serine administration was linked to a significant reduction in legal errors on the Groton Maze Learning Test, which evaluates spatial memory, learning, and problem-solving (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03). memory: A study assessed the impact of a Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) on sanitation behaviors, revealing that intervention villages had lower open defecation rates compared to control villages. The intervention promoted improved sanitation facilities, mostly JMP-defined latrines, with few rudimentary facilities. Among adults, 75% of households in intervention villages reported daily open defecation, compared to 84% in control villages for men (mean difference: 9.5%; p = 0.001) and 73% versus 83% for women (mean difference: 10%; p < 0.001). For children under 5, the rate was 84% in intervention villages versus 89% in control villages (mean difference: 5%; p = 0.014). Despite these reductions, they were smaller than the increase in improved sanitation facility availability. In intervention villages, 41% of households with improved sanitation facilities still reported daily open defecation by adults, compared to 28% in control villages with similar facilities. These findings suggest that while the TSC increased access to improved sanitation, it had a more limited impact on changing open defecation behaviors. Source: [PMC4144850].
text: The Total Sanitation Campaign reduced open defecation compared to control, with lower rates among adults (men: 75% vs. 84%, p=0.001; women: 73% vs. 83%, p<0.001) and children under 5 (84% vs. 89%, p=0.014). However, the behavioral change was smaller than the increase in sanitation facilities. Source: [PMC4144850].

memory: A 24-week, multicenter, randomized clinical trial involving 132 MS patients across six countries evaluated the efficacy of prolonged-release fampridine (PR-fampridine) versus placebo. The study focused on improvements in mobility and balance, assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) speed, the Multiple Sclerosis Walking Scale-12 (MSWS-12) score, and the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) total score. Patients receiving PR-fampridine demonstrated greater median improvements in all three outcomes compared to those on placebo. A higher proportion of PR-fampridine-treated patients achieved significant improvements at predefined MSWS-12 thresholds: ≥7 points (p = 0.0275), ≥8 points (p = 0.0153), and ≥9 points (p = 0.0088), as well as TUG speed thresholds of ≥10% (p = 0.0021) and ≥15% (p = 0.0262). These results indicate that PR-fampridine may offer meaningful improvements in mobility and balance for MS patients over 24 weeks. The findings were published in the Front section of the source article [PMC4749757].

memory: In a clinical study comparing oral ibandronate 50 mg to placebo, the median time to first skeletal event was 90.3 weeks for ibandronate and 64.9 weeks for placebo (P=0.089). While this difference was not statistically significant, multivariate Poisson regression analysis showed a significant risk reduction for skeletal events in the ibandronate group, with a hazard ratio of 0.62 (95% CI=0.48, 0.79, P<0.0001), equivalent to a 38% risk reduction compared to placebo. Additionally, patients receiving oral ibandronate 50 mg demonstrated a significant decrease in urinary CTx levels over 96 weeks, with a median change of −77.3%, compared to a median change of +11.0% in the placebo group (P<0.001). These results indicate that oral ibandronate 50 mg effectively reduces the risk of skeletal events and decreases bone resorption markers compared to placebo. Source: [PMC2409647]
text: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduces the risk of skeletal events compared to placebo, with a 38% risk reduction (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001). It also decreases urinary CTx levels by 77.3% versus +11.0% in placebo (P<0.001). Source: [PMC2409647]

memory: In a clinical study [PMC5336430], a combination of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 0.5% and salicylic acid 10% demonstrated significantly better efficacy than vehicle in achieving partial clearance (PC) of lesions. Specifically, 69.5% of patients achieved PC with the combination therapy, compared to 34.6% with vehicle (OR 4.9; 95% CI 2.3, 10.5; P < 0.0001). However, the treatment was associated with a higher frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events, primarily application- and administration-site reactions. In the 5-FU/salicylic acid group, 99.1% of patients reported such events, compared to 83.6% in the vehicle group. These findings indicate that while the combination therapy is more effective in achieving PC, it is also associated with a greater incidence of local adverse events. The study highlights the trade-off between efficacy and safety when using this combination for lesion clearance.
text: The combination of 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% resulted in a higher frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events (99.1%) compared to vehicle (83.6%) [PMC5336430]. These events were primarily local reactions.

memory: A study compared bupropion and nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) for smoking cessation, finding similar abstinence rates (27.9% for bupropion vs. 24.2% for NRT) with no significant difference (odds ratio = 1.21, 95% CI = 0.883–1.67). Combination therapy did not show improved outcomes compared to either treatment alone (24.2%). Subgroup analysis suggested that bupropion may be more effective in individuals with a history of depression (29.8% vs. 18.5%), though the difference was not statistically significant (χ² = 2.86, P = 0.091).
