text: Bupropion and NRT show similar smoking cessation rates (27.9% vs. 24.2%, OR=1.21). Combination therapy does not improve outcomes. Bupropion may be more effective in those with depression, though not statistically significant. Bupropion has more side effects. Source: PMC4282128.

memory: An 11-week study compared the 'FIFA 11 for Health' programme (intervention group, IG) to a control group (CG) and found significant improvements in cardiovascular and body composition parameters in the IG. Systolic blood pressure decreased by −3.5 mm Hg in the IG, compared to an increase of 0.9 mm Hg in the CG (p<0.05). Mean arterial blood pressure also decreased more in the IG (−1.9 mm Hg) than in the CG (0.4 mm Hg) (p<0.05). BMI decreased by −0.02 kg/m² in the IG, versus an increase of 0.13 kg/m² in the CG (p<0.05). Body fat percentage decreased by −0.83% in the IG, compared to −0.04% in the CG (p<0.05). Within the IG, 20 m sprint time improved slightly (from 4.09±0.29 to 4.06±0.28 s), and YYIR1C performance increased (from 852±464 to 896±517 m), but these changes were not significantly different from the CG. Balance and jump performance remained unchanged in both groups. The study suggests that the 'FIFA 11 for Health' programme may offer cardiovascular and body composition benefits compared to no intervention. Source: [PMC5136709]
text: The 'FIFA 11 for Health' programme significantly reduced body fat percentage (−0.83%) compared to control (−0.04%) (p<0.05). Source: [PMC5136709].

memory: In a study comparing Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) to a placebo, the intestinal microbiota composition was analyzed in relation to health status. At 18 months of age, children in the placebo group had higher levels of Clostridium difficile et rel compared to those in the LGG group (1.19 ± 0.85% vs. 0.78 ± 0.60%, p=0.047). This suggests that LGG may have a protective effect against elevated levels of Clostridium difficile et rel. The full data on phylum-like and genus-like level analyses, along with their corresponding p-values, are detailed in Additional file 7 and Additional file 8 of the source article [PMC3563445].
text: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG reduces Clostridium difficile et rel levels at 18 months compared to placebo (0.78% vs. 1.19%, p=0.047), suggesting a protective effect [PMC3563445].
outcome: Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age

memory: In a study [PMC5761719], minimal-risk patients had a lower pre-test probability of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) compared to the rest of the cohort, as determined by the CADC risk score (30.0% vs 47.0%, p < 0.001). These patients were also less likely to present with typical angina symptoms (24.1% vs 42.6%, p < 0.001). HDL-C data was missing for 28.7% of patients (506 individuals) and was imputed for analysis.
text: Patients with minimal-risk had a lower pre-test probability of obstructive CAD (30.0% vs 47.0%, p < 0.001) compared to the remainder of the cohort, as per the CADC risk score [PMC5761719].

memory: A clinical study compared partial matrix excision (Group I) with segmental phenolization (Group II) by evaluating postoperative complications. Moderate pain was reported by three patients in Group I and two in Group II, with all cases managed using analgesics for three days. No statistically significant differences were observed between the groups in terms of postoperative complications or recurrences (P = 0.688). However, Group II patients returned to normal daily activities significantly faster than Group I patients (P < 0.05). The findings were derived from the article [PMC3726903].
text: A clinical study found no statistically significant difference in postoperative complications between partial matrix excision (Group I) and segmental phenolization (Group II) (P = 0.688). However, Group II patients returned to normal activities faster (P < 0.05). Source: [PMC3726903].

memory: In a clinical study [PMC4312979], patients receiving kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity reported significantly reduced pain compared to those receiving placebo, as measured by the visual analog scale (VAS). The active treatment group had a baseline average VAS score of 5.5, which decreased to 1.2 at 15 minutes post-treatment. The placebo group's scores decreased from 4.9 to 3.9. The difference in pain score changes between the two groups was 3.3 points (95% CI: 2.3, 4.4), with a P-value < .001. The difference was significant as early as 5 minutes post-treatment (1.9 points, P = .007) and remained significant at 2 hours post-treatment (3.7 points, P < .001). These results suggest that KOS may have a rapid and sustained analgesic effect compared to placebo.
text: Kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity significantly reduces pain scores compared to placebo, as shown by a clinical study (PMC4312979). VAS scores decreased by 3.3 points (95% CI: 2.3, 4.4; P < .001) in the KOS group versus placebo. The effect was rapid, significant at 5 minutes, and sustained for at least 2 hours.
intervention: kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity

memory: In a community-based intervention study (n = 141), an intervention was compared to usual care. The primary outcome, the SF-12 Physical Component Summary (PCS), showed no statistically significant difference between the intervention and control groups at 6 months. However, significant improvements were observed in secondary outcomes for the intervention group: the SF-12 general health subdomain (mean difference = 3.11, 95% CI = 0.05–5.71, P = .02), Mental Component Summary (MCS) (mean difference = 2.74, 95% CI = 0.28–5.19, P = .03), and the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities (SDSCA) (mean difference = 3.74, 95% CI = 0.9–6.57, P = .01). No significant differences were found for the CES-D (depression), GAD-7 (anxiety), or self-efficacy measures. The complete-case analysis was supported by multiple imputation results. These findings suggest that while the intervention did not significantly impact physical health as measured by the PCS, it had positive effects on mental health and diabetes self-care behaviors. The study highlights the potential of the intervention to improve specific aspects of health-related quality of life in participants. Source: [PMC5836873].
text: A community-based intervention showed no significant effect on SF-12 PCS compared to usual care but improved MCS (mean diff 2.74, P = .03) and SDSCA (mean diff 3.74, P = .01) at 6 months. Source: [PMC5836873].
outcome: 12‐item Short‐Form Health Survey (SF‐12), Mental Component Summary (MCS), Summary of Diabetes Self‐Care Activities (SDSCA)

memory: A clinical study compared bladder training plus tolterodine (Co), tolterodine only (To), and bladder training only (BT) in terms of improvements in micturition frequency and urgency scores. Patients in the Co group showed greater improvements in both frequency and urgency scores compared to the BT group (p < 0.05 each). Both To and Co groups had significantly greater improvements in urgency scores than the BT group (p = 0.017 and p = 0.021, respectively). No significant difference was found between the To and Co groups regarding urgency score improvements. At 12 weeks, satisfaction scores did not differ significantly among the three groups. The BT group had a satisfaction score of 1.5 with 53.9% improvement, the To group had a score of 1.4 with 63.0% improvement, and the Co group had a score of 1.3 with 71.0% improvement. Source: PMC2721929.
text: Bladder training plus tolterodine (Co) showed greater improvement in micturition frequency compared to tolterodine only (To), with Co also showing greater improvements in urgency scores. No significant difference was found between Co and To regarding urgency scores. Source: PMC2721929.

memory: A clinical study compared three anesthetic regimens: Group RH (remifentanil 0.3), Group KRH (remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5), and Group RL (remifentanil 0.05). Demographic and anesthetic parameters were similar across groups, except for end-tidal desflurane concentration. Group RH had significantly higher additional analgesic consumption, higher NRS scores at 6 and 24 hours post-surgery, and greater cumulative fentanyl dose compared to Groups KRH and RL. The Touch-Test sensory evaluation was significantly more negative in Group RH, indicating greater sensory recovery or sensitivity. These findings suggest that higher remifentanil doses (Group RH) may be associated with increased postoperative pain, greater analgesic requirements, and altered sensory outcomes. Source: [PMC4610927]
text: Group RH (remifentanil 0.3) showed a more negative Touch-Test sensory evaluation compared to Groups KRH and RL, indicating greater sensory recovery or sensitivity. This suggests higher remifentanil doses may alter postoperative sensory outcomes. Source: [PMC4610927].
comparator: Remifentanil 0.3 + ketamine 0.5 (group KRH) or remifentanil 0.05 (Group RL)
outcome: Value of the Touch-Test sensory evaluation after surgery

memory: No significant differences were observed between the exercise training and control groups in changes in blood pressure (BP), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, or C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. However, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol increased in the exercise group compared to controls (source: Results > Changes In Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Table 2). When stratified by the presence of carotid plaques, LDL cholesterol levels increased in the exercise group compared to controls only in patients with plaques [0.20 mmol/L (0.00 to 0.41) vs −0.13 mmol/L (−0.37 to 0.12), p = 0.044], but not in patients without plaques (p = 0.40). These findings suggest that exercise training may influence LDL cholesterol levels in individuals with existing carotid plaques, but not in those without. The study did not find significant effects of exercise on BP, HDL, or CRP across the overall population or in the plaque subgroups.
text: Exercise training did not significantly affect HDL cholesterol levels compared to control (source: Results > Changes In Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Table 2).

memory: A clinical study compared heated infusions with a control group and found faster postoperative recovery in the warming infusion group. Time to spontaneous breathing was 4.06 ± 0.72 minutes (warming) versus 4.47 ± 0.84 minutes (control; P = 0.042). Eye opening occurred earlier in the warming group (6.72 ± 1.73 minutes) compared to the control (8.66 ± 2.03 minutes; P < 0.001). Consciousness recovery was quicker in the warming group (9.91 ± 1.91 minutes) versus the control (11.19 ± 1.49 minutes; P = 0.004). The mean time to extubation was also shorter in the warming group (10.09 ± 1.91 minutes) compared to the control (11.13 ± 1.34 minutes; P = 0.015). No significant difference was found in hospital stay duration. These results suggest that heated infusions may improve postoperative recovery, particularly in terms of consciousness and respiratory function. Source: [PMC5380277]
text: Heated infusions significantly reduced consciousness recovery time compared to control (9.91 ± 1.91 vs. 11.19 ± 1.49 minutes; P = 0.004). Source: [PMC5380277]

memory: In a clinical study comparing the Charité artificial disc (intervention) with anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) using BAK cages (control), superficial wound infection rates were 6.3% in the intervention group versus 2.0% in the control group, representing a threefold increase, though not statistically significant (P = .103). The overall infection rate was higher in the intervention group (12.7%) compared to the control group (8.1%). No deep wound infections requiring irrigation, debridement, or intravenous antibiotics were reported in either group. The control group had 3 (3.0%) cases of iliac crest donor site infection. Source: PMC4365564.
text: The Charité artificial disc was associated with a higher rate of superficial wound infection (6.3%) compared to ALIF with BAK cages (2.0%), though not statistically significant (P = .103). Source: PMC4365564.

memory: A clinical study compared GBB supplementation (n = 30) to a placebo (n = 28) over 6 months, focusing on changes in bone mineral density (BMD). At the femoral neck, GBB supplementation maintained BMD, while the placebo group experienced a significant decrease (p = 0.007). The difference in BMD between the groups at the femoral neck was 1.3% (p < 0.05). At Ward's triangle, the GBB group showed a +2.3% increase in BMD, compared to a −1.1% decrease in the placebo group (p < 0.05). These results indicate that GBB supplementation may help preserve BMD compared to a placebo over a 6-month period. Source: [PMC3549413]
text: The placebo group showed a significant decrease in BMD compared to baseline at 6 months (p = 0.007), while GBB supplementation helped maintain BMD. Source: [PMC3549413]
outcome: bone mineral density (BMD) At the 6-month time point

memory: In a study [PMC5330006], athletes received 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks (intervention group) and were compared to a placebo group. The study evaluated the effect of cranberry supplementation and exercise on total antioxidant capacity (TAC). In Trial I (before supplementation), both groups showed a significant post-exercise decrease in serum TAC. In Trial II (after supplementation), the cranberry group had significantly higher resting, post-exercise, and post-recovery TAC levels compared to the placebo group. Although the cranberry group still experienced a post-exercise TAC decrease in Trial II, their levels remained higher than the control group. This suggests that cranberry supplementation may enhance antioxidant status in athletes, potentially offering protective benefits during and after exercise. The data are visualized in Fig. 1, which illustrates TAC levels during exercise tests before and after supplementation (mean ± SD).
text: Receiving 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks significantly increases total antioxidant capacity (TAC) compared to a placebo group [PMC5330006]. The cranberry group showed higher resting, post-exercise, and post-recovery TAC levels, indicating enhanced antioxidant status.
intervention: receiving 1200 mg of cranberry extract for 6 weeks

memory: A clinical study assessed the efficacy of propolis gel for pain relief compared to no treatment. Both the propolis gel and no treatment groups showed significant reductions in pain and erythema scores from baseline to the second follow-up (P = 0.000 for both). However, there was no statistically significant difference in the degree of pain or erythema score reduction between the two groups (P = 0.255). These findings suggest that although both interventions led to improvement, propolis gel did not offer a significantly greater benefit than no treatment. Source: [PMC5863413]
text: A clinical study found that propolis gel and no treatment both significantly reduced pain and erythema (P = 0.000). However, there was no significant difference in pain reduction between the two (P = 0.255). Thus, propolis gel did not show greater benefit than no treatment. Source: [PMC5863413]

memory: A study compared ESM-I (six weeks of Ecological Momentary Assessment with weekly feedback on positive affective experiences) to two control groups: (i) ESM without feedback and (ii) a pseudo-intervention. Outcomes related to symptomatic remission were evaluated. At 32 weeks, ESM-I showed a mean HDRS score 3 units lower than the control group (B = −3.1, p = 0.051, intention-to-treat analysis), though the result was not statistically significant by conventional alpha. No significant difference was found between ESM-I and the pseudo-intervention group (B = −1.13, p = 0.47). Regarding symptomatic remission, ESM-I participants did not show a higher rate of remission compared to the control group (OR = 2.65, p = 0.12) or the pseudo-intervention group (OR = 1.84, p = 0.29). These findings suggest that while ESM-I showed a trend toward lower depression scores, it did not lead to a statistically significant increase in remission rates compared to the comparator groups. Source: [PMC5747107]
text: The study found no statistically significant effect of ESM-I with feedback on symptomatic remission compared to ESM without feedback (OR = 2.65, p = 0.12) or a pseudo-intervention (OR = 1.84, p = 0.29). Source: [PMC5747107].
intervention: ESM-I consisting of six weeks of ESM combined with weekly feedback regarding the individual’s positive affective experiences
comparator: (ii) six weeks of ESM without feedback,

memory: A study compared hyaluronic acid (HA) intervention to baseline conditions by evaluating salivary tissue factor (TF) levels. In the control group, no statistically significant differences in TF levels were observed across three time points. In contrast, the HA group showed significantly lower salivary TF levels one week post-intervention, as determined by One-Way ANOVA for Repeated Measures (p<0.05). Post-hoc comparisons using the LSD test revealed that the mean TF level at time point T2 was significantly lower than at both T0 and T1. These findings suggest that HA may reduce salivary TF levels over time. Source: PMC5393542.
text: Hyaluronic acid (HA) significantly reduces salivary tissue factor (TF) levels compared to baseline, with lower TF observed one week post-intervention (p<0.05, PMC5393542).

memory: A study compared locking plate fixation with nonlocking plate fixation in 41 subjects. No significant difference in range of motion (ROM) was found between the groups (122.35 ± 12.93° vs. 115.71 ± 20.14°, P = 0.219), with 22.0% of subjects in both groups having ROM ≤ 100°. However, the locking plate group showed significantly higher mean knee scores at follow-up (80.20 ± 10.21 vs. 72.52 ± 14.75, P = 0.039), with 65.0% achieving excellent scores compared to 33.3% in the nonlocking group. Additionally, the locking plate group had higher functional scores (77.26 ± 9.95 vs. 69.55 ± 10.22, P = 0.026). These results suggest that, although ROM was similar, locking plate fixation may provide better functional and knee score outcomes. Source: PMC4045368.
text: Locking plate fixation significantly improves mean knee scores at follow-up compared to nonlocking plate fixation (80.20 ± 10.21 vs. 72.52 ± 14.75, P = 0.039). Source: PMC4045368.

memory: In a study published in [PMC4687242], participants received either Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera [L.] Dunal) or a placebo. The Ashwagandha group (n = 24) demonstrated a significantly greater increase in mean VO2 max from baseline compared to the placebo group (n = 25) at both 8 weeks (4.91 vs. 1.42, P < 0.0001) and 12 weeks (5.67 vs. 1.86, P < 0.0001). Additionally, quality of life (QOL) scores across all subdomains improved significantly more in the Ashwagandha group at 12 weeks compared to the placebo group (P < 0.05). The study utilized KSM-66 Ashwagandha as the intervention.
text: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera [L.] Dunal) significantly increased mean VO2 max from baseline after 8 weeks compared to placebo (4.91 vs. 1.42, P < 0.0001) [PMC4687242].
outcome: Increase from baseline in the mean VO2 max after 8 weeks

memory: A study comparing Sitagliptin and Voglibose found no significant differences between the two groups in changes related to HbA1c, GIP, GLP-1, C-peptide, lipid profile, oxidative stress markers, inflammatory markers, or eGFR (Source: PMC4149239, Table 3, Results section, Secondary Efficacy Measures). These results suggest that both drugs have comparable effects on these secondary efficacy measures. The lack of significant differences implies that both Sitagliptin and Voglibose may be similarly effective in managing these outcomes in the studied population. The findings contribute to the understanding of the comparative efficacy of DPP-4 inhibitors and alpha-glucosidase inhibitors in terms of glycemic control and metabolic parameters. The study supports further investigation into potential differences in other clinical outcomes or patient subgroups not evaluated in this trial.
text: A study found no significant differences between Sitagliptin and Voglibose in changes related to Gastric Inhibitory Polypeptide (GIP) (Source: PMC4149239). Both drugs showed comparable effects on GIP levels, suggesting similar impacts on this metabolic parameter.

memory: A study compared Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) with individual support (IS) in women with moderate baseline felt stigma (score = 1.98). Participants were randomly assigned to treatment groups. Results from [PMC5808396] indicate that the IS group experienced more severe felt stigma than the CPT group, with this difference being statistically significant (Table 2). Both groups showed a reduction in felt stigma over time; however, the decline was significantly greater in the CPT group by the end of treatment. The difference in stigma reduction between groups was quantified with a beta coefficient of −0.44 and a p-value of 0.02, indicating that CPT was more effective than IS in reducing felt stigma. These findings suggest that CPT may be superior to standard individual support in reducing felt stigma among the study population.
text: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) is more effective than individual support in reducing felt stigma after treatment. The CPT group showed a significantly greater decline in stigma (β = −0.44, p = 0.02) compared to the individual support group, according to [PMC5808396].

memory: In a study on acute ischemia-reperfusion injury in isolated rat hearts (PMC3637243), lixisenatide treatment significantly reduced infarct size when given 10 minutes before ischemia ended. The infarct area was 162 ± 12 mm² in placebo-treated hearts versus 98 ± 9 mm² in lixisenatide-treated hearts (n=10-11, p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in left ventricular total area (543 ± 16 mm² for placebo vs. 505 ± 7 mm² for lixisenatide) or left ventricular risk area (306 ± 9 mm² for placebo vs. 288 ± 5 mm² for lixisenatide). The infarct area to risk area ratio was reduced by 36% in lixisenatide-treated hearts. Rate pressure product (LVP x HR) and coronary flow remained unchanged during reperfusion at 5 and 120 minutes (Figure 1B and C). These findings suggest that lixisenatide provides protective effects against ischemia-reperfusion injury without affecting hemodynamic parameters or coronary flow.
text: Lixisenatide significantly reduced infarct size (98 ± 9 mm² vs. 162 ± 12 mm², p < 0.05) but did not significantly affect left ventricular risk area (288 ± 5 mm² vs. 306 ± 9 mm²) in a rat model of ischemia-reperfusion injury (PMC3637243).

memory: A clinical study compared PEG-lactulose with lactulose alone for treating hyperammonemia. The intervention group received 20-30 grams of lactulose (oral or rectal) combined with 280 grams of PEG in 4 liters of water as a single oral dose over 30-120 minutes. The comparator group received either 20-30 grams of lactulose orally or via nasogastric tube, or 200 grams of lactulose enema via rectal tube. The primary outcome was blood ammonia levels after 24 hours. Results showed no significant difference in ammonia reduction between the groups (p = 0.858). However, the PEG-lactulose regimen was associated with a shorter hospital stay compared to lactulose alone (p = 0.03). This suggests that both treatments are equally effective in lowering ammonia levels, but PEG-lactulose may offer clinical benefits in reducing hospitalization duration. Source: PMC5308129.
text: The PEG–lactulose regimen showed no significant difference in blood ammonia reduction compared to lactulose alone (p = 0.858). However, it was associated with a shorter hospital stay (p = 0.03). Source: PMC5308129.
intervention: PEG–lactulose group received the 20-30 grams of lactulose of oral or rectal lactulose, plus 280 grams of PEG in 4 liters of water orally as a single dose in 30-120 minutes
comparator: 20-30 grams of lactulose orally or by a nasogastric tube, or 200 grams of lactulose enema by a rectal tube

memory:
Source: PMC4681902  
Intervention: 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction of masticatory muscles  
Comparator: 10% maximal voluntary isometric contraction of masticatory muscles  
Outcome: Longus colli thickness  
Finding: During masticatory muscle contraction, longus colli thickness increased in proportion to contraction intensity. The increase was significantly greater with 80% contraction compared to 10% contraction (p<0.05). The study indicates a dose-response relationship between contraction intensity and longus colli thickness during masticatory muscle activation. Higher intensity contractions led to greater increases in longus colli thickness compared to low-intensity contractions. The results suggest that contraction intensity plays a significant role in modulating muscle thickness outcomes during masticatory muscle activation. This comparison highlights the potential importance of intensity in influencing muscle response in this context.
text: An 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction of masticatory muscles significantly increases longus colli thickness more than a 10% contraction (p<0.05), indicating a dose-response relationship (PMC4681902).

memory: Source article [PMC3009979]: A clinical study compared Ampicillin/sulbactam to Cefuroxime and another group, with median hospitalization duration as the outcome. text: Ampicillin/sulbactam and Cefuroxime had similar median hospitalization durations (4 days) with no statistically significant difference (p=0.09). Interquartile ranges were 4-4 for Ampicillin/sulbactam and 4-5 for Cefuroxime. (Source: PMC3009979)

memory: A study compared the effects of flaxseed and wheat bran supplementation on fasting plasma glucose and insulin levels. Flaxseed significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose compared to baseline and the wheat bran group (5.92 ± 0.31 vs. 4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L, respectively), while the wheat bran group showed no significant change in fasting plasma glucose. Flaxseed did not significantly affect fasting plasma insulin levels. However, wheat bran supplementation over 12 weeks led to a significant reduction in plasma insulin compared to baseline (p = 0.026). The study could not analyze dietary intake of α-linolenic acid and insoluble/soluble fiber due to software limitations. Antioxidant vitamins (C, E, and beta carotene) consumed as food were not significantly different among participants. These findings suggest that flaxseed may be more effective than wheat bran in reducing fasting plasma glucose, while wheat bran may improve insulin levels. Source: [PMC3112403].
text: Flaxseed significantly reduces fasting plasma glucose compared to wheat bran (5.92 ± 0.31 vs. 4.79 ± 0.17 mmol/L), while wheat bran lowers insulin levels. Source: [PMC3112403].

memory: In a study comparing LCI699 to placebo, LCI699 significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) at 12 hours post-dose on Day 1. Compared to a 37% increase in PAC with placebo, LCI699 doses of 0.5 mg, 1 mg, and 3 mg reduced PAC by 49%, 47%, and 63%, respectively (all P < 0.001 vs. placebo). PAC returned to baseline after 24 hours. No additional reduction in PAC was observed with the 10 mg dose (data not shown). On Days 7 and 14, LCI699 (0.5–3 mg) continued to reduce PAC from pre-dose baseline levels. These findings are from the "Human Pharmacokinetic And Pharmacodynamic Studies > Safety And Tolerability" section of the source article [PMC4301837].
text: LCI699 significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) at 12 hours post-dose compared to placebo, with reductions of 49% to 63% (all P < 0.001). Placebo increased PAC by 37%. These findings are from [PMC4301837].

memory: In a study comparing system-oriented therapy to a reference intervention, a significantly higher proportion of participants in the individual intervention group failed to complete follow-up compared to the system-oriented group (15/40 vs. 4/30, P = 0.017). Participants in the individual intervention group received an average of 3 sessions (SD 2.1) and no booster sessions (SD 0.7). The system-oriented intervention achieved a fulfillment of standards of 43% in the hospital. These findings highlight differences in follow-up completion rates and intervention delivery between the two groups. Source: PMC4060171.
text: System-oriented therapy was associated with a higher completed follow-up rate compared to the reference intervention (4/30 vs. 15/40, P = 0.017). Source: PMC4060171.

memory: In a study comparing IPE (4g/day) to placebo in individuals with diabetes (median baseline A1c = 6.8%), no significant changes were observed in fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin levels, or HOMA-estimated insulin resistance in either group. However, among patients with less-controlled diabetes (baseline A1c above median), IPE was associated with greater reductions in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and apolipoprotein B (Apo B). These findings suggest potential cardiometabolic benefits of IPE in individuals with higher baseline glycemic control issues. The study highlights that while IPE did not significantly alter primary metabolic markers, it may have beneficial effects on inflammatory and lipid-related biomarkers in a subgroup of patients with more severe diabetes. Source: PMC3718763, Abstract > Results.
text: IPE (4g/day) did not significantly affect fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR compared to placebo in diabetic patients (median baseline A1c 6.8%). However, in less-controlled diabetes (A1c above median), IPE reduced hsCRP and Apo B, suggesting potential cardiometabolic benefits. Source: PMC3718763.
outcome: fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or homeostasis model assessment-estimated insulin total (all subjects with diabetes—overall median baseline glycosylated hemoglobin A1c [A1c] = 6.8%), better-controlled diabetes (below median baseline A1c), and less-controlled diabetes (above median baseline A1c).

memory: A study compared real-time fMRI neurofeedback (rtfMRI-nf) targeting the left amygdala (LA) and the horizontal segment of the intraparietal sulcus (HIPS), with a focus on mood changes. The LA group exhibited significantly greater increases in happiness compared to the HIPS group (t(19) = 2.33, p = 0.01). While changes in POMS depression were not significant (t(19) = 1.33, p = 0.10), the LA group experienced significant decreases in POMS anger (t(13) = 2.42, p = 0.015), trait anxiety (STAI-Trait; t(13) = 2.62, p = 0.01), and state anxiety (STAI-State; t(13) = 2.34, p = 0.02). Additionally, VAS ratings for restlessness (t(13) = 2.23, p = 0.02), anxiety (t(13) = 4.37, p < 0.001), and irritability (t(13) = 2.14, p = 0.025) were significantly reduced in the LA group. The difference in state anxiety between groups was also significant (t(19) = 2.58, p = 0.03). No other mood ratings showed significant pre-post scan changes (ts(13) < 1.85, ps > 0.08). These results suggest that rtfMRI-nf targeting the LA may have a more pronounced effect on mood compared to HIPS. Source: PMC3921228.

memory: Source article [PMC4663570] evaluated the effect of Agave-derived fructans versus formula on C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum ferritin levels in infants. The study measured mean CRP concentrations at baseline (around 20 days old) and at three months of age, along with changes in CRP (ΔCRP) and serum ferritin (Δserum ferritin). Using the Wilcoxon test, no statistically significant differences were found between the groups for these variables (p = 0.05). A Fisher Student T-Test compared CRP and ferritin levels between cesarean and vaginal delivery methods, revealing no significant differences in initial and final concentrations (p > 0.05). Findings are summarized in Table 3 of the article, which outlines CRP and serum ferritin levels across study groups. The study concluded that Agave-derived fructans did not significantly affect CRP or serum ferritin levels compared to formula, regardless of delivery method.
text: A study (PMC4663570) found no significant effect of Agave-derived fructans compared to formula on C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels in infants. No statistically significant differences were observed in CRP concentrations between the groups (p = 0.05).

memory: In a study comparing Vitamin D + Calcium (VitD + C) with Calcium alone in diabetic and non-diabetic CKD patients, serum IL-10 levels were better preserved in the VitD + C group (p = 0.06), while the Calcium-only group experienced significant declines at weeks 6 and 12. IL-10, an anti-inflammatory cytokine, suggests that calcitriol in the VitD + C regimen helps maintain anti-inflammatory effects. This benefit was more pronounced in non-diabetic CKD patients, who may require the added benefit of calcitriol. Diabetic CKD patients showed benefits from calcium supplementation with or without calcitriol. A similar protective effect of combining vitamin D3 with calcium was noted in chronic heart failure patients [21]. These findings suggest that calcitriol may play a role in maintaining anti-inflammatory responses in CKD patients, particularly in non-diabetic individuals.
text: Vitamin D + Calcium better preserves serum IL-10 compared to Calcium alone in CKD patients (p = 0.06), with greater benefit in non-diabetic individuals. This suggests calcitriol enhances anti-inflammatory effects.

memory: A study assessed the use of sunflower cake as a substitute for soybean meal in goat diets and found no significant differences in body weight at slaughter, carcass yields, or rib eye area (p>0.05). memory: Source: PMC5986505. A study evaluated the effects of three olive oil interventions—Virgin olive oil (VOO), Optimized virgin olive oil (OVOO), and Functional olive oil (FOO)—on cardiovascular markers. Baseline fasting plasma triacylglycerol levels were low (78 ± 5 mg/dL). VOO and OVOO significantly increased triacylglycerol levels (p = 0.037 and p = 0.002, respectively), while FOO had no effect. Total cholesterol increased with FOO (p = 0.021), but LDLc remained unchanged. Systolic blood pressure (SBP) decreased after VOO (p = 0.019) but increased after FOO (p = 0.004). Diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and pulse pressure showed no significant changes across interventions. These findings suggest that different olive oil formulations can have distinct effects on lipid profiles and blood pressure, with VOO and OVOO influencing triacylglycerol levels and FOO affecting total cholesterol and SBP.

memory: Source: PMC4007144. A study evaluated an IPV prevention program for men, focusing on conflict management and attitudes toward IPV, compared to a control group. A study explored the relationship between personality traits and suturing test performance using the NEO-FFI (Neuroticism, Extraversion, Openness, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness). Mean scores were: N = 46.70 ± 11.08, E = 49.03 ± 10.45, O = 48.36 ± 11.93, A = 49.73 ± 11.08, and C = 53.45 ± 11.07. Results showed that students with high Extraversion (E) scores completed the suturing test significantly faster than those with average E scores (regression coefficient = −418.2, P = 0.0118). The findings suggest a potential link between Extraversion and procedural skill efficiency in surgical simulations.

memory: A study comparing laryngeal mask (LM) ventilation with endotracheal intubation (ETI) [Source: PMC4727391] found no significant differences between the two methods in several critical outcomes. memory: In a study [PMC3085176], p-synephrine (50 mg) was tested alone and in combination with naringin and hesperidin to evaluate its effect on resting metabolic rate (RMR). Participants were divided into four groups. Group 1 (placebo) fasted for 8-10 hours, resulting in a slight RMR decrease. All treatment groups showed increased RMR compared to the placebo. Group 2, which received 50 mg p-synephrine alone, experienced a 65 kcal increase in calorie consumption. Group 3, receiving 50 mg p-synephrine plus 600 mg naringin, had a larger increase of 122 kcal over the placebo. Group 4, which received 50 mg p-synephrine, 600 mg naringin, and 100 mg hesperidin, had the highest increase of 183 kcal compared to the placebo group. These findings suggest that p-synephrine, particularly when combined with naringin and hesperidin, significantly enhances RMR relative to a placebo. The study highlights the potential of these compounds in metabolic modulation.
text: p-Synephrine (50 mg) alone increased resting metabolic rate (RMR) by 65 kcal compared to placebo (PMC3085176). This suggests that p-synephrine alone has a significant positive effect on RMR.

memory: In a clinical study comparing Lanreotide Autogel® 120 mg (Lan ATG 120 mg) with lanreotide microparticles 30 mg (Lan MP 30 mg) for symptom control in acromegaly, patients generally experienced mild to moderate symptoms. memory: A 36-month study compared perindopril to placebo in assessing flow-mediated vasodilatation (FMD). Baseline FMD was 2.6% in the perindopril group and 2.8% in the placebo group. After 36 months, FMD increased to 3.3% in the perindopril group and 3.0% in the placebo group. The absolute change in FMD was 0.55% higher in the perindopril group, but this difference was not statistically significant (95% CI: −0.36 to 1.47; p = 0.23). However, when analyzing the rate of change in FMD per 6 months, the perindopril group showed a 0.14% increase (SE 0.05, p = 0.02), compared to 0.02% in the placebo group (SE 0.05, p = 0.74), resulting in a 0.12% difference in the rate of change (p = 0.07). This indicates a trend toward a more favorable improvement in FMD with perindopril over time, although not statistically significant at the 0.05 level. Source: PMC2039813.

memory: In a clinical study comparing two weaning strategies from mechanical ventilation—progressive discontinuation of pressure support ventilation (PSV) with SmartCare™ versus respiratory physiotherapy–driven weaning—baseline physiological parameters were similar between groups, including maximal inspiratory pressure, maximal expiratory pressure, forced vital capacity, and rapid shallow breathing index. At the start of the weaning trial, PEEP, tidal volume (VT), fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2), oxygen saturation (SpO2), respiratory rate, end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2), and P0.1 were comparable, although PSV levels differed (median: 8 vs. 10 cmH2O; p = 0.007). memory: Study [PMC4636858] assessed the effects of Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone versus no treatment on MS plaques and EDSS scores in 71 participants (28 men, 43 women). During treatment, MRI plaque counts decreased in both groups (2.29 vs. 2.17), but the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.782). At six months post-trial, plaque numbers slightly increased in both groups (0.72 vs. 0.77), with no significant difference (P = 0.611). EDSS scores decreased significantly at the end of treatment in both groups (0.79 and 0.53), though no group difference was observed (P = 0.953). Six months after treatment, EDSS scores increased in both groups (0.35 vs. 0.43), with no significant difference (P = 0.624). memory: A clinical study compared artesunate monotherapy (2 mg/kg/day or 4 mg/kg/day once daily) with quinine plus doxycycline (three times daily for 7 days) for treating malaria. The primary outcome was median fever clearance time (FCT). Results showed that the 2 mg/kg/day artesunate group had a median FCT of 17.9 hours (IQR: 4.6–20.7), the 4 mg/kg/day group had a median FCT of 19.1 hours (IQR: 6.6–23.6), and the quinine plus doxycycline group had a median FCT of 29.3 hours (IQR: 16.0–43.1). Artesunate monotherapy significantly reduced FCT compared to the control regimen (P = 0.001). These findings suggest that artesunate is more effective than quinine plus doxycycline in achieving faster clinical response in malaria treatment. Source: [PMC3525560]

memory: In a study involving 101 patients, isomaltulose was compared to sucrose as an intervention. The primary outcome, HbA1c levels at 12 weeks, showed no significant difference between the isomaltulose group (7.24 ± 0.76%) and the sucrose group (7.39 ± 0.78%), with a regression coefficient of 0.02 (95% CI: −0.21 to 0.25), P = 0.844. However, triglyceride levels at 12 weeks were significantly lower in the isomaltulose group compared to the sucrose group, with a regression coefficient of 34.01 (95% CI: 6.59–61.44), P = 0.016. No significant differences were observed between the groups for other secondary parameters. Source: PMC3357231.
text: Isomaltulose significantly lowers triglycerides compared to sucrose (regression coefficient 34.01, 95% CI: 6.59–61.44, P = 0.016) in a 12-week study of 101 patients. No significant difference was found in HbA1c levels. Source: PMC3357231.

memory: In a study comparing a diet supplemented with Curcuminoids extract, hydrolyzed Collagen, and green Tea extract (CCOT) to a control diet in dogs with osteoarthritis (OA), pain interference (PI) outcomes were analyzed. The change in pain severity (PS) from baseline (T0) to 3 months (T3) was significantly different between CCOT and control groups (p = 0.009). However, the overall change in PI scores was not statistically significant (CCOT: T0: 3.26 ± 0.54; T3: 2.96 ± 0.45; p = 0.101; control: T0: 3.44 ± 0.59; T3: 3.86 ± 0.66; p = 0.633; p = 0.063). Analysis of individual PI questions revealed a significant improvement in the CCOT group's ability to rise from lying down compared to the control group (p = 0.029). These results suggest that while the overall PI change was not significant, the CCOT diet had a specific beneficial effect on a particular aspect of pain interference in OA dogs. Source: [PMC5738810] (Fig. 5a and 5b).
text: The experimental diet with CCOT showed no significant overall effect on pain interference change (p = 0.063) compared to the control diet. However, it significantly improved the ability to rise from lying down (p = 0.029) in dogs with OA. Source: [PMC5738810].
intervention: an experimental diet supplemented with Curcuminoids extract, hydrolyzed COllagen and green Tea extract (CCOT)

memory: A clinical study investigated the effect of fermented milk (FM) with or without Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055) on fecal fat excretion. Participants consumed 100 g of FM, either containing LG2055 or not. No significant differences in fecal wet weight were observed before or after FM intake between the groups. However, fecal fat levels significantly increased in the active group (with LG2055) after FM intake compared to pre-intake levels. In contrast, the control group (FM without probiotic) did not show a significant increase in fecal fat. The change in fecal fat levels from pre- to post-FM intake was greater in the active group than in the control group, although this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.086). These findings suggest a potential effect of LG2055 on fecal fat excretion, but further research is needed to confirm this effect. Source: PMC4391304.
text: Consuming 100 g of fermented milk with Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 significantly increased fecal fat levels compared to pre-intake, while the control group without LG2055 did not show a significant increase. The difference between groups was not statistically significant (P = 0.086). Source: PMC4391304.
intervention: 100&amp;nbsp;g of fermented milk (FM) + Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055)

memory: Source article [PMC1468428] evaluated the impact of a 1-litre saline enema on puerperal and neonatal infection rates compared to no enema. The study used balanced allocation and achieved an 86% one-month follow-up rate. Newborn infection rates were 20% overall, while puerperal infection rates were 18%. In the enema group, puerperal infection rates were 22% (41/190), compared to 14% (26/182) in the no enema group. The relative risk (RR) was 0.66 (95% CI: 0.43 to 1.03), which was not statistically significant. Neonatal infection rates were 20% (38/191) with enema and 22% (40/179) without enema, with an RR of 1.12 (95% CI: 0.76 to 1.66), also not significant. Median labour duration was similar between groups (515 minutes with enema vs. 585 minutes without enema; P = 0.24). Episiorraphy dehiscence rates were 12% with enema and 17% without enema (P = 0.30), again not significantly different. The study found no significant benefits of the saline enema in reducing infection rates or other outcomes in either mothers or newborns.
text: A 1-litre saline enema did not significantly reduce puerperal or neonatal infection rates compared to no enema (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43-1.03 for puerperal; RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76-1.66 for neonatal). Other outcomes, including episiorraphy dehiscence and labour duration, also showed no significant differences. (Source: PMC1468428)

memory: A 10-week yoga program was compared to a control group in a study assessing flexibility and autonomic nervous system responses. Flexibility, measured via the sit & reach test, significantly improved in the yoga group (p < 0.001). Heart rate variability (HRV) outcomes showed no overall group differences, except for a significant increase in the LF:HF ratio (p = 0.04) and a decrease in pNN50 (p = 0.04) in the yoga group, which contradicted initial hypotheses. Post hoc analysis of participants who completed ≥70% of yoga sessions (n = 11) versus control (n = 19) confirmed the flexibility results and revealed reduced state anxiety (p = 0.02) and RMSSD (p = 0.05), along with a trend toward improved push-up performance (p = 0.07). No other significant changes were observed. Source: [PMC3648394]
text: A 10-week yoga program significantly improved flexibility (p < 0.001) compared to control. Post hoc analysis confirmed these results in completers (n = 11) versus control (n = 19). Source: [PMC3648394]

memory: A clinical study assessed the efficacy of two istradefylline doses (20 mg and 40 mg) versus placebo in Parkinson’s disease patients, focusing on motor function and dyskinesia management. Both doses significantly increased daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia compared to placebo: 20 mg (+1.09 hours, P = .003) and 40 mg (+1.08 hours, P = .004), with placebo showing only a minor increase (+0.26 hours). No significant difference was found between the two istradefylline doses. Neither dose increased daily ON time with troublesome dyskinesia. Additionally, both istradefylline doses significantly improved UPDRS Part II scores (OFF state) compared to placebo: 20 mg (−1.4, P = .034) and 40 mg (−1.7, P = .009), while placebo showed minimal improvement (−0.6). These findings suggest that both istradefylline doses are effective in improving motor function and reducing dyskinesia without increasing the risk of problematic dyskinesia. Source: [PMC3842830].
text: Both istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg significantly increased daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia compared to placebo, with no significant difference between the doses (PMC3842830).
outcome: Daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia

memory: In a clinical study, oral liarozole at 150 mg was compared to a placebo. The intervention group showed statistically significant improvements from baseline compared to the placebo group in three domains: 'daily activities' (P = 0.008), 'leisure' (P = 0.026), and 'symptoms and feelings' (P = 0.023). These results suggest that liarozole may have a positive effect on these aspects of patient well-being. The findings are derived from the source article [PMC4232915].
text: Oral liarozole (150 mg) significantly improved 'daily activities' (P = 0.008), 'leisure' (P = 0.026), and 'symptoms and feelings' (P = 0.023) compared to placebo, suggesting a positive effect on patient well-being [PMC4232915].

memory: A clinical study compared 15-pulse anti-tachycardia pacing (ATP) with eight-pulse ATP, evaluating syncope and near-syncope episodes as secondary endpoints. Table 2 from [PMC2836470] reported seven syncope (1.7%) and nine near-syncope (1.8%) episodes in 14 patients, all associated with fascicular ventricular tachycardia (FVT) episodes. The incidence of syncope and near-syncope per FVT episode was 0.5% and 2.8% in the eight-pulse ATP group, and 3.2% and 0.7% in the 15-pulse ATP group, respectively. However, no statistically significant differences were found between the two groups for syncope or near-syncope occurrence (p = 0.690). These results suggest that the number of ATP pulses did not significantly influence the frequency of syncope or near-syncope episodes in patients with FVT. The study indicates that both eight-pulse and 15-pulse ATP strategies are similarly effective in preventing syncope and near-syncope in this patient population.
text: A clinical study found no significant difference between 15-pulse and eight-pulse ATP in preventing syncope or near-syncope episodes (p = 0.690). Both strategies appear similarly effective in patients with fascicular ventricular tachycardia [PMC2836470].

memory: In a study [PMC3131514], prednisolone at 7.5 mg and 30 mg once daily was compared to placebo in evaluating metabolic outcomes. Both doses reduced insulin’s suppression of endogenous glucose production, with decreases of 17 ± 6% and 46 ± 7%, respectively. Peripheral glucose uptake was not significantly affected by the 7.5 mg dose but decreased by 34 ± 6% with the 30 mg dose (p < 0.0001). Insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis was reduced by both doses, by 11 ± 5% and 34 ± 6%, compared to placebo. In the fasted state, prednisolone showed a trend toward decreased lipolysis (p = 0.062). Prednisolone also increased whole-body proteolysis during hyperinsulinaemia, with a trend toward greater effect from the 30 mg dose (5 ± 2%; p = 0.06). No side effects were reported. The study demonstrates dose-dependent effects of prednisolone on glucose and lipid metabolism, with higher doses causing more pronounced metabolic changes.
text: Both prednisolone doses (7.5 mg and 30 mg) reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis compared to placebo, by 11 ± 5% and 34 ± 6%, respectively [PMC3131514]. The effect was dose-dependent.
intervention: prednisolone 30 mg once daily and  prednisolone 7,5 mg once daily

memory: Source article [PMC1550608] evaluated return rates between online and mailed paper questionnaires, defining return rate as the proportion of participants who returned or completed questionnaires relative to those randomized. Internet respondents were more likely to be married compared to mailed questionnaire participants (P=.043). Mailed questionnaire participants had a higher incidence of asthma (p=.096). These demographic factors, along with other variables, were included as covariates in ANCOVA models to adjust for group differences.
text: The study found that subjects who were married were more likely to respond to online questionnaires compared to mailed paper versions (P=.043). No significant effect on married subjects' response rates was directly reported, but demographic differences were adjusted in statistical models.

memory: A study compared the effect of using one's own Facebook profile versus quiet reading on psychosocial stress recovery. No significant differences were found between the two conditions at any time point (p < 0.05) for subjective stress markers. The study included raw cortisol values, as shown in Plot D, though log-transformed scores were used for statistical analyses. Participants in the intervention group used their own Facebook profiles, while the control group engaged in quiet reading. The results suggest that neither activity had a significantly different impact on stress recovery, based on the measured subjective stress markers and cortisol levels. Source: [PMC5610684].
text: Using one's own Facebook profile had no significant effect on subjective stress markers compared to quietly reading (p < 0.05). Both conditions showed similar impacts on stress recovery, according to the study [PMC5610684].

memory:
Source: [PMC4823408]  
Intervention: 8 cm pillow during tracheal intubation  
Comparator: 4 cm pillow during tracheal intubation  
Outcome: Discomfort score for tracheal intubation  

Results: No significant differences were found between the 8 cm and 4 cm pillow groups regarding laryngeal view or number of intubation trials (Table 2). However, the discomfort score during tracheal intubation was higher in the 8 cm group during sequence I (Table 2). Objective measurements indicated that angles from the horizontal line to the laryngeal, pharyngeal, and oral axes were greater in the 8 cm group compared to the 4 cm group (Table 3). Angular differences between adjacent axes were similar between the two groups. Notably, one patient in the 8 cm group required two intubation attempts, while the same patient was successfully intubated on the first attempt using the 4 cm pillow.
text: Using an 8 cm pillow during tracheal intubation was associated with a higher discomfort score compared to a 4 cm pillow (PMC4823408). No significant differences were found in laryngeal view or number of intubation trials.

memory: A study compared endodontic materials, with the intervention group using Gutta-percha combined with a new endodontic cement (NEC) and the comparator group using Gutta-percha with AH26. The outcome measured was coronal dye penetration, an indicator of root canal seal quality. Results showed no significant differences in mean apical dye penetration between groups using Gutta-percha with AH26 (LGP/AH26), Gutta-percha with MTA (SGP/MTA), and Gutta-percha with NEC (SGP/NEC). However, the SGP/NEC group showed significantly less coronal dye penetration compared to the other groups (P < 0.001), indicating better coronal sealing properties with NEC. These findings suggest that NEC may offer improved coronal sealing when used with Gutta-percha compared to AH26. The study's findings are reported in the abstract of the source article [PMC3712263].
text: The use of Gutta-percha combined with new endodontic cement (NEC) showed significantly less coronal dye penetration compared to Gutta-percha with AH26, indicating better coronal sealing (PMC3712263).

memory: A study compared intermediate progressive addition lenses (PALs) with distance single vision lenses and found no significant differences in gait safety parameters. Key measures included vertical toe clearance on ascent (Wald χ2 = 0.4, p = 0.54), its variability (Wald χ2 = 0.1, p = 0.93), ascent duration (Wald χ2 = 1.4, p = 0.25), heel clearance on descent (Wald χ2 = 0.7, p = 0.42), its variability (Wald χ2 = 2.4, p = 0.12), and descent duration (Wald χ2 = 1.6, p = 0.20). These results suggest that intermediate PALs do not significantly differ from distance single vision lenses in terms of gait safety. Gait safety with intermediate PALs was also comparable to participants’ own spectacles. However, participants were all well-adapted PAL wearers, and intermediate bifocals were found to provide poorer gait safety parameters compared to intermediate PALs and/or distance single vision lenses (Table 1). The findings indicate that for gait safety, intermediate PALs perform similarly to distance single vision lenses and are not worse than participants’ habitual lenses.
text: Intermediate progressive addition lenses (PALs) do not significantly affect ascent vertical toe clearance compared to distance single vision lenses (p = 0.54). Gait safety parameters were similar between the two lens types.

memory: In a behavioral lifestyle intervention study, children attended group meetings over a 3-month intensive phase. Attendance was generally good, with five boys and five girls missing two meetings, and two boys and five girls missing one meeting. The rest attended all sessions. Short-term (T2 at 3 months) and long-term (T3 at 1-year follow-up) results showed significant reductions in adiposity measures in the intervention group compared to an obese control group. At the 1-year follow-up, BMI-SDS decreased by 10% and WC-SDS by 19% in the intervention group from baseline. The control group showed no change in these measures. Additionally, the intervention group demonstrated a 20% increase in VO2peak-SDS-kg, while the control group experienced an 18% reduction. Borg scores for perceived exertion remained stable over time in both groups. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the behavioral lifestyle intervention in improving adiposity and cardiorespiratory fitness in children compared to controls. Source: [PMC3302141]
text: A behavioral lifestyle intervention significantly reduced waist circumference (WC-SDS by 19%) compared to control at 1-year follow-up, while control showed no change. Source: [PMC3302141]

memory: The study integrated Mediterranean and portfolio dietary patterns, both associated with reduced cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Participants initially consumed more discretionary foods than recommended. Energy intakes before and after the intervention exceeded the 2011–2012 Australian Health Survey (AHS) national average of 8672 kJ, though the proportion of energy from discretionary foods (34.6% of total energy for adults) remained stable. Macronutrient contributions were largely unchanged and aligned with national averages, with minimal differences between control and intervention groups. Saturated fat intake, as measured by food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), showed no significant change. However, self-reported dietary habit questions indicated a potential reduction in saturated fat intake, possibly due to changes in meat cut choices.
text: Before intervention, participants' dietary intakes exceeded the national average in energy, with similar proportions of discretionary foods and macronutrients. Saturated fat intake showed no significant change via FFQ, though self-reported habits suggested a potential reduction (Source: Study).

memory: A study compared the effects of ezetimibe/simvastatin 10/20mg (ES10/20) and rosuvastatin 10mg (R10) on low-density lipoprotein-particle number (LDL-P), particularly small LDL particle concentrations (sLDL-P). Percent changes in LDL-P were strongly correlated with changes in sLDL-P (P<0.0001). Both ES10/20 and R10 significantly reduced sLDL-P compared to double the dose of the initial statin (1.0 nmol/L). ES10/20 reduced sLDL-P by 34.7 nmol/L, while R10 reduced it by 23.3 nmol/L. However, the difference in sLDL-P reduction between ES10/20 and R10 was not statistically significant (data not shown). The findings are based on the Results section of the study, focusing on lipid and apolipoprotein effects, as presented in Figure 2B through 2D of the source article [PMC4845107].
text: Both ES10/20 and R10 significantly reduced sLDL-P compared to double the initial statin dose. ES10/20 reduced sLDL-P by 34.7 nmol/L, while R10 reduced it by 23.3 nmol/L. However, the difference between the two was not statistically significant (PMC4845107).

memory: A weight management intervention combining diet, physical activity, and usual care significantly increased fiber intake compared to usual care alone (M between-group difference = 5.7 g/day, p < .001), but did not significantly reduce fat consumption (−2.3 g/day, p = 0.13). Higher fiber intake was associated with greater weight loss at four months (M difference = −1.98 kg, p < .01; R2 = 0.2, p < 0.005) and 12 months (M difference = −1.85 kg, p = 0.1; R2 = 0.1, p < 0.01). The intervention enhanced mediators of behavior change, consistent with the PMBLC model’s mechanisms. Increased self-efficacy and understanding of behavior change were linked to greater engagement in coping planning and self-monitoring, supporting sustained dietary improvements at both four and 12 months. Source: [PMC4304200].
text: A weight management intervention combining diet, physical activity, and usual care significantly increased fiber intake by 5.7 g/day at 12 months compared to usual care alone (p < .001). Source: [PMC4304200].
intervention: weight management intervention targeting diet and physical activity plus usual care

memory: A study evaluated tamsulosin dosing strategies in patients with no improvement in lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) by grouping them into nonescalators (0.2 mg/d) and escalators (increased to 0.4 mg/d). Erectile function was assessed using IIEF-5 scores. In 15 patients without LUTS improvement, there was no significant difference in IIEF-5 scores between groups (1.2 for escalators vs. 0.8 for nonescalators, p=0.859). However, in 35 patients who showed LUTS improvement, escalators had a significantly greater increase in IIEF-5 scores compared to nonescalators (4.6 vs. 1.7, p=0.002). These results suggest that dose escalation of tamsulosin may enhance erectile function outcomes in patients who experience improvement in LUTS. Source: [PMC3580298]
text: In patients with no improvement in LUTS, there was no significant difference in IIEF-5 scores between tamsulosin nonescalators and escalators (p=0.859). Source: [PMC3580298]
comparator: increase their dose to 0.4 mg once daily (escalators)
outcome: International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5)  in patients who showed no improvement of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)

memory: A clinical study in healthy volunteers evaluated two doses of gepotidacin: 1,000 mg and 1,800 mg. Adverse events (AEs) were reported by 46% (23 subjects) at 1,000 mg and 64% (34 subjects) at 1,800 mg. AEs were generally mild to moderate and included nausea, abdominal pain, abdominal discomfort, vomiting, salivary hypersecretion, feeling hot, and oropharyngeal discomfort. Moderate AEs occurred more frequently at 1,800 mg, with vomiting in 8 subjects (15%), nausea in 4 (8%), throat tightness in 1 (2%), and dizziness in 1 (2%). Five subjects (9%) discontinued the study due to AEs: one case of throat tightness, three with positive *Clostridium difficile* tests, and one with *C. difficile* infection. These findings indicate a dose-related increase in adverse events, with some leading to study discontinuation.
text: The 1,800 mg dose of gepotidacin in healthy volunteers was associated with a higher incidence of moderate adverse events (15% vomiting, 8% nausea) compared to 1,000 mg (4% nausea). This suggests a dose-related increase in moderate AEs (Source: clinical study).

memory: In a study comparing etomidate and propofol (based on midazolam), differences in adverse event incidence were noted. The propofol group had a significantly higher rate of transient hypotension (41.9%) compared to the etomidate group (24.2%) (P = .036). In contrast, the etomidate group experienced a significantly higher rate of adverse events that disturbed the procedure (25.8% vs. 8.1% in the propofol group; P = .008). Furthermore, the incidence of myoclonus was significantly higher in the etomidate group (16.1%) compared to the propofol group (1.6%) (P = .004). These findings were reported in the abstract of the source article [PMC5976307].
text: Etomidate significantly increases the incidence rate of myoclonus (16.1%) compared to propofol based on midazolam (1.6%; P = .004) [PMC5976307].

memory: A study compared a diet with 85 g/day of almonds to a control diet, examining plasma α-tocopherol and γ-tocopherol levels. The almond diet significantly increased vitamin E intake by 103% compared to the control. During the almond intervention, plasma α-tocopherol increased by 5.8% and γ-tocopherol decreased by 15.4% from baseline. In contrast, the control diet showed no significant changes in either tocopherol. Post-intervention, compared to the control, the almond diet led to a 10.2% increase in α-tocopherol (P = 0.0065) and a 16.5% decrease in γ-tocopherol (P = 0.047). These findings suggest that almond consumption alters the plasma tocopherol profile, increasing α-tocopherol and decreasing γ-tocopherol. The control diet had no significant effect on these markers. Source: [PMC4469426].
text: The CON diet with 85 g/day almonds significantly increased plasma α-tocopherol by 10.2% compared to the CON diet (P = 0.0065). Source: [PMC4469426].

memory: A study compared an area-wide, computerised diabetes register with a full structured recall and individualised patient management system (intervention) to a standard structured and recall management system (comparator). The intervention group showed improved documentation of diabetes-related care. Patients in the intervention group were more likely to have at least one diabetes appointment recorded (OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.02, 3.91), a foot check recorded (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.09, 3.21), dietary advice recorded (OR 2.77, 95% CI 1.22, 6.29), and blood pressure recorded (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.06, 4.36). No differences were found in mean HbA1c or BP levels, but mean cholesterol levels were significantly lower in the intervention group (-0.15 mmol/l, 95% CI -0.25, -0.06). No differences were observed in patient-reported outcomes, drug use, or uptake of health services. Source: [PMC1804280].
text: The area-wide computerised diabetes register improved documentation of diabetes-related care, including more frequent diabetes appointments (OR 2.00), foot checks (OR 1.87), dietary advice (OR 2.77), and blood pressure recording (OR 2.14) compared to standard management. Source: [PMC1804280].
intervention: area-wide, computerised diabetes register incorporating a full structured recall and individualised patient management system
comparator: standard structured and recall management system
outcome: Frequency of at least one diabetes appointment, a foot check, receiving dietary advice, recording of blood pressure
