text: Both Alfentanil and Remifentanil showed similar effects on awakening, verbal response, and discharge times. Alfentanil had a shorter, though non-significant, respiration return time. Remifentanil was associated with higher nausea/vomiting (P<0.05).
intervention: 10 μg/kg of Alfentanil, infusion of Alfentanil 1 μg/kg/min
comparator: Remifentanil 0.5 μg/kg, infusion of Remifentanil 0.1 μg/kg/min
outcome: stopping the anesthesia drugs up to opening eyes, return to verbal response, and discharge from the recovery

memory: Primaquine reduced clearance time (1 vs. 12 days, HR 7.3, p=0.01) and gametocyte carriage (2.1% vs. 15%, PR 0.12, p=0.03) compared to non-primaquine [PMC5462369]. Hemoglobin reduction was 24.8% vs. 7.1% (p=0.14).
text: Adding primaquine to dihydroartemisin-piperaquine significantly reduces gametocyte carriage (2.1% vs. 15%, PR 0.12, p=0.03) [PMC5462369].

memory: Health warnings reduced product ratings (F(2,42)=7.01, p=.002, ηp²=.25), with pictorial labels most effective (p=.002). Text and no warning showed no difference (p=.10). 'No health warning' led to faster consumption than text and pictorial (p<.001), which did not differ (p=.76).
text: Visual warnings (text) had no significant effect on the speed of alcohol consumption compared to no warning (p=.10). However, "No health warning" led to faster consumption than both text and pictorial warnings (p<.001).

memory: No significant DXA or μCT differences in L4 vertebrae. RAL reduced blood glucose AUC vs. VEH-ND (p=0.048), with similar endpoint values. RAL improved femoral toughness and diabetes incidence. VEH-D had worse trabecular parameters than RAL and VEH-ND. Source: PMC4171519.
text: Raloxifene (RAL) improved femoral toughness compared to control (VEH-ND) and reduced diabetes incidence. Source: PMC4171519.

memory: Alcohol vs mechanical: 90.9% vs 93.4% visual acuity (P=0.08), 90% vs 92.2% refractive error (P=0.23), 96s vs 118s time (P=0.035), −4.37D vs −3.8D (P=0.78).
text: Alcohol-assisted epithelial removal showed no significant effect on mean spherical equivalent compared to mechanical removal (−4.37D vs −3.8D, P=0.78).

memory: Study [PMC3441280] found proximal-release ATP pellets and naso-duodenal tube administration significantly increased uric acid (~50%) compared to placebo (P=0.003 and P=0.001). Distal-release pellets had no effect. Proximal-release pellets also increased plasma lithium AUC more than distal-release (P=0.001).
text: Administration via proximal-release pellets significantly increases plasma lithium AUC compared to distal-release pellets (P=0.001) [PMC3441280].

memory: A study [PMC1868022] found no change in total protein, IL-8, IL-1β, or IL-6 in cervical vault lavage cytokines before and after Pap smear. However, IL-12 p70, TNF-α, and IL-10 increased. No differences in socio-demographics or sexual behavior were observed between groups.
text: The Pap smear at enrollment was associated with increased IL-10 levels compared to no intervention, according to [PMC1868022]. No changes were observed in other cytokines like IL-6 or IL-8.

memory: At week 24, SB4 showed equivalent ACR50/ACR70 response rates to ETN (PPS/FAS), with 95% CI −9.41% to 4.98% within −15% to 15% equivalence margin. SB4 had significantly lower ADA incidence (0.7% vs 13.1%, p<0.001), with only one ETN sample showing neutralising capacity.
text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, demonstrated therapeutic equivalence to etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate, with similar ACR50/ACR70 responses at week 24 (95% CI −9.41% to 4.98%). SB4 showed significantly lower anti-drug antibody incidence (0.7% vs 13.1%, p<0.001).
outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: Robotic group had higher LGE encirclement (94% vs 88%, P=0.03) and increased 6-month arrhythmia recurrence with LGE (43% vs 30%, P=0.001).
text: The robotic-assisted navigation (Hansen Sensei® X) resulted in higher mean LGE encirclement at 6 months compared to standard navigation (94% vs 88%, P=0.03). This suggests a potential increased effect on LGE coverage with robotic assistance.
outcome: mean LGE encirclement at 6 months follow-up

memory: Prophylaxis reduced infant systemic reactions (p < 0.05). Paracetamol showed 79% efficacy (95% CI: 3.9, 97.7) in reducing fever >39°C post-toddler dose. Fever ≥38°C reduction was significant in infants (43.0%, 95% CI: 17.4, 61.2).
text: Paracetamol 250 mg significantly reduced fever activity compared to control (p < 0.05), with 79% efficacy in reducing fever >39°C and 43% reduction in fever ≥38°C in infants.

memory: In the NF period, soft stools were more frequent (17%, n=4) than with SF (p=0.046). NF showed greater improvement in stool consistency (90% vs 50%), though not significant (p=0.14). Both groups had increased defecation frequency (p=0.36). Painful defecation and masses showed no significant differences between NF and SF.
text: The new formula (NF) showed a higher frequency of soft stools (17%) compared to standard formula (SF) (p=0.046). However, improvement in stool consistency was not significant (p=0.14). Defecation frequency increased in both groups (p=0.36), with no differences in painful defecation or masses. Source: Working notes.

memory: Kegel exercises improved FVC, FEV1, PER, FEF 25–75%, IC, and MVV in the experimental group compared to no change in controls. FEV1/FVC changes were not significant. Source: [PMC4668172].
text: Kegel exercises improved peak expiratory flow (PER) compared to control. Source: [PMC4668172].

memory: Peramivir and oseltamivir showed similar symptom duration (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65), TSS scores (-7.1 vs. -5.9, no sig diff), fever alleviation (40.0 vs. 37.8 hrs, P = .69), and virus titer reduction (both ~4 days, P = .51).
text: Peramivir and oseltamivir had similar effects on influenza symptom duration (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65), with no significant differences in other outcomes.
outcome: The numbers of days required for the disappearance of influenza symptoms

memory: Telemonitored group had higher medication dose increases compared to usual care. No significant difference in emergency visits (p=0.286). Home BP telemonitoring cost £115.32 more per patient (95% CI £83.49 to £146.63; p<0.001). Source: PMC3657667.
text: The hypertension telemonitoring-based service did not significantly affect accident and emergency visits costs (p=0.286). However, it increased home BP monitoring costs by £115.32 per patient (PMC3657667).

memory: Placebo arm showed intermittent ADM use linked to diabetes (1.34 [0.99–1.81]). Continuous antidepressant use increased diabetes risk in placebo (2.34 [1.32–4.15]) and lifestyle arms (2.48 [1.45–4.22]), but not in metformin arm (0.55 [0.25–1.19]).
text: Antidepressant users had increased diabetes risk in placebo (1.34) and lifestyle arms (2.48), but not in metformin arm. Continuous use raised risk further in placebo (2.34) and lifestyle arms (2.48). Source: Working notes.

memory: BMDMC therapy improved survival in CLP-induced ARDS, reduced lung elastance, alveolar collapse, tissue and BALF cellularity, collagen content, and IL-1β, while increasing chemokine expression. Day 7 survival was 100% for groups C, LPS-SAL, LPS-BMDMC, and sham mice (PMC3856598).
text: BMDMC therapy reduced alveolar collapse in CLP-induced ARDS compared to control mice (PMC3856598).
intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)

memory: Infants with vaginal operative delivery had lower pain response with plastic vs. metal ventouse cups (p < 0.001). Metal cups caused more scalp trauma (13.2% vs. 6.6%), p = 0.51. EDIN ≥5 was higher in metal/placebo vs. plastic/placebo, not significant. Source: [PMC5282794].
text: Infants undergoing vaginal operative delivery exhibited lower pain response with plastic ventouse cups compared to metal ones (p < 0.001). Metal cups caused more scalp trauma (13.2% vs. 6.6%), though not statistically significant (p = 0.51). Source: [PMC5282794].

memory: Source [PMC2825665] found antibody responders had significant improvements in Dependence Scale (p=0.033) and Disability Assessment for Dementia (p=0.015) after 4.6 years vs. placebo. CDR-SOB showed 20.2% less decline, but not statistically significant (p=0.185).
text: Synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) showed a significant improvement in Dependence Scale compared to placebo (p=0.033) in antibody responders after 4.6 years, according to [PMC2825665].

memory: Levamizol added to intramuscular and intradermal vaccinations increased antibody titers by 514.2 IU/L (p=0.001) and 176.1 IU/L (p=0.01), respectively. Seroconversion rates were 60% vs. 70% (not statistically significant). Source: PMC1540413.
text: The effect of "40 μg HB vaccine intramuscularly" compared with "20 μg HB vaccine intradermally" on the percent of seroconversion rate showed no statistically significant difference (60% vs. 70%). Source: PMC1540413.

Compared to control, "Physical activity + Healthy eating" significantly reduces cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.53–0.75). Individual components show mixed effects, with PA alone showing a moderate benefit and HE alone showing minimal impact.

memory: A web-based intervention did not significantly improve medication intensification for glucose, BP, or lipids in rural diabetic patients. Both groups showed increased A1c medication intensification (p<0.05), but no group-time interaction (p=0.948). BP intensification was similar between arms. Source: [PMC3467590].
text: The web-based CME, feedback, and quality improvement tools did not significantly improve incremental benefits in medication intensification for glucose, BP, or lipids in rural diabetic patients compared to the control group (p=0.948). Source: [PMC3467590].
intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

memory: Diabetic mice showed elevated NT immunoreactivity and reduced cardiac contractility (Ees, PRSW). Cinaciguat reduced PDE-5, increased PKG activity (p-VASP/VASP), improved PRSW and Tau, and reduced nitro-oxidative stress and histological damage (PMC4628236).
text: The sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic mice compared to placebo, as shown in PMC4628236.
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

memory: Lemon verbena showed trends in increased GPxP activity (p=0.0681) and reduced exercise-induced muscle strength loss (p=0.0311) vs. placebo, with less MVC reduction (p=0.0311). No significant changes in CK or IL-6. Pain reduction trended (p=0.0788). Source: PMC5781260.
text: Lemon verbena extract showed a trend toward reduced exercise-induced muscle strength loss (p=0.0311) compared to placebo, with less MVC reduction. However, no significant changes in CK or IL-6 were observed. Source: PMC5781260.

memory: Arformoterol improved quality of life (SGRQ, CCQ) and lung function (FEV1, FVC) vs placebo (P < .05). Adverse event rates were similar (72.9% vs 68.2%). Risk of first respiratory SAE was 50% lower with arformoterol (P = .003).
text: Arformoterol significantly improved quality of life (SGRQ, CCQ) and lung function (FEV1, FVC) compared to placebo (P < .05). Adverse events were similar, but arformoterol reduced the risk of first respiratory SAE by 50% (P = .003).
outcome: improvements in quality of life (overall St. George's Hospital Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire)

memory: In rats, GX reduced Ca absorption and bone breaking force, while FOS diets (GF, GIF) improved Ca absorption and prevented bone fragility (p<0.05). Isoflavone had no effect on breaking force. GIF increased equol levels compared to GI (p<0.05).
text: The Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF) improved calcium absorption and bone strength compared to the Control diet (GC), preventing femur fragility (p<0.05). Isoflavone alone had no effect on breaking force.
intervention: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF)

memory: PTEF increased significantly after albuterol and saline, with no difference between treatments (P = 0.6). TEF10 and 25/PT decreased significantly (P < 0.05) after albuterol. No significant changes in VPTEF/VE or tPTEF/tE with either treatment (Table 3).
text: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) significantly decreased the 25/PT ratio compared to saline (3 ml), while both increased PTEF without difference between treatments (P = 0.6). Source: Table 3.
intervention: nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline)
outcome: ratio of the tidal expiratory flow at 25% of the remaining tidal volume to PTEF (25/PT)

memory: Male patients with slight BMI elevation (≤32 kg/m²) and moderate hypertension (mean OBP 152/100 mm Hg). Genome-wide associations identified three SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) significantly linked to ASBP response to bisoprolol.
text: Bisoprolol showed a significant association with ASBP response linked to SNPs rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037 on chromosome 11 in male patients with moderate hypertension and slight BMI elevation, compared to losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide. Source: Working notes.
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

memory: ANOVA showed lower pulmonary function in HbA1c ≥8.0 group. At week 26, intervention group had higher HbA1c ≤7.0% (18.18% vs. 10.81%), no significant difference. TC decreased more in intervention (−4.27 mg/dL; P < 0.05). BMI decline similar (P > 0.05). No serious cutaneous AEs.
text: The combination of metformin (500 mg, bid po) and alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) showed a higher proportion of patients with HbA1c ≤7.0% (18.18%) compared to metformin alone (10.81%) at week 26, though the difference was not statistically significant. (Source: Working notes)
intervention: metformin (500 mg, bid po) combined with alogliptin (25 mg, qd po)
outcome: proportion of patients with glycosylated hemoglobinA1c (HbA1c) ≤7.0%

memory: FAST treatment increased pulse rate (P=0.022), MAP, sBP, and dBP (P=0.035; 0.046; 0.035) compared to SLOW. No significant differences were found in venous acid-base variables, electrolytes, oxygen saturations, haemoglobin, glucose, lactate, BNP-NT, CI, SVRI, or DO2 between groups.
text: FAST treatment significantly increased pulse rate, MAP, sBP, and dBP compared to SLOW treatment (P=0.022; 0.035; 0.046; 0.035). No significant differences were observed in other haemodynamic or metabolic variables.

memory: No significant differences in post-surgery bleeding (P = 0.208) or hemoglobin changes (P = 0.134) between groups. Control group had higher thrombocytopenia (P = 0.012). Age, surgery duration, and coagulation tests were similar (P > 0.05).
text: Desmopressin did not significantly affect thrombocytopenia rate compared to placebo (P = 0.012). Placebo group had higher thrombocytopenia. No differences in bleeding or hemoglobin changes.

memory: No effect of SR or SR + RT on femoral artery diameter, leg blood flow, or mean arterial pressure (P > 0.05). Heart rate was higher in the fed state (P < 0.0001). Intracellular free phenylalanine enrichments did not differ between legs or across time (P = 0.40, P = 0.22). Source: PMC4562579.
text: Resistance exercise does not significantly affect leg blood flow compared to control (P > 0.05). Source: PMC4562579.

memory: Trametinib improved PFS (4.8 vs 1.5 m, HR 0.45, P<0.001) and 6-m OS (81% vs 67%, HR 0.54, P=0.01) over chemotherapy. Selumetinib showed non-significant OS (9.4 vs 5.2 m, HR 0.8, p=0.21).
text: Oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) significantly improved 6-month overall survival (81% vs 67%, HR 0.54, P=0.01) compared with intravenous chemotherapy (dacarbazine or paclitaxel). Source: Study data.
comparator: intravenous chemotherapy consisting of either dacarbazine (1000mg/m2) or paclitaxel (175mg/m2), every 3weeks
outcome: At 6 months, the rate of overall survival

memory: In [PMC2784472], GD showed trends of greater benefit than placebo across most endpoints. GSRS abdominal pain (p=0.046) and total score (p=0.048) reached significance, with abdominal distension showing a strong trend (p=0.061). SF-36v2 MCS and VAS-Gas scores showed no significant differences.
text: The "Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula" showed trends of greater benefit than placebo on GSRS VAS-Gas scores, though no significant differences were found (PMC2784472).
intervention: Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) group
outcome: Improvement in GSRS (Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale) VAS-Gas score - in adults with post prandial intestinal gas-related symptoms and no GI diagnoses

memory: D-serine reduced legal errors in the Groton Maze Learning test (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03), with no significant effects on n-back, Set-Shifting, visual attention, or mood (p > 0.05).
text: D-serine significantly reduced legal errors in the Groton Maze Learning Test compared to control (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03). No significant effects were observed on other cognitive domains.
outcome: Groton Maze Learning Test legal errors

memory: All three mouth rinses significantly reduced salivary S. mutans counts individually. No statistically significant differences were found between rinses, despite numerical variations.
text: Chlorhexidine mouth rinse significantly reduces Streptococcus mutans counts compared to control, but no significant differences were found between rinses despite numerical variations (source).

memory: Postoperative TNR showed no significant difference between 33 patients and 30 controls. Nasal consonant analysis revealed no pre- or post-surgery differences, but F3 formant frequency differed significantly from controls at 1 and 3 months (P=0.022, P=0.024). /a/ vowel analysis showed no significant differences pre- or post-surgery or compared to controls.
text: Septoplasty did not significantly improve "a" vowel production compared to controls. While F3 formant frequency showed differences, /a/ vowel analysis revealed no significant pre- or post-surgery changes. Source: Working notes.

memory: Rejection rates remained stable pre- and post-training (p > 0.05). HCP scores improved significantly (p < 0.05). Error rates decreased for unaccountable preanalytical (0.32→0.30) and request form (0.17→0.15). Source: PMC5419060.
text: The phlebotomy training program significantly improved HCP scores (p < 0.05) and reduced error rates in preanalytical and request form processes, though rejection rates remained stable (p > 0.05). Source: PMC5419060.

memory: In the No-IMID subgroup, OSS increased emergency admissions (aRRR 2.12) and appropriate treatment (aRRR 1.98), while reducing antimalarial prescriptions (aRRR 0.49). In IMID-MLP, OSS improved malaria treatment (aRRR 1.26) and AFB-negative empiric treatment (aRRR 2.04).
text: In the IMID-MLP group, on-site support increased the proportion of patients with a negative malaria test result prescribed an antimalarial (aRRR 1.26).
outcome: proportion of patients with a negative malaria test result prescribed an antimalarial in integrated management of infectious diseases (IMID)- mid-level practitioners (MLP) group

memory: VO2 peak improved dose-dependently in exercise groups. Simple Attention showed equivalent improvement vs. controls; Visuospatial Processing showed a dose-response trend. AE were more common in 150 and 225 min/wk groups. Verbal Memory and Reasoning improved similarly across groups, suggesting practice effects.
text: Aerobic exercise at 150 or 225 min/wk improved VO2 peak compared to no exercise, with a dose-dependent effect. Source: Working notes.

memory: No anemia or growth differences between groups. Intervention villages had lower open defecation (p<0.001 for adults, p=0.014 for children <5) and higher sanitation coverage (+19 pp, p<0.001). E. coli levels (p=0.143) and helminth prevalence (p=0.001) were similar. Intervention gains smaller than IHL.
text: The Total Sanitation Campaign significantly reduced open defecation compared to control (p<0.001 for adults, p=0.014 for children <5), with higher sanitation coverage (+19 pp, p<0.001). However, intervention effects were smaller than those of IHL.

memory: Group II showed reduced stain intensity vs. Group I at 14d (P=0.025) and 21d (P=0.005). Groups II and III had significantly less plaque than Group I at 1st, 2nd, and 3rd weeks (P=0.000). Group III had less plaque than Group I at 3 weeks, but this was not significant (P=0.104).
text: Group III (H2O2 1.5% + CHX) showed a non-significant reduction in plaque compared to Group I (CHX 0.2% alone) at 3 weeks (P=0.104). Groups II and III had significantly less plaque than Group I during all weeks (P=0.000).
intervention: group III used hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) 1.5% followed by chlorhexidine (CHX)
comparator: group I rinsed with chlorhexidine (CHX) 0.2% alone
outcome: amount of plaque formed at end of week 3

memory: Paricalcitol vs. placebo in children showed greater iPTH reduction (P < 0.001) and fewer adverse events (P = 0.005). 27.8% achieved ≥30% iPTH reduction (P = 0.045). Fewer reached KDOQI range (P = 0.128). No significant lab changes. See Fig. 4.
text: Paricalcitol compared with control showed greater iPTH reduction (P < 0.001) but no significant effect on calcium levels. Fewer adverse events were reported with paricalcitol (P = 0.005). Source: Working notes.

memory: Placebo vs PR-fampridine showed similar AE rates (77% vs 75%). PR-fampridine improved MSWS-12, TUG speed, and BBS scores (p < 0.05). Post-hoc analysis showed higher PGIC improvement at week 2 (46% vs 26%, p=0.023). Study included 132 patients across 24 sites in 6 countries.
text: Prolonged-release fampridine improved TUG speed compared to placebo (p < 0.05) over 24 weeks. This conclusion is based on a study involving 132 patients across 24 sites in 6 countries.
outcome: Improvement in Timed Up and Go (TUG) speed during 24 weeks

memory: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced new bone events (P=0.004), urinary CTx (P<0.001), and skeletal event risk (HR 0.62, P<0.0001) vs placebo. Risk reduction mainly from radiotherapy/surgery events (P<0.001, P=0.037).
text: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced the risk of skeletal events compared to placebo (HR 0.62, P<0.0001), primarily due to fewer radiotherapy/surgery events. It also reduced new bone events (P=0.004) and urinary CTx (P<0.001).
outcome: risk reduction for a skeletal event

memory: 5-FU 0.5%/SA 10% showed higher CCC (49.5% vs. 18.2%, OR 3.9, P=0.0006) and better TSQM scores (P<0.0064) vs. vehicle at 8 weeks. More AEs (99.1% vs. 83.6%). No significant differences in convenience or side effect scores.
text: The combination of 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% resulted in more treatment-emergent adverse events (99.1% vs. 83.6%) compared to vehicle, though no significant differences were found in convenience or side effect scores (P<0.0064).

memory: No significant difference in smoking cessation effectiveness between bupropion, NRT, or their combination with behavioral support (OR=1.21, 95% CI=0.883–1.67). Abstinence rates: bupropion 27.9%, NRT 24.2%, combination 24.2%. No site or prescription method differences. Source: PMC4282128.
text: Bupropion and NRT show similar effectiveness for smoking cessation, with no significant difference (OR=1.21, 95% CI=0.883–1.67). Abstinence rates were 27.9% for bupropion and 24.2% for NRT. Source: PMC4282128.

memory: IG showed non-significant improvements in 20m sprint and YYIR1C compared to CG. IG had significant decreases in systolic BP, mean arterial BP, BMI, and body fat (p<0.05). Balance and jump performance remained unchanged in both groups. Source: PMC5136709.
text: The "FIFA 11 for Health" programme significantly reduced body fat percentage compared to the control group (p<0.05). Source: PMC5136709.

memory: No significant HITChip differences at 6 months between placebo and L. rhamnosus GG. At 18 months, L. rhamnosus GG increased Anaerostipes caccae (p=0.03) and Eubacterium ventriosum (p=0.04), while placebo showed higher Clostridium difficile (p=0.047).
text: At 18 months, L. rhamnosus GG was associated with lower Clostridium difficile compared to placebo (p=0.047). This suggests a potential protective effect of L. rhamnosus GG against C. difficile colonization at 18 months of age.
outcome: Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age

memory: PROMISE minimal-risk tool showed better discrimination (c-stat 0.805) than CADC (0.730, p < 0.001). Minimal-risk patients had lower typical angina (24.1% vs 42.6%) and lower CAD risk (30.0% vs 47.0%). Both models had poor fit (HL p < 0.001).
text: Patients with minimal-risk had a lower pre-test probability of obstructive CAD (30.0% vs. 47.0%) compared to the remainder of the cohort. The PROMISE minimal-risk tool demonstrated better discrimination (c-stat 0.805) than CADC (0.730, p < 0.001).

memory: No significant differences in postoperative complications, recurrence rates, or pain levels (P > 0.05) between groups. Group II patients resumed normal activities faster (P < 0.05). No soft tissue infections observed in either group.
text: No significant differences in postoperative complications between partial matrix excision and segmental phenolization (P > 0.05). Both groups had similar recurrence rates and pain levels, but group II resumed normal activities faster. No soft tissue infections were observed.

memory: Active treatment reduced pain scores more than placebo (5.5→1.2 vs 4.9→3.9, diff 3.3, P<.001). Placebo had no significant change in headache days. Pain intensity and duration trends favored active treatment (P=.42, .37). Source: PMC4312979.
text: Kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity significantly reduced pain scores more than placebo (5.5→1.2 vs 4.9→3.9, diff 3.3, P<.001). Source: PMC4312979.
intervention: kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity

outcome: 12‐item Short‐Form Health Survey (SF‐12), Mental Component Summary (MCS), Summary of Diabetes Self‐Care Activities (SDSCA)

memory: In a study comparing BT, To, and Co groups, urgency scores decreased by 44.8%, 62.2%, and 60.2%, respectively. To and Co showed greater improvement than BT (p<0.05). Co had greater improvements in frequency and urgency than BT (p<0.05). No difference between To and Co groups.

memory: Superficial wound infection rates were 6.3% (investigational) vs. 2.0% (control), P = .103. Major neurological complications were similar (4.4% vs. 4.0%). Retrograde ejaculation occurred in 3.3% (investigational) and 5.5% (control), P = .515. No significant differences observed.

text: The couples' educational workshop did not significantly affect the preference for normal vaginal delivery compared to the control group (P = 0.017). text: Linagliptin significantly reduced urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) at 24 weeks compared to control (−32% vs. −6%, between-group difference −28%, 95% CI −47 to −2; P=0.0357). This effect was evident by 12 weeks. Source: [PMC3816860].

intervention: 10 μg/kg of Alfentanil, infusion of Alfentanil 1 μg/kg/min

memory: Source [PMC1868022] found that Pap smear at enrollment significantly increased IL-10 levels compared to no intervention, suggesting a regulatory immune response. text: Pap smear at enrollment significantly increased IL-10 levels compared to no intervention, suggesting a regulatory immune response (PMC1868022). No changes in proinflammatory cytokines were observed.

memory: Study [PMC5264222] demonstrated SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, is therapeutically equivalent to etanercept (ETN) in RA patients on methotrexate. At week 24, ACR50 and ACR70 response rates were equivalent, with a 95% CI of the adjusted treatment difference (-9.41% to 4.98%) within the -15% to 15% equivalence margin. SB4 had a significantly lower incidence of anti-drug antibodies (ADA) compared to ETN (0.7% vs. 13.1%, p<0.001), and only one ETN sample showed neutralizing capacity. These findings support SB4's therapeutic equivalence and improved immunogenicity profile over ETN.
text: SB4, an etanercept biosimilar, is therapeutically equivalent to etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate, with equivalent ACR50/ACR70 responses (PMC5264222). SB4 showed lower anti-drug antibodies (0.7% vs. 13.1%, p<0.001) and better immunogenicity profile.
outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: Source [PMC5534217] found no significant difference between peramivir and oseltamivir in days for influenza symptom disappearance (5.26 vs. 5.38 days, P = .65). outcome: The numbers of days required for the disappearance of influenza symptoms

memory: A study [PMC3467590] assessed a web-based CME intervention with performance feedback and quality improvement tools on medication intensification in diabetic patients managed by rural physicians. intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

memory: Study [PMC4330076] identified that in male hypertensive patients, SNPs rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037 on chromosome 11 were significantly associated with ASBP response to bisoprolol, but not to losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide. text: The PEG–lactulose group showed no significant difference in blood ammonia levels compared to the lactulose-only group (p=0.858) [PMC5308129]. PEG–lactulose improved HESA scores and reduced hospital stay. No evidence supports a difference in ammonia levels between groups.
intervention: PEG–lactulose group received the 20-30 grams of lactulose of oral or rectal lactulose, plus 280 grams of PEG in 4 liters of water orally as a single dose in 30-120 minutes

memory: Study [PMC4681902] found that longus colli thickness increased significantly with higher masticatory muscle contraction intensity (p<0.05), particularly when combined with deep cervical flexor training. No significant changes were observed in sternocleidomastoid thickness across contraction intensities (p>0.05). This suggests that higher contraction intensity, such as 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction, may have a greater effect on longus colli thickness compared to 10% maximal voluntary isometric contraction.
text: Higher masticatory muscle contraction intensity, such as 80% maximal voluntary isometric contraction, significantly increases longus colli thickness compared to 10% (p<0.05), particularly when combined with deep cervical flexor training (PMC4681902).

memory: Source [PMC3009979] found no significant difference in hospitalization duration between ampicillin/sulbactam and cefuroxime (median 4 days, IQR 4-4; p = 0.09). text: Ampicillin/sulbactam and cefuroxime had similar effects on hospitalization duration (median 4 days, IQR 4-4; p = 0.09) according to [PMC3009979]. No significant differences were found in infection rates or post-cesarean endometritis.

memory: LCI699 significantly reduced plasma aldosterone concentration at 12 h by 49–63% compared to placebo (P < 0.001). memory: Study [PMC4060171] found no significant differences in hospitalization duration or bed days between system-oriented therapy and reference intervention. System-oriented therapy showed a trend toward better compliance and PANSS scores, though not statistically significant. A significantly higher proportion of the reference group failed to complete follow-up (15/40) compared to the system-oriented group (4/30; P=0.017). Missing data were handled via multiple imputation, with non-significant results. The higher follow-up completion rate in the system-oriented group suggests potential benefits in treatment adherence or engagement. Overall, no significant clinical outcome differences were found, but follow-up completion rates hint at possible advantages.
text: System-oriented therapy showed a higher follow-up completion rate compared to reference intervention (4/30 vs. 15/40, P=0.017), suggesting potential benefits in treatment adherence. No significant differences were found in clinical outcomes like hospitalization duration or PANSS scores.

memory: IPE (4g/day) vs. placebo in diabetes patients (median baseline A1c 6.8%) showed no significant changes in fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR in all groups. text: IPE (4g/day) did not significantly affect fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or HOMA-IR in diabetes patients compared to placebo. However, it reduced lipid markers and hsCRP in total and less-controlled diabetes groups, without adverse glycemic effects. Source: [PMC3718763].
outcome: fasting plasma glucose, A1c, insulin, or homeostasis model assessment-estimated insulin total (all subjects with diabetes—overall median baseline glycosylated hemoglobin A1c [A1c] = 6.8%), better-controlled diabetes (below median baseline A1c), and less-controlled diabetes (above median baseline A1c).

memory: Source [PMC4663570] found no statistically significant differences (Wilcoxon test p = 0.05) in ΔC-reactive protein between "Agave derived fructans" and "Formula" groups at three months of age compared to baseline (20 days old). memory: Source [PMC4440033]: A 12-week study in CKD patients with low vitamin D found that Vitamin D + Calcium (VitD + C) did not significantly reduce pro-inflammatory markers (IL-6, hs-CRP) compared to Calcium alone, except for a reduction in IL-6 among non-diabetics. text: In CKD patients, "Vitamin D + Calcium" did not significantly alter serum IL-10 compared to "Calcium" alone (p = 0.06). Calcium alone caused a significant decrease in IL-10 at weeks 6 and 12. Source: [PMC4440033].

memory: No significant differences (p>0.05) were observed in body weight at slaughter (21.78 kg), hot and cold carcass weights (8.65 kg and 8.59 kg), carcass yields (40.27% and 39.20%), or rib eye area (7.73 cm²) between goats fed sunflower cake vs. soybean meal [PMC4092926]. memory: Source [PMC4727391] found no significant differences in adverse events between laryngeal mask (LM) and endotracheal intubation (ETI). Both methods had similar success rates (LM: 94.4%, ETI: 90.6%), insertion times (LM: 7.58 ± 1.16 s vs. ETI: 7.89 ± 1.52 s), Apgar scores, response time, ventilation time, and successful resuscitation (LM: 86.1%, ETI: 96.9%). memory: Source [PMC5343026] reports that craving persistence is dose-dependent, with classic cigarettes inducing longer-lasting cravings compared to e-cigarettes. No differences in gesture measures were found between products. E-cigarette use did not affect attention, executive function, or working memory. E-cigarettes may serve as a coping mechanism by substituting smoking rituals.
text: Classic cigarettes induce longer-lasting cravings compared to e-cigarettes, according to [PMC5343026]. E-cigarettes may reduce craving persistence and serve as a coping mechanism by substituting smoking rituals. No differences in attention or memory were observed.

memory: SRT2104 significantly reduced body weight (−0.93 kg, 95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) and bradykinin-induced vasodilatation (mean difference −1.291, 95% CI −2.296 to −0.285, p=0.012) compared to placebo. text: Oral SRT2104 (2.0 g/day) for 28 days significantly reduced body weight by −0.93 kg (95% CI −1.72 to −0.15, p=0.0236) compared to placebo in people with T2DM.
outcome: body weight in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)

text: A study found no significant difference between "Natural childbirth preparation" and "Standard antenatal education" on elective Caesarean rates (RR 0.9, 0.6–1.6). Source: [PMC2759981].

memory: A study compared simulation with standardized patients (SP) and mannequins. SP simulations led to significantly higher post-test scores in three out of four scenarios (P=0.01). text: SP-based scenarios significantly improved realism scores compared to mannequin-based scenarios (P=0.002). They also led to higher post-test scores in most scenarios, with a greater improvement in the calcium channel blocker overdose case (P=0.03).

memory: Baseline PDSS scores were similar between exercise (2.4±1.1) and control (2.2±0.8) groups (p=0.76). text: Exercise significantly reduced Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scores compared to control (p=0.02), with greater reductions in the exercise group. No significant differences were found in BDI-II scores (p=0.09).

memory: In a study [PMC3546023], smokers had lower NK cell percentages than nonsmokers (p < 0.0001), with this difference persisting after palmvitee supplementation. Smokers also had higher CD4+ and B cell counts. Vitamin E supplementation increased B cell percentages in nonsmokers but not smokers. Urinary cotinine and serum α1-antitrypsin were higher in smokers (p < 0.05). Palmvitee increased plasma tocopherol and tocotrienol concentrations in both groups from 12 weeks onward (p < 0.05). NK cell percentages remained lower in smokers post-supplementation.
text: In the study [PMC3546023], smokers had lower NK cell percentages than nonsmokers, and this difference remained after 200 mg/day palmvitee supplementation. Thus, palmvitee did not alter the effect of smoking on NK cell percentages.

memory: In a study [PMC4871571], 35 volunteers received CN54rgp140/GLA-AF immunizations. However, home telemonitoring of blood pressure was significantly more costly, with a mean difference of £115.32 per patient (95% CI £83.49 to £146.63; p<0.001). Source: PMC3657667.
text: The hypertension telemonitoring-based service was associated with lower accident and emergency visits but higher costs compared to control. While the difference in visits was not statistically significant (p=0.286), telemonitoring increased costs by £115.32 per patient (p<0.001). Source: PMC3657667.

memory: In the placebo arm, intermittent antidepressant (ADM) use showed a trend toward increased diabetes risk (HR 1.34 [0.99–1.81]). Continuous ADM use was linked to higher diabetes risk compared to no use in the placebo (HR 2.34 [1.32–4.15]) and lifestyle (HR 2.48 [1.45–4.22]) arms, but not in the metformin arm (HR 0.55 [0.25–1.19]). All associations were adjusted for diabetes risk factors.
text: Antidepressant users had higher diabetes risk compared to non-users in placebo (HR 2.34) and lifestyle (HR 2.48) arms, but not in metformin arm (HR 0.55). Adjusted for diabetes risk factors.

memory: BMDMC therapy improved survival in CLP-induced ARDS models, reducing lung elastance, alveolar collapse, tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage cellularity, collagen content, and IL-1β levels, while increasing chemokine expression (KC and MCP-1) in lung tissue. These effects were consistent across ARDS models. At day 7, survival rates for groups C, LPS-SAL, LPS-BMDMC, and sham mice were all 100% (source: PMC3856598).
text: BMDMC therapy reduced alveolar collapse in CLP-induced ARDS models compared to control mice, as shown by decreased lung elastance and tissue changes (PMC3856598).
intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)

memory: Source [PMC5282794] found that infants delivered via vaginal operative delivery using plastic cup ventouse had lower pain responses than those with metal cups (p < 0.001). Metal cups were linked to higher rates of scalp trauma (cephalhematoma and skin abrasions/lacerations): 13.2% (12/90) vs. 6.6% (2/30) for plastic cups, though this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.51). The proportion of EDIN ≥ 5 was higher in the metal/placebo group compared to the plastic/placebo group, but this difference was also not statistically significant.
text: Infants delivered with plastic cup ventouse had lower pain responses than those with metal cups (p < 0.001). Metal cups were associated with higher scalp trauma rates, though not statistically significant.

memory: Source [PMC2825665] indicates antibody responders showed significant improvements over placebo on dementia scales. On the Dependence Scale, responders had a significant difference (p=0.033). For the DAD scale, responders experienced significantly less decline after 4.6 years (p=0.015). On the CDR-SOB scale, responders had 20.2% less decline than placebo, though not statistically significant (p=0.185). Mean changes were 7.63 ± 4.48 for placebo and 6.09 ± 4.75 for responders. These results suggest potential benefits of the antibody treatment in slowing dementia-related decline.
text: Synthetic Aβ42 (AN1792) showed a significant improvement compared to placebo on the Dependence Scale (p=0.033) in antibody responders, suggesting potential benefits in slowing dementia-related decline [PMC2825665].

memory: Levamizol added to intramuscular and intradermal vaccinations increased antibody titers by 514.2 IU/L (p = 0.001) and 176.1 IU/L (p = 0.01), respectively, according to [PMC1540413]. Group A had a 60% seroconversion rate compared to 70% in group B, but the difference was not statistically significant.
text: The effect of "40 μg HB vaccine intramuscularly" compared with "20 μg HB vaccine intradermally" on the percent of seroconversion rate was not statistically significant, as group A had 60% versus group B with 70% (p > 0.05), according to the provided data.
"Physical activity + Healthy eating" significantly reduces cardiovascular mortality compared to control (OR 0.49–0.70, P<0.001–0.031). Source: PMC4973627.

memory: A web-based multicomponent intervention did not significantly improve medication intensification for glucose, BP, or lipids in rural diabetic patients. Unadjusted analyses showed increased A1c medication intensification in both intervention (26.4% to 32.6%, p=0.022) and control arms (24.8% to 31.1%, p=0.033), with no significant difference in BP intensification (p=0.080). Adjusted analyses confirmed A1c intensification (intervention AOR 1.37, control AOR 1.41). No group-by-time interaction was observed (p=0.948). Source: PMC3467590.
text: The intervention showed no significant incremental benefit over the control group in improving medication intensification for glucose, BP, or lipids (p=0.948). Source: PMC3467590.
intervention: web-based continuing medical education (CME), performance feedback and quality improvement tools

memory: Diabetic mice showed elevated NT immunoreactivity and nitro-oxidative stress in LV myocardium, which cinaciguat reduced. Cinaciguat decreased PDE-5 expression and increased PKG activity (p-VASP/VASP ratio). Contractility indexes Ees and PRSW were reduced in diabetic mice, with cinaciguat improving PRSW and showing a trend for Ees improvement (P = 0.092). Cinaciguat enhanced systolic (PRSW: 66.8 ± 3.6 mmHg) and diastolic (Tau: 14.9 ± 0.6 ms) function and reduced EDPVR slope (P = 0.063). These findings suggest cinaciguat prevents DM-related myocardial changes and improves cardiac function. (Source: PMC4628236)
text: The sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks reduced nitro-oxidative stress in diabetic mice compared to placebo, as shown by decreased NT immunoreactivity and improved cardiac function (PMC4628236).
intervention: the sGC activator cinaciguat (10 mg/kg/day) orally for 8 weeks

memory: Lemon verbena extract showed a trend toward increased glutathione peroxidase (GPxP) activity (p = 0.0681) and reduced exercise-related muscle strength loss (p = 0.0311) compared to placebo. There was also a trend toward less movement-induced pain (p = 0.0788). Exercise-induced CK levels were not significantly different between groups (p = 0.9412), though both showed significant time effects. IL-6 increased post-exercise with high variability but no group differences (p = 0.5824). MVC was significantly less reduced in the lemon verbena group (p = 0.0311), with a significant time effect (p = 0.0051). Source: PMC5781260.
text: Lemon verbena extract showed a significant reduction in exercise-related muscle strength loss (p = 0.0311) compared to placebo, with a trend toward increased GPxP activity (p = 0.0681) and less movement-induced pain (p = 0.0788). Source: PMC5781260.

memory: Arformoterol improved quality of life (SGRQ and CCQ) compared to placebo (P < .05). Trough FEV1 and FVC increased more with arformoterol than with placebo (0.051 L, P = .030 and 0.075 L, P = .018). Adverse event rates were similar between groups (72.9% vs 68.2%). Arformoterol reduced first respiratory SAEs by 50% compared to placebo (P = .003). Source: [PMC4251615].
text: Arformoterol significantly improved quality of life (SGRQ and CCQ) compared to placebo (P < .05). It also increased FEV1 and FVC more than placebo (P = .030 and .018). Adverse events were similar, but arformoterol reduced first respiratory SAEs by 50% (P = .003). Source: [PMC4251615].
outcome: improvements in quality of life (overall St. George's Hospital Respiratory Questionnaire and Clinical COPD Questionnaire)

memory: In a study [PMC3432828], GX reduced Ca absorption and bone breaking force. Rats on FOS diets (GF, GIF) showed improved Ca absorption and preserved bone strength compared to controls (GC; p<0.05), suggesting FOS prevents bone fragility. GIF-fed rats had higher equol levels than GI-fed rats (p<0.05), while isoflavone alone did not prevent decreased bone breaking force. These findings indicate that FOS enhances Ca absorption and bone strength, likely through promotion of equol production.
text: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF) improved femur bone strength compared to Control diet (GC) by enhancing calcium absorption and promoting equol production (PMC3432828). GIF showed greater benefits than GF alone.
intervention: Fructooligosaccharides diet (GF) and Isoflavone + Fructooligosaccharides diet (GIF)

memory: PTEF significantly increased after albuterol and saline treatments, with no difference between them (P = 0.6). TEF10 and 25/PT significantly decreased after albuterol (P < 0.05). No significant changes were observed in VPTEF/VE or tPTEF/tE with either treatment (Table 3). The decrease in TEF10 and 25/PT was consistent following albuterol administration, as noted in the study.
text: Nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline) significantly decreased the 25/PT ratio compared to saline (3 ml), while both treatments increased PTEF without significant differences between them (P = 0.6).
intervention: nebulized albuterol (0.15 mg/kg in 3 ml saline)
outcome: ratio of the tidal expiratory flow at 25% of the remaining tidal volume to PTEF (25/PT)

memory: A clinical study examined male patients with mild obesity (BMI <32 kg/m²) and moderate hypertension (mean OBP 152/100 mm Hg). Genome-wide analysis of ~630,000 SNPs assessed antihypertensive responses to losartan, bisoprolol, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. Three SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) showed genome-wide significant associations with ASBP response to bisoprolol (source: PMC4330076).
text: Bisoprolol showed genome-wide significant associations with ASBP response linked to SNPs rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037 on chromosome 11, whereas losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide did not (PMC4330076).
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

memory: Source [PMC5370803]: ANOVA revealed reduced pulmonary function (FVC%, FEV1%, PEF%, FEV1/FVC, DLCO%, DLCO/VA%) in HbA1c ≥8.0 group. No significant differences in VC%, FEV1%, MVV%, TLC%. At week 26, 18.18% (8/44) in intervention vs 10.81% (4/37) in controls achieved HbA1c ≤7.0% (P > 0.05). No serious cutaneous AEs. Intervention group had greater TC reduction (−4.27 vs −1.59 mg/dL, P < 0.05) and BMI decline (−2.07 vs −1.78 kg/m2, P > 0.05).
text: The combination of metformin (500 mg, bid po) and alogliptin (25 mg, qd po) did not significantly improve the proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤7.0% compared to metformin (1000 mg, bid po) (18.18% vs 10.81%, P > 0.05) (Source: PMC5370803).
intervention: metformin (500 mg, bid po) combined with alogliptin (25 mg, qd po)
outcome: proportion of patients with glycosylated hemoglobinA1c (HbA1c) ≤7.0%

memory: A longitudinal study [PMC4957966] found that FAST treatment significantly increased pulse rate (P = 0.022), mean arterial pressure (MAP), systolic blood pressure (sBP), and diastolic blood pressure (dBP) compared to SLOW treatment (P = 0.035; P = 0.046; P = 0.035). No significant differences were observed in venous acid-base variables, electrolytes, oxygen saturations, haemoglobin, glucose, lactate, BNP-NT, cardiac index (CI), systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI), or oxygen delivery (DO2) between the two treatments. Results are detailed in Table 2 of the source article.
text: FAST treatment significantly increased pulse rate, MAP, sBP, and dBP compared to SLOW treatment (P ≤ 0.046). No significant differences were found in other haemodynamic variables. Source: [PMC4957966].

memory: No significant difference in post-surgery bleeding rates was observed between group D and the control group (P = 0.208). Thrombocytopenia occurred more frequently in the control group (P = 0.012). Both groups showed significant postoperative Hb decreases (P = 0.0001), but no significant difference between groups (P = 0.134). No significant differences were found between groups in age, gender, pump time, clamp time, surgery duration, complications, or changes in hemoglobin and coagulation tests (P > 0.05).
text: Desmopressin did not significantly affect post-surgery bleeding rates compared to placebo (P = 0.208). However, thrombocytopenia occurred more frequently in the placebo group (P = 0.012). No significant differences were found in other parameters between the groups.

memory: Source [PMC4562579] found no effect of SR and SR + RT on femoral artery diameter, leg blood flow, or mean arterial pressure. Heart rate was higher in the fed state (P < 0.0001), but leg blood flow did not differ between legs. Intracellular free phenylalanine enrichments were similar across SR and SR + RT conditions, both fasted and fed (P = 0.40 for legs, P = 0.22 for time). No significant differences were observed between SR and SR + RT in the measured parameters.
text: Resistance exercise does not significantly affect leg blood flow compared to control, as shown in a study (PMC4562579) where no differences were observed in leg blood flow between resistance exercise and control conditions.

memory: In a clinical study [PMC3626705], trametinib significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) compared to chemotherapy (median 4.8 vs. 1.5 months; HR 0.45; P < 0.001). At 6 months, overall survival (OS) was 81% in the trametinib group versus 67% in the chemotherapy group (HR 0.54; P = 0.01). Selumetinib showed a median OS of 9.4 months vs. 5.2 months in the control group, but the difference was not statistically significant (HR 0.8; 95% CI 0.56-1.14; p = 0.21).
text: Oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) significantly improved 6-month overall survival (81%) compared to intravenous chemotherapy (67%; HR 0.54; P = 0.01) [PMC3626705].
comparator: intravenous chemotherapy consisting of either dacarbazine (1000mg/m2) or paclitaxel (175mg/m2), every 3weeks
outcome: At 6 months, the rate of overall survival

memory: In study [PMC2784472], GD showed a trend toward greater benefit over placebo across most endpoints, though not all reached statistical significance. The probiotic group had significant improvements in GSRS abdominal pain subscore (p=0.046) and GSRS total score (p=0.048), with a strong trend for GSRS abdominal distension subscore (p=0.061). Benefits were observed in most outcomes, except for SF-36v2 MCS and VAS-Gas score, where no directional differences were seen.
text: In the study [PMC2784472], the GD group showed a trend toward greater improvement in GSRS VAS-Gas score compared to placebo, though it did not reach statistical significance. Most other endpoints showed significant benefits.
intervention: Digestive AdvantageTM Gas Defense Formula (GD) group
outcome: Improvement in GSRS (Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale) VAS-Gas score - in adults with post prandial intestinal gas-related symptoms and no GI diagnoses

memory: D-serine reduced legal errors on the Groton Maze Learning test (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03), suggesting improved spatial memory, learning, and problem-solving in older adults. No significant effects were observed on the n-back working memory test (accuracy, p > 0.1), Set-Shifting task (extra-dimensional shift errors, p = 0.47), or visual attention test (errors, p > 0.7). Mood was unaffected (p > 0.05). These findings indicate a specific benefit of D-serine on spatial memory tasks without broad cognitive enhancement. Source: [PMC4914255].
text: D-serine reduced legal errors on the Groton Maze Learning Test (F(3, 38) = 4.74, p = 0.03), suggesting improved spatial memory and problem-solving in older adults, compared to control. No significant effects were observed on other cognitive tasks. Source: [PMC4914255].
outcome: Groton Maze Learning Test legal errors

memory: All three mouth rinses significantly reduced salivary S. mutans counts when used individually. No statistically significant differences were found between the rinses in terms of their effectiveness, based on pairwise comparisons.
text: Chlorhexidine mouth rinse significantly reduces Streptococcus mutans counts compared to control, but no significant difference was found between chlorhexidine and other rinses (Source: Working notes).

memory: Postoperative TNR showed no significant difference between 33 patients and 30 healthy volunteers. Nasal consonant /n/ analysis revealed no significant pre- and post-surgery changes at 1 and 3 months, but significant differences in F3 formant frequency compared to controls at both time points (P=0.022 and P=0.024). For /a/ vowel analysis, no significant pre- and post-surgery differences were found, and no significant differences compared to the control group were observed (Table 3).
text: Septoplasty did not significantly improve "a" vowel production compared to controls, as no significant pre- and post-surgery differences or group differences were observed (Table 3).

memory: Sample rejection rates remained stable pre- and post-training (p > 0.05). Preanalytical errors, including unaccountable (0.32% to 0.30%, p = 0.85) and request form errors (0.17% to 0.15%, p = 0.85), showed minimal change. HCP questionnaire scores significantly improved at all sites (p < 0.05): CHC A (63% to 96%), CHC B (58% to 93%), CDC C (60% to 97%), CDC D (63% to 97%). [PMC5419060]
text: The phlebotomy training program significantly improved phlebotomy questionnaire scores compared to the control (p < 0.05). Scores increased from 58% to 93% across sites [PMC5419060].

memory: No-IMID subgroup: OSS increased emergency/priority admissions (aRRR=2.12, p=0.006) and appropriate emergency treatment (aRRR=1.98, p<0.001), while decreasing antimalarial prescriptions for negative tests (aRRR=0.49, p=0.004). Overall, OSS increased appropriate emergency treatment (aRRR=2.00, p=0.003) and reduced antimalarial prescriptions (aRRR=0.65, p=0.006). IMID-MLP subgroup: OSS improved appropriate antimalarial treatment (aRRR=1.26, p=0.005) and empiric treatment for AFB-negative patients (aRRR=2.04, p=0.005). [PMC4972969]
text: In the IMID-MLP group, OSS improved appropriate antimalarial treatment (aRRR=1.26, p=0.005) and empiric treatment for AFB-negative patients (aRRR=2.04, p=0.005), but did not directly address the proportion of patients with negative malaria tests prescribed antimalarials. [PMC4972969]
outcome: proportion of patients with a negative malaria test result prescribed an antimalarial in integrated management of infectious diseases (IMID)- mid-level practitioners (MLP) group

memory: VO2 peak increased dose-dependently with exercise. In per-protocol exercisers (n=77), Simple Attention improved similarly across exercise groups vs. controls, while Visuospatial Processing showed a dose-response trend. Groups exercising 150min/wk (n=40) and 225min/wk (n=36) had more adverse events (AEs) than 75min/wk (n=15), mostly mild. Visuospatial Processing improved dose-dependently, though 75min/wk and 150min/wk groups were similar. Verbal Memory and Reasoning improved across all groups, including controls, suggesting a practice effect. Source: [PMC4497726]
text: Aerobic exercise at 150 min/wk or 225 min/wk significantly increased VO2 peak compared to no exercise, with a dose-dependent effect. Source: [PMC4497726]

memory: No differences in anemia or growth outcomes between groups. Intervention villages showed reduced open defecation (adult men: 75% vs. 84%, p=0.001; adult women: 73% vs. 83%, p<0.001; children <5: 84% vs. 89%, p=0.014) and improved sanitation coverage (41.4% vs. 22.6%, p<0.001). Modest hygiene improvements were observed. E. coli presence in water sources was similar (74% control vs. 70% intervention, p=0.143). No significant difference in helminth prevalence (p=0.001, CI −0.021 to 0.023).
text: The Total Sanitation Campaign significantly reduced open defecation compared to control (p<0.001 for adults, p=0.014 for children <5). Sanitation coverage also improved in intervention villages. No significant differences were found in anemia, growth, helminth prevalence, or E. coli presence in water. (Source: Study)

memory: Group II showed significantly lower stain intensity than Group I at 14 and 21 days (P = 0.025 and 0.005, respectively). Group II also had significantly less plaque than Group I at weeks 1, 2, and 3 (P = 0.000 for all). Group III had significantly less plaque than Group I at weeks 1 (P = 0.000) and 2 (P = 0.017), but not at week 3 (P = 0.104). All comparisons were made against Group I, the control group.
text: Group III (H2O2 1.5% + CHX) had significantly less plaque than Group I (CHX alone) at weeks 1 and 2, but not week 3. Group II showed consistently lower plaque than Group I across all weeks. Source: Study comparing plaque formation after different mouth rinses.
intervention: group III used hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) 1.5% followed by chlorhexidine (CHX)
comparator: group I rinsed with chlorhexidine (CHX) 0.2% alone
outcome: amount of plaque formed at end of week 3

memory: In a study comparing paricalcitol to placebo in children, a higher proportion of the paricalcitol group achieved final iPTH levels within the KDOQI range (33.3% vs. 11.1%), though not statistically significant (P = 0.128). Paricalcitol showed a greater reduction in iPTH from baseline (mean change −72.4 pg/mL; P < 0.001), with 27.8% achieving two consecutive ≥30% reductions versus none in the placebo group (P = 0.045). Adverse events were more common in the placebo group (88.9% vs. 38.9%; P = 0.005). No significant differences were observed in laboratory measures like eGFR, creatinine, calcium, or phosphorus between groups over 12 weeks (Fig. 4).
text: Paricalcitol did not significantly affect calcium levels compared to control in a 12-week study (P = NS). The study showed no significant differences in calcium levels between paricalcitol and placebo groups over 12 weeks.

memory: A 24-week study with 132 MS patients across six countries found PR-fampridine had similar AE rates to placebo (77% vs. 75%). PR-fampridine showed greater improvements in MSWS-12 scores, TUG speed, and BBS total scores. At week 2, 46% of PR-fampridine patients reported improvement on PGIC compared to 26% of placebo patients (p=0.023). Statistically significant improvements were observed in MSWS-12 and TUG speed at multiple thresholds (p<0.05). The results suggest PR-fampridine may provide clinical benefits for MS patients without increasing adverse events.
text: Prolonged-release fampridine significantly improved TUG speed compared to placebo over 24 weeks (p<0.05) without increasing adverse events. This suggests clinical benefits for MS patients. Source: 24-week study with 132 MS patients.
outcome: Improvement in Timed Up and Go (TUG) speed during 24 weeks

memory: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced mean SMPR for new bone events compared to placebo (P=0.004) and decreased urinary CTx by −77.3% versus +11.0% (P<0.001). The ibandronate group had fewer new bone events and fewer measurement periods with events (P=0.008 and 0.015). Multivariate analysis showed a 38% risk reduction for skeletal events (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001), mainly due to fewer events requiring radiotherapy (P<0.001) or surgery (P=0.037). Source: PMC2409647.
text: Oral ibandronate 50 mg significantly reduced the risk of skeletal events compared to placebo, with a 38% risk reduction (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.79, P<0.0001), mainly due to fewer events requiring radiotherapy or surgery. Source: PMC2409647.
outcome: risk reduction for a skeletal event

memory: At 8 weeks post-treatment, 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% significantly improved TSQM satisfaction (69.2 vs. 56.1, P=0.0019) and effectiveness (70.8 vs. 59.2, P=0.0064) compared to vehicle. Complete clinical clearance (CCC) was higher (49.5% vs. 18.2%, OR 3.9, P=0.0006), with more patients achieving PC (69.5% vs. 34.6%, OR 4.9, P<0.0001). Adverse events were more frequent (99.1% vs. 83.6%). ITT and PP analyses confirmed CCC differences. No significant differences in TSQM convenience or side effect scores.
text: The 5-FU 0.5%/salicylic acid 10% treatment significantly increased treatment-emergent adverse events (99.1% vs. 83.6%) compared to vehicle, though it improved efficacy outcomes. Source: Working notes.

memory: No significant difference in smoking cessation effectiveness between bupropion, NRT, and their combination with behavioral support (OR=1.21, 95% CI=0.883–1.67). Abstinence rates were 27.9% for bupropion, 24.2% for NRT, and 24.2% for combination. No site differences in abstinence rates (χ2=13.7, P=0.003), but no treatment effect heterogeneity across sites (χ2=1.24, P=0.745). Bupropion delivery method (direct vs. GP) did not affect abstinence rates (χ2=0.372, P=0.542).
text: Bupropion and NRT show similar effectiveness for smoking cessation, with no significant difference in abstinence rates (OR=1.21, 95% CI=0.883–1.67). Combination with behavioral support did not enhance outcomes. No site or delivery method differences were observed.

memory: In the IG, within-group improvements (p<0.05) were observed for 20 m sprint (4.09±0.29 to 4.06±0.28 s) and YYIR1C performance (852±464 to 896±517 m), though not significantly different from CG. text: The "FIFA 11 for Health" programme significantly reduced body fat percentage (−0.83%) compared to control (−0.04%) over 11 weeks (p<0.05).

memory: No significant differences in HITChip signals at 6 months between L. rhamnosus GG and placebo. text: At 18 months, L. rhamnosus GG was associated with lower Clostridium difficile et rel (0.78 ± 0.60%) compared to placebo (1.19 ± 0.85%, p=0.047). Source: PMC3563445.
outcome: Clostridium difficile et rel at 18 months of age

memory: The PROMISE minimal-risk tool demonstrated better discrimination than the CADC model (c-stat 0.785 vs 0.730, p < 0.001) and improved further to 0.805 (p < 0.001). text: Patients with minimal-risk had a lower pre-test probability of obstructive CAD (30.0% vs 47.0%, p < 0.001) compared to the remainder of the cohort. Source: [PMC5761719]

memory: No significant differences were observed in postoperative complications, recurrences, or pain levels between Group I and Group II (P = 0.688 and P > 0.05, respectively). Both groups had no cases of soft tissue infection. However, Group II demonstrated a significantly shorter time to return to normal daily activities compared to Group I (P < 0.05).
text: No significant differences in postoperative complications were found between partial matrix excision and segmental phenolization (P = 0.688). Both groups had no soft tissue infections, but segmental phenolization allowed a faster return to daily activities.

memory: In a study [PMC4312979], active treatment significantly reduced pain compared to placebo, as measured by VAS scores (5.5 to 1.2 vs. 4.9 to 3.9; 3.3-point difference, 95% CI: 2.3, 4.4; P < .001). text: Kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity significantly reduced pain scores compared to placebo, as measured by VAS scores (3.3-point difference, P < .001). Placebo showed no significant pain reduction. Trends favored KOS for pain intensity and duration, though not statistically significant. (Source: PMC4312979)
intervention: kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity

memory: The primary outcome (PCS) showed no significant 6-month group difference adjusted for baseline. Total cost change (excluding hospital) was $236.92 favoring the intervention, but not significant. No significant differences in CES-D, GAD-7, or self-efficacy. The intervention significantly improved SF-12 general health (MD=3.11, 95% CI 0.05–5.71, P=0.02), MCS (MD=2.74, 95% CI 0.28–5.19, P=0.03), and SDSCA (MD=3.74, 95% CI 0.9–6.57, P=0.01). text: A community-based intervention significantly improved SF-12 MCS (MD=2.74, P=0.03) and SDSCA (MD=3.74, P=0.01) compared to usual care, but not the PCS. Source: [PMC5836873].
outcome: 12‐item Short‐Form Health Survey (SF‐12), Mental Component Summary (MCS), Summary of Diabetes Self‐Care Activities (SDSCA)

memory: In a study comparing three groups (BT, To, Co), mean urgency scores decreased by 44.8%, 62.2%, and 60.2%, respectively. memory: Source article [PMC4215531] found that 20 daily 1-hour sessions of facial affect training (FAT) significantly increased alpha power during the pre-recognition period of the FAR criterion task compared to prestimulus baseline within the FAT group (F(1,18) = 5.61, p = .03). This indicates that FAT enhances alpha power over time. The study also showed significant improvements in cognitive domains such as Processing Speed, Attentional Vigilance, and Visual Learning in the FAT group over time. A Domain × Time interaction (F(6,324) = 4.05, p = .001) supported these cognitive improvements. When comparing FAT with treatment-as-usual (TAU), a significant Intervention × Time interaction (F(1,36) = 4.78, p = .04) showed greater improvement in the FAT group, while TAU showed nonsignificant decline. These results suggest that FAT may modulate neural activity, as evidenced by increased alpha power, and improve cognitive outcomes. The findings support FAT as a potential intervention to enhance neural and cognitive functioning. The evidence comes from within-group analyses of the FAT group and comparisons with the TAU group. The study highlights the potential of FAT to influence both alpha power and cognitive performance in specific domains.
text: Twenty daily 1-hour sessions of facial affect training (FAT) significantly increased alpha power during the pre-recognition period compared to baseline (F(1,18) = 5.61, p = .03). This suggests FAT enhances alpha power over time.

memory: Excerpts from source article [PMC4173331]: Adding clonidine to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RCF) did not significantly affect hemodynamic parameters compared to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) or ropivacaine-clonidine (RC) groups (P>0.05). No significant differences in analgesic effects were observed between the groups. However, the RF group had a significantly higher incidence of nausea/vomiting (40%) compared to the RC group (15%) and the RCF group (10%) (P<0.05). The study suggests that RCF does not significantly improve or worsen hemodynamic stability or analgesic properties compared to RF or RC. The reduction of clonidine and fentanyl in the RCF group did not lead to significant differences in hemodynamic or analgesic outcomes relative to other groups. These results indicate that adding clonidine to ropivacaine-fentanyl does not provide additional benefits in terms of hemodynamic stability or analgesia but may help reduce the incidence of nausea and vomiting.
text: Adding clonidine to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RCF) does not significantly affect hemodynamic parameters compared to ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) (P>0.05). RCF may reduce nausea/vomiting incidence compared to RF (PMC4173331).

memory: Study [PMC5684963] found that low glycemic index (LGI) interventions significantly reduced glycemic response (GR) after lunch compared to high glycemic index (HGI) interventions (p = 0.02). Over 48 hours, HGI caused a significantly greater mean amplitude of glycemic excursion (MAGE) than LGI (p = 0.03). Additionally, the daily total area under the curve (AUC) was significantly higher for HGI than LGI (p = 0.03), with a notable reduction in AUC on day 2 of LGI treatment (p = 0.03). These results suggest that LGI diets lead to more stable glycemic responses after lunch and over a 48-hour period compared to HGI diets. The study supports the potential of LGI interventions in managing postprandial glycemic fluctuations, especially following lunch and over extended timeframes. The findings highlight the importance of dietary glycemic index in modulating glycemic control and may inform dietary recommendations for individuals at risk of or managing conditions related to glycemic instability.
text: A low glycemic index (LGI) intervention significantly reduces glycemic response after lunch compared to a high glycemic index (HGI) intervention (p = 0.02). Study [PMC5684963].

memory: Source article [PMC4141382] evaluated the effect of "Caudal Sufentanil + neostigmine" (Group CSuNeo and Group CSuNeoAdr) versus "Caudal Sufentanil" (Group CSu and Group CSuAdr) on the need for Dipyrone as rescue analgesia. Patients receiving the combination had a significantly longer time to first Dipyrone administration (10-11 h) compared to other groups (P < 0.05). They also required lower total Dipyrone doses over 24 hours (P < 0.005), indicating reduced analgesic requirements. The addition of neostigmine to caudal sufentanil was associated with improved analgesic efficacy. Intraoperative isoflurane consumption was similar among Group CSuNeo, Group CSuNeoAdr, and Group IVSu (P > 0.05), but lower than in groups receiving caudal sufentanil alone or with adrenaline (Group CSu = Group CSuAdr) (P < 0.02). VAS scores for sedation on reversal of anesthesia were lower in Group CSuNeo and Group CSuNeoAdr compared to Group CSu, Group CSuAdr, and Group IVSu (P < 0.005), suggesting better sedation outcomes. These findings support that adding neostigmine to caudal sufentanil may enhance analgesic efficacy and reduce the need for additional analgesics like Dipyrone.
text: Adding neostigmine to caudal sufentanil significantly delays the need for Dipyrone (10-11 h vs. other groups, P < 0.05) and reduces total 24-hour Dipyrone use (P < 0.005), indicating improved analgesic efficacy (PMC4141382).

memory: Source article [PMC5320759] found no significant difference in intubation success rates at first, second, and third attempts between the transillumination-assisted technique group (T group) and the midline approach technique group (R group) (P > 0.05). Intubation times were similar overall (P > 0.05), though T group patients who succeeded on the second attempt had significantly longer intubation times (P = 0.0006). The overall success rate was not significantly different between groups (P > 0.05). However, the T group had higher post-intubation complication rates: dry throat (52.2% vs. 40.4%, P = 0.020), sore throat (26.8% vs. 16.8%, P = 0.009), and hoarseness (14% vs. 8%, P = 0.045). No significant difference in intubation time was observed among successfully intubated cases (P > 0.05).
text: The transillumination-assisted technique group (T group) showed no significant difference in intubation success rates at first, second, and third attempts compared to the midline approach technique group (R group) (P > 0.05).
outcome: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempt

memory: Source article [PMC3525032] found that cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation were significantly higher than baseline in both the PLMA and ETT groups (p = 0.001). However, cortisol levels in the PLMA group were significantly lower than in the ETT group following CO2 insufflation (p = 0.024). No significant differences were observed between or within groups for adrenalin, noradrenalin, or dopamine levels. The study shows that both PLMA and ETT lead to increased cortisol levels compared to baseline after CO2 insufflation, but the PLMA may elicit a smaller cortisol response than ETT. The study does not directly compare PLMA or ETT with baseline cortisol levels, only comparing the two groups after CO2 insufflation. These findings suggest that the type of airway management device may influence the cortisol response to CO2 insufflation. The results support the hypothesis that airway management techniques can affect the stress response, as measured by cortisol levels. However, further research is needed to directly compare PLMA and ETT with baseline cortisol levels in the context of CO2 insufflation.
text: Both PLMA and ETT significantly increased cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation compared to baseline (p = 0.001). PLMA induced a smaller cortisol response than ETT (p = 0.024). No significant differences were found for other stress hormones. (Source: PMC3525032)
outcome: cortisol levels 20 minutes after CO2 insufflation

memory: The study compared "Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs" with "No interventions" on baseline characteristics. Both groups were comparable in demographic data and baseline QOL scores across performance, health, socioeconomic, psychological, spiritual, and familial dimensions, as well as satisfaction and importance (PMC4776564). Independent t-tests confirmed no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the groups. Post-intervention results showed significantly higher QOL scores in the satisfaction area for the intervention group compared to the control group, both immediately [70.7 (8.5) vs. 59.2 (12.5)] and 1 month after [75.2 (7.4) vs. 59.4 (12.9)] (P < 0.05). A similar trend was observed in the importance area, with significantly higher scores in the intervention group immediately [73.6 (5.8) vs. 65.7 (7.5)] and 1 month post-intervention [76.3 (8.1) vs. 66.8 (8.5)] (P < 0.05). These findings suggest that hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs positively influenced QOL dimensions of satisfaction and importance. The comparable baseline characteristics between groups ensure the validity of the intervention's impact on post-intervention outcomes. The study highlights the potential effectiveness of such interventions in enhancing QOL related to satisfaction and importance, while maintaining balanced baseline characteristics between the groups.
text: The study found no significant differences in baseline characteristics between groups receiving hope-promoting religious interventions and those receiving no interventions (PMC4776564). Both groups were comparable in demographics, QOL scores, and other baseline measures.
intervention: Hope-promoting interventions based on religious beliefs

memory: Butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream (Gynazole-1) demonstrated a faster median time to first relief of symptoms (17.5 hours) compared to oral fluconazole 150 mg tablets (Diflucan) (22.9 hours), with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001). At 12 hours post-treatment, 44.4% of butoconazole patients experienced first symptom relief, compared to 29.1% of fluconazole patients (p = 0.044). By 24 hours post-treatment, 72.8% of butoconazole patients reported first symptom relief, compared to 55.7% of fluconazole patients (p = 0.024). However, no significant differences were observed between the two treatment groups in terms of time to total relief of symptoms or recurrence of infection within 30 days of treatment. These findings indicate that butoconazole nitrate provides more rapid initial symptom relief compared to fluconazole, though both treatments are comparable in terms of overall symptom resolution and recurrence rates. Source: [PMC1784583].
text: Butoconazole nitrate 2% vaginal cream provides a faster median time to first relief of symptoms (17.5 hours) compared to oral fluconazole 150 mg (22.9 hours; p < 0.001). Source: [PMC1784583].
intervention: butoconazole nitrate 2% Site Release vaginal cream (Gynazole-1)
outcome: The median time to first relief of symptoms

memory: A study evaluated the effect of "Vit D as 50 000 IU/week" versus "placebo" on fasting blood sugar (FBS), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1C), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP). Baseline serum vitamin D levels were comparable between groups. After the intervention, serum vitamin D levels were significantly elevated in the Vit D group. However, no statistically significant differences were observed between the groups for FBS, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP (P>0.05). A significant difference in proteinuria levels was noted between groups pre- and post-intervention (70.38±553.71 vs. 215.89±451.44, P=0.028). These results suggest that while vitamin D supplementation effectively increased serum vitamin D levels, it did not significantly impact the metabolic or inflammatory markers assessed. Source: [PMC5106877].
text: Vitamin D supplementation (50,000 IU/week) did not significantly affect FBS, HbA1C, ESR, or CRP compared to placebo (P>0.05). Source: [PMC5106877].
outcome: fasting blood sugar (FBS), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1C), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels

memory: Source article [PMC2888205] found that LPA led to significantly greater pain reduction compared to FME (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67). Baseline pain scores were 21.6 ± 9.8 for the LPA group, which decreased slightly post-intervention to 21.2 ± 11.3. The FME group had a mean change of 0.8 (-0.35 to 1.9), with no significant difference (P = 0.172). LPA also showed significant improvements in FIQ scores (P = .032; Cohen's d = .53). The study included 84 participants, with 73 completing post-intervention assessments. No significant differences were found between groups in BMI or fatigue severity post-intervention. These results suggest that LPA may be more effective than FM education in reducing pain in individuals with fibromyalgia.
text: Lifestyle physical activity (LPA) significantly reduced pain more than fibromyalgia education (FME) (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67). Pain scores slightly decreased in LPA (21.6 ± 9.8 to 21.2 ± 11.3), while FME showed no significant change (P = 0.172). LPA also improved FIQ scores (P = .032). Source: [PMC2888205].
intervention: lifestyle physical activity (LPA) - 30 minutes of self-selected moderate-intensity LPA, five to seven days per week
