memory: A study compared warming infusions to room temperature infusions and found that warming infusions were associated with faster recovery times post-anesthesia. Patients receiving warming infusions achieved spontaneous breathing sooner (4.06 ± 0.72 minutes) compared to the control group (4.47 ± 0.84 minutes, P = 0.042). Eye opening occurred more quickly in the warming group (6.72 ± 1.73 minutes) versus the control group (8.66 ± 2.03 minutes, P < 0.001). Consciousness recovery was also faster in the warming infusion group (9.91 ± 1.91 minutes) compared to the control group (11.19 ± 1.49 minutes, P = 0.004). Additionally, the mean time to extubation was shorter in the warming group (10.09 ± 1.91 minutes) than in the control group (11.13 ± 1.34 minutes, P = 0.015). However, operation time for patients receiving room temperature fluid was significantly longer (3.094 ± 0.254 minutes) compared to those receiving warmed infusions (2.925 ± 0.216 minutes, P < 0.05). These findings suggest that warming infusions may contribute to improved recovery outcomes following anesthesia.

memory: A 12-week study compared flaxseed and wheat bran supplementation in terms of their effects on waist circumference, BMI, glucose levels, and inflammation. memory: LCI699 doses of 0.5–3 mg significantly inhibited ACTH-stimulated aldosterone levels on Day 6, with peak reductions of 41–64% from baseline (P < 0.001 vs placebo). At 12 h on Day 1, LCI699 doses of 0.5, 1, and 3 mg reduced plasma aldosterone by 49%, 47%, and 63%, respectively (all P < 0.001 vs placebo). Single doses of 30, 100, or 200 mg of LCI699 significantly reduced 24-h urinary cortisol by 34–42% (P ≤ 0.001 vs placebo), though no clear dose-dependence was observed. However, doses ≥100 mg caused a marked increase in cortisol precursor 11-deoxycortisol (942% and 584% for 100 mg and 200 mg, respectively; P < 0.001 vs placebo), likely due to off-target inhibition of 11-β hydroxylase. In contrast, eplerenone 100 mg caused a 29% increase in pre-ACTH aldosterone levels on Day 6 (P ≤ 0.01 vs placebo) and a 63% increase in peak aldosterone levels following ACTH stimulation (Figure 7A). These findings highlight the differential effects of LCI699 and eplerenone on aldosterone regulation and cortisol metabolism.

memory: A 12-week study compared calcitriol + calcium carbonate (Vitamin D + C) to calcium carbonate alone in CKD patients with low vitamin D levels, examining pro-inflammatory biomarkers: IL-6, hs-CRP, and IL-10. No significant differences were observed between groups in IL-6 or hs-CRP reduction. However, non-diabetic participants in the Vitamin D + C group showed a notable decrease in IL-6. Serum IL-10 levels were maintained in the Vitamin D + C group (p = 0.06), while the calcium-only group experienced significant decreases at weeks 6 and 12. The data were presented in a table with mean values and p-values for each group. These findings suggest that calcitriol may offer benefits in reducing IL-6 for non-diabetic CKD patients, though no overall significant improvement in inflammatory markers was found compared to calcium carbonate alone. The study highlights the complex relationship between vitamin D supplementation and inflammation in CKD, with potential differences based on diabetes status. Source data included mean values and p-values, supporting these conclusions.

memory: A study compared sevoflurane (SEVO) and isoflurane (ISOF) during surgery, evaluating the impact of fentanyl boluses on the surgical stress index (SSI). Fentanyl boluses had a similar effect on SSI in both groups, but SSI values were higher in the SEVO group compared to the ISOF group, suggesting potentially greater surgical stress with SEVO. Before fentanyl administration, minimum alveolar concentration (MAC) and surgical emergence (SE) values were comparable between the groups. MAC values were 0.74 ± 0.12 for SEVO and 0.77 ± 0.17 for ISOF (P = .32), while SE values were 43.5 ± 8.1 for SEVO and 45.2 ± 8.3 for ISOF (P = .47). After fentanyl boluses, changes in SE and heart rate (HR) were similar between the groups, and MAC values remained stable in both groups. These findings suggest that while both anesthetics respond similarly to fentanyl in terms of hemodynamic and anesthetic depth parameters, SEVO may be associated with a higher SSI, indicating potentially greater surgical stress. (Source: PMC2911596)

Source article [PMC5447816] found that personality traits and learning method influence microsuture performance. Students with higher Extraversion ("E") scores completed the suturing test significantly faster than those with average E scores (regression coefficient = −418.2, P = 0.0118). Those with lower Agreeableness ("A") scores showed a non-significant trend toward faster task completion compared to average A scorers (regression coefficient = −290.9, P = 0.057). 

The simulator-learning group outperformed the video-learning group in the NUMSAS length score (median = 15.0 vs. 13.5, P = 0.02673), but overall NUMSAS scores were not significantly different (video-learning median = 52.0, simulator-learning median = 54.0, P = 0.11287). The simulator group also completed the task significantly faster than the video group. These findings suggest that both personality traits (Extraversion and Agreeableness) and learning method (simulator vs. video) affect performance in microsuture tasks.

memory: Source article [PMC4112798] describes a clinical trial comparing erlotinib to placebo. No statistically significant differences were found between treatment groups for neurological progression-free survival (PFS), with unadjusted HR = 0.99 (95% CI = 0.62 to 1.58; P = .97) and adjusted HR = 0.95 (95% CI = 0.59 to 1.54; P = .84). memory: A six-month yogic intervention showed significant improvements in psychological and well-being domains compared to a control group, as detailed in Table 3 of [PMC4794540]. memory: In a randomized, controlled trial (PMC5689110), patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio using interactive voice-response system/interactive web response to low-dose aripiprazole (5 mg/day for <50 kg, 10 mg/day for ≥50 kg), high-dose aripiprazole (10 mg/day for <50 kg, 20 mg/day for ≥50 kg), or placebo for 8 weeks. Both low- and high-dose aripiprazole groups showed statistically significant improvement in the change from baseline to week 8 in the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale-Total Tic Score (YGTSS-TTS) compared to placebo (p = 0.002 for low-dose; p < 0.0001 for high-dose). The least squares (LS) mean (SE) change from baseline in YGTSS total motor tic score at week 8 was −6.7 (0.9) for low-dose, −8.0 (0.9) for high-dose, and −2.7 (0.8) for placebo. Treatment differences versus placebo were −4.0 (95% CI: −6.2 to −1.9) for low-dose and −5.3 (95% CI: −7.5 to −3.2) for high-dose, with p-values of 0.0002. However, the high-dose group had 10 patients who discontinued treatment, resulting in a higher hazard ratio versus placebo (5.51, p = 0.0278). These findings suggest that both low- and high-dose aripiprazole significantly reduced tic severity compared to placebo, although the high-dose group had a higher discontinuation rate.

memory: In a clinical study comparing artesunate doses and a control group, parasite clearance times (PCTs) were similar between the two artesunate arms (29.8 h and 29.5 h, respectively) but significantly faster than the control group (43.1 h, P<0.001). Median fever clearance times (FCTs) were 17.9, 19.1, and 29.3 h for Arms 1–3, respectively, with artesunate arms showing a significantly faster clinical response compared to the control (P = 0.001). All patients cleared asexual parasitemia within the first week. Cure rates at 28 and 42 days were 97.8% (87.8–99.8%) for Arm 1, 100% (91.1–100%) for Arm 2, and 100% (83.4–100%) for Arm 3. Parasite reduction ratios at 12, 24, 36, and 48 h showed varying degrees of reduction across arms, with Arm 3 demonstrating the most significant reductions. Adverse events were reported in 48 out of 78 recorded cases (61.5%, 95% CI: 49.8–72.1%), but no significant difference in adverse event rates was observed between groups (P = 0.91). Source: [PMC3525560]
text: Artesunate monotherapy (2 or 4 mg/kg/day) significantly reduced median FCT compared to quinine plus doxycycline (17.9–19.1 h vs. 29.3 h, P=0.001). Source: [PMC3525560]
intervention: artesunate monotherapy with 2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily
comparator: quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days

memory: In a study of obese African American patients with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and severe hyperglycemia, metformin and sitagliptin were linked to better outcomes than placebo. Patients who remained in remission had higher DI (P = 0.02) and incremental AUCi (P < 0.001), with no significant changes in Si. Both metformin (HR 0.28 [95% CI 0.10–0.81]) and sitagliptin (HR 0.31 [0.10–0.98]) significantly reduced the risk of hyperglycemia relapse compared to placebo. Relapse-free survival was significantly higher in the metformin and sitagliptin groups than in the placebo group (P = 0.015). A Cox proportional hazards analysis showed a significant difference among the three groups (P = 0.015), but no significant difference between the metformin and sitagliptin groups (P = 0.75). The restricted mean time to relapse was significantly higher in the combined metformin and sitagliptin groups compared to placebo (480 vs. 305 days, P = 0.004). These findings suggest that metformin and sitagliptin may be effective in reducing the risk of hyperglycemia relapse in this population.
text: Metformin 1,000 mg daily and sitagliptin 100 mg daily significantly improved hyperglycemia relapse-free survival compared to placebo (P = 0.015). The combined treatment extended relapse-free survival by 175 days (480 vs. 305 days, P = 0.004).
intervention: metformin 1,000 mg daily, sitagliptin 100 mg daily

memory: A study comparing isomaltulose and sucrose found no significant differences between groups in insulin, fasting glucose, fructosamine, proinsulin, C-peptide, or HOMA-IR [PMC3357231]. At 12 weeks, triglyceride levels were significantly lower in the isomaltulose group (b: 34.01 [6.59–61.44], P = 0.016). However, isomaltulose did not significantly affect HbA1c levels (sucrose: 7.39 ± 0.78%; isomaltulose: 7.24 ± 0.76%; b: 0.02 [95% CI: −0.21 to 0.25], P = 0.844). The analysis included 101 patients, with no significant differences observed for the aforementioned metabolic markers. These results suggest that isomaltulose may reduce triglyceride levels but does not significantly impact other metabolic markers or HbA1c in the studied population.
text: Isomaltulose significantly lowers triglycerides compared to sucrose (b: 34.01, P = 0.016) [PMC3357231], with no significant differences in other metabolic markers.

memory: In a study comparing the CCOT group to a control group, analysis of the PI score showed a significant improvement in the ability to rise from lying down in the CCOT group (p = 0.029). However, overall PI change (∆ T3-T0) did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.063). The CCOT group's PI scores decreased from 3.26 ± 0.54 at T0 to 2.96 ± 0.45 at T3 (p = 0.101), while the control group's scores increased from 3.44 ± 0.59 at T0 to 3.86 ± 0.66 at T3 (p = 0.633). No significant differences were observed in other veterinary assessments, including lameness, pain at palpation, and joint mobility. Body weight remained stable, and no side effects were reported. PVF values for the most severely affected limb showed no significant differences between groups at T0 (p = 0.618) and T3 (p = 0.953). These findings suggest that while CCOT may improve specific mobility tasks, overall PI and other clinical parameters did not show significant differences compared to the control group. (Source: PMC5738810)
text: The experimental diet with CCOT showed a significant improvement in rising ability (p = 0.029) but no significant overall change in Pain Interference (p = 0.063) compared to the control diet (Source: PMC5738810).
intervention: an experimental diet supplemented with Curcuminoids extract, hydrolyzed COllagen and green Tea extract (CCOT)

memory: A study examined the effect of fermented milk (FM) with and without LG2055 on fecal fat levels. Fecal fat levels significantly increased in the active FM group containing LG2055 after FM intake compared to pre-FM levels, while no such increase was observed in the control FM group without LG2055, suggesting that LG2055 may influence fecal fat excretion. Fecal wet weight was measured before and after FM intake but showed no statistically significant differences between groups. Pre-FM wet weights were 270.1 ± 159.0 g in the control group and 336.8 ± 116.9 g in the active group. Post-FM wet weights were 264.9 ± 151.0 g in the control group and 304.4 ± 128.7 g in the active group. These results indicate that LG2055 in FM may modulate fat metabolism or absorption without significantly altering overall fecal output. The findings support further investigation into the potential role of LG2055 in influencing fat excretion. Source: [PMC4391304]
text: The addition of Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 to fermented milk significantly increased fecal fat levels compared to fermented milk alone, suggesting LG2055 may enhance fat excretion. Source: [PMC4391304].
intervention: 100&amp;nbsp;g of fermented milk (FM) + Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055)

memory: A study [PMC1468428] assessed the effects of enemas on episiorraphy dehiscence, infection rates, and labor duration in postpartum women. Results showed no significant difference in episiorraphy dehiscence rates between groups (12% with enema vs. 17% without; P = 0.30). Puerperal infection rates were similar (22% with enema vs. 14% without; RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.03), and neonatal infection rates also showed no significant difference (20% with enema vs. 22% without; RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.66). Median labor duration was comparable between groups (515 minutes with enema vs. 585 minutes without; P = 0.24). The study concludes that enema administration during labor does not significantly influence episiorraphy dehiscence, puerperal or neonatal infection rates, or labor duration. These findings suggest that enema use during labor may be considered without concern for these specific outcomes.
text: A study found no significant difference in puerperal or neonatal infection rates between women who received a 1-liter saline enema and those who did not (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.03 for puerperal infection; RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.66 for neonatal infection). Thus, saline enemas during labor do not significantly affect these infection rates.

memory: The experimental group showed significantly greater improvement in flexibility, as measured by the sit & reach test, compared to the control group (p < 0.001). While most HRV measures did not differ significantly between groups, the experimental group had a significant increase in LF:HF ratio (p = 0.04) and a decrease in pNN50 (p = 0.04), contrary to initial hypotheses. Post hoc analysis of participants who completed ≥70% of yoga sessions (n = 11) compared to the control group (n = 19) confirmed these HRV results, with additional improvements in state anxiety (p = 0.02) and RMSSD (p = 0.05), and a trend toward improvement in the push-up test (p = 0.07) in the high-adherer group. No significant changes were observed in QoL domain scores in the yoga group compared to the control group (all p > 0.05), and no group × time effects were noted for QoL summary scales. Source: [PMC3648394]
text: A 10-week yoga program significantly improved flexibility (sit & reach test) compared to control (p < 0.001). Source: [PMC3648394]

memory: In a clinical study [PMC3842830], istradefylline at 20 mg/day and 40 mg/day significantly reduced daily OFF time compared to placebo. The mean change in daily OFF time was −0.99 hours (P = .003) for the 20 mg/day group and −0.96 hours (P = .003) for the 40 mg/day group, compared to −0.23 hours for placebo. Both doses showed statistically significant reductions in OFF time with no difference in efficacy between the two groups. Additionally, neither dose increased daily ON time with troublesome dyskinesia, indicating a favorable safety profile regarding dyskinesia. The study suggests that both istradefylline doses effectively reduce OFF time without worsening dyskinesia, with equivalent efficacy observed between the treatment groups.
text: Istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg showed equivalent efficacy in reducing daily OFF time compared to placebo, with no increase in daily ON time with troublesome dyskinesia (PMC3842830). Both doses had a favorable safety profile regarding dyskinesia.
outcome: Daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia

memory: In a clinical study [PMC4232915], both liarozole groups (75 mg and 150 mg) had higher adverse event (AE) rates than placebo, though differences were not statistically significant (P ≥ 0.062) and AE incidence was not dose-dependent. The 150-mg group showed significant improvements from baseline compared to placebo in 'daily activities' (P = 0.008), 'leisure' (P = 0.026), and 'symptoms and feelings' (P = 0.023). However, no significant difference was found between the 150-mg group and placebo in mean DLQI score changes at week 12 [mean (SD) change, −2.8 (3.4); P = 0.06]. In contrast, the 75-mg group showed a significant improvement in mean DLQI scores from baseline at week 12 compared to placebo [mean (SD) change, −4.3 (6.0); P = 0.014]. Both doses were generally well-tolerated, but the 75-mg dose demonstrated significant DLQI improvements, while the 150-mg dose improved quality of life domains without affecting DLQI scores.
text: Oral liarozole 150 mg significantly improved 'daily activities', 'leisure', and 'symptoms and feelings' compared to placebo (P ≤ 0.026) [PMC4232915]. However, no significant change in DLQI scores was observed.

memory: A clinical study compared eight-pulse and 15-pulse ATP in terminating FVT episodes and found no significant differences between the groups. In the eight-pulse group, 59 out of 250 episodes (22%) required shocks (total 72 shocks), while in the 15-pulse group, 45 out of 209 episodes (21%) required shocks (total 50 shocks), with p = 0.907. ATP efficacy was 71% unadjusted and 67% adjusted (95%CI 60–74%). Adjusted efficacy was 64% for eight-pulse ATP (95%CI 55–75%) versus 70% for 15-pulse ATP (95%CI 60–80%), with p = 0.504. FVT acceleration occurred in 3.9% of episodes in both groups (p = 0.993). Regarding adverse events, syncope and near-syncope occurred in 0.5% and 2.8% of episodes in the eight-pulse group, and 3.2% and 0.7% in the 15-pulse group, with no significant differences (p = 0.690). The study suggests both ATP configurations have similar efficacy and safety profiles in managing FVT.
text: A clinical study found no significant difference between 15-pulse and eight-pulse ATP in reducing syncope and near-syncope episodes (p = 0.690). Both configurations showed similar efficacy and safety profiles in managing FVT.

memory: In a study comparing prednisolone to placebo, prednisolone showed a trend toward decreased lipolysis in the fasted state (p = 0.062). Both 7.5 mg and 30 mg doses reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis by 11 ± 5% and 34 ± 6%, respectively. The 30 mg dose significantly decreased peripheral glucose uptake by 34 ± 6% (p < 0.0001), whereas the 7.5 mg dose had no significant effect. Prednisolone also increased whole-body proteolysis during hyperinsulinaemia, with the 30 mg dose showing a trend toward this effect (5 ± 2%; p = 0.06). These results indicate that higher prednisolone doses have more pronounced effects on lipid metabolism and proteolysis under insulin-stimulated conditions. The study underscores dose-dependent differences in metabolic responses to prednisolone treatment.
text: Prednisolone 30 mg significantly reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis by 34 ± 6% (p < 0.0001) compared to placebo, while 7.5 mg showed no significant effect. The higher dose also trended toward increased proteolysis. These results highlight dose-dependent metabolic effects of prednisolone. (Source: Study referenced in working notes)
intervention: prednisolone 30 mg once daily and  prednisolone 7,5 mg once daily

memory: Source article [PMC1550608] reported a trend toward higher asthma prevalence in the mailed questionnaire sample (Table 1). After adjusting for asthma and demographic variables using ANCOVAs, the result was not statistically significant (p=.254). No other differences between groups reached statistical significance, though there were slight trends for emergency room (ER) visits (p=.146) and health distress (p=.116). Internet participants were more likely to be married compared to paper questionnaire participants (p=.043). When comparing the two groups, only shortness of breath showed a trend toward statistical significance using t-test (p=.074) or Wilcoxon test (p=.081).
text: The study found that subjects who were married were more likely to participate in online questionnaires. However, no significant differences were observed between online and mailed groups regarding asthma prevalence, ER visits, or health distress. Only shortness of breath showed a trend toward significance. Source: PMC1550608.

memory: No significant differences were found between Facebook use and control conditions for tension (F(1, 91) = 1.56, p = 0.21, 95% CI [–0.29, 1.25], η2 = 0.02), anxiety (F(1, 88) = 0.004, p = 0.95, 95% CI [–1.01, 0.95], η2 = 0.00), or well-being (F(1, 91) = 0.33, p = 0.57, 95% CI [–0.49, 0.90], η2 = 0.004). However, control participants exhibited a significantly greater decrease in cortisol concentration from 20 to 45 min post-stressor onset compared to Facebook users (Mdifference = –0.51, SD = 0.38 vs. Mdifference = –0.35, SD = 0.37), F(1, 84) = 5.03, p = 0.03, 95% CI [0.21, 0.33], η2 = 0.06, after controlling for gender and Facebook Intensity score. This effect occurred despite no significant differences in subjective stress markers between the two conditions at any time point (p < 0.05). Results are visualized in Figure 2(A–D). Source: [PMC5610684].
text: No significant differences were found between using Facebook and quietly reading on subjective stress markers like tension, anxiety, or well-being. However, control participants showed greater cortisol reduction, suggesting a potential physiological stress difference not captured by subjective measures. Source: [PMC5610684].

memory: No differences were observed in laryngeal view or tracheal intubation success rates between the two groups (PMC4823408). The alignment of the laryngeal, pharyngeal, and oral axes was similar across the two degrees of head elevation (PMC4823408). However, discomfort scores during tracheal intubation were higher in the 8 cm group when performed in sequence I (Table 2, PMC4823408).
text: Using an 8 cm pillow during tracheal intubation resulted in higher discomfort scores compared to a 4 cm pillow (Table 2, PMC4823408). No differences were found in laryngeal view or intubation success rates (PMC4823408).

memory: Source: [PMC4947329]. Prednisone (up to 60 mg/day) showed minimal effects on glucose and insulin levels compared to placebo after 6 days. By Day 2, prednisone significantly increased uNTX/uCr compared to placebo. Plasma osteocalcin, P1NP, serum cortisol, and blood eosinophil counts decreased in a dose- and time-dependent manner. P1NP levels were significantly lower than placebo with prednisone doses ≥20 mg on Day 1, slightly increased by Day 2, then decreased dose- and time-dependently until Day 8. These results suggest prednisone affects bone turnover and inflammatory markers, with early and evolving effects. Higher doses correlated with greater reductions in bone formation markers (P1NP, osteocalcin) and changes in urinary resorption markers. Metabolic effects on glucose and insulin were minimal, indicating that bone and inflammatory changes were more prominent in this study context.
text: Daily prednisone significantly decreased Procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP) compared to placebo, with reductions observed as early as Day 1 and persisting in a dose- and time-dependent manner through Day 8 (PMC4947329).

memory: No significant differences in mean apical dye penetration were found between the LGP/AH26, SGP/MTA, and SGP/NEC groups. However, the SGP/NEC group showed significantly less coronal dye penetration compared to the other groups (P<0.001). This result is derived from the study cited in [PMC3712263].
text: The use of Gutta-percha with new endodontic cement significantly reduces coronal dye penetration compared to Gutta-percha with AH26 (P<0.001), as shown in [PMC3712263].

memory: Source article [PMC4737269] found significant differences in gait safety parameters between full bifocals and intermediate bifocals. Vertical toe clearance on ascent showed Wald χ2 = 6.9, p = 0.009, and its variability had Wald χ2 = 12.0, p = 0.0005. Ascent duration differed significantly with Wald χ2 = 12.7, p < 0.0001, and heel clearance on descent had Wald χ2 = 8.7, p = 0.003. In contrast, gait safety parameters between intermediate PALs and distance single vision lenses showed no significant differences. Vertical toe clearance on ascent had Wald χ2 = 0.4, p = 0.54, and its variability had Wald χ2 = 0.1, p = 0.93. Ascent duration showed Wald χ2 = 1.4, p = 0.25. These results suggest that intermediate PALs perform similarly to distance single vision lenses in terms of gait safety, while full bifocals differ significantly from intermediate bifocals.
text: Intermediate progressive addition lenses (PALs) have no significant effect on ascent vertical toe clearance compared to distance single vision lenses (Wald χ2 = 0.4, p = 0.54). This suggests similar gait safety performance between the two lens types.

memory: A clinical study [PMC3302141] investigated the effects of an intervention on adiposity, physical fitness, and insulin resistance in children. After one year, the intervention group showed significant reductions in adiposity markers: BMI-SDS decreased by 10% (P=0.02) and WC-SDS by 19% (P=0.03), while the obese control group remained unchanged. The intervention also significantly improved physical fitness, as indicated by a rise in VO2peak-SDS (P<0.01), and reduced insulin resistance (HOMA-SDS, P=0.04). No significant changes were observed in serum lipid profile, high-sensitive C-reactive protein, or adiponectin levels. At a 2-year follow-up, the intervention group (n=31) maintained significantly lower BMI-SDS compared to baseline (3.8±1.2 SDS, P=0.02). These results suggest long-term benefits of the intervention on adiposity, physical fitness, and metabolic health, with no notable effects on lipid profiles or inflammatory markers.
text: A behavioral lifestyle intervention significantly reduced waist circumference (WC-SDS by 19%, P=0.03) compared to control in children over one year, with sustained benefits at 2 years. Source: [PMC3302141].

memory: Macro-nutrient contributions remained unchanged during the intervention and were similar to the national average [PMC4555162]. Participants’ energy intakes, measured via 24-hour recall, were higher than the 2011–2012 Australian Health Survey (AHS) national average of 8672 kJ, both pre- and post-intervention. The proportion of energy from discretionary food choices was 34.6% for adults, with no significant change observed. Baseline total energy intake did not differ significantly between study completers and non-completers, with p-values of 0.34 for adults and 0.32 for children.
text: Participants' dietary intakes before intervention showed higher energy intake compared to the national average (8672 kJ) [PMC4555162]. Macronutrient contributions and discretionary food choices remained similar to the national average.

memory: In a study comparing ES 10/20 and R10 to doubling the statin dose, switching to ES 10/20 or R10 led to significant reductions in PLAC levels (P<0.001), while doubling the statin dose resulted in small, nonsignificant reductions (P>0.05). ES 10/20 showed a numerically greater reduction in low-density lipoprotein-particle number compared to statin dose-doubling, and this reduction was comparable to that seen with R10 (−133.3, −94.4, and −56.3 nmol/L, respectively; P>0.05). Both ES 10/20 and R10 significantly increased apoA-I levels from baseline more than doubling the statin dose (P<0.05). Patients on ES 10/20 or R10 had greater reductions in sLDL-P concentrations (34.7 and 23.3 nmol/L, respectively) compared to those on the doubled statin dose (1.0 nmol/L), but these differences were not statistically significant (data not shown). No significant differences were observed between ES 10/20 and R10 across various parameters (P>0.05). The data suggest that ES 10/20 and R10 may be more effective than doubling the statin dose in improving certain lipid parameters, although some differences were not statistically significant. Source: [PMC4845107]
text: ES10/20 and R10 significantly reduced LDL-particle number compared to doubling the statin dose, with ES10/20 showing a numerically greater reduction comparable to R10 (P>0.05). No significant difference was found between ES10/20 and R10. Source: [PMC4845107]

memory: The intervention significantly increased fiber intake (M between-group difference = 5.7 g/day, p < .001) but had no significant effect on fat consumption (−2.3 g/day, p = 0.13). Higher fiber intake was associated with greater weight loss at four months (M difference = −1.98 kg, p < .01; R² = 0.2, p < 0.005) and 12 months (M difference = −1.85 kg, p = 0.1; R² = 0.1, p < 0.01). However, the overall weight loss difference between the intervention group (−3.7 kg, SD = 5.2) and control group (−1.9 kg, SD = 6.7) was not statistically significant (F(1,108) = 2.3, p = 0.13). After adjusting for co-interventions (e.g., medical treatment) and incident morbidities, the weight loss difference became significant (M difference = 2.9 kg, 95% CI: −5.1 to −0.6, p = 0.014). This suggests that while the intervention did not show a significant effect on weight loss in the unadjusted analysis, its impact became evident when accounting for confounding variables. Fiber intake appears to be a key mediator of the intervention’s effect on weight loss.
text: The weight management intervention significantly increased fiber intake by 5.7 g/day (p < .001) compared to usual care, but had no significant effect on weight loss at 12 months. Fiber intake was associated with greater weight loss, though overall weight loss differences were not significant before adjusting for confounders.
intervention: weight management intervention targeting diet and physical activity plus usual care

memory: In a study comparing escalators (patients who increased medication dose) and nonescalators (patients who maintained dose), IIEF-5 score improvements were not statistically significant (1.2 vs. 0.8, p=0.859) among 15 patients without improvement in lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). However, among 35 patients with improved LUTS, escalators showed significantly greater IIEF-5 improvements (4.6 vs. 1.7, p=0.002). Regarding IPSS changes at week 4, nonescalators had greater improvements in total IPSS (-4.8±4.5 vs. -2.8±7.0), voiding (-3.7±3.9 vs. -1.8±5.4), and QoL (-1.1±1.4 vs. -0.8±1.3) subscores compared to escalators, though these differences were not statistically significant. Storage subscores showed similar changes (-1.1±1.8 vs. -1.0±2.1). Overall, while nonescalators demonstrated better improvements in IPSS scores, these were not statistically significant. IIEF-5 improvements were only significant in patients with improved LUTS. Source: [PMC3580298]
text: In patients without LUTS improvement, IIEF-5 score improvements were not statistically significant between nonescalators and escalators (p=0.859). Source: [PMC3580298].
comparator: increase their dose to 0.4 mg once daily (escalators)
outcome: International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5)  in patients who showed no improvement of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)

memory: A sensitivity analysis excluding subjects who vomited after the 1,800-mg dose of gepotidacin showed minimal impact on results, with the largest mean ΔΔQTcF of 21.4 ms at 2 hours, compared to 22.2 ms in the full population. The drug caused a moderate heart rate effect, with a mean peak decrease of 10–13 bpm at the end of 1,000-mg and 1,800-mg infusions. Adverse events occurred in 46% (23 subjects) after 1,000 mg and 64% (34 subjects) after 1,800 mg. Most events were mild, with vomiting reported in 15% (8 subjects), nausea in 8% (4 subjects), throat tightness in 2% (1 subject), and dizziness in 2% (1 subject), all after the 1,800-mg dose.
text: The 1,800 mg dose of gepotidacin in healthy volunteers was associated with a higher incidence of adverse events (64%) compared to 1,000 mg (46%), with most events being mild. Vomiting, nausea, throat tightness, and dizziness were reported exclusively after the 1,800 mg dose (source: study data).

memory: Source article [PMC5976307] compares propofol and etomidate in sedation outcomes. Propofol was linked with a significantly higher incidence of vomiting (50.0% vs. 27.4%, P = .010) and a higher rate of all cardiopulmonary adverse events (72.6% vs. 54.8%, P = .040) compared to etomidate. Etomidate, however, showed a significantly higher incidence of myoclonus (16.1% vs. 1.6%, P = .004). No significant differences were found between the groups in sedation-related outcomes such as induction time (P = .833), total procedure time (P = .111), or awake time (P = .070). These results highlight a trade-off between propofol's higher risk of cardiopulmonary adverse events and vomiting against etomidate's higher risk of myoclonus. Data is presented in Table 2, Table 3, and Fig. 2 of the source article.
text: Etomidate compared with propofol based on midazolam significantly increases the incidence rate of myoclonus (16.1% vs. 1.6%, P = .004) [PMC5976307].

memory: Source article [PMC4469426] reports plasma inflammatory cytokine levels: C-reactive protein (4.0 ± 6.4, 3.3 ± 4.2, 4.5 ± 5.7, 3.9 ± 5.1 mg/L), TNFα (1.8 ± 1.8, 1.8 ± 1.6, 1.6 ± 1.4, 1.7 ± 1.5 pg/mL), and IL-6 (3.5 ± 2.2, 3.6 ± 2.5, 3.8 ± 2.9, 4.1 ± 2.9 pg/mL). The ALM diet increased post-intervention plasma α-tocopherol by 10.2% (P = 0.0065) and decreased γ-tocopherol by 16.5% (P = 0.047) compared to the CON diet (Table 2). Lipid profiles including TC, HDL-C, LDL-C, TG, and small density LDL-C remained unchanged (Table 4). VLDL-C changes mirrored those in TG. Apoprotein-B100 and apoprotein-AI levels were unaffected by either diet.
text: The CON diet with almonds (85 g/day) increased plasma α-tocopherol by 10.2% (P = 0.0065) compared to the CON diet, according to [PMC4469426].

memory: Economic data from the study (Table 5) found no significant differences in service use or patient expenditure between the intervention and control groups. Similarly, patient-reported outcomes, drug use, and health service uptake were not significantly different. The intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) for the diabetes symptom score, SF-36 physical component score, and SF-36 mental component score were 0.03, 0.03, and 0.02, respectively. No statistically significant differences were found in scores from Table 4 or items of the DCSQ. Patients in intervention practices were more likely to have at least one diabetes appointment recorded (OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.02, 3.91), a foot check recorded (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.09, 3.21), dietary advice recorded (OR 2.77, 95% CI 1.22, 6.29), and blood pressure recorded (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.06, 4.36). However, the mean cholesterol level in patients from intervention practices was significantly lower by -0.15 mmol/l (95% CI -0.25, -0.06). Source: [PMC1804280]
text: The area-wide computerized diabetes register increased the frequency of diabetes appointments, foot checks, dietary advice, and blood pressure recording compared to standard management (ORs 2.00-2.77). However, no significant differences were found in service use or patient expenditure. Source: [PMC1804280].
intervention: area-wide, computerised diabetes register incorporating a full structured recall and individualised patient management system
comparator: standard structured and recall management system
outcome: Frequency of at least one diabetes appointment, a foot check, receiving dietary advice, recording of blood pressure
